@@@ include/abi/caps.h @@@
1:/*
2: * include/abi/caps.h
3: * Privilege levels and capability bits — the single source of truth shared
4: * by the kernel (kernel/include/kernel/sched.h) and userland (os1.h).
5: * USR-SEC-03 #79.
6: *
7: * A process has one PRIVILEGE LEVEL (the root of access control and the
8: * resolver for the future multi-user model) and a CAPABILITY MASK (the
9: * fine-grained authority enforced at the syscall boundary).
10: */
11:#ifndef NEXS_API_CAPS_H
12:#define NEXS_API_CAPS_H
13:
14:/* Privilege levels — lower number = more privilege.  PLVL_MACHINE is the
15: * machine's own identity (kernel/nxinit/services): NOT a login user,
16: * unkillable, bypasses every capability check.  Real users slot in at
17: * root/user/guest. */
18:#define PLVL_MACHINE 0
19:#define PLVL_ROOT 1
20:#define PLVL_USER 2
21:#define PLVL_GUEST 3
22:#define PLVL_COUNT 4
23:
24:/* Fine-grained capabilities — one per gated syscall surface. */
25:#define CAP_SPAWN (1u << 0)     /* SYS_SPAWN / spawn_level / spawn_caps */
26:#define CAP_FS_WRITE (1u << 1)  /* SYS_FILE_WRITE + open-for-write      */
27:#define CAP_IPC_ANY (1u << 2)   /* SYS_SEND to non-relatives           */
28:#define CAP_WINDOW (1u << 3)    /* SYS_CREATE_WINDOW + SET_FOCUS(self) */
29:#define CAP_REG_WRITE (1u << 4) /* SYS_REGISTRY write op               */
30:#define CAP_ALL                                                                \
31:  (CAP_SPAWN | CAP_FS_WRITE | CAP_IPC_ANY | CAP_WINDOW | CAP_REG_WRITE)
32:
33:/*
34: * caps_for_level - the DEFAULT capability mask a privilege level is created
35: * with.  THE single source of truth for the level->mask policy, deliberately
36: * here in the shared caps header rather than in the scheduler.
37: *
38: * It used to live as `level_ceiling[]` inside kernel/sched/process.c and was
39: * MIRRORED by hand in userland (nxperm.h nxperm_level_mask()).  Two copies of
40: * one policy in two trees is a latent drift bug — a level's authority would
41: * silently disagree between what the kernel grants and what the permissions UI
42: * claims.  Both now derive from this one function, which is also where a future
43: * per-service manifest (ASTRA §7.11 Q5) layers its overrides.
44: *
45: * Semantics of the LEVELS themselves (the capability MASK is only half of it —
46: * the other half is the per-namespace ACLs: the VFS write tree in
47: * vfs_write_allowed(), the registry owner model, /sys/bin immutability):
48: *   machine  full authority, bypasses every capability check (it IS the check).
49: *   root     full capability mask; restricted only by the resource ACLs
50: *            (cannot write /sys/bin or /system — that is the VFS ACL's job,
51: *            not the mask's).
52: *   user     full capability mask today; the per-service tightening and the
53: *            per-user home partition are the forward work (B2.3/B2.4).  A user
54: *            is separated from root by the ACLs, not yet by the mask.
55: *   guest    windows only — the one level whose MASK is genuinely narrowed.
56: *
57: * A static inline so it costs nothing and both freestanding kernel and
58: * userland translation units can use it without a linked object.
59: */
60:static inline unsigned int caps_for_level(int level) {
61:  switch (level) {
62:  case PLVL_MACHINE:
63:  case PLVL_ROOT:
64:  case PLVL_USER:
65:    return CAP_ALL;
66:  case PLVL_GUEST:
67:    return CAP_WINDOW;
68:  default:
69:    return 0u;
70:  }
71:}
72:
73:/* Spawn-mode flags (arg3 of SYS_SPAWN / SYS_SPAWN_CAPS) — the nxexec model
74: * (#193): a DETACHED child does NOT inherit the spawner as its controlling
75: * terminal (ctty_win stays -1).  For launchers (nxlauncher): a windowless
76: * child spawned detached fails closed (no output surface) instead of writing
77: * into the launcher's soon-minimized window as if it were a shell.  Windowed
78: * children are unaffected (own-window-first stdout resolution). */
79:#define SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED (1u << 0)
80:/* Every bit outside SPAWN_FLAGS_ALL is REJECTED kernel-side with -EINVAL
81: * (fail closed): the spawn surface is the front door of process execution
82: * and must never silently accept unknown semantics (#193 hardening). */
83:#define SPAWN_FLAGS_ALL SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED
84:
85:/*
86: * fd redirection on spawn (Phase 4, shell `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`).  The PARENT opens
87: * the redirect targets (getting handles in its OWN table), then hands the kernel
88: * a list of {child_fd <- parent_fd} pairs; SYS_SPAWN dups each parent handle
89: * into the child's fd slot, OVERWRITING the pre-installed console (fork+dup2
90: * semantics, no string marshaling).  A child reading fd 0 / writing fd 1 then
91: * hits the FILE object instead of the terminal.  The parent closes its own
92: * copies after the spawn returns.
93: */
94:#define SPAWN_MAX_REDIR 8
95:struct spawn_redir {
96:  int child_fd;  /* slot in the CHILD's table (0=stdin,1=stdout,2=stderr,…) */
97:  int parent_fd; /* an open handle to dup down, in source_pid's table */
98:  /* source_pid: whose table `parent_fd` belongs to.
99:   *   0  = the SPAWNER's own table (the ordinary case: a shell redirecting its
100:   *        own descriptors into its own child).
101:   *   >0 = ANOTHER process's table.  This exists because an execution SERVICE
102:   *        spawns on a client's behalf, so the fds belong to the CLIENT, not to
103:   *        the spawner.
104:   *
105:   * AUTHORITY: a non-zero source_pid is accepted only from a PRIVILEGED caller.
106:   * Reaching into another process's handle table is a system-service power, not
107:   * an application one — the same rule, and the same reasoning, as
108:   * OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER.  Without the gate any process could siphon descriptors
109:   * out of any other by naming them here. */
110:  int source_pid;
111:};
112:
113:#endif /* NEXS_API_CAPS_H */
114:

@@@ include/abi/nx_abi.h @@@
1:#ifndef _ABI_NX_ABI_H
2:#define _ABI_NX_ABI_H
3:/*
4: * nx_abi.h — compile-time layout contracts for structures that cross a
5: * boundary this compiler cannot see across.
6: *
7: * WHY THIS IS IN abi/ AND NOT IN kernel/.  Three consumers share these
8: * structures and only one of them is the kernel:
9: *
10: *   - the kernel, compiled for amd64 AND for aarch64;
11: *   - userland, compiled separately against its own api headers;
12: *   - hand-written assembly, which addresses fields by constant offset.
13: *
14: * Nothing in the build makes those agree.  A field added to a shared struct
15: * recompiles every consumer happily and changes what each of them means by the
16: * same bytes — and the symptom appears wherever the mismatch is first read,
17: * never where it was introduced.  `kernel/nx_contract.h` includes THIS header
18: * rather than defining its own copy, because two definitions of one contract
19: * is the duplication failure these asserts exist to catch.
20: *
21: * Use them on: anything in an IPC message, anything a syscall copies to or
22: * from userland, anything assembly touches, and anything written to disk.
23: */
24:
25:/* NX_ABI_ASSERT - a claim checked at compile time, on every build of every
26: * arch and of userland.  C11 `_Static_assert` is available in both toolchains
27: * this project uses; there is no runtime cost and no way to skip it. */
28:#define NX_ABI_ASSERT(cond, msg) _Static_assert((cond), msg)
29:
30:/* NX_ASSERT_OFFSET - pin a field's position.  The message names the consumers
31: * that break, because "offsetof changed" tells the next reader nothing about
32: * what to go and look at. */
33:#define NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(type, field, off)                                     \
34:  NX_ABI_ASSERT(__builtin_offsetof(type, field) == (off),                      \
35:                #type "." #field " moved: assembly, the other architecture "   \
36:                      "and/or userland address this by constant offset")
37:
38:/* NX_ASSERT_SIZE - pin a whole structure.  Size matters independently of
39: * offsets: an array of these is indexed by stride, so growing the struct moves
40: * every element even when no field moved. */
41:#define NX_ASSERT_SIZE(type, bytes)                                            \
42:  NX_ABI_ASSERT(sizeof(type) == (bytes),                                       \
43:                "sizeof(" #type ") changed: any array of it is indexed by "    \
44:                "stride, so every element moves — check userland, the other "  \
45:                "architecture, and on-disk images")
46:
47:#endif /* _ABI_NX_ABI_H */
48:

@@@ include/abi/object.h @@@
1:/*
2: * include/abi/object.h
3: * Object / handle / capability ABI — the single source of truth shared by the
4: * kernel (kernel/include/kernel/object.h) and userland (os1.h), exactly like
5: * caps.h.  This is the REAL capability layer mandated by ASTRA §6.1/6.2/6.5
6: * (seL4 capability semantics, Mach ports-as-objects, NT per-process handle
7: * table): authority is an UNFORGEABLE handle to a kernel OBJECT, not ambient
8: * identity (a PID/level mask).
9: *
10: * A handle is a small non-negative integer naming a slot in the calling
11: * process's PRIVATE handle table.  The integer is meaningless in any other
12: * process and cannot be forged into authority: a value with no installed slot
13: * is -EBADF.  Each handle carries a RIGHTS subset; rights are separable
14: * (a handle may hold READ without WRITE) and attenuable (duplicate/grant can
15: * only drop rights, never add — escalation is impossible by construction,
16: * mirroring the monotonic spawn cut in caps.h).
17: *
18: * Relationship to the B3 model: caps.h (CAP_* level mask) is the AMBIENT
19: * authority that gates *acquiring* a capability (e.g. CAP_FS_WRITE to open a
20: * file for write); object.h is the per-object capability you then hold and
21: * delegate.  The B3 per-process fd table (kernel/fd.h) is the seed this
22: * generalizes (ASTRA §6.2).
23: */
24:#ifndef NEXS_API_OBJECT_H
25:#define NEXS_API_OBJECT_H
26:
27:/* Object types (kobject.type and the `type` argument of handle_create). */
28:#define OBJ_TYPE_NONE    0
29:#define OBJ_TYPE_FILE    1 /* a VFS-backed file (read/write/seek by offset)   */
30:#define OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS 2 /* a process: wait on exit, query, capability IPC  */
31:#define OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY  3 /* a registry key: read/write its value (§6.6)     */
32:#define OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW  4 /* a compositor window: read info / minimize / restore /
33:                            * focus / close via a handle (ASTRA §6.7)         */
34:#define OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE 5 /* a controlling-terminal stream (stdin/stdout/stderr):
35:                            * read() drains keyboard input, write() goes to the
36:                            * caller's window/ctty.  Handles 0/1/2 are pre-installed
37:                            * as this (ASTRA §6.2 "Input device" + window-stream);
38:                            * the per-process fd table folded into it.         */
39:#define OBJ_TYPE_PIPE    6 /* an anonymous byte pipe: a kernel ring buffer with a
40:                            * READ end and a WRITE end (separate handles/rights).
41:                            * read() blocks until data or the last writer closes
42:                            * (EOF); write() appends.  Created by SYS_PIPE; the
43:                            * shell wires `cmd | cmd` by dup'ing the ends into the
44:                            * children's fd 0/1 (ASTRA §6.2).                   */
45:#define OBJ_TYPE_PORT    7 /* a MACH-style PORT: a first-class message mailbox that
46:                            * IS a capability (ASTRA §6.5).  Rights are the port
47:                            * rights: OS1_RIGHT_WRITE = send right,
48:                            * OS1_RIGHT_READ = receive right.  A service keeps the
49:                            * receive right and hands clients attenuated SEND-only
50:                            * handles, so a client addresses the SERVICE rather
51:                            * than a pid — repairing the seL4 rule "no
52:                            * PID-by-number access without a capability" that the
53:                            * ambient pid-addressed SYS_SEND violates.  The
54:                            * semantics ride on the existing IPC message type; a
55:                            * port only relocates the QUEUE and the AUTHORITY. */
56:#define OBJ_TYPE_COUNT   8 /* number of distinct OBJ_TYPE_* values (NONE..PORT);
57:                            * sizes per-type accounting arrays (e.g. live-object
58:                            * stats in include/api/sysstats.h)                 */
59:/* Reserved for later migrations (ASTRA §6.2/§6.7): gpu, audio. */
60:
61:/* Access rights — a per-handle subset, separable and attenuable (seL4). */
62:#define OS1_RIGHT_READ      (1u << 0) /* OS1_object_read                       */
63:#define OS1_RIGHT_WRITE     (1u << 1) /* OS1_object_write                      */
64:#define OS1_RIGHT_WAIT      (1u << 2) /* OS1_object_wait                       */
65:#define OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE (1u << 3) /* OS1low_handle_duplicate               */
66:#define OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER  (1u << 4) /* OS1low_cap_grant to another process   */
67:#define OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY   (1u << 5) /* destroy the underlying object         */
68:#define OS1_RIGHT_MUTATE    (1u << 7) /* mutate the namespace rooted at a DIR  */
69:#define OS1_RIGHT_ALL                                                          \
70:  (OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_WAIT | OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE |   \
71:   OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER | OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY | OS1_RIGHT_MUTATE)
72:/* OS1_RIGHT_CREATE — ACQUISITION-ONLY flag for handle_create(OS1_NS_FS): a
73: * missing path is created as an empty FILE through the provider (ASTRA §6.8,
74: * open(O_CREAT) → handle_create), gated by the same vfs_write_allowed seam as
75: * every write.  Meaningful only together with OS1_RIGHT_WRITE.  NOT part of
76: * OS1_RIGHT_ALL: it is stripped before the handle is installed, so it never
77: * appears in cap_query results and cannot be duplicated/granted. */
78:#define OS1_RIGHT_CREATE    (1u << 6)
79:
80:/* Control verbs for OS1_object_ctl(handle, cmd, arg) — type-specific actions
81: * on an object you hold a capability to (seL4: the right IS the authority). */
82:#define OBJ_CTL_KILL     1 /* PROCESS: terminate the target (needs OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY)  */
83:#define OBJ_CTL_MINIMIZE 2 /* WINDOW: hide to background, dock-restorable (RIGHT_WRITE) */
84:#define OBJ_CTL_RESTORE  3 /* WINDOW: show + raise + focus (RIGHT_WRITE)                */
85:#define OBJ_CTL_FOCUS    4 /* WINDOW: give keyboard focus + raise (RIGHT_READ — focus is
86:                            * unprivileged, matching the compositor's open click-to-focus) */
87:#define OBJ_CTL_CLOSE    5 /* WINDOW: destroy just this window (RIGHT_DESTROY)          */
88:#define OBJ_CTL_SEEK     6 /* FILE: set the object's byte offset to arg; returns it     */
89:#define OBJ_CTL_STAT     7 /* FILE: return the current size in bytes (lseek/stat)       */
90:#define OBJ_CTL_STOP     8 /* PROCESS: suspend the target (job control; RIGHT_DESTROY)  */
91:#define OBJ_CTL_CONT     9 /* PROCESS: resume a stopped target (job control; DESTROY)   */
92:#define OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER 11 /* PROCESS: set the target's LOGICAL parent (owner) to
93:                             * `arg` (needs OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY on the target AND a
94:                             * PRIVILEGED caller).  Used by an execution service
95:                             * that spawns on a client's behalf: the spawn makes
96:                             * the SERVICE the mechanical parent, this hands the
97:                             * job back to the requesting CLIENT so kill/stop/cont
98:                             * authority (an ancestry walk) still reaches it.
99:                             * Privileged-only because it DELEGATES authority over
100:                             * a process — it is not a hint (ASTRA §6.5).       */
101:#define OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE 10 /* FILE: truncate to `arg` bytes (needs RIGHT_WRITE).  The
102:                             * provider primitive is whole-file-replace (an offset-0
103:                             * write REPLACES the file), so only arg == 0 (truncate to
104:                             * empty) is expressible here — the case a POSIX
105:                             * write(fd,...,0) CANNOT express, since that is a no-op.
106:                             * Non-empty lengths are composed in libc's ftruncate()
107:                             * (read the head back, rewrite it from offset 0) and never
108:                             * reach the kernel; arg != 0 returns -EINVAL.    */
109:#define OBJ_CTL_MKDIR    12 /* DIR: create the one-component name at user pointer
110:                             * `arg` (needs RIGHT_MUTATE).  The parent directory
111:                             * capability names the namespace being changed.      */
112:#define OBJ_CTL_UNLINK   13 /* DIR: remove the one-component name at user pointer
113:                             * `arg` (needs RIGHT_MUTATE).  Recursive removal is
114:                             * deliberately a userland composition.              */
115:
116:/* Namespaces for handle_create: how the `path` argument is interpreted. */
117:#define OS1_NS_FS   1 /* path is a filesystem path → OBJ_TYPE_FILE            */
118:#define OS1_NS_PROC 2 /* path is a decimal PID string → OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS      */
119:#define OS1_NS_REG  3 /* path is a registry key (dotted) → OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY    */
120:#define OS1_NS_WIN  4 /* path is a decimal window id → OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW        */
121:#define OS1_NS_PORT 5 /* path is a service port NAME → OBJ_TYPE_PORT (§6.5).
122:                       * Acquiring with OS1_RIGHT_READ (receive right) CREATES
123:                       * the port and makes the caller its owner — that is how a
124:                       * service publishes itself; acquiring without READ yields
125:                       * a SEND-only capability to an existing port, which is how
126:                       * a client reaches a SERVICE BY NAME instead of by pid. */
127:
128:/* cap_query packs the object type and the held rights into one return value:
129: * (type << 24) | rights.  A negative return is an errno (-EBADF). */
130:#define OS1_CAPQ_PACK(type, rights) (((long)((type) & 0xFF) << 24) | ((rights) & 0x00FFFFFF))
131:#define OS1_CAPQ_TYPE(v)            (((v) >> 24) & 0xFF)
132:#define OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(v)          ((v) & 0x00FFFFFF)
133:
134:/* Window state bits for struct window_info.flags (ASTRA §6.7: windows as
135: * objects).  A window manager (e.g. /sys/bin/nxui, the dock) reads these to lay
136: * out its app list; an app reads its own window's bits via OS1_object_read. */
137:#define WININFO_VISIBLE   (1u << 0) /* currently composited (shown)             */
138:#define WININFO_MINIMIZED (1u << 1) /* sent to background, dock-restorable      */
139:#define WININFO_TOPMOST   (1u << 2) /* always-on-top overlay, no decorations    */
140:#define WININFO_FOCUSED   (1u << 3) /* owns keyboard focus                      */
141:#define WININFO_PASSIVE   (1u << 4) /* click-through (system popup)             */
142:
143:/* One enumerated window.  Returned in bulk by SYS_WINDOW_ENUM / OS1_window_enum
144: * and singly by OS1_object_read() on an OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW handle.  `title` mirrors
145: * struct window.title[64] in the compositor. */
146:struct window_info {
147:  int id;             /* compositor window id                  */
148:  int pid;            /* owning process                        */
149:  int x, y;           /* on-screen position                    */
150:  int w, h;           /* on-screen draw size                   */
151:  unsigned int flags; /* WININFO_* bitmask                     */
152:  char title[64];     /* window title                          */
153:};
154:
155:#endif /* NEXS_API_OBJECT_H */
156:

125:/* os1_strerror - errno -> human-readable string.  Single source of truth for
126: * BOTH kernel and userland (this header is already the shared home of the
127: * EPERM..ENOTEMPTY macros above, included by the kernel build via
128: * -Iinclude/api same as userland) — previously userland's lib.c carried its
129: * own 11-case switch (strerror()) that silently fell back to "Unknown
130: * error" for anything past ENOSYS.  static inline: safe to include in any
131: * number of translation units, no libc calls. */

273:/* IPC message types */
274:#define IPC_TYPE_RAW 0
275:#define IPC_TYPE_INPUT 1
276:#define IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY 0x100
277:#define IPC_TYPE_MOUSE 4
278:#define IPC_TYPE_RESIZE                                                        \
279:  0x200 /* window/desktop resize: data1=w, data2=h (GFX-DYN-01) */
280:
281:/* IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC - marks an IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY message (in .data2) as a
282: * SILENT compositor look-changed ping (nxres_broadcast_look, user/sys/bin/
283: * nxres.h) rather than a user-facing notification — a real notify() call
284: * never sets data2, so the two can never collide.  Lives here (not in
285: * nxres.h) because input_poll_event (user/sys/lib/lib.c) — the SINGLE
286: * consumer of every windowed app's IPC mailbox — needs it too: every app
287: * already funnels keyboard/mouse/resize through that one try_recv() call,
288: * so a second, competing try_recv() loop elsewhere in the same app (the
289: * first version of this feature) silently STOLE mouse/keyboard messages
290: * before input_poll_event ever saw them.  Recognizing the ping inside
291: * input_poll_event itself (as INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED, input.h) keeps the
292: * mailbox single-consumer, exactly like IPC_TYPE_RESIZE already is. */
293:#define IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC 0x4C4F4F4Bu /* "LOOK" */

295:/* IPC message structure */
296:struct ipc_message {
297:  int from;
298:  int type;
299:  uint64_t data1;
300:  uint64_t data2;
301:  char payload[64];
302:};
303:
304:/*
305: * The IPC wire format.  Every keystroke, pointer event, resize and notification
306: * crosses this structure, and it is read by BOTH kernels and by userland's
307: * input_poll_event() — which additionally unpacks a scancode out of the high
308: * bits of data1, so the field WIDTHS are part of the contract and not just the
309: * offsets.  Nothing in the build makes those three views agree; these do.
310: */
311:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct ipc_message, from, 0);
312:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct ipc_message, type, 4);
313:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct ipc_message, data1, 8);
314:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct ipc_message, data2, 16);
315:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct ipc_message, payload, 24);
316:NX_ASSERT_SIZE(struct ipc_message, 88);
317:
318:/*
319: * abi_stat — what SYS_STAT returns.  The kernel-side truth is `struct vfs_stat`
320: * (size + VFS_TYPE_*); this is its ABI shape, so the kernel never has to
321: * include a userland <sys/stat.h> to fill it and userland never has to guess a
322: * layout. libc maps it onto POSIX `struct stat`.
323: *
324: * ABI_S_TYPE_* deliberately match VFS_TYPE_FILE/VFS_TYPE_DIR by value, so the
325: * kernel copies the field through without a translation table that could drift.
326: */
327:#define ABI_S_TYPE_FILE 1
328:#define ABI_S_TYPE_DIR 2
329:
330:struct abi_stat {
331:  unsigned long long size;
332:  unsigned int type; /* ABI_S_TYPE_* */
333:  unsigned int _pad; /* explicit: keeps the struct 16 bytes on both arches */
334:};
335:
336:/* The comment above already CLAIMS 16 bytes on both arches.  This is that claim
337: * checked instead of asserted in prose. */
338:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct abi_stat, size, 0);
339:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct abi_stat, type, 8);
340:NX_ASSERT_SIZE(struct abi_stat, 16);
341:
342:#endif /* _POSIX_TYPES_H */

1:/*
2: * include/abi/syscall_nums.h
3: * NEXS syscall numbers — THE single source of truth (ABI-01/ABI-SYS-01).
4: *
5: * Included by BOTH sides of the ABI:
6: *   - kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c (the dispatch switch)
7: *   - include/api/os1.h (userland API)
8: *   - user/arch/{aarch64,amd64}/syscall.S and user/sys/lib/syscall.S
9: *     (the .S stubs are preprocessed, so they use these macros directly)
10: * A number changed here changes everywhere atomically; there is no second
11: * table to drift out of sync.
12: *
13: * #define-only on purpose: this header must stay assembler-safe.
14: *
15: * Numbering: the POSIX-shaped calls keep their Linux-aarch64 numbers
16: * (63/64/93/169/172) for familiarity; NEXS-specific calls live in the
17: * 200..299 block.  The legacy duplicate IPC numbers (30/31/32) are GONE:
18: * SEND/RECV/TRY_RECV are 230/231/233 only.
19: *
20: * Error model (ABI-02): every syscall returns a negative errno value from
21: * <posix_types.h> on failure (-EFAULT, -ENOMEM, -EINVAL, ...) and >= 0 on
22: * success — the Linux kernel convention.  No global errno is consumed by
23: * the kernel; userland wrappers may derive one if they wish.
24: */

@@@ include/abi/sysstats.h @@@
1:/*
2: * include/abi/sysstats.h
3: * System statistics ABI — the single source of truth shared by the kernel
4: * (kernel/sched/process.c: sys_sysstats) and userland (os1.h, /bin/memstat),
5: * exactly like object.h / ps_info.
6: *
7: * This is the low-overhead instrumentation surface for the progressive-slowdown
8: * campaign (perf brief §1).  A single OS1_sys_stats() syscall (SYS_SYSSTATS,
9: * high-level OS1_ introspection namespace, sibling of SYS_GETPROCS/
10: * SYS_GET_IDENTITY) copies ONE struct os1_sysstats snapshot to userland; a
11: * userspace poller (/bin/memstat) diffs successive snapshots to derive rates,
12: * per-interval mean latency, and monotonic-drift signals.  No per-tick console
13: * printing — the snapshot is pulled on demand to avoid the console-contention
14: * Heisenbug.
15: *
16: * NO HARDCODED SYSTEM DIMENSIONS (capability / real-source-of-truth model):
17: * this struct never invents its own CPU count or object-type count.
18: *   - The CPU count reported (sched_ncpu) is the REAL detected count (kernel
19: *     `nr_cpus`, set at SMP bring-up).  Scheduler load is reported as
20: *     aggregates (runnable total + deepest single-CPU runqueue) rather than a
21: *     fixed-size per-CPU array, so the ABI layout depends on NO CPU-count
22: *     constant at all — adding cores never changes the struct.
23: *   - obj_live_by_type[] is dimensioned by OBJ_TYPE_COUNT from object.h (the
24: *     real object-type source of truth), not a private copy.
25: *
26: * Counter conventions:
27: *   - *_calls / *_switches / *_ns_total are CUMULATIVE since boot; the poller
28: *     subtracts successive samples to get per-interval rates and means.
29: *   - *_ns_max / *_high_water_bytes are running maxima since boot.
30: *   - largest_contig_run / free_run_count / zombie_count / runnable /
31: *     runq_max / live_by_type are INSTANTANEOUS snapshots at collection time.
32: *
33: * Types: deliberately uses unsigned long long (8 B) / unsigned int (4 B) only,
34: * so the header needs no stdint dependency and has identical layout on both
35: * LP64 targets (x86_64-elf, aarch64-none-elf).  Versioned (version +
36: * struct_size) so the struct can grow without breaking older pollers.
37: */
38:#ifndef NEXS_API_SYSSTATS_H
39:#define NEXS_API_SYSSTATS_H
40:
41:#include "object.h" /* OBJ_TYPE_COUNT — real object-type source of truth */
42:
43:#define OS1_SYSSTATS_VERSION 1
44:
45:struct os1_sysstats {
46:  unsigned int version;     /* = OS1_SYSSTATS_VERSION                            */
47:  unsigned int struct_size; /* = sizeof(struct os1_sysstats), forward-compat     */
48:  unsigned long long uptime_ns; /* monotonic ns since boot (rate denominator)    */
49:
50:  /* --- PMM (page-frame allocator), page-granular --- */
51:  unsigned long long pmm_total_pages;
52:  unsigned long long pmm_free_pages;
53:  unsigned long long pmm_largest_contig_run;     /* pages — fragmentation signal */
54:  unsigned long long pmm_free_run_count;         /* distinct free runs — frag.    */
55:  unsigned long long pmm_alloc_calls;            /* cumulative                    */
56:  unsigned long long pmm_free_calls;             /* cumulative                    */
57:  unsigned long long pmm_alloc_search_ns_total;  /* cumulative bitmap-search time */
58:  unsigned long long pmm_alloc_search_ns_max;    /* worst single search (ns)      */
59:
60:  /* --- kmalloc (kernel heap) --- */
61:  unsigned long long km_heap_total_bytes;        /* pool size (never shrinks yet) */
62:  unsigned long long km_bytes_in_use;            /* live user bytes               */
63:  unsigned long long km_high_water_bytes;        /* peak bytes_in_use             */
64:  unsigned long long km_live_allocs;             /* live allocations              */
65:
66:  /* --- scheduler (aggregates over the REAL online CPUs, no fixed array) --- */
67:  unsigned long long sched_ctx_switches; /* cumulative real switches             */
68:  unsigned int sched_nproc;              /* active process slots                 */
69:  unsigned int sched_zombie_count;       /* DEAD/ZOMBIE not yet reaped           */
70:  unsigned int sched_ncpu;               /* REAL online CPUs (kernel nr_cpus)    */
71:  unsigned int sched_runnable;           /* READY+RUNNING processes (load)       */
72:  unsigned int sched_runq_max;           /* deepest single-CPU runqueue (imbalance) */
73:  unsigned int _pad0;                    /* keep following ull array 8-aligned    */
74:
75:  /* --- object/handle manager (capability layer) --- */
76:  unsigned long long obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_COUNT]; /* live kobjects per type */
77:};
78:
79:#endif /* NEXS_API_SYSSTATS_H */
80:

@@@ include/api/sys/wait.h @@@
1:#ifndef _SYS_WAIT_H
2:#define _SYS_WAIT_H
3:
4:#include <posix_types.h>
5:
6:/*
7: * Minimal POSIX <sys/wait.h> for the OS1 userspace libc.
8: *
9: * waitpid() wraps the PROCESS-capability wait and now delivers the REAL exit
10: * code (PLAN-2026-07-17 Phase 2): the kernel stores exit_code on sys_exit and
11: * the libc encodes it into the standard status word.  OS1 has no signal model,
12: * but a process that died by KILL/fault (never called exit) is reported as
13: * WIFSIGNALED with a stand-in SIGKILL(9), vs WIFEXITED for a clean exit.  Impl
14: * in the libc layer, NOT an OS1 syscall.  Note: the POSIX wait(int*) is
15: * intentionally NOT declared here — it would collide with the OS1 base
16: * wait(int pid); ported code uses waitpid().
17: */
18:
19:#define WNOHANG   1
20:#define WUNTRACED 2
21:
22:/* Standard status encoding: the exit code sits in bits 8..15, the low byte is
23: * the terminating signal (always 0 here — no signals). */
24:#define WIFEXITED(status)   (((status) & 0x7f) == 0)
25:#define WEXITSTATUS(status) (((status) >> 8) & 0xff)
26:#define WIFSIGNALED(status) (((status) & 0x7f) != 0)
27:#define WTERMSIG(status)    ((status) & 0x7f)
28:
29:pid_t waitpid(pid_t pid, int *status, int options);
30:
31:#endif /* _SYS_WAIT_H */
32:

@@@ include/api/ctype.h @@@
1:#ifndef _CTYPE_H
2:#define _CTYPE_H
3:
4:static inline int tolower(int c) {
5:    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') return c + ('a' - 'A');
6:    return c;
7:}
8:
9:static inline int toupper(int c) {
10:    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') return c - ('a' - 'A');
11:    return c;
12:}
13:
14:static inline int isspace(int c) {
15:    return (c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\n' || c == '\v' || c == '\f' || c == '\r');
16:}
17:
18:static inline int isblank(int c) {
19:    return (c == ' ' || c == '\t');
20:}
21:
22:static inline int isdigit(int c) {
23:    return (c >= '0' && c <= '9');
24:}
25:
26:static inline int isxdigit(int c) {
27:    return (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F');
28:}
29:
30:static inline int isalpha(int c) {
31:    return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z');
32:}
33:
34:static inline int isalnum(int c) {
35:    return isalpha(c) || isdigit(c);
36:}
37:
38:static inline int isupper(int c) {
39:    return (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z');
40:}
41:
42:static inline int islower(int c) {
43:    return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z');
44:}
45:
46:static inline int isprint(int c) {
47:    return (c >= 0x20 && c < 0x7f);
48:}
49:
50:static inline int iscntrl(int c) {
51:    return (c >= 0 && c < 0x20) || c == 0x7f;
52:}
53:
54:static inline int isgraph(int c) {
55:    return (c > 0x20 && c < 0x7f);
56:}
57:
58:static inline int ispunct(int c) {
59:    return isgraph(c) && !isalnum(c);
60:}
61:
62:#endif

@@@ include/api/execsvc.h @@@
1:/*
2: * include/api/execsvc.h
3: * Execution service protocol — the contract between a client and nxexec
4: * (ASTRA §6.4 SRL service, §6.5 port capability).
5: *
6: * This is an API header, NOT an ABI one: the protocol never crosses the syscall
7: * boundary.  It is carried by userland primitives the kernel already exports
8: * (a port capability + a pipe), so include/abi stays reserved for the
9: * kernel<->userland contract.
10: *
11: * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
12: * TRANSPORT — why the request does NOT travel inside the message
13: *
14: * struct ipc_message carries a 64-byte payload; a realistic request (program
15: * path + argv + redirections + cwd) is far larger.  Truncating argv would
16: * silently corrupt commands, so the protocol uses the split ASTRA §6.5 already
17: * names ("sync RPC + async messaging, OUT-OF-LINE MEMORY TRANSFER"):
18: *
19: *   1. the PORT message is a small RENDEZVOUS header naming the service (as a
20: *      capability, never a pid) and carrying handles to the out-of-line
21: *      channels;
22: *   2. the request BODY travels through a PIPE the client created and delegated
23: *      with OS1low_cap_grant() — arbitrary size, flow-controlled, and already
24: *      device-verified;
25: *   3. the REPLY returns the same way on a second pipe.
26: *
27: * The delegation is also what AUTHORISES the transfer: the service receives
28: * exactly the two channels the client chose to hand it, and no ambient reach.
29: *
30: * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31: * WIRE FORMAT — fixed header + VARIABLE body
32: *
33: * The body is variable-length by design.  A fixed worst-case record wasted over
34: * a kilobyte on every short command AND still imposed an arbitrary ceiling on
35: * argv; sizing the transfer to the request removes both problems at once.
36: *
37: * The header is fixed and declares `body_len`, so the receiver validates the
38: * length BEFORE reading and never sizes a buffer from an unbounded client
39: * number — the length is checked against EXECSVC_BODY_MAX first.  Every string
40: * in the body is NUL-terminated and every parse step is bounded by body_len, so
41: * a malformed or hostile body cannot walk off the end.
42: *
43: * Body layout (packed, in this order):
44: *     struct execsvc_redir redir[nredir]
45: *     cwd '\0'
46: *     argv[0] '\0' argv[1] '\0' ... argv[argc-1] '\0'
47: */
48:#ifndef _EXECSVC_H
49:#define _EXECSVC_H
50:
51:#include <caps.h> /* struct spawn_redir, SPAWN_MAX_REDIR, SPAWN_FLAG_* */
52:#include <os1.h>  /* OS1NX_PORT_EXEC, struct ipc_message */
53:
54:/* Protocol version: a client and a service built at different times must fail
55: * LOUDLY rather than misread each other's layout. */
56:#define EXECSVC_VERSION 2
57:
58:/* ipc_message.type values for the rendezvous header. */
59:#define EXECSVC_REQ_SPAWN 0x4558 /* 'EX': please execute; see field map below */
60:
61:/*
62: * Rendezvous header layout inside struct ipc_message (the only part that must
63: * fit in 64 bytes — it carries references, not content):
64: *
65: *   type       = EXECSVC_REQ_SPAWN
66: *   payload[0] = (int) REQUEST pipe READ end   } as the SERVICE sees them
67: *   payload[1] = (int) REPLY   pipe WRITE end  }
68: *   from       = stamped by the kernel; the service's only trustworthy
69: *                statement of WHO is asking, and therefore the basis for
70: *                authorising the request and assigning the job's logical
71: *                owner (Q3).
72: *
73: * The client sends with OS1_port_send_caps(port, &msg, {req_r, rep_w}, 2) and
74: * does NOT fill those slots itself: a handle index means something only inside
75: * ONE process's table, so the kernel TRANSLATES the transferred handles into
76: * the receiver's table and writes the receiver-side indices here.  Putting the
77: * client's own numbers on the wire would hand the service meaningless slots —
78: * which is exactly the bug this layout note exists to prevent.
79: */
80:
81:/*
82: * How the service obtains the descriptor backing one redirection — the Q2
83: * hybrid, so both mechanisms coexist without a protocol break.
84: *
85: *   GRANTED:   the client already delegated the handle with OS1low_cap_grant(),
86: *              so `ref` indexes the SERVICE's own table.  Capability-correct:
87: *              an explicit, per-handle delegation the client consented to.
88: *              Costs a grant round-trip per fd.
89: *
90: *   CLIENT_FD: `ref` indexes the CLIENT's table and the kernel takes it
91: *              directly (spawn_redir.source_pid).  No per-fd round-trip.
92: *              AUTHORITY RULE: the kernel permits a non-zero source_pid only
93: *              from a PRIVILEGED caller — the same rule as OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER,
94: *              and for the same reason: reaching into another process's handle
95: *              table is a system-service power, not an application one.  The
96: *              service additionally restricts the source to the REQUESTER
97: *              (ipc_message.from), so it can never be talked into harvesting a
98: *              third party's descriptors.
99: */
100:#define EXECSVC_FD_GRANTED   0
101:#define EXECSVC_FD_CLIENT_FD 1
102:
103:struct execsvc_redir {
104:  int child_fd; /* slot in the CHILD (0=stdin, 1=stdout, 2=stderr, …) */
105:  int source;   /* EXECSVC_FD_* — how to interpret `ref`               */
106:  int ref;      /* handle index, in the service's or the client's table */
107:};
108:
109:/* Hard ceiling the service enforces before reading a body.  Generous for real
110: * command lines, small enough that a hostile client cannot make the service
111: * commit meaningful memory. */
112:#define EXECSVC_BODY_MAX 4096
113:#define EXECSVC_ARG_MAX  32  /* argv entries (bound, not a fixed cost) */
114:#define EXECSVC_PATH_MAX 128
115:
116:struct execsvc_spawn_hdr {
117:  unsigned int version;  /* EXECSVC_VERSION */
118:  unsigned int flags;    /* SPAWN_FLAG_* (caps.h) */
119:  int argc;              /* 1..EXECSVC_ARG_MAX */
120:  int nredir;            /* 0..SPAWN_MAX_REDIR */
121:  int want_ctty;         /* non-zero: child gets a controlling terminal */
122:  unsigned int body_len; /* bytes following this header; <= EXECSVC_BODY_MAX */
123:};
124:
125:/* The reply is small and fixed — it carries no user-controlled vector. */
126:struct execsvc_spawn_rep {
127:  unsigned int version;
128:  int pid;       /* > 0 on success, else a negative errno */
129:  int owner_pid; /* logical owner the service assigned (Q3) */
130:  int reserved;
131:  char resolved[EXECSVC_PATH_MAX]; /* the path actually executed */
132:};
133:
134:/*
135: * execsvc_spawn - client stub: ask the execution service to run argv.
136: * Returns the child pid, or < 0 if the service is unreachable — callers MUST
137: * fall back to spawning directly, because the service is supervised and can be
138: * briefly absent across a respawn.  Implemented in user/sys/lib/execsvc_client.c
139: * (its own unit, so Phase 10a/12 can move service clients out of the libc as a
140: * build change rather than another extraction).
141: */
142:int execsvc_spawn(int argc, char *const argv[], unsigned int flags);
143:
144:#endif /* _EXECSVC_H */
145:

@@@ include/api/image.h @@@
1:#ifndef OS1_IMAGE_H
2:#define OS1_IMAGE_H
3:
4:#include <stdint.h>
5:#include <stdlib.h>
6:#include <ctype.h>
7:#include <graphics.h>
8:#include <os1.h>
9:#include <string.h>
10:
11:typedef struct {
12:  int w;
13:  int h;
14:  uint32_t *pixels;
15:} os1_image_t;
16:
17:#define OS1_IMAGE_OK 0
18:#define OS1_IMAGE_ERR_ARG      (-1)
19:#define OS1_IMAGE_ERR_IO       (-2)
20:#define OS1_IMAGE_ERR_FORMAT   (-3)
21:#define OS1_IMAGE_ERR_NOMEM    (-4)
22:#define OS1_IMAGE_ERR_LIMIT    (-5)
23:
24:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_FILE_BYTES (16u * 1024u * 1024u)
25:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION  4096
26:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS     (4096u * 4096u)
27:
28:/*
29: * OS1 stdimage baseline.
30: *
31: * Decoders return sanitized ARGB32 pixels only. Encoded bytes are read into a
32: * bounded scratch buffer, metadata/script chunks are not exposed to callers, and
33: * all display paths consume this inert pixel buffer instead of the source file.
34: */
35:static inline os1_image_t *os1_image_load(const char *path) {
36:  int w = 0;
37:  int h = 0;
38:  uint32_t *raw_pixels = graphics_load_image(path, &w, &h);
39:  if (!raw_pixels) {
40:    return NULL;
41:  }
42:
43:  os1_image_t *img = (os1_image_t *)malloc(sizeof(os1_image_t));
44:  if (!img) {
45:    free(raw_pixels);
46:    return NULL;
47:  }
48:
49:  img->w = w;
50:  img->h = h;
51:  img->pixels = raw_pixels;
52:  return img;
53:}
54:
55:static inline int os1_image_ext_eq(const char *a, const char *b) {
56:  if (!a || !b)
57:    return 0;
58:  while (*a && *b) {
59:    if (tolower((unsigned char)*a) != tolower((unsigned char)*b))
60:      return 0;
61:    a++;
62:    b++;
63:  }
64:  return *a == '\0' && *b == '\0';
65:}
66:
67:static inline int os1_image_path_has_known_ext(const char *path) {
68:  static const char *const exts[] = {
69:      ".png",  ".apng", ".jpg",  ".jpeg", ".jpe",  ".jfif", ".pjpeg",
70:      ".pjp",  ".bmp",  ".dib",  ".gif",  ".tga",  ".icb",  ".vda",
71:      ".vst",  ".psd",  ".pic",  ".ppm",  ".pgm",  ".pbm",  ".pnm",
72:      ".webp", ".tif",  ".tiff", ".ico",  ".cur",  ".qoi",  ".avif",
73:      ".heic", ".heif", ".jp2",  ".j2k",  ".jxl",  ".exr",  NULL};
74:  if (!path)
75:    return 0;
76:  const char *ext = strrchr(path, '.');
77:  if (!ext || ext == path)
78:    return 0;
79:  for (int i = 0; exts[i]; i++) {
80:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, exts[i]))
81:      return 1;
82:  }
83:  return 0;
84:}
85:
86:static inline int os1_image_path_has_decodable_ext(const char *path) {
87:  static const char *const exts[] = {
88:      ".png", ".apng", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".jpe", ".jfif", ".pjpeg", ".pjp",
89:      ".bmp", ".dib",  ".gif", ".tga",  ".icb", ".vda",  ".vst",   ".psd",
90:      ".pic", ".ppm",  ".pgm", ".pbm",  ".pnm", NULL};
91:  if (!path)
92:    return 0;
93:  const char *ext = strrchr(path, '.');
94:  if (!ext || ext == path)
95:    return 0;
96:  for (int i = 0; exts[i]; i++) {
97:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, exts[i]))
98:      return 1;
99:  }
100:  return 0;
101:}
102:
103:static inline void os1_image_draw(int win_id, int x, int y, os1_image_t *img) {
104:  if (!img || !img->pixels || win_id < 0)
105:    return;
106:  graphics_blit(win_id, x, y, img->w, img->h, img->pixels);
107:}
108:
109:static inline void os1_image_free(os1_image_t *img) {
110:  if (!img)
111:    return;
112:  free(img->pixels);
113:  free(img);
114:}
115:
116:static inline int os1_image_fit_size(int src_w, int src_h, int max_w, int max_h,
117:                                     int allow_upscale, int *out_w,
118:                                     int *out_h) {
119:  if (src_w <= 0 || src_h <= 0 || max_w <= 0 || max_h <= 0 || !out_w || !out_h)
120:    return OS1_IMAGE_ERR_ARG;
121:
122:  uint64_t w_by_h = (uint64_t)max_h * (uint64_t)src_w;
123:  uint64_t h_by_w = (uint64_t)max_w * (uint64_t)src_h;
124:  int w;
125:  int h;
126:
127:  if (w_by_h <= h_by_w) {
128:    h = max_h;
129:    w = (int)(w_by_h / (uint64_t)src_h);
130:  } else {
131:    w = max_w;
132:    h = (int)(h_by_w / (uint64_t)src_w);
133:  }
134:
135:  if (!allow_upscale && w >= src_w && h >= src_h) {
136:    w = src_w;
137:    h = src_h;
138:  }
139:  if (w < 1)
140:    w = 1;
141:  if (h < 1)
142:    h = 1;
143:  *out_w = w;
144:  *out_h = h;
145:  return OS1_IMAGE_OK;
146:}
147:
148:static inline os1_image_t *os1_image_resample(const os1_image_t *src, int dst_w,
149:                                              int dst_h) {
150:  if (!src || !src->pixels || src->w <= 0 || src->h <= 0 || dst_w <= 0 ||
151:      dst_h <= 0)
152:    return NULL;
153:  if ((uint64_t)dst_w * (uint64_t)dst_h > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS)
154:    return NULL;
155:
156:  os1_image_t *dst = (os1_image_t *)malloc(sizeof(os1_image_t));
157:  if (!dst)
158:    return NULL;
159:  dst->pixels = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)dst_w * (size_t)dst_h * 4u);
160:  if (!dst->pixels) {
161:    free(dst);
162:    return NULL;
163:  }
164:  dst->w = dst_w;
165:  dst->h = dst_h;
166:
167:  for (int y = 0; y < dst_h; y++) {
168:    int sy = (int)(((uint64_t)y * (uint64_t)src->h) / (uint64_t)dst_h);
169:    if (sy >= src->h)
170:      sy = src->h - 1;
171:    for (int x = 0; x < dst_w; x++) {
172:      int sx = (int)(((uint64_t)x * (uint64_t)src->w) / (uint64_t)dst_w);
173:      if (sx >= src->w)
174:        sx = src->w - 1;
175:      dst->pixels[y * dst_w + x] = src->pixels[sy * src->w + sx];
176:    }
177:  }
178:  return dst;
179:}
180:
181:static inline os1_image_t *os1_image_resample_fit(const os1_image_t *src,
182:                                                  int max_w, int max_h,
183:                                                  int allow_upscale) {
184:  int w = 0;
185:  int h = 0;
186:  if (!src ||
187:      os1_image_fit_size(src->w, src->h, max_w, max_h, allow_upscale, &w, &h) !=
188:          OS1_IMAGE_OK)
189:    return NULL;
190:  return os1_image_resample(src, w, h);
191:}
192:
193:#endif // OS1_IMAGE_H

@@@ include/api/input.h @@@
1:#ifndef _INPUT_H
2:#define _INPUT_H
3:
4:#include <os1.h>
5:#include <posix_types.h>
6:
7:/* Input event types */
8:#define INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD 1
9:#define INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE 2
10:#define INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE                                                      \
11:  3 /* window/desktop resized: event.resize.w/h (GFX-DYN-01) */
12:#define INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED                                                \
13:  4 /* compositor style/theme/bg changed elsewhere                             \
14:     * (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h) — no                                  \
15:     * payload; re-read nxres_get_*() and                                      \
16:     * reload the palette.  Delivered via the                                  \
17:     * same try_recv() input_poll_event already                                \
18:     * drains (IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC, posix_types.h)                             \
19:     * instead of a second competing recv loop. */
20:
21:/* Key states */
22:#define KEY_RELEASED 0
23:#define KEY_PRESSED 1
24:#define KEY_REPEAT 2
25:
26:/* Mouse buttons — evdev BTN_* codes as delivered in input_event_t.mouse.button
27: * (the compositor forwards the raw evdev code, NOT a 0/1/2 index).  Shared here
28: * so every app matches the same constants instead of redefining them. */
29:#ifndef MOUSE_BTN_LEFT
30:#define MOUSE_BTN_LEFT 0x110
31:#define MOUSE_BTN_RIGHT 0x111
32:#define MOUSE_BTN_MIDDLE 0x112
33:#endif
34:
35:/* evdev scancodes for special (non-ASCII) keys, reported in
36: * input_event_t.keyboard.scancode.  Windowed apps that need cursor/navigation
37: * keys match on these (the ASCII .key byte is 0 for them).  Values mirror the
38: * Linux/virtio-input keycodes the driver emits. */
39:#define INPUT_KEY_ESC 1
40:#define INPUT_KEY_BACKSPACE 14
41:#define INPUT_KEY_TAB 15
42:#define INPUT_KEY_ENTER 28
43:#define INPUT_KEY_HOME 102
44:#define INPUT_KEY_UP 103
45:#define INPUT_KEY_LEFT 105
46:#define INPUT_KEY_RIGHT 106
47:#define INPUT_KEY_DOWN 108
48:#define INPUT_KEY_END 107
49:#define INPUT_KEY_DELETE 111
50:
51:typedef struct {
52:  int type;
53:  union {
54:    struct {
55:      unsigned char key;
56:      int state;
57:      uint16_t scancode;
58:      char utf8[8];
59:    } keyboard;
60:    struct {
61:      int button;
62:      int state;
63:      int x, y;
64:    } mouse;
65:    struct {
66:      int w, h; /* new logical size of the window (or desktop) */
67:    } resize;
68:  };
69:} input_event_t;
70:
71:/**
72: * Poll for an input event.
73: * Returns 1 if an event was retrieved, 0 if no events are pending, -1 on error.
74: */
75:int input_poll_event(input_event_t *event);
76:
77:#endif

7:/* ============================================================================
8: * NexsOS1 Math Library — IEEE-754 single-precision (float) and double
9: *
10: * Built for bare-metal userland (-nostdlib -fno-builtin -ffreestanding).
11: * No libgcc/libm dependency; all algorithms are self-contained.
12: *
13: * Coverage:
14: *   - float:  sqrtf, fabsf, floorf, ceilf, fmodf, powf, expf, logf,
15: *             sinf, cosf, tanf, asinf, acosf, atanf, atan2f,
16: *             fminf, fmaxf, roundf, truncf
17: *   - double: sqrt, fabs, floor, ceil, fmod, pow, exp, log,
18: *             sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2,
19: *             fmin, fmax, round, trunc
20: *   - int:    abs, labs
21: *   - fixed:  sin_fp, cos_fp, fixmul (legacy 16.16, kept for compat)
22: * ============================================================================
23: */

118: * read().  Was void; widened to long so ported POSIX code can check the count
119: * (libc-layer change only — the SYS_WRITE syscall already returns it). */
120:long write(int fd, const char *buf, size_t count);
121:long get_time(void);   /* compat shim for OS1_time_now() (DIR-01 F4) */
122:int  get_pid(void);
123:void exit(int status);
124:long gethostid(void);
125:int  spawn(const char *path);
126:/* spawn_args: like spawn(), but hands the child an argv vector (the shell
127: * uses it to pass a filename, e.g. `kilo notes.txt`).  argv[0] is the program
128: * name as invoked; argv[argc] need not be NULL (the kernel terminates the
129: * copy at argc).  The kernel marshals the strings onto the child's stack and
130: * sets argc/argv as main()'s first two arguments per the C ABI. */
131:int  spawn_args(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[]);
132:/* Sandboxed spawn (USR-SEC-03 #79).  level = PLVL_*; caps = OR of CAP_*.
133: * The kernel clamps both: a child is never more privileged than its parent,
134: * never above the level's ceiling, never more than the parent holds.
135: * spawn_level() uses the level's default capability preset. */
136:long spawn_caps(const char *path, int level, unsigned long caps);
137:long spawn_level(const char *path, int level);
138:int  kill_process(int pid);
139:int  wait(int pid);
140:void yield(void);
141:
142:/* --- Process control: OS1low_ canonical primitives (ASTRA §6.1, DIR-01 F4) ---
143: * The stable low-level process surface.  The bare verbs above
144: * (spawn/spawn_args/spawn_caps/spawn_level/kill_process/wait/yield/get_pid/exit)
145: * are kept as zero-breakage compat shims that forward to these — every existing
146: * caller keeps compiling, while new code should prefer the OS1low_ names. */
147:long OS1low_process_spawn(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[]);

309:/* Environment — the OS1 NATIVE surface (ASTRA §6.8: POSIX is a personality
310: * ABOVE this, never beside it).
311: *
312: * The environment is per-process state the kernel owns and inherits at spawn,
313: * structurally identical to cwd — hence its place next to OS1_fs_chdir.
314: *
315: * These functions OWN the fact that the kernel exposes the environment through
316: * the `sys.proc.<pid>.env.*` registry namespace, with `sys.env.*` underneath as
317: * the machine defaults.  Nothing above this layer knows that: getenv/setenv are
318: * a thin mapping onto these, exactly as pipe() maps onto OS1low_pipe() and
319: * chdir() onto OS1_fs_chdir().  The first cut of Phase 17 got this wrong — it
320: * built registry key strings inside getenv/setenv, which put the registry's
321: * path syntax into the POSIX API (plan S8).
322: *
323: * OS1_env_get   0 on hit, negative if this process has no such variable AND no
324: *               machine default exists.  Resolution is process-first: a value
325: *               set by this process SHADOWS the default, for it and its
326: *               children only.
327: * OS1_env_set   set for THIS process.  A NULL/empty value unsets.  Writing
328: *               another process's environment needs privilege and is not
329: *               reachable from here by design.
330: * OS1_env_unset remove this process's value, exposing any machine default.
331: * OS1_env_enum  newline-separated NAMEs of this process's own variables;
332: *               returns the length written, or negative. */
333:int OS1_env_get(const char *name, char *buf, size_t size);
334:int OS1_env_set(const char *name, const char *value);
335:int OS1_env_unset(const char *name);
336:int OS1_env_enum(char *buf, size_t size);
337:int file_write(const char *path, const void *buf, int size, int offset);
338:int file_read(const char *path, void *buf, int size, int offset);
339:int list_dir(const char *path, char *buf, size_t size);
340:int chdir(const char *path);
341:#ifndef _NEXSOS_GETCWD_POSIX

364:/* --- Service ports (ASTRA §6.5: a port IS a capability) -------------------
365: * A port lets a client address a SERVICE BY NAME instead of by pid, which is
366: * the seL4 rule ("no PID-by-number access without a capability") that the
367: * ambient pid-addressed OS1low_ipc_send cannot satisfy.  Rights ARE the port
368: * rights: receive = OS1_RIGHT_READ (the service), send = OS1_RIGHT_WRITE
369: * (its clients).  These are thin wrappers over handle_create + object I/O —
370: * no new transport, per ASTRA "the semantics ride on the existing IPC layer".
371: *
372: * NAMING STANDARD for system services (2026-07-18): "OS1nx_<service>".
373: */
374:#define OS1NX_PORT_EXEC "OS1nx_exec" /* the nxexec execution service */
375:
376:/* OS1_port_create - publish a service port and take its RECEIVE right (making
377: * this process its owner).  Fails with -EEXIST if the name is already served,
378: * so a rogue process cannot steal a service identity by racing it. */
379:int  OS1_port_create(const char *name);
380:/* OS1_port_open - acquire a SEND-only capability to an existing service port.
381: * -ENOENT if no service published that name. */
382:int  OS1_port_open(const char *name);
383:/* OS1_port_send / OS1_port_recv - one whole ipc_message per call.  send needs
384: * the send right, recv the receive right; recv BLOCKS until a message arrives
385: * and returns 0 when the last sender is gone (so a service loop terminates).
386: * The kernel stamps msg->from, so the sender identity cannot be forged. */
387:long OS1_port_send(int handle, const struct ipc_message *msg);
388:long OS1_port_recv(int handle, struct ipc_message *msg);
389:/* OS1_port_send_caps - send a message AND transfer handles with it.  The
390: * receiver-side indices are written into the leading int slots of msg->payload,
391: * so a service reads usable handles directly.  This is what lets a client
392: * delegate (e.g. pipe ends) to a service it found BY NAME, without ever needing
393: * the service's pid — the property ports exist to provide. */
394:long OS1_port_send_caps(int handle, struct ipc_message *msg, const int *fds,
395:                        int nfds);

43:static inline int os1vid_path_has_known_ext(const char *path) {
44:  if (!path)
45:    return 0;
46:  const char *ext = 0;
47:  for (const char *p = path; *p; p++)
48:    if (*p == '.')
49:      ext = p;
50:  if (!ext)
51:    return 0;
52:  char a[8];
53:  int n = 0;
54:  for (const char *p = ext; *p && n < 7; p++, n++)
55:    a[n] = (char)((*p >= 'A' && *p <= 'Z') ? *p + 32 : *p);
56:  a[n] = '\0';
57:  return strcmp(a, ".mpg") == 0 || strcmp(a, ".mpeg") == 0;
58:}
59:
60:/* ===================================================================== */
61:#ifdef OS1VID_IMPLEMENTATION
62:
63:#define PL_MPEG_IMPLEMENTATION
64:#include "pl_mpeg.h"
65:
66:static uint8_t *os1vid_load_file(const char *path, size_t *out_size) {
67:  *out_size = 0;
68:  long handle =
69:      OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
70:  if (handle < 0)
71:    return 0;
72:
73:  long stat_size = OS1_object_ctl((int)handle, OBJ_CTL_STAT, 0);
74:  if (stat_size <= 0 || (uint64_t)stat_size > OS1VID_MAX_FILE_BYTES) {
75:    OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
76:    return 0;
77:  }
78:
79:  size_t size = (size_t)stat_size;
80:  uint8_t *data = (uint8_t *)malloc(size);
81:  if (!data) {
82:    OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
83:    return 0;
84:  }
85:
86:  size_t total = 0;
87:  while (total < size) {
88:    size_t want = size - total;
89:    if (want > OS1VID_READ_CHUNK_BYTES)
90:      want = OS1VID_READ_CHUNK_BYTES;
91:    long got = OS1_object_read((int)handle, data + total, (unsigned long)want);
92:    if (got <= 0) {
93:      OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
94:      free(data);
95:      return 0;
96:    }
97:    total += (size_t)got;
98:  }
99:  OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
100:
101:  if (total != size) {
102:    free(data);
103:    return 0;
104:  }
105:
106:  *out_size = size;
107:  return data;
108:}
109:
110:os1vid_t *os1vid_open(const char *path) {
111:  if (!path)
112:    return 0;
113:
114:  size_t size = 0;
115:  uint8_t *data = os1vid_load_file(path, &size);
116:  if (!data)
117:    return 0;
118:
119:  plm_t *plm = plm_create_with_memory(data, size, 1);
120:  if (!plm) {
121:    free(data);
122:    return 0;
123:  }
124:
125:  int w = plm_get_width(plm);
126:  int h = plm_get_height(plm);
127:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) {
128:    plm_destroy(plm);
129:    return 0;
130:  }
131:
132:  /* Calculate padded luma dimensions like pl_mpeg does internally (multiples of
133:   * 16) */
134:  int mb_w = (w + 15) >> 4;
135:  int mb_h = (h + 15) >> 4;
136:  int luma_w = mb_w << 4;
137:  int luma_h = mb_h << 4;
138:
139:  os1vid_t *v = (os1vid_t *)malloc(sizeof(os1vid_t));
140:  if (!v) {
141:    plm_destroy(plm);
142:    return 0;
143:  }
144:  memset(v, 0, sizeof(*v));
145:  v->plm = plm;
146:  v->width = w;
147:  v->height = h;
148:  v->luma_width = luma_w;
149:  v->luma_height = luma_h;
150:  v->framerate = plm_get_framerate(plm);
151:
152:  /* Allocate both padded (for decoder) and packed (for drawing) buffers */
153:  v->pixels = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)luma_w * (size_t)luma_h * 4u);
154:  v->packed_pixels = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)w * (size_t)h * 4u);
155:  if (!v->pixels || !v->packed_pixels) {
156:    plm_destroy(plm);
157:    free(v->pixels);
158:    free(v->packed_pixels);
159:    free(v);
160:    return 0;
161:  }
162:
163:  for (int i = 0; i < w * h; i++)
164:    v->packed_pixels[i] = 0xFF000000u;
165:  for (int i = 0; i < luma_w * luma_h; i++)
166:    v->pixels[i] = 0xFF000000u;
167:
168:  plm_set_audio_enabled(plm, 0);
169:  plm_set_loop(plm, 0);
170:
171:  return v;
172:}
173:
174:static void os1vid_video_cb(plm_t *plm, plm_frame_t *frame, void *user) {
175:  (void)plm;
176:  os1vid_t *v = (os1vid_t *)user;
177:
178:  /* Decode into padded buffer with correct stride */
179:  plm_frame_to_bgra(frame, (uint8_t *)v->pixels, v->luma_width * 4);
180:
181:  /* Pack it into packed_pixels (discard macroblock padding) */
182:  for (int y = 0; y < v->height; y++) {
183:    memcpy(&v->packed_pixels[y * v->width], &v->pixels[y * v->luma_width],
184:           v->width * 4);
185:  }
186:  v->has_frame = 1;
187:}
188:
189:int os1vid_update(os1vid_t *v) {
190:  if (!v || !v->plm)
191:    return 0;
192:  v->has_frame = 0;
193:
194:  unsigned long long now = os1_mono_ns();
195:
196:  if (v->paused) {
197:    v->last_ns = now;
198:    return 0;
199:  }
200:
201:  double dt;
202:  if (v->last_ns == 0) {
203:    dt = 0.0;
204:  } else {
205:    dt = (double)(now - v->last_ns) / 1e9;
206:    if (dt > 0.25)
207:      dt = 0.25;
208:  }
209:  v->last_ns = now;
210:
211:  plm_set_video_decode_callback(v->plm, os1vid_video_cb, v);
212:  plm_decode(v->plm, dt);
213:
214:  if (plm_has_ended(v->plm))
215:    v->ended = 1;
216:
217:  return v->has_frame;
218:}
219:
220:void os1vid_set_loop(os1vid_t *v, int loop) {
221:  if (v && v->plm)
222:    plm_set_loop(v->plm, loop);
223:}
224:
225:int os1vid_has_ended(const os1vid_t *v) { return v ? v->ended : 1; }
226:
227:void os1vid_pause(os1vid_t *v) {
228:  if (v)
229:    v->paused = 1;
230:}
231:
232:void os1vid_resume(os1vid_t *v) {
233:  if (!v)
234:    return;
235:  v->paused = 0;
236:  v->last_ns = os1_mono_ns();
237:}
238:
239:int os1vid_is_paused(const os1vid_t *v) { return v ? v->paused : 0; }
240:
241:int os1vid_seek(os1vid_t *v, double seconds) {
242:  if (!v || !v->plm)
243:    return 0;
244:
245:  double dur = plm_get_duration(v->plm);
246:  if (seconds < 0.0)
247:    seconds = 0.0;
248:  if (dur > 0.0 && seconds > dur)
249:    seconds = dur;
250:
251:  plm_set_video_decode_callback(v->plm, os1vid_video_cb, v);
252:  int ok = plm_seek(v->plm, seconds, 1);
253:  if (!ok)
254:    return 0;
255:
256:  v->last_ns = os1_mono_ns();
257:  if (dur <= 0.0 || seconds < dur)
258:    v->ended = 0;
259:
260:  return 1;
261:}
262:
263:double os1vid_get_time(const os1vid_t *v) {
264:  if (!v || !v->plm)
265:    return 0.0;
266:  return plm_get_time(v->plm);
267:}
268:
269:double os1vid_get_duration(const os1vid_t *v) {
270:  if (!v || !v->plm)
271:    return 0.0;
272:  return plm_get_duration(v->plm);
273:}
274:
275:void os1vid_close(os1vid_t *v) {
276:  if (!v)
277:    return;
278:  if (v->plm)
279:    plm_destroy(v->plm);
280:  free(v->pixels);
281:  free(v->packed_pixels);
282:  free(v);
283:}
284:
285:#endif /* OS1VID_IMPLEMENTATION */
286:#endif /* OS1_VID_H */

@@@ include/api/pl_mpeg.h @@@
1:/*
2:PL_MPEG - MPEG1 Video decoder, MP2 Audio decoder, MPEG-PS demuxer
3:SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
4:
5:Dominic Szablewski - https://phoboslab.org
6:
7:
8:-- Synopsis
9:
10:// Define `PL_MPEG_IMPLEMENTATION` in *one* C/C++ file before including this
11:// library to create the implementation.
12:
13:#define PL_MPEG_IMPLEMENTATION
14:#include "plmpeg.h"
15:
16:// This function gets called for each decoded video frame
17:void my_video_callback(plm_t *plm, plm_frame_t *frame, void *user) {
18:	// Do something with frame->y.data, frame->cr.data, frame->cb.data
19:}
20:
21:// This function gets called for each decoded audio frame
22:void my_audio_callback(plm_t *plm, plm_samples_t *frame, void *user) {
23:	// Do something with samples->interleaved
24:}
25:
26:// Load a .mpg (MPEG Program Stream) file
27:plm_t *plm = plm_create_with_filename("some-file.mpg");
28:
29:// Install the video & audio decode callbacks
30:plm_set_video_decode_callback(plm, my_video_callback, my_data);
31:plm_set_audio_decode_callback(plm, my_audio_callback, my_data);
32:
33:
34:// Decode
35:do {
36:	plm_decode(plm, time_since_last_call);
37:} while (!plm_has_ended(plm));
38:
39:// All done
40:plm_destroy(plm);
41:
42:
43:
44:-- Documentation
45:
46:This library provides several interfaces to load, demux and decode MPEG video
47:and audio data. A high-level API combines the demuxer, video & audio decoders
48:in an easy to use wrapper.
49:
50:Lower-level APIs for accessing the demuxer, video decoder and audio decoder, 
51:as well as providing different data sources are also available.
52:
53:Interfaces are written in an object oriented style, meaning you create object 
54:instances via various different constructor functions (plm_*create()),
55:do some work on them and later dispose them via plm_*destroy().
56:
57:plm_* ......... the high-level interface, combining demuxer and decoders
58:plm_buffer_* .. the data source used by all interfaces
59:plm_demux_* ... the MPEG-PS demuxer
60:plm_video_* ... the MPEG1 Video ("mpeg1") decoder
61:plm_audio_* ... the MPEG1 Audio Layer II ("mp2") decoder
62:
63:
64:With the high-level interface you have two options to decode video & audio:
65:
66: 1. Use plm_decode() and just hand over the delta time since the last call.
67:    It will decode everything needed and call your callbacks (specified through
68:    plm_set_{video|audio}_decode_callback()) any number of times.
69:
70: 2. Use plm_decode_video() and plm_decode_audio() to decode exactly one
71:    frame of video or audio data at a time. How you handle the synchronization 
72:    of both streams is up to you.
73:
74:If you only want to decode video *or* audio through these functions, you should
75:disable the other stream (plm_set_{video|audio}_enabled(FALSE))
76:
77:Video data is decoded into a struct with all 3 planes (Y, Cr, Cb) stored in
78:separate buffers. You can either convert this to RGB on the CPU (slow) via the
79:plm_frame_to_rgb() function or do it on the GPU with the following matrix:
80:
81:mat4 bt601 = mat4(
82:	1.16438,  0.00000,  1.59603, -0.87079,
83:	1.16438, -0.39176, -0.81297,  0.52959,
84:	1.16438,  2.01723,  0.00000, -1.08139,
85:	0, 0, 0, 1
86:);
87:gl_FragColor = vec4(y, cb, cr, 1.0) * bt601;
88:
89:Audio data is decoded into a struct with either one single float array with the
90:samples for the left and right channel interleaved, or if the 
91:PLM_AUDIO_SEPARATE_CHANNELS is defined *before* including this library, into
92:two separate float arrays - one for each channel.
93:
94:
95:Data can be supplied to the high level interface, the demuxer and the decoders
96:in three different ways:
97:
98: 1. Using plm_create_from_filename() or with a file handle with 
99:    plm_create_from_file().
100:
101: 2. Using plm_create_with_memory() and supplying a pointer to memory that
102:    contains the whole file.
103:
104: 3. Using plm_create_with_buffer(), supplying your own plm_buffer_t instance and
105:    periodically writing to this buffer.
106:
107:When using your own plm_buffer_t instance, you can fill this buffer using 
108:plm_buffer_write(). You can either monitor plm_buffer_get_remaining() and push 
109:data when appropriate, or install a callback on the buffer with 
110:plm_buffer_set_load_callback() that gets called whenever the buffer needs more 
111:data.
112:
113:A buffer created with plm_buffer_create_with_capacity() is treated as a ring
114:buffer, meaning that data that has already been read, will be discarded. In
115:contrast, a buffer created with plm_buffer_create_for_appending() will keep all
116:data written to it in memory. This enables seeking in the already loaded data.
117:
118:
119:There should be no need to use the lower level plm_demux_*, plm_video_* and 
120:plm_audio_* functions, if all you want to do is read/decode an MPEG-PS file.
121:However, if you get raw mpeg1video data or raw mp2 audio data from a different
122:source, these functions can be used to decode the raw data directly. Similarly, 
123:if you only want to analyze an MPEG-PS file or extract raw video or audio
124:packets from it, you can use the plm_demux_* functions.
125:
126:
127:This library uses malloc(), realloc() and free() to manage memory. Typically 
128:all allocation happens up-front when creating the interface. However, the
129:default buffer size may be too small for certain inputs. In these cases plmpeg
130:will realloc() the buffer with a larger size whenever needed. You can configure
131:the default buffer size by defining PLM_BUFFER_DEFAULT_SIZE *before* 
132:including this library.
133:
134:You can also define PLM_MALLOC, PLM_REALLOC and PLM_FREE to provide your own
135:memory management functions.
136:
137:
138:See below for detailed the API documentation.
139:
140:*/
141:

153:// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
154:// Public Data Types
155:
156:
157:// Object types for the various interfaces
158:
159:typedef struct plm_t plm_t;
160:typedef struct plm_buffer_t plm_buffer_t;
161:typedef struct plm_demux_t plm_demux_t;
162:typedef struct plm_video_t plm_video_t;
163:typedef struct plm_audio_t plm_audio_t;
164:
165:
166:// Demuxed MPEG PS packet
167:// The type maps directly to the various MPEG-PES start codes. PTS is the
168:// presentation time stamp of the packet in seconds. Note that not all packets
169:// have a PTS value, indicated by PLM_PACKET_INVALID_TS.
170:
171:#define PLM_PACKET_INVALID_TS -1
172:
173:typedef struct {
174:	int type;
175:	double pts;
176:	size_t length;
177:	uint8_t *data;
178:} plm_packet_t;
179:
180:
181:// Decoded Video Plane 
182:// The byte length of the data is width * height. Note that different planes
183:// have different sizes: the Luma plane (Y) is double the size of each of 
184:// the two Chroma planes (Cr, Cb) - i.e. 4 times the byte length.
185:// Also note that the size of the plane does *not* denote the size of the 
186:// displayed frame. The sizes of planes are always rounded up to the nearest
187:// macroblock (16px).
188:
189:typedef struct {
190:	unsigned int width;
191:	unsigned int height;
192:	uint8_t *data;
193:} plm_plane_t;
194:
195:
196:// Decoded Video Frame
197:// width and height denote the desired display size of the frame. This may be
198:// different from the internal size of the 3 planes.
199:
200:typedef struct {
201:	double time;
202:	unsigned int width;
203:	unsigned int height;
204:	plm_plane_t y;
205:	plm_plane_t cr;
206:	plm_plane_t cb;
207:} plm_frame_t;
208:
209:
210:// Callback function type for decoded video frames used by the high-level
211:// plm_* interface
212:
213:typedef void(*plm_video_decode_callback)
214:	(plm_t *self, plm_frame_t *frame, void *user);
215:
216:
217:// Decoded Audio Samples
218:// Samples are stored as normalized (-1, 1) float either interleaved, or if
219:// PLM_AUDIO_SEPARATE_CHANNELS is defined, in two separate arrays.
220:// The `count` is always PLM_AUDIO_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME and just there for
221:// convenience.
222:
223:#define PLM_AUDIO_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME 1152
224:
225:typedef struct {
226:	double time;
227:	unsigned int count;
228:	#ifdef PLM_AUDIO_SEPARATE_CHANNELS
229:		float left[PLM_AUDIO_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME];
230:		float right[PLM_AUDIO_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME];
231:	#else
232:		float interleaved[PLM_AUDIO_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME * 2];
233:	#endif
234:} plm_samples_t;
235:
236:
237:// Callback function type for decoded audio samples used by the high-level
238:// plm_* interface
239:
240:typedef void(*plm_audio_decode_callback)
241:	(plm_t *self, plm_samples_t *samples, void *user);
242:

244:// Callback function for plm_buffer when it needs more data
245:

247:
248:

250:

299:// Get whether we have headers on all available streams and we can report the

308:// Probe the MPEG-PS data to find the actual number of video and audio streams
309:// within the buffer. For certain files (e.g. VideoCD) this can be more accurate
310:// than just reading the number of streams from the headers.
311:// This should only be used when the underlying plm_buffer is seekable, i.e. for 
312:// files, fixed memory buffers or _for_appending buffers. If used with dynamic

315:// a few hundred KB should be enough to find all streams.

443:// Seek to the specified time, clamped between 0 -- duration. This can only be 
444:// used when the underlying plm_buffer is seekable, i.e. for files, fixed 
445:// memory buffers or _for_appending buffers. 
446:// If seek_exact is TRUE this will seek to the exact time, otherwise it will 
447:// seek to the last intra frame just before the desired time. Exact seeking can 
448:// be slow, because all frames up to the seeked one have to be decoded on top of
449:// the previous intra frame.
450:// If seeking succeeds, this function will call the video_decode_callback 
451:// exactly once with the target frame. If audio is enabled, it will also call
452:// the audio_decode_callback any number of times, until the audio_lead_time is
453:// satisfied.
454:// Returns TRUE if seeking succeeded or FALSE if no frame could be found.
455:
456:int plm_seek(plm_t *self, double time, int seek_exact);

467:// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
468:// plm_buffer public API
469:// Provides the data source for all other plm_* interfaces
470:
471:
472:// The default size for buffers created from files or by the high-level API
473:
474:#ifndef PLM_BUFFER_DEFAULT_SIZE
475:#define PLM_BUFFER_DEFAULT_SIZE (128 * 1024)
476:#endif
477:
478:#ifndef PLM_NO_STDIO
479:
480:// Create a buffer instance with a filename. Returns NULL if the file could not
481:// be opened.
482:
483:plm_buffer_t *plm_buffer_create_with_filename(const char *filename);
484:
485:
486:// Create a buffer instance with a file handle. Pass TRUE to close_when_done
487:// to let plmpeg call fclose() on the handle when plm_destroy() is called.
488:
489:plm_buffer_t *plm_buffer_create_with_file(FILE *fh, int close_when_done);
490:
491:#endif // PLM_NO_STDIO
492:
493:
494:// Create a buffer instance with custom callbacks for loading, seeking and
495:// telling the position. This behaves like a file handle, but with user-defined
496:// callbacks, useful for file handles that don't use the standard FILE API.
497:// Setting the length and closing/freeing has to be done manually.
498:
499:plm_buffer_t *plm_buffer_create_with_callbacks(
500:	plm_buffer_load_callback load_callback,
501:	plm_buffer_seek_callback seek_callback,
502:	plm_buffer_tell_callback tell_callback,
503:	size_t length,
504:	void *user
505:);
506:
507:
508:// Create a buffer instance with a pointer to memory as source. This assumes
509:// the whole file is in memory. The bytes are not copied. Pass 1 to 
510:// free_when_done to let plmpeg call free() on the pointer when plm_destroy() 
511:// is called.
512:
513:plm_buffer_t *plm_buffer_create_with_memory(uint8_t *bytes, size_t length, int free_when_done);
514:
515:
516:// Create an empty buffer with an initial capacity. The buffer will grow
517:// as needed. Data that has already been read, will be discarded.
518:
519:plm_buffer_t *plm_buffer_create_with_capacity(size_t capacity);
520:
521:
522:// Create an empty buffer with an initial capacity. The buffer will grow
523:// as needed. Decoded data will *not* be discarded. This can be used when
524:// loading a file over the network, without needing to throttle the download. 
525:// It also allows for seeking in the already loaded data.
526:
527:plm_buffer_t *plm_buffer_create_for_appending(size_t initial_capacity);
528:
529:
530:// Destroy a buffer instance and free all data
531:
532:void plm_buffer_destroy(plm_buffer_t *self);
533:
534:
535:// Copy data into the buffer. If the data to be written is larger than the 
536:// available space, the buffer will realloc() with a larger capacity. 
537:// Returns the number of bytes written. This will always be the same as the
538:// passed in length, except when the buffer was created _with_memory() for
539:// which _write() is forbidden.
540:
541:size_t plm_buffer_write(plm_buffer_t *self, uint8_t *bytes, size_t length);
542:
543:
544:// Mark the current byte length as the end of this buffer and signal that no 
545:// more data is expected to be written to it. This function should be called
546:// just after the last plm_buffer_write().
547:// For _with_capacity buffers, this is cleared on a plm_buffer_rewind().
548:
549:void plm_buffer_signal_end(plm_buffer_t *self);
550:
551:
552:// Set a callback that is called whenever the buffer needs more data
553:
554:void plm_buffer_set_load_callback(plm_buffer_t *self, plm_buffer_load_callback fp, void *user);
555:
556:
557:// Rewind the buffer back to the beginning. When loading from a file handle,
558:// this also seeks to the beginning of the file.
559:
560:void plm_buffer_rewind(plm_buffer_t *self);
561:
562:
563:// Get the total size. For files, this returns the file size. For all other 
564:// types it returns the number of bytes currently in the buffer.
565:
566:size_t plm_buffer_get_size(plm_buffer_t *self);
567:
568:
569:// Get the number of remaining (yet unread) bytes in the buffer. This can be
570:// useful to throttle writing.
571:
572:size_t plm_buffer_get_remaining(plm_buffer_t *self);
573:
574:
575:// Get whether the read position of the buffer is at the end and no more data 
576:// is expected.
577:
578:int plm_buffer_has_ended(plm_buffer_t *self);

592:static const int PLM_DEMUX_PACKET_AUDIO_3 = 0xC2;

740:// Convert the YCrCb data of a frame into interleaved R G B data. The stride
741:// specifies the width in bytes of the destination buffer. I.e. the number of

743:// (frame->width * bytes_per_pixel). The buffer pointed to by *dest must have a
