7087:static int stbi__hdr_test_core(stbi__context *s, const char *signature)
7088:{
7089:   int i;
7090:   for (i=0; signature[i]; ++i)
7091:      if (stbi__get8(s) != signature[i])
7092:          return 0;
7093:   stbi__rewind(s);
7094:   return 1;
7095:}
7096:
7097:static int stbi__hdr_test(stbi__context* s)
7098:{
7099:   int r = stbi__hdr_test_core(s, "#?RADIANCE\n");
7100:   stbi__rewind(s);
7101:   if(!r) {
7102:       r = stbi__hdr_test_core(s, "#?RGBE\n");
7103:       stbi__rewind(s);
7104:   }
7105:   return r;
7106:}
7107:
7108:#define STBI__HDR_BUFLEN  1024
7109:static char *stbi__hdr_gettoken(stbi__context *z, char *buffer)
7110:{
7111:   int len=0;
7112:   char c = '\0';
7113:
7114:   c = (char) stbi__get8(z);
7115:
7116:   while (!stbi__at_eof(z) && c != '\n') {
7117:      buffer[len++] = c;
7118:      if (len == STBI__HDR_BUFLEN-1) {
7119:         // flush to end of line
7120:         while (!stbi__at_eof(z) && stbi__get8(z) != '\n')
7121:            ;
7122:         break;
7123:      }
7124:      c = (char) stbi__get8(z);
7125:   }
7126:
7127:   buffer[len] = 0;
7128:   return buffer;
7129:}
7130:
7131:static void stbi__hdr_convert(float *output, stbi_uc *input, int req_comp)
7132:{
7133:   if ( input[3] != 0 ) {
7134:      float f1;
7135:      // Exponent
7136:      f1 = (float) ldexp(1.0f, input[3] - (int)(128 + 8));
7137:      if (req_comp <= 2)
7138:         output[0] = (input[0] + input[1] + input[2]) * f1 / 3;
7139:      else {
7140:         output[0] = input[0] * f1;
7141:         output[1] = input[1] * f1;
7142:         output[2] = input[2] * f1;
7143:      }
7144:      if (req_comp == 2) output[1] = 1;
7145:      if (req_comp == 4) output[3] = 1;
7146:   } else {
7147:      switch (req_comp) {
7148:         case 4: output[3] = 1; /* fallthrough */
7149:         case 3: output[0] = output[1] = output[2] = 0;
7150:                 break;
7151:         case 2: output[1] = 1; /* fallthrough */
7152:         case 1: output[0] = 0;
7153:                 break;
7154:      }
7155:   }
7156:}
7157:
7158:static float *stbi__hdr_load(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp, int req_comp, stbi__result_info *ri)
7159:{
7160:   char buffer[STBI__HDR_BUFLEN];
7161:   char *token;
7162:   int valid = 0;
7163:   int width, height;
7164:   stbi_uc *scanline;
7165:   float *hdr_data;
7166:   int len;
7167:   unsigned char count, value;
7168:   int i, j, k, c1,c2, z;
7169:   const char *headerToken;
7170:   STBI_NOTUSED(ri);
7171:
7172:   // Check identifier
7173:   headerToken = stbi__hdr_gettoken(s,buffer);
7174:   if (strcmp(headerToken, "#?RADIANCE") != 0 && strcmp(headerToken, "#?RGBE") != 0)
7175:      return stbi__errpf("not HDR", "Corrupt HDR image");
7176:
7177:   // Parse header
7178:   for(;;) {
7179:      token = stbi__hdr_gettoken(s,buffer);
7180:      if (token[0] == 0) break;
7181:      if (strcmp(token, "FORMAT=32-bit_rle_rgbe") == 0) valid = 1;
7182:   }
7183:
7184:   if (!valid)    return stbi__errpf("unsupported format", "Unsupported HDR format");
7185:
7186:   // Parse width and height
7187:   // can't use sscanf() if we're not using stdio!
7188:   token = stbi__hdr_gettoken(s,buffer);
7189:   if (strncmp(token, "-Y ", 3))  return stbi__errpf("unsupported data layout", "Unsupported HDR format");
7190:   token += 3;
7191:   height = (int) strtol(token, &token, 10);
7192:   while (*token == ' ') ++token;
7193:   if (strncmp(token, "+X ", 3))  return stbi__errpf("unsupported data layout", "Unsupported HDR format");
7194:   token += 3;
7195:   width = (int) strtol(token, NULL, 10);
7196:
7197:   if (height > STBI_MAX_DIMENSIONS) return stbi__errpf("too large","Very large image (corrupt?)");
7198:   if (width > STBI_MAX_DIMENSIONS) return stbi__errpf("too large","Very large image (corrupt?)");
7199:
7200:   *x = width;
7201:   *y = height;
7202:
7203:   if (comp) *comp = 3;
7204:   if (req_comp == 0) req_comp = 3;
7205:
7206:   if (!stbi__mad4sizes_valid(width, height, req_comp, sizeof(float), 0))
7207:      return stbi__errpf("too large", "HDR image is too large");
7208:
7209:   // Read data
7210:   hdr_data = (float *) stbi__malloc_mad4(width, height, req_comp, sizeof(float), 0);
7211:   if (!hdr_data)
7212:      return stbi__errpf("outofmem", "Out of memory");
7213:
7214:   // Load image data
7215:   // image data is stored as some number of sca
7216:   if ( width < 8 || width >= 32768) {
7217:      // Read flat data
7218:      for (j=0; j < height; ++j) {
7219:         for (i=0; i < width; ++i) {
7220:            stbi_uc rgbe[4];
7221:           main_decode_loop:
7222:            stbi__getn(s, rgbe, 4);
7223:            stbi__hdr_convert(hdr_data + j * width * req_comp + i * req_comp, rgbe, req_comp);
7224:         }
7225:      }
7226:   } else {
7227:      // Read RLE-encoded data
7228:      scanline = NULL;
7229:
7230:      for (j = 0; j < height; ++j) {
7231:         c1 = stbi__get8(s);
7232:         c2 = stbi__get8(s);
7233:         len = stbi__get8(s);
7234:         if (c1 != 2 || c2 != 2 || (len & 0x80)) {
7235:            // not run-length encoded, so we have to actually use THIS data as a decoded
7236:            // pixel (note this can't be a valid pixel--one of RGB must be >= 128)
7237:            stbi_uc rgbe[4];
7238:            rgbe[0] = (stbi_uc) c1;
7239:            rgbe[1] = (stbi_uc) c2;
7240:            rgbe[2] = (stbi_uc) len;
7241:            rgbe[3] = (stbi_uc) stbi__get8(s);
7242:            stbi__hdr_convert(hdr_data, rgbe, req_comp);
7243:            i = 1;
7244:            j = 0;
7245:            STBI_FREE(scanline);
7246:            goto main_decode_loop; // yes, this makes no sense
7247:         }
7248:         len <<= 8;
7249:         len |= stbi__get8(s);
7250:         if (len != width) { STBI_FREE(hdr_data); STBI_FREE(scanline); return stbi__errpf("invalid decoded scanline length", "corrupt HDR"); }
7251:         if (scanline == NULL) {
7252:            scanline = (stbi_uc *) stbi__malloc_mad2(width, 4, 0);
7253:            if (!scanline) {
7254:               STBI_FREE(hdr_data);
7255:               return stbi__errpf("outofmem", "Out of memory");
7256:            }
7257:         }
7258:
7259:         for (k = 0; k < 4; ++k) {
7260:            int nleft;
7261:            i = 0;
7262:            while ((nleft = width - i) > 0) {
7263:               count = stbi__get8(s);
7264:               if (count > 128) {
7265:                  // Run
7266:                  value = stbi__get8(s);
7267:                  count -= 128;
7268:                  if ((count == 0) || (count > nleft)) { STBI_FREE(hdr_data); STBI_FREE(scanline); return stbi__errpf("corrupt", "bad RLE data in HDR"); }
7269:                  for (z = 0; z < count; ++z)
7270:                     scanline[i++ * 4 + k] = value;
7271:               } else {
7272:                  // Dump
7273:                  if ((count == 0) || (count > nleft)) { STBI_FREE(hdr_data); STBI_FREE(scanline); return stbi__errpf("corrupt", "bad RLE data in HDR"); }
7274:                  for (z = 0; z < count; ++z)
7275:                     scanline[i++ * 4 + k] = stbi__get8(s);
7276:               }
7277:            }
7278:         }
7279:         for (i=0; i < width; ++i)
7280:            stbi__hdr_convert(hdr_data+(j*width + i)*req_comp, scanline + i*4, req_comp);
7281:      }
7282:      if (scanline)
7283:         STBI_FREE(scanline);
7284:   }
7285:
7286:   return hdr_data;
7287:}

7289:static int stbi__hdr_info(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp)
7290:{
7291:   char buffer[STBI__HDR_BUFLEN];
7292:   char *token;
7293:   int valid = 0;
7294:   int dummy;
7295:
7296:   if (!x) x = &dummy;
7297:   if (!y) y = &dummy;
7298:   if (!comp) comp = &dummy;
7299:
7300:   if (stbi__hdr_test(s) == 0) {
7301:       stbi__rewind( s );
7302:       return 0;
7303:   }
7304:
7305:   for(;;) {
7306:      token = stbi__hdr_gettoken(s,buffer);
7307:      if (token[0] == 0) break;
7308:      if (strcmp(token, "FORMAT=32-bit_rle_rgbe") == 0) valid = 1;
7309:   }
7310:
7311:   if (!valid) {
7312:       stbi__rewind( s );
7313:       return 0;
7314:   }
7315:   token = stbi__hdr_gettoken(s,buffer);
7316:   if (strncmp(token, "-Y ", 3)) {
7317:       stbi__rewind( s );
7318:       return 0;
7319:   }
7320:   token += 3;
7321:   *y = (int) strtol(token, &token, 10);
7322:   while (*token == ' ') ++token;
7323:   if (strncmp(token, "+X ", 3)) {
7324:       stbi__rewind( s );
7325:       return 0;
7326:   }
7327:   token += 3;
7328:   *x = (int) strtol(token, NULL, 10);
7329:   *comp = 3;
7330:   return 1;
7331:}
7332:#endif // STBI_NO_HDR

7335:static int stbi__bmp_info(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp)
7336:{
7337:   void *p;
7338:   stbi__bmp_data info;
7339:
7340:   info.all_a = 255;
7341:   p = stbi__bmp_parse_header(s, &info);
7342:   if (p == NULL) {
7343:      stbi__rewind( s );
7344:      return 0;
7345:   }
7346:   if (x) *x = s->img_x;
7347:   if (y) *y = s->img_y;
7348:   if (comp) {
7349:      if (info.bpp == 24 && info.ma == 0xff000000)
7350:         *comp = 3;
7351:      else
7352:         *comp = info.ma ? 4 : 3;
7353:   }
7354:   return 1;
7355:}
7356:#endif
7357:
7358:#ifndef STBI_NO_PSD
7359:static int stbi__psd_info(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp)
7360:{
7361:   int channelCount, dummy, depth;
7362:   if (!x) x = &dummy;
7363:   if (!y) y = &dummy;
7364:   if (!comp) comp = &dummy;
7365:   if (stbi__get32be(s) != 0x38425053) {
7366:       stbi__rewind( s );
7367:       return 0;
7368:   }
7369:   if (stbi__get16be(s) != 1) {
7370:       stbi__rewind( s );
7371:       return 0;
7372:   }
7373:   stbi__skip(s, 6);
7374:   channelCount = stbi__get16be(s);
7375:   if (channelCount < 0 || channelCount > 16) {
7376:       stbi__rewind( s );
7377:       return 0;
7378:   }
7379:   *y = stbi__get32be(s);
7380:   *x = stbi__get32be(s);
7381:   depth = stbi__get16be(s);
7382:   if (depth != 8 && depth != 16) {
7383:       stbi__rewind( s );
7384:       return 0;
7385:   }
7386:   if (stbi__get16be(s) != 3) {
7387:       stbi__rewind( s );
7388:       return 0;
7389:   }
7390:   *comp = 4;
7391:   return 1;
7392:}
7393:
7394:static int stbi__psd_is16(stbi__context *s)
7395:{
7396:   int channelCount, depth;
7397:   if (stbi__get32be(s) != 0x38425053) {
7398:       stbi__rewind( s );
7399:       return 0;
7400:   }
7401:   if (stbi__get16be(s) != 1) {
7402:       stbi__rewind( s );
7403:       return 0;
7404:   }
7405:   stbi__skip(s, 6);
7406:   channelCount = stbi__get16be(s);
7407:   if (channelCount < 0 || channelCount > 16) {
7408:       stbi__rewind( s );
7409:       return 0;
7410:   }
7411:   STBI_NOTUSED(stbi__get32be(s));
7412:   STBI_NOTUSED(stbi__get32be(s));
7413:   depth = stbi__get16be(s);
7414:   if (depth != 16) {
7415:       stbi__rewind( s );
7416:       return 0;
7417:   }
7418:   return 1;
7419:}
7420:#endif
7421:
7422:#ifndef STBI_NO_PIC
7423:static int stbi__pic_info(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp)
7424:{
7425:   int act_comp=0,num_packets=0,chained,dummy;
7426:   stbi__pic_packet packets[10];
7427:
7428:   if (!x) x = &dummy;
7429:   if (!y) y = &dummy;
7430:   if (!comp) comp = &dummy;
7431:
7432:   if (!stbi__pic_is4(s,"\x53\x80\xF6\x34")) {
7433:      stbi__rewind(s);
7434:      return 0;
7435:   }
7436:
7437:   stbi__skip(s, 88);
7438:
7439:   *x = stbi__get16be(s);
7440:   *y = stbi__get16be(s);
7441:   if (stbi__at_eof(s)) {
7442:      stbi__rewind( s);
7443:      return 0;
7444:   }
7445:   if ( (*x) != 0 && (1 << 28) / (*x) < (*y)) {
7446:      stbi__rewind( s );
7447:      return 0;
7448:   }
7449:
7450:   stbi__skip(s, 8);
7451:
7452:   do {
7453:      stbi__pic_packet *packet;
7454:
7455:      if (num_packets==sizeof(packets)/sizeof(packets[0]))
7456:         return 0;
7457:
7458:      packet = &packets[num_packets++];
7459:      chained = stbi__get8(s);
7460:      packet->size    = stbi__get8(s);
7461:      packet->type    = stbi__get8(s);
7462:      packet->channel = stbi__get8(s);
7463:      act_comp |= packet->channel;
7464:
7465:      if (stbi__at_eof(s)) {
7466:          stbi__rewind( s );
7467:          return 0;
7468:      }
7469:      if (packet->size != 8) {
7470:          stbi__rewind( s );
7471:          return 0;
7472:      }
7473:   } while (chained);
7474:
7475:   *comp = (act_comp & 0x10 ? 4 : 3);
7476:
7477:   return 1;
7478:}
7479:#endif

7481:// *************************************************************************************************
7482:// Portable Gray Map and Portable Pixel Map loader
7483:// by Ken Miller
7484://
7485:// PGM: http://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/pgm.html
7486:// PPM: http://netpbm.sourceforge.net/doc/ppm.html
7487://

7489://    Does not support comments in the header section
7490://    Does not support ASCII image data (formats P2 and P3)

7494:static int      stbi__pnm_test(stbi__context *s)
7495:{
7496:   char p, t;
7497:   p = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7498:   t = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7499:   if (p != 'P' || (t != '5' && t != '6')) {
7500:       stbi__rewind( s );
7501:       return 0;
7502:   }
7503:   return 1;
7504:}
7505:
7506:static void *stbi__pnm_load(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp, int req_comp, stbi__result_info *ri)
7507:{
7508:   stbi_uc *out;
7509:   STBI_NOTUSED(ri);
7510:
7511:   ri->bits_per_channel = stbi__pnm_info(s, (int *)&s->img_x, (int *)&s->img_y, (int *)&s->img_n);
7512:   if (ri->bits_per_channel == 0)
7513:      return 0;
7514:
7515:   if (s->img_y > STBI_MAX_DIMENSIONS) return stbi__errpuc("too large","Very large image (corrupt?)");
7516:   if (s->img_x > STBI_MAX_DIMENSIONS) return stbi__errpuc("too large","Very large image (corrupt?)");
7517:
7518:   *x = s->img_x;
7519:   *y = s->img_y;
7520:   if (comp) *comp = s->img_n;
7521:
7522:   if (!stbi__mad4sizes_valid(s->img_n, s->img_x, s->img_y, ri->bits_per_channel / 8, 0))
7523:      return stbi__errpuc("too large", "PNM too large");
7524:
7525:   out = (stbi_uc *) stbi__malloc_mad4(s->img_n, s->img_x, s->img_y, ri->bits_per_channel / 8, 0);
7526:   if (!out) return stbi__errpuc("outofmem", "Out of memory");
7527:   if (!stbi__getn(s, out, s->img_n * s->img_x * s->img_y * (ri->bits_per_channel / 8))) {
7528:      STBI_FREE(out);
7529:      return stbi__errpuc("bad PNM", "PNM file truncated");
7530:   }
7531:
7532:   if (req_comp && req_comp != s->img_n) {
7533:      if (ri->bits_per_channel == 16) {
7534:         out = (stbi_uc *) stbi__convert_format16((stbi__uint16 *) out, s->img_n, req_comp, s->img_x, s->img_y);
7535:      } else {
7536:         out = stbi__convert_format(out, s->img_n, req_comp, s->img_x, s->img_y);
7537:      }
7538:      if (out == NULL) return out; // stbi__convert_format frees input on failure
7539:   }
7540:   return out;
7541:}
7542:
7543:static int      stbi__pnm_isspace(char c)
7544:{
7545:   return c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\n' || c == '\v' || c == '\f' || c == '\r';
7546:}
7547:
7548:static void     stbi__pnm_skip_whitespace(stbi__context *s, char *c)
7549:{
7550:   for (;;) {
7551:      while (!stbi__at_eof(s) && stbi__pnm_isspace(*c))
7552:         *c = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7553:
7554:      if (stbi__at_eof(s) || *c != '#')
7555:         break;
7556:
7557:      while (!stbi__at_eof(s) && *c != '\n' && *c != '\r' )
7558:         *c = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7559:   }
7560:}
7561:
7562:static int      stbi__pnm_isdigit(char c)
7563:{
7564:   return c >= '0' && c <= '9';
7565:}
7566:
7567:static int      stbi__pnm_getinteger(stbi__context *s, char *c)
7568:{
7569:   int value = 0;
7570:
7571:   while (!stbi__at_eof(s) && stbi__pnm_isdigit(*c)) {
7572:      value = value*10 + (*c - '0');
7573:      *c = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7574:      if((value > 214748364) || (value == 214748364 && *c > '7'))
7575:          return stbi__err("integer parse overflow", "Parsing an integer in the PPM header overflowed a 32-bit int");
7576:   }
7577:
7578:   return value;
7579:}
7580:
7581:static int      stbi__pnm_info(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp)
7582:{
7583:   int maxv, dummy;
7584:   char c, p, t;
7585:
7586:   if (!x) x = &dummy;
7587:   if (!y) y = &dummy;
7588:   if (!comp) comp = &dummy;
7589:
7590:   stbi__rewind(s);
7591:
7592:   // Get identifier
7593:   p = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7594:   t = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7595:   if (p != 'P' || (t != '5' && t != '6')) {
7596:       stbi__rewind(s);
7597:       return 0;
7598:   }
7599:
7600:   *comp = (t == '6') ? 3 : 1;  // '5' is 1-component .pgm; '6' is 3-component .ppm
7601:
7602:   c = (char) stbi__get8(s);
7603:   stbi__pnm_skip_whitespace(s, &c);
7604:
7605:   *x = stbi__pnm_getinteger(s, &c); // read width
7606:   if(*x == 0)
7607:       return stbi__err("invalid width", "PPM image header had zero or overflowing width");
7608:   stbi__pnm_skip_whitespace(s, &c);
7609:
7610:   *y = stbi__pnm_getinteger(s, &c); // read height
7611:   if (*y == 0)
7612:       return stbi__err("invalid width", "PPM image header had zero or overflowing width");
7613:   stbi__pnm_skip_whitespace(s, &c);
7614:
7615:   maxv = stbi__pnm_getinteger(s, &c);  // read max value
7616:   if (maxv > 65535)
7617:      return stbi__err("max value > 65535", "PPM image supports only 8-bit and 16-bit images");
7618:   else if (maxv > 255)
7619:      return 16;
7620:   else
7621:      return 8;
7622:}
7623:
7624:static int stbi__pnm_is16(stbi__context *s)
7625:{
7626:   if (stbi__pnm_info(s, NULL, NULL, NULL) == 16)
7627:	   return 1;
7628:   return 0;
7629:}
7630:#endif

7632:static int stbi__info_main(stbi__context *s, int *x, int *y, int *comp)
7633:{
7634:   #ifndef STBI_NO_JPEG
7635:   if (stbi__jpeg_info(s, x, y, comp)) return 1;
7636:   #endif
7637:
7638:   #ifndef STBI_NO_PNG
7639:   if (stbi__png_info(s, x, y, comp))  return 1;
7640:   #endif
7641:
7642:   #ifndef STBI_NO_GIF
7643:   if (stbi__gif_info(s, x, y, comp))  return 1;
7644:   #endif
7645:
7646:   #ifndef STBI_NO_BMP
7647:   if (stbi__bmp_info(s, x, y, comp))  return 1;
7648:   #endif
7649:
7650:   #ifndef STBI_NO_PSD
7651:   if (stbi__psd_info(s, x, y, comp))  return 1;
7652:   #endif
7653:
7654:   #ifndef STBI_NO_PIC
7655:   if (stbi__pic_info(s, x, y, comp))  return 1;
7656:   #endif
7657:
7658:   #ifndef STBI_NO_PNM
7659:   if (stbi__pnm_info(s, x, y, comp))  return 1;
7660:   #endif
7661:
7662:   #ifndef STBI_NO_HDR
7663:   if (stbi__hdr_info(s, x, y, comp))  return 1;
7664:   #endif
7665:
7666:   // test tga last because it's a crappy test!
7667:   #ifndef STBI_NO_TGA
7668:   if (stbi__tga_info(s, x, y, comp))
7669:       return 1;
7670:   #endif
7671:   return stbi__err("unknown image type", "Image not of any known type, or corrupt");
7672:}

7674:static int stbi__is_16_main(stbi__context *s)
7675:{

7677:   if (stbi__png_is16(s))  return 1;
7678:   #endif
7679:
7680:   #ifndef STBI_NO_PSD
7681:   if (stbi__psd_is16(s))  return 1;
7682:   #endif
7683:
7684:   #ifndef STBI_NO_PNM
7685:   if (stbi__pnm_is16(s))  return 1;
7686:   #endif
7687:   return 0;
7688:}

7692:{
7693:    FILE *f = stbi__fopen(filename, "rb");
7694:    int result;
7695:    if (!f) return stbi__err("can't fopen", "Unable to open file");
7696:    result = stbi_info_from_file(f, x, y, comp);
7697:    fclose(f);
7698:    return result;
7699:}

7707:   r = stbi__info_main(&s,x,y,comp);
7708:   fseek(f,pos,SEEK_SET);
7709:   return r;
7710:}

@@@ include/api/stdbit.h @@@
1:/*
2: * include/api/stdbit.h
3: * C23 standard bit manipulation macros for NexsOS1.
4: */
5:
6:#ifndef _STDBIT_H
7:#define _STDBIT_H
8:
9:#include <limits.h>
10:
11:#ifndef ULLONG_WIDTH
12:#define ULLONG_WIDTH 64
13:#endif
14:
15:#ifndef UINT_WIDTH
16:#define UINT_WIDTH 32
17:#endif
18:
19:#define stdc_leading_zeros_ull(x) ((x) == 0 ? 64 : __builtin_clzll(x))
20:#define stdc_leading_zeros_ui(x)  ((x) == 0 ? 32 : __builtin_clz(x))
21:#define stdc_leading_zeros_ul(x)  ((x) == 0 ? (sizeof(unsigned long) * 8) : __builtin_clzl(x))
22:#define stdc_leading_zeros_us(x)  ((x) == 0 ? 16 : __builtin_clz((unsigned int)(x)) - (sizeof(unsigned int) * 8 - 16))
23:#define stdc_leading_zeros_uc(x)  ((x) == 0 ? 8 : __builtin_clz((unsigned int)(x)) - (sizeof(unsigned int) * 8 - 8))
24:#define stdc_leading_zeros(n)     ((sizeof(n) == 1) ? stdc_leading_zeros_uc((unsigned char)(n)) : \
25:                                  (sizeof(n) == sizeof(unsigned short)) ? stdc_leading_zeros_us((unsigned short)(n)) : \
26:                                  (sizeof(n) == sizeof(unsigned int)) ? stdc_leading_zeros_ui((unsigned int)(n)) : \
27:                                  (sizeof(n) == sizeof(unsigned long)) ? stdc_leading_zeros_ul((unsigned long)(n)) : \
28:                                  stdc_leading_zeros_ull((unsigned long long)(n)))
29:#define stdc_trailing_zeros_ull(x) ((x) == 0 ? 64 : __builtin_ctzll(x))
30:#define stdc_trailing_zeros_ui(x)  ((x) == 0 ? 32 : __builtin_ctz(x))
31:#define stdc_trailing_zeros_ul(x)  ((x) == 0 ? (sizeof(unsigned long) * 8) : __builtin_ctzl(x))
32:#define stdc_trailing_zeros_us(x)  ((x) == 0 ? 16 : __builtin_ctz((unsigned int)(x)))
33:#define stdc_trailing_zeros_uc(x)  ((x) == 0 ? 8 : __builtin_ctz((unsigned int)(x)))
34:#define stdc_trailing_zeros(n)     ((sizeof(n) == 1) ? stdc_trailing_zeros_uc((unsigned char)(n)) : \
35:                                  (sizeof(n) == sizeof(unsigned short)) ? stdc_trailing_zeros_us((unsigned short)(n)) : \
36:                                  (sizeof(n) == sizeof(unsigned int)) ? stdc_trailing_zeros_ui((unsigned int)(n)) : \
37:                                  (sizeof(n) == sizeof(unsigned long)) ? stdc_trailing_zeros_ul((unsigned long)(n)) : \
38:                                  stdc_trailing_zeros_ull((unsigned long long)(n)))
39:#define stdc_count_ones_ull(x)     __builtin_popcountll(x)
40:#define stdc_count_ones_ui(x)      __builtin_popcount(x)
41:#define stdc_bit_width_ull(x)      ((x) == 0 ? 0 : 64 - stdc_leading_zeros_ull(x))
42:#define stdc_bit_width_ui(x)       ((x) == 0 ? 0 : 32 - stdc_leading_zeros_ui(x))
43:#define stdc_bit_width_ul(x)       ((x) == 0 ? 0 : (sizeof(unsigned long) * 8) - stdc_leading_zeros_ul(x))
44:#define stdc_bit_width(x)          ((sizeof(x) == sizeof(unsigned int)) ? stdc_bit_width_ui((unsigned int)(x)) : \
45:                                   (sizeof(x) == sizeof(unsigned long)) ? stdc_bit_width_ul((unsigned long)(x)) : \
46:                                   stdc_bit_width_ull((unsigned long long)(x)))
47:
48:static inline unsigned long long stdc_rotate_right_ull(unsigned long long x, unsigned int n) {
49:    n &= 63;
50:    return n == 0 ? x : (x >> n) | (x << (64 - n));
51:}
52:
53:static inline unsigned long long stdc_rotate_left_ull(unsigned long long x, unsigned int n) {
54:    n &= 63;
55:    return n == 0 ? x : (x << n) | (x >> (64 - n));
56:}
57:
58:#define stdc_rotate_right(x, n) stdc_rotate_right_ull((unsigned long long)(x), (n))
59:#define stdc_rotate_left(x, n)  stdc_rotate_left_ull((unsigned long long)(x), (n))
60:
61:#endif /* _STDBIT_H */

@@@ include/api/stdio.h @@@
1:#ifndef _STDIO_H

7:/* FILE_WBUF_SIZE: userland write-buffer capacity for positional (path-backed)
8: * streams.  Sized to the ext4 block so buffered flushes land block-aligned and
9: * a per-byte fwrite loop (e.g. a savegame written field-by-field) coalesces
10: * into one syscall per 4 KiB instead of one per call. */
11:#define FILE_WBUF_SIZE 4096
12:#define FILE_RBUF_SIZE 4096
13:
14:typedef struct {
15:    int fd;
16:    int pos;
17:    int size;
18:    int error;
19:    int eof;
20:    char path[128];
21:    int ungetc_buf;
22:    int has_ungetc;
23:    int is_tmp;
24:    /* Write buffer for positional streams (fd < 0).  'wcount' bytes are pending;
25:     * their on-disk offset is (pos - wcount).  Empty (wcount == 0) for read
26:     * streams and the console std streams, which stay unbuffered. */
27:    int wcount;
28:    char wbuf[FILE_WBUF_SIZE];
29:    /* READ buffer, symmetric with the write one and for the same reason: the
30:     * filesystem reads a whole 4 KiB block for any partial read, so an
31:     * unbuffered byte-at-a-time reader re-reads the same block once per byte.
32:     * rhead is the consumed offset inside rbuf, rcount the valid bytes; rbase
33:     * is the file offset rbuf[0] came from, so a seek can tell whether the
34:     * cached window still covers the new position. */
35:    int rcount;
36:    int rhead;
37:    int rbase;
38:    char rbuf[FILE_RBUF_SIZE];
39:} FILE;
40:

42:extern FILE _stdout_struct;
43:extern FILE _stderr_struct;
44:

81:/* NX_PRINTFLIKE - tell the compiler these take a printf format string, so
82: * -Wformat (already on via -Wall -Werror) actually CHECKS the arguments.
83: *
84: * Without this the checking is silently absent: a `%s` fed an int compiles
85: * clean and then dereferences that integer as a pointer at runtime.  That
86: * exact bug crashed the dock on every frame, and because init has no respawn
87: * rate limiting it became a boot-killing loop and finally a kernel panic — from
88: * a mismatch the compiler was fully capable of catching. */
89:#define NX_PRINTFLIKE(fmt_idx, first_arg)                                      \
90:  __attribute__((format(printf, fmt_idx, first_arg)))
91:
92:int printf(const char *format, ...) NX_PRINTFLIKE(1, 2);
93:int sprintf(char *str, const char *format, ...) NX_PRINTFLIKE(2, 3);
94:int snprintf(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, ...)
95:    NX_PRINTFLIKE(3, 4);
96:int asprintf(char **strp, const char *format, ...)
97:    NX_PRINTFLIKE(2, 3);
98:int vasprintf(char **strp, const char *format, va_list ap);

100:int vsnprintf(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, va_list ap);

102:int vfprintf(FILE *stream, const char *format, va_list ap);
103:int vprintf(const char *format, va_list ap);

@@@ include/api/termios.h @@@
1:#ifndef _TERMIOS_H
2:#define _TERMIOS_H
3:
4:/*
5: * Minimal POSIX <termios.h> for the OS1 userspace libc.
6: *
7: * OS1 has no line discipline: a window already delivers input character by
8: * character through read()/input_poll_event (see the kilo port). tcgetattr /
9: * tcsetattr (lib.c) are therefore safe no-ops that succeed, so raw-mode code
10: * ported from POSIX (base-nexs, linenoise-style editors) compiles and runs
11: * unchanged. Implemented in the libc layer, NOT as an OS1 syscall.
12: */
13:
14:typedef unsigned long tcflag_t;
15:typedef unsigned char cc_t;

@@@ include/api/time.h @@@
1:#ifndef _TIME_H
2:#define _TIME_H
3:
4:/*
5: * include/api/time.h
6: * POSIX-like time layer built ON TOP of the os1.h base primitives
7: * (os1_mono_ns / os1_cpu_ns). os1.h is NEXS's proprietary base API; this header
8: * is the start of the real POSIX/libc surface that sits above it. See
9: * docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4.
10: */
11:
12:#include <stddef.h>
13:
14:typedef long time_t;
15:
16:struct tm_zone {
17:  struct tm_zone *next;
18:  char tz_is_set;
19:  char abbrs[];
20:};
21:
22:typedef struct tm_zone *timezone_t;
23:
24:timezone_t tzalloc(const char *name);
25:void tzfree(timezone_t tz);
26:
27:typedef int clockid_t;
28:
29:struct timespec {
30:  time_t tv_sec; /* seconds */
31:  long tv_nsec;  /* nanoseconds [0, 999999999] */
32:};
33:
34:struct tm {
35:  int tm_sec;   /* seconds after the minute [0, 60] */
36:  int tm_min;   /* minutes after the hour [0, 59] */
37:  int tm_hour;  /* hours since midnight [0, 23] */
38:  int tm_mday;  /* day of the month [1, 31] */
39:  int tm_mon;   /* months since January [0, 11] */
40:  int tm_year;  /* years since 1900 */
41:  int tm_wday;  /* days since Sunday [0, 6] */
42:  int tm_yday;  /* days since January 1 [0, 365] */
43:  int tm_isdst; /* Daylight Saving Time flag */
44:};
45:
46:/* Clock ids. Mapped onto the two kernel clocks (monotonic / process CPU).
47: * REALTIME currently aliases MONOTONIC — there is no wall-clock RTC yet. */
48:#define CLOCK_REALTIME 0
49:#define CLOCK_MONOTONIC 0
50:#define CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID 1
51:
52:/* clock_gettime: fill *ts with the current value of clk. Returns 0 on success,
53: * -1 if ts is NULL. Backed by os1_mono_ns() / os1_cpu_ns(). */
54:int clock_gettime(clockid_t clk, struct timespec *ts);
55:
56:/* nanosleep: POSIX blocking sleep for req->tv_sec + req->tv_nsec, on top of the
57: * SYS_NANOSLEEP primitive (the caller is descheduled, no busy-wait). Sleeps are
58: * not interruptible here, so they always run to completion: *rem (if non-NULL)
59: * is zeroed and 0 is returned. -1 on a NULL/invalid req. The kernel rounds the
60: * deadline up to the tick (~10 ms at HZ=100) but tracks it in real wall time.
61: */
62:int nanosleep(const struct timespec *req, struct timespec *rem);
63:
64:/* time: return seconds since epoch, or set *t if non-NULL. */
65:time_t time(time_t *t);
66:
67:/* mktime: convert struct tm to time_t. */
68:time_t mktime(struct tm *tm);
69:
70:/* difftime: difference between two time_t values in seconds. */
71:double difftime(time_t time1, time_t time0);
72:
73:/* localtime/gmtime: convert time_t to struct tm. */
74:struct tm *localtime(const time_t *timep);
75:struct tm *gmtime(const time_t *timep);
76:
77:/* mktime_z / localtime_rz: timezone-aware conversions (NexsOS1 stubs).
78: * NexsOS1 does not support timezones; these delegate to standard functions. */
79:time_t mktime_z(timezone_t tz, struct tm *tm);
80:struct tm *localtime_rz(timezone_t tz, const time_t *t, struct tm *tm);
81:
82:/* strftime: format time into string. */
83:size_t strftime(char *s, size_t max, const char *format, const struct tm *tm);
84:
85:/* clock: return processor time used by the program (in CLOCKS_PER_SEC units).
86: */
87:typedef long clock_t;
88:#ifndef CLOCKS_PER_SEC
89:#define CLOCKS_PER_SEC 1000000000L
90:#endif
91:clock_t clock(void);
92:
93:#endif /* _TIME_H */

@@@ include/api/unistd.h @@@
1:/*
2: * include/api/unistd.h
3: * The POSIX <unistd.h> PERSONALITY over the OS1 base API (ASTRA layering).
4: *
5: * Layering contract (docs/ASTRA.md, PLAN-2026-07-17 stratification):
6: *   - `OS1_*` / `OS1low_*` (os1.h) are the NEXS base API — the single
7: *     implementation of every primitive.
8: *   - the POSIX names here are a THIN COMPATIBILITY MAPPING onto them, so
9: *     ported software can `#include <unistd.h>` and get the standard surface
10: *     while NEXS-native code keeps calling the OS1 verbs directly.  Both are
11: *     available; neither re-implements the other (no duplicated logic).
12: *
13: * This header is the authoritative POSIX entry point: including it gives the
14: * COMPLETE set below.  Some names are declared in os1.h (which this includes)
15: * because they predate the split — they are listed here so the POSIX surface is
16: * documented in one place, but are deliberately NOT re-declared, so there is
17: * exactly one declaration of each and the two headers cannot drift.
18: *
19: * POSIX name        OS1 primitive it maps to            declared in
20: * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
21: * read()            OS1_object_read / SYS_READ          os1.h
22: * write()           OS1_object_write / SYS_WRITE        os1.h
23: * close()           OS1low_handle_close                 os1.h
24: * lseek()           OBJ_CTL_SEEK on the handle          os1.h
25: * chdir()           OS1_fs_chdir                        os1.h
26: * getcwd()          OS1_fs_getcwd                       os1.h
27: * sbrk()            OS1low_vm_sbrk                      os1.h
28: * pipe()            OS1low_pipe (SYS_PIPE, OBJ_TYPE_PIPE)   here
29: * unlink()          OS1_fs_unlink (parent DIR capability)   here
30: * truncate()        OS1_fs_read/OS1_fs_write (whole-file)   here
31: * ftruncate()       lseek/read/write + OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE     here
32: * isatty()          OS1low_cap_query (type == CONSOLE)      here
33: * getpid()          get_pid / OS1low_process_self           here
34: * usleep()          SYS_NANOSLEEP (real timer sleep)        here
35: *
36: * KNOWN DEVIATIONS from strict POSIX (intentional, documented rather than
37: * silently wrong):
38: *   - read()/write() take `char *` / `const char *`, not `void *`, and return
39: *     `long` rather than `ssize_t`.
40: *   - getcwd() returns int (0 on success), NOT `char *`.
41: *   - sleep(unsigned seconds) is NOT declared: os1.h's OS1_sleep() takes
42: *     MILLISECONDS, and declaring a POSIX sleep() here would silently change
43: *     the unit for existing callers.  Use usleep()/nanosleep() or OS1_sleep().
44: */
45:#ifndef _UNISTD_H
46:#define _UNISTD_H
47:
48:#include <os1.h>
49:
50:/* Standard file descriptors. */
51:#define STDIN_FILENO  0
52:#define STDOUT_FILENO 1
53:#define STDERR_FILENO 2
54:
55:/* usleep(usec): microseconds, POSIX-compatible, backed by the real kernel timer
56: * (SYS_NANOSLEEP) — the caller is descheduled and woken by its core's tick, no
57: * busy-wait.  The primitive is nanosleep-granular (rounded up to the tick,
58: * ~10 ms at HZ=100).  For ns/timespec sleeps and the monotonic clock use
59: * <time.h> (nanosleep(), clock_gettime()). */
60:int usleep(unsigned int usec);
61:
62:/* pipe: a real anonymous byte pipe (OBJ_TYPE_PIPE via SYS_PIPE).  pipefd[0] is
63: * the READ end, pipefd[1] the WRITE end; both are ordinary descriptors, so
64: * read()/write()/close() work on them and the shell can hand either end to a
65: * child as its stdin/stdout.  Returns 0, or -1 with errno set. */
66:int pipe(int pipefd[2]);
67:
68:/* unlink: parent-directory capability mutation via OS1_fs_unlink(), same as
69: * remove(). */
70:int unlink(const char *pathname);
71:int link(const char *oldpath, const char *newpath);
72:
73:/* isatty: true iff the descriptor's underlying object is a CONSOLE.  This is a
74: * real capability-type test (OS1low_cap_query), NOT "fd < 3" — with shell
75: * redirection fd 1 may be a FILE (`cmd > out`) or a PIPE (`cmd | cmd`), and
76: * interactive programs (the lua REPL) must correctly see isatty()==0 there. */
77:int isatty(int fd);
78:
79:/* getpid: POSIX name for the OS1 get_pid(). */
80:int getpid(void);
81:
82:/* truncate/ftruncate: set a file's length exactly.  Built on the FS-layer
83: * whole-file-replace primitive (an offset-0 write REPLACES the file — the
84: * Phase 1 truncation standard); ftruncate reaches the same effect through an
85: * open descriptor, using OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE for the truncate-to-empty case that a
86: * zero-length write cannot express (POSIX write(fd,...,0) is a no-op). */
87:int truncate(const char *path, long length);
88:int ftruncate(int fd, long length);
89:int fchdir(int fd);
90:unsigned int sleep(unsigned int seconds);
91:int getpagesize(void);
92:pid_t fork(void);

68:/* LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE is a physical address; registers are accessed at its
69: * direct-map kernel VA (phys_to_virt — identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE==0). */
70:static inline uint32_t lapic_read(uint32_t reg) {
71:    return *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE + reg);
72:}
73:
74:static inline void lapic_write(uint32_t reg, uint32_t val) {
75:    *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE + reg) = val;
76:}

86:/* tsc_calibrate: measure the TSC frequency against the PIT and publish it into
87: * tsc_hz (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §1).  Called once on the BSP from
88: * lapic_timer_calibrate(); idempotent.  tsc_hz is read by
89: * arch_impl_timer_get_freq() (arch/arch.h) to feed the arch-neutral mono_ns(). */
90:void tsc_calibrate(void);

@@@ kernel/include/drivers/gpu/gpu.h @@@
1:#ifndef _DRIVERS_GPU_H
2:#define _DRIVERS_GPU_H
3:
4:#include <stddef.h>
5:#include <stdint.h>
6:
7:struct gpu_device;
8:
9:struct gpu_ops {
10:  int (*init)(struct gpu_device *dev);
11:  /* Reconfigure the scanout to width x height at runtime.  Recreates the host
12:   * resource + backing and re-points the scanout; updates dev->width/height
13:   * and the framebuffer pointer.  0 on success.  (GFX-DYN-01 #49) */
14:  int (*set_mode)(struct gpu_device *dev, int width, int height);
15:  void *(*get_framebuffer)(struct gpu_device *dev, size_t *size);
16:  int (*flush)(struct gpu_device *dev, int x, int y, int w, int h);
17:  /* Atomically copy a region of a caller-owned ARGB8888 source (src_w x src_h,
18:   * stride == src_w) into the scanout backing AND transfer+flush it to the
19:   * host, all under the driver's own lock (S-STAB / RC2).  The compositor uses
20:   * this instead of get_framebuffer()+memcpy()+flush(): doing the copy under
21:   * the same lock that set_mode() takes to swap+free the backing closes the
22:   * use-after-free where a concurrent resolution/zoom change frees the scanout
23:   * mid-copy.  The driver copies only the intersection with its CURRENT scanout
24:   * and returns <0 (skip this frame) if src geometry no longer matches — never
25:   * an OOB.  0 on success (region presented). */
26:  int (*present)(struct gpu_device *dev, const uint32_t *src, int src_w,
27:                 int src_h, int x, int y, int w, int h);
28:  void (*destroy)(struct gpu_device *dev);
29:  /* Query the host's current preferred display size (what the device
30:   * advertises via GET_DISPLAY_INFO).  0 on success.  (GFX-DYN-01 #54) */
31:  int (*get_display_info)(struct gpu_device *dev, int *width, int *height);
32:  /* Poll for a host-initiated display-change event.  Returns 1 and fills
33:   * new_w/new_h when the host resized the output, 0 if nothing changed,
34:   * <0 on error/unsupported transport. */
35:  int (*poll_events)(struct gpu_device *dev, int *new_w, int *new_h);
36:};
37:
38:struct gpu_device {
39:  char name[32];
40:  int width;
41:  int height;
42:  int bpp;
43:  /* The scanout buffer is reached ONLY through ops->get_framebuffer (S-ALIGN
44:   * F7) — the old raw framebuffer_virt field was a second, field-level path
45:   * to the same memory and is retired. */
46:  size_t framebuffer_size;
47:  struct gpu_ops *ops;
48:  void *priv;              /* Driver private data */
49:  struct gpu_device *next; /* Linked list for multi-gpu */
50:};
51:
52:/* Core GPU Management */
53:int gpu_register(struct gpu_device *dev);
54:void gpu_unregister(struct gpu_device *dev);
55:struct gpu_device *gpu_get_primary(void);
56:
57:/* Contract wrappers over the primary GPU (GFX-DYN-01).  The kernel core
58: * (compositor) calls these instead of reaching into a driver: no driver
59: * internals, no magic numbers in the core. */
60:int gpu_set_mode(int width, int height);
61:int gpu_get_display_info(int *width, int *height);
62:int gpu_poll_events(int *new_w, int *new_h);
63:
64:/* Surface-speaking present (graphics-port): the provider contract talks the
65: * same semantic unit the whole stack does — a validated gfx_surface plus a
66: * damage rect — instead of raw pointer+geometry ints.  The S-STAB
67: * gfx_surface_verify() gate runs HERE, at the core/driver seam, so a
68: * geometry/allocation desync panics loudly at the source instead of becoming
69: * a silent OOB copy in a driver.  Present semantics are unchanged underneath
70: * (atomic copy+flush under the driver lock, <0 = skip this frame). */
71:struct gfx_rect;
72:struct gl_surface;
73:int gpu_present_surface(const struct gl_surface *src,
74:                        const struct gfx_rect *damage);
75:
76:#endif

@@@ kernel/include/drivers/usb/usb.h @@@
1:#ifndef _DRIVERS_USB_USB_H
2:#define _DRIVERS_USB_USB_H
3:
4:/*
5: * kernel/include/drivers/usb/usb.h
6: * USB core — controller-agnostic bus model.
7: *
8: * Layering (ASTRA): a host controller driver (xHCI / EHCI / UHCI) registers a
9: * struct usb_hcd implementing usb_hcd_ops. The core enumerates each port,
10: * reads standard descriptors over the control pipe, and hands HID interfaces
11: * to usb_hid.c, which translates reports into the existing evdev input core
12: * (virtio_input_add_event). The HCD never knows about HID; the HID driver
13: * never knows whether the transport is xHCI/EHCI/UHCI.
14: *
15: * Addressing is delegated to the HCD via enumerate_port(): UHCI/EHCI send a
16: * SET_ADDRESS on the default pipe, xHCI issues an Address Device command — the
17: * core must not assume either.
18: */
19:
20:#include <kernel/types.h>
21:
22:/* --- USB speeds --- */
23:#define USB_SPEED_LOW   1
24:#define USB_SPEED_FULL  2
25:#define USB_SPEED_HIGH  3
26:#define USB_SPEED_SUPER 4
27:
28:/* --- Standard request types (bmRequestType) --- */
29:#define USB_DIR_OUT 0x00
30:#define USB_DIR_IN  0x80
31:#define USB_TYPE_STANDARD 0x00
32:#define USB_TYPE_CLASS    0x20
33:#define USB_RECIP_DEVICE    0x00
34:#define USB_RECIP_INTERFACE 0x01
35:
36:/* --- Standard requests (bRequest) --- */
37:#define USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR 0x06
38:#define USB_REQ_SET_ADDRESS    0x05
39:#define USB_REQ_SET_CONFIG     0x09
40:
41:/* HID class requests */
42:#define HID_REQ_SET_PROTOCOL 0x0B
43:#define HID_REQ_SET_IDLE     0x0A
44:#define HID_PROTO_BOOT 0
45:#define HID_PROTO_REPORT 1
46:
47:/* --- Descriptor types --- */
48:#define USB_DT_DEVICE    0x01
49:#define USB_DT_CONFIG    0x02
50:#define USB_DT_INTERFACE 0x04
51:#define USB_DT_ENDPOINT  0x05
52:#define USB_DT_HID       0x21
53:#define USB_DT_HID_REPORT 0x22
54:
55:/* --- Class codes --- */
56:#define USB_CLASS_HID 0x03
57:#define USB_CLASS_HUB 0x09
58:#define HID_SUBCLASS_BOOT 0x01
59:#define HID_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD 0x01
60:#define HID_PROTOCOL_MOUSE    0x02
61:
62:/* --- Hub class (USB 2.0 ch.11) --- */
63:#define USB_DT_HUB 0x29
64:#define USB_REQ_GET_STATUS    0x00
65:#define USB_REQ_CLEAR_FEATURE 0x01
66:#define USB_REQ_SET_FEATURE   0x03
67:#define HUB_FEAT_PORT_RESET   4
68:#define HUB_FEAT_PORT_POWER   8
69:#define HUB_FEAT_C_PORT_CONNECTION 16
70:#define HUB_FEAT_C_PORT_RESET 20
71:#define HUB_PORT_CONNECTION 0x0001
72:#define HUB_PORT_ENABLE     0x0002
73:#define HUB_PORT_RESET      0x0010
74:#define HUB_PORT_LOWSPEED   0x0200
75:#define HUB_PORT_HIGHSPEED  0x0400
76:#define USB_RECIP_OTHER 0x03
77:
78:/* 8-byte SETUP packet */
79:struct usb_setup {
80:    uint8_t  bmRequestType;
81:    uint8_t  bRequest;
82:    uint16_t wValue;
83:    uint16_t wIndex;
84:    uint16_t wLength;
85:} __attribute__((packed));
86:
87:struct usb_device_descriptor {
88:    uint8_t  bLength;
89:    uint8_t  bDescriptorType;
90:    uint16_t bcdUSB;
91:    uint8_t  bDeviceClass;
92:    uint8_t  bDeviceSubClass;
93:    uint8_t  bDeviceProtocol;
94:    uint8_t  bMaxPacketSize0;
95:    uint16_t idVendor;
96:    uint16_t idProduct;
97:    uint16_t bcdDevice;
98:    uint8_t  iManufacturer;
99:    uint8_t  iProduct;
100:    uint8_t  iSerialNumber;
101:    uint8_t  bNumConfigurations;
102:} __attribute__((packed));
103:
104:struct usb_config_descriptor {
105:    uint8_t  bLength;
106:    uint8_t  bDescriptorType;
107:    uint16_t wTotalLength;
108:    uint8_t  bNumInterfaces;
109:    uint8_t  bConfigurationValue;
110:    uint8_t  iConfiguration;
111:    uint8_t  bmAttributes;
112:    uint8_t  bMaxPower;
113:} __attribute__((packed));
114:
115:struct usb_interface_descriptor {
116:    uint8_t  bLength;
117:    uint8_t  bDescriptorType;
118:    uint8_t  bInterfaceNumber;
119:    uint8_t  bAlternateSetting;
120:    uint8_t  bNumEndpoints;
121:    uint8_t  bInterfaceClass;
122:    uint8_t  bInterfaceSubClass;
123:    uint8_t  bInterfaceProtocol;
124:    uint8_t  iInterface;
125:} __attribute__((packed));

128:    uint8_t  bLength;
129:    uint8_t  bDescriptorType;
130:    uint8_t  bEndpointAddress;
131:    uint8_t  bmAttributes;
132:    uint16_t wMaxPacketSize;
133:    uint8_t  bInterval;
134:} __attribute__((packed));

136:struct usb_hcd;
137:
138:/* A USB device the core enumerated and addressed. */
139:struct usb_device {
140:    struct usb_hcd *hcd;
141:    uint8_t  addr;            /* USB address (1..127), HCD-assigned */
142:    uint8_t  speed;
143:    int      port;            /* root-hub port index (for root devices) */
144:    uint8_t  max_packet0;     /* EP0 max packet */
145:    uint16_t vendor, product;
146:    uint8_t  dev_class, dev_subclass, dev_protocol;
147:    void    *hcd_priv;        /* HCD per-device state (xHCI slot, etc.) */
148:
149:    /* Topology (for devices behind external hubs). */
150:    struct usb_device *parent; /* upstream hub, NULL if on the root hub */
151:    uint8_t  hub_port;         /* 1-based port on the parent hub */
152:    uint8_t  root_port;        /* 1-based root-hub port at the top of the path */
153:    uint32_t route;            /* xHCI route string (0 for root devices) */
154:    uint8_t  tier;             /* hub depth from root (0 = root device) */
155:    int      is_hub;
156:
157:    /* HID interface of interest (filled by usb_hid bind) */
158:    int      hid_iface;
159:    uint8_t  hid_ep_in;       /* endpoint address (with 0x80 IN bit) */
160:    int      hid_ep_max;      /* wMaxPacketSize of that endpoint */
161:    uint8_t  hid_interval;
162:    uint8_t  hid_protocol;    /* HID_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD / _MOUSE (boot) */
163:    int      hid_use_report;  /* 1 = report-protocol HID (non-boot, e.g. tablet) */
164:    int      hid_report_len;  /* report-descriptor length (HID desc wDescriptorLength) */
165:    /* Absolute pointer, parsed from the HID report descriptor (USB tablet). */
166:    int      hid_is_abs;      /* 1 = reports absolute X/Y */
167:    uint16_t hid_abs_x_off;   /* bit offset of X within the input report */
168:    uint16_t hid_abs_y_off;   /* bit offset of Y */
169:    uint8_t  hid_abs_bits;    /* X/Y field size in bits */
170:    uint32_t hid_abs_max;     /* logical max of X/Y (for scaling) */
171:    int16_t  hid_btn_off;     /* bit offset of the first button, -1 if none */
172:    int      in_use;
173:};
174:
175:/* Host controller driver contract. */
176:struct usb_hcd_ops {
177:    int  (*num_ports)(struct usb_hcd *hcd);
178:    int  (*port_connected)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port);
179:    /* Reset + address a device on root-hub `port`; fill *out (addr/speed/
180:     * max_packet0/hcd_priv). Returns 0 on success, <0 on failure/no device. */
181:    int  (*enumerate_port)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port, struct usb_device *out);
182:    /* Address a device whose topology (parent/route/tier/root_port/speed) the
183:     * core already filled, reached through an external hub. The hub did the
184:     * port reset; this only assigns the address/slot. Optional (NULL = no hub
185:     * support on this controller). Returns 0 on success. */
186:    int  (*address_dev)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev);
187:    /* Control transfer on the device's default pipe. data may be NULL.
188:     * Returns bytes transferred (>=0) or <0 on error. */
189:    int  (*control)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
190:                    const struct usb_setup *setup, void *data, int len);
191:    /* Configure an interrupt IN endpoint for periodic polling. */
192:    int  (*intr_open)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
193:                      uint8_t ep_addr, int max_packet, int interval);
194:    /* Non-blocking poll of the interrupt IN endpoint: copies up to len bytes
195:     * into buf. Returns bytes (0 if nothing new) or <0. */
196:    int  (*intr_poll)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
197:                      uint8_t ep_addr, void *buf, int len);
198:};
199:
200:struct usb_hcd {
201:    const char *name;
202:    struct usb_hcd_ops *ops;
203:    void *priv;
204:};
205:
206:/* --- USB core API --- */
207:
208:/* Called by each HCD after it has reset its controller. The core immediately
209: * enumerates the controller's ports and binds HID devices. */
210:void usb_register_hcd(struct usb_hcd *hcd);
211:
212:/* Control-transfer convenience used by the core and class drivers. */
213:int  usb_control(struct usb_device *dev, uint8_t bmRequestType, uint8_t bRequest,
214:                 uint16_t wValue, uint16_t wIndex, void *data, uint16_t wLength);
215:
216:/* Subsystem entry point: register the HCD drivers and run driver matching so
217: * each present controller is probed. Called from the input init path. */
218:void usb_init(void);
219:
220:/* Periodic poll of all bound HID endpoints; drives the evdev input core.
221: * Called from the same place keyboard_poll() is serviced. */
222:void usb_hid_poll(void);
223:
224:/* Internal: usb_hid.c entry, called by the core for each enumerated device. */
225:void usb_hid_probe_device(struct usb_device *dev);
226:
227:/* HCD driver registration hooks (each calls driver_register on its driver). */
228:void xhci_register(void);
229:void ehci_register(void);
230:void uhci_register(void);
231:
232:#endif /* _DRIVERS_USB_USB_H */

1:/*
2: * kernel/include/drivers/timer.h
3: * ARM Generic Timer
4: */
5:#ifndef _DRIVERS_TIMER_H
6:#define _DRIVERS_TIMER_H
7:
8:#include <kernel/list.h>
9:#include <kernel/types.h>
10:
11:/* Timer frequency (will be read from CNTFRQ_EL0) */
12:extern uint64_t timer_freq;
13:
14:/* System ticks since boot */
15:extern volatile uint64_t jiffies;
16:
17:/* Timer configuration */
18:#define HZ                                                                     \
19:  100 /* Reduced frequency for better performance in non-optimized kernel */
20:
21:/* Time conversion macros */
22:#define MSEC_PER_SEC 1000UL
23:#define USEC_PER_SEC 1000000UL
24:#define NSEC_PER_SEC 1000000000UL
25:
26:#define msecs_to_jiffies(m) ((uint64_t)(m) * HZ / MSEC_PER_SEC)
27:#define jiffies_to_msecs(j) ((uint64_t)(j) * MSEC_PER_SEC / HZ)
28:
29:/* Nanoseconds per scheduler tick (the jiffies granularity). The whole 3-tier
30: * model (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md) reconciles the tick clocks against this real-time
31: * stride derived from the hardware counter. */
32:#define NS_PER_TICK (NSEC_PER_SEC / HZ)
33:
34:/* Functions */
35:void timer_init(void);
36:void timer_init_percpu(void);
37:uint64_t timer_get_ticks(void);
38:uint64_t timer_get_us(void);
39:void timer_delay_us(uint64_t us);
40:void timer_delay_ms(uint64_t ms);
41:
42:/* mono_ns - monotonic nanoseconds since boot, derived from the free-running
43: * hardware counter (arch_timer_get_count / arch_timer_get_freq). This is the
44: * arch-neutral REAL-TIME reference every timer tier compares against to recover
45: * lost ticks; jiffies is a cheap integer view of it. Defined in core/timer.c. */
46:uint64_t mono_ns(void);
47:/* timer_get_ns - alias of mono_ns() (the canonical real-time clock); replaces
48: * the per-arch timer_get_us() path so amd64 stops returning jiffies*1000. */
49:uint64_t timer_get_ns(void);
50:/* timer_counts_to_ns - scale a raw hardware-counter delta to nanoseconds.
51: * The scheduler accumulates per-process CPU time in raw counter units (a cheap
52: * subtraction, no divide in the hot path) and converts via this only on read. */
53:uint64_t timer_counts_to_ns(uint64_t counts);
54:
55:/* Tier 2 per-CPU clock — HAL-driven, arch-neutral (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §3).
56: * timer_percpu_tick(): per-tick drift accounting + compare reprogram against the
57: *   hardware counter (arch_timer_get_freq/count/set_compare); catch-up clamp
58: *   recovers lost ticks. Called from each arch's timer IRQ before the scheduler
59: *   tick. arch_timer_set_compare() reprograms a one-shot timer (aarch64) and is
60: *   a no-op for a periodic timer (amd64), so the one routine serves both.
61: * timer_percpu_arm(): seed the per-CPU schedule on this core's timer bring-up. */
62:struct cpu_info;
63:void timer_percpu_tick(struct cpu_info *cpu);
64:void timer_percpu_arm(struct cpu_info *cpu);
65:
66:/* Internal Handlers */
67:struct pt_regs;
68:struct pt_regs *timer_handler(struct pt_regs *regs);
69:struct pt_regs *kernel_timer_tick(struct pt_regs *regs);
70:
71:/* Timer callback type */
72:typedef void (*timer_callback_t)(void *data);
73:
74:/* Software timer structure */
75:struct timer {
76:  struct list_head list;
77:  uint64_t expires; /* Expiration time in jiffies (global monotonic base) */
78:  timer_callback_t callback;
79:  void *data;
80:  bool pending;
81:  int cpu; /* CPU whose per-CPU timer_list this timer is armed on (-1 = none) */
82:};
83:
84:/* Software timer functions */
85:void timer_setup(struct timer *t, timer_callback_t callback, void *data);
86:void timer_add(struct timer *t, uint64_t expires);
87:void timer_del(struct timer *t);
88:bool timer_pending(struct timer *t);
89:
90:#endif /* _DRIVERS_TIMER_H */

1:/*
2: * kernel/include/drivers/uart.h
3: * UART driver interface
4: */
5:#ifndef _DRIVERS_UART_H
6:#define _DRIVERS_UART_H
7:
8:#include <kernel/types.h>

10:/* PL011 UART registers for QEMU virt machine */
11:#define UART0_BASE 0x09000000UL
12:#define UART0_IRQ 33
13:
14:/* PL011 Register offsets */
15:#define UART_DR 0x00    /* Data Register */
16:#define UART_RSR 0x04   /* Receive Status Register */
17:#define UART_FR 0x18    /* Flag Register */
18:#define UART_ILPR 0x20  /* IrDA Low-Power Counter */
19:#define UART_IBRD 0x24  /* Integer Baud Rate */
20:#define UART_FBRD 0x28  /* Fractional Baud Rate */
21:#define UART_LCR_H 0x2C /* Line Control */
22:#define UART_CR 0x30    /* Control Register */
23:#define UART_IFLS 0x34  /* Interrupt FIFO Level Select */
24:#define UART_IMSC 0x38  /* Interrupt Mask Set/Clear */
25:#define UART_RIS 0x3C   /* Raw Interrupt Status */
26:#define UART_MIS 0x40   /* Masked Interrupt Status */
27:#define UART_ICR 0x44   /* Interrupt Clear */
28:#define UART_DMACR 0x48 /* DMA Control */
29:
30:/* Flag Register bits */
31:#define UART_FR_TXFE BIT(7) /* TX FIFO Empty */
32:#define UART_FR_RXFF BIT(6) /* RX FIFO Full */
33:#define UART_FR_TXFF BIT(5) /* TX FIFO Full */
34:#define UART_FR_RXFE BIT(4) /* RX FIFO Empty */
35:#define UART_FR_BUSY BIT(3) /* UART Busy */
36:
37:/* Control Register bits */
38:#define UART_CR_RXE BIT(9)    /* Receive Enable */
39:#define UART_CR_TXE BIT(8)    /* Transmit Enable */
40:#define UART_CR_UARTEN BIT(0) /* UART Enable */
41:
42:/* Line Control bits */
43:#define UART_LCR_H_WLEN_8 (3 << 5) /* 8 bits */
44:#define UART_LCR_H_FEN BIT(4)      /* FIFO Enable */
45:
46:/* Functions */
47:void uart_init(void);
48:void uart_putc(char c);
49:char uart_getc(void);
50:int uart_getc_nonblock(void);
51:void uart_puts(const char *s);
52:void uart_puthex(uint64_t val);
53:
54:/* uart_putc_emergency - lock-free TX for fault context (see kernel/fault.h).
55: * Identical output path to uart_putc but never takes a spinlock: usable from
56: * an exception handler even when uart_lock is held by a wedged CPU.  May
57: * interleave with concurrent normal output. */
58:void uart_putc_emergency(char c);
59:
60:#endif /* _DRIVERS_UART_H */

15:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_ID 0x008
16:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_VENDOR_ID 0x00c

21:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_GUEST_PAGE_SIZE 0x028
22:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL 0x030
23:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX 0x034
24:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM 0x038
25:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_ALIGN 0x03c
26:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_PFN 0x040
27:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_READY 0x044
28:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY 0x050
29:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_STATUS 0x060

31:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS 0x070
32:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_DESC_LOW 0x080

35:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_DRIVER_HIGH 0x094
36:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_DEVICE_LOW 0x0a0
37:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_DEVICE_HIGH 0x0a4

39:#define VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG 0x100

42:#define VIRTIO_DEV_NET 1
43:#define VIRTIO_DEV_BLOCK 2
44:#define VIRTIO_DEV_CONSOLE 3
45:#define VIRTIO_DEV_GPU 16
46:#define VIRTIO_DEV_INPUT 18

49:#define VIRTIO_STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE 1
50:#define VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER 2
51:#define VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER_OK 4
52:#define VIRTIO_STATUS_FEATURES_OK 8
53:#define VIRTIO_STATUS_DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET 64
54:#define VIRTIO_STATUS_FAILED 128
55:
56:/* VirtIO Ring Descriptors */
57:#define VRING_DESC_F_NEXT 1
58:#define VRING_DESC_F_WRITE 2
59:#define VRING_DESC_F_INDIRECT 4
60:
61:/* transport ops */
62:struct virtio_device;
63:struct virtio_transport_ops {
64:  uint32_t (*read32)(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset);
65:  void (*write32)(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset, uint32_t val);
66:  void (*notify)(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t queue_idx);
67:};
68:
69:struct virtio_device {
70:  hal_device_t hal_dev;
71:  uintptr_t base;
72:  uint32_t irq;
73:  uint32_t device_id;
74:  bool is_legacy;
75:  const struct virtio_transport_ops *ops;
76:  uintptr_t isr_base;
77:  uintptr_t notify_base;
78:  void *priv;
79:  spinlock_t lock;
80:};
81:
82:typedef struct virtio_device *virtio_handle_t;
83:
84:/* VirtIO Ring Descriptors */
85:#define VRING_DESC_F_NEXT 1
86:#define VRING_DESC_F_WRITE 2
87:#define VRING_DESC_F_INDIRECT 4
88:
89:struct vring_desc {
90:  uint64_t addr;
91:  uint32_t len;
92:  uint16_t flags;
93:  uint16_t next;
94:};
95:
96:struct vring_avail {
97:  uint16_t flags;
98:  uint16_t idx;
99:  uint16_t ring[];
100:};
101:
102:struct vring_used_elem {
103:  uint32_t id;
104:  uint32_t len;
105:};
106:
107:struct vring_used {
108:  uint16_t flags;
109:  uint16_t idx;
110:  struct vring_used_elem ring[];
111:};
112:
113:/* API */
114:static inline uint32_t virtio_read_reg(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset) {
115:  return dev->ops->read32(dev, offset);
116:}
117:
118:static inline void virtio_write_reg(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset,
119:                                    uint32_t val) {
120:  dev->ops->write32(dev, offset, val);
121:}
122:
123:static inline void virtio_notify(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t queue_idx) {
124:  dev->ops->notify(dev, queue_idx);
125:}
126:
127:/* Device-config space access (GFX-DYN-01 F7): reads/writes a device's
128: * device-specific configuration at byte 'offset', transport-agnostically.
129: * On VirtIO-MMIO this is base+VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG+offset; on VirtIO-PCI modern it
130: * is the device-specific capability region.  Implemented by the arch transport
131: * so drivers (e.g. virtio-gpu events) need not know the transport. */
132:uint32_t virtio_config_read32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset);
133:void virtio_config_write32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset, uint32_t val);
134:
135:/* Discovery & Setup */
136:void arch_virtio_scan(void);
137:int arch_virtio_get_count(uint32_t device_id);
138:int arch_virtio_get_device(uint32_t device_id, int index,
139:                           virtio_handle_t *out_dev, uint32_t *out_irq);
140:void virtio_setup_queue(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t queue_idx,
141:                        uint64_t desc_addr, uint64_t avail_addr,
142:                        uint64_t used_addr);
143:
144:#endif /* _DRIVERS_VIRTIO_H */

@@@ kernel/include/graphics/gl.h @@@
1:#ifndef _GRAPHICS_GL_H
2:#define _GRAPHICS_GL_H
3:
4:#include <stddef.h>
5:#include <stdint.h>
6:
7:/*
8: * TinyGL: A simple software rasterization library.
9: * Operates on 32-bit ARGB buffers.
10: */
11:
12:struct gl_surface {
13:  int width;
14:  int height;
15:  int stride; /* in pixels, usually width */
16:  uint32_t *buffer;
17:  uint8_t *alpha_mask;
18:  /* S-STAB: number of valid uint32_t words actually backing 'buffer'.  The
19:   * whole raster path indexes buffer[y*stride+x] and only ever bounds-checks
20:   * against width/height, which is memory-safe ONLY if the geometry matches the
21:   * allocation (stride>=width AND height*stride<=capacity).  Nothing enforced
22:   * that invariant, so any geometry desync (a resize race, a stale scanout, a
23:   * driver reporting a size that outran its buffer) turned into a silent OOB
24:   * write into adjacent kernel RAM — the class of bug behind the UTM panics.
25:   * capacity makes the invariant checkable at the source; 0 = "unknown/legacy"
26:   * (an unconverted construction site), which gfx_surface_verify() treats as
27:   * un-instrumented rather than as a violation. */
28:  size_t capacity;
29:};
30:
31:/* gfx_surface_verify - S-STAB invariant gate.  Panics with the full geometry vs
32: * allocation if a surface is internally inconsistent (stride<width, or
33: * height*stride>capacity), catching a geometry desync at bind time — before the
34: * first OOB write scribbles kernel memory — instead of a mangled fault later.
35: * 'where' names the bind site for the panic message.  No-op when capacity==0
36: * (site not yet instrumented) so partial rollout never false-panics. */
37:void gfx_surface_verify(const struct gl_surface *surf, const char *where);
38:
39:/* Exact round-to-nearest divide-by-255 for x in [0, ~65790] (classic identity,
40: * no integer division).  Replaces the ">>8" (÷256) approximation that dimmed
41: * blended pixels — GFX-DYN-01 #121.4. */
42:static inline uint32_t gl_div255(uint32_t x) {
43:  x += 128;
44:  return (x + (x >> 8)) >> 8;
45:}
46:
47:/* Alpha-blend a source ARGB pixel over a destination ARGB pixel (straight
48: * over operator, opaque result).  Shared by the compositor and the terminal
49: * emulator so both use one definition. */
50:static inline uint32_t gl_blend_pixel(uint32_t fg, uint32_t bg) {
51:  uint32_t alpha = (fg >> 24) & 0xFF;
52:  if (alpha == 255)
53:    return fg;
54:  if (alpha == 0)
55:    return bg;
56:  uint32_t inv_alpha = 255 - alpha;
57:  uint32_t r =
58:      gl_div255(((fg >> 16) & 0xFF) * alpha + ((bg >> 16) & 0xFF) * inv_alpha);
59:  uint32_t g =
60:      gl_div255(((fg >> 8) & 0xFF) * alpha + ((bg >> 8) & 0xFF) * inv_alpha);
61:  uint32_t b = gl_div255((fg & 0xFF) * alpha + (bg & 0xFF) * inv_alpha);
62:  return 0xFF000000 | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
63:}
64:
65:/* Primitives */
66:void gl_clear(struct gl_surface *surf, uint32_t color);
67:void gl_draw_pixel(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, uint32_t color);
68:void gl_draw_line(struct gl_surface *surf, int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1,
69:                  uint32_t color);
70:void gl_draw_rect(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, int w, int h,
71:                  uint32_t color);
72:void gl_draw_rect_fill(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, int w, int h,
73:                       uint32_t color);
74:void gl_blit(struct gl_surface *dst, struct gl_surface *src, int dx, int dy);
75:void gl_draw_char(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, uint32_t codepoint,
76:                  uint32_t color);
77:void gl_draw_string(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, const char *str,
78:                    uint32_t color);
79:/* Clipped variant: identical to gl_draw_string but writes only pixels inside
80: * [cx1,cx2) x [cy1,cy2).  Used by the damage-clipped compositor so title text
81: * never paints outside the per-frame damage box. */
82:void gl_draw_string_clipped(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y,
83:                            const char *str, uint32_t color, int cx1, int cy1,
84:                            int cx2, int cy2);

26: * context.  A kernel thread calls this to enter schedule() without a hardware
27: * trap; it "returns" only when this thread is scheduled again.  Implemented
28: * per-arch (aarch64 exception.S / amd64 isr_stubs.S) by building a pt_regs

30: * be masked by the caller (kthread_block).  This is the foundation for

35: * leg stalls CPU0; do not build new blocking primitives on this until that is
36: * fixed.  See docs/report/KTHREAD-STATUS.md. */

1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/block.h
3: * Block-device contract (ASTRA seam: virtio-blk -> block -> fs provider -> VFS).
4: *
5: * The FS stack (GPT, ext4, buffer cache) consumes ONLY this contract; it never
6: * names a concrete backend.  Today's backends are virtio-blk (the real device,
7: * `make run` and the dev loop) and the RAM-backed ramdisk (a GRUB multiboot2
8: * module, the self-contained release ISO).  Sectors are 512 bytes.
9: */

16:struct block_dev {

19:  int (*write)(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count);
20:};
21:
22:/* Make 'dev' the active block backend (last registration wins).  main.c
23: * registers virtio-blk first and lets the ramdisk override it only when a
24: * boot module is present, so the dev loop keeps using the real device. */
25:void block_register(const struct block_dev *dev);
26:
27:/* Name of the active backend, or NULL if none registered (for logging). */
28:const char *block_active_name(void);

30:/* Read/write 'count' 512-byte sectors at 'sector' through the active backend.
31: * Return 0 on success, negative on failure (no backend -> failure). */
32:int block_read(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) NX_MUST_USE;
33:int block_write(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) NX_MUST_USE;

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/bootphase.h @@@
1:#ifndef _KERNEL_BOOTPHASE_H
2:#define _KERNEL_BOOTPHASE_H
3:
4:/* Boot-phase tracking (S-ALIGN F9) — the K1/K2/K3 boot model made explicit:
5: *   K1  memory/hardware bring-up (CPU, IRQ, timer, PMM/VMM, SMP)
6: *   K2  kernel subsystem init (bus/block/GPU/VFS/registry/sched/compositor)
7: *   K3  userland bring-up (PID1) — enters ONLY after K1+K2 are confirmed
8: *   RUN steady state
9: * The phase is single-writer (the BSP during kernel_main) and read by
10: * panic() to stamp fault reports and scope failure policy: a K3-only
11: * failure (userland won't load) must not take down a healthy K1+K2 —
12: * the kernel stays alive and diagnosable (kernel-alone mode). */
13:enum boot_phase {
14:  BOOT_PHASE_K1_HW = 0,
15:  BOOT_PHASE_K2_SUBSYS,
16:  BOOT_PHASE_K3_USERLAND,
17:  BOOT_PHASE_RUNNING,
18:};
19:
20:void boot_phase_set(enum boot_phase p);
21:enum boot_phase boot_phase_get(void);
22:const char *boot_phase_name(enum boot_phase p);
23:
24:#endif /* _KERNEL_BOOTPHASE_H */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/buffer.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/buffer.h
3: * Buffer Cache (Zero-Copy) for Block Devices
4: *
5: * Declares the public API for the buffer cache (kernel/mm/buffer.c).
6: *
7: * The buffer cache sits between the filesystem (ext4) and the VirtIO block
8: * driver.  Each cached block occupies one 4KB PMM page (BLOCK_SIZE ==
9: * PAGE_SIZE).  buf->data points directly into that PMM page (zero-copy).
10: *
11: * Callers must bracket every use of a buffer with buffer_get() / buffer_put()
12: * to maintain the ref_count; buffers with ref_count > 0 are pinned and will
13: * not be evicted.
14: *
15: * Known issues (see docs/review/analysis/01-mm-memory-management.md):
16: *   MM-BUF-01  (W3 BUG)         MAX_BUFFERS not a hard cap.
17: *   MM-BUF-02  (W2 PERF)        Duplicate disk reads on concurrent miss.
18: *   MM-BUF-03  (W2 BUG/SECURITY) No per-buffer content lock; data race.
19: *   MM-BUF-04  (W2 REFINE)      buffer_sync() flushes at most 64 buffers.
20: *   MM-BUF-05  (W1 REFINE)      Weak hash and fixed bucket count.
21: */
22:#ifndef _KERNEL_BUFFER_H
23:#define _KERNEL_BUFFER_H
24:
25:#include <kernel/list.h>
26:#include <kernel/types.h>
27:
28:/* BLOCK_SIZE: filesystem block size; matches PAGE_SIZE (4KB) for zero-copy. */
29:#define BLOCK_SIZE 4096 /* Matches Page Size */
30:#ifndef SECTOR_SIZE
31:#define SECTOR_SIZE 512
32:#endif /* SECTOR_SIZE */
33:/* SECTORS_PER_BLOCK: number of 512-byte disk sectors per cached block (= 8). */
34:#define SECTORS_PER_BLOCK (BLOCK_SIZE / SECTOR_SIZE)
35:
36:/* BUFFER_UPTODATE: buf->data reflects the on-disk content (read has completed). */
37:#define BUFFER_UPTODATE 0x1
38:/* BUFFER_DIRTY: buf->data has been modified and must be written to disk before
39: * the buffer can be evicted.  Set by filesystem code; cleared by buffer_sync(). */
40:#define BUFFER_DIRTY 0x2
41:
42:/*
43: * struct block_buffer - cache entry for one 4KB disk block.
44: *
45: * block:     logical block number (in BLOCK_SIZE units, not sector units).
46: *            Callers multiply by SECTORS_PER_BLOCK to get the sector offset.
47: * data:      pointer to a 4KB PMM page holding the block content.
48: *            NOTE(MM-BUF-03): There is no per-buffer lock protecting data;
49: *            concurrent reads and buffer_sync() writes race.
50: * flags:     OR of BUFFER_UPTODATE / BUFFER_DIRTY; protected by buffer_lock.
51: * ref_count: caller reference count; protected by buffer_lock.
52: *            Buffers with ref_count > 0 cannot be evicted.
53: * list:      entry in the global LRU list; head = most recently used.
54: * hash:      entry in hash_table[bucket] collision list.
55: */
56:struct block_buffer {
57:  uint64_t block; /* Block index (4KB units) */
58:  uint8_t *data;  /* Pointer to 4KB page (Zero-copy) */
59:  uint32_t flags;
60:  uint32_t ref_count;
61:
62:  struct list_head list; /* LRU List */
63:  struct list_head hash; /* Hash Table Collision List */
64:};
65:
66:/* API */
67:void buffer_init(void);
68:
69:/* Get a buffer for a block. Reads from disk if not cached.
70: * Increments ref_count. */
71:struct block_buffer *buffer_get(uint64_t block);
72:
73:/* Release a buffer. Decrements ref_count. */
74:void buffer_put(struct block_buffer *buf);
75:
76:/* Write all dirty buffers to disk */
77:void buffer_sync(void);
78:
79:#endif /* _KERNEL_BUFFER_H */
80:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/compositor_style.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/compositor_style.h
3: * Compositor appearance model (GFX-DYN-01 / DIR-07).
4: *
5: * Four orthogonal concerns, deliberately separated (the maintainer's model):
6: *
7: *   Policy     = behaviour   (floating / tiled / mobile window management)
8: *   Style      = form        (titlebar? borders? rounded? shadows? sizes)
9: *   Theme      = colours     (window palette: titlebar, text, accent)
10: *   Background = desktop     (base colour + gradient reference colours)
11: *
12: * Style and Theme never touch the scene graph, surfaces, input or buffers —
13: * they only change HOW the existing windows are rendered.  The compositor reads
14: * the active style/theme/background each frame; switching them re-renders with
15: * no other state change.
16: */

24: * desktop-vs-mobile transform; floating is the only one wired today. */
25:typedef enum {
26:  WINDOW_POLICY_FLOATING = 0,
27:  WINDOW_POLICY_TILED,
28:  WINDOW_POLICY_MOBILE,
29:} window_policy_t;

36:  int shadows;         /* draw drop shadows                                */
37:  int animations;      /* enable open/close/move animations               */
38:  int titlebar_height; /* px; 0 ⇒ no chrome regardless of `titlebar`       */
39:  int border_radius;   /* px corner radius when rounded_corners            */
40:  int shadow_size;     /* px shadow spread when shadows                    */
41:  int shadow_type;     /* 0=solid win_bg (Retro), 1=fast SDF, 2=premium grad.  */
42:  int button_shape;    /* 0 = circle (macOS), 1 = square (Retro/Win95) */
43:  int button_side;     /* 0 = left, 1 = right */
44:} compositor_style_t;

47:typedef struct compositor_theme {

50:  uint32_t title_inactive;      /* unfocused title bar                      */

55:  uint32_t accent;              /* accent (caret/selection)                 */

62:  uint32_t bg_bottom;           /* reference colour 2 (gradient bottom)     */
63:} compositor_background_t;
64:
65:/* Preset identifiers (stable small ints — also the SYS_SET_STYLE args). */
66:enum {
67:  STYLE_NEXS = 0, /* NEXS default                     */
68:  STYLE_CLASSIC,  /* X11/Motif: square, no shadow                       */
69:  STYLE_MATERIAL, /* Android/Material 3: rounded, soft shadow           */

10:/* Forward declaraton */
11:struct process;

13:/* Per-CPU information structure */
14:struct cpu_info {
15:  struct cpu_info *self; /* Must be at offset 0 for %gs:0 access on x86_64 */
16:  uint32_t cpu_id;
17:  uint32_t online;
18:  uint64_t stack_top;      /* Kernel Stack Top */
19:  uint64_t user_stack_tmp; /* Temp storage for user RSP during syscall/interrupt */
20:  struct process *current_task;
21:  uint64_t next_tick_target;
22:  uint64_t tick_error_acc;
23:  uint64_t tick_count;
24:  /* Raw hardware-counter value at which the current task last started running on
25:   * this CPU; schedule() charges (arch_timer_get_count() - sched_run_count) to
26:   * the outgoing task's cpu_time_counts (Tier 3 per-process CPU time, converted
27:   * to ns only on read — docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4). */
28:  uint64_t sched_run_count;
29:
30:  /* Scheduler Local Data (Multicore Optimization) */
31:  struct list_head runqueues[32];
32:  uint32_t prio_bitmap;
33:  spinlock_t sched_lock; /* Local runqueue protection */
34:  struct process *idle_task;
35:
36:  /* Per-CPU software timer wheel (kernel/core/timer.c): each CPU fires its OWN
37:   * timers in kernel_timer_tick against the global jiffies clock, so a process
38:   * sleeping on this core is woken locally — no cross-CPU dependency, no global
39:   * timer-lock contention. */
40:  struct list_head timer_list;
41:  spinlock_t timer_lock;
42:
43:  char printk_buf[2048];
44:  char syscall_buf[2048];
45:  uint32_t in_printk;
46:  uint32_t printk_dropped;
47:
48:  /* Fault recursion depth (Phase A, kernel/fault.h).  Incremented by
49:   * fault_enter() at exception-dispatch entry; depth > 1 means a fault
50:   * occurred inside a fault handler — the dispatcher emits one raw line via
51:   * fault_printf and halts instead of recursing to a triple fault. */
52:  uint32_t in_fault;
53:
54:  /* Set while arch_copy_{from,to}_user is dereferencing user memory.  The
55:   * fault classifier treats a kernel-mode fault on a user VA as a recoverable
56:   * uaccess fault ONLY when this is set (CPU-AARCH64-01: a wild kernel
57:   * pointer that merely lands in user VA range must panic, not silently
58:   * terminate the current process). */
59:  uint32_t uaccess_active;
60:
61:  /* Reap stack head (SCHED-UAF-01): processes terminated by process_terminate()
62:   * awaiting deferred destruction, chained via the legacy process.next field;
63:   * drained at the top of the next schedule() on this CPU, after we have
64:   * switched away from them. */
65:  struct process *deferred_free_proc;
66:  /* SCHED-UAF (#169/#170): a task preempted on this CPU is held here for ONE
67:   * schedule before going back on a runqueue.  If it were re-enqueued
68:   * immediately, another CPU could work-steal and run it while THIS CPU is still
69:   * executing on its kernel stack (the IRQ EOI + dispatch epilogue run on prev's
70:   * stack AFTER schedule() returns, before the iretq switches away; the LAPIC EOI
71:   * MMIO write widens that window on UTM).  Two CPUs on one stack smash the
72:   * in-flight return frame.  Drained at the top of the next schedule() here,
73:   * after this CPU has provably iretq'd off that stack — mirrors deferred_free. */
74:  struct process *pending_reenqueue;
75:};
76:#endif

88: * acquire-wait for the ack.  0 = online, -1 = wake failed, -2 = ack timeout.
89: * smp_ack_boot: release-store ack, called by the secondary once initialized. */
90:int smp_bringup_secondary(uint32_t cpu, void (*entry)(void), void *stack_top) NX_MUST_USE;

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/driver.h @@@
1:#ifndef _KERNEL_DRIVER_H
2:#define _KERNEL_DRIVER_H
3:
4:/*
5: * kernel/include/kernel/driver.h
6: * Driver-binding contract (ASTRA wiring layer).
7: *
8: * A device_driver declares what it can drive — either a specific vendor:device
9: * pair (virtio, Bochs VBE, ...) or a generic PCI class triplet
10: * (xHCI = 0x0C/0x03/0x30, AHCI = 0x01/0x06/0x01, VGA = 0x03/0x00/..., ...).
11: * driver_match_all() walks the hal_device registry and calls probe() on every
12: * still-unbound device a driver matches.  This is the seam that lets a "board"
13: * be just a bag of class-identified providers, with no hardcoded model list.
14: */
15:
16:#include <kernel/types.h>
17:#include <kernel/hal.h>
18:
19:#define DRV_ANY_ID    0xFFFF  /* wildcard for vendor/device */
20:#define DRV_ANY_CLASS 0xFF    /* wildcard for class_code/subclass/prog_if */
21:
22:struct device_driver {
23:    const char *name;
24:
25:    /* ID match (either-or with class match): set to DRV_ANY_ID to ignore. */
26:    uint16_t vendor;
27:    uint16_t device;
28:
29:    /* Class match: set any field to DRV_ANY_CLASS to ignore that field. */
30:    uint8_t class_code;
31:    uint8_t subclass;
32:    uint8_t prog_if;
33:
34:    /* Called once per matching, still-unbound device. Return 0 to claim the
35:     * device (it becomes bound), non-zero to decline (stays available). */
36:    int (*probe)(struct hal_device *dev);
37:
38:    struct device_driver *next; /* internal: linked-list link */
39:};
40:
41:/* Register a driver. Safe to call before or after the bus scan; matching is
42: * performed by driver_match_all(), not at registration time. */
43:void driver_register(struct device_driver *drv);
44:
45:/* Probe every registered driver against every unbound device in the hal
46: * registry. Idempotent: already-bound devices are skipped, so it may be called
47: * again after registering more drivers (e.g. once per subsystem init). */
48:void driver_match_all(void);
49:
50:#endif /* _KERNEL_DRIVER_H */

152: * A node is: one ext4_extent_header followed by eh_entries records —
