@@@ kernel/include/kernel/vfs.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/vfs.h
3: * Virtual Filesystem Switch — the filesystem provider contract.
4: *
5: * ASTRA seam (docs/ASTRA.md): the kernel core (syscall dispatch, ELF loader)
6: * consumes ONLY this interface; the concrete filesystem driver (ext4 today)
7: * is a provider registered behind it at boot.  The composition root is
8: * kernel/main.c: vfs_register_fs(&ext4_fs_ops) then vfs_init().
9: *
10: * Resolution model (deliberately minimal for now):
11: *   - One root mount ("/"), chosen at vfs_init() by probing the GPT/MBR
12: *     partitions with every registered provider, in partition order.
13: *   - Paths handed to providers are absolute, normalized (see
14: *     vfs_resolve_path) and relative to the provider's own root.
15: *   - vfs_node is a plain value type: no refcount, no open-file table; it
16: *     stays valid as long as its mount stays mounted.  The root mount is
17: *     never torn down; non-root mounts can be retired with vfs_umount()
18: *     (in-flight path ops are counted and umount refuses with -EBUSY; a
19: *     node HELD across umount is the caller's responsibility until the
20: *     fd-layer refcount lands — docs/userland-port PLAN phase 4).  The
21: *     per-process fd table is ABI-03 (epic #93) and will layer on top.
22: */
23:#ifndef _KERNEL_VFS_H
24:#define _KERNEL_VFS_H
25:
26:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
27:#include <kernel/types.h>
28:#include <object.h> /* OBJ_TYPE_* — a namespace path resolves to a typed object */
29:
30:struct partition; /* kernel/gpt.h */
31:struct vfs_mount;
32:
33:/* Node types (vfs_node.type / vfs_stat.type) */
34:#define VFS_TYPE_FILE 1
35:#define VFS_TYPE_DIR 2
36:
37:/* An open filesystem object. */
38:struct vfs_node {
39:  struct vfs_mount *mnt;
40:  uint64_t id;   /* provider-private identifier (ext4: inode number) */
41:  uint64_t size; /* size in bytes at open time */
42:  uint32_t type; /* VFS_TYPE_* */
43:};
44:
45:struct vfs_stat {
46:  uint64_t size;
47:  uint32_t type; /* VFS_TYPE_* */
48:};
49:
50:/* A typed object a namespace path resolves to (the path→object bridge: in the
51: * unified model a path IS a typed capability object, not merely a file).  Filled
52: * by fs_ops.object_at and consumed by handle_create(OS1_NS_FS), which builds the
53: * matching kobject. */
54:struct vfs_objref {
55:  uint8_t obj_type;     /* OBJ_TYPE_* (include/api/object.h) */
56:  int pid;              /* OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS */
57:  int window_id;        /* OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW */
58:  struct vfs_node node; /* OBJ_TYPE_FILE */
59:};
60:
61:/*
62: * The provider contract.
63: *
64: * mount: probe 'part' and, if the on-disk format is recognised AND
65: *        supported, fill mnt->fs_private and return 0.  A format that is
66: *        simply not this filesystem must fail QUIETLY (probing is normal);
67: *        a recognised-but-unsupported filesystem must fail LOUDLY (pr_err)
68: *        so feature gaps never turn into silent corruption.
69: * open:  resolve path → node.  Returns 0 / negative error.
70: * read:  random-access read; returns bytes read (clamped at EOF) or <0.
71: * write: path-based write (provider may not support it: NULL or -1).
72: * list:  fill buf with space-separated names; returns length, -1 not
73: *        found, -2 not a directory.
74: */
75:struct fs_ops {
76:  const char *name;
77:  int (*mount)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, struct partition *part);
78:  int (*open)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, struct vfs_node *out);
79:  int (*read)(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf,
80:              uint32_t size);
81:  int (*write)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, uint64_t offset,
82:               const void *buf, uint32_t size);
83:  int (*list)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, char *buf,
84:              uint32_t size);
85:  /* unlink: remove the file/node at 'path' (provider may not support it:
86:   * NULL pointer or a negative errno such as -ENOSYS). */
87:  int (*unlink)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path);
88:  /* create: create an empty file/dir at 'path' (type is VFS_TYPE_FILE or
89:   * VFS_TYPE_DIR).  Provider may not support it: NULL pointer or a negative
90:   * errno such as -ENOSYS.  Caller must have already verified 'path' does
91:   * NOT exist (M4.5-FS-WRITE / issue #126). */
92:  int (*create)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, uint32_t type);
93:  /* object_at: map 'path' to the TYPED object it names (the namespace→object
94:   * bridge).  Fill *out and return 0; -1 not found; -2 it is a directory.
95:   * Optional — a NULL object_at means the provider's paths are plain FILE
96:   * objects (ext4, regfs); see vfs_resolve_object's default. */
97:  int (*object_at)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
98:                   struct vfs_objref *out);
99:  /* umount: release fs_private and any provider state for this mount.
100:   * Optional — NULL means the provider holds no teardown state.  Called by
101:   * vfs_umount() AFTER the mount slot is retired (no new operations can
102:   * reach the provider), never with operations in flight. */
103:  int (*umount)(struct vfs_mount *mnt);
104:};
105:
106:struct vfs_mount {
107:  const struct fs_ops *ops;
108:  void *fs_private;        /* provider state, owned by ops->mount */
109:  const char *mountpoint;  /* absolute mount path ("/", "/reg", ...) — Plan 9 namespace */
110:  uint32_t part_index;     /* GPT/MBR partition index backing this mount (0 = synthetic) */
111:  int in_use;
112:  /* Path-based operations in flight on this mount (incremented by the
113:   * dispatchers in vfs.c under mounts_lock, decremented on completion).
114:   * vfs_umount refuses with -EBUSY while non-zero, so a provider can never
115:   * be torn down under a running dispatch (the S-STAB lifetime rule the
116:   * "mounts are never torn down" era did not need). */
117:  volatile int active_ops;
118:};
119:
120:/* Provider registration + mounting (called from the composition root) */
121:int vfs_register_fs(const struct fs_ops *ops) NX_MUST_USE;
122:void vfs_init(void);
123:/* vfs_mount_at - mount a provider at an absolute path (Plan 9-style namespace
124: * mount).  'fs_private' is the provider's state (NULL for a stateless synthetic
125: * server like regfs).  Path resolution routes by LONGEST matching mountpoint;
126: * the root "/" mount is the fallback.  Returns 0, or -1 if the table is full /
127: * args are bad.  Called from the composition root, single-threaded. */
128:int vfs_mount_at(const char *mountpoint, const struct fs_ops *ops, void *fs_private) NX_MUST_USE;
129:
130:/* vfs_umount - retire a NON-root mount by exact mountpoint match.  Fails with
131: * -EBUSY while path operations are in flight on it, -1 if not found or root
132: * ("/" teardown arrives with the ISO-boot rework, PLAN phase 4).  The
133: * provider's optional umount op runs after the slot is retired.  NOTE: a
134: * vfs_node held across umount is the caller's responsibility until the
135: * fd-layer refcount lands (documented limitation, docs/userland-port). */
136:int vfs_umount(const char *mountpoint) NX_MUST_USE;
137:
138:/* vfs_resolve_object - resolve a path to the TYPED capability object it names
139: * (delegates to the provider's object_at, else defaults to a FILE).  Returns 0
140: * with *out filled, -1 not found, -2 it is a directory.  Backs open() ≡
141: * handle_create(OS1_NS_FS): everything resolvable in the namespace is an object. */
142:int vfs_resolve_object(const char *path, struct vfs_objref *out) NX_MUST_USE;
143:
144:/* Core-facing API (the only filesystem surface outside kernel/fs/) */
145:int vfs_open(const char *path, struct vfs_node *out) NX_MUST_USE;
146:int vfs_read(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf, uint32_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
147:/* vfs_read_file: buf==NULL / size==0 returns the file size (legacy internal
148: * helper; userland metadata probes use OBJ_CTL_STAT). */
149:int vfs_read_file(const char *path, void *buf, uint32_t size, uint64_t offset) NX_MUST_USE;
150:/* vfs_write_allowed: THE single write-authority seam (CAP_FS_WRITE + the
151: * /sys,/bin immutable-tree ACL) shared by WRITE/MUTATE-handle acquisition.
152: * Takes a vfs_resolve_path()-canonical
153: * path; returns 0, -EPERM or -EACCES.  (S-ALIGN F6) */
154:int vfs_write_allowed(const char *resolved_path) NX_MUST_USE;
155:int vfs_write_file(const char *path, const void *buf, uint32_t size,
156:                   uint64_t offset) NX_MUST_USE;
157:int vfs_list_dir(const char *path, char *buf, uint32_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
158:int vfs_unlink(const char *path) NX_MUST_USE; /* remove a file/node by path */
159:/* vfs_create - create an empty file/dir at 'path' (VFS_TYPE_FILE/_DIR)
160: * through the responsible mount's provider.  Returns 0, or negative (the
161: * provider has no create support, or its own error).  Does NOT check
162: * write authority or pre-existence - callers (syscall_dispatch.c) must call
163: * vfs_write_allowed()/vfs_stat() first (issue #126). */
164:int vfs_create(const char *path, uint32_t type) NX_MUST_USE;
165:int vfs_stat(const char *path, struct vfs_stat *st) NX_MUST_USE;
166:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/vmm.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/vmm.h
3: * Virtual Memory Manager
4: *
5: * Defines the public API of the VMM and all PTE flag constants for both
6: * AArch64 and AMD64.  The constants are mutually exclusive between arches
7: * via the ARCH_AARCH64 / ARCH_AMD64 preprocessor guards.
8: *
9: * Central invariant (DIRECT MAP, see kernel/memlayout.h):
10: *   phys_to_virt()/virt_to_phys() are a single-offset translation
11: *   (KERNEL_VIRT_BASE; 0 == identity while the higher-half flip is staged).
12: *
13: *   MM-VMM-02 + MM-PMM-07 (contract sweep, Phase B2): every PA-to-pointer
14: *   crossing in the tree goes through that pair — page-table walkers,
15: *   PMM returns/frees, process PGD loads (TTBR0/CR3), user-frame maps,
16: *   virtio DMA addresses, MMIO accessors.  Flipping KERNEL_VIRT_BASE plus
17: *   the boot/linker changes is all that remains for the higher half.
18: *
19: * Known issues (see docs/review/analysis/01-mm-memory-management.md):
20: *   MM-VMM-01 through MM-VMM-07.
21: */
22:#ifndef _KERNEL_VMM_H
23:#define _KERNEL_VMM_H
24:
25:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
26:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
27:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
28:#include <kernel/types.h>
29:
30:/* Virtual Memory Map
31: *
32: * 0x0000_0000_0000_0000 - 0x0000_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF : User Space (256 TB)
33: * 0xFFFF_0000_0000_0000 - 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF : Kernel Space (256 TB)
34: *
35: * MM-VMM-02 RESOLVED: this layout is now LIVE on both arches.  The kernel
36: * image and the direct map of all RAM/MMIO live at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + PA
37: * (memlayout.h); user space owns the low half exclusively (aarch64: TTBR0
38: * per process; amd64: PML4 entries 0..255 private per process).
39: */
40:
41:/* PTE flag constants -- selected by arch at compile time. */
42:#ifdef ARCH_AARCH64
43:/* --- AArch64 Page Table Entry (PTE) Flags --- */
44:/* AArch64 descriptor format and bit details:
45: * AArch64 uses descriptor format: bits [1:0] = 0b11 for page, 0b01 for block.
46: * Attribute index (bits [4:2]) selects the MAIR_EL1 slot (Normal vs Device).
47: * Shareability: bits [9:8]; Inner Shareable = 0b11.
48: * Access flag (AF, bit 10): must be set or a permission fault occurs on first access.
49: * AP bits [7:6]: EL0 read/write access control.
50: * UXN (bit 54): unprivileged execute-never; PXN (bit 53): privileged execute-never. */
51:#define PTE_VALID (1UL << 0)
52:#define PTE_PAGE  (1UL << 1)
53:#define PTE_BLOCK (0UL << 1)
54:
55:#define PTE_AP_EL1_RW (0UL << 6)
56:#define PTE_AP_EL1_RO (2UL << 6)
57:#define PTE_AP_EL0_RW (1UL << 6)
58:#define PTE_AP_EL0_RO (3UL << 6)
59:
60:#define PTE_RW       PTE_AP_EL1_RW
61:#define PTE_USER     PTE_AP_EL0_RW
62:#define PTE_RO       PTE_AP_EL1_RO
63:
64:#define PTE_TABLE    PTE_PAGE
65:
66:/* PTE_IS_TABLE: does this VALID directory entry point to a next-level table?
67: * AArch64: bits[1:0] == 0b11 → table; 0b01 → block. */
68:#define PTE_IS_TABLE(e) (((e) & 0x3UL) == 0x3UL)
69:
70:#define PTE_INNER_SHARE (3UL << 8)
71:#define PTE_AF          (1UL << 10)
72:
73:/* PAGE_KERNEL: kernel RW, not executable (PXN+UXN set).  This is the W^X
74: * default for all RAM (MM-VMM-01 resolved); only the kernel text window is
75: * mapped PAGE_KERNEL_RX by vmm_map_ram_wx(). */
76:#define PAGE_KERNEL \
77:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
78:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RW | PTE_UXN | PTE_PXN)
79:/* PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC: kernel RW + executable.  W^X-violating by definition;
80: * kept only for exceptional uses — no RAM-wide mapping uses it anymore. */
81:#define PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC \
82:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
83:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RW | PTE_UXN)
84:/* PAGE_KERNEL_RX: kernel text — read-only at EL1, executable at EL1 only. */
85:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RX \
86:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
87:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RO | PTE_UXN)
88:/* PAGE_KERNEL_RO: kernel rodata — read-only, never executable. */
89:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RO \
90:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
91:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RO | PTE_UXN | PTE_PXN)
92:/* PAGE_DEVICE: strongly-ordered Device-nGnRnE memory, not executable. */
93:#define PAGE_DEVICE \
94:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_DEVICE) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
95:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RW | PTE_UXN | PTE_PXN)
96:/* PAGE_USER: EL0 (user) RW, not executable at EL1.  EL0-executable: use for
97: * ELF code segments only. */
98:#define PAGE_USER \
99:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
100:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL0_RW | PTE_PXN)
101:/* PAGE_USER_DATA: user RW data (stack/heap) — never executable (W^X). */
102:#define PAGE_USER_DATA (PAGE_USER | PTE_UXN)
103:/* PAGE_USER_RX: user read-only + EL0-executable (ELF text). PXN keeps it
104: * non-executable at EL1 — the kernel must never execute a user page. */
105:#define PAGE_USER_RX \
106:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
107:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL0_RO | PTE_PXN)
108:/* PAGE_USER_RO: user read-only data (ELF rodata) — never executable (W^X). */
109:#define PAGE_USER_RO (PAGE_USER_RX | PTE_UXN)
110:
111:#elif defined(ARCH_AMD64)
112:/* --- AMD64 Page Table Entry (PTE) Flags --- */
113:/* AMD64 bit layout details:
114: * AMD64 uses a simpler flat bit layout; no MAIR equivalent.
115: * PTE_NX (bit 63) requires IA32_EFER.NXE=1 (set by arch init).
116: * NOTE(MM-VMM-01): PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC == PAGE_KERNEL on AMD64 (no NX bit set),
117: * so no W^X enforcement exists on this arch either. */
118:#define PTE_VALID (1UL << 0) 
119:#define PTE_RW    (1UL << 1) 
120:#define PTE_USER  (1UL << 2) 
121:#define PTE_PWT   (1UL << 3) 
122:#define PTE_PCD   (1UL << 4) 
123:#define PTE_AF    (1UL << 5) 
124:#define PTE_DIRTY (1UL << 6) 
125:#define PTE_PS    (1UL << 7) 
126:#define PTE_NX    (1ULL << 63)
127:
128:#define PTE_PAGE  (0UL)
129:#define PTE_RO    (0UL)
130:
131:#define PTE_TABLE (PTE_RW | PTE_USER)
132:
133:/* PTE_IS_TABLE: does this VALID directory entry point to a next-level table?
134: * AMD64: PS (bit 7) clear → table; PS set → 2MB/1GB page.  (PTE_TABLE above
135: * is NOT usable for this test — it is an RW|US flag combo for new tables.) */
136:#define PTE_IS_TABLE(e) (!((e) & PTE_PS))
137:
138:/* W^X page profiles (MM-VMM-01/AMMU-01 resolved).  PTE_NX requires
139: * IA32_EFER.NXE=1, set next to LME in start.S (BSP) and trampoline.S (APs);
140: * CR0.WP is set at boot so the kernel honours read-only PTEs. */
141:#define PAGE_KERNEL      (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW | PTE_NX)
142:#define PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW) /* W+X: no RAM-wide user left */
143:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RX   (PTE_VALID)               /* text: RO + executable */
144:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RO   (PTE_VALID | PTE_NX)      /* rodata: RO, no exec */
145:#define PAGE_DEVICE      (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW | PTE_PCD | PTE_PWT | PTE_NX)
146:#define PAGE_USER        (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW | PTE_USER)
147:/* PAGE_USER_DATA: user RW data (stack/heap) — never executable (W^X). */
148:#define PAGE_USER_DATA   (PAGE_USER | PTE_NX)
149:/* PAGE_USER_RX: user read-only + executable (ELF text). */
150:#define PAGE_USER_RX     (PTE_VALID | PTE_USER)
151:/* PAGE_USER_RO: user read-only data (ELF rodata) — never executable (W^X). */
152:#define PAGE_USER_RO     (PTE_VALID | PTE_USER | PTE_NX)
153:
154:#endif
155:
156:/* --- Architecture-Neutral Attribute Definitions --- */
157:/* PTE_ATTR_INDX selects MAIR_EL1 slot on AArch64; unused on AMD64. */
158:#define PTE_ATTR_NORMAL 0UL
159:#define PTE_ATTR_DEVICE 1UL
160:#define PTE_ATTR_INDX(x) ((uint64_t)(x) << 2)
161:
162:/* Execute-Never Bits (Mapped by Arch MMU) */
163:/* AArch64 only; encoded in bits 54/53 of PTE.
164: * On AMD64, PTE_NX plays this role instead. */
165:#define PTE_UXN (1UL << 54)
166:#define PTE_PXN (1UL << 53)
167:
168:/* VMM Types */
169:typedef uint64_t gva_t;
170:typedef uint64_t gpa_t;
171:typedef uint64_t pte_t;
172:/* typedef aliases for documentation clarity:
173: * gva_t = guest/kernel virtual address
174: * gpa_t = guest/kernel physical address
175: * pte_t = raw page table entry value */
176:
177:/* Address Translation: phys_to_virt()/virt_to_phys() live in
178: * kernel/memlayout.h (single KERNEL_VIRT_BASE offset, identity while the
179: * offset is 0).  Included above so all existing users keep compiling. */
180:
181:/* vmm_create_pgd: allocate a new process PGD with kernel half pre-filled. */
182:uint64_t *vmm_create_pgd(void);
183:uint64_t arch_vmm_create_process_pgd(void);
184:/* vmm_destroy_pgd: free the process-private page-table pages AND the user
185: * RAM frames (PTEs carrying PTE_USER) of 'pgd' (MM-VMM-04 resolved).
186: * Entries shared with kernel_pgd (compared by value) are never touched. */
187:void vmm_destroy_pgd(uint64_t *pgd);
188:
189:/* vmm_init: phase-1 MMU bring-up; maps 128 MB bootstrap window; enables MMU. */
190:void vmm_init(void);
191:/* vmm_dynamic_remap: phase-2; maps all detected RAM; switches to new PGD.
192: * NOTE(MM-VMM-03): leaks bootstrap PGD; no IPI to secondary CPUs.
193: * NOTE(MM-VMM-01): maps all RAM PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC; no W^X. */
194:void vmm_dynamic_remap(void);
195:/* vmm_map_page: map one 4KB page; delegates to arch_vmm_map(). */
196:int vmm_map_page(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
197:/* vmm_unmap_page: unmap one page with cross-CPU TLB shootdown (MM-VMM-05
198: * resolved): on return no online CPU translates 'virt' via the old entry. */
199:void vmm_unmap_page(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt);
200:/* vmm_protect: rewrite the attributes of existing mappings in [virt,
201: * virt+size) to the given PAGE/PTE profile (AMMU-02 resolved).  Frame
202: * addresses are preserved; large pages are split for 4KB precision; ends
203: * with a cross-CPU TLB shootdown.  Returns 0, or -1 on a hole in range. */
204:int vmm_protect(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
205:uint64_t vmm_get_phys(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt);
206:
207:struct process;
208:/* vmm_map_page_locked: vmm_map_page wrapped with proc->mm_lock. */
209:int vmm_map_page_locked(struct process *proc, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
210:/* vmm_unmap_page_locked: vmm_unmap_page wrapped with proc->mm_lock. */
211:void vmm_unmap_page_locked(struct process *proc, uint64_t virt);
212:
213:/* vmm_map: map a contiguous range; 4KB pages only; partial on error (no rollback). */
214:int vmm_map(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
215:/* vmm_map_ram_wx: map a usable RAM range at its direct-map VA with the W^X
216: * split: kernel text RX, rodata RO+NX, everything else RW+NX
217: * (MM-VMM-01/AMMU-01). */
218:void vmm_map_ram_wx(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
219:/* vmm_check_range: verify all pages in range are mapped with required flags. */
220:int vmm_check_range(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags_mask) NX_MUST_USE;
221:
222:/*
223: * vmm_is_user_addr - return true if 'addr' falls in the user virtual range.
224: *
225: * Checks that addr >= 0x1000 (excludes NULL page) and that the top 16 bits
226: * are zero (canonical user-space addresses in a 48-bit VA space).
227: * Used by syscall handlers to validate user pointers before access.
228: */
229:static inline bool vmm_is_user_addr(uint64_t addr) {
230:  return (addr >= 0x1000) && ((addr & 0xFFFF000000000000ULL) == 0);
231:}

234:#include <kernel/hal_uaccess.h>
235:#define vmm_copy_from_user(dest, src, n) arch_copy_from_user(dest, src, n)
236:#define vmm_copy_to_user(dest, src, n) arch_copy_to_user(dest, src, n)
237:/* TOLERANT copy: truncation is accepted.  Where a shortened string would be a
238: * DIFFERENT string (paths, registry keys/values, environment), use
239: * hal_copy_string_from_user_strict() instead — see kernel/hal_uaccess.h. */
240:#define vmm_copy_string_from_user(dest, src, max_len) hal_copy_string_from_user(dest, src, max_len)
241:#define vmm_copy_string_from_user_strict(dest, src, max_len) hal_copy_string_from_user_strict(dest, src, max_len)

@@@ user/arch/aarch64/syscall.S @@@
1:/*
2: * user/syscall.S
3: * AArch64 System Call Wrappers
4: *
5: * Implements the ABI:
6: * x8: Syscall Number
7: * x0-x5: Arguments
8: * svc #0: Trap to Kernel
9: */
10:/* Syscall numbers come from the shared ABI header (ABI-01/ABI-SYS-01):
11: * the same macros the kernel dispatch switch compiles against. */
12:#include <syscall_nums.h>
13:
14:.text
15:.global _start
16:_start:
17:    /* SP is already set by kernel */
18:    bl main
19:    /* Exit with main's return value */
20:    bl exit
21:    /* Should never reach here */
22:1:  b 1b
23:
24:.global _sys_open
25:.global _sys_close
26:.global _sys_lseek
27:.global _sys_read
28:.global _sys_write
29:.global _sys_get_pid
30:.global _sys_exit
31:.global _sys_get_time
32:.global _sys_spawn
33:.global _sys_spawn_redir
34:.global _sys_spawn_caps
35:.global _sys_kill
36:.global _sys_wait
37:.global _sys_yield
38:.global _sys_nanosleep
39:.global _sys_clock_gettime
40:.global _sys_send
41:.global _sys_recv
42:.global _sys_draw
43:.global _sys_create_window
44:.global _sys_window_draw
45:.global _sys_window_write
46:.global _sys_window_of_pid
47:.global _sys_window_blit
48:.global _sys_compositor_render
49:.global _sys_set_font
50:.global _sys_stat
51:
52:/* 
53: * Generic Syscall Wrapper Macros could be used, but manual is clearer for now
54: */
55:
56:/* int _sys_open(const char *path, int flags) */
57:_sys_open:
58:    mov x8, #SYS_OPEN
59:    svc #0
60:    ret
61:
62:/* int _sys_close(int fd) */
63:_sys_close:
64:    mov x8, #SYS_CLOSE
65:    svc #0
66:    ret
67:
68:/* long _sys_lseek(int fd, long off, int whence) */
69:_sys_lseek:
70:    mov x8, #SYS_LSEEK
71:    svc #0
72:    ret
73:
74:/* long _sys_read(int fd, char *buf, unsigned long count) */
75:/* x0=fd, x1=buf, x2=count */
76:_sys_read:
77:    mov x8, #SYS_READ
78:    svc #0
79:    ret
80:
81:/* void _sys_write(int fd, const char *buf, size_t count) */
82:_sys_write:
83:    mov x8, #SYS_WRITE
84:    svc #0
85:    ret
86:
87:/* long _sys_get_time(void) */
88:_sys_get_time:
89:    mov x8, #SYS_GET_TIME
90:    svc #0
91:    ret
92:
93:/* int _sys_get_pid(void) */
94:_sys_get_pid:
95:    mov x8, #SYS_GETPID
96:    svc #0
97:    ret
98:
99:/* void _sys_exit(int status) */
100:_sys_exit:
101:    mov x8, #SYS_EXIT
102:    svc #0
103:    ret
104:
105:/* int _sys_spawn(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[], uint flags)
106: * The kernel now also reads arg4/arg5 (fd-redirection list + count, Phase 4);
107: * a plain spawn has none, so ZERO x4/x5 here — otherwise leftover register
108: * values would be misread as a redirection array. */
109:_sys_spawn:
110:    mov x4, #0
111:    mov x5, #0
112:    mov x8, #SYS_SPAWN
113:    svc #0
114:    ret
115:
116:/* long _sys_spawn_redir(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[],
117: *                       uint flags, const struct spawn_redir *redir, int n)
118: * Same SYS_SPAWN, but x4/x5 carry the redirection list — pass them through. */
119:_sys_spawn_redir:
120:    mov x8, #SYS_SPAWN
121:    svc #0
122:    ret
123:
124:/* long _sys_spawn_caps(const char *path, int level, unsigned long caps) */
125:_sys_spawn_caps:
126:    mov x8, #SYS_SPAWN_CAPS
127:    svc #0
128:    ret
129:
130:/* int _sys_kill(int pid) */
131:_sys_kill:
132:    mov x8, #SYS_KILL
133:    svc #0
134:    ret
135:
136:/* int _sys_wait(int pid)
137: * The kernel now also reads arg1 (an OPTIONAL user int* for the exit status,
138: * Phase 9b); this form has none, so ZERO x1 here.  x1 is a scratch register
139: * with undefined contents at a one-argument call, so leftover values would be
140: * misread as a status pointer and the kernel would write four bytes into a
141: * semi-random address in the caller's own address space.  Exactly the hazard
142: * _sys_spawn zeroes x4/x5 for. */
143:_sys_wait:
144:    mov x1, #0
145:    mov x8, #SYS_WAIT
146:    svc #0
147:    ret
148:
149:/* int _sys_wait_status(int pid, int *code) — same SYS_WAIT, arg1 = status out */
150:.global _sys_wait_status
151:_sys_wait_status:
152:    mov x8, #SYS_WAIT
153:    svc #0
154:    ret
155:
156:/* void _sys_yield(void) */
157:_sys_yield:
158:    mov x8, #SYS_YIELD
159:    svc #0
160:    ret

434:.global setjmp
435:setjmp:
436:    /* x0 contains the address of jmp_buf */
437:    /* Save callee-saved registers x19-x29 */
438:    stp x19, x20, [x0, #0]
439:    stp x21, x22, [x0, #16]
440:    stp x23, x24, [x0, #32]
441:    stp x25, x26, [x0, #48]
442:    stp x27, x28, [x0, #64]
443:    str x29,      [x0, #80]
444:    /* Save SP (x31) and LR (x30) */
445:    mov x9, sp
446:    str x9,      [x0, #88]
447:    str x30,     [x0, #96]
448:    /* Return 0 */
449:    mov x0, #0
450:    ret
451:
452:.global longjmp
453:longjmp:
454:    /* x0 contains the address of jmp_buf, x1 contains the val */
455:    /* Restore callee-saved registers x19-x29 */
456:    ldp x19, x20, [x0, #0]
457:    ldp x21, x22, [x0, #16]
458:    ldp x23, x24, [x0, #32]
459:    ldp x25, x26, [x0, #48]
460:    ldp x27, x28, [x0, #64]
461:    ldr x29,      [x0, #80]
462:    /* Restore SP and LR */
463:    ldr x9,      [x0, #88]
464:    mov sp, x9
465:    ldr x30,     [x0, #96]
466:    /* If val is 0, return 1; else return val */
467:    mov w0, #1
468:    cmp w1, #0
469:    csel w0, w1, w0, ne
470:    ret
471:
472:/* int _sys_stat(const char *path, struct abi_stat *out) */
473:_sys_stat:
474:    mov x8, #SYS_STAT
475:    svc #0
476:    ret
477:

@@@ user/arch/amd64/syscall.S @@@
1:/*
2: * user/arch/amd64/syscall.S
3: * x86-64 System Call Wrappers
4: *
5: * ABI:
6: *   RAX: syscall number
7: *   RDI, RSI, RDX, R10, R8, R9: arguments (R10 replaces RCX)
8: *   syscall instruction traps to kernel
9: */
10:/* Syscall numbers come from the shared ABI header (ABI-01/ABI-SYS-01):
11: * the same macros the kernel dispatch switch compiles against. */
12:#include <syscall_nums.h>
13:
14:.text
15:.global _start
16:_start:
17:    /* SP is already set by kernel ELF loader */
18:    call main
19:    /* Exit with main's return value */
20:    movq %rax, %rdi
21:    call _sys_exit
22:1:  hlt
23:    jmp 1b
24:
25:.global _sys_open
26:_sys_open:
27:    movq $SYS_OPEN, %rax
28:    syscall
29:    ret
30:
31:.global _sys_close
32:_sys_close:
33:    movq $SYS_CLOSE, %rax
34:    syscall
35:    ret
36:

38:_sys_lseek:
39:    movq $SYS_LSEEK, %rax
40:    syscall
41:    ret

44:_sys_read:
45:    movq $SYS_READ, %rax
46:    syscall
47:    ret

50:_sys_write:
51:    movq $SYS_WRITE, %rax
52:    syscall
53:    ret
54:

57:    movq $SYS_GET_TIME, %rax
58:    syscall
59:    ret
60:

64:    syscall

68:_sys_exit:
69:    movq $SYS_EXIT, %rax
70:    syscall

73:.global _sys_spawn
74:_sys_spawn:
75:    movq $SYS_SPAWN, %rax
76:    movq %rcx, %r10   /* arg3: spawn-mode flags (SPAWN_FLAG_*, #193) */
77:    /* The kernel now also reads arg4/arg5 (fd-redirection list + count,
78:     * Phase 4); a plain spawn has none, so ZERO r8/r9 — otherwise leftover
79:     * register values would be misread as a redirection array. */
80:    xorq %r8, %r8
81:    xorq %r9, %r9
82:    syscall
83:    ret
84:
85:.global _sys_spawn_redir
86:/* long _sys_spawn_redir(path, argc, argv, flags, redir, n) — same SYS_SPAWN,
87: * but r8/r9 carry the redirection list (arg4/arg5); pass them through. */
88:_sys_spawn_redir:
89:    movq $SYS_SPAWN, %rax
90:    movq %rcx, %r10   /* arg3: spawn-mode flags */
91:    syscall
92:    ret
93:
94:.global _sys_spawn_caps
95:_sys_spawn_caps:
96:    movq $SYS_SPAWN_CAPS, %rax
97:    movq %rcx, %r10   /* arg3: spawn-mode flags (SPAWN_FLAG_*, #193) */
98:    syscall
99:    ret
100:
101:.global _sys_kill
102:_sys_kill:
103:    movq $SYS_KILL, %rax
104:    syscall
105:    ret
106:
107:.global _sys_wait
108:_sys_wait:
109:    movq $SYS_WAIT, %rax
110:    /* The kernel now also reads arg1 (an OPTIONAL user int* for the exit
111:     * status, Phase 9b); this form has none, so ZERO rsi.  rsi is a scratch
112:     * register with undefined contents at a one-argument call, so a leftover
113:     * value would be misread as a status pointer and the kernel would write
114:     * four bytes into a semi-random address in the caller's own address space.
115:     * Exactly the hazard _sys_spawn zeroes r8/r9 for. */
116:    xorq %rsi, %rsi
117:    syscall
118:    ret
119:

123:    syscall
124:    ret

411:.global setjmp
412:setjmp:
413:    /* rdi contains the address of jmp_buf */
414:    movq %rbx, 0(%rdi)
415:    movq %rbp, 8(%rdi)
416:    movq %r12, 16(%rdi)
417:    movq %r13, 24(%rdi)
418:    movq %r14, 32(%rdi)
419:    movq %r15, 40(%rdi)
420:    /* Save stack pointer (rsp) as it was BEFORE the call */
421:    leaq 8(%rsp), %rax
422:    movq %rax, 48(%rdi)
423:    /* Save return address (rip) */
424:    movq (%rsp), %rax
425:    movq %rax, 56(%rdi)
426:    /* Return 0 */
427:    xorl %eax, %eax
428:    ret
429:
430:.global longjmp
431:longjmp:
432:    /* rdi contains the address of jmp_buf, rsi contains the val */
433:    movq 0(%rdi), %rbx
434:    movq 8(%rdi), %rbp
435:    movq 16(%rdi), %r12
436:    movq 24(%rdi), %r13
437:    movq 32(%rdi), %r14
438:    movq 40(%rdi), %r15
439:    /* Restore stack pointer */
440:    movq 48(%rdi), %rsp
441:    /* Jump to return address (rip) */
442:    movq 56(%rdi), %rdx
443:    /* If val is 0, return 1; else return val */
444:    movl %esi, %eax
445:    testl %eax, %eax
446:    jnz 1f
447:    movl $1, %eax
448:1:
449:    jmp *%rdx
450:
451:/* int _sys_stat(const char *path, struct abi_stat *out) */
452:.global _sys_stat
453:_sys_stat:
454:    movq $SYS_STAT, %rax
455:    syscall
456:    ret
457:

1:/* Kilo -- A very simple editor in less than 1-kilo lines of code (as counted
2: *         by "cloc"). Originally emitted VT100 escapes directly to a real
3: *         terminal via termios.
4: *
5: * -----------------------------------------------------------------------
6: * OS1/NEXS PORT
7: * -----------------------------------------------------------------------
8: * This is a port of antirez's "kilo" to the OS1/NEXS userspace API
9: * (<os1.h>, <graphics.h>, <posix_types.h>, <syscall_nums.h>).
10: *
11: * Porting strategy (deliberately minimal — see notes at EOF):
12: *
13: *   1. INPUT:  kilo's editorReadKey() already works as a blocking
14: *      byte-stream read() on fd 0. OS1's read(0, buf, count) gives us
15: *      exactly that (stdin = keyboard stream for our own window), so the
16: *      core key-reading / escape-sequence-decoding logic is UNCHANGED.
17: *
18: *   2. OUTPUT: kilo's editorRefreshScreen() builds one big VT100/ANSI
19: *      escape buffer and writes it with a single write(). OS1's
20: *      write(1, buf, count) routes to "own window" (per os1.h), whose
21: *      backing terminal emulator in the compositor understands cursor
22: *      positioning + xterm-style SGR color codes. So the *rendering*
23: *      logic is also UNCHANGED — only the syscalls underneath differ.
24: *
25: *   3. SCREEN SIZE: there is no ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ) / SIGWINCH in OS1.
26: *      We create our own window with create_window() at a fixed pixel
27: *      size and derive screenrows/screencols from the terminal cell
28: *      size (CELL_W x CELL_H below). No live resize support.
29: *
30: *   4. FILES: editorOpen() reads the whole file with fopen/fseek/fread and
31: *      splits it into lines itself (no getline()). editorSave() writes the
32: *      whole buffer in one shot via file_write(), OS1's create-or-overwrite
33: *      helper: a from-start write truncates the file to exactly the buffer
34: *      length on the FS side (ext4_write), so shortening a file saves
35: *      correctly. (open() supports O_CREAT/O_TRUNC now too, but the
36: *      whole-file write is simpler here.)
37: *
38: *   5. MISC: no termios, no signal(), no errno/strerror/perror, no
39: *      ctype.h, no time(). Tiny local shims are provided below.
40: *
41: * Everything else — the row/buffer model, syntax highlighting, search,
42: * cursor movement, keypress dispatch — is the original kilo logic,
43: * untouched.
44: * -----------------------------------------------------------------------
45: *
46: * Copyright (C) 2016 Salvatore Sanfilippo <antirez at gmail dot com>
47: *
48: * All rights reserved.
49: *
50: * Redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without
51: * modification, are permitted provided that the following conditions are
52: * met:
53: *
54: *  *  Redistributions of source code must retain the above copyright
55: *     notice, this list of conditions and the following disclaimer.
56: *
57: *  *  Redistributions in binary form must reproduce the above copyright
58: *     notice, this list of conditions and the following disclaimer in the
59: *     documentation and/or other materials provided with the distribution.
60: *
61: * THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED BY THE COPYRIGHT HOLDERS AND CONTRIBUTORS
62: * "AS IS" AND ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT
63: * LIMITED TO, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR
64: * A PARTICULAR PURPOSE ARE DISCLAIMED. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT
65: * HOLDER OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL,
66: * SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES (INCLUDING, BUT NOT
67: * LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; LOSS OF USE,
68: * DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON ANY
69: * THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT
70: * (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE
71: * OF THIS SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE.
72: */

86:/* fd numbers for the "own window" stdio model (os1.h: 0=stdin, 1/2=own
87: * window). Kept as named constants so the body of kilo below reads the
88: * same as upstream. */
89:#define STDIN_FILENO 0
90:#define STDOUT_FILENO 1

92:/* --- ctype.h shim (only the three predicates kilo actually uses) --- */
93:static int os1_isspace(int c) {
94:  return c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\n' || c == '\r' || c == '\f' ||
95:         c == '\v';
96:}
97:static int os1_isdigit(int c) { return c >= '0' && c <= '9'; }
98:static int os1_isprint(int c) { return c >= 32 && c < 127; }
99:#define isspace os1_isspace

103:/* --- terminal cell geometry ---------------------------------------------
104: * The compositor's text/terminal renderer is bitmap-font based. These two
105: * values are the pixel size of one character cell; adjust them to match
106: * the actual font used by the window terminal emulator on your build.
107: * 8x16 is the common default for VGA-style bitmap fonts. */
108:#define CELL_W 8
109:#define CELL_H 16
110:
111:/* Window geometry: 80x25 "terminal" -> pixel size. */
112:#define WIN_COLS 80
113:#define WIN_ROWS 25
114:#define WIN_X 40
115:#define WIN_Y 40
116:#define WIN_W (WIN_COLS * CELL_W)
117:#define WIN_H (WIN_ROWS * CELL_H)

125:#define HL_NORMAL 0
126:#define HL_NONPRINT 1
127:#define HL_COMMENT 2   /* Single line comment. */
128:#define HL_MLCOMMENT 3 /* Multi-line comment. */

210:/* =========================== Syntax highlights DB =========================
211: *
212: * In order to add a new syntax, define two arrays with a list of file name
213: * matches and keywords. The file name matches are used in order to match
214: * a given syntax with a given file name: if a match pattern starts with a
215: * dot, it is matched as the last past of the filename, for example ".c".
216: * Otherwise the pattern is just searched inside the filenme, like "Makefile").
217: *
218: * The list of keywords to highlight is just a list of words, however if they
219: * a trailing '|' character is added at the end, they are highlighted in
220: * a different color, so that you can have two different sets of keywords.
221: *
222: * Finally add a stanza in the HLDB global variable with two two arrays
223: * of strings, and a set of flags in order to enable highlighting of
224: * comments and numbers.
225: *
226: * The characters for single and multi line comments must be exactly two
227: * and must be provided as well (see the C language example).
228: *
229: * There is no support to highlight patterns currently. */
230:
231:/* C / C++ */
232:static const char *C_HL_extensions[] = {".c",   ".h",  ".cpp",
233:                                        ".hpp", ".cc", NULL};
234:static const char *C_HL_keywords[] = {
235:    /* C Keywords */
236:    "auto", "break", "case", "continue", "default", "do", "else", "enum",
237:    "extern", "for", "goto", "if", "register", "return", "sizeof", "static",
238:    "struct", "switch", "typedef", "union", "volatile", "while", "NULL",
239:
240:    /* C++ Keywords */
241:    "alignas", "alignof", "and", "and_eq", "asm", "bitand", "bitor", "class",
242:    "compl", "constexpr", "const_cast", "deltype", "delete", "dynamic_cast",
243:    "explicit", "export", "false", "friend", "inline", "mutable", "namespace",
244:    "new", "noexcept", "not", "not_eq", "nullptr", "operator", "or", "or_eq",
245:    "private", "protected", "public", "reinterpret_cast", "static_assert",
246:    "static_cast", "template", "this", "thread_local", "throw", "true", "try",
247:    "typeid", "typename", "virtual", "xor", "xor_eq",
248:
249:    /* C types */
250:    "int|", "long|", "double|", "float|", "char|", "unsigned|", "signed|",
251:    "void|", "short|", "auto|", "const|", "bool|", NULL};
252:
253:/* Here we define an array of syntax highlights by extensions, keywords,
254: * comments delimiters and flags. */
255:static struct editorSyntax HLDB[] = {
256:    {/* C / C++ */
257:     C_HL_extensions, C_HL_keywords, "//", "/*", "*/",
258:     HL_HIGHLIGHT_STRINGS | HL_HIGHLIGHT_NUMBERS}};
259:
260:#define HLDB_ENTRIES (sizeof(HLDB) / sizeof(HLDB[0]))
261:
262:/* ======================= Low level input handling ========================= */
263:/* (Upstream had termios raw-mode setup here. OS1 windows already deliver
264: *  a raw, unbuffered keystream on fd 0 to the focused window, so there is
265: *  nothing to enable/disable -- this section is intentionally empty.) */
266:
267:/* Read one logical key, blocking until something arrives.
268: *
269: * OS1 PORT: instead of a raw byte stream + ESC-sequence decoding, we use the
270: * unified input abstraction (input_poll_event, <input.h>).  Special keys carry
271: * an evdev scancode with an ASCII byte of 0, so arrows/Enter/Backspace/Tab/Esc
272: * are matched on scancode; printable characters and Ctrl-folded control codes
273: * (Ctrl-S/Q/F, delivered by the keyboard driver as 0x01..0x1A) arrive as the
274: * ASCII .key byte.  Releases are ignored; we yield() while idle. */
275:static int editorReadKey(int fd) {
276:  (void)fd;
277:  input_event_t ev;
278:
279:  while (1) {
280:    while (input_poll_event(&ev)) {
281:      if (ev.type != INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD)
282:        continue;
283:      if (ev.keyboard.state == KEY_RELEASED)
284:        continue; /* press or repeat only */
285:
286:      switch (ev.keyboard.scancode) {
287:      case INPUT_KEY_UP:
288:        return ARROW_UP;
289:      case INPUT_KEY_DOWN:
290:        return ARROW_DOWN;
291:      case INPUT_KEY_LEFT:
292:        return ARROW_LEFT;
293:      case INPUT_KEY_RIGHT:
294:        return ARROW_RIGHT;
295:      case INPUT_KEY_BACKSPACE:
296:        return BACKSPACE;
297:      case INPUT_KEY_ENTER:
298:        return ENTER;
299:      case INPUT_KEY_TAB:
300:        return TAB;
301:      case INPUT_KEY_ESC:
302:        return ESC;
303:      default:
304:        break;
305:      }
306:
307:      unsigned char c = ev.keyboard.key;
308:      if (c == '\r' || c == '\n')
309:        return ENTER; /* normalise LF/CR to kilo's ENTER (13) */
310:      if (c == 127)
311:        return BACKSPACE;
312:      if (c != 0)
313:        return c; /* printable, or Ctrl-x control code */
314:    }
315:    yield();
316:  }
317:}
318:
319:/* ====================== Syntax highlight color scheme  ==================== */
320:
321:static int is_separator(int c) {
322:  return c == '\0' || isspace(c) || strchr(",.()+-/*=~%[];", c) != NULL;
323:}
324:
325:/* Return true if the specified row last char is part of a multi line comment
326: * that starts at this row or at one before, and does not end at the end
327: * of the row but spawns to the next row. */
328:static int editorRowHasOpenComment(erow *row) {
329:  if (row->hl && row->rsize && row->hl[row->rsize - 1] == HL_MLCOMMENT &&
330:      (row->rsize < 2 || (row->render[row->rsize - 2] != '*' ||
331:                          row->render[row->rsize - 1] != '/')))
332:    return 1;
333:  return 0;
334:}
335:
336:/* Set every byte of row->hl (that corresponds to every character in the line)
337: * to the right syntax highlight type (HL_* defines). */
338:static void editorUpdateSyntax(erow *row) {
339:  row->hl = realloc(row->hl, row->rsize);
340:  memset(row->hl, HL_NORMAL, row->rsize);
341:
342:  if (E.syntax == NULL)
343:    return; /* No syntax, everything is HL_NORMAL. */
344:
345:  int i, prev_sep, in_string, in_comment;
346:  char *p;
347:  const char **keywords = E.syntax->keywords;
348:  char *scs = E.syntax->singleline_comment_start;
349:  char *mcs = E.syntax->multiline_comment_start;
350:  char *mce = E.syntax->multiline_comment_end;
351:
352:  /* Point to the first non-space char. */
353:  p = row->render;
354:  i = 0; /* Current char offset */
355:  while (*p && isspace(*p)) {
356:    p++;
357:    i++;
358:  }
359:  prev_sep = 1;   /* Tell the parser if 'i' points to start of word. */
360:  in_string = 0;  /* Are we inside "" or '' ? */
361:  in_comment = 0; /* Are we inside multi-line comment? */
362:
363:  /* If the previous line has an open comment, this line starts
364:   * with an open comment state. */
365:  if (row->idx > 0 && editorRowHasOpenComment(&E.row[row->idx - 1]))
366:    in_comment = 1;
367:
368:  while (*p) {
369:    /* Handle // comments. */
370:    if (prev_sep && *p == scs[0] && *(p + 1) == scs[1]) {
371:      /* From here to end is a comment */
372:      memset(row->hl + i, HL_COMMENT, row->size - i);
373:      return;
374:    }
375:
376:    /* Handle multi line comments. */
377:    if (in_comment) {
378:      row->hl[i] = HL_MLCOMMENT;
379:      if (*p == mce[0] && *(p + 1) == mce[1]) {
380:        row->hl[i + 1] = HL_MLCOMMENT;
381:        p += 2;
382:        i += 2;
383:        in_comment = 0;
384:        prev_sep = 1;
385:        continue;
386:      } else {
387:        prev_sep = 0;
388:        p++;
389:        i++;
390:        continue;
391:      }
392:    } else if (*p == mcs[0] && *(p + 1) == mcs[1]) {
393:      row->hl[i] = HL_MLCOMMENT;
394:      row->hl[i + 1] = HL_MLCOMMENT;
395:      p += 2;
396:      i += 2;
397:      in_comment = 1;
398:      prev_sep = 0;
399:      continue;
400:    }
401:
402:    /* Handle "" and '' */
403:    if (in_string) {
404:      row->hl[i] = HL_STRING;
405:      if (*p == '\\') {
406:        row->hl[i + 1] = HL_STRING;
407:        p += 2;
408:        i += 2;
409:        prev_sep = 0;
410:        continue;
411:      }
412:      if (*p == in_string)
413:        in_string = 0;
414:      p++;
415:      i++;
416:      continue;
417:    } else {
418:      if (*p == '"' || *p == '\'') {
419:        in_string = *p;
420:        row->hl[i] = HL_STRING;
421:        p++;
422:        i++;
423:        prev_sep = 0;
424:        continue;
425:      }
426:    }
427:
428:    /* Handle non printable chars. */
429:    if (!isprint(*p)) {
430:      row->hl[i] = HL_NONPRINT;
431:      p++;
432:      i++;
433:      prev_sep = 0;
434:      continue;
435:    }
436:
437:    /* Handle numbers */
438:    if ((isdigit(*p) && (prev_sep || row->hl[i - 1] == HL_NUMBER)) ||
439:        (*p == '.' && i > 0 && row->hl[i - 1] == HL_NUMBER)) {
440:      row->hl[i] = HL_NUMBER;
441:      p++;
442:      i++;
443:      prev_sep = 0;
444:      continue;
445:    }
446:
447:    /* Handle keywords and lib calls */
448:    if (prev_sep) {
449:      int j;
450:      for (j = 0; keywords[j]; j++) {
451:        int klen = strlen(keywords[j]);
452:        int kw2 = keywords[j][klen - 1] == '|';
453:        if (kw2)
454:          klen--;
455:
456:        if (!memcmp(p, keywords[j], klen) && is_separator(*(p + klen))) {
457:          /* Keyword */
458:          memset(row->hl + i, kw2 ? HL_KEYWORD2 : HL_KEYWORD1, klen);
459:          p += klen;
460:          i += klen;
461:          break;
462:        }
463:      }
464:      if (keywords[j] != NULL) {
465:        prev_sep = 0;
466:        continue; /* We had a keyword match */
467:      }
468:    }
469:
470:    /* Not special chars */
471:    prev_sep = is_separator(*p);
472:    p++;
473:    i++;
474:  }
475:
476:  /* Propagate syntax change to the next row if the open commen
477:   * state changed. This may recursively affect all the following rows
478:   * in the file. */
479:  int oc = editorRowHasOpenComment(row);
480:  if (row->hl_oc != oc && row->idx + 1 < E.numrows)
481:    editorUpdateSyntax(&E.row[row->idx + 1]);
482:  row->hl_oc = oc;
483:}
484:
485:/* Maps syntax highlight token types to terminal colors. */
486:static int editorSyntaxToColor(int hl) {
487:  switch (hl) {
488:  case HL_COMMENT:
489:  case HL_MLCOMMENT:
490:    return 36; /* cyan */
491:  case HL_KEYWORD1:
492:    return 33; /* yellow */
493:  case HL_KEYWORD2:
494:    return 32; /* green */
495:  case HL_STRING:
496:    return 35; /* magenta */
497:  case HL_NUMBER:
498:    return 31; /* red */
499:  case HL_MATCH:
500:    return 34; /* blu */
501:  default:
502:    return 37; /* white */
503:  }
504:}
505:
506:/* Select the syntax highlight scheme depending on the filename,
507: * setting it in the global state E.syntax. */
508:static void editorSelectSyntaxHighlight(char *filename) {
509:  for (unsigned int j = 0; j < HLDB_ENTRIES; j++) {
510:    struct editorSyntax *s = HLDB + j;
511:    unsigned int i = 0;
512:    while (s->filematch[i]) {
513:      char *p;
514:      int patlen = strlen(s->filematch[i]);
515:      if ((p = strstr(filename, s->filematch[i])) != NULL) {
516:        if (s->filematch[i][0] != '.' || p[patlen] == '\0') {
517:          E.syntax = s;
518:          return;
519:        }
520:      }
521:      i++;
522:    }
523:  }
524:}
525:
526:/* ======================= Editor rows implementation ======================= */
527:
528:/* Update the rendered version and the syntax highlight of a row. */
529:static void editorUpdateRow(erow *row) {
530:  unsigned int tabs = 0, nonprint = 0;
531:  int j, idx;
532:
533:  /* Create a version of the row we can directly print on the screen,
534:   * respecting tabs, substituting non printable characters with '?'. */
535:  free(row->render);
536:  for (j = 0; j < row->size; j++)
537:    if (row->chars[j] == TAB)
538:      tabs++;
539:
540:  unsigned long long allocsize =
541:      (unsigned long long)row->size + tabs * 8 + nonprint * 9 + 1;
542:  if (allocsize > UINT32_MAX) {
543:    printf("Some line of the edited file is too long for kilo\n");
544:    exit(1);
545:  }
546:
547:  row->render = malloc(row->size + tabs * 8 + nonprint * 9 + 1);
548:  idx = 0;
549:  for (j = 0; j < row->size; j++) {
550:    if (row->chars[j] == TAB) {
551:      row->render[idx++] = ' ';
552:      while ((idx + 1) % 8 != 0)
553:        row->render[idx++] = ' ';
554:    } else {
555:      row->render[idx++] = row->chars[j];
556:    }
557:  }
558:  row->rsize = idx;
559:  row->render[idx] = '\0';
560:
561:  /* Update the syntax highlighting attributes of the row. */
562:  editorUpdateSyntax(row);
563:}
564:
565:/* Insert a row at the specified position, shifting the other rows on the bottom
566: * if required. */
567:static void editorInsertRow(int at, const char *s, size_t len) {
568:  if (at > E.numrows)
569:    return;
570:  E.row = realloc(E.row, sizeof(erow) * (E.numrows + 1));
571:  if (at != E.numrows) {
572:    memmove(E.row + at + 1, E.row + at, sizeof(E.row[0]) * (E.numrows - at));
573:    for (int j = at + 1; j <= E.numrows; j++)
574:      E.row[j].idx++;
575:  }
576:  E.row[at].size = len;
577:  E.row[at].chars = malloc(len + 1);
578:  memcpy(E.row[at].chars, s, len);
579:  E.row[at].chars[len] = '\0';
580:  E.row[at].hl = NULL;
581:  E.row[at].hl_oc = 0;
582:  E.row[at].render = NULL;
583:  E.row[at].rsize = 0;
584:  E.row[at].idx = at;
585:  editorUpdateRow(E.row + at);
586:  E.numrows++;
587:  E.dirty++;
588:}
589:
590:/* Free row's heap allocated stuff. */
591:static void editorFreeRow(erow *row) {
592:  free(row->render);
593:  free(row->chars);
594:  free(row->hl);
595:}
596:
597:/* Remove the row at the specified position, shifting the remainign on the
598: * top. */
599:static void editorDelRow(int at) {
600:  erow *row;
601:
602:  if (at >= E.numrows)
603:    return;
604:  row = E.row + at;
605:  editorFreeRow(row);
606:  memmove(E.row + at, E.row + at + 1, sizeof(E.row[0]) * (E.numrows - at - 1));
607:  for (int j = at; j < E.numrows - 1; j++)
608:    E.row[j].idx++;
609:  E.numrows--;
610:  E.dirty++;
611:}
612:
613:/* Turn the editor rows into a single heap-allocated string.
614: * Returns the pointer to the heap-allocated string and populate the
615: * integer pointed by 'buflen' with the size of the string, escluding
616: * the final nulterm. */
617:static char *editorRowsToString(int *buflen) {
618:  char *buf = NULL, *p;
619:  int totlen = 0;
620:  int j;
621:
622:  /* Compute count of bytes */
623:  for (j = 0; j < E.numrows; j++)
624:    totlen += E.row[j].size + 1; /* +1 is for "\n" at end of every row */
625:  *buflen = totlen;
626:  totlen++; /* Also make space for nulterm */
627:
628:  p = buf = malloc(totlen);
629:  for (j = 0; j < E.numrows; j++) {
630:    memcpy(p, E.row[j].chars, E.row[j].size);
631:    p += E.row[j].size;
632:    *p = '\n';
633:    p++;
634:  }
635:  *p = '\0';
636:  return buf;
637:}
638:
639:/* Insert a character at the specified position in a row, moving the remaining
640: * chars on the right if needed. */
641:static void editorRowInsertChar(erow *row, int at, int c) {
642:  if (at > row->size) {
643:    /* Pad the string with spaces if the insert location is outside the
644:     * current length by more than a single character. */
645:    int padlen = at - row->size;
646:    /* In the next line +2 means: new char and null term. */
647:    row->chars = realloc(row->chars, row->size + padlen + 2);
648:    memset(row->chars + row->size, ' ', padlen);
649:    row->chars[row->size + padlen + 1] = '\0';
650:    row->size += padlen + 1;
651:  } else {
652:    /* If we are in the middle of the string just make space for 1 new
653:     * char plus the (already existing) null term. */
654:    row->chars = realloc(row->chars, row->size + 2);
655:    memmove(row->chars + at + 1, row->chars + at, row->size - at + 1);
656:    row->size++;
657:  }
658:  row->chars[at] = c;
659:  editorUpdateRow(row);
660:  E.dirty++;
661:}
662:
663:/* Append the string 's' at the end of a row */
664:static void editorRowAppendString(erow *row, char *s, size_t len) {
665:  row->chars = realloc(row->chars, row->size + len + 1);
666:  memcpy(row->chars + row->size, s, len);
667:  row->size += len;
668:  row->chars[row->size] = '\0';
669:  editorUpdateRow(row);
670:  E.dirty++;
671:}
672:
673:/* Delete the character at offset 'at' from the specified row. */
674:static void editorRowDelChar(erow *row, int at) {
675:  if (row->size <= at)
676:    return;
677:  memmove(row->chars + at, row->chars + at + 1, row->size - at);
678:  editorUpdateRow(row);
679:  row->size--;
680:  E.dirty++;
681:}
682:
683:/* Insert the specified char at the current prompt position. */
684:static void editorInsertChar(int c) {
685:  int filerow = E.rowoff + E.cy;
686:  int filecol = E.coloff + E.cx;
687:  erow *row = (filerow >= E.numrows) ? NULL : &E.row[filerow];
688:
689:  /* If the row where the cursor is currently located does not exist in our
690:   * logical representaion of the file, add enough empty rows as needed. */
691:  if (!row) {
692:    while (E.numrows <= filerow)
693:      editorInsertRow(E.numrows, "", 0);
694:  }
695:  row = &E.row[filerow];
696:  editorRowInsertChar(row, filecol, c);
697:  if (E.cx == E.screencols - 1)
698:    E.coloff++;
699:  else
700:    E.cx++;
701:  E.dirty++;
702:}
703:
704:/* Inserting a newline is slightly complex as we have to handle inserting a
705: * newline in the middle of a line, splitting the line as needed. */
706:static void editorInsertNewline(void) {
707:  int filerow = E.rowoff + E.cy;
708:  int filecol = E.coloff + E.cx;
709:  erow *row = (filerow >= E.numrows) ? NULL : &E.row[filerow];
710:
711:  if (!row) {
712:    if (filerow == E.numrows) {
713:      editorInsertRow(filerow, "", 0);
714:      goto fixcursor;
715:    }
716:    return;
717:  }
718:  /* If the cursor is over the current line size, we want to conceptually
719:   * think it's just over the last character. */
720:  if (filecol >= row->size)
721:    filecol = row->size;
722:  if (filecol == 0) {
723:    editorInsertRow(filerow, "", 0);
724:  } else {
725:    /* We are in the middle of a line. Split it between two rows. */
726:    editorInsertRow(filerow + 1, row->chars + filecol, row->size - filecol);
727:    row = &E.row[filerow];
728:    row->chars[filecol] = '\0';
729:    row->size = filecol;
730:    editorUpdateRow(row);
731:  }
732:fixcursor:
733:  if (E.cy == E.screenrows - 1) {
734:    E.rowoff++;
735:  } else {
736:    E.cy++;
737:  }
738:  E.cx = 0;
739:  E.coloff = 0;
740:}
741:
742:/* Delete the char at the current prompt position. */
743:static void editorDelChar(void) {
744:  int filerow = E.rowoff + E.cy;
745:  int filecol = E.coloff + E.cx;
746:  erow *row = (filerow >= E.numrows) ? NULL : &E.row[filerow];
747:
748:  if (!row || (filecol == 0 && filerow == 0))
749:    return;
750:  if (filecol == 0) {
751:    /* Handle the case of column 0, we need to move the current line
752:     * on the right of the previous one. */
753:    filecol = E.row[filerow - 1].size;
754:    editorRowAppendString(&E.row[filerow - 1], row->chars, row->size);
755:    editorDelRow(filerow);
756:    row = NULL;
757:    if (E.cy == 0)
758:      E.rowoff--;
759:    else
760:      E.cy--;
761:    E.cx = filecol;
762:    if (E.cx >= E.screencols) {
763:      int shift = (E.screencols - E.cx) + 1;
764:      E.cx -= shift;
765:      E.coloff += shift;
766:    }
767:  } else {
768:    editorRowDelChar(row, filecol - 1);
769:    if (E.cx == 0 && E.coloff)
770:      E.coloff--;
771:    else
772:      E.cx--;
773:  }
774:  if (row)
775:    editorUpdateRow(row);
776:  E.dirty++;
777:}
778:
779:/* ============================ File I/O (OS1) ============================= */
780:
781:/* Load the specified program in the editor memory and returns 0 on success
782: * or 1 on error.
783: *
784: * OS1 NOTE: upstream used getline() in a loop. OS1's libc has no getline(),
785: * so we read the whole file in one shot (fopen/fseek/ftell/fread, all
786: * available per <stdio.h>) and split it into rows ourselves. */
787:static int editorOpen(char *filename) {
788:  FILE *fp;
789:  char *data = NULL;
790:  long fsize = 0;
791:
792:  E.dirty = 0;
793:  free(E.filename);
794:  size_t fnlen = strlen(filename) + 1;
795:  E.filename = malloc(fnlen);
796:  if (!E.filename)
797:    return 1; /* OOM on the filename copy: cannot proceed */
798:  memcpy(E.filename, filename, fnlen);
799:
800:  fp = fopen(filename, "r");
801:  if (!fp) {
802:    /* New file: nothing to load, start with an empty buffer. */
803:    return 1;
804:  }
805:
806:  if (fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END) != 0) {
807:    fclose(fp);
808:    return 1;
809:  }
810:  fsize = ftell(fp);
811:  if (fsize < 0) {
812:    fclose(fp);
813:    return 1;
814:  }
815:  if (fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET) != 0) {
816:    fclose(fp);
817:    return 1;
818:  }
819:
820:  if (fsize > 0) {
821:    data = malloc((size_t)fsize + 1);
822:    if (!data) {
823:      /* OOM on a large file: don't fread() into NULL — bail out cleanly and
824:       * start with an empty buffer instead of crashing. */
825:      fclose(fp);
826:      return 1;
827:    }
828:    size_t got = fread(data, 1, (size_t)fsize, fp);
829:    data[got] = '\0';
830:    fsize = (long)got;
831:  }
832:  fclose(fp);
833:
834:  if (data) {
835:    char *line = data;
836:    long i;
837:    for (i = 0; i < fsize; i++) {
838:      if (data[i] == '\n') {
839:        long linelen = i - (line - data);
840:        if (linelen > 0 && line[linelen - 1] == '\r')
841:          linelen--;
842:        editorInsertRow(E.numrows, line, (size_t)linelen);
843:        line = data + i + 1;
844:      }
845:    }
846:    /* Trailing partial line with no terminating newline. */
847:    if (line < data + fsize) {
848:      long linelen = (data + fsize) - line;
849:      if (linelen > 0 && line[linelen - 1] == '\r')
850:        linelen--;
851:      if (linelen > 0)
852:        editorInsertRow(E.numrows, line, (size_t)linelen);
853:    }
854:    free(data);
855:  }
856:
857:  E.dirty = 0;
858:  return 0;
859:}
860:
861:/* Save the current file on disk. Return 0 on success, 1 on error.
862: *
863: * OS1 NOTE: upstream used open(O_CREAT)+ftruncate()+write().  This port uses
864: * file_write(path, buf, len, 0): a from-start write now BOTH creates the file
865: * and truncates it to exactly 'len' bytes on the FS side (ext4_write), so a
866: * shortened save no longer leaves the old tail behind — one call does the
867: * whole create-or-overwrite.  (open(O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) is kernel-supported now
868: * too, but the positional whole-file write is simpler here.) */
869:static int editorSave(void) {
870:  int len;
871:  char *buf = editorRowsToString(&len);
872:  if (!buf)
873:    return 1; /* OOM assembling the buffer: nothing safe to write */
874:
875:  int written = file_write(E.filename, buf, len, 0);
876:  free(buf);
877:
878:  if (written < 0 || written != len) {
879:    editorSetStatusMessage("Can't save! I/O error (%d)", written);
880:    return 1;
881:  }
882:
883:  E.dirty = 0;
884:  editorSetStatusMessage("%d bytes written on disk", len);
885:  return 0;
886:}
887:
888:/* ============================= Terminal update ============================ */
889:
890:/* We define a very simple "append buffer" structure, that is an heap
891: * allocated string where we can append to. This is useful in order to
892: * write all the escape sequences in a buffer and flush them to the standard
893: * output in a single call, to avoid flickering effects. */
894:struct abuf {
895:  char *b;
896:  int len;
897:};
898:
899:#define ABUF_INIT {NULL, 0}
900:
901:static void abAppend(struct abuf *ab, const char *s, int len) {
902:  char *new = realloc(ab->b, ab->len + len);
903:
904:  if (new == NULL)
905:    return;
906:  memcpy(new + ab->len, s, len);
907:  ab->b = new;
908:  ab->len += len;
909:}
910:
911:static void abFree(struct abuf *ab) { free(ab->b); }
912:
913:/* This function writes the whole screen using VT100 escape characters
914: * starting from the logical state of the editor in the global state 'E'.
915: *
916: * OS1 NOTE: write(1, ...) is "own window" per os1.h; the window's
917: * terminal-emulator backend interprets the same cursor/SGR escapes a real
918: * VT100 terminal would. compositor_render() is called at the end to make
919: * sure the frame actually hits the screen. */
920:static void editorRefreshScreen(void) {
921:  int y;
922:  erow *r;
923:  char buf[32];
924:  struct abuf ab = ABUF_INIT;
925:
926:  abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[?25l", 6); /* Hide cursor. */
927:  abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[H", 3);    /* Go home. */
928:  for (y = 0; y < E.screenrows; y++) {
929:    int filerow = E.rowoff + y;
930:
931:    if (filerow >= E.numrows) {
932:      if (E.numrows == 0 && y == E.screenrows / 3) {
933:        char welcome[80];
934:        int welcomelen =
935:            snprintf(welcome, sizeof(welcome),
936:                     "Kilo editor -- verison %s\x1b[0K\r\n", KILO_VERSION);
937:        int padding = (E.screencols - welcomelen) / 2;
938:        if (padding) {
939:          abAppend(&ab, "~", 1);
940:          padding--;
941:        }
942:        while (padding--)
943:          abAppend(&ab, " ", 1);
944:        abAppend(&ab, welcome, welcomelen);
945:      } else {
946:        abAppend(&ab, "~\x1b[0K\r\n", 7);
947:      }
948:      continue;
949:    }
950:
951:    r = &E.row[filerow];
952:
953:    int len = r->rsize - E.coloff;
954:    int current_color = -1;
955:    if (len > 0) {
956:      if (len > E.screencols)
957:        len = E.screencols;
958:      char *c = r->render + E.coloff;
959:      unsigned char *hl = r->hl + E.coloff;
960:      int j;
961:      for (j = 0; j < len; j++) {
962:        if (hl[j] == HL_NONPRINT) {
963:          char sym;
964:          abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[7m", 4);
965:          if (c[j] <= 26)
966:            sym = '@' + c[j];
967:          else
968:            sym = '?';
969:          abAppend(&ab, &sym, 1);
970:          abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[0m", 4);
971:        } else if (hl[j] == HL_NORMAL) {
972:          if (current_color != -1) {
973:            abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[39m", 5);
974:            current_color = -1;
975:          }
976:          abAppend(&ab, c + j, 1);
977:        } else {
978:          int color = editorSyntaxToColor(hl[j]);
979:          if (color != current_color) {
980:            char cbuf[16];
981:            int clen = snprintf(cbuf, sizeof(cbuf), "\x1b[%dm", color);
982:            current_color = color;
983:            abAppend(&ab, cbuf, clen);
984:          }
985:          abAppend(&ab, c + j, 1);
986:        }
987:      }
988:    }
989:    abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[39m", 5);
990:    abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[0K", 4);
991:    abAppend(&ab, "\r\n", 2);
992:  }
993:
994:  /* Create a two rows status. First row: */
995:  abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[0K", 4);
996:  abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[7m", 4);
997:  char status[80], rstatus[80];
998:  int len = snprintf(status, sizeof(status), "%.20s - %d lines %s", E.filename,
999:                     E.numrows, E.dirty ? "(modified)" : "");
1000:  int rlen = snprintf(rstatus, sizeof(rstatus), "%d/%d", E.rowoff + E.cy + 1,
1001:                      E.numrows);
1002:  if (len > E.screencols)
1003:    len = E.screencols;
1004:  abAppend(&ab, status, len);
1005:  while (len < E.screencols) {
1006:    if (E.screencols - len == rlen) {
1007:      abAppend(&ab, rstatus, rlen);
1008:      break;
1009:    } else {
1010:      abAppend(&ab, " ", 1);
1011:      len++;
1012:    }
1013:  }
1014:  abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[0m\r\n", 6);
1015:
1016:  /* Second row depends on E.statusmsg and the status message update time. */
1017:  abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[0K", 4);
1018:  int msglen = strlen(E.statusmsg);
1019:  if (msglen && get_time() - E.statusmsg_time < 5000)
1020:    abAppend(&ab, E.statusmsg, msglen <= E.screencols ? msglen : E.screencols);
1021:
1022:  /* Put cursor at its current position. Note that the horizontal position
1023:   * at which the cursor is displayed may be different compared to 'E.cx'
1024:   * because of TABs. */
1025:  int j;
1026:  int cx = 1;
1027:  int filerow = E.rowoff + E.cy;
1028:  erow *row = (filerow >= E.numrows) ? NULL : &E.row[filerow];
1029:  if (row) {
1030:    for (j = E.coloff; j < (E.cx + E.coloff); j++) {
1031:      if (j < row->size && row->chars[j] == TAB)
1032:        cx += 7 - ((cx) % 8);
1033:      cx++;
1034:    }
1035:  }
1036:  snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "\x1b[%d;%dH", E.cy + 1, cx);
1037:  abAppend(&ab, buf, strlen(buf));
1038:  abAppend(&ab, "\x1b[?25h", 6); /* Show cursor. */
1039:  write(STDOUT_FILENO, ab.b, ab.len);
1040:  abFree(&ab);
1041:
1042:  /* Make sure the compositor actually presents the frame we just wrote. */
1043:  compositor_render();
1044:}
1045:
1046:/* Set an editor status message for the second line of the status, at the
1047: * end of the screen. */
1048:static void editorSetStatusMessage(const char *fmt, ...) {
1049:  va_list ap;
1050:  va_start(ap, fmt);
1051:  vsnprintf(E.statusmsg, sizeof(E.statusmsg), fmt, ap);
1052:  va_end(ap);
1053:  E.statusmsg_time = get_time();
1054:}
1055:
1056:/* =============================== Find mode ================================ */
1057:
1058:#define KILO_QUERY_LEN 256
1059:
1060:static void editorFind(int fd) {
1061:  char query[KILO_QUERY_LEN + 1] = {0};
1062:  int qlen = 0;
1063:  int last_match = -1;    /* Last line where a match was found. -1 for none. */
1064:  int find_next = 0;      /* if 1 search next, if -1 search prev. */
1065:  int saved_hl_line = -1; /* No saved HL */
1066:  char *saved_hl = NULL;
1067:
1068:#define FIND_RESTORE_HL                                                        \
1069:  do {                                                                         \
1070:    if (saved_hl) {                                                            \
1071:      memcpy(E.row[saved_hl_line].hl, saved_hl, E.row[saved_hl_line].rsize);   \
1072:      free(saved_hl);                                                          \
1073:      saved_hl = NULL;                                                         \
1074:    }                                                                          \
1075:  } while (0)
1076:
1077:  /* Save the cursor position in order to restore it later. */
1078:  int saved_cx = E.cx, saved_cy = E.cy;
1079:  int saved_coloff = E.coloff, saved_rowoff = E.rowoff;
1080:
1081:  while (1) {
1082:    editorSetStatusMessage("Search: %s (Use ESC/Arrows/Enter)", query);
1083:    editorRefreshScreen();
1084:
1085:    int c = editorReadKey(fd);
1086:    if (c == DEL_KEY || c == CTRL_H || c == BACKSPACE) {
1087:      if (qlen != 0)
1088:        query[--qlen] = '\0';
1089:      last_match = -1;
1090:    } else if (c == ESC || c == ENTER) {
1091:      if (c == ESC) {
1092:        E.cx = saved_cx;
1093:        E.cy = saved_cy;
1094:        E.coloff = saved_coloff;
1095:        E.rowoff = saved_rowoff;
1096:      }
1097:      FIND_RESTORE_HL;
1098:      editorSetStatusMessage("");
1099:      return;
1100:    } else if (c == ARROW_RIGHT || c == ARROW_DOWN) {
1101:      find_next = 1;
1102:    } else if (c == ARROW_LEFT || c == ARROW_UP) {
1103:      find_next = -1;
1104:    } else if (isprint(c)) {
1105:      if (qlen < KILO_QUERY_LEN) {
1106:        query[qlen++] = c;
1107:        query[qlen] = '\0';
1108:        last_match = -1;
1109:      }
1110:    }
1111:
1112:    /* Search occurrence. */
1113:    if (last_match == -1)
1114:      find_next = 1;
1115:    if (find_next) {
1116:      char *match = NULL;
1117:      int match_offset = 0;
1118:      int i, current = last_match;
1119:
1120:      for (i = 0; i < E.numrows; i++) {
1121:        current += find_next;
1122:        if (current == -1)
1123:          current = E.numrows - 1;
1124:        else if (current == E.numrows)
1125:          current = 0;
1126:        match = strstr(E.row[current].render, query);
1127:        if (match) {
1128:          match_offset = match - E.row[current].render;
1129:          break;
1130:        }
1131:      }
1132:      find_next = 0;
1133:
1134:      /* Highlight */
1135:      FIND_RESTORE_HL;
1136:
1137:      if (match) {
1138:        erow *row = &E.row[current];
1139:        last_match = current;
1140:        if (row->hl) {
1141:          saved_hl_line = current;
1142:          saved_hl = malloc(row->rsize);
1143:          memcpy(saved_hl, row->hl, row->rsize);
1144:          memset(row->hl + match_offset, HL_MATCH, qlen);
1145:        }
1146:        E.cy = 0;
1147:        E.cx = match_offset;
1148:        E.rowoff = current;
1149:        E.coloff = 0;
1150:        /* Scroll horizontally as needed. */
1151:        if (E.cx > E.screencols) {
1152:          int diff = E.cx - E.screencols;
1153:          E.cx -= diff;
1154:          E.coloff += diff;
1155:        }
1156:      }
1157:    }
1158:  }
1159:}
1160:
1161:/* ========================= Editor events handling  ======================== */
1162:
1163:/* Handle cursor position change because arrow keys were pressed. */
1164:static void editorMoveCursor(int key) {
1165:  int filerow = E.rowoff + E.cy;
1166:  int filecol = E.coloff + E.cx;
1167:  int rowlen;
1168:  erow *row = (filerow >= E.numrows) ? NULL : &E.row[filerow];
1169:
1170:  switch (key) {
1171:  case ARROW_LEFT:
1172:    if (E.cx == 0) {
1173:      if (E.coloff) {
1174:        E.coloff--;
1175:      } else {
1176:        if (filerow > 0) {
1177:          E.cy--;
1178:          E.cx = E.row[filerow - 1].size;
1179:          if (E.cx > E.screencols - 1) {
1180:            E.coloff = E.cx - E.screencols + 1;
1181:            E.cx = E.screencols - 1;
1182:          }
1183:        }
1184:      }
1185:    } else {
1186:      E.cx -= 1;
1187:    }
1188:    break;
1189:  case ARROW_RIGHT:
1190:    if (row && filecol < row->size) {
1191:      if (E.cx == E.screencols - 1) {
1192:        E.coloff++;
1193:      } else {
1194:        E.cx += 1;
1195:      }
1196:    } else if (row && filecol == row->size) {
1197:      E.cx = 0;
1198:      E.coloff = 0;
1199:      if (E.cy == E.screenrows - 1) {
1200:        E.rowoff++;
1201:      } else {
1202:        E.cy += 1;
1203:      }
1204:    }
1205:    break;
1206:  case ARROW_UP:
1207:    if (E.cy == 0) {
1208:      if (E.rowoff)
1209:        E.rowoff--;
1210:    } else {
1211:      E.cy -= 1;
1212:    }
1213:    break;
1214:  case ARROW_DOWN:
1215:    if (filerow < E.numrows) {
1216:      if (E.cy == E.screenrows - 1) {
1217:        E.rowoff++;
1218:      } else {
1219:        E.cy += 1;
1220:      }
1221:    }
1222:    break;
1223:  }
1224:  /* Fix cx if the current line has not enough chars. */
1225:  filerow = E.rowoff + E.cy;
1226:  filecol = E.coloff + E.cx;
1227:  row = (filerow >= E.numrows) ? NULL : &E.row[filerow];
1228:  rowlen = row ? row->size : 0;
1229:  if (filecol > rowlen) {
1230:    E.cx -= filecol - rowlen;
1231:    if (E.cx < 0) {
1232:      E.coloff += E.cx;
1233:      E.cx = 0;
1234:    }
1235:  }
1236:}
1237:
1238:/* Process events arriving from the input stream, which is, the user
1239: * is typing on the keyboard. */
1240:#define KILO_QUIT_TIMES 3
1241:static void editorProcessKeypress(int fd) {
1242:  /* When the file is modified, requires Ctrl-q to be pressed N times
1243:   * before actually quitting. */
1244:  static int quit_times = KILO_QUIT_TIMES;
1245:
1246:  int c = editorReadKey(fd);
1247:  switch (c) {
1248:  case ENTER: /* Enter */
1249:    editorInsertNewline();
1250:    break;
1251:  case CTRL_C: /* Ctrl-c */
1252:    /* We ignore ctrl-c, it can't be so simple to lose the changes
1253:     * to the edited file. */
1254:    break;
1255:  case CTRL_Q: /* Ctrl-q */
1256:    /* Quit if the file was already saved. */
1257:    if (E.dirty && quit_times) {
1258:      editorSetStatusMessage("WARNING!!! File has unsaved changes. "
1259:                             "Press Ctrl-Q %d more times to quit.",
1260:                             quit_times);
1261:      quit_times--;
1262:      return;
1263:    }
1264:    exit(0);
1265:    break;
1266:  case CTRL_S: /* Ctrl-s */
1267:    editorSave();
1268:    break;
1269:  case CTRL_F:
1270:    editorFind(fd);
1271:    break;
1272:  case BACKSPACE: /* Backspace */
1273:  case CTRL_H:    /* Ctrl-h */
1274:  case DEL_KEY:
1275:    editorDelChar();
1276:    break;
1277:  case PAGE_UP:
1278:  case PAGE_DOWN:
1279:    if (c == PAGE_UP && E.cy != 0)
1280:      E.cy = 0;
1281:    else if (c == PAGE_DOWN && E.cy != E.screenrows - 1)
1282:      E.cy = E.screenrows - 1;
1283:    {
1284:      int times = E.screenrows;
1285:      while (times--)
1286:        editorMoveCursor(c == PAGE_UP ? ARROW_UP : ARROW_DOWN);
1287:    }
1288:    break;
1289:
1290:  case ARROW_UP:
1291:  case ARROW_DOWN:
1292:  case ARROW_LEFT:
1293:  case ARROW_RIGHT:
1294:    editorMoveCursor(c);
1295:    break;
1296:  case CTRL_L: /* ctrl+l, clear screen */
1297:    /* Just refresht the line as side effect. */
1298:    break;
1299:  case ESC:
1300:    /* Nothing to do for ESC in this mode. */
1301:    break;
1302:  default:
1303:    editorInsertChar(c);
1304:    break;
1305:  }
1306:
1307:  quit_times = KILO_QUIT_TIMES; /* Reset it to the original value. */
1308:}
1309:
1310:/* ============================== Init / main =============================== */
1311:
1312:/* OS1 NOTE: no ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ), no SIGWINCH.  The compositor terminal cell
1313: * size depends on the active (proportional) font, so the real grid is NOT
1314: * 80x25 — we query it from the window with window_grid() and reserve two rows
1315: * for the status bar + message line.  win_id < 0 (or a failed query) falls
1316: * back to the compile-time WIN_COLS/WIN_ROWS estimate. */
1317:static void updateWindowSize(int win_id) {
1318:  int cols = WIN_COLS, rows = WIN_ROWS;
1319:  if (win_id >= 0)
1320:    window_grid(win_id, &cols, &rows);
1321:  if (cols < 1)
1322:    cols = WIN_COLS;
1323:  if (rows < 3)
1324:    rows = WIN_ROWS;
1325:  E.screencols = cols;
1326:  E.screenrows = rows - 2;
1327:}
1328:
1329:static void initEditor(void) {
1330:  E.cx = 0;
1331:  E.cy = 0;
1332:  E.rowoff = 0;
1333:  E.coloff = 0;
1334:  E.numrows = 0;
1335:  E.row = NULL;
1336:  E.dirty = 0;
1337:  E.filename = NULL;
1338:  E.syntax = NULL;
1339:  updateWindowSize(-1); /* provisional; refined once the window exists */
1340:}
1341:
1342:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
1343:  if (argc != 2) {
1344:    printf("Usage: kilo <filename>\n");
1345:    exit(1);
1346:  }
1347:
1348:  /* Create our own window and grab keyboard focus. fd 0/1 ("own window")
1349:   * then refer to this window's input stream / terminal renderer. */
1350:  int win = create_window(WIN_X, WIN_Y, WIN_W, WIN_H, "kilo");
1351:  if (win < 0) {
1352:    printf("kilo: create_window failed (%d)\n", win);
1353:    exit(1);
1354:  }
1355:  set_focus(get_pid());
1356:
1357:  initEditor();
1358:  updateWindowSize(win); /* size to the real terminal grid of our window */
1359:  editorSelectSyntaxHighlight(argv[1]);
1360:  editorOpen(argv[1]);
1361:  editorSetStatusMessage("HELP: Ctrl-S = save | Ctrl-Q = quit | Ctrl-F = find");
1362:  while (1) {
1363:    editorRefreshScreen();
1364:    editorProcessKeypress(STDIN_FILENO);
1365:  }
1366:  return 0;
1367:}
1368:
1369:/* ===========================================================================
1370: * PORTING NOTES / TODO
1371: * ===========================================================================
1372: *
1373: * - CELL_W/CELL_H (8x16): tune these to match the actual bitmap font used
1374: *   by the compositor's window terminal emulator, otherwise the status
1375: *   bar / wrap column will be visually off even though the logic is correct.
1376: *
1377: * - editorReadKey() assumes the window input stream forwards arrow keys,
1378: *   Home/End, PageUp/Down and Del as standard "ESC [ ..." sequences (as a
1379: *   real VT100/xterm would). If OS1's keyboard IPC delivers raw scancodes
1380: *   or a different encoding instead, only editorReadKey()'s ESC-sequence
1381: *   switch needs to change -- everything above (the row/buffer model) and
1382: *   below (movement/keypress dispatch) is keycode-agnostic via the
1383: *   KEY_ACTION enum.
1384: *
1385: * - compositor_render() is called once per refresh (i.e. roughly once per
1386: *   keystroke). If this is too slow/flickery on real hardware, it can be
1387: *   removed if window_write()/write(1,...) already triggers a compositor
1388: *   update on its own.
1389: *
1390: * - No SIGWINCH / live resize: the window is created at a fixed WIN_W x
1391: *   WIN_H. If OS1 windows can be resized by the user, editorRefreshScreen()
1392: *   will keep using the original WIN_COLS x WIN_ROWS grid regardless.
1393: *
1394: * - file_write() creates the file if missing and, for a from-start (offset 0)
1395: *   write, truncates it to exactly `len` bytes — the FS-side ext4_write does
1396: *   the truncation now, so editorSave()'s single whole-file write is correct
1397: *   even when the buffer shrinks (no delete-then-write / ftruncate needed).
1398: */

@@@ user/bin/kilo/README.md @@@
1:Kilo
2:===
3:
4:Kilo is a small text editor in less than 1K lines of code (counted with cloc).
5:
6:A screencast is available here: https://asciinema.org/a/90r2i9bq8po03nazhqtsifksb
7:
8:Usage: kilo `<filename>`
9:
10:Keys:
11:
12:    CTRL-S: Save
13:    CTRL-Q: Quit
14:    CTRL-F: Find string in file (ESC to exit search, arrows to navigate)
15:
16:Kilo does not depend on any library (not even curses). It uses fairly standard
17:VT100 (and similar terminals) escape sequences. The project is in alpha
18:stage and was written in just a few hours taking code from my other two
19:projects, load81 and linenoise.
20:
21:People are encouraged to use it as a starting point to write other editors
22:or command line interfaces that are more advanced than the usual REPL
23:style CLI.
24:
25:Kilo was written by Salvatore Sanfilippo aka antirez and is released
26:under the BSD 2 clause license.
27:

@@@ user/bin/capkill_child.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/capkill_child.c
3: * Kill target for the capability process-control test (see capkill.c).
4: * Spawned as PLVL_GUEST; loops forever until the parent terminates it through
5: * a PROCESS capability holding OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY.
6: */
7:#include <os1.h>
8:
9:int main(void) {
10:  printf("[capkill] child PID %d alive, looping\n", get_pid());
11:  while (1)
12:    yield();
13:  return 0;
