@@@ user/bin/captest.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/captest.c
3: * Capability / object-manager test (ASTRA §6.1/6.2/6.5).
4: *
5: * Proves the REAL capability layer end to end, using the OS1 NATIVE base API
6: * (OS1low_* / OS1_object_*) — not POSIX:
7: *   1. handle_create(FILE, READ) yields a handle; OS1_object_read works.
8: *   2. rights are SEPARABLE+ENFORCED: write through a READ-only handle -> -EPERM.
9: *   3. cap_query reports (type, rights).
10: *   4. UNFORGEABILITY: a handle integer with no slot -> -EBADF (query + read).
11: *   5. ATTENUATION: duplicate(READ|WRITE) of a READ|DUP handle yields READ only.
12: *   6. duplicate needs OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE on the source -> else -EPERM.
13: *   7. lifecycle: close -> 0; use after close -> -EBADF; double close -> -EBADF.
14: *   8. PROCESS object: a handle to self; rights enforced (read needs READ).
15: *   9. DELEGATION is gated: grant without OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER -> -EPERM.
16: *  10. O_CREAT: CREATE|WRITE creates a missing file; CREATE bit is stripped.
17: *  11. Creation is explicit: no CREATE (or CREATE w/o WRITE) -> -ENOENT.
18: *  12. Acquisition ACL: CREATE under /sys/bin -> -EACCES for USER.
19: *  13. Parent-directory MUTATE capability: /home mkdir+unlink succeeds;
20: *      /sys/bin acquisition is denied; malformed child names cannot escape.
21: * Results go to a window AND the serial console (grep "[captest]").
22: */
23:#include <execsvc.h> /* execution-service protocol (Phase 9 section below) */
24:#include <fcntl.h>
25:#include <os1.h>
26:#include <stdio.h>
27:#include <stdlib.h> /* getenv/setenv/unsetenv (Phase 17 section) */
28:#include <string.h>
29:#include <sys/wait.h> /* waitpid + WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS (Phase 9b section) */
30:#include <unistd.h>
31:
32:static int failures = 0;
33:static int checks = 0;
34:
35:static void check(int win_id, const char *name, int ok) {
36:  checks++;
37:  printf_win(win_id, "%s: %s\n", name, ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
38:  printf("[captest] %s: %s\n", name, ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
39:  if (!ok)
40:    failures++;
41:}
42:
43:/* section - group header.  This suite is the SYSTEM regression test and grows
44: * with each phase (maintainer directive 2026-07-18), so results are organised
45: * by layer rather than appended flat: a failure should say WHICH layer broke.
46: * Layer order deliberately mirrors the debugging order used on this project:
47: * kernel object/capability -> kernel IPC & streams -> POSIX personality. */
48:static void section(int win_id, const char *name) {
49:  printf_win(win_id, "-- %s --\n", name);
50:  printf("[captest] ---- %s ----\n", name);
51:}
52:
53:int main(void) {
54:  int win_id = create_window(140, 140, 440, 320, "Cap Test");
55:  if (win_id < 0)
56:    return 1;
57:
58:  const char *path = "/etc/init.cfg"; /* readable+writable rootfs file */
59:  char a[16];
60:  int ok;
61:
62:  printf_win(win_id, "Object/capability tests...\n");
63:  printf("[captest] start (OS1 native object/capability ABI)\n");
64:
65:  /* 1. create a READ capability to a file and read through it */
66:  int h = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
67:  memset(a, 0, sizeof(a));
68:  ok = h >= 0 && OS1_object_read(h, a, 8) == 8;
69:  check(win_id, "create+object_read", ok);
70:
71:  /* 2. rights enforced: no WRITE right -> object_write denied */
72:  ok = OS1_object_write(h, "ZZZZ", 4) == -EPERM;
73:  check(win_id, "deny-write-no-right", ok);
74:
75:  /* 3. cap_query reports type + the exact held rights */
76:  long q = OS1low_cap_query(h);
77:  ok = q >= 0 && OS1_CAPQ_TYPE(q) == OBJ_TYPE_FILE &&
78:       OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(q) == OS1_RIGHT_READ;
79:  check(win_id, "cap_query", ok);
80:
81:  /* 4. unforgeability: a handle with no installed slot is -EBADF */
82:  ok = OS1low_cap_query(9999) == -EBADF &&
83:       OS1_object_read(9999, a, 1) == -EBADF &&
84:       OS1low_cap_query(-1) == -EBADF;
85:  check(win_id, "unforgeable", ok);
86:
87:  /* 5. attenuation: dup(READ|WRITE) of a READ|DUP handle yields READ only */
88:  int hd = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path,
89:                                     OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE,
90:                                     OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
91:  int h2 = (int)OS1low_handle_duplicate(hd, OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_WRITE);
92:  long q2 = (h2 >= 0) ? OS1low_cap_query(h2) : -1;
93:  ok = hd >= 0 && h2 >= 0 && q2 >= 0 &&
94:       OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(q2) == OS1_RIGHT_READ; /* WRITE attenuated away */
95:  check(win_id, "dup-attenuate", ok);
96:
97:  /* 6. duplicate needs OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE on the source (h lacks it) */
98:  ok = OS1low_handle_duplicate(h, OS1_RIGHT_READ) == -EPERM;
99:  check(win_id, "dup-needs-right", ok);
100:
101:  /* 7. lifecycle: close, then use-after-close and double-close are -EBADF */
102:  ok = OS1low_handle_close(h) == 0 && OS1_object_read(h, a, 1) == -EBADF &&
103:       OS1low_handle_close(h) == -EBADF;
104:  check(win_id, "close-lifecycle", ok);
105:
106:  /* 8. PROCESS object: a capability to self; rights enforced */
107:  char pidbuf[16];
108:  sprintf(pidbuf, "%d", get_pid());
109:  int ph = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, pidbuf, OS1_RIGHT_WAIT,
110:                                     OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
111:  long pq = (ph >= 0) ? OS1low_cap_query(ph) : -1;
112:  ok = ph >= 0 && pq >= 0 && OS1_CAPQ_TYPE(pq) == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS &&
113:       OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(pq) == OS1_RIGHT_WAIT &&
114:       OS1_object_read(ph, a, 1) == -EPERM; /* no READ right on a process */
115:  check(win_id, "process-object", ok);
116:  printf("[captest] object_wait(self)=%ld (alive=-1)\n", OS1_object_wait(ph, 0));
117:
118:  /* 8b. PROCESS object READ (state via the object mechanism): a READ handle to
119:   * self reads the live status block — it begins "pid=" and is non-empty.  This
120:   * is the process NOTIFYING its state through OS1_object_read, not a side
121:   * channel. */
122:  {
123:    int phr = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, pidbuf, OS1_RIGHT_READ,
124:                                        OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
125:    char st[128];
126:    memset(st, 0, sizeof(st));
127:    long rn = (phr >= 0) ? OS1_object_read(phr, st, sizeof(st) - 1) : -1;
128:    ok = phr >= 0 && rn > 0 && strncmp(st, "pid=", 4) == 0;
129:    check(win_id, "process-read-state", ok);
130:    if (phr >= 0)
131:      OS1low_handle_close(phr);
132:  }
133:
134:  /* 8c. namespace → TYPED object (deep fusion): acquire /proc/<self> via the
135:   * filesystem namespace (a PATH, not a pid) — it resolves to the SAME PROCESS
136:   * capability object (cap_query confirms the type) and reads its state.  Proves
137:   * "everything resolvable in the namespace is a typed capability object". */
138:  {
139:    char procpath[32];
140:    sprintf(procpath, "/proc/%d", get_pid());
141:    int pf = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, procpath, OS1_RIGHT_READ,
142:                                       OBJ_TYPE_FILE); /* type hint overridden */
143:    long pq2 = (pf >= 0) ? OS1low_cap_query(pf) : -1;
144:    char st2[128];
145:    memset(st2, 0, sizeof(st2));
146:    long rn2 = (pf >= 0) ? OS1_object_read(pf, st2, sizeof(st2) - 1) : -1;
147:    ok = pf >= 0 && pq2 >= 0 && OS1_CAPQ_TYPE(pq2) == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS &&
148:         rn2 > 0 && strncmp(st2, "pid=", 4) == 0;
149:    check(win_id, "proc-namespace-object", ok);
150:    if (pf >= 0)
151:      OS1low_handle_close(pf);
152:  }
153:
154:  /* 9. delegation gated: grant without OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER -> -EPERM */
155:  int hng = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ,
156:                                      OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
157:  ok = hng >= 0 && OS1low_cap_grant(get_pid(), hng, OS1_RIGHT_READ) == -EPERM;
158:  check(win_id, "grant-needs-transfer", ok);
159:
160:  /* 10. O_CREAT via capability (C1): CREATE|WRITE on a MISSING path creates
161:   * the file behind the vfs_write_allowed seam; CREATE is acquisition-only
162:   * (stripped from the installed rights, never visible to cap_query); data
163:   * written through the handle reads back via a fresh READ handle. */
164:  {
165:    const char *npath = "/home/captest.tmp";
166:    OS1_fs_unlink(npath); /* ensure missing; ignore result */
167:    int hc = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, npath,
168:                                       OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_CREATE,
169:                                       OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
170:    long qc = (hc >= 0) ? OS1low_cap_query(hc) : -1;
171:    long wn = (hc >= 0) ? OS1_object_write(hc, "cap!", 4) : -1;
172:    if (hc >= 0)
173:      OS1low_handle_close(hc);
174:    int hr = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, npath, OS1_RIGHT_READ,
175:                                       OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
176:    char rb[8];
177:    memset(rb, 0, sizeof(rb));
178:    long rn = (hr >= 0) ? OS1_object_read(hr, rb, 4) : -1;
179:    if (hr >= 0)
180:      OS1low_handle_close(hr);
181:    ok = hc >= 0 && qc >= 0 && OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(qc) == OS1_RIGHT_WRITE &&
182:         wn == 4 && rn == 4 && memcmp(rb, "cap!", 4) == 0;
183:    check(win_id, "create-via-handle", ok);
184:    OS1_fs_unlink(npath);
185:  }
186:
187:  /* 11. creation is explicit: a missing path without CREATE stays -ENOENT,
188:   * and CREATE without WRITE is meaningless (also -ENOENT). */
189:  ok = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, "/home/captest.missing",
190:                            OS1_RIGHT_WRITE, OBJ_TYPE_FILE) == -ENOENT &&
191:       OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, "/home/captest.missing",
192:                            OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_CREATE,
193:                            OBJ_TYPE_FILE) == -ENOENT;
194:  check(win_id, "create-needs-flag+write", ok);
195:
196:  /* 12. acquisition ACL: CREATE under the machine-only /sys/bin tree is
197:   * denied at handle_create (the same vfs_write_allowed seam) — USER never
198:   * acquires a write/create capability into the boot chain. */
199:  ok = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, "/sys/bin/captest.t",
200:                            OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_CREATE,
201:                            OBJ_TYPE_FILE) == -EACCES;
202:  check(win_id, "create-acl-sysbin", ok);
203:
204:  /* 13. R1b: directory namespace mutation is a message on a parent-directory
205:   * capability. The parent ACL gates acquisition; the held capability names
206:   * the namespace, and the child name cannot contain a path separator. */
207:  int home_dir = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, "/home",
208:                                            OS1_RIGHT_MUTATE, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
209:  long escaped = (home_dir >= 0)
210:                     ? OS1_object_ctl(home_dir, OBJ_CTL_MKDIR, (long)"a/b")
211:                     : -1;
212:  if (home_dir >= 0)
213:    OS1low_handle_close(home_dir);
214:  ok = OS1_fs_mkdir("/home/captest.dir") == 0 &&
215:       OS1_fs_unlink("/home/captest.dir") == 0 &&
216:       OS1_fs_mkdir("/sys/bin/captest.dir") == -EACCES && escaped == -EINVAL;
217:  check(win_id, "dir-mutate-capability", ok);
218:
219:  /* --- 14..18: service PORTS (ASTRA §6.5 — a port IS a capability) --------
220:   * These verify the property that motivates ports: a client reaches a SERVICE
221:   * BY NAME with an unforgeable capability, never by pid. */
222:  const char *pname = "OS1nx_captest";
223:  int psrv = OS1_port_create(pname); /* service side: takes the RECEIVE right */
224:  check(win_id, "port-create", psrv >= 0);
225:
226:  /* 15. the name is now SERVED: a second receiver is refused, so a rogue
227:   * process cannot steal a published service identity by racing it. */
228:  int pdup = OS1_port_create(pname);
229:  check(win_id, "port-name-unique", pdup < 0);
230:  if (pdup >= 0)
231:    OS1low_handle_close(pdup);
232:
233:  /* 16. a client acquires a SEND-only capability by NAME (no pid involved). */
234:  int pcli = OS1_port_open(pname);
235:  check(win_id, "port-open-send", pcli >= 0);
236:
237:  /* 17. round-trip: send through the client capability, receive on the service
238:   * capability, and the kernel-stamped `from` must be our own pid (unforgeable
239:   * — we deliberately fill it with a lie below). */
240:  struct ipc_message tx, rx;
241:  memset(&tx, 0, sizeof(tx));
242:  memset(&rx, 0, sizeof(rx));
243:  tx.type = 4242;
244:  tx.data1 = 0xC0FFEE;
245:  tx.from = 999999; /* forged: the kernel must overwrite this */
246:  ok = pcli >= 0 && psrv >= 0 &&
247:       OS1_port_send(pcli, &tx) == (long)sizeof(tx) &&
248:       OS1_port_recv(psrv, &rx) == (long)sizeof(rx) && rx.type == 4242 &&
249:       rx.data1 == 0xC0FFEE && rx.from == get_pid();
250:  check(win_id, "port-roundtrip+from-unforgeable", ok);
251:
252:  /* 18. an unpublished name yields no capability at all. */
253:  int pmiss = OS1_port_open("OS1nx_nosuchservice");
254:  check(win_id, "port-open-missing", pmiss < 0);
255:  if (pmiss >= 0)
256:    OS1low_handle_close(pmiss);
257:
258:  if (pcli >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(pcli);
259:  if (psrv >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(psrv);
260:
261:  /* ================= process ownership / authority (Q3) ================= */
262:  section(win_id, "process ownership");
263:  {
264:    /* A DESTROY capability to SELF is always acquirable (self-kill is allowed),
265:     * which gives us a legitimately-held handle to probe SETOWNER with. */
266:    int selfh = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, "self",
267:                                          OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY, OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
268:    if (selfh < 0) { /* namespace wants a decimal pid string */
269:      char pidstr[16];
270:      snprintf(pidstr, sizeof(pidstr), "%d", get_pid());
271:      selfh = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, pidstr, OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY,
272:                                        OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
273:    }
274:    check(win_id, "own-self-destroy-cap", selfh >= 0);
275:
276:    /* THE security property: setting a logical owner DELEGATES authority over a
277:     * process, so an unprivileged caller must be refused even though it holds a
278:     * legitimate DESTROY capability.  Otherwise a process could re-home itself
279:     * under a victim and borrow that victim's authority chain. */
280:    long r = (selfh >= 0) ? OS1_object_ctl(selfh, OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER, 1) : 0;
281:    check(win_id, "own-setowner-denied-unprivileged", selfh >= 0 && r < 0);
282:
283:    /* A nonsense owner is rejected on argument grounds, not silently taken. */
284:    long r2 = (selfh >= 0) ? OS1_object_ctl(selfh, OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER, 0) : 0;
285:    check(win_id, "own-setowner-rejects-bad-arg", selfh >= 0 && r2 < 0);
286:
287:    /* Regression guard for the ancestry walk itself: adding owner_pid changed
288:     * process_kill_allowed(), so verify the ordinary self/descendant path still
289:     * resolves (a WAIT capability to self must still be acquirable). */
290:    int waith = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, "self", OS1_RIGHT_WAIT,
291:                                          OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
292:    if (waith < 0) {
293:      char pidstr[16];
294:      snprintf(pidstr, sizeof(pidstr), "%d", get_pid());
295:      waith = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, pidstr, OS1_RIGHT_WAIT,
296:                                        OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
297:    }
298:    check(win_id, "own-ancestry-walk-intact", waith >= 0);
299:    if (waith >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(waith);
300:    if (selfh >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(selfh);
301:  }
302:
303:  /* ============================ pipes (§6.2) ============================ */
304:  section(win_id, "pipes");
305:  {
306:    int pf[2] = {-1, -1};
307:    ok = pipe(pf) == 0 && pf[0] >= 0 && pf[1] >= 0;
308:    check(win_id, "pipe-create", ok);
309:
310:    if (ok) {
311:      /* The ends are DIFFERENT capabilities to one object: read end must not be
312:       * writable, write end must not be readable. */
313:      long qr = OS1low_cap_query(pf[0]);
314:      long qw = OS1low_cap_query(pf[1]);
315:      check(win_id, "pipe-type-is-PIPE",
316:            qr >= 0 && OS1_CAPQ_TYPE(qr) == OBJ_TYPE_PIPE);
317:      check(win_id, "pipe-ends-rights-split",
318:            qr >= 0 && qw >= 0 && (OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(qr) & OS1_RIGHT_READ) &&
319:                !(OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(qr) & OS1_RIGHT_WRITE) &&
320:                (OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(qw) & OS1_RIGHT_WRITE) &&
321:                !(OS1_CAPQ_RIGHTS(qw) & OS1_RIGHT_READ));
322:
323:      char rb[16];
324:      memset(rb, 0, sizeof(rb));
325:      ok = write(pf[1], "hello", 5) == 5 && read(pf[0], rb, 5) == 5 &&
326:           memcmp(rb, "hello", 5) == 0;
327:      check(win_id, "pipe-roundtrip", ok);
328:
329:      /* EOF is the property the lua fix depends on: a reader must get 0 (not a
330:       * block) once every writer is gone. */
331:      close(pf[1]);
332:      check(win_id, "pipe-eof-on-last-writer-close", read(pf[0], rb, 4) == 0);
333:      close(pf[0]);
334:    }
335:  }
336:
337:  /* ================= POSIX personality (standardisation) ================ */
338:  section(win_id, "posix surface");
339:  {
340:    /* getpid must be the POSIX spelling of the OS1 verb, not a second impl. */
341:    check(win_id, "posix-getpid-matches-OS1", getpid() == get_pid());
342:
343:    /* isatty is a real capability-TYPE test, not "fd < 3".  This is exactly the
344:     * property that made `echo ... | lua` work: with a redirected stdin lua must
345:     * see isatty()==0 and EXECUTE stdin instead of opening a REPL. */
346:    check(win_id, "posix-isatty-console", isatty(1) == 1);
347:    int pf2[2] = {-1, -1};
348:    if (pipe(pf2) == 0) {
349:      check(win_id, "posix-isatty-pipe-is-false", isatty(pf2[0]) == 0);
350:      close(pf2[0]);
351:      close(pf2[1]);
352:    } else {
353:      check(win_id, "posix-isatty-pipe-is-false", 0);
354:    }
355:
356:    const char *tp = "/home/captest.trunc";
357:    int tfd = open(tp, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644);
358:    if (tfd >= 0) {
359:      check(win_id, "posix-isatty-file-is-false", isatty(tfd) == 0);
360:      ok = write(tfd, "0123456789", 10) == 10;
361:      /* shrink: composed from lseek+read+rewrite (offset-0 write REPLACES) */
362:      ok = ok && ftruncate(tfd, 4) == 0 && lseek(tfd, 0, SEEK_END) == 4;
363:      check(win_id, "posix-ftruncate-shrink", ok);
364:      /* extend: zero-fill from the old EOF */
365:      ok = ftruncate(tfd, 9) == 0 && lseek(tfd, 0, SEEK_END) == 9;
366:      check(win_id, "posix-ftruncate-extend", ok);
367:      /* to empty: the case POSIX write(fd,buf,0) CANNOT express (it is a
368:       * no-op), hence the OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE verb */
369:      ok = ftruncate(tfd, 0) == 0 && lseek(tfd, 0, SEEK_END) == 0;
370:      check(win_id, "posix-ftruncate-to-empty", ok);
371:      close(tfd);
372:      OS1_fs_unlink(tp);
373:    } else {
374:      check(win_id, "posix-ftruncate-shrink", 0);
375:    }
376:
377:    /* fdopen: wrap an existing descriptor in a FILE* — how ported POSIX code
378:     * consumes a pipe/file through stdio.  Was DECLARED but unimplemented. */
379:    const char *fp = "/home/captest.fdopen";
380:    int wfd = open(fp, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644);
381:    ok = 0;
382:    if (wfd >= 0) {
383:      write(wfd, "abc", 3);
384:      close(wfd);
385:      int rfd = open(fp, O_RDONLY, 0);
386:      if (rfd >= 0) {
387:        FILE *f = fdopen(rfd, "r");
388:        char fb[8];
389:        memset(fb, 0, sizeof(fb));
390:        ok = f && fread(fb, 1, 3, f) == 3 && memcmp(fb, "abc", 3) == 0;
391:        if (f)
392:          fclose(f); /* also closes rfd (POSIX ownership) */
393:        else
394:          close(rfd);
395:      }
396:      OS1_fs_unlink(fp);
397:    }
398:    check(win_id, "posix-fdopen-stream", ok);
399:  }
400:
401:  /* ========== per-process view is VIRTUAL, never stale (Phase 5b) ======== */
402:  section(win_id, "virtual proc view");
403:  {
404:    char v[64];
405:    char k[64];
406:    /* Our OWN entry must be live and correct, with nobody having written it. */
407:    snprintf(k, sizeof(k), "sys.proc.%d.name", get_pid());
408:    memset(v, 0, sizeof(v));
409:    ok = OS1_registry_get(k, v, sizeof(v)) == 0 && v[0] != '\0';
410:    check(win_id, "vproc-name-live", ok);
411:
412:    snprintf(k, sizeof(k), "sys.proc.%d.state", get_pid());
413:    memset(v, 0, sizeof(v));
414:    check(win_id, "vproc-state-live",
415:          OS1_registry_get(k, v, sizeof(v)) == 0 && v[0] != '\0');
416:
417:    /* THE property the unification buys: a DEAD pid has no value.  With the old
418:     * userland-written copy this is exactly what went stale and needed a
419:     * garbage collector; virtualised, there is nothing stored to leak. */
420:    snprintf(k, sizeof(k), "sys.proc.%d.name", 999999);
421:    memset(v, 0, sizeof(v));
422:    OS1_registry_get(k, v, sizeof(v));
423:    check(win_id, "vproc-dead-pid-empty", v[0] == '\0');
424:  }
425:
426:  /* ============ environment (Phase 17a) ================================= */
427:  section(win_id, "environment");
428:  {
429:    char v[64], k[96];
430:
431:    /* The seam is a NAMESPACE PATH, not a shared struct: userland never sees
432:     * the kernel's env block, only strings through sys_registry.  That is the
433:     * whole reason the syscall dispatcher exists. */
434:    check(win_id, "env-set", setenv("CAPTEST_A", "one", 1) == 0);
435:    const char *got = getenv("CAPTEST_A");
436:    check(win_id, "env-get-roundtrip", got && strcmp(got, "one") == 0);
437:
438:    check(win_id, "env-overwrite", setenv("CAPTEST_A", "two", 1) == 0 &&
439:                                       (got = getenv("CAPTEST_A")) &&
440:                                       strcmp(got, "two") == 0);
441:
442:    /* overwrite=0 must NOT replace an existing value. */
443:    setenv("CAPTEST_A", "three", 0);
444:    got = getenv("CAPTEST_A");
445:    check(win_id, "env-no-overwrite", got && strcmp(got, "two") == 0);
446:
447:    unsetenv("CAPTEST_A");
448:    check(win_id, "env-unset", getenv("CAPTEST_A") == (char *)0);
449:
450:    /* The MACHINE default layer: HOME is seeded by init as a stored key, and
451:     * getenv falls through to it with nothing copied into this process. */
452:    got = getenv("HOME");
453:    check(win_id, "env-machine-default", got && got[0] == '/');
454:
455:    /* A process value SHADOWS the default for this process only... */
456:    setenv("HOME", "/captest", 1);
457:    got = getenv("HOME");
458:    check(win_id, "env-process-shadows-default",
459:          got && strcmp(got, "/captest") == 0);
460:    /* ...and removing it exposes the default again, unharmed: the two layers
461:     * are layers, not two copies of one value. */
462:    unsetenv("HOME");
463:    got = getenv("HOME");
464:    check(win_id, "env-default-survives-shadow",
465:          got && strcmp(got, "/captest") != 0 && got[0] == '/');
466:
467:    /* S5: a value that does not fit is REFUSED, never silently shortened.  A
468:     * truncated value is a DIFFERENT value, so the write would "succeed" and
469:     * the matching read would miss — the failure mode this replaces. */
470:    {
471:      char big[512];
472:      memset(big, 'x', sizeof(big) - 1);
473:      big[sizeof(big) - 1] = '\0';
474:      int r = setenv("CAPTEST_BIG", big, 1);
475:      check(win_id, "env-oversize-refused-not-truncated", r != 0);
476:      check(win_id, "env-oversize-left-unset",
477:            getenv("CAPTEST_BIG") == (char *)0);
478:    }
479:
480:    /* Same property one layer down, at the registry seam itself — this bit
481:     * EVERY long registry write, not just the environment. */
482:    {
483:      char big[512];
484:      memset(big, 'y', sizeof(big) - 1);
485:      big[sizeof(big) - 1] = '\0';
486:      check(win_id, "registry-oversize-value-refused",
487:            OS1_registry_set("captest.big", big) != 0);
488:    }
489:
490:    /* Writing a COMPUTED field is meaningless, not merely unprivileged: it
491:     * must be refused rather than stored as a node the computed value would
492:     * then shadow forever. */
493:    snprintf(k, sizeof(k), "sys.proc.%d.name", get_pid());
494:    check(win_id, "vproc-computed-field-readonly",
495:          OS1_registry_set(k, "hijacked") != 0);
496:    memset(v, 0, sizeof(v));
497:    check(win_id, "vproc-name-still-true",
498:          OS1_registry_get(k, v, sizeof(v)) == 0 && strcmp(v, "hijacked") != 0);
499:
500:    /* Another process's environment is not ours to write. */
501:    check(win_id, "env-other-process-denied",
502:          OS1_registry_set("sys.proc.1.env.CAPTEST", "x") != 0);
503:  }
504:
505:  /* ============ exit status survives reaping (Phase 9b) ================= */
506:  section(win_id, "exit status retention");
507:  {
508:    /* A child that fails FAST is reaped before its parent polls, and the status
509:     * used to die with the corpse — so a FAILING command reported SUCCESS.
510:     * Timing-dependent, hence it looked like flakiness.  Spawn a child that
511:     * exits non-zero immediately and only THEN wait, which is the losing order. */
512:    char *av[3];
513:    av[0] = (char *)"/bin/lua";
514:    av[1] = (char *)"-e";
515:    av[2] = (char *)"os.exit(3)";
516:    int pid = (int)spawn_args("/bin/lua", 3, av);
517:    check(win_id, "status-child-spawned", pid > 0);
518:    if (pid > 0) {
519:      /* Give it time to die AND be collected, so we are testing the retained
520:       * status rather than racing the corpse. */
521:      for (int i = 0; i < 60; i++)
522:        OS1_sleep(15);
523:      int st = 0;
524:      int w = waitpid(pid, &st, 0);
525:      check(win_id, "status-reported-after-reap", w == pid);
526:      printf("[captest] status raw=0x%x exited=%d code=%d signalled=%d\n", st,
527:             WIFEXITED(st) ? 1 : 0, WEXITSTATUS(st), WIFSIGNALED(st) ? 1 : 0);
528:      check(win_id, "status-nonzero-survives", w == pid && WIFEXITED(st) &&
529:                                                   WEXITSTATUS(st) == 3);
530:      /* Collected once, like a real wait(): a second call must NOT re-report. */
531:      int st2 = 0;
532:      check(win_id, "status-consumed-once", waitpid(pid, &st2, 0) != pid);
533:    }
534:  }
535:
536:  /* ===================== execution service (Phase 9) ==================== */
537:  section(win_id, "exec service");
538:  {
539:    /* Connect — never spawn.  A client that spawned the service would get an
540:     * UNPRIVILEGED one (monotonic creator clamp), and the daemon's defining
541:     * powers (SETOWNER, taking client fds) are privileged-only: it would answer
542:     * requests but silently fail to delegate.  The service is started by init. */
543:    int svc = OS1_port_open(OS1NX_PORT_EXEC);
544:    check(win_id, "exec-service-published", svc >= 0);
545:
546:    if (svc >= 0) {
547:      int reqp[2] = {-1, -1}, repp[2] = {-1, -1};
548:      ok = pipe(reqp) == 0 && pipe(repp) == 0;
549:      check(win_id, "exec-channels", ok);
550:
551:      if (ok) {
552:        /* Build a variable-size request: header + [redir][cwd\0][argv\0...]. */
553:        struct execsvc_spawn_hdr hdr;
554:        char body[256];
555:        unsigned int off = 0;
556:        const char *a0 = "/bin/lua", *a1 = "-e", *a2 = "os.exit(0)";
557:        memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr));
558:        hdr.version = EXECSVC_VERSION;
559:        hdr.argc = 3;
560:        hdr.nredir = 0;
561:        body[off++] = '\0'; /* cwd: empty */
562:        memcpy(body + off, a0, strlen(a0) + 1); off += strlen(a0) + 1;
563:        memcpy(body + off, a1, strlen(a1) + 1); off += strlen(a1) + 1;
564:        memcpy(body + off, a2, strlen(a2) + 1); off += strlen(a2) + 1;
565:        hdr.body_len = off;
566:
567:        struct ipc_message m;
568:        memset(&m, 0, sizeof(m));
569:        m.type = EXECSVC_REQ_SPAWN;
570:
571:        /* Transfer the two channels THROUGH the port.  A handle index only means
572:         * something in one process's table, so the rights must travel with the
573:         * message; the kernel installs them in the service and rewrites the
574:         * leading payload slots with the indices IT will see.  Doing this by
575:         * cap_grant instead would need the service's PID — dragging pid
576:         * addressing back into the one path that exists to remove it. */
577:        int give[2] = {reqp[0], repp[1]};
578:        long sent = OS1_port_send_caps(svc, &m, give, 2);
579:        check(win_id, "exec-caps-transferred", sent == (long)sizeof(m));
580:
581:        if (sent == (long)sizeof(m)) {
582:          /* The service reads the request body from the pipe we handed it. */
583:          write(reqp[1], (const char *)&hdr, sizeof(hdr));
584:          write(reqp[1], body, off);
585:          close(reqp[1]); /* EOF, so a short body cannot hang the service */
586:
587:          struct execsvc_spawn_rep rep;
588:          memset(&rep, 0, sizeof(rep));
589:          long got = read(repp[0], (char *)&rep, sizeof(rep));
590:          check(win_id, "exec-reply-received", got == (long)sizeof(rep));
591:          check(win_id, "exec-spawned-pid", got == (long)sizeof(rep) &&
592:                                                 rep.pid > 0);
593:          /* THE Q3 PROPERTY: the job must belong to US, not to the service that
594:           * mechanically spawned it — otherwise a shell migrated onto the daemon
595:           * would silently lose kill/stop/cont over its own jobs. */
596:          check(win_id, "exec-owner-is-requester",
597:                got == (long)sizeof(rep) && rep.owner_pid == get_pid());
598:          if (got == (long)sizeof(rep) && rep.pid > 0)
599:            kill_process(rep.pid);
600:        } else {
601:          close(reqp[1]);
602:        }
603:
604:        close(reqp[0]);
605:        close(repp[0]);
606:        close(repp[1]);
607:      }
608:      OS1low_handle_close(svc);
609:    }
610:  }
611:
612:  if (hd >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(hd);
613:  if (h2 >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(h2);
614:  if (ph >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(ph);
615:  if (hng >= 0) OS1low_handle_close(hng);
616:
617:  printf_win(win_id, "done: %d/%d passed, %d failure(s)\n", checks - failures,
618:             checks, failures);
619:  printf("[captest] done: %d/%d passed, %d failure(s)\n", checks - failures,
620:         checks, failures);
621:
622:  for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++)
623:    yield();
624:  return failures ? 1 : 0;
625:}

@@@ user/bin/coreutils_test.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/coreutils_test.c
3: * Minimal smoke-test harness for the NexsOS1 GNU Coreutils port.
4: *
5: * This is intentionally a runtime validation program, not a host emulator or
6: * Linux-compat layer test. It exercises the real userland execution path:
7: *  - user app -> libc system() -> /sys/bin/nxshell -c <cmd> -> spawn()
8: *  - kernel process creation with the OS1 ABI
9: */
10:
11:#include <os1.h>
12:#include <stdio.h>
13:#include <stdlib.h>
14:#include <string.h>
15:
16:struct coreutils_case {
17:    const char *name;
18:    const char *cmd;
19:    int expect_nonzero;
20:};
21:
22:static int run_case(const struct coreutils_case *tc) {
23:    int rc = system(tc->cmd);
24:    int ok = (tc->expect_nonzero) ? (rc != 0) : (rc == 0);
25:
26:    printf("[%s] %s -> rc=%d %s\n",
27:           ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL",
28:           tc->name,
29:           rc,
30:           tc->cmd);
31:    return ok ? 0 : 1;
32:}
33:
34:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
35:    (void)argc;
36:    (void)argv;
37:
38:    const struct coreutils_case tests[] = {
39:        { "echo", "echo coreutils-ok", 0 },
40:        { "uname", "uname -s", 0 },
41:        { "pwd", "pwd", 0 },
42:        { "basename", "basename /bin/echo", 0 },
43:        { "dirname", "dirname /bin/echo", 0 },
44:        { "printenv", "printenv PATH", 0 },
45:        { "true", "true", 0 },
46:        { "false", "false", 1 },
47:        { "sleep", "sleep 0", 0 },
48:        { "mkdir", "mkdir /tmp/nxctestdir", 0 },
49:        { "touch", "touch /tmp/nxctestdir/file.txt", 0 },
50:        { "cat", "cat /tmp/nxctestdir/file.txt", 0 },
51:        { "wc", "wc -c /etc/init.cfg", 0 },
52:        { "head", "head -n 2 /etc/init.cfg", 0 },
53:        { "tail", "tail -n 1 /etc/init.cfg", 0 },
54:        { "unlink", "unlink /tmp/nxctestdir/file.txt", 0 },
55:        { "rmdir", "rmdir /tmp/nxctestdir", 0 },
56:        { "sync", "sync", 0 },
57:        { "whoami", "whoami", 0 },
58:        { "seq", "seq 1 3", 0 },
59:        { "basename2", "basename /etc/init.cfg", 0 },
60:        { "dirname2", "dirname /etc/init.cfg", 0 },
61:        { "readlink", "readlink /bin/echo", 0 },
62:        { "realpath", "realpath /bin/echo", 0 },
63:        { "tty", "tty", 0 }
64:    };
65:
66:    int failed = 0;
67:    const size_t ntests = sizeof(tests) / sizeof(tests[0]);
68:
69:    printf("=== NexsOS1 Coreutils Runtime Smoke Test ===\n");
70:    for (size_t i = 0; i < ntests; i++) {
71:        failed += run_case(&tests[i]);
72:    }
73:
74:    printf("summary: %zu test(s), %d failure(s)\n", ntests, failed);
75:    return failed == 0 ? 0 : 1;
76:}

@@@ user/bin/counter.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/counter.c
3: * Counter Demo — animated progress-bar window
4: *
5: * Demonstrates the compositor window API: creates a small window, then in a
6: * tight loop draws a dark background and an incrementing green progress bar
7: * whose width cycles through 0..198 pixels (i % 100 * 2).
8: *
9: * Every 256 (0x100) iterations the current counter value is printed to UART
10: * via print_hex() to give a heartbeat on the serial console.
11: *
12: * text rendering:
13: *   window_draw() only fills solid rectangles; there is no userland text
14: *   renderer available via this syscall, so the counter value cannot be shown
15: *   as digits in the window.  UART output is the fallback.
16: *
17: * Known issues:
18: *   USR-BLOAT-01 (W2 BAD-IMPL·PERF) counter.elf is ~503KB [verified]; 70% is
19: *                DWARF debug data (-g), ~52KB is stb_image/stb_easy_font from
20: *                lib.o that counter never uses.
21: *   USR-BLOAT-02 (W2 BAD-IMPL) No --gc-sections or strip step in the link
22: *                rule; debug symbols not removed for release builds.
23: */
24:#include <os1.h>
25:
26:/* Duplicate #include <os1.h> below is a copy-paste artifact; harmless due to
27: * header include guards but indicates sloppy editing. */
28:#include <os1.h>
29:
30:/*
31: * main - counter entry point; does not return.
32: *
33: * Creates a 200x100 compositor window at (700, 50).  On each iteration:
34: *   1. Fills background with dark grey (0xFF222222).
35: *   2. Draws a green bar of width (i % 100)*2 pixels — a visual progress
36: *      indicator cycling every 100 increments.
37: *   3. Calls flush() (-> SYS_FLUSH/#201) to push the update to the display.
38: *   4. Every 256 iterations prints the counter to UART for serial monitoring.
39: *   5. Sleeps ~100ms (real milliseconds) between frames.
40: *
41: * Returns 1 if window creation fails; never returns otherwise.
42: */
43:int main(void) {
44:  print("Counter Process Started\n");
45:
46:  char title[32];
47:  sprintf(title, "Counter PID %d", get_pid());
48:  int win = create_window(700, 50, 200, 100, title);
49:  if (win <= 0) {
50:    print("Counter: Failed to create window\n");
51:    return 1;
52:  }
53:
54:  int i = 0;
55:  while (1) {
56:    /* Draw Background */
57:    window_draw(win, 0, 0, 200, 100, 0xFFFCFCFD);
58:
59:    /* Draw Count */
60:    /* Crude digit drawing or assume window_draw handles text? No, it's just
61:       rects. We need a text drawing helper. For now, just visually flash or use
62:       printf to UART. */
63:    /* Since we don't have window_draw_text in lib.c yet, we rely on UART for
64:       text. But to satisfy "drawing correctly", I should draw a progress bar or
65:       rect! */
66:
67:    /* Progress bar: width cycles 0..198 pixels (i%100 * 2), green fill. */
68:    int bar_width = (i % 100) * 2;
69:    window_draw(win, 10, 40, bar_width, 20, 0xFF00FF00);
70:
71:    /* Flush global compositor */
72:    // _sys_compositor_render();
73:    // Wait, flush() does that.
74:    flush();
75:
76:    /* Print counter to UART every 256 iterations as a serial heartbeat. */
77:    if ((i & 0xFF) == 0) {
78:      print("Count: ");
79:      print_hex(i);
80:      print("\n");
81:    }
82:    i++;
83:
84:    /* Sleep ~100ms between frames (OS1_sleep() now takes milliseconds). */
85:    OS1_sleep(100);
86:  }
87:
88:  return 0;
89:}

@@@ user/bin/crash.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/crash.c
3: * Kernel Fault Handler Test — intentional null pointer dereference
4: *
5: * This process deliberately dereferences address 0 to trigger a hardware
6: * exception (data abort on AArch64, page fault on x86-64).  Its purpose is
7: * to verify that the kernel's fault handler correctly catches the exception,
8: * terminates the offending process, and does not corrupt the rest of the
9: * system.
10: *
11: * The `volatile` qualifier on p prevents the compiler from optimising away
12: * the write even in optimised builds (-O2).
13: *
14: * Known issues:
15: *   USR-BLOAT-01 (W2 BAD-IMPL·PERF) crash.elf is ~502KB [verified], almost
16: *                entirely DWARF debug data and stb_image from lib.o — none of
17: *                which is used by this 9-line binary.
18: *   USR-BLOAT-02 (W2 BAD-IMPL) -g debug symbols and -fno-omit-frame-pointer
19: *                are retained with no strip step.
20: */
21:#include <os1.h>
22:
23:/*
24: * main - triggers a null pointer dereference and does not return.
25: *
26: * After the write to address 0 the kernel should fault-terminate this process.
27: * The `return 0` is unreachable dead code.
28: */
29:int main(void) {
30:  printf("Crash test starting...\n");
31:  /* Trigger a null pointer dereference to test kernel fault handling */
32:  volatile int *p = (int *)0;
33:  *p = 123;   /* Expected: data abort / page fault at address 0x0 */
34:  return 0;
35:}

@@@ user/bin/demo3d.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/demo3d.c
3: * Solid 3D Cube Demo — fixed-point software rasterizer
4: *
5: * Implements a real-time rotating solid cube with:
6: *   - Fixed-point 16.16 arithmetic throughout (FP_SHIFT=16, FP_ONE=65536).
7: *   - Per-axis rotation (rotate_x, rotate_y) using cos_fp/sin_fp from
8: *     kernel/lib/math.c (included via lib.c).
9: *   - Perspective projection (project) with a focal distance of 3*FP_ONE;
10: *     z is clamped to 100 to prevent division by zero near the camera.
11: *   - Backface culling via the Z component of the cross product of two face
12: *     edge vectors (nz < 0 means the face is visible from the camera).
13: *   - Flat shading: intensity is proportional to -nz (more face-on = brighter).
14: *   - Scan-line fill (fill_triangle): splits each quadrilateral into two
15: *     triangles and fills each with an integer step-interpolation rasterizer.
16: *   - Double-buffer-style rendering: the full frame is composed into the
17: *     static framebuffer[] array and uploaded with a single window_blit() call.
18: *
19: * The Italian-language comments in the main loop and fill_triangle describe
20: * the mathematical steps in the original author's language; they are preserved
21: * here as written.
22: */
23:#include <os1.h>
24:
25:#include "../sys/lib/portability/d3d9/os1_d3d9_present.h"
26:
27:/* Fixed-point 16.16 format:
28: *   FP_SHIFT = 16: lower 16 bits are the fractional part.
29: *   FP_ONE   = 65536 = 1.0 in fixed-point.
30: * DEG_TO_FP_RAD, cos_fp, sin_fp, fixmul are defined in kernel/lib/math.c
31: * (included transitively via lib.c). */
32:#ifndef FP_SHIFT
33:#define FP_SHIFT 16
34:#endif /* FP_SHIFT */
35:#ifndef FP_ONE
36:#define FP_ONE (1 << FP_SHIFT)
37:#endif /* FP_ONE */
38:
39:#define WIN_W 300
40:#define WIN_H 250
41:#define BUFFER_SIZE (WIN_W * WIN_H)
42:
43:/* framebuffer: the D3D9-style swapchain's locked backbuffer for the current
44: * frame.  The cube is rasterized CPU-side into it, then shown with one
45: * Present() — the same lock/draw/unlock/present cycle the D3D9 personality
46: * will drive, exercised here end to end. */
47:static unsigned int *framebuffer;
48:
49:/* vec3_t: a 3D point in fixed-point 16.16 space.
50: * All arithmetic on these values uses fixmul() for multiplication and
51: * right-shifts for division by powers of two. */
52:typedef struct {
53:  int x, y, z; /* Fixed-point 16.16 */
54:} vec3_t;
55:
56:/* NUM_VERTS=8: the 8 corners of a cube (+-s in each axis). */
57:#define NUM_VERTS 8
58:static vec3_t verts[NUM_VERTS];
59:
60:/*
61: * init_shape - populate the 8 cube vertices with half-size s.
62: *
63: * s is in fixed-point units.  The cube spans [-s, s] in all three axes.
64: * Vertices are enumerated in a consistent order that matches the face
65: * definitions in faces[][] below.
66: *
67: * Called once at startup with s = FP_ONE/3 (a cube of radius ~0.33 units).
68: */
69:static void init_shape(int s) {
70:  verts[0] = (vec3_t){-s, -s, -s};
71:  verts[1] = (vec3_t){s, -s, -s};
72:  verts[2] = (vec3_t){s, s, -s};
73:  verts[3] = (vec3_t){-s, s, -s};
74:  verts[4] = (vec3_t){-s, -s, s};
75:  verts[5] = (vec3_t){s, -s, s};
76:  verts[6] = (vec3_t){s, s, s};
77:  verts[7] = (vec3_t){-s, s, s};
78:}
79:
80:/* faces[6][4]: each row is one quad face, listing 4 vertex indices in
81: * counter-clockwise winding order as seen from outside the cube.
82: * The backface culling test uses the sign of the 3D cross-product Z component
83: * of the first two edges; CCW winding means nz < 0 -> face towards camera. */
84:static int faces[6][4] = {
85:    {0, 3, 2, 1}, /* Front */
86:    {4, 5, 6, 7}, /* Back */
87:    {4, 7, 3, 0}, /* Left */
88:    {1, 2, 6, 5}, /* Right */
89:    {3, 7, 6, 2}, /* Top */
90:    {4, 0, 1, 5}  /* Bottom */
91:};
92:
93:/* face_colors[6]: base RGB colour for each face; shaded at render time by the
94: * flat-shading intensity derived from the face normal's Z component. */
95:static unsigned int face_colors[6] = {
96:    0xFF3333, /* Red */
97:    0x33FF33, /* Green */
98:    0x3333FF, /* Blue */
99:    0xFFFF33, /* Yellow */
100:    0x33FFFF, /* Cyan */
101:    0xFF33FF  /* Magenta */
102:};
103:
104:/*
105: * rotate_y - rotate a fixed-point 3D point around the Y axis.
106: *
107: * angle: rotation angle in degrees (converted to fixed-point radians via
108: *        DEG_TO_FP_RAD before calling cos_fp/sin_fp).
109: *
110: * Standard 2D rotation of the xz plane:
111: *   x' = x*cos - z*sin
112: *   z' = x*sin + z*cos
113: * y is unchanged.  fixmul() performs 16.16 * 16.16 -> 16.16 multiplication.
114: */
115:static vec3_t rotate_y(vec3_t p, int angle) {
116:  int rad = DEG_TO_FP_RAD(angle);
117:  int c = cos_fp(rad);
118:  int s = sin_fp(rad);
119:  vec3_t r;
120:  r.x = fixmul(p.x, c) - fixmul(p.z, s);
121:  r.y = p.y;
122:  r.z = fixmul(p.x, s) + fixmul(p.z, c);
123:  return r;
124:}
125:
126:/*
127: * rotate_x - rotate a fixed-point 3D point around the X axis.
128: *
129: * Standard rotation of the yz plane:
130: *   y' = y*cos - z*sin
131: *   z' = y*sin + z*cos
132: * x is unchanged.
133: */
134:static vec3_t rotate_x(vec3_t p, int angle) {
135:  int rad = DEG_TO_FP_RAD(angle);
136:  int c = cos_fp(rad);
137:  int s = sin_fp(rad);
138:  vec3_t r;
139:  r.x = p.x;
140:  r.y = fixmul(p.y, c) - fixmul(p.z, s);
141:  r.z = fixmul(p.y, s) + fixmul(p.z, c);
142:  return r;
143:}
144:
145:/* Project 3D to 2D */
146:static void project(vec3_t p, int *sx, int *sy) {
147:  int dist = 3 * FP_ONE;
148:  int z_eff = p.z + dist;
149:  if (z_eff < 100)
150:    z_eff = 100;
151:
152:  long long x_proj = ((long long)p.x * dist) / z_eff;
153:  long long y_proj = ((long long)p.y * dist) / z_eff;
154:
155:  int proj_x = (int)(x_proj >> 8);
156:  int proj_y = (int)(y_proj >> 8);
157:
158:  /* Scala ridotta al 75% per rientrare nella finestra senza risultare troppo
159:   * piccola */
160:  *sx = WIN_W / 2 + (proj_x * 3) / 4;
161:  *sy = WIN_H / 2 - (proj_y * 3) / 4;
162:}
163:
164:/* * Flat-shaded software triangle rasterizer
165: * Splits the generic triangle into top and bottom flat sections.
166: */
167:static void fill_triangle(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2, int x3, int y3,
168:                          unsigned int color) {
169:  /* Sort vertices by Y ascending */
170:  if (y1 > y2) {
171:    int t = x1;
172:    x1 = x2;
173:    x2 = t;
174:    t = y1;
175:    y1 = y2;
176:    y2 = t;
177:  }
178:  if (y2 > y3) {
179:    int t = x2;
180:    x2 = x3;
181:    x3 = t;
182:    t = y2;
183:    y2 = y3;
184:    y3 = t;
185:  }
186:  if (y1 > y2) {
187:    int t = x1;
188:    x1 = x2;
189:    x2 = t;
190:    t = y1;
191:    y1 = y2;
192:    y2 = t;
193:  }
194:
195:  if (y1 == y3)
196:    return; /* Degenerate */
197:
198:  long long dx13 = x3 - x1;
199:  long long dy13 = y3 - y1;
200:  long long step13 = dy13 ? (dx13 << 16) / dy13 : 0;
201:
202:  long long curx1 = (long long)x1 << 16;
203:  long long curx2 = (long long)x1 << 16;
204:
205:  /* Top half */
206:  if (y2 > y1) {
207:    long long dx12 = x2 - x1;
208:    long long dy12 = y2 - y1;
209:    long long step12 = dy12 ? (dx12 << 16) / dy12 : 0;
210:    for (int y = y1; y < y2; y++) {
211:      int cx1 = curx1 >> 16;
212:      int cx2 = curx2 >> 16;
213:      if (cx1 > cx2) {
214:        int t = cx1;
215:        cx1 = cx2;
216:        cx2 = t;
217:      }
218:
219:      if (y >= 0 && y < WIN_H) {
220:        int start = cx1 < 0 ? 0 : cx1;
221:        int end = cx2 >= WIN_W ? WIN_W - 1 : cx2;
222:        for (int x = start; x <= end; x++) {
223:          framebuffer[y * WIN_W + x] = color;
224:        }
225:      }
226:      curx1 += step13;
227:      curx2 += step12;
228:    }
229:  }
230:
231:  /* Bottom half */
232:  curx2 = (long long)x2 << 16;
233:  if (y3 > y2) {
234:    long long dx23 = x3 - x2;
235:    long long dy23 = y3 - y2;
236:    long long step23 = dy23 ? (dx23 << 16) / dy23 : 0;
237:    for (int y = y2; y <= y3; y++) {
238:      int cx1 = curx1 >> 16;
239:      int cx2 = curx2 >> 16;
240:      if (cx1 > cx2) {
241:        int t = cx1;
242:        cx1 = cx2;
243:        cx2 = t;
244:      }
245:
246:      if (y >= 0 && y < WIN_H) {
247:        int start = cx1 < 0 ? 0 : cx1;
248:        int end = cx2 >= WIN_W ? WIN_W - 1 : cx2;
249:        for (int x = start; x <= end; x++) {
250:          framebuffer[y * WIN_W + x] = color;
251:        }
252:      }
253:      curx1 += step13;
254:      curx2 += step23;
255:    }
256:  }
257:}
258:
259:/* Clear framebuffer */
260:static void clear_buffer(unsigned int color) {
261:  if (color == 0) {
262:    memset(framebuffer, 0, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(unsigned int));
263:  } else {
264:    unsigned int *ptr = framebuffer;
265:    int n = BUFFER_SIZE;
266:    while (n-- > 0)
267:      *ptr++ = color;
268:  }
269:}
270:
271:int main(void) {
272:  int pid = get_pid();
273:  char title[64];
274:  sprintf(title, "3D Demo (Solid Cube) PID %d", pid);
275:
276:  /* Presentation chain: the D3D9-style swapchain over os1_video_platform. */
277:  struct os1_d3d9_present_params params = {50, 50, WIN_W, WIN_H, title};
278:  struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain = 0;
279:  if (os1_d3d9_swapchain_create(&params, &swapchain) != 0) {
280:    print("[Demo3D] Error creating swapchain\n");
281:    exit(1);
282:  }
283:
284:  /* The swapchain's own window already exists at this point (sw_create ->
285:   * os1_video_window_create -> _sys_create_window) — a plain printf() here
286:   * would draw text straight into demo3d's own backbuffer via the console
287:   * fallback, so this goes through the existing notification popup
288:   * (OS1_notify_post, lib.c) instead. */
289:  char msg[64];
290:  snprintf(msg, sizeof(msg), "Real Solid GL Engine Init. PID %d (backend %d)",
291:           pid, os1_d3d9_swapchain_backend(swapchain));
292:  OS1_notify_post("Demo3D", msg);
293:
294:  /* Cube size scaled to fit window optimally */
295:  init_shape(FP_ONE / 3);
296:
297:  int angle_y = 0;
298:  int angle_x = 0;
299:
300:  while (1) {
301:    /* Lock the backbuffer for CPU rasterization (D3D9 LockRect cycle).  The
302:     * cube rasterizer assumes a tight WIN_W-pixel pitch; the software backend
303:     * guarantees it, a future GPU backend may not. */
304:    struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect locked;
305:    if (os1_d3d9_swapchain_lock(swapchain, &locked) != 0 ||
306:        locked.pitch != WIN_W * sizeof(unsigned int)) {
307:      print("[Demo3D] Backbuffer lock failed\n");
308:      break;
309:    }
310:    framebuffer = locked.bits;
311:
312:    clear_buffer(0); /* Dark gray background */
313:
314:    vec3_t transformed[NUM_VERTS];
315:    int sx[NUM_VERTS], sy[NUM_VERTS];
316:
317:    /* Trasformazione e proiezione matematica dei vertici */
318:    for (int i = 0; i < NUM_VERTS; i++) {
319:      vec3_t v = verts[i];
320:      v = rotate_x(v, angle_x);
321:      v = rotate_y(v, angle_y);
322:      transformed[i] = v;
323:      project(v, &sx[i], &sy[i]);
324:    }
325:
326:    /* Rasterizzazione delle 6 facce */
327:    for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
328:      vec3_t t0 = transformed[faces[i][0]];
329:      vec3_t t1 = transformed[faces[i][1]];
330:      vec3_t t2 = transformed[faces[i][2]];
331:
332:      /* Vettori sullo spazio 3D trasformato per cross product */
333:      long long v1x = t1.x - t0.x;
334:      long long v1y = t1.y - t0.y;
335:      long long v2x = t2.x - t0.x;
336:      long long v2y = t2.y - t0.y;
337:
338:      /* Calcolo normale Asse Z (Profondità) ridotto in scala */
339:      long long nz = (v1x * v2y - v1y * v2x) >> FP_SHIFT;
340:
341:      /* Backface culling e Shading (nz < 0 = faccia rivolta alla telecamera) */
342:      if (nz < 0) {
343:        long long max_nz =
344:            (4 * FP_ONE) /
345:            9; /* Massima estensione derivata dalla scala FP_ONE / 3 */
346:        if (max_nz == 0)
347:          max_nz = 1;
348:
349:        int ambient = 40;
350:        int intensity = ambient + (int)((-nz * (255 - ambient)) / max_nz);
351:        if (intensity > 255)
352:          intensity = 255;
353:        if (intensity < 0)
354:          intensity = 0;
355:
356:        /* Applicazione intensità Flat Shading sul colore base */
357:        unsigned int base = face_colors[i];
358:        int r = ((base >> 16) & 0xFF) * intensity / 255;
359:        int g = ((base >> 8) & 0xFF) * intensity / 255;
360:        int b = (base & 0xFF) * intensity / 255;
361:        unsigned int shaded = 0xFF000000 | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
362:
363:        int s0x = sx[faces[i][0]], s0y = sy[faces[i][0]];
364:        int s1x = sx[faces[i][1]], s1y = sy[faces[i][1]];
365:        int s2x = sx[faces[i][2]], s2y = sy[faces[i][2]];
366:        int s3x = sx[faces[i][3]], s3y = sy[faces[i][3]];
367:
368:        /* Costruzione delle primitive a triangolo */
369:        fill_triangle(s0x, s0y, s1x, s1y, s2x, s2y, shaded);
370:        fill_triangle(s0x, s0y, s2x, s2y, s3x, s3y, shaded);
371:      }
372:    }
373:
374:    /* Unlock + Present: one full-frame presentation per cycle. */
375:    os1_d3d9_swapchain_unlock(swapchain);
376:    if (os1_d3d9_swapchain_present(swapchain, 0) != 0) {
377:      print("[Demo3D] Present failed\n");
378:      break;
379:    }
380:
381:    /* Modifica i gradi di rotazione limitandoli a 360 per prevenire overflow
382:     * numerici */
383:    angle_x = (angle_x + 1) % 360;
384:    angle_y = (angle_y + 2) % 360;
385:
386:    /* Frame pacing ~60 FPS via il timer reale (sleep bloccante in ms): senza
387:     * questo il loop di rendering girava a CPU piena. */
388:    OS1_sleep(16);
389:  }
390:
391:  os1_d3d9_swapchain_destroy(swapchain);
392:  exit(0);
393:  return 0;
394:}

@@@ user/bin/env.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/env.c
3: * Standard 'env' command utility for NexsOS1.
4: */
5:#include <os1.h>
6:#include <stdio.h>
7:#include <stdlib.h>
8:#include <string.h>
9:
10:static int print_environment(void) {
11:    char buf[4096];
12:    int n = OS1_env_enum(buf, sizeof(buf));
13:    if (n < 0)
14:        return -1;
15:
16:    char *save = NULL;
17:    for (char *k = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); k; k = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save)) {
18:        const char *value = getenv(k);
19:        printf("%s=%s\n", k, value ? value : "");
20:    }
21:    return 0;
22:}
23:
24:static int spawn_with_stdio_passthrough(const char *path, int argc,
25:                                       char *const argv[]) {
26:    struct spawn_redir redir[3];
27:    int nredir = 0;
28:
29:    for (int fd = 0; fd < 3; fd++) {
30:        if (OS1low_cap_query(fd) < 0)
31:            continue;
32:        redir[nredir].child_fd = fd;
33:        redir[nredir].parent_fd = fd;
34:        redir[nredir].source_pid = 0;
35:        nredir++;
36:    }
37:
38:    if (nredir == 0)
39:        return _sys_spawn(path, argc, argv, 0);
40:
41:    return _sys_spawn_redir(path, argc, argv, 0, redir, nredir);
42:}
43:
44:int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
45:    int i = 1;
46:    int clear_env = 0;
47:
48:    while (i < argc) {
49:        if (strcmp(argv[i], "-i") == 0) {
50:            clear_env = 1;
51:            i++;
52:            continue;
53:        }
54:
55:        if (strcmp(argv[i], "-u") == 0) {
56:            if (i + 1 >= argc) {
57:                fprintf(stderr, "env: option requires an argument -- 'u'\n");
58:                return 125;
59:            }
60:            unsetenv(argv[++i]);
61:            i++;
62:            continue;
63:        }
64:
65:        if (strchr(argv[i], '=')) {
66:            char *eq = strchr(argv[i], '=');
67:            *eq = '\0';
68:            if (setenv(argv[i], eq + 1, 1) != 0) {
69:                fprintf(stderr, "env: unable to set %s\n", argv[i]);
70:                return 125;
71:            }
72:            i++;
73:            continue;
74:        }
75:
76:        break;
77:    }
78:
79:    if (clear_env) {
80:        clearenv();
81:        /* Re-apply assignments after the reset so NAME=value pairs still work. */
82:        int j = 1;
83:        while (j < i) {
84:            if (strcmp(argv[j], "-i") == 0 || strcmp(argv[j], "-u") == 0) {
85:                j++;
86:                if (strcmp(argv[j - 1], "-u") == 0 && j < argc)
87:                    j++;
88:                continue;
89:            }
90:            if (strchr(argv[j], '=')) {
91:                char *eq = strchr(argv[j], '=');
92:                *eq = '\0';
93:                setenv(argv[j], eq + 1, 1);
94:            }
95:            j++;
96:        }
97:    }
98:
99:    if (i >= argc) {
100:        return print_environment() == 0 ? 0 : 125;
101:    }
102:
103:    /* Command specified: spawn it */
104:    const char *cmd = argv[i];
105:    char path[256];
106:
107:    int pid = -1;
108:    int sub_argc = argc - i;
109:    char *const *sub_argv = &argv[i];
110:
111:    /* Try exact path first */
112:    pid = spawn_with_stdio_passthrough(cmd, sub_argc, sub_argv);
113:
114:    /* Try /bin/cmd if relative */
115:    if (pid < 0 && cmd[0] != '/') {
116:        snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/bin/%s", cmd);
117:        pid = spawn_with_stdio_passthrough(path, sub_argc, sub_argv);
118:    }
119:
120:    /* Try /sys/bin/cmd if relative */
121:    if (pid < 0 && cmd[0] != '/') {
122:        snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/sys/bin/%s", cmd);
123:        pid = spawn_with_stdio_passthrough(path, sub_argc, sub_argv);
124:    }
125:
126:    if (pid < 0) {
127:        fprintf(stderr, "env: %s: No such file or directory\n", cmd);
128:        return 127;
129:    }
130:
131:    int code = 0;
132:    OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code);
133:    return code;
134:}
135:

@@@ user/bin/fdtest.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/fdtest.c
3: * Per-process fd-table test app (ABI-03, epic #93).
4: *
5: * Exercises the POSIX-style descriptor path end to end against the rootfs
6: * file /etc/init.cfg (also used by writetest — config files are writable,
7: * /bin and /sys are not):
8: *   1. open(O_RDONLY) returns a fd >= 3; sequential read()s advance the
9: *      offset (two reads return different, adjacent content);
10: *   2. lseek(SEEK_SET 0) rewinds: the next read returns the first bytes
11: *      again; lseek(SEEK_END 0) returns the file size (matches the
12: *      file_read size probe);
13: *   3. open(O_RDWR): write at offset 0 through the fd, lseek back, read
14: *      back and compare, then restore the original bytes;
15: *   4. denials: open("/bin/nxshell", O_WRONLY) -> -EACCES (user process),
16: *      open missing path -> -ENOENT, read/lseek on a closed fd -> -EBADF,
17: *      write on an O_RDONLY fd -> -EBADF, O_CREAT -> -EINVAL.
18: * Results go to the window AND the serial console (printf).
19: */
20:#include <fcntl.h>
21:#include <os1.h>
22:#include <string.h>
23:
24:static int failures = 0;
25:
26:static void check(int win_id, const char *name, int ok) {
27:  printf_win(win_id, "%s: %s\n", name, ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
28:  printf("[fdtest] %s: %s\n", name, ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
29:  if (!ok)
30:    failures++;
31:}
32:
33:int main(void) {
34:  int win_id = create_window(120, 120, 400, 300, "FD Test");
35:  if (win_id < 0)
36:    return 1;
37:
38:  const char *path = "/etc/init.cfg";
39:  char a[9], b[9], c[9], orig[9];
40:  int ok;
41:
42:  printf_win(win_id, "Testing fd table on %s...\n", path);
43:  printf("[fdtest] target %s\n", path);
44:
45:  /* 1. open + sequential reads advance the offset */
46:  int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
47:  ok = fd >= 3;
48:  if (ok) {
49:    memset(a, 0, sizeof(a));
50:    memset(b, 0, sizeof(b));
51:    ok = read(fd, a, 8) == 8 && read(fd, b, 8) == 8 &&
52:         memcmp(a, b, 8) != 0; /* adjacent chunks, not the same bytes */
53:  }
54:  check(win_id, "open+seq-read", ok);
55:
56:  /* 2. lseek rewind + SEEK_END == size probe */
57:  long size = file_read(path, (void *)0, 0, 0);
58:  memset(c, 0, sizeof(c));
59:  ok = lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) == 0 && read(fd, c, 8) == 8 &&
60:       memcmp(a, c, 8) == 0 && lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END) == size && size > 0;
61:  check(win_id, "lseek-rewind+end", ok);
62:
63:  /* 3. read-write fd: overwrite, read back, restore */
64:  int wfd = open(path, O_RDWR);
65:  ok = wfd >= 3 && wfd != fd;
66:  if (ok) {
67:    memset(orig, 0, sizeof(orig));
68:    ok = read(wfd, orig, 8) == 8 && lseek(wfd, 0, SEEK_SET) == 0;
69:    if (ok) {
70:      write(wfd, "FDTEST!!", 8);
71:      memset(c, 0, sizeof(c));
72:      ok = lseek(wfd, 0, SEEK_SET) == 0 && read(wfd, c, 8) == 8 &&
73:           memcmp(c, "FDTEST!!", 8) == 0;
74:      /* restore the original bytes whatever happened */
75:      lseek(wfd, 0, SEEK_SET);
76:      write(wfd, orig, 8);
77:    }
78:  }
79:  check(win_id, "rdwr-write-readback", ok);
80:
81:  /* 4a. capability: /bin is read-only for user processes */
82:  ok = open("/bin/nxshell", O_WRONLY) == -EACCES;
83:  check(win_id, "deny-bin-wronly", ok);
84:
85:  /* 4b. missing path, closed fd, mode and flag misuse */
86:  ok = open("/no/such/file", O_RDONLY) == -ENOENT;
87:  check(win_id, "enoent", ok);
88:
89:  int rfd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
90:  if (rfd >= 3) {
91:    /* write on an O_RDONLY fd must not modify the file (the userland
92:     * write() wrapper returns void, so verify by content) */
93:    write(rfd, "XXXXXXXX", 8);
94:  }
95:  memset(c, 0, sizeof(c));
96:  ok = rfd >= 3 && file_read(path, c, 8, 0) == 8 && memcmp(c, orig, 8) == 0;
97:  check(win_id, "deny-write-on-rdonly", ok);
98:
99:  ok = rfd >= 3 && close(rfd) == 0 && read(rfd, a, 1) == -EBADF &&
100:       lseek(rfd, 0, SEEK_SET) == -EBADF && close(rfd) == -EBADF;
101:  check(win_id, "ebadf-after-close", ok);
102:
103:  ok = open(path, O_RDONLY | O_CREAT) == -EINVAL;
104:  check(win_id, "einval-o-creat", ok);
105:
106:  if (fd >= 0)
107:    close(fd);
108:  if (wfd >= 0)
109:    close(wfd);
110:
111:  printf_win(win_id, "done: %d failure(s)\n", failures);
112:  printf("[fdtest] done: %d failure(s)\n", failures);
113:
114:  /* Keep the window up briefly so the result is visible interactively. */
115:  for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++)
116:    yield();
117:  return failures ? 1 : 0;
118:}
119:

@@@ user/bin/forkbomb.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/bin/forkbomb.c
3: * Resource-exhaustion / quota test (SCHED-DOS-01 #122).
4: *
5: * Runs as a standalone TTY graphical window app, creating its own
6: * canvas within the NEXS compositor to bypass FD inheritance limitations.
7: */
8:#include <os1.h>
9:
10:/* Helper locale per convertire interi in stringa nello stack */
11:static void local_itoa(int n, char *s) {
12:  int i, sign;
13:  if ((sign = n) < 0)
14:    n = -n;
15:  i = 0;
16:  do {
17:    s[i++] = n % 10 + '0';
18:  } while ((n /= 10) > 0);
19:  if (sign < 0)
20:    s[i++] = '-';
21:  s[i] = '\0';
22:  for (int j = 0, k = i - 1; j < k; j++, k--) {
23:    char temp = s[j];
24:    s[j] = s[k];
25:    s[k] = temp;
26:  }
27:}
28:
29:static int local_strlen(const char *s) {
30:  int len = 0;
31:  while (s[len] != '\0')
32:    len++;
33:  return len;
34:}
35:
36:int main(void) {
37:  int created = 0;
38:  char buf[32];
39:
40:  /* * Corretto secondo include/api/os1.h:
41:   * Coordinate: x=100, y=100, w=400, h=300, seguito dal Titolo.
42:   */
43:  int my_win = _sys_create_window(100, 100, 400, 300, "Forkbomb Sandbox TTY");
44:  if (my_win < 0) {
45:    print("[forkbomb] Errore: Impossibile allocare una nuova finestra TTY\n");
46:    return 1;
47:  }
48:
49:  /* Pulizia dello schermo e banner di avvio nella nuova finestra grafica */
50:  _sys_window_write(my_win, "\033[H\033[J", 6); // ANSI Clear Screen
51:  _sys_window_write(my_win, "\033[1;31m========================================\n",
52:             46);
53:  _sys_window_write(my_win, "  NEXS QUOTA DOS TEST (SCHED-DOS-01)\n", 37);
54:  _sys_window_write(my_win, "========================================\033[0m\n\n", 46);
55:
56:  _sys_window_write(my_win, "[TTY] Finestra inizializzata. PID: ", 35);
57:  local_itoa(get_pid(), buf);
58:  _sys_window_write(my_win, buf, local_strlen(buf));
59:  _sys_window_write(my_win,
60:             "\n[TTY] Avvio attacco controllato sulla coda dei processi...\n\n",
61:             60);
62:
63:  /* Ciclo di Forkbomb */
64:  for (int i = 0; i < 2000; i++) {
65:    int pid = spawn("/bin/counter");
66:    if (pid > 0) {
67:      created++;
68:
69:      /* Feedback visivo immediato nella finestra dedicata */
70:      _sys_window_write(my_win, "[+] Creato figlio PID: ", 23);
71:      local_itoa(pid, buf);
72:      _sys_window_write(my_win, buf, local_strlen(buf));
73:      _sys_window_write(my_win, "\n", 1);
74:    } else {
75:      /* La quota di protezione per-parent (32 processi) è scattata con
76:       * successo! */
77:      _sys_write(
78:          my_win,
79:          "\n\033[1;33m[!] STOP COMPULSIRE! Lo spawn e' stato rifiutato.\n",
80:          54);
81:      _sys_window_write(my_win, "[!] Totale figli allocati prima del blocco: ", 44);
82:      local_itoa(created, buf);
83:      _sys_window_write(my_win, buf, local_strlen(buf));
84:
85:      _sys_window_write(my_win, "\n[!] Codice di errore restituito dal kernel: ", 45);
86:      local_itoa(pid, buf);
87:      _sys_window_write(my_win, buf, local_strlen(buf));
88:      _sys_window_write(my_win, " (Quota attiva con successo)\033[0m\n", 34);
89:      break;
90:    }
91:
92:    /* Cediamo il passo alle altre CPU (SMP) per far ridisegnare i testi
93:     * correnti */
94:    yield();
95:  }
96:
97:  _sys_write(
98:      my_win,
99:      "\n\033[1;32m[OK] Sistema protetto. La shell originale e' reattiva.\n",
100:      61);
101:  _sys_window_write(my_win,
102:             "[OK] Puoi fare 'kill' di questo processo in sicurezza.\033[0m\n",
103:             61);
104:
105:  /* Rimane in ascolto indefinito per consentire l'ispezione visiva */
106:  while (1) {
107:    yield();
108:  }
109:
110:  return 0;
111:}

149:    test_inttostr();
150:    test_bitrotate();
151:    test_gl_list();
152:    test_gnulib_os1_glue();
153:    test_gnulib_vfs_io();
154:
155:    int total_suites = 7;
156:    int passed_suites = (g_failed == 0) ? total_suites : (total_suites - g_failed);
157:    if (passed_suites < 0) passed_suites = 0;
158:
159:    printf("gnulibtest] done: %d/%d passed, %d failure(s)\n", passed_suites, total_suites, g_failed);
160:    return (g_failed == 0) ? 0 : 1;
161:}

@@@ user/bin/libctest.c @@@
1:/*
2: * libctest — conformance harness for the stream layer and the two layers under
3: * it.
4: *
5: * WHY THIS EXISTS.  Every stdio defect this system has hit was found by an
6: * APPLICATION, not by a test: doom's savegame load (unbuffered reads against
7: * ext4's 4 KiB block granularity), the file manager's "cannot open directory"
8: * (two consumers relying on an unwritten invariant), and Lua failing to load a
9: * script with a `#!` line (fgetc bypassing the read buffer, so a later fread
10: * refilled from a stale offset).  Each was a pattern some real program used and
11: * no test did.  So the cases here are named after the program whose behaviour
12: * they encode — when one fails, the failure names the app that will break.
13: *
14: * LAYERING.  POSIX and the C library are a personality ABOVE the native OS1
15: * layer; the native layer must not depend on them.  This harness therefore
16: * exercises both and, in group C, asserts they AGREE — a divergence between
17: * `stat()` and what a stream reports is the shape the file-manager bug had.
18: *
19: * Output matches captest: one line per case, then a machine-greppable summary.
20: */
21:
22:#include <dirent.h>
23:#include <errno.h>
24:#include <fcntl.h>
25:#include <os1.h>
26:#include <stdio.h>
27:#include <stdlib.h>
28:#include <string.h>
29:#include <sys/stat.h>
30:#include <unistd.h>
31:
32:static int g_pass, g_fail;
33:
34:static void ok(const char *name) {
35:  g_pass++;
36:  printf("[libctest] PASS %s\n", name);
37:}
38:
39:static void bad(const char *name, const char *why) {
40:  g_fail++;
41:  printf("[libctest] FAIL %s: %s\n", name, why);
42:}
43:
44:#define CHECK(name, cond, why)                                                 \
45:  do {                                                                         \
46:    if (!(cond)) {                                                             \
47:      bad((name), (why));                                                      \
48:      return;                                                                  \
49:    }                                                                          \
50:  } while (0)
51:
52:#define TMP "/home/.libctest.tmp"
53:
54:/* write_file - lay down exact bytes with the NATIVE layer, so a stream defect
55: * can never fabricate the fixture it is then measured against. */
56:static int write_file(const char *path, const char *data, int len) {
57:  return OS1_fs_write(path, data, len, 0) == len ? 0 : -1;
58:}
59:
60:/* ---------- group A: the stream layer, per real application pattern ------- */
61:
62:/*
63: * A1 — Lua's loader.  lauxlib.c skipcomment() consumes a `#!` line with getc()
64: * and leaves the FIRST byte of line 2 in hand; getF() then switches to fread()
65: * for the rest.  The two must be one continuous stream.  When fgetc bypassed
66: * the read buffer it also never advanced fp->pos, so fread refilled from 0 and
67: * re-read the file from the top — Lua saw "-" followed by "#" and reported
68: * "unexpected symbol near '-'".
69: */
70:static void t_lua_shebang_getc_then_fread(void) {
71:  const char *name = "lua/getc-then-fread";
72:  const char *src = "#!../lua\n-- comment\nprint(1)\n";
73:  int len = (int)strlen(src);
74:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, src, len) == 0, "fixture write failed");
75:
76:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");
77:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen failed");
78:
79:  int c = fgetc(f); /* skipBOM */
80:  while (c != EOF && c != '\n')
81:    c = fgetc(f); /* skip the shebang line */
82:  c = fgetc(f);   /* first byte of line 2 */
83:  CHECK(name, c == '-', "getc did not land on line 2");
84:
85:  char rest[64];
86:  size_t n = fread(rest, 1, sizeof(rest), f);
87:  fclose(f);
88:  CHECK(name, n == (size_t)len - 10, "fread returned the wrong length");
89:  CHECK(name, memcmp(rest, src + 10, n) == 0,
90:        "fread did not continue where getc stopped");
91:  ok(name);
92:}
93:
94:/* A2 — the reverse order: a block read, then byte reads. */
95:static void t_fread_then_getc(void) {
96:  const char *name = "stream/fread-then-getc";
97:  const char *src = "ABCDEFGHIJ";
98:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, src, 10) == 0, "fixture write failed");
99:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");
100:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen failed");
101:  char head[4];
102:  CHECK(name, fread(head, 1, 4, f) == 4, "short fread");
103:  CHECK(name, memcmp(head, "ABCD", 4) == 0, "wrong head");
104:  CHECK(name, fgetc(f) == 'E', "getc did not resume after fread");
105:  CHECK(name, fgetc(f) == 'F', "getc did not advance");
106:  fclose(f);
107:  ok(name);
108:}

110:/*
111: * A3 — fputc/fputs must share the write buffer with fwrite.  While they wrote
112: * straight to the descriptor, buffered bytes flushed LATER and landed at a
113: * different offset: the file came out reordered, silently.
114: */
115:static void t_fputc_fputs_fwrite_ordering(void) {
116:  const char *name = "stream/fputc-fputs-fwrite-order";
117:  OS1_fs_unlink(TMP);
118:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "w");
119:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen(w) failed");
120:  fputc('A', f);
121:  fputs("BC", f);
122:  fwrite("DE", 1, 2, f);
123:  fputc('F', f);
124:  CHECK(name, fclose(f) == 0, "fclose failed");
125:
126:  char back[16];
127:  int r = OS1_fs_read(TMP, back, sizeof(back), 0);
128:  CHECK(name, r == 6, "file length wrong");
129:  CHECK(name, memcmp(back, "ABCDEF", 6) == 0, "bytes landed out of order");
130:  ok(name);
131:}

133:/*
134: * A4 — read-after-write and write-after-read on ONE stream.  fread flushes
135: * pending writes; fwrite drops the cached read window.  Without the second
136: * half, a read following a write is served stale bytes from the old position.
137: */
138:static void t_interleaved_read_write(void) {
139:  const char *name = "stream/interleaved-rw";
140:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "0123456789", 10) == 0, "fixture write failed");
141:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r+");
142:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen(r+) failed");
143:  char c4[4];
144:  CHECK(name, fread(c4, 1, 4, f) == 4, "short fread");
145:  CHECK(name, memcmp(c4, "0123", 4) == 0, "wrong prefix");
146:  CHECK(name, fwrite("XY", 1, 2, f) == 2, "short fwrite");
147:  char c2[2];
148:  CHECK(name, fread(c2, 1, 2, f) == 2, "short fread after write");
149:  CHECK(name, memcmp(c2, "67", 2) == 0, "stale read window after write");
150:  fclose(f);
151:  char back[16];
152:  CHECK(name, OS1_fs_read(TMP, back, sizeof(back), 0) == 10, "length changed");
153:  CHECK(name, memcmp(back, "0123XY6789", 10) == 0, "write landed wrong");
154:  ok(name);
155:}

157:/* A5 — POSIX: a successful fseek undoes the effects of ungetc. */
158:static void t_fseek_undoes_ungetc(void) {
159:  const char *name = "posix/fseek-undoes-ungetc";
160:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "abcdef", 6) == 0, "fixture write failed");
161:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");
162:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen failed");
163:  CHECK(name, fgetc(f) == 'a', "first byte wrong");
164:  CHECK(name, ungetc('Z', f) == 'Z', "ungetc rejected");
165:  CHECK(name, fseek(f, 3, SEEK_SET) == 0, "fseek failed");
166:  CHECK(name, fgetc(f) == 'd', "pushback survived the seek");
167:  fclose(f);
168:  ok(name);

171:/* A6 — ungetc is visible to fread, not only to fgetc. */
172:static void t_ungetc_then_fread(void) {

174:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "abcdef", 6) == 0, "fixture write failed");
175:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");

186:/*
187: * A7 — a line straddling the 4096-byte buffer boundary.  kilo reads files line
188: * by line; a refill in the middle of a line is exactly where an off-by-one in
189: * the buffer accounting shows up.
190: */
191:static void t_fgets_across_buffer_boundary(void) {
192:  const char *name = "kilo/fgets-across-4k-boundary";
193:  static char big[FILE_RBUF_SIZE + 200];
194:  int n = 0;
195:  while (n < FILE_RBUF_SIZE - 4)
196:    big[n++] = 'x';
197:  big[n++] = '\n';
198:  const char *tail = "straddle-me-across-the-refill\n";
199:  memcpy(big + n, tail, strlen(tail));
200:  n += (int)strlen(tail);
201:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, big, n) == 0, "fixture write failed");
202:
203:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");
204:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen failed");
205:  static char line[FILE_RBUF_SIZE + 200];
206:  CHECK(name, fgets(line, sizeof(line), f) != NULL, "first fgets failed");
207:  CHECK(name, (int)strlen(line) == FILE_RBUF_SIZE - 3, "first line truncated");
208:  CHECK(name, fgets(line, sizeof(line), f) != NULL, "second fgets failed");
209:  CHECK(name, strcmp(line, tail) == 0, "line lost across the buffer refill");
210:  fclose(f);
211:  ok(name);
212:}

215:static void t_ftell_tracks_every_path(void) {
216:  const char *name = "stream/ftell-tracks-all-paths";
217:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "0123456789", 10) == 0, "fixture write failed");
218:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");
219:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen failed");

223:  char b[4];

226:  fseek(f, 2, SEEK_CUR);
227:  CHECK(name, ftell(f) == 7, "ftell did not follow SEEK_CUR");
228:  fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
229:  CHECK(name, ftell(f) == 10, "SEEK_END did not reach the size");

234:/* A9 — EOF is set by reading PAST the end, not by reaching it; rewind clears
235: * it again (and the error indicator, which plain fseek does not). */
236:static void t_eof_and_rewind(void) {
237:  const char *name = "posix/eof-and-rewind";
238:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "abc", 3) == 0, "fixture write failed");
239:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");
240:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen failed");
241:  char b[3];
242:  CHECK(name, fread(b, 1, 3, f) == 3, "short fread");
243:  CHECK(name, fgetc(f) == EOF, "read past end did not report EOF");
244:  CHECK(name, feof(f) != 0, "feof not set after reading past the end");
245:  rewind(f);
246:  CHECK(name, feof(f) == 0, "rewind did not clear EOF");
247:  CHECK(name, ftell(f) == 0, "rewind did not reset the position");
248:  CHECK(name, fgetc(f) == 'a', "rewind did not restore readability");
249:  fclose(f);
250:  ok(name);

266:/* A11 — doom's savegame shape: many small writes, reopened and read back in
267: * many small reads.  This is the case whose unbuffered form took minutes. */
268:static void t_doom_savegame_roundtrip(void) {
269:  const char *name = "doom/savegame-roundtrip";
270:  OS1_fs_unlink(TMP);
271:  FILE *w = fopen(TMP, "w");
272:  CHECK(name, w != NULL, "fopen(w) failed");
273:  for (int i = 0; i < 5000; i++)
274:    fputc((char)('A' + (i % 26)), w);
275:  CHECK(name, fclose(w) == 0, "fclose failed");
276:
277:  FILE *r = fopen(TMP, "r");
278:  CHECK(name, r != NULL, "fopen(r) failed");
279:  for (int i = 0; i < 5000; i++) {
280:    int c = fgetc(r);
281:    if (c != ('A' + (i % 26))) {
282:      fclose(r);
283:      bad(name, "byte mismatch on read-back");
284:      return;
285:    }
286:  }
287:  CHECK(name, fgetc(r) == EOF, "extra bytes after the payload");
288:  fclose(r);
289:  ok(name);
290:}

319:  CHECK(name, read(fd, b, 4) == 4, "short read after lseek");

333:  CHECK(name, memcmp(b, "6789", 4) == 0, "offset read wrong bytes");

338:/* ---------- group C: the two layers must agree --------------------------- */
339:
340:/*
341: * C1 — stat() and the stream layer must report the same size.  A divergence
342: * here is what made the file manager unable to open files: two consumers
343: * disagreeing about what the filesystem said.
344: */
345:static void t_stat_agrees_with_stream(void) {
346:  const char *name = "layers/stat-agrees-with-stream";
347:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "0123456789ab", 12) == 0, "fixture write failed");
348:  struct stat st;
349:  CHECK(name, stat(TMP, &st) == 0, "stat failed");
350:  CHECK(name, st.st_size == 12, "stat reported the wrong size");
351:  CHECK(name, S_ISREG(st.st_mode), "stat did not call a file a file");
352:  FILE *f = fopen(TMP, "r");
353:  CHECK(name, f != NULL, "fopen failed");
354:  fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
355:  long via_stream = ftell(f);
356:  fclose(f);
357:  CHECK(name, via_stream == st.st_size, "stream and stat disagree on size");
358:  ok(name);
359:}
360:
361:/*
362: * C2 — a directory must be distinguishable from a file WITHOUT trying to list
363: * it.  The regression this encodes: the distinction used to be inferred from
364: * "listing succeeded", an unwritten invariant two callers depended on.
365: */
366:static void t_stat_file_vs_dir(void) {
367:  const char *name = "layers/stat-file-vs-dir";
368:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "x", 1) == 0, "fixture write failed");
369:  struct stat sf, sd;
370:  CHECK(name, stat(TMP, &sf) == 0, "stat(file) failed");
371:  CHECK(name, stat("/home", &sd) == 0, "stat(dir) failed");
372:  CHECK(name, S_ISREG(sf.st_mode), "a file did not report as a file");
373:  CHECK(name, S_ISDIR(sd.st_mode), "a directory did not report as one");
374:  CHECK(name, !S_ISDIR(sf.st_mode), "a file reported as a directory");
375:  ok(name);
376:}

378:/* C3 — opendir accepts a directory and refuses a file.  The file manager calls
379: * this on whatever the user clicked. */
380:static void t_opendir_rejects_a_file(void) {
381:  const char *name = "filemgr/opendir-file-vs-dir";
382:  CHECK(name, write_file(TMP, "x", 1) == 0, "fixture write failed");
383:  DIR *d = opendir("/home");
384:  CHECK(name, d != NULL, "opendir on a directory failed");
385:  int saw = 0;
386:  while (readdir(d))
387:    saw++;
388:  closedir(d);
389:  CHECK(name, saw > 0, "directory listed as empty");
390:  DIR *bad_dir = opendir(TMP);
391:  if (bad_dir) {
392:    closedir(bad_dir);
393:    bad(name, "opendir accepted a regular file");
394:    return;
395:  }
396:  ok(name);
397:}
