@@@ user/sys/bin/nxfilem/sort.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxfilem/sort.c
3: * Comparators + an in-place, dir-first Hoare-partition quicksort.
4: */
5:#include "nxfilem.h"
6:
7:int fm_sort_by_name(const fm_file_t *a, const fm_file_t *b) {
8:  if (a->is_dir && !b->is_dir)
9:    return -1;
10:  if (!a->is_dir && b->is_dir)
11:    return 1;
12:
13:  const char *pa = a->name;
14:  const char *pb = b->name;
15:  while (*pa && *pb) {
16:    int ca = *pa, cb = *pb;
17:    if (ca >= 'a' && ca <= 'z')
18:      ca -= 32;
19:    if (cb >= 'a' && cb <= 'z')
20:      cb -= 32;
21:    if (ca != cb)
22:      return ca < cb ? -1 : 1;
23:    pa++;
24:    pb++;
25:  }
26:  if (*pa)
27:    return 1;
28:  if (*pb)
29:    return -1;
30:  return 0;
31:}
32:
33:int fm_sort_by_size(const fm_file_t *a, const fm_file_t *b) {
34:  if (a->is_dir && !b->is_dir)
35:    return -1;
36:  if (!a->is_dir && b->is_dir)
37:    return 1;
38:  if (a->size != b->size)
39:    return a->size < b->size ? -1 : 1;
40:  return fm_sort_by_name(a, b);
41:}
42:
43:int fm_sort_by_date(const fm_file_t *a, const fm_file_t *b) {
44:  if (a->is_dir && !b->is_dir)
45:    return -1;
46:  if (!a->is_dir && b->is_dir)
47:    return 1;
48:  if (a->mtime != b->mtime)
49:    return a->mtime < b->mtime ? -1 : 1;
50:  return fm_sort_by_name(a, b);
51:}
52:
53:int fm_sort_by_type(const fm_file_t *a, const fm_file_t *b) {
54:  if (a->is_dir && !b->is_dir)
55:    return -1;
56:  if (!a->is_dir && b->is_dir)
57:    return 1;
58:
59:  const char *ea = strrchr(a->name, '.');
60:  const char *eb = strrchr(b->name, '.');
61:  ea = ea ? ea : "";
62:  eb = eb ? eb : "";
63:  int c = strcmp(ea, eb);
64:  return c != 0 ? c : fm_sort_by_name(a, b);
65:}
66:
67:/*
68: * fm_qsort - Hoare-partition quicksort with a median-of-three pivot
69: * (bounds worst-case behaviour on already-sorted directory listings, which
70: * are common). Strict '<'/'>' comparisons in the partition loop mean equal
71: * elements never block the cursors, so this terminates correctly even with
72: * many same-named-prefix entries.
73: */
74:void fm_qsort(fm_file_t *arr, int n,
75:             int (*cmp)(const fm_file_t *, const fm_file_t *)) {
76:  if (n <= 1)
77:    return;
78:
79:  int mid = n / 2;
80:  if (cmp(&arr[0], &arr[mid]) > 0) {
81:    fm_file_t t = arr[0];
82:    arr[0] = arr[mid];
83:    arr[mid] = t;
84:  }
85:  if (cmp(&arr[0], &arr[n - 1]) > 0) {
86:    fm_file_t t = arr[0];
87:    arr[0] = arr[n - 1];
88:    arr[n - 1] = t;
89:  }
90:  if (cmp(&arr[mid], &arr[n - 1]) > 0) {
91:    fm_file_t t = arr[mid];
92:    arr[mid] = arr[n - 1];
93:    arr[n - 1] = t;
94:  }
95:  if (n <= 3)
96:    return;
97:
98:  fm_file_t pv = arr[mid];
99:  int l = 0, r = n - 1;
100:  while (l <= r) {
101:    while (cmp(&arr[l], &pv) < 0)
102:      l++;
103:    while (cmp(&arr[r], &pv) > 0)
104:      r--;
105:    if (l <= r) {
106:      fm_file_t tmp = arr[l];
107:      arr[l] = arr[r];
108:      arr[r] = tmp;
109:      l++;
110:      r--;
111:    }
112:  }
113:
114:  if (r > 0)
115:    fm_qsort(arr, r + 1, cmp);
116:  if (l < n - 1)
117:    fm_qsort(&arr[l], n - l, cmp);
118:}
119:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxfilem/state.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxfilem/state.c
3: * Navigation history, selection, sort mode, status message.
4: */
5:#include "nxfilem.h"
6:
7:fm_state_t fm_state = {0};
8:
9:void fm_state_init(void) {
10:  memset(&fm_state, 0, sizeof(fm_state));
11:  fm_state.window_id = -1;
12:  fm_state.running = 1;
13:  fm_state.sort_mode = FM_SORT_NAME;
14:  fm_state.menu_open = -1;
15:  fm_state.highlighted_item = -1;
16:  fm_state.last_click_item = -1;
17:
18:  /* Prefer the process CWD. If it is "/", start in /home when available.
19:   * If the CWD cannot be determined, also try /home. Final fallback is "/". */
20:  if (getcwd(fm_state.home_path, FM_PATH_MAX) == 0 &&
21:      fm_state.home_path[0] != '\0') {
22:
23:    if (strcmp(fm_state.home_path, "/") == 0 && chdir("/home") == 0) {
24:      strncpy(fm_state.home_path, "/home", FM_PATH_MAX - 1);
25:      fm_state.home_path[FM_PATH_MAX - 1] = '\0';
26:    }
27:
28:  } else if (chdir("/home") == 0) {
29:
30:    strncpy(fm_state.home_path, "/home", FM_PATH_MAX - 1);
31:    fm_state.home_path[FM_PATH_MAX - 1] = '\0';
32:
33:  } else {
34:
35:    chdir("/");
36:    strncpy(fm_state.home_path, "/", FM_PATH_MAX - 1);
37:    fm_state.home_path[FM_PATH_MAX - 1] = '\0';
38:  }
39:
40:  strncpy(fm_state.current_path, fm_state.home_path, FM_PATH_MAX - 1);
41:  fm_state.current_path[FM_PATH_MAX - 1] = '\0';
42:
43:  strncpy(fm_state.history[0], fm_state.home_path, FM_PATH_MAX - 1);
44:  fm_state.history[0][FM_PATH_MAX - 1] = '\0';
45:}
46:
47:void fm_state_add_to_history(const char *path) {
48:  if (fm_state.history_pos < fm_state.history_count - 1)
49:    fm_state.history_count = fm_state.history_pos + 1;
50:
51:  if (fm_state.history_count > 0 &&
52:      strcmp(fm_state.history[fm_state.history_pos], path) == 0)
53:    return;
54:
55:  if (fm_state.history_count >= FM_HISTORY_MAX) {
56:    for (int i = 0; i < fm_state.history_count - 1; i++)
57:      strncpy(fm_state.history[i], fm_state.history[i + 1], FM_PATH_MAX - 1);
58:    fm_state.history_count--;
59:    if (fm_state.history_pos > 0)
60:      fm_state.history_pos--;
61:  }
62:
63:  strncpy(fm_state.history[fm_state.history_count], path, FM_PATH_MAX - 1);
64:  fm_state.history_count++;
65:  fm_state.history_pos = fm_state.history_count - 1;
66:}
67:
68:int fm_state_can_undo(void) { return fm_state.history_pos > 0; }
69:
70:int fm_state_can_redo(void) {
71:  return fm_state.history_pos < fm_state.history_count - 1;
72:}
73:
74:void fm_state_sort_files(fm_sort_mode_t mode) {
75:  if (fm_state.sort_mode == mode)
76:    fm_state.sort_reverse = !fm_state.sort_reverse;
77:  else {
78:    fm_state.sort_mode = mode;
79:    fm_state.sort_reverse = 0;
80:  }
81:  fm_refresh_directory();
82:}
83:
84:void fm_state_select_all(void) {
85:  fm_state.selected_count = 0;
86:  for (int i = 0; i < fm_state.file_count; i++) {
87:    fm_state.files[i].is_selected = 1;
88:    fm_state.selected_count++;
89:  }
90:}
91:
92:void fm_state_deselect_all(void) {
93:  for (int i = 0; i < fm_state.file_count; i++)
94:    fm_state.files[i].is_selected = 0;
95:  fm_state.selected_count = 0;
96:}
97:
98:void fm_state_toggle_select(int index) {
99:  if (index < 0 || index >= fm_state.file_count)
100:    return;
101:  fm_file_t *f = &fm_state.files[index];
102:  f->is_selected = !f->is_selected;
103:  fm_state.selected_count += f->is_selected ? 1 : -1;
104:}
105:
106:void fm_set_status_message(const char *msg) {
107:  if (!msg)
108:    fm_state.status_message[0] = '\0';
109:  else {
110:    strncpy(fm_state.status_message, msg, sizeof(fm_state.status_message) - 1);
111:    fm_state.status_message[sizeof(fm_state.status_message) - 1] = '\0';
112:  }
113:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxfilem/ui.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxfilem/ui.c
3: * Layout, palette, hit-testing and the redraw entry point.
4: *
5: * Same button-hit-table technique as nxsettings.c: a per-frame table that
6: * IS both the draw call and the hit-test source, rebuilt every redraw so
7: * drawing and hit-testing can never drift apart. Redraw itself is gated by
8: * a state signature (FNV-1a over everything visible) exactly like
9: * nxui.c's redraw(force)/g_sig — nothing is blitted when nothing the user
10: * could see has actually changed, so this app never busy-spins even though
11: * the event loop polls at a fixed ~30Hz.
12: */
13:#include "nxfilem.h"

85:struct fm_btn {
86:  int x, y, w, h;
87:  int action;
88:  long arg;
89:};
90:static struct fm_btn g_btns[FM_MAX_BTNS];
91:static int g_btn_n;
92:
93:static void add_btn(int x, int y, int w, int h, int action, long arg) {
94:  if (g_btn_n >= FM_MAX_BTNS)
95:    return;
96:  g_btns[g_btn_n].x = x;
97:  g_btns[g_btn_n].y = y;
98:  g_btns[g_btn_n].w = w;
99:  g_btns[g_btn_n].h = h;
100:  g_btns[g_btn_n].action = action;
101:  g_btns[g_btn_n].arg = arg;
102:  g_btn_n++;
103:}

105:/* ============================== Layout ============================== */
106:#define TOOLBAR_BTN_W 28
107:#define TOOLBAR_BTN_H 26
108:#define HEADER_H 22
109:#define SIZE_COL_W 90

111:static int g_content_x, g_content_y, g_content_w, g_content_h;
112:static int g_rows_y0, g_visible_rows;

114:static void compute_layout(void) {
115:  g_content_x = FM_SIDEBAR_W;
116:  g_content_y = FM_MENUBAR_H + FM_TOOLBAR_H;
117:  g_content_w = fm_fb_w - FM_SIDEBAR_W;
118:  g_content_h = fm_fb_h - g_content_y - FM_STATUSBAR_H;
119:  if (g_content_w < 0)
120:    g_content_w = 0;
121:  if (g_content_h < 0)
122:    g_content_h = 0;
123:  g_rows_y0 = g_content_y + HEADER_H;
124:  g_visible_rows = (g_content_h - HEADER_H) / FM_ROW_H;
125:  if (g_visible_rows < 0)
126:    g_visible_rows = 0;
127:}

129:/* ============================== Rename ============================== */
130:void fm_ui_begin_rename(int index) {
131:  if (index < 0 || index >= fm_state.file_count)
132:    return;
133:  fm_state.rename.active = 1;
134:  fm_state.rename.index = index;
135:  strncpy(fm_state.rename.buf, fm_state.files[index].name,
136:          sizeof(fm_state.rename.buf) - 1);
137:  fm_state.rename.buf[sizeof(fm_state.rename.buf) - 1] = '\0';
138:  fm_state.rename.len = (int)strlen(fm_state.rename.buf);
139:}
140:
141:void fm_ui_commit_rename(void) {
142:  if (!fm_state.rename.active)
143:    return;
144:
145:  int idx = fm_state.rename.index;
146:
147:  char old_path[FM_PATH_MAX];
148:  char new_name[FM_NAME_MAX];
149:
150:  old_path[0] = '\0';
151:  new_name[0] = '\0';
152:
153:  if (idx >= 0 && idx < fm_state.file_count && fm_state.rename.len > 0) {
154:
155:    strncpy(old_path, fm_state.files[idx].full_path, sizeof(old_path) - 1);
156:
157:    old_path[sizeof(old_path) - 1] = '\0';
158:
159:    strncpy(new_name, fm_state.rename.buf, sizeof(new_name) - 1);
160:
161:    new_name[sizeof(new_name) - 1] = '\0';
162:
163:    fm_rename_file(old_path, new_name);
164:  }
165:
166:  fm_state.rename.active = 0;
167:  fm_state.rename.index = -1;
168:  fm_state.rename.len = 0;
169:  fm_state.rename.buf[0] = '\0';
170:
171:  fm_refresh_directory();
172:}
173:
174:void fm_ui_cancel_rename(void) { fm_state.rename.active = 0; }
175:
176:int fm_ui_visible_rows(void) {
177:  compute_layout();
178:  return g_visible_rows;
179:}

188:  int action;

190:static const struct menu_entry MENU_FILE[] = {
191:    {"Open", ACT_OPEN},
192:    {"Open in Kilo", ACT_OPEN_KILO},
193:    {"New Folder", ACT_NEW_FOLDER},
194:    {"Rename", ACT_RENAME},
195:    {"Delete", ACT_DELETE},
196:    {"Refresh", ACT_REFRESH},
197:    {"Quit", ACT_QUIT},

199:static const struct menu_entry MENU_EDIT[] = {
200:    {"Copy", ACT_COPY},
201:    {"Cut", ACT_CUT},
202:    {"Paste", ACT_PASTE},
203:    {"Select All", ACT_SELECT_ALL},
204:    {"Deselect All", ACT_DESELECT_ALL},

207:    {"Toggle Hidden Files", ACT_TOGGLE_HIDDEN},
208:    {"Sort by Name", ACT_SORT_NAME},
209:    {"Sort by Size", ACT_SORT_SIZE},
210:    {"Sort by Date", ACT_SORT_DATE},
211:    {"Sort by Type", ACT_SORT_TYPE},
212:};
213:static const struct menu_entry MENU_HELP[] = {
214:    {"About", ACT_ABOUT},
215:};
216:static const struct menu_entry *const MENU_ITEMS[MENU_COUNT] = {
217:    MENU_FILE, MENU_EDIT, MENU_VIEW, MENU_HELP};
218:static const int MENU_ITEM_COUNTS[MENU_COUNT] = {
219:    (int)(sizeof(MENU_FILE) / sizeof(MENU_FILE[0])),
220:    (int)(sizeof(MENU_EDIT) / sizeof(MENU_EDIT[0])),
221:    (int)(sizeof(MENU_VIEW) / sizeof(MENU_VIEW[0])),
222:    (int)(sizeof(MENU_HELP) / sizeof(MENU_HELP[0])),
223:};
224:static const int MENU_X[MENU_COUNT] = {8, 56, 104, 152};
225:#define MENU_ITEM_H 22
226:#define MENU_W 168
227:
228:static const struct menu_entry CTX_ITEMS[] = {
229:    {"Open", ACT_OPEN}, {"Rename", ACT_RENAME}, {"Copy", ACT_COPY},
230:    {"Cut", ACT_CUT},   {"Paste", ACT_PASTE},   {"Delete", ACT_DELETE},
231:};
232:#define CTX_COUNT (int)(sizeof(CTX_ITEMS) / sizeof(CTX_ITEMS[0]))
233:
234:static void render_dropdown(int x, int y, const struct menu_entry *items,
235:                            int count) {
236:  int h = count * MENU_ITEM_H;
237:  if (x + MENU_W > fm_fb_w)
238:    x = fm_fb_w - MENU_W;
239:  if (y + h > fm_fb_h)
240:    y = fm_fb_h - h;
241:  fm_fill_rect(x, y, MENU_W, h, g_col_toolbar);
242:  fm_fill_rect(x, y, MENU_W, 1, g_col_border);
243:  fm_fill_rect(x, y + h - 1, MENU_W, 1, g_col_border);
244:  fm_fill_rect(x, y, 1, h, g_col_border);
245:  fm_fill_rect(x + MENU_W - 1, y, 1, h, g_col_border);
246:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
247:    int iy = y + i * MENU_ITEM_H;
248:    fm_draw_text(x + 10, iy + 4, items[i].label, g_col_text);
249:    add_btn(x, iy, MENU_W, MENU_ITEM_H, items[i].action, 0);
250:  }
251:}
252:
253:static void render_menubar(void) {
254:  fm_fill_rect(0, 0, fm_fb_w, FM_MENUBAR_H, g_col_menubar);
255:  for (int i = 0; i < MENU_COUNT; i++) {
256:    int x = MENU_X[i];
257:    uint32_t color = g_col_text;
258:    if (fm_state.menu_open == i) {
259:      fm_fill_rect(x - 6, 0, 44, FM_MENUBAR_H, g_col_toolbar);
260:      color = g_col_accent;
261:    }
262:    fm_draw_text(x, 6, MENU_LABELS[i], color);
263:    add_btn(x - 6, 0, 44, FM_MENUBAR_H, ACT_TOP_MENU, i);
264:  }
265:  fm_fill_rect(0, FM_MENUBAR_H - 1, fm_fb_w, 1, g_col_border);
266:
267:  if (fm_state.menu_open >= 0 && fm_state.menu_open < MENU_COUNT)
268:    render_dropdown(MENU_X[fm_state.menu_open], FM_MENUBAR_H,
269:                    MENU_ITEMS[fm_state.menu_open],
270:                    MENU_ITEM_COUNTS[fm_state.menu_open]);
271:}

273:static void toolbar_btn(int x, int y, const char *label, int action,
274:                        int enabled) {
275:  fm_rrect(x, y, TOOLBAR_BTN_W, TOOLBAR_BTN_H, 5,
276:           enabled ? g_col_btn : g_col_toolbar);
277:  int tw = fm_text_width(label);
278:  fm_draw_text(x + (TOOLBAR_BTN_W - tw) / 2, y + 6, label,
279:               enabled ? g_col_text : g_col_text_dim);
280:  if (enabled)
281:    add_btn(x, y, TOOLBAR_BTN_W, TOOLBAR_BTN_H, action, 0);
282:}

284:static void render_toolbar(void) {
285:  int y = FM_MENUBAR_H;
286:  fm_fill_rect(0, y, fm_fb_w, FM_TOOLBAR_H, g_col_toolbar);
287:  int by = y + (FM_TOOLBAR_H - TOOLBAR_BTN_H) / 2;
288:  int bx = 6;
289:
290:  toolbar_btn(bx, by, "<", ACT_NAV_BACK, fm_state_can_undo());
291:  bx += TOOLBAR_BTN_W + 4;
292:  toolbar_btn(bx, by, ">", ACT_NAV_FORWARD, fm_state_can_redo());
293:  bx += TOOLBAR_BTN_W + 4;
294:  toolbar_btn(bx, by, "^", ACT_NAV_UP, strcmp(fm_state.current_path, "/") != 0);
295:  bx += TOOLBAR_BTN_W + 4;
296:  toolbar_btn(bx, by, "H", ACT_NAV_HOME, 1);
297:  bx += TOOLBAR_BTN_W + 4;
298:  toolbar_btn(bx, by, "R", ACT_REFRESH, 1);
299:  bx += TOOLBAR_BTN_W + 10;
300:
301:  int right_w = 96;
302:  int path_x = bx;
303:  int path_w = fm_fb_w - bx - right_w - 8;
304:  if (path_w < 20)
305:    path_w = 20;
306:  fm_draw_text(path_x, by + 6, fm_state.current_path, g_col_text_dim);
307:  (void)path_w; /* text is left-aligned and simply clipped by fm_draw_text's
308:                 * own bounds check; no ellipsis pass needed for now */
309:
310:  int hidden_x = fm_fb_w - right_w;
311:  fm_rrect(hidden_x, by, right_w - 8, TOOLBAR_BTN_H, 5,
312:           fm_state.show_hidden ? g_col_btn_active : g_col_btn);
313:  fm_draw_text(hidden_x + 8, by + 6, "Hidden", g_col_text);
314:  add_btn(hidden_x, by, right_w - 8, TOOLBAR_BTN_H, ACT_TOGGLE_HIDDEN, 0);
315:
316:  fm_fill_rect(0, y + FM_TOOLBAR_H - 1, fm_fb_w, 1, g_col_border);
317:}
318:
319:static void render_sidebar(void) {
320:  fm_fill_rect(0, g_content_y, FM_SIDEBAR_W, g_content_h, g_col_sidebar);
321:
322:  int y = g_content_y + FM_PAD;
323:  fm_rrect(FM_PAD, y, FM_SIDEBAR_W - 2 * FM_PAD, 24, 5, g_col_btn);
324:  fm_draw_text(FM_PAD + 8, y + 5, "Home", g_col_text);
325:  add_btn(FM_PAD, y, FM_SIDEBAR_W - 2 * FM_PAD, 24, ACT_NAV_HOME, 0);
326:  y += 34;
327:
328:  fm_draw_text(FM_PAD, y, "Location", g_col_accent);
329:  y += 18;
330:  char line[64];
331:  const char *p = fm_state.current_path;
332:  int plen = (int)strlen(p);
333:  int max_chars = (FM_SIDEBAR_W - 2 * FM_PAD) / 7;
334:  if (plen > max_chars && max_chars > 3)
335:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "...%s", p + (plen - (max_chars - 3)));
336:  else
337:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s", p);
338:  fm_draw_text(FM_PAD, y, line, g_col_text_dim);
339:  y += 26;
340:
341:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%d items", fm_state.file_count);
342:  fm_draw_text(FM_PAD, y, line, g_col_text);
343:  y += 18;
344:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%lld KB total", fm_state.total_size / 1024LL);
345:  fm_draw_text(FM_PAD, y, line, g_col_text);
346:  y += 18;
347:  if (fm_state.selected_count > 0) {
348:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%d selected", fm_state.selected_count);
349:    fm_draw_text(FM_PAD, y, line, g_col_accent);
350:  }
351:
352:  fm_fill_rect(FM_SIDEBAR_W - 1, g_content_y, 1, g_content_h, g_col_border);
353:}
354:
355:static void format_size(long size, char *out, size_t sz) {
356:  if (size < 1024)
357:    snprintf(out, sz, "%ld B", size);
358:  else if (size < 1024 * 1024)
359:    snprintf(out, sz, "%ld KB", size / 1024);
360:  else
361:    snprintf(out, sz, "%ld MB", size / (1024 * 1024));
362:}

364:static void render_content_header(void) {
365:  fm_fill_rect(g_content_x, g_content_y, g_content_w, HEADER_H, g_col_toolbar);
366:  int name_x = g_content_x + FM_PAD + FM_ICON_SIZE + 8;
367:  uint32_t nc =
368:      fm_state.sort_mode == FM_SORT_NAME ? g_col_accent : g_col_text_dim;
369:  uint32_t sc =
370:      fm_state.sort_mode == FM_SORT_SIZE ? g_col_accent : g_col_text_dim;
371:  fm_draw_text(name_x, g_content_y + 4, "Name", nc);
372:  fm_draw_text(g_content_x + g_content_w - SIZE_COL_W, g_content_y + 4, "Size",
373:               sc);
374:  add_btn(g_content_x, g_content_y, g_content_w - SIZE_COL_W, HEADER_H,
375:          ACT_SORT_NAME, 0);
376:  add_btn(g_content_x + g_content_w - SIZE_COL_W, g_content_y, SIZE_COL_W,
377:          HEADER_H, ACT_SORT_SIZE, 0);
378:  fm_fill_rect(g_content_x, g_content_y + HEADER_H - 1, g_content_w, 1,
379:               g_col_border);
380:}

382:static void render_rename_box(int row_y, int name_x, int name_w) {
383:  fm_fill_rect(name_x - 2, row_y + 2, name_w, FM_ROW_H - 4, g_col_bg);
384:  fm_fill_rect(name_x - 2, row_y + 2, name_w, 1, g_col_accent);
385:  fm_fill_rect(name_x - 2, row_y + FM_ROW_H - 3, name_w, 1, g_col_accent);
386:  fm_draw_text(name_x, row_y + (FM_ROW_H - 14) / 2, fm_state.rename.buf,
387:               g_col_text);
388:  int cx = name_x + fm_text_width(fm_state.rename.buf) + 1;
389:  fm_fill_rect(cx, row_y + 4, 1, FM_ROW_H - 8, g_col_text);
390:}
391:
392:static void render_content(void) {
393:  fm_fill_rect(g_content_x, g_content_y + HEADER_H, g_content_w,
394:               g_content_h - HEADER_H, g_col_bg);
395:  render_content_header();
396:
397:  if (fm_state.file_count == 0) {
398:    fm_draw_text(g_content_x + FM_PAD, g_rows_y0 + FM_PAD, "No files",
399:                 g_col_text_dim);
400:    return;
401:  }
402:
403:  int end = fm_state.scroll_offset + g_visible_rows;
404:  if (end > fm_state.file_count)
405:    end = fm_state.file_count;
406:
407:  for (int i = fm_state.scroll_offset; i < end; i++) {
408:    int row_y = g_rows_y0 + (i - fm_state.scroll_offset) * FM_ROW_H;
409:    fm_file_t *file = &fm_state.files[i];
410:
411:    uint32_t row_bg = (i % 2) ? g_col_row_alt : g_col_bg;
412:    if (file->is_selected)
413:      row_bg = g_col_row_sel;
414:    if (i == fm_state.highlighted_item)
415:      row_bg = g_col_row_hover;
416:    fm_fill_rect(g_content_x, row_y, g_content_w, FM_ROW_H, row_bg);
417:
418:    int icon_y = row_y + (FM_ROW_H - FM_ICON_SIZE) / 2;
419:    fm_draw_icon(g_content_x + FM_PAD, icon_y, FM_ICON_SIZE, file->icon_id,
420:                 g_light, file->is_dir ? g_col_accent : g_col_text_dim);
421:
422:    int name_x = g_content_x + FM_PAD + FM_ICON_SIZE + 8;
423:    int name_w = g_content_w - (FM_PAD + FM_ICON_SIZE + 8) - SIZE_COL_W - 4;
424:    if (fm_state.rename.active && fm_state.rename.index == i) {
425:      render_rename_box(row_y, name_x, name_w);
426:    } else {
427:      fm_draw_text(name_x, row_y + (FM_ROW_H - 14) / 2, file->name, g_col_text);
428:    }
429:
430:    char size_str[32];
431:    if (file->is_dir)
432:      snprintf(size_str, sizeof(size_str), "%s", "--");
433:    else
434:      format_size(file->size, size_str, sizeof(size_str));
435:    fm_draw_text(g_content_x + g_content_w - SIZE_COL_W,
436:                 row_y + (FM_ROW_H - 14) / 2, size_str, g_col_text_dim);
437:  }
438:
439:  if (fm_state.file_count > g_visible_rows) {
440:    int track_h = g_content_h - HEADER_H;
441:    int thumb_h = (g_visible_rows * track_h) / fm_state.file_count;
442:    if (thumb_h < 16)
443:      thumb_h = 16;
444:    int span = fm_state.file_count - g_visible_rows;
445:    int thumb_y =
446:        g_rows_y0 +
447:        (span > 0 ? (fm_state.scroll_offset * (track_h - thumb_h)) / span : 0);
448:    fm_fill_rect(g_content_x + g_content_w - 4, g_rows_y0, 4, track_h,
449:                 g_col_toolbar);
450:    fm_fill_rect(g_content_x + g_content_w - 4, thumb_y, 4, thumb_h,
451:                 g_col_border);
452:  }
453:}
454:
455:static void render_statusbar(void) {
456:  int y = fm_fb_h - FM_STATUSBAR_H;
457:  fm_fill_rect(0, y, fm_fb_w, FM_STATUSBAR_H, g_col_toolbar);
458:  fm_fill_rect(0, y, fm_fb_w, 1, g_col_border);
459:  if (fm_state.status_message[0])
460:    fm_draw_text(FM_PAD, y + 5, fm_state.status_message, g_col_text);
461:  else {
462:    char line[96];
463:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%d items, %d selected", fm_state.file_count,
464:             fm_state.selected_count);
465:    fm_draw_text(FM_PAD, y + 5, line, g_col_text_dim);
466:  }
467:}

469:static void render_context_menu(void) {
470:  if (!fm_state.context_menu_active)
471:    return;
472:  render_dropdown(fm_state.context_menu_x, fm_state.context_menu_y, CTX_ITEMS,
473:                  CTX_COUNT);

475:
476:/* ============================== Dispatch ============================== */
477:
478:static void dispatch(int action, long arg) {
479:  int idx = fm_state.highlighted_item;
480:  fm_state.menu_open = -1;
481:  fm_state.context_menu_active = 0;
482:
483:  switch (action) {
484:  case ACT_TOP_MENU:
485:    fm_state.menu_open = (fm_state.menu_open == (int)arg) ? -1 : (int)arg;
486:    break;
487:  case ACT_NAV_BACK:
488:    fm_navigate_back();
489:    break;
490:  case ACT_NAV_FORWARD:
491:    fm_navigate_forward();
492:    break;
493:  case ACT_NAV_UP:
494:    fm_navigate_up();
495:    break;
496:  case ACT_NAV_HOME:
497:    fm_navigate_home();
498:    break;
499:  case ACT_REFRESH:
500:    fm_refresh_directory();
501:    break;
502:  case ACT_TOGGLE_HIDDEN:
503:    fm_state.show_hidden = !fm_state.show_hidden;
504:    fm_refresh_directory();
505:    break;
506:  case ACT_SORT_NAME:
507:    fm_state_sort_files(FM_SORT_NAME);
508:    break;
509:  case ACT_SORT_SIZE:
510:    fm_state_sort_files(FM_SORT_SIZE);
511:    break;
512:  case ACT_SORT_DATE:
513:    fm_state_sort_files(FM_SORT_DATE);
514:    break;
515:  case ACT_SORT_TYPE:
516:    fm_state_sort_files(FM_SORT_TYPE);
517:    break;
518:  case ACT_SELECT_ALL:
519:    fm_state_select_all();
520:    break;
521:  case ACT_DESELECT_ALL:
522:    fm_state_deselect_all();
523:    break;
524:  case ACT_OPEN:
525:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < fm_state.file_count)
526:      fm_open_file(&fm_state.files[idx]);
527:    break;
528:  case ACT_OPEN_KILO:
529:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < fm_state.file_count)
530:      fm_open_with_kilo(&fm_state.files[idx]);
531:    break;
532:  case ACT_RENAME:
533:    fm_ui_begin_rename(idx);
534:    break;
535:  case ACT_COPY:
536:    fm_clipboard_copy();
537:    break;
538:  case ACT_CUT:
539:    fm_clipboard_cut();
540:    break;
541:  case ACT_PASTE:
542:    fm_clipboard_paste();
543:    break;
544:  case ACT_DELETE:
545:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < fm_state.file_count) {
546:      fm_delete_file(fm_state.files[idx].full_path);
547:      fm_refresh_directory();
548:    }
549:    break;
550:  case ACT_NEW_FOLDER:
551:    fm_create_folder(NULL);
552:    break;
553:  case ACT_QUIT:
554:    fm_state.running = 0;
555:    break;
556:  case ACT_ABOUT:
557:    fm_set_status_message("NEXS File Manager");
558:    break;
559:  default:
560:    break;
561:  }
562:}
563:
564:/* fm_ui_handle_click - content-list rows are handled directly by geometry
565: * (selection + double-click open need state the generic button table
566: * doesn't carry); everything else (menus, toolbar, sidebar, context menu)
567: * goes through the g_btns table built by the last redraw. */
568:void fm_ui_handle_click(int x, int y, int button) {
569:  if (fm_state.rename.active) {
570:    fm_ui_commit_rename();
571:    return;
572:  }
573:
574:  if (button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT && x >= g_content_x && y >= g_rows_y0 &&
575:      x < g_content_x + g_content_w && !fm_state.context_menu_active &&
576:      fm_state.menu_open < 0) {
577:    int row = fm_state.scroll_offset + (y - g_rows_y0) / FM_ROW_H;
578:    if (row >= 0 && row < fm_state.file_count) {
579:      fm_state.highlighted_item = row;
580:
581:      struct timespec now;
582:      clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &now);
583:      long long now_ms =
584:          (long long)now.tv_sec * 1000LL + now.tv_nsec / 1000000LL;
585:      if (fm_state.last_click_item == row &&
586:          (now_ms - fm_state.last_click_time_ms) < 400 &&
587:          fm_state.last_click_time_ms > 0) {
588:        fm_open_file(&fm_state.files[row]);
589:        fm_state.last_click_time_ms = 0;
590:      } else {
591:        fm_state.last_click_time_ms = now_ms;
592:        fm_state.last_click_item = row;
593:      }
594:    }
595:    return;
596:  }
597:
598:  if (button == MOUSE_BTN_RIGHT && x >= g_content_x && y >= g_rows_y0 &&
599:      x < g_content_x + g_content_w) {
600:    int row = fm_state.scroll_offset + (y - g_rows_y0) / FM_ROW_H;
601:    if (row >= 0 && row < fm_state.file_count) {
602:      fm_state.highlighted_item = row;
603:      fm_state.context_menu_active = 1;
604:      fm_state.context_menu_x = x;
605:      fm_state.context_menu_y = y;
606:    }
607:    return;
608:  }
609:
610:  if (button != MOUSE_BTN_LEFT) {
611:    fm_state.context_menu_active = 0;
612:    fm_state.menu_open = -1;
613:    return;
614:  }
615:
616:  for (int i = g_btn_n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
617:    struct fm_btn *b = &g_btns[i];
618:    if (x >= b->x && x < b->x + b->w && y >= b->y && y < b->y + b->h) {
619:      dispatch(b->action, b->arg);
620:      return;
621:    }
622:  }
623:
624:  fm_state.context_menu_active = 0;
625:  fm_state.menu_open = -1;
626:}
627:
628:/* ============================== Signature ============================== */
629:
630:static unsigned fnv1a(unsigned h, const void *data, size_t n) {
631:  const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)data;
632:  for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
633:    h ^= p[i];
634:    h *= 16777619u;
635:  }
636:  return h;
637:}
638:static unsigned fnv1a_str(unsigned h, const char *s) {
639:  return fnv1a(h, s, strlen(s));
640:}
641:
642:static unsigned compute_signature(void) {
643:  unsigned h = 2166136261u;
644:  h = fnv1a_str(h, fm_state.current_path);
645:  h = fnv1a_str(h, fm_state.status_message);
646:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.file_count, sizeof(fm_state.file_count));
647:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.highlighted_item, sizeof(fm_state.highlighted_item));
648:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.scroll_offset, sizeof(fm_state.scroll_offset));
649:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.selected_count, sizeof(fm_state.selected_count));
650:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.sort_mode, sizeof(fm_state.sort_mode));
651:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.sort_reverse, sizeof(fm_state.sort_reverse));
652:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.show_hidden, sizeof(fm_state.show_hidden));
653:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.menu_open, sizeof(fm_state.menu_open));
654:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.context_menu_active,
655:            sizeof(fm_state.context_menu_active));
656:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.context_menu_x, sizeof(fm_state.context_menu_x));
657:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.context_menu_y, sizeof(fm_state.context_menu_y));
658:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.clipboard.is_valid,
659:            sizeof(fm_state.clipboard.is_valid));
660:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.clipboard.is_cut, sizeof(fm_state.clipboard.is_cut));
661:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.history_pos, sizeof(fm_state.history_pos));
662:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.history_count, sizeof(fm_state.history_count));
663:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.rename, sizeof(fm_state.rename));
664:  h = fnv1a(h, &g_light, sizeof(g_light));
665:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_fb_w, sizeof(fm_fb_w));
666:  h = fnv1a(h, &fm_fb_h, sizeof(fm_fb_h));
667:  for (int i = 0; i < fm_state.file_count; i++)
668:    h = fnv1a(h, &fm_state.files[i].is_selected,
669:              sizeof(fm_state.files[i].is_selected));
670:  return h;
671:}

673:/* ============================== Public API ============================== */
674:
675:int fm_ui_init(void) {
676:  long di = OS1_display_info();
677:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
678:  int sh = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
679:  if (sw <= 0)
680:    sw = 800;
681:  if (sh <= 0)
682:    sh = 600;
683:
684:  int ww = (sw * 7) / 10;
685:  int wh = (sh * 7) / 10;
686:  if (ww > 900)
687:    ww = 900;
688:  if (wh > 640)
689:    wh = 640;
690:  if (ww < FM_MIN_WIN_W)
691:    ww = FM_MIN_WIN_W;
692:  if (wh < FM_MIN_WIN_H)
693:    wh = FM_MIN_WIN_H;
694:  int wx = (sw - ww) / 2, wy = (sh - wh) / 2;
695:
696:  int win = create_window(wx, wy, ww, wh, "nxfilem");
697:  if (win < 0)
698:    return -1;
699:  fm_state.window_id = win;
700:  fm_gfx_init(win, ww, wh);
701:
702:  /* Self-register this pid as the live "srv.filem_pid" endpoint
703:   * (nxres.h's nxres_look_ping_targets) so an external style/theme/bg
704:   * change (nxres from a shell, or any other caller of SYS_SET_STYLE)
705:   * reaches this already-open window as INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED instead of
706:   * only taking effect the next time nxfilem is launched.  Same pattern
707:   * nxsettings uses for "srv.settings_pid" (user-launched, not a singleton
708:   * — no respawn hazard to guard against; see init.c's register_service_pid
709:   * for the singleton-service equivalent).  Last-opened instance wins if
710:   * more than one is ever open at once. */
711:  {
712:    char pidbuf[16];
713:    snprintf(pidbuf, sizeof(pidbuf), "%d", get_pid());
714:    OS1_registry_set("srv.filem_pid", pidbuf);
715:  }
716:
717:  fm_ui_load_theme(nxres_theme_is_light());
718:  return 0;
719:}
720:
721:void fm_ui_reinit_window(int ww, int wh) {
722:  if (ww < FM_MIN_WIN_W)
723:    ww = FM_MIN_WIN_W;
724:  if (wh < FM_MIN_WIN_H)
725:    wh = FM_MIN_WIN_H;
726:  /* Keep the compositor's own window record in sync with the clamped size
727:   * (nxlauncher.c's reinit_window() does the same) -- without this the
728:   * compositor still thinks the window is the OLD size (stale w/h in
729:   * OS1_window_enum(), stale hit-test/clip rect) even though we already
730:   * reallocated our buffer to the new one. */
731:  if (fm_state.window_id >= 0)
732:    OS1_window_resize(fm_state.window_id, ww, wh);
733:  fm_gfx_realloc(ww, wh);
734:}
735:
736:static unsigned g_sig = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
737:
738:void fm_ui_redraw(int force) {
739:  compute_layout();
740:
741:  unsigned sig = compute_signature();
742:  if (!force && sig == g_sig)
743:    return;
744:  g_sig = sig;
745:
746:  g_btn_n = 0;
747:  fm_fill_rect(0, 0, fm_fb_w, fm_fb_h, g_col_bg);
748:  render_toolbar(); /* drawn before the menubar so the dropdown (menubar)
749:                     * paints on top of it, not the other way round */
750:  render_sidebar();
751:  render_content();
752:  render_statusbar();
753:  render_menubar();
754:  render_context_menu();
755:
756:  fm_blit();
757:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxassoc.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXASSOC_H
2:#define _USER_NXASSOC_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxassoc.h
6: * File-type -> launcher-program association table (nxfilem rewrite).
7: *
8: * Header-only, static-inline, same pattern as nxicon.h/nxres.h/nxexec.h:
9: * dropped into any translation unit that needs it, no separate .c/link step.
10: *
11: * This is the single, reusable place that decides WHAT program opens a given
12: * file path, by extension. It does NOT decide HOW to launch it — that
13: * remains nxexec.h's job (nxexec_spawn_search()/nxexec_spawn_detached()).
14: * Before this header, the association was a hardcoded if/else chain private
15: * to nxfilem/fileops.c; any other app that wanted "open this file with the
16: * right program" (a future nxshell `open <path>`, a desktop double-click
17: * elsewhere) had no shared logic to call.
18: *
19: * Resolution order (nxassoc_resolve):
20: *   1. images (os1_image_path_has_known_ext, image.h — reused, not
21: *      duplicated) -> /sys/bin/nximage
22: *   2. exact-extension match against nxassoc_table[] (case-insensitive,
23: *      os1_image_ext_eq from image.h) -> the mapped program, including
24: *      ".lua" -> /bin/lua
25: *   3. an extensionless path under /bin/ or /sys/bin/ -> itself, executed
26: *      directly (NXASSOC_KIND_EXEC, no argv[1])
27: *   4. fallback -> /bin/kilo (plain text editor)
28: *
29: * Directories are the caller's responsibility (nxassoc_resolve never sees
30: * one) — nxfilem navigates into a directory instead of "opening" it.
31: */
32:
33:#include <image.h>
34:#include <os1.h>
35:#include <os1vid.h>
36:#include <string.h>
37:
38:/* NXASSOC_KIND_ARG: launch "<prog> <path>" (argv[0]=prog, argv[1]=path).
39: * NXASSOC_KIND_EXEC: launch "<path>" directly (path IS the program). */
40:#define NXASSOC_KIND_ARG 0
41:#define NXASSOC_KIND_EXEC 1
42:
43:#define NXASSOC_PROG_MAX 32
44:
45:typedef struct {
46:  const char *ext;
47:  const char *prog;
48:} nxassoc_rule_t;
49:
50:/* Extension table, longest/most-specific alternatives are not needed here
51: * since matching is exact (os1_image_ext_eq), not prefix-based. Ordered by
52: * rough popularity, not that order matters for correctness. */
53:static const nxassoc_rule_t nxassoc_table[] = {
54:    {".lua", "/bin/lua"},  {".c", "/bin/kilo"},    {".h", "/bin/kilo"},
55:    {".cpp", "/bin/kilo"}, {".hpp", "/bin/kilo"},  {".s", "/bin/kilo"},
56:    {".S", "/bin/kilo"},   {".md", "/bin/kilo"},   {".txt", "/bin/kilo"},
57:    {".log", "/bin/kilo"}, {".cfg", "/bin/kilo"},  {".json", "/bin/kilo"},
58:    {".ini", "/bin/kilo"}, {".toml", "/bin/kilo"}, {".yaml", "/bin/kilo"},
59:    {".yml", "/bin/kilo"}, {".html", "/bin/kilo"}, {".htm", "/bin/kilo"},
60:    {".css", "/bin/kilo"}, {".sh", "/bin/kilo"},   {".py", "/bin/kilo"},
61:};
62:#define NXASSOC_NRULES (int)(sizeof(nxassoc_table) / sizeof(nxassoc_table[0]))
63:
64:/* nxassoc_is_exec_path - an extensionless path directly under /bin/ or
65: * /sys/bin/: treated as a launchable executable rather than routed to any
66: * editor/viewer. */
67:static inline int nxassoc_is_exec_path(const char *path) {
68:  if (!path)
69:    return 0;
70:  int under_bin =
71:      (strncmp(path, "/bin/", 5) == 0 || strncmp(path, "/sys/bin/", 9) == 0);
72:  if (!under_bin)
73:    return 0;
74:  const char *name = strrchr(path, '/');
75:  name = name ? name + 1 : path;
76:  const char *dot = strrchr(name, '.');
77:  return dot == NULL || dot == name; /* no extension, or a dotfile */
78:}
79:
80:/*
81: * nxassoc_resolve - resolve 'path' to a launch program + kind.
82: * out_prog (NXASSOC_PROG_MAX bytes) receives the program path (for
83: * NXASSOC_KIND_EXEC, out_prog is a copy of 'path' itself).  Returns
84: * NXASSOC_KIND_ARG or NXASSOC_KIND_EXEC.  'path' is never a directory
85: * (caller's responsibility, see header comment).
86: */
87:static inline int nxassoc_resolve(const char *path, char *out_prog, size_t sz) {
88:  if (os1_image_path_has_known_ext(path) || os1vid_path_has_known_ext(path)) {
89:    snprintf(out_prog, sz, "%s", "/sys/bin/nximage");
90:    return NXASSOC_KIND_ARG;
91:  }
92:
93:  const char *name = strrchr(path, '/');
94:  name = name ? name + 1 : path;
95:  const char *ext = strrchr(name, '.');
96:  if (ext && ext != name) {
97:    for (int i = 0; i < NXASSOC_NRULES; i++) {
98:      if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, nxassoc_table[i].ext)) {
99:        snprintf(out_prog, sz, "%s", nxassoc_table[i].prog);
100:        return NXASSOC_KIND_ARG;
101:      }
102:    }
103:  }
104:  if (nxassoc_is_exec_path(path)) {
105:    snprintf(out_prog, sz, "%s", path);
106:    return NXASSOC_KIND_EXEC;
107:  }
108:
109:  snprintf(out_prog, sz, "%s", "/bin/kilo");
110:  return NXASSOC_KIND_ARG;
111:}
112:
113:#endif /* _USER_NXASSOC_H */
114:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxbar.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxbar.c
3: * NEXS top bar (nxbar) — classic-X11-style menu/status bar.
4: *
5: * nxbar is nxui's counterpart at the TOP of the screen.  It now shares nxui's
6: * exact visual language (FIX(GFX-NXBAR-04) — previously it was a flat,
7: * full-width, opaque, square-corner X11/Motif strip flush against the top
8: * edge, visually inconsistent with nxui's floating rounded dock, and — worse
9: * — the compositor had no notion of nxbar's flush-to-edge footprint as
10: * reserved chrome, so ordinary windows could be placed/dragged right
11: * underneath it; see compositor.c FIX(GFX-COMP-RESERVE-01)):
12: *   - inset from the screen edges by BAR_MARGIN_SIDE/BAR_MARGIN_TOP, same
13: *     values nxui uses for DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE/DOCK_MARGIN_BOTTOM;
14: *   - rounded outer corners (BAR_RADIUS == nxui's DOCK_RADIUS);
15: *   - the same semi-translucent panel colour family (COL_BAR_BG carries the
16: *     same 0xE8 alpha as nxui's COL_DOCK_BG).
17: * Same posture as nxui otherwise: a top_most, chromeless compositor window,
18: * self-rendered into an owned ARGB buffer and blitted every frame it
19: * actually changes.  Being inset (not flush at y==0) does NOT stop the
20: * compositor from reserving its footprint any more — the reservation is
21: * geometry-based (any top_most window within a few px of a screen edge), not
22: * "y must be exactly 0".
23: *
24: * Layout, left to right, within the fixed BAR_H strip:
25: *   [X]  <reserved per-app menu strip>  <focused window title>  ...........
26: *        ...........  [battery stub] [notifications v] [date + time]
27: *
28: *   - [X]: the root menu button.  Click opens a dropdown with:
29: *       "System Info"  -> launches /sys/bin/nxinfo (nxinfo.h's read-only
30: *                          system summary) via nxexec_spawn_hosted(), the
31: *                          same launcher path nxlauncher's tiles use — this
32: *                          is the "link to shell info" entry.
33: *       "Power..."     -> launches /sys/bin/nxpower (see nxpower.c), the
34: *                          dedicated shutdown/restart program.
35: *     nxbar holds no power-management logic itself; it only launches the
36: *     dedicated tool, same separation nxui keeps from the apps it manages.
37: *
38: *   - reserved per-app menu strip (MENU_RESERVED_W): deliberately left
39: *     BLANK today.  A classic X11/Mac-style bar eventually grows a menu that
40: *     belongs to whichever app is focused (File/Edit/... — not implemented
41: *     anywhere in this codebase yet).  The space is reserved now so that
42: *     slot can be filled in later without re-flowing every other widget's
43: *     x position; see NOTE(GFX-NXBAR-01) below.
44: *
45: *   - focused window title: read the same way nxui tracks g_last_focus —
46: *     OS1_window_enum() + WININFO_FOCUSED — but nxbar only needs the TITLE,
47: *     not window control, so it holds no control authority at all (strictly
48: *     read-only over other windows; contrast nxui, which legitimately needs
49: *     OS1_window_focus/minimize/restore for its job).
50: *
51: *   - battery: STUB (NOTE(GFX-NXBAR-02) below) — no battery/ACPI syscall
52: *     exists anywhere in this codebase today, so this always reads "AC"
53: *     with a solid (charging) dot.  Real readings need a kernel-side
54: *     battery-status syscall; until then this is an honest placeholder, not
55: *     a fabricated percentage.
56: *
57: *   - notifications: a small badge button (unread count from the SAME
58: *     sys.ntfy.log.* registry ring nxnotify.c/nxntfy_srv.c/nxsettings.c
59: *     already read) that expands the SAME window downward to show the most
60: *     recent notifications (see "Dropdown model" below).  Read-only over
61: *     the registry (OS1_registry_get/enum_under) — nxbar never writes a
62: *     notification's read/unread state itself; that stays nxntfy_srv's job.
63: *
64: *   - date/time: OS1_time_now() formatted with a small self-contained civil
65: *     calendar routine (no <time.h>/localtime anywhere in this codebase to
66: *     build on).  NOTE(GFX-NXBAR-03): OS1_time_now()'s own doc comment calls
67: *     it "wall-clock seconds", but get_time()'s doc comment (nxinfo.h) calls
68: *     the same-shaped value "the millisecond monotonic clock" — the two
69: *     comments in the shared header do not agree on what this call returns.
70: *     nxbar treats the value as wall-clock seconds ONLY if it is at least
71: *     NXBAR_EPOCH_SANITY (a date not obviously "shortly after boot"); below
72: *     that threshold it shows plain elapsed uptime (HH:MM:SS since boot)
73: *     instead of a bogus 1970-ish date. Whichever behavior OS1_time_now()
74: *     actually has, the bar never lies about it.
75: *
76: * Dropdown model: a THIRD, separate top_most overlay window per dropdown
77: * was considered and rejected — input_event_t has no documented window-id
78: * field anywhere in this codebase's headers, so which window a second
79: * concurrently-open window of the SAME process would receive events for is
80: * not something this codebase demonstrates anywhere, and guessing at that
81: * is exactly the kind of "looks plausible, unverifiable" shortcut worth
82: * avoiding.  Instead, nxbar's own window simply GROWS downward (destroy +
83: * recreate at BAR_H + panel_h, precisely the technique nxui's dock_reinit
84: * already uses on a resolution change) when a dropdown opens, and shrinks
85: * back to exactly BAR_H when it closes or a click lands outside it — so
86: * there is never an invisible click-catching area over whatever sits below
87: * the bar, and every click stays in the one window/one input_poll_event
88: * loop this codebase's model already relies on everywhere else.
89: *
90: * SECURITY MODEL: nxbar reads OS1_window_enum() (titles/flags of everything,
91: * same as nxwins/nxui) and the registry notification ring — both already
92: * readable at nxbar's own level; it holds no window CONTROL capability and
93: * launches only two fixed, hardcoded paths (no arbitrary spawn from user
94: * input). Secure by caller, widens nothing, exactly like nxui/nxwins.
95: *
96: * Discovery/lifecycle: spawned once by init at boot (like nxui/nxntfy_srv),
97: * singleton-guarded by window title ("nxbar") the same way nxui guards
98: * itself, so a legitimate init respawn after a crash proceeds normally.
99: *
100: * FIX(GFX-NXBAR-05): visual-consistency pass. Three concrete problems, not
101: * vague "looks off" ones:
102: *   1. BAR_RADIUS copied nxui's DOCK_RADIUS as an ABSOLUTE value (12px), but
103: *      nxbar's strip (BAR_H=26) is less than half the dock's height (56).
104: *      Same absolute radius on a much shorter shape means the corner arc
105: *      eats ~46% of the strip's height instead of the dock's ~21% — a
106: *      different, larger PROPORTION, which is why it read as over-rounded
107: *      and out of step with the rest of the desktop even though the number
108: *      matched nxui's. Fixed by matching the RATIO instead of the raw
109: *      value (see BAR_RADIUS/BAR_BTN_RADIUS below).
110: *   2. The renderer itself: nxbar now uses the EXACT same quarter-circle
111: *      mask test nxui.c does for its dock (binary in/out, same per-pixel
112: *      test, same shape). Trying to be "softer" with a smoothstep/feather
113: *      would make the bar look DIFFERENT from the dock at the pixel level
114: *      — a half-pixel mismatch between two adjacent chrome surfaces is
115: *      louder than a wrong colour. A single renderer for both strips is
116: *      the actual fix for "sembla finto".
117: *   3. The dropdown panels (menu/notify) were drawn as fully independent
118: *      four-corner rounded rects flush against the strip's own fully
119: *      rounded bottom edge — two separate "pill" shapes touching at a
120: *      seam, which is the concrete source of the reported visual clutter.
121: *      The strip now drops its BOTTOM corner rounding while a panel is
122: *      open (flat join edge) and the panel drops its TOP corner rounding
123: *      (also flat) and rounds only its bottom two corners — one continuous
124: *      shape that visibly hangs from the bar instead of two shapes glued
125: *      together. fb_rrect_4 (4 independent radii) is the primitive that
126: *      makes this possible.
127: * Also added: a compact layout (BAR_COMPACT_W) that drops the "AC" label
128: * and the "Notif" text and shortens the clock to HH:MM under a narrow
129: * (phone-width) desktop, so the same single layout works on mobile and
130: * desktop instead of overflowing/crowding the right cluster on the former.
131: *
132: * FIX(GFX-NXBAR-06): 1px identity ring around the [X] menu button glyph.
133: * Originally the ring was drawn around the whole button square, which made
134: * the X look like a floating sticker.  Later a manually drawn "X" shape was
135: * tried, but it looked harsh and out of place.  The final solution keeps the
136: * original font glyph (buf_draw_text("X")) and creates a 1‑pixel outline by
137: * drawing the glyph four times, offset by (±1,0) and (0,±1), in the border
138: * colour, and then once more in the centre with the glyph colour.  This
139: * gives a crisp, 1‑px ring that hugs the actual letterform and stays
140: * perfectly consistent with the rest of the text on the bar.
141: */
142:#include <font_lib.h>
143:#include <input.h>
144:#include <os1.h>
145:#include <string.h>

282:/* ============================================================
283: *           Pixel + font helpers (same technique as
284: *           nxlauncher.c/nximage.c/nxsettings.c — no shared
285: *           header for this exists in the codebase yet)
286: * ============================================================ */
287:static uint32_t *g_fb;
288:static int g_bw; /* buffer/window width  == desktop width (full-width bar) */
289:static int g_wh; /* buffer/window height == BAR_H, or BAR_H+panel when a
290:                  * dropdown is open (see "Dropdown model" above)         */
291:static struct font_ctx *g_font;
292:
293:static void fb_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h, uint32_t c) {
294:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
295:    return;
296:  int x2 = x + w, y2 = y + h;
297:  if (x2 > g_bw)
298:    x2 = g_bw;
299:  if (y2 > g_wh)
300:    y2 = g_wh;
301:  for (int j = (y < 0 ? 0 : y); j < y2; j++)
302:    for (int i = (x < 0 ? 0 : x); i < x2; i++)
303:      g_fb[j * g_bw + i] = c;
304:}
305:
306:/* fb_rrect_4 - filled rectangle with FOUR INDEPENDENT corner radii, the SAME
307: * quarter-circle mask test nxui.c uses (GFX-NXBAR-05). Two things this gives
308: * us, both on purpose:
309: *
310: *   1. Visual coherence with the dock: nxui's rounded rect IS a binary
311: *      "inside/outside the quarter-circle" test — no alpha falloff, no
312: *      feather. Picking the same shape here means the bar and the dock
313: *      read as drawn by the same renderer at the same physical pixel
314: *      step. Anything fancier (smoothstep, supersampling) would make the
315: *      bar look SOFTER than the dock and re-introduce exactly the "stona
316: *      con il sistema" reaction the user is reporting — a half-pixel
317: *      mismatch reads louder than a wrong colour.
318: *
319: *   2. A flush join between the strip and a dropdown. The strip draws
320: *      with r_bl=r_br=0 (flat bottom) when a panel is open, and the
321: *      panel draws with r_tl=r_tr=0 (flat top) — same shape, no seam,
322: *      and the two read as ONE body that hangs from the bar instead of
323: *      two pills glued side by side. When no panel is open, all four
324: *      corners of the strip round normally.
325: *
326: * r_tl/r_tr/r_bl/r_br: 0 = square for that corner, non-zero = quarter-circle
327: * radius. Each is independently clamped to w/2 and h/2. */
328:static void fb_rrect_4(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r_tl, int r_tr, int r_bl,
329:                       int r_br, uint32_t c) {
330:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
331:    return;
332:  if (r_tl < 0)
333:    r_tl = 0;
334:  if (r_tr < 0)
335:    r_tr = 0;
336:  if (r_bl < 0)
337:    r_bl = 0;
338:  if (r_br < 0)
339:    r_br = 0;
340:  if (r_tl > w / 2)
341:    r_tl = w / 2;
342:  if (r_tr > w / 2)
343:    r_tr = w / 2;
344:  if (r_bl > w / 2)
345:    r_bl = w / 2;
346:  if (r_br > w / 2)
347:    r_br = w / 2;
348:  if (r_tl > h / 2)
349:    r_tl = h / 2;
350:  if (r_tr > h / 2)
351:    r_tr = h / 2;
352:  if (r_bl > h / 2)
353:    r_bl = h / 2;
354:  if (r_br > h / 2)
355:    r_br = h / 2;
356:
357:  for (int j = 0; j < h; j++) {
358:    for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
359:      int ccx = -1, ccy = 0, r = 0;
360:      if (i < r_tl && j < r_tl) {
361:        r = r_tl;
362:        ccx = r;
363:        ccy = r;
364:      } else if (i >= w - r_tr && j < r_tr) {
365:        r = r_tr;
366:        ccx = w - r - 1;
367:        ccy = r;
368:      } else if (i < r_bl && j >= h - r_bl) {
369:        r = r_bl;
370:        ccx = r;
371:        ccy = h - r - 1;
372:      } else if (i >= w - r_br && j >= h - r_br) {
373:        r = r_br;
374:        ccx = w - r - 1;
375:        ccy = h - r - 1;
376:      }
377:
378:      if (ccx >= 0) {
379:        int dx = i - ccx, dy = j - ccy;
380:        if (dx * dx + dy * dy > r * r)
381:          continue;
382:      }
383:
384:      int px = x + i, py = y + j;
385:      if (px >= 0 && px < g_bw && py >= 0 && py < g_wh)
386:        g_fb[py * g_bw + px] = c;
387:    }
388:  }
389:}
390:
391:/* fb_rrect - convenience wrapper: all four corners share the same radius
392: * (the common case — buttons, the closed strip with no dropdown open). */
393:static void fb_rrect(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint32_t c) {
394:  fb_rrect_4(x, y, w, h, r, r, r, r, c);
395:}
396:
397:static void buf_draw_glyph(int x, int y, uint32_t codepoint, uint32_t color) {
398:  if (!g_font)
399:    return;
400:  int idx = (int)codepoint - g_font->header.first_char;
401:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= g_font->header.num_chars)
402:    return;
403:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &g_font->glyphs[idx];
404:  uint8_t *bitmap = g_font->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
405:  int start_x = x + gi->x0;
406:  int start_y = y + g_font->header.ascent + gi->y0;
407:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
408:    for (int gx = 0; gx < gi->width; gx++) {
409:      uint8_t alpha = bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx];
410:      if (alpha > 64) {
411:        int px = start_x + gx, py = start_y + gy;
412:        if (px >= 0 && px < g_bw && py >= 0 && py < g_wh)
413:          g_fb[py * g_bw + px] = color;
414:      }
415:    }
416:  }
417:}
418:
419:static int buf_text_width(const char *s) {
420:  if (!g_font || !s)
421:    return 0;
422:  return font_string_width(g_font, s);
423:}
424:
425:static void buf_draw_text(int x, int y, const char *s, uint32_t color) {
426:  if (!g_font || !s)
427:    return;
428:  uint32_t cp;
429:  int consumed, cursor = x;
430:  size_t rem = strlen(s);
431:  const char *p = s;
432:  while (*p) {
433:    consumed = utf8_decode(p, rem, &cp);
434:    if (consumed <= 0) {
435:      p++;
436:      rem--;
437:      continue;
438:    }
439:    buf_draw_glyph(cursor, y, cp, color);
440:    int idx = (int)cp - g_font->header.first_char;
441:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < g_font->header.num_chars)
442:      cursor += g_font->glyphs[idx].advance;
443:    p += consumed;
444:    rem -= consumed;
445:  }
446:}
