448:/* ============================================================
449: *              Self-contained wall-clock formatting
450: *      (no <time.h>/localtime anywhere in this codebase)
451: * ============================================================ */
452:
453:/* civil_from_days: days-since-1970-01-01 -> proleptic-Gregorian (y, m, d).
454: * Standard constant-time algorithm (Hinnant, public-domain technique). */
455:static void civil_from_days(long z, int *y, int *m, int *d) {
456:  z += 719468;
457:  long era = (z >= 0 ? z : z - 146096) / 146097;
458:  unsigned long doe = (unsigned long)(z - era * 146097);
459:  unsigned long yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365;
460:  long yy = (long)yoe + era * 400;
461:  unsigned long doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
462:  unsigned long mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
463:  unsigned long dd = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
464:  unsigned long mm = mp + (mp < 10 ? 3 : (unsigned long)-9);
465:  *y = (int)(yy + (mm <= 2 ? 1 : 0));
466:  *m = (int)mm;
467:  *d = (int)dd;
468:}
469:
470:static void format_datetime(char *buf, int n) {
471:  static const char *WD[7] = {"Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"};
472:  long t = OS1_time_now();
473:
474:  if (t >= NXBAR_EPOCH_SANITY) {
475:    long days = t / 86400;
476:    long secs = t % 86400;
477:    int hh = (int)(secs / 3600);
478:    int mi = (int)((secs / 60) % 60);
479:    int ss = (int)(secs % 60);
480:    int y, mo, d;
481:    civil_from_days(days, &y, &mo, &d);
482:    int wd = (int)(((days % 7) + 10) % 7); /* 1970-01-01 was a Thursday */
483:    snprintf(buf, n, "%s %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d", WD[wd], y, mo, d, hh,
484:             mi, ss);
485:  } else {
486:    /* Not a plausible wall-clock reading (see NOTE(GFX-NXBAR-03)) — show
487:     * elapsed time since boot instead of a bogus date. */
488:    long ms = get_time();
489:    long secs = ms / 1000;
490:    int hh = (int)(secs / 3600);
491:    int mi = (int)((secs / 60) % 60);
492:    int ss = (int)(secs % 60);
493:    snprintf(buf, n, "up %02d:%02d:%02d", hh, mi, ss);
494:  }
495:}
496:
497:/* ============================================================
498: *                 Notification ring reader
499: *   (same sys.ntfy.log.* record format as nxnotify.c/nxsettings.c)
500: * ============================================================ */
501:struct nxbar_nrec {
502:  int pid;
503:  int sev;
504:  char state;
505:  char text[48];
506:};
507:
508:/* --- ordinamento per PID (bubble sort, n <= 16) --- */
509:static int cmp_pid(const struct nxbar_nrec *a, const struct nxbar_nrec *b) {
510:  return a->pid - b->pid;
511:}
512:static void sort_recs(struct nxbar_nrec *r, int n) {
513:  for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++)
514:    for (int j = 0; j < n - i - 1; j++)
515:      if (cmp_pid(&r[j], &r[j + 1]) > 0) {
516:        struct nxbar_nrec tmp = r[j];
517:        r[j] = r[j + 1];
518:        r[j + 1] = tmp;
519:      }
520:}
521:
522:static int nxbar_notify_fetch(struct nxbar_nrec *out, int max) {
523:  char keys[640];
524:  int n = OS1_registry_enum_under("sys.ntfy.log.", keys, sizeof(keys));
525:  if (n <= 0)
526:    return 0;
527:  int cnt = 0;
528:  char key[64];
529:  int k = 0;
530:  for (const char *p = keys; cnt < max; p++) {
531:    if (*p == '\n' || *p == '\0') {
532:      if (k > 0) {
533:        key[k] = '\0';
534:        char val[80];
535:        if (OS1_registry_get(key, val, sizeof(val)) == 0) {
536:          const char *q = val;
537:          out[cnt].pid = atoi(q);
538:          while (*q && *q != '|')
539:            q++;
540:          if (*q)
541:            q++;
542:          out[cnt].sev = atoi(q);
543:          while (*q && *q != '|')
544:            q++;
545:          if (*q)
546:            q++;
547:          out[cnt].state = *q ? *q : 'U';
548:          while (*q && *q != '|')
549:            q++;
550:          if (*q)
551:            q++;
552:          int t = 0;
553:          for (; *q && t < 47; q++)
554:            out[cnt].text[t++] = *q;
555:          out[cnt].text[t] = '\0';
556:          cnt++;
557:        }
558:      }
559:      k = 0;
560:      if (*p == '\0')
561:        break;
562:    } else if (k < (int)sizeof(key) - 1) {
563:      key[k++] = *p;
564:    }
565:  }
566:  return cnt;
567:}
568:
569:/* ============================================================
570: *                         Bar state
571: * ============================================================ */
572:static int g_win = -1;
573:static int g_dsw, g_dsh; /* last-seen DESKTOP size (bar is always full-width) */
574:static unsigned g_sig;
575:
576:enum { PANEL_NONE = 0, PANEL_MENU, PANEL_NOTIFY };
577:static int g_panel = PANEL_NONE;
578:static long g_panel_opened_ms;
579:#define PANEL_AUTOCLOSE_MS 8000
580:
581:static char g_focus_title[64] = "";
582:
583:/* hit-rects, rebuilt every redraw */
584:static int g_xbtn_x, g_xbtn_w;
585:static int g_notifbtn_x, g_notifbtn_w;
586:static int g_notify_panel_h; /* current notif panel height, recomputed live */
587:static int g_notify_panel_x; /* X position of notification panel */
588:
589:enum { MENU_SETTINGS = 0, MENU_POWER = 1 };
590:
591:/* set_window_height - grow/shrink the bar's own window to exactly
592: * BAR_H + extra_h (see "Dropdown model" in the header comment). Reuses the
593: * destroy+recreate-at-new-size idiom nxui's dock_reinit already uses on a
594: * resolution change, so this is a proven technique, not a new one. */
595:static void set_window_height(int extra_h) {
596:  int wh = BAR_H + (extra_h > 0 ? extra_h : 0);
597:  if (wh == g_wh && g_win >= 0)
598:    return;
599:  uint32_t *nb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)g_bw * wh * 4);
600:  if (nb) {
601:    free(g_fb);
602:    g_fb = nb;
603:  }
604:  g_wh = wh;
605:  if (g_win >= 0)
606:    destroy_window(g_win);
607:  /* GFX-NXBAR-04: inset from the top/side edges like nxui's dock_reinit,
608:   * instead of flush at (0,0). The compositor's reservation (see
609:   * compositor.c FIX(GFX-COMP-RESERVE-01)) is geometry-based, not "y must be
610:   * 0", so this stays correctly reserved. */
611:  g_win = create_window(BAR_MARGIN_SIDE, BAR_MARGIN_TOP, g_bw, g_wh, "nxbar");
612:  if (g_win >= 0)
613:    set_window_flags(g_win, 1); /* top_most, chromeless — see nxui's dock */
614:  g_sig = 0;                    /* force a repaint at the new size */
615:}
616:
617:/* bar_reinit - (re)create for a new DESKTOP width (or first start).
618: * Keeps whatever panel is currently open at its own height. Insets the bar's
619: * own width from the desktop width by BAR_MARGIN_SIDE on each side, same as
620: * nxui's dock_reinit computes g_sw from DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE (GFX-NXBAR-04). */
621:static void bar_reinit(int sw, int sh) {
622:  g_dsw = sw;
623:  g_dsh = sh;
624:  int bw = (sw > 0 ? sw : 800) - 2 * BAR_MARGIN_SIDE;
625:  if (bw < BAR_MIN_W)
626:    bw = BAR_MIN_W;
627:  g_bw = bw;
628:  int extra = (g_panel == PANEL_MENU)     ? MENU_H
629:              : (g_panel == PANEL_NOTIFY) ? g_notify_panel_h
630:                                          : 0;
631:  g_wh = 0; /* force set_window_height to always (re)create at the new width */
632:  set_window_height(extra);
633:}
634:
635:static void close_panel(void) {
636:  /* Segnala che il pannello notifiche è stato chiuso, così nxntfy_srv può
637:   * ricominciare a mostrare i popup. */
638:  if (g_panel == PANEL_NOTIFY)
639:    OS1_registry_set("sys.ntfy.panel_open", "0");
640:  g_panel = PANEL_NONE;
641:  set_window_height(0);
642:}
643:
644:static void open_menu(void) {
645:  g_panel = PANEL_MENU;
646:  g_panel_opened_ms = get_time();
647:  set_window_height(MENU_H);
648:}
649:
650:static void open_notify(int panel_h) {
651:  g_panel = PANEL_NOTIFY;
652:  g_notify_panel_h = panel_h;
653:  g_panel_opened_ms = get_time();
654:  set_window_height(panel_h);
655:  /* Segnala che il pannello notifiche è aperto, così nxntfy_srv non mostrerà
656:   * popup sovrapposti. */
657:  OS1_registry_set("sys.ntfy.panel_open", "1");
658:}
659:
660:static void redraw(int force) {
661:  /* ---- focused window title (read-only; same technique as nxui's
662:   * g_last_focus, but nxbar never calls OS1_window_focus/minimize) ---- */
663:  struct window_info wi[MAX_TILES];
664:  int n = (int)OS1_window_enum(wi, MAX_TILES);
665:  if (n < 0)
666:    n = 0;
667:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
668:    if (wi[i].id == g_win)
669:      continue;
670:    if (wi[i].flags & (WININFO_TOPMOST | WININFO_PASSIVE))
671:      continue;
672:    if (wi[i].flags & WININFO_FOCUSED) {
673:      /* Phase 3: prefer the launch identity nxexec published
674:       * (sys.proc.<pid>.name) over the app's own window title, so the bar
675:       * shows a stable, canonical name; fall back to the title when a window
676:       * has no registered identity (e.g. a system service). */
677:      char idkey[48], idname[40];
678:      snprintf(idkey, sizeof(idkey), "sys.proc.%d.name", wi[i].pid);
679:      if (OS1_registry_get(idkey, idname, sizeof(idname)) == 0 && idname[0])
680:        snprintf(g_focus_title, sizeof(g_focus_title), "%s", idname);
681:      else
682:        snprintf(g_focus_title, sizeof(g_focus_title), "%s", wi[i].title);
683:      break;
684:    }
685:  }
686:
687:  /* ---- notifications: fetch every frame (cheap, bounded to 16 records) —
688:   * drives both the badge count and, when open, the panel's own rows ---- */
689:  struct nxbar_nrec recs[NXBAR_NOTIFY_MAX];
690:  int nrec = nxbar_notify_fetch(recs, NXBAR_NOTIFY_MAX);
691:  int unread = 0;
692:  for (int i = 0; i < nrec; i++)
693:    if (recs[i].state == 'U')
694:      unread++;
695:
696:  /* If the notify panel is open, its height tracks the live record count;
697:   * grow/shrink the window to match before drawing into it. */
698:  if (g_panel == PANEL_NOTIFY) {
699:    int want_h = (nrec > 0 ? nrec : 1) * NOTIFY_ROW_H + 10;
700:    if (want_h > NOTIFY_PANEL_MAX_H)
701:      want_h = NOTIFY_PANEL_MAX_H;
702:    if (want_h != g_notify_panel_h) {
703:      g_notify_panel_h = want_h;
704:      set_window_height(want_h);
705:    }
706:  }
707:
708:  char dt[40];
709:  format_datetime(dt, sizeof(dt));
710:
711:  /* auto-close whichever dropdown is open after PANEL_AUTOCLOSE_MS idle */
712:  if (g_panel != PANEL_NONE &&
713:      get_time() - g_panel_opened_ms > PANEL_AUTOCLOSE_MS)
714:    close_panel();
715:
716:  unsigned sig = 2166136261u ^ (unsigned)g_bw ^ ((unsigned)unread << 8) ^
717:                 ((unsigned)g_panel << 16);
718:  for (const char *p = dt; *p; p++)
719:    sig = (sig ^ (unsigned)*p) * 16777619u;
720:  for (const char *p = g_focus_title; *p; p++)
721:    sig = (sig ^ (unsigned)*p) * 16777619u;
722:  if (!force && sig == g_sig)
723:    return;
724:  g_sig = sig;
725:
726:  /* --- strip + optional dropdown, drawn as a SINGLE coherent body ---
727:   *
728:   * GFX-NXBAR-05: when no panel is open, the strip rounds all four corners
729:   * exactly like the closed bar. When a panel IS open, the strip's bottom
730:   * two corners go flat (r_bl=r_br=0) and the panel's top two corners go
731:   * flat (r_tl=r_tr=0) — the two shapes share the seam at y=BAR_H and
732:   * read as one continuous body hanging from the bar, not two pills
733:   * stacked. The panel keeps its bottom rounded (r_bl=r_br=BAR_RADIUS)
734:   * because the bottom edge is in open air, same way the closed bar's
735:   * bottom edge is. */
736:  if (g_panel == PANEL_NONE) {
737:    fb_rrect(0, 0, g_bw, BAR_H, BAR_RADIUS, g_col_bar_bg);
738:  } else {
739:    /* strip: top rounded, bottom flat so it flush-joins the panel */
740:    fb_rrect_4(0, 0, g_bw, BAR_H, BAR_RADIUS, BAR_RADIUS, 0, 0, g_col_bar_bg);
741:    /* area below the strip is transparent, NOT the strip's own colour —
742:     * the panel will draw its own background over [BAR_H, BAR_H+panel_h)
743:     * with a flat top that matches the strip's flat bottom. */
744:    fb_rect(0, BAR_H, g_bw, g_wh - BAR_H, 0x00000000);
745:  }
746:
747:  /* 1px top hairline (GFX-NXBAR-05): the dock has its own tile highlights
748:   * and reads as a textured surface; a flat translucent strip on its own
749:   * looks "dead". One barely-there brighter line along the very top edge
750:   * is the same glass-panel trick nxsettings already uses on its panels —
751:   * applied here so nxbar stops looking like the odd one out. Skipped
752:   * on the rounded corner pixels (they're outside the rect anyway). */
753:  if (g_col_bar_hi != 0) {
754:    int hi_x0 = BAR_RADIUS;
755:    int hi_x1 = g_bw - BAR_RADIUS;
756:    if (hi_x1 > hi_x0) {
757:      for (int x = hi_x0; x < hi_x1; x++) {
758:        uint32_t dst = g_fb[0 * g_bw + x];
759:        uint32_t dr = (dst >> 16) & 0xFF, dg = (dst >> 8) & 0xFF,
760:                 db = dst & 0xFF;
761:        uint32_t sr = 0xFF, sg = 0xFF, sb = 0xFF;
762:        uint32_t a = (g_col_bar_hi >> 24) & 0xFF;
763:        uint32_t out_r = (sr * a + dr * (255 - a)) / 255;
764:        uint32_t out_g = (sg * a + dg * (255 - a)) / 255;
765:        uint32_t out_b = (sb * a + db * (255 - a)) / 255;
766:        g_fb[0 * g_bw + x] =
767:            (0xFF000000u) | (out_r << 16) | (out_g << 8) | out_b;
768:      }
769:    }
770:  }
771:
772:  g_xbtn_x = 6;
773:  g_xbtn_w = X_BTN_W;
774:  /* Sfondo del pulsante: rettangolo arrotondato come prima. */
775:  fb_rrect(g_xbtn_x, 0, g_xbtn_w, BAR_H, BAR_BTN_RADIUS,
776:           g_panel == PANEL_MENU ? g_col_xbtn_active : g_col_xbtn);
777:  /* GFX-NXBAR-06: contorno di 1 px attorno al glifo X del font.
778:   * Disegniamo la "X" quattro volte nel colore del bordo, spostata di 1 px
779:   * nelle quattro direzioni cardinali, e poi una volta al centro con il
780:   * colore del glifo.  Il risultato è un anello sottile che segue esattamente
781:   * la forma del carattere, senza deformazioni geometriche. */
782:  if (g_font) {
783:    int tw = buf_text_width("X");
784:    int x0 = g_xbtn_x + (g_xbtn_w - tw) / 2;
785:    int y0 = (BAR_H - 16) / 2; /* 16 = altezza font; centrato verticalmente */
786:
787:    /* contorno */
788:    buf_draw_text(x0 - 1, y0, "X", g_col_xbtn_border);
789:    buf_draw_text(x0 + 1, y0, "X", g_col_xbtn_border);
790:    buf_draw_text(x0, y0 - 1, "X", g_col_xbtn_border);
791:    buf_draw_text(x0, y0 + 1, "X", g_col_xbtn_border);
792:
793:    /* glifo vero, sopra – ora prende il colore del background LIVE */
794:    buf_draw_text(x0, y0, "X", nxres_bg_color());
795:  }
796:
797:  /* reserved per-app-menu strip: intentionally blank, see GFX-NXBAR-01 */
798:  int after_reserved = g_xbtn_x + g_xbtn_w + MENU_RESERVED_W;
799:
800:  int dt_w = buf_text_width(dt);
801:  int right_cluster_w = BATTERY_W + RIGHT_GAP + NOTIF_BTN_W + RIGHT_GAP + dt_w;
802:  int right_x = g_bw - PAD - right_cluster_w;
803:  if (right_x < after_reserved)
804:    right_x = after_reserved;
805:
806:  /* battery stub (GFX-NXBAR-02): no ACPI/battery syscall exists yet */
807:  int batt_x = right_x;
808:  fb_rect(batt_x + 2, (BAR_H - 8) / 2, 8, 8, g_col_battery_dot);
809:  if (g_font)
810:    buf_draw_text(batt_x + 16, (BAR_H - 16) / 2, "AC", g_col_text_dim);
811:
812:  /* notifications button (badge = unread count) */
813:  g_notifbtn_x = batt_x + BATTERY_W + RIGHT_GAP;
814:  g_notifbtn_w = NOTIF_BTN_W;
815:  fb_rrect(g_notifbtn_x, 2, g_notifbtn_w, BAR_H - 4, BAR_BTN_RADIUS,
816:           g_panel == PANEL_NOTIFY ? g_col_notif_btn_active : g_col_notif_btn);
817:  if (g_font)
818:    buf_draw_text(g_notifbtn_x + 6, (BAR_H - 16) / 2, "Notif", g_col_text);
819:  if (unread > 0) {
820:    char cnt[8];
821:    snprintf(cnt, sizeof(cnt), "%d", unread > 99 ? 99 : unread);
822:    int bw = 8 + 6 * (int)strlen(cnt);
823:    int bx = g_notifbtn_x + g_notifbtn_w - bw - 2;
824:    fb_rect(bx, 1, bw, 12, g_col_badge);
825:    if (g_font)
826:      buf_draw_text(bx + 3, -2, cnt, g_col_badge_text);
827:  }
828:
829:  /* date/time, flush right */
830:  int dt_x = g_notifbtn_x + g_notifbtn_w + RIGHT_GAP;
831:  if (g_font)
832:    buf_draw_text(dt_x, (BAR_H - 16) / 2, dt, g_col_text);
833:
834:  /* focused window title: fills whatever is left between the reserved strip
835:   * and the right cluster, truncated with "..." if it does not fit */
836:  int title_x = after_reserved;
837:  int title_max_w = dt_x - RIGHT_GAP - title_x;
838:  if (g_font && title_max_w > 20 && g_focus_title[0]) {
839:    char shown[64];
840:    snprintf(shown, sizeof(shown), "%s", g_focus_title);
841:    while (buf_text_width(shown) > title_max_w && strlen(shown) > 3) {
842:      int l = (int)strlen(shown);
843:      shown[l - 4] = '.';
844:      shown[l - 3] = '.';
845:      shown[l - 2] = '.';
846:      shown[l - 1] = '\0';
847:    }
848:    buf_draw_text(title_x, (BAR_H - 16) / 2, shown, g_col_text);
849:  }
850:
851:  /* --- dropdown panel, drawn into [BAR_H, g_wh) when open --- */
852:  if (g_panel == PANEL_MENU) {
853:    /* Menu a comparsa vicino al pulsante X. Top corners flat so it
854:     * flush-joins the strip above; bottom corners rounded because
855:     * the bottom edge is in open air. */
856:    int menu_x = g_xbtn_x;
857:    fb_rrect_4(menu_x, BAR_H, MENU_W, MENU_H, 0, 0, BAR_RADIUS, BAR_RADIUS,
858:               g_col_panel_bg);
859:    fb_rect(menu_x, BAR_H + MENU_ITEM_H, MENU_W, 1, g_col_panel_sep);
860:    if (g_font) {
861:      buf_draw_text(menu_x + 14, BAR_H + (MENU_ITEM_H - 16) / 2, "Settings",
862:                    g_col_text);
863:      buf_draw_text(menu_x + 14,
864:                    BAR_H + MENU_ITEM_H + 3 + (MENU_ITEM_H - 16) / 2,
865:                    "Power...", g_col_text);
866:    }
867:  } else if (g_panel == PANEL_NOTIFY) {
868:    /* Pannello notifiche posizionato vicino al bottone "Notif".
869:     * Same flat-top join as the menu. */
870:    g_notify_panel_x = g_notifbtn_x + g_notifbtn_w - NOTIFY_PANEL_W;
871:    if (g_notify_panel_x < 0)
872:      g_notify_panel_x = 0;
873:    fb_rrect_4(g_notify_panel_x, BAR_H, NOTIFY_PANEL_W, g_notify_panel_h, 0, 0,
874:               BAR_RADIUS, BAR_RADIUS, g_col_panel_bg);
875:    if (nrec == 0) {
876:      if (g_font)
877:        buf_draw_text(g_notify_panel_x + 12, BAR_H + 4, "no notifications",
878:                      g_col_text_dim);
879:    } else {
880:      sort_recs(recs, nrec);
881:      int max_rows = (g_notify_panel_h - 10) / NOTIFY_ROW_H;
882:      int drawn = 0;
883:      int last_pid = -1;
884:      int pid_count = 0;
885:      for (int i = 0; i < nrec && drawn < max_rows && g_font; i++) {
886:        if (recs[i].pid == last_pid) {
887:          pid_count++;
888:          if (i < nrec - 1 && recs[i + 1].pid == last_pid)
889:            continue;
890:        } else {
891:          last_pid = recs[i].pid;
892:          pid_count = 1;
893:        }
894:        char line[64];
895:        const char *sev = recs[i].sev == 2   ? "!!"
896:                          : recs[i].sev == 1 ? "! "
897:                                             : "  ";
898:        uint32_t col = recs[i].sev == 2   ? 0xFFFF6B6Bu
899:                       : recs[i].sev == 1 ? 0xFFFFD080u
900:                                          : g_col_text;
901:        if (pid_count > 1)
902:          snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s PID %d (%d msgs): %s", sev,
903:                   recs[i].pid, pid_count, recs[i].text);
904:        else
905:          snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s PID %d: %s", sev, recs[i].pid,
906:                   recs[i].text);
907:        /* Truncate with "..." to the panel's own content width (same
908:         * technique as the focused-window title above) — snprintf only
909:         * bounds the BYTE count (line[64]), not the rendered PIXEL width,
910:         * so an unclipped line could draw well past NOTIFY_PANEL_W's right
911:         * edge (buf_draw_glyph only clips to the whole WINDOW, not to this
912:         * panel's own rounded rect). */
913:        int line_max_w = NOTIFY_PANEL_W - 24; /* panel width minus l/r margin */
914:        while (buf_text_width(line) > line_max_w && strlen(line) > 3) {
915:          int l = (int)strlen(line);
916:          line[l - 4] = '.';
917:          line[l - 3] = '.';
918:          line[l - 2] = '.';
919:          line[l - 1] = '\0';
920:        }
921:        buf_draw_text(g_notify_panel_x + 12, BAR_H + 4 + drawn * NOTIFY_ROW_H,
922:                      line, col);
923:        drawn++;
924:      }
925:    }
926:  }
927:
928:  window_blit(g_win, 0, 0, g_bw, g_wh, g_fb);
929:}
930:
931:/* ============================================================
932: *                         Click handling
933: * ============================================================
934: * Every click arrives in THIS window's own coordinate space (see "Dropdown
935: * model" above) — my >= BAR_H means it landed in whichever panel is open. */
936:static void handle_click(int mx, int my) {
937:  if (my < BAR_H) {
938:    if (mx >= g_xbtn_x && mx < g_xbtn_x + g_xbtn_w) {
939:      if (g_panel == PANEL_MENU)
940:        close_panel();
941:      else
942:        open_menu();
943:      return;
944:    }
945:    if (mx >= g_notifbtn_x && mx < g_notifbtn_x + g_notifbtn_w) {
946:      if (g_panel == PANEL_NOTIFY)
947:        close_panel();
948:      else {
949:        struct nxbar_nrec recs[NXBAR_NOTIFY_MAX];
950:        int nrec = nxbar_notify_fetch(recs, NXBAR_NOTIFY_MAX);
951:        int h = (nrec > 0 ? nrec : 1) * NOTIFY_ROW_H + 10;
952:        if (h > NOTIFY_PANEL_MAX_H)
953:          h = NOTIFY_PANEL_MAX_H;
954:        open_notify(h);
955:      }
956:      return;
957:    }
958:    /* click landed elsewhere on the bar strip: dismiss whichever panel
959:     * was open (classic "click outside to dismiss" behaviour) */
960:    if (g_panel != PANEL_NONE)
961:      close_panel();
962:    return;
963:  }
964:
965:  /* click landed inside an open panel */
966:  if (g_panel == PANEL_MENU) {
967:    int idx = (my - BAR_H) / MENU_ITEM_H;
968:    if (idx == MENU_SETTINGS)
969:      nxexec_spawn_hosted("/sys/bin/nxsettings");
970:    else if (idx == MENU_POWER)
971:      nxexec_spawn_hosted("/sys/bin/nxpower");
972:    close_panel();
973:  } else if (g_panel == PANEL_NOTIFY) {
974:    /* read-only list today: any click inside it just dismisses it */
975:    close_panel();
976:  }
977:}
978:
979:int main(void) {
980:  /* Singleton, same technique as nxui: bow out if another "nxbar" window
981:   * already exists; a legitimate init respawn after a crash finds none. */
982:  {
983:    struct window_info wi[MAX_TILES];
984:    int n = (int)OS1_window_enum(wi, MAX_TILES);
985:    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
986:      if (strncmp(wi[i].title, "nxbar", 6) == 0)
987:        return 0;
988:  }
989:
990:  g_font = font_load("/fonts/Rewir-Light.off");
991:
992:  long di = OS1_display_info();
993:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
994:  int sh = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
995:  if (sw <= 0)
996:    sw = 800;
997:  if (sh <= 0)
998:    sh = 600;
999:
1000:  nxbar_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
1001:  g_col_xbtn_glyph = nxres_bg_color(); /* dipende dal background, NON dal
1002:                                        * tema — nxres_bg_color() legge
1003:                                        * "background.name" e risolve via
1004:                                        * os1_bg_colors (nxres.h) */
1005:
1006:  g_fb = NULL;
1007:  g_win = -1;
1008:  g_wh = 0;
1009:  bar_reinit(sw, sh);
1010:  if (g_win < 0)
1011:    return 1;
1012:
1013:  redraw(1);
1014:
1015:  for (;;) {
1016:    long d = OS1_display_info();
1017:    int cw = (int)((d >> 16) & 0xFFFF), ch = (int)(d & 0xFFFF);
1018:    if (cw > 0 && ch > 0 && (cw != g_dsw || ch != g_dsh))
1019:      bar_reinit(cw, ch);
1020:
1021:    redraw(0);
1022:
1023:    input_event_t ev;
1024:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
1025:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE && ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
1026:          ev.mouse.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
1027:        handle_click(ev.mouse.x, ev.mouse.y);
1028:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE) {
1029:        long d2 = OS1_display_info();
1030:        int rw = (int)((d2 >> 16) & 0xFFFF), rh = (int)(d2 & 0xFFFF);
1031:        if (rw > 0 && rh > 0)
1032:          bar_reinit(rw, rh);
1033:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED) {
1034:        /* External style/theme/bg change (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h),
1035:         * surfaced through this SAME input_poll_event() loop — see nxres.h's
1036:         * header comment for why a second try_recv() loop is wrong here.
1037:         * The ping covers ALL three look axes, so a background change
1038:         * reloads the theme palette too — re-deriving the border is cheap
1039:         * and keeps a single redraw path. */
1040:        nxbar_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
1041:        g_col_xbtn_glyph = nxres_bg_color();
1042:        redraw(1);
1043:      }
1044:    }
1045:
1046:    /* Phase 3: GC stale sys.proc.<pid> identity keys (dead detached apps) on a
1047:     * slow cadence — ~every 5 s, not every 33 ms frame. */
1048:    static long g_last_prune_ms = 0;
1049:    long now_ms = get_time();
1050:    if (now_ms - g_last_prune_ms > 5000) {
1051:      g_last_prune_ms = now_ms;
1052:      nxexec_prune_identities();
1053:    }
1054:
1055:    OS1_sleep(33); /* ~30 Hz, descheduled between ticks, like nxui */
1056:  }
1057:  return 0;
1058:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxexec.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxexec.c
3: * NEXS execution service (SRL, ASTRA §6.4) — issue #193.
4: *
5: * nxexec is THE launcher-side executor: the one process that decides HOW a
6: * program is run and gives a terminal program the terminal it needs. The
7: * dock/launcher spawns `nxexec <program> [args]` DETACHED (the launcher is
8: * never anyone's controlling terminal); nxexec then:
9: *
10: * 1. opens ONE terminal window (hidden during the grace probe below);
11: * 2. spawns <program> EXACTLY ONCE as its own child, so nxexec is the
12: *    child's controlling terminal (its stdout lands in nxexec's window);
13: * 3. detects the child's KIND at runtime — using the existing window-ownership
14: *    signal (SYS_WINDOW_OF_PID), no new mechanism:
15: *    - the child opens its OWN window -> it is a graphical app; nxexec
16: *      closes (its hidden window is never shown) and the app runs alone,
17: *      managed like any other windowed app (nxwins/dock);
18: *    - the child is windowless -> it is a terminal program;
19: *      nxexec SHOWS its terminal (the output written while hidden is
20: *      already in the window buffer) so the output is visible;
21: * 4. after a windowless child EXITS, keeps its output on screen and waits
22: *    for the user to press Enter (or a 10 s timeout), THEN closes — so the
23: *    output is readable but nothing accumulates;
24: * 5. while a windowless child is still RUNNING, stays open watching it
25: *    (Ctrl-C kills it); if the user closes nxexec's window the kernel's
26: *    window-aware subtree kill takes the windowless child with it
27: *    (docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md — "child closed with parent").
28: *
29: * Capability posture (the child is the most-exercised spawn path, so it is
30: * the one to keep tight): nxexec adds NO ambient authority of its own. The
31: * child goes through the same CAP_SPAWN-gated, per-path-preset, monotonic
32: * creator-clamped kernel spawn as everything else (secure-by-caller): a
33: * child under /bin lands at PLVL_USER even though nxexec runs from /sys/bin.
34: * The spawn ABI rejects unknown flag bits (kernel, SPAWN_FLAGS_ALL).
35: */
36:#include "nxexec.h"
37:#include <execsvc.h>
38:#include <os1.h>
39:#include <string.h>
40:#include <unistd.h>
41:
42:#define NXEXEC_GRACE_MS 500     /* window-vs-windowless decision window */
43:#define NXEXEC_DISMISS_MS 10000 /* auto-close after a finished job */
44:
45:/*
46: * wait_dismiss - block until the USER presses Enter or timeout_ms elapses.
47: *
48: * Called only AFTER the child has exited, so any keyboard input now is
49: * unambiguously the user's (not a newline consumed by the running program) —
50: * this fulfills the "distinguish internal newlines from user newlines"
51: * requirement: we simply do not read the keyboard while the child runs.
52: */
53:static void wait_dismiss(int timeout_ms) {
54:  int elapsed = 0;
55:  while (elapsed < timeout_ms) {
56:    struct ipc_message m;
57:    if (try_recv(-1, &m) == 0 && m.type == IPC_TYPE_INPUT && m.data2 != 0) {
58:      char c = m.payload[0];
59:      if (c == '\r' || c == '\n')
60:        return;
61:    }
62:    OS1_sleep(50);
63:    elapsed += 50;
64:  }
65:}
66:
67:/*
68: * read_full - a pipe read may return SHORT (it is a stream, and the writer may
69: * still be filling it).  The request is a fixed-size record, so anything less
70: * than the whole record is a malformed request, not a partial success — loop
71: * until complete, or fail.
72: */
73:static int read_full(int fd, void *buf, int want) {
74:  char *p = (char *)buf;
75:  int got = 0;
76:  while (got < want) {
77:    long r = read(fd, p + got, (unsigned long)(want - got));
78:    if (r <= 0)
79:      return got; /* 0 = writer closed early; <0 = error */
80:    got += (int)r;
81:  }
82:  return got;
83:}
84:
85:/*
86: * execsvc_handle_spawn - serve ONE spawn request (ASTRA §6.4 SRL service).
87: *
88: * The rendezvous message carries only references; the body arrives out-of-line
89: * through the pipe the client delegated to us (its 1272-byte request cannot fit
90: * in a 64-byte ipc_message payload).  m->from is kernel-stamped and is our only
91: * trustworthy statement of WHO is asking — it is both the authorisation basis
92: * and the logical owner we assign to the job.
93: */
94:static void execsvc_handle_spawn(const struct ipc_message *m) {
95:  /* The channel handles arrive TRANSLATED into our own table by
96:   * SYS_PORT_SEND_CAPS, which publishes them in the leading payload slots — a
97:   * handle index is meaningless across process boundaries, so the client's own
98:   * numbers (whatever it held) are deliberately NOT used here. */
99:  int reqh = -1, reph = -1;
100:  memcpy(&reqh, m->payload + 0 * sizeof(int), sizeof(int));
101:  memcpy(&reph, m->payload + 1 * sizeof(int), sizeof(int));
102:  if (reqh < 0 || reph < 0)
103:    return; /* no usable channels: nothing to answer on */
104:
105:  struct execsvc_spawn_hdr hdr;
106:  static char body[EXECSVC_BODY_MAX]; /* static: the service is single-threaded
107:                                       * and 4 KiB does not belong on the stack */
108:  struct execsvc_spawn_rep rep;
109:  struct execsvc_redir rq[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR];
110:  int nrq = 0;
111:  memset(&rep, 0, sizeof(rep));
112:  rep.version = EXECSVC_VERSION;
113:  rep.pid = -EINVAL;
114:
115:  /* Validate the header BEFORE trusting any length it declares: body_len is a
116:   * client-chosen number, so it is bounded against EXECSVC_BODY_MAX first and
117:   * only then used to size a read. */
118:  if (read_full(reqh, (char *)&hdr, (int)sizeof(hdr)) == (int)sizeof(hdr) &&
119:      hdr.version == EXECSVC_VERSION && hdr.argc > 0 &&
120:      hdr.argc <= EXECSVC_ARG_MAX && hdr.nredir >= 0 &&
121:      hdr.nredir <= SPAWN_MAX_REDIR && hdr.body_len <= EXECSVC_BODY_MAX &&
122:      read_full(reqh, body, (int)hdr.body_len) == (int)hdr.body_len) {
123:
124:    /* Parse the packed body.  EVERY step is bounded by body_len, so a truncated
125:     * or hostile body cannot walk past the buffer. */
126:    unsigned int off = 0;
127:    int ok_parse = 1;
128:    char *av[EXECSVC_ARG_MAX];
129:
130:    unsigned int rbytes = (unsigned int)hdr.nredir * sizeof(struct execsvc_redir);
131:    if (rbytes > hdr.body_len) {
132:      ok_parse = 0;
133:    } else {
134:      memcpy(rq, body, rbytes);
135:      nrq = hdr.nredir;
136:      off = rbytes;
137:    }
138:
139:    /* cwd, then argv — each a NUL-terminated run inside the body. */
140:    const char *cwd = "";
141:    if (ok_parse) {
142:      cwd = body + off;
143:      while (off < hdr.body_len && body[off])
144:        off++;
145:      if (off >= hdr.body_len)
146:        ok_parse = 0; /* unterminated: refuse rather than read on */
147:      else
148:        off++; /* step past the NUL */
149:    }
150:    for (int i = 0; ok_parse && i < hdr.argc; i++) {
151:      if (off >= hdr.body_len) {
152:        ok_parse = 0;
153:        break;
154:      }
155:      av[i] = body + off;
156:      while (off < hdr.body_len && body[off])
157:        off++;
158:      if (off >= hdr.body_len) {
159:        ok_parse = 0; /* unterminated final argument */
160:        break;
161:      }
162:      off++;
163:    }
164:    /* cwd: adopt the REQUESTER's for the duration of this spawn.
165:     *
166:     * The child inherits cwd from its CREATOR, which is this service — so
167:     * without this every relative path in a served command resolved against
168:     * the service's "/" instead of the caller's directory.  It was parsed and
169:     * then discarded ((void)cwd), which made the hole invisible in review: the
170:     * protocol looked like it carried cwd and nothing consumed it.
171:     *
172:     * Adopt-spawn-restore is safe HERE and only here: the service loop is
173:     * single-threaded and serves one request to completion, so no second
174:     * request can observe the borrowed directory.  It is a stopgap with a
175:     * named successor — Phase 9d carries cwd, ctty and environment in the
176:     * spawn itself, as ONE mechanism, which is what removes the borrowing.
177:     *
178:     * Restoring to "/" rather than to the previous value is deliberate: "/"
179:     * is the service's own cwd at start-up and the only value it is ever
180:     * supposed to hold at rest, so a failed restore cannot strand the service
181:     * inside a client's directory. */
182:    int cwd_adopted = 0;
183:    if (ok_parse && cwd[0])
184:      cwd_adopted = (chdir(cwd) == 0);
185:
186:    /* Translate the abstract fd sources into kernel redirections (Q2 hybrid):
187:     *   GRANTED   -> the client delegated the handle to US, so it indexes our
188:     *                own table: source_pid stays 0.
189:     *   CLIENT_FD -> the handle stays in the CLIENT's table and the kernel
190:     *                takes it directly.  We pin the source to m->from — the
191:     *                KERNEL-STAMPED requester — so the service can never be
192:     *                talked into harvesting a third party's descriptors, even
193:     *                though it is privileged enough to do so. */
194:    struct spawn_redir redir[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR];
195:    int nredir = 0, bad = !ok_parse;
196:    for (int i = 0; !bad && i < nrq; i++) {
197:      redir[nredir].child_fd = rq[i].child_fd;
198:      redir[nredir].parent_fd = rq[i].ref;
199:      if (rq[i].source == EXECSVC_FD_GRANTED)
200:        redir[nredir].source_pid = 0;
201:      else if (rq[i].source == EXECSVC_FD_CLIENT_FD)
202:        redir[nredir].source_pid = m->from;
203:      else {
204:        bad = 1;
205:        break;
206:      }
207:      nredir++;
208:    }
209:
210:    if (!bad) {
211:      char path[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
212:      int pid = nxexec_spawn_search_redir(hdr.argc, av, path,
213:                                          (hdr.flags & SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED) != 0,
214:                                          redir, nredir);
215:      if (pid > 0) {
216:        /* Hand the job to the REQUESTER (Q3): we are the mechanical parent, but
217:         * the client owns it, so its kill/stop/cont authority still reaches the
218:         * job.  Without this the requesting shell would silently lose job
219:         * control over everything it launched. */
220:        char pidstr[16];
221:        snprintf(pidstr, sizeof(pidstr), "%d", pid);
222:        int ph = (int)OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, pidstr,
223:                                           OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY, OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
224:        if (ph >= 0) {
225:          OS1_object_ctl(ph, OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER, m->from);
226:          OS1low_handle_close(ph);
227:        }
228:        rep.pid = pid;
229:        rep.owner_pid = m->from;
230:        snprintf(rep.resolved, EXECSVC_PATH_MAX, "%s", path);
231:      } else {
232:        rep.pid = -ENOENT;
233:      }
234:    }
235:
236:    /* Give the borrowed directory back before answering, so the service is at
237:     * rest in a known place no matter which branch above ran. */
238:    if (cwd_adopted)
239:      chdir("/");
240:  }
241:
242:  write(reph, (const char *)&rep, sizeof(rep));
243:  /* Drop the delegated channels AND any handle the client GRANTED us for the
244:   * child: the kernel already dup'd what it needed into the child, so holding
245:   * them here would keep pipes/files open for the service's lifetime — a slow
246:   * descriptor leak in a process that never exits.  CLIENT_FD refs are NOT ours
247:   * to close: they live in the client's table. */
248:  close(reqh);
249:  close(reph);
250:  for (int i = 0; i < nrq && i < SPAWN_MAX_REDIR; i++) {
251:    if (rq[i].source == EXECSVC_FD_GRANTED)
252:      close(rq[i].ref);
253:  }
254:}
255:
256:/*
257: * nxexec_service - the R6 privileged execution daemon.
258: *
259: * Publishes the OS1nx_exec port and serves spawn requests.  Taking the RECEIVE
260: * right IS the claim on the service identity: if another nxexec already serves
261: * it, OS1_port_create fails and this instance exits instead of competing.
262: */
263:static int nxexec_service(void) {
264:  /*
265:   * Claiming the name is RETRIED, briefly, before giving up.
266:   *
267:   * The port is unpublished when its last RECEIVER handle closes, which
268:   * happens while the dead instance's handle table is being torn down — after
269:   * init has already seen the corpse and queued a respawn.  So the ordinary,
270:   * expected respawn lands in a window where the old name is still served and
271:   * OS1_port_create() returns -EEXIST.  Exiting there turned a clean restart
272:   * into a crash loop: init respawns, the new instance loses the same race,
273:   * exits, init respawns... which is what the supervisor's backoff then had to
274:   * absorb, and what presented as init endlessly restarting things.
275:   *
276:   * A bounded retry — not an unbounded one: if some OTHER process genuinely
277:   * holds the name, this instance must still exit and say so rather than spin
278:   * forever competing for a service identity it does not own.
279:   */
280:#define SERVICE_CLAIM_TRIES 20
281:#define SERVICE_CLAIM_WAIT_MS 100
282:  int port = -1;
283:  for (int attempt = 0; attempt < SERVICE_CLAIM_TRIES; attempt++) {
284:    port = OS1_port_create(OS1NX_PORT_EXEC);
285:    if (port >= 0)
286:      break;
287:    OS1_sleep(SERVICE_CLAIM_WAIT_MS);
288:  }
289:  if (port < 0) {
290:    printf("nxexec: cannot publish %s after %d attempts (already served?)\n",
291:           OS1NX_PORT_EXEC, SERVICE_CLAIM_TRIES);
292:    return 1;
293:  }
294:  printf("nxexec: execution service listening on %s\n", OS1NX_PORT_EXEC);
295:  for (;;) {
296:    struct ipc_message m;
297:    long r = OS1_port_recv(port, &m);
298:    if (r == 0)
299:      break; /* every sender closed: nothing can ever arrive again */
300:    if (r < 0)
301:      continue;
302:    if (m.type == EXECSVC_REQ_SPAWN)
303:      execsvc_handle_spawn(&m);
304:  }
305:  OS1low_handle_close(port);
306:  return 0;
307:}
308:
309:int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
310:  /* Service mode (R6 daemon).  Kept as a MODE of the same binary rather than a
311:   * separate one: the execution policy below (path resolution, argv[0]
312:   * normalisation, hosting, job control) must not fork into two divergent
313:   * copies — that divergence is the very bug this daemon exists to remove. */
314:  if (argc >= 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "--service") == 0)
315:    return nxexec_service();
316:
317:  if (argc < 2)
318:    return 1; /* nothing to run */
319:
320:  int jargc = argc - 1; /* drop our own argv[0] */
321:  char **jargv = &argv[1];
322:
323:  /*
324:   * Normalize executable name before using it for window titles,
325:   * diagnostics, and spawn resolution.
326:   *
327:   * This prevents shell-style quoted paths such as:
328:   *   "\"/bin/lua\""
329:   *
330:   * from appearing as literal filenames or UI strings.
331:   */
332:  char clean_exec[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
333:
334:  jargv[0] = (char *)nxexec_strip_path_quotes(jargv[0], clean_exec,
335:                                              sizeof(clean_exec));
336:
337:  /* Phase 3: the canonical display name is the exe basename ("/bin/lua" ->
338:   * "lua"); title the hosted window with it and publish it in the registry
339:   * (below) so the bar serialises this launch by pid. */
340:  const char *dispname = nxexec_basename(jargv[0]);
341:
342:  int win = create_window(140, 120, 560, 360, dispname);
343:  if (win < 0)
344:    return 1;
345:
346:  /* Hidden during the grace probe: a graphical child never flashes an empty
347:   * terminal. Flag bits (compositor_set_window_flags): 4 = hide, 2 = show. */
348:  set_window_flags(win, 4);
349:
350:  /*
351:   * Apply `<` `>` `>>` `2>` on the HOSTED path too (Phase 9 step 2).
352:   *
353:   * Until now redirection existed only in the shell, so the two launch paths
354:   * were not merely separate implementations — they had different CAPABILITIES:
355:   * a terminal user could redirect, a graphical caller could not.  nxlauncher
356:   * and nxfilem already route through this binary, so parsing here is what
357:   * finally lets a GUI caller pass a full command line (the nxpopup argument
358:   * entry) and get the same behaviour the terminal has always had.
359:   *
360:   * Errors are reported into this window, which must therefore be REVEALED
361:   * first: it was hidden for the grace probe, and a failure message written to
362:   * a hidden window would be invisible — the launch would look like it silently
363:   * did nothing.
364:   */
365:  struct spawn_redir redir[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR];
366:  int rfds[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR], nredir = 0, nrfds = 0;
367:  if (nxexec_strip_redirections(&jargc, jargv, redir, &nredir, rfds, &nrfds) !=
368:          0 ||
369:      jargc == 0) {
370:    set_window_flags(win, 2);
371:    set_focus(get_pid());
372:    if (jargc == 0)
373:      printf("nxexec: no command to run\r\n");
374:    wait_dismiss(NXEXEC_DISMISS_MS);
375:    for (int i = 0; i < nrfds; i++)
376:      close(rfds[i]);
377:    return 1;
378:  }
379:
380:  char path[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
381:  int pid = nxexec_spawn_search_redir(jargc, jargv, path, /*detached=*/0, redir,
382:                                      nredir);
383:  /* The child holds its own dups; drop ours so the files close when both sides
384:   * are done, instead of staying open for this terminal's whole lifetime. */
385:  for (int i = 0; i < nrfds; i++)
386:    close(rfds[i]);
387:
388:  if (pid <= 0) {
389:    set_window_flags(win, 2);
390:    set_focus(get_pid());
391:    printf("nxexec: unable to execute '%s'\r\n", jargv[0]);
392:    wait_dismiss(NXEXEC_DISMISS_MS);
393:    return 1;
394:  }
395:
396:  /* Publish the launch identity now that we have a live pid.  A GUI app that
397:   * detaches (returns below) keeps it — it is still running and the bar shows
398:   * it; a stale key for a later-dead pid is harmless (that pid has no window). */
399:  nxexec_register_identity(pid, dispname);
400:
401:  /* Grace probe, DEBOUNCED (docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md §5): a GUI app settles
402:   * on a PERSISTENT window (same id for NXEXEC_STABLE_POLLS polls) -> vanish;
403:   * a fast CLI exits -> host + dismiss; a terminal program that only churns
404:   * transient windows (stress --gui) never accumulates a stable count and
405:   * falls through to being hosted, so its output stays visible in the
406:   * terminal instead of nxexec wrongly detaching and dropping it. */
407:  int job_done = 0, last_win = -1, stable = 0;
408:  for (int i = 0; (i * 15) < NXEXEC_GRACE_MS; i++) {
409:    if (nxexec_window_stable(pid, &last_win, &stable))
410:      return 0; /* persistent own window -> GUI app, vanish */
411:
412:    if (wait(pid) != -1) {
413:      job_done = 1; /* fast CLI finished within the probe */
414:      break;
415:    }
416:    OS1_sleep(15);
417:  }
418:
419:  /* Windowless: reveal the terminal (its output is already in the buffer). */
420:  set_window_flags(win, 2);
421:  set_focus(get_pid());
422:
423:  if (!job_done) {
424:    /* Long-running windowless job: watch it (Ctrl-C kills; if the user closes
425:     * this window the kernel subtree-kill takes the child). The debounced
426:     * watch returns DETACHED only for a stable own window (a slow-to-open GUI
427:     * app), not for stress's transient churn.
428:     *
429:     * Ctrl-Z suspends the job (detected, not swallowed): a standalone terminal
430:     * has no shell to adopt a stopped job, so instead of orphaning it or
431:     * self-closing, keep this window open and offer resume (Enter) / kill
432:     * (Ctrl-C).  Only Ctrl-C or the program exiting closes a hosted terminal. */
433:    int r;
434:    while ((r = nxexec_run_foreground(pid)) == NXEXEC_JOB_STOPPED) {
435:      printf("\r\n\033[90m[suspended — Enter to resume, Ctrl-C to close]"
436:             "\033[0m\r\n");
437:      if (!nxexec_wait_stopped_action(pid)) {
438:        job_done = 1; /* Ctrl-C: child killed -> fall through and close */
439:        break;
440:      }
441:      OS1_process_cont(pid); /* Enter: resume and keep watching */
442:    }
443:    if (r == NXEXEC_JOB_DETACHED)
444:      return 0; /* it settled on its own window -> vanish */
445:  }
446:
447:  /* The hosted job has terminated (windowless job exited/Ctrl-C'd) — drop its
448:   * registry identity; a detached GUI app took the early return above and kept
449:   * its identity. */
450:  nxexec_unregister_identity(pid);
451:
452:  /* Job finished: leave the output on screen, let the user read it, close on
453:   * Enter or after the timeout. No interactive prompt, no accumulation. */
454:  printf("\r\n\033[90m[process terminated — press Enter to close]\033[0m");
455:  wait_dismiss(NXEXEC_DISMISS_MS);
456:  return 0;
457:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxexec.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXEXEC_H
2:#define _USER_NXEXEC_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxexec.h
6: * NEXS stratified process-LAUNCH helper (ASTRA service layer) — issue #193.
7: *
8: * THE single place that encodes HOW a process is launched, separated out of
9: * nxshell/nxlauncher (which used to each hand-roll a divergent copy).  Two
10: * launch modes, matching the maintainer's standalone-vs-needs-shell model:
11: *
12: *   FOREGROUND (needs-shell, terminal-attached) — nxexec_run_foreground():
13: *     the spawner IS the child's controlling terminal (default ctty
14: *     inheritance).  Runtime window detection decides the outcome: the child
15: *     opens its OWN window -> it detaches (graphical app, lives
16: *     independently, managed via nxwins/dock); it stays windowless -> it runs
17: *     as a shell job (stdout in the spawner's window, Ctrl-C kills it, the
18: *     spawner blocks until it exits).
19: *
20: *   DETACHED (standalone, launcher-style) — nxexec_spawn_detached():
21: *     the child does NOT inherit the spawner as ctty (SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED,
22: *     kernel-enforced).  A windowed child behaves identically (own-window
23: *     stdout).  A windowless child fails CLOSED (no output surface) instead
24: *     of silently writing into the launcher's soon-minimized window as if the
25: *     launcher were a shell — the #193 bug.
26: *
27: * Lifecycle note: windowless children die with their parent (the kill model
28: * is already window-aware, process_kill_subtree spares windowed subtrees —
29: * docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md), which completes the maintainer's policy:
30: * "crea una finestra? gestione window; altrimenti figlio, chiuso col padre".
31: *
32: * SECURITY MODEL: no ambient checks of its own (the nxproc.h pattern) —
33: * spawn is CAP_SPAWN-gated kernel-side per caller; the helper neither widens
34: * nor narrows that.
35: *
36: * Consumers: nxshell.c (foreground path), nxlauncher.c (detached path).
37: */
38:
39:/* execsvc.h is the client-facing WIRE CONTRACT (structs + version only); this
40: * header is the executor's POLICY IMPLEMENTATION.  They stay separate so a
41: * client that merely asks for an execution links the protocol alone, instead of
42: * dragging in window probing, identity registration and the foreground watch
43: * loop below (Phase 12: "i servizi vanno divisi dalla libc e integrati in
44: * maniera modulare").  Included here so nxexec.c and the existing consumers get
45: * it transitively — one definition, no duplication. */
46:#include <execsvc.h>
47:#include <fcntl.h> /* O_* + open() — redirection parsing below */
48:#include <os1.h>
49:#include <stdlib.h> /* getenv() — see the dynamic HOME resolution in
50:                      * nxexec_resolve_path()'s tier 2 below. */
51:#include <string.h>
52:#include <unistd.h> /* close() */
53:
54:#define NXEXEC_PATH_MAX 96
55:#define NXEXEC_ARGV_MAX                                                        \
56:  16 /* matches OS1low_process_spawn_detached's argv cap                       \
57:      * (kernel-enforced); nxexec itself takes argc-1                          \
58:      * of these and forwards them to the child. */
59:
60:/* A child is treated as "windowed" (a GUI app that should detach) only if it
61: * owns the SAME window id across this many consecutive polls.  A transient
62: * create/destroy churn — stress's --gui lane opens back-to-back windows with
63: * DIFFERENT ids (docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md §5) — never accumulates a stable
64: * count, so it is correctly hosted as a terminal program instead of being
65: * mistaken for a persistent GUI app and wrongly detached.  ~6 polls x ~15ms
66: * = ~90ms of an unchanging window; a real app holds its window far longer,
67: * a churner never holds one id that long. */
68:#define NXEXEC_STABLE_POLLS 6
69:
70:/*
71: * nxexec_window_stable - one step of the "has this pid settled on its own
72: * persistent window?" debounce, factored out because the exact same state
73: * machine used to be hand-copied in three places (nxexec_run_foreground()
74: * below, nxexec.c main()'s grace probe, and nxjobs.h's nxjobs_poll() for
75: * background jobs) — three chances for the threshold or the reset rule to
76: * quietly drift apart between callers that all need to agree on what
77: * "windowed" means.
78: *
79: * Caller owns the debounce state (*last_win, *stable) across calls — one
80: * call per poll tick, whatever that caller's tick source is (a blocking
81: * OS1_sleep loop, a probe loop, or an outer shell tick). Returns 1 once
82: * window_of_pid(pid) has reported the SAME positive window id for
83: * NXEXEC_STABLE_POLLS consecutive calls (a persistent own window -> GUI
84: * app), 0 otherwise. A transient/changing window id (create/destroy churn,
85: * see the NXEXEC_STABLE_POLLS comment above) resets the run instead of
86: * accumulating, so it never falsely reaches the threshold.
87: */
88:static inline int nxexec_window_stable(int pid, int *last_win, int *stable) {
89:  int w = window_of_pid(pid);
90:  if (w > 0 && w == *last_win)
91:    (*stable)++;
92:  else
93:    *stable = (w > 0) ? 1 : 0;
94:  *last_win = w;
95:  return *stable >= NXEXEC_STABLE_POLLS;
96:}
97:
98:/* nxexec_run_foreground return codes. */
99:#define NXEXEC_JOB_EXITED 0 /* the child finished (or was Ctrl-C'd) */
100:#define NXEXEC_JOB_DETACHED                                                    \
101:  1 /* the child owns a stable window -> it is a GUI app */
102:#define NXEXEC_JOB_STOPPED 2 /* Ctrl-Z: the child was suspended (PROC_STOPPED);
103:                              * the caller should register it as a stopped job */
104:
105:/*
106: * NXEXEC path-resolution tiers, aligned with POSIX/execvp (previously
107: * duplicated ad hoc across system(), nxassoc, and nxlauncher, each with
108: * its own resolution logic):
109: *
110: *   1. ABSOLUTE ROOT PATH   "/foo/bar" -> used exactly as provided.
111: *   2. HOME-RELATIVE PATH   "~" / "~/x" -> "~" is expanded to "/home"
112: *                                         (single-user system, no getpwuid()).
113: *   3. PROCESS-VFS-RELATIVE PATH   any other path containing a '/'
114: *      (e.g. "./x", "sub/dir/x") -> resolved against the CALLING PROCESS'
115: *      current working directory (getcwd()) — the cwd is maintained
116: *      per process, never as a global prefix.
117: *   4. BARE NAME (no '/') -> searched, in order, in /bin and then /sys/bin
118: *      (existing behavior, unchanged).
119: *
120: * This exactly matches the execvp() rule: a name containing a slash is
121: * treated as a path (resolved, never searched); a bare name is searched.
122: */
123:#define NXEXEC_HOME_DIR "/home"
124:
125:/*
126: * Remove surrounding quotes from an executable path.
127: *
128: * Shell-like callers may provide quoted executable paths
129: * (for example "\"/bin/lua\"" or "'/bin/lua'").
130: * Path resolution must operate on the real path and ignore
131: * only matching outer quotes.
132: *
133: * Internal quotes are preserved.
134: */
135:static inline const char *nxexec_strip_path_quotes(const char *name, char *out,
136:                                                   size_t sz) {
137:  if (!name || !out || sz == 0)
138:    return name;
139:
140:  size_t len = strlen(name);
141:
142:  if (len >= 2 && ((name[0] == '"' && name[len - 1] == '"') ||
143:                   (name[0] == '\'' && name[len - 1] == '\''))) {
144:
145:    len -= 2;
146:
147:    if (len >= sz)
148:      len = sz - 1;
149:
150:    memcpy(out, name + 1, len);
151:    out[len] = '\0';
152:
153:    return out;
154:  }
155:
156:  return name;
157:}
158:
159:/*
160: * Phase 3 — process identity (PLAN-2026-07-17): nxexec is the launch authority,
161: * so it assigns the ONE canonical display name for a program (the exe's
162: * basename, quotes already stripped: "/bin/lua" -> "lua") and publishes it two
163: * ways, per the maintainer's "window-title convention + registry namespace"
164: * decision:
165: *   - it titles the window it hosts with that name (the bar reads titles);
166: *   - it no longer registers any identity key: sys.proc.<pid>.* is computed by
167: *     the kernel (Phase 5b) and the icon follows from the program name (17a)
168: *     can serialise ANY pid's identity by number, independent of an app's own
169: *     (possibly colliding or changing) window title.
170: * The icon key is the same canonical name; nxicon classifies it.
171: */
172:static inline const char *nxexec_basename(const char *path) {
173:  if (!path)
174:    return "";
175:  const char *b = path;
176:  for (const char *p = path; *p; p++)
177:    if (*p == '/')
178:      b = p + 1;
179:  return b;
180:}
181:
182:static inline void nxexec_register_identity(int pid, const char *name) {
183:  /* NOTHING to publish (Phase 5b, corrected in 17a).
184:   *
185:   * `sys.proc.<pid>.name` is VIRTUAL — the kernel computes it from the process
186:   * table on every read — so writing it here would recreate exactly the second,
187:   * best-effort copy whose staleness needed a garbage collector.
188:   *
189:   * The ICON does not need a key either.  5b published `sys.appicon.<name>`
190:   * mapping a name to ITSELF: zero information.  Worse, it keyed on the
191:   * BASENAME while the only reader (nxui) builds the key from the kernel's FULL
192:   * path, so it could never even hit.  `nxicon_classify` already strips the
193:   * path and classifies the program name directly, which is the whole job. */
194:  (void)pid;
195:  (void)name;
196:}
197:
198:static inline void nxexec_unregister_identity(int pid) {
199:  /* Nothing to unregister: the per-process view is virtual, so a dead pid has
200:   * no keys by construction.  Kept as a no-op so callers read naturally. */
201:  (void)pid;
202:}
203:
204:/* nxexec_prune_identities - REMOVED in Phase 5b.  It existed to sweep
205: * `sys.proc.<pid>` keys that outlived their processes; virtualising that view
206: * deleted the staleness class, so the collector has nothing left to collect.
207: * Retained as a no-op only so existing callers keep compiling until they are
208: * updated. */
209:static inline void nxexec_prune_identities(void) {}
210:
211:static inline int nxexec_resolve_path(const char *name, char *out_path,
212:                                      size_t sz) {
213:  if (!name || !*name || !out_path || sz == 0)
214:    return -1;
215:
216:  char clean_name[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
217:
218:  name = nxexec_strip_path_quotes(name, clean_name, sizeof(clean_name));
219:
220:  if (name[0] == '/') { /* 1: root-assoluto */
221:    snprintf(out_path, sz, "%s", name);
222:    return 0;
223:  }
224:
225:  if (name[0] == '~') { /* 2: home-relativo */
226:    /* Dynamic: ask getenv("HOME") first (lib.c currently stubs it to
227:     * NXEXEC_HOME_DIR itself, but that's an implementation detail of the
228:     * stub, not a contract) and fall back to NXEXEC_HOME_DIR only if HOME
229:     * is unset/empty — a real per-user HOME later becomes a getenv() change
230:     * alone, no nxexec.h edit, no rebuild of every consumer (nxshell.c,
231:     * nxlauncher.c, and whatever "standard for non-system programs" launch
232:     * path follows this pattern next). */
233:    const char *home = getenv("HOME");
234:    if (!home || !*home)
235:      home = NXEXEC_HOME_DIR;
236:    if (name[1] == '\0')
237:      snprintf(out_path, sz, "%s", home);
238:    else if (name[1] == '/')
239:      snprintf(out_path, sz, "%s%s", home, name + 1);
240:    else
241:      return -1; /* forma "~utente": non supportata, non c'è una pwdb
242:                    multi-utente */
243:    return 0;
244:  }
245:
246:  if (strchr(name, '/')) { /* 3: process-vfs-relativo */
247:    char cwd[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
248:    if (getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd)) != 0)
249:      snprintf(cwd, sizeof(cwd), "/"); /* fallback best-effort */
250:    size_t cl = strlen(cwd);
251:    if (cl > 0 && cwd[cl - 1] == '/')
252:      snprintf(out_path, sz, "%s%s", cwd, name);
253:    else
254:      snprintf(out_path, sz, "%s/%s", cwd, name);
255:    return 0;
256:  }
257:
258:  return 1; /* 4: nome nudo -> il chiamante fa la ricerca /bin, /sys/bin */
259:}
260:
261:/*
262: * nxexec_run_foreground - watch a freshly-spawned child as a foreground job
263: * (USR-TTY-01 #123), with a DEBOUNCED window-ownership test so a transient
264: * window (stress --gui) is not mistaken for "this is a GUI app, detach".
265: *
266: * Returns NXEXEC_JOB_DETACHED if the child settled on its own persistent
267: * window (the caller should stop hosting it), or NXEXEC_JOB_EXITED if the
268: * child finished or was killed by Ctrl-C (ETX via keyboard IPC).
269: */
270:static inline int nxexec_run_foreground_ex(int pid, int *out_status) {
271:  if (pid <= 0)
272:    return NXEXEC_JOB_EXITED;
273:  int last_win = -1;
274:  int stable = 0;
275:  while (1) {
276:    if (nxexec_window_stable(pid, &last_win, &stable))
277:      return NXEXEC_JOB_DETACHED; /* a persistent own window -> GUI app */
278:
279:    /* Reap WITH the exit status (Phase 2 exit_code channel).  *out_status gets
280:     * the shell-style status: the exit code for a normal exit, 128+signal for a
281:     * killed child — this is what lets `nxshell -c` exit with the command's
282:     * status, which system()/os.execute() test. */
283:    int code = 0;
284:    if (OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code) != -1) {
285:      if (out_status)
286:        *out_status = (code >= 0) ? (code & 0xff) : (128 + (-code));
287:      return NXEXEC_JOB_EXITED; /* child finished (dead/zombie/gone) */
288:    }
289:
290:    /* Relay keyboard input to the child (USR-TTY-01 #123 problem 2): a
291:     * windowless child can never hold compositor focus (focus is per-window),
292:     * so it never sees its own keystrokes unless we forward them here -
293:     * without this, any program that reads stdin interactively (a REPL, an
294:     * editor, ...) blocks forever on its first read() after printing a
295:     * prompt, indistinguishable from a hang. Ctrl-C stays a local kill
296:     * instead of being forwarded, matching the existing job-control model.
297:     *
298:     * No termios/cooked-mode layer exists anywhere in this OS - every
299:     * reader echoes its OWN input explicitly (nxshell.c's read(0,...) loop
300:     * is the reference). We still hold the window/focus while hosting, so
301:     * echo has to happen here too, in the same style, or the cursor never
302:     * advances even though the child is receiving every keystroke. */
303:    struct ipc_message m;
304:    if (try_recv(-1, &m) == 0 && m.type == IPC_TYPE_INPUT && m.data2 != 0) {
305:      char c = m.payload[0];
306:      if (c == 0x03) {
307:        kill_process(pid);
308:        print("^C\n");
309:        if (out_status)
310:          *out_status = 130; /* 128 + SIGINT, the shell convention */
311:        return NXEXEC_JOB_EXITED;
312:      }
313:      if (c == 0x1a) { /* Ctrl-Z: suspend the foreground job and hand back to
314:                        * the caller (NXEXEC_JOB_STOPPED). nxshell adopts it as
315:                        * a job; nxexec.c keeps its terminal open with a
316:                        * resume/kill prompt (never orphaning it). */
317:        if (OS1_process_stop(pid) == 0) {
318:          print("^Z\n");
319:          return NXEXEC_JOB_STOPPED;
320:        }
321:        /* stop refused (e.g. windowed/own-terminal child): relay as a key */
322:      }
323:      send(pid, &m);
324:      if (c == '\n' || c == '\r')
325:        print("\r\n");
326:      else if (c == '\b' || c == 127)
327:        print("\b \b");
328:      else if (c >= 32 && c < 127)
329:        print(m.payload);
330:    }
331:    OS1_sleep(15); /* time base for the debounce; keeps Ctrl-C responsive */
332:  }
333:}
334:
335:/* nxexec_run_foreground - status-less form, for callers that only need the
336: * NXEXEC_JOB_* outcome (nxexec.c's hosted terminal). */
337:static inline int nxexec_run_foreground(int pid) {
338:  return nxexec_run_foreground_ex(pid, 0);
339:}
340:
341:/*
342: * nxexec_wait_stopped_action - the hosted job was Ctrl-Z-suspended
343: * (NXEXEC_JOB_STOPPED).  A standalone terminal has no shell to hand a stopped
344: * job to, so instead of orphaning the process or closing the window it keeps
345: * the window open and blocks here until the user chooses: Enter -> resume
346: * (return 1), Ctrl-C -> kill the child (return 0).  Only these two, or the
347: * program exiting, ever close a hosted terminal.
348: */
349:static inline int nxexec_wait_stopped_action(int pid) {
350:  while (1) {
351:    struct ipc_message m;
352:    if (try_recv(-1, &m) == 0 && m.type == IPC_TYPE_INPUT && m.data2 != 0) {
353:      char c = m.payload[0];
354:      if (c == '\r' || c == '\n')
355:        return 1; /* resume */
356:      if (c == 0x03) {
357:        kill_process(pid);
358:        print("^C\n");
359:        return 0; /* killed */
360:      }
361:    }
362:    OS1_sleep(15);
363:  }
364:}
365:
366:/*
367: * nxexec_spawn_search - resolve a bare program name against /bin then
368: * /sys/bin (absolute paths bypass the search) and spawn it with argv.
369: * out_path (NXEXEC_PATH_MAX bytes) receives the resolved path for the
370: * caller's diagnostics.  Returns the PID or <= 0 on failure.
371: * detached != 0 selects the DETACHED launch mode (see header comment).
372: */
373:static inline int nxexec_spawn_search(int argc, char *argv[], char *out_path,
374:                                      int detached) {
375:  long (*do_spawn)(const char *, int, char *const[]) =
376:      detached ? OS1low_process_spawn_detached : OS1low_process_spawn;
377:
378:  /* Dequote ONCE, up front, and write the cleaned name back into argv[0] so
379:   * it is used consistently for BOTH resolution and the bare-name /bin,
380:   * /sys/bin search — and so the child sees a clean argv[0] (its progname).
381:   * The previous code stripped quotes only inside nxexec_resolve_path()'s
382:   * local buffer, then fell through to the bare-name branch still holding the
383:   * quoted original, producing the "/bin/\"lua\"" not-found seen from
384:   * os.execute('"lua" ...'). */
385:  static char clean_name[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
386:  argv[0] =
387:      (char *)nxexec_strip_path_quotes(argv[0], clean_name, sizeof(clean_name));
388:  const char *name = argv[0];
389:
390:  /* argv[0] = the RESOLVED path (Phase 9) — see nxexec_spawn_search_redir. */
391:  int r = nxexec_resolve_path(name, out_path, NXEXEC_PATH_MAX);
392:  if (r == 0) {
393:    argv[0] = out_path;
394:    return (int)do_spawn(out_path, argc, argv);
395:  }
396:  if (r < 0)
397:    return -1; /* path malformato (es. "~utente") */
398:
399:  /* Nome nudo: ricerca /bin poi /sys/bin (ora sul nome ripulito). */
400:  snprintf(out_path, NXEXEC_PATH_MAX, "/bin/%s", name);
401:  argv[0] = out_path;
402:  int pid = (int)do_spawn(out_path, argc, argv);
403:  if (pid > 0)
404:    return pid;
405:  snprintf(out_path, NXEXEC_PATH_MAX, "/sys/bin/%s", name);
406:  argv[0] = out_path;
407:  return (int)do_spawn(out_path, argc, argv);
408:}
409:
410:/*
411: * nxexec_lookup_identity - read back the canonical display name nxexec
412: * published for a pid (sys.proc.<pid>.name, Phase 3 identity).  The consumer
413: * side of nxexec_register_identity, shared so the bar, the dock and the shell's
414: * job table all name a process the SAME way instead of re-deriving it.
415: * Returns 1 and fills out[] on success, 0 if the pid has no registered
416: * identity (e.g. a system service that never went through nxexec).
417: */
418:static inline int nxexec_lookup_identity(int pid, char *out, int outsz) {
419:  char key[48];
420:  snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "sys.proc.%d.name", pid);
421:  if (OS1_registry_get(key, out, (size_t)outsz) != 0 || !out[0])
422:    return 0;
423:  return 1;
424:}
425:
426:/*
427: * nxexec_strip_redirections - pull shell redirection operators (`<` `>` `>>`
428: * `2>`) and their targets out of argv, open the targets, and build the
429: * spawn_redir list the kernel dups into the child.  Both the spaced form
430: * (`> out`) and the attached form (`>out`) are recognised.
431: *
432: * THIS IS EXECUTOR POLICY, NOT SHELL POLICY (maintainer, 2026-07-18: "nxexec
433: * deve essere il modo principale e gestire tutto ciò che sta gestendo la
434: * shell").  It lived in nxshell.c, which is why the GRAPHICAL launch path —
435: * nxlauncher/nxfilem, which already spawn through nxexec correctly — could not
436: * redirect or take arguments the way the terminal could.  Moving it here gives
437: * every caller ONE parser: the shell, the hosted terminal, and the service.
438: *
439: * On return argv (and *pargc) hold ONLY the command and its real arguments;
440: * redir[] (and *nredir) describe the child fd remap; fds[] (and *nfds) are the
441: * handles THIS process opened — the caller MUST close them after the spawn (the
442: * child holds its own dups).  Returns 0, or -1 after reporting an open/syntax
443: * error (having closed anything already opened).  A missing input file (`<`) is
444: * fatal; an output target is created (O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) / appended (`>>`).
445: */
446:static inline int nxexec_strip_redirections(int *pargc, char *argv[],
447:                                            struct spawn_redir *redir,
448:                                            int *nredir, int fds[], int *nfds) {
449:  int argc = *pargc, out = 0;
450:  *nredir = 0;
451:  *nfds = 0;
452:  for (int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
453:    char *t = argv[i];
454:    int child_fd, oflags;
455:    const char *fname = 0;
456:    if (strcmp(t, "<") == 0) {
457:      child_fd = 0, oflags = O_RDONLY;
458:    } else if (strcmp(t, ">") == 0) {
459:      child_fd = 1, oflags = O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC;
460:    } else if (strcmp(t, ">>") == 0) {
461:      child_fd = 1, oflags = O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND;
462:    } else if (strcmp(t, "2>") == 0) {
463:      child_fd = 2, oflags = O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC;
464:    } else if (t[0] == '<' && t[1]) {
465:      child_fd = 0, oflags = O_RDONLY, fname = t + 1;
466:    } else if (t[0] == '2' && t[1] == '>' && t[2]) {
467:      child_fd = 2, oflags = O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, fname = t + 2;
468:    } else if (t[0] == '>' && t[1] == '>' && t[2]) {
469:      child_fd = 1, oflags = O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND, fname = t + 2;
470:    } else if (t[0] == '>' && t[1]) {
471:      child_fd = 1, oflags = O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, fname = t + 1;
472:    } else {
473:      argv[out++] = t; /* an ordinary command argument */
474:      continue;
475:    }
476:    if (!fname) { /* bare operator token: the filename is the next token */
477:      if (i + 1 >= argc) {
478:        printf("nxexec: syntax error near '%s'\n", t);
479:        goto fail;
480:      }
481:      fname = argv[++i];
482:    }
483:    if (*nredir >= SPAWN_MAX_REDIR) {
484:      print("nxexec: too many redirections\n");
485:      goto fail;
486:    }
487:    int fd = open(fname, oflags, 0644);
488:    if (fd < 0) {
489:      printf("nxexec: cannot open %s\n", fname);
490:      goto fail;
491:    }
492:    fds[(*nfds)++] = fd;
493:    redir[*nredir].child_fd = child_fd;
494:    redir[*nredir].parent_fd = fd;
495:    redir[*nredir].source_pid = 0; /* our own table (non-zero selects the
496:                                    * privileged take-from-another-process
497:                                    * path — never leave it uninitialised) */
498:    (*nredir)++;
499:  }
500:  argv[out] = 0;
501:  *pargc = out;
502:  return 0;
503:fail:
504:  for (int j = 0; j < *nfds; j++)
505:    close(fds[j]);
506:  *nfds = 0;
507:  *nredir = 0;
508:  return -1;
509:}
510:
511:/*
512: * nxexec_spawn_search_redir - nxexec_spawn_search + fd redirection (Phase 4
513: * shell `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`).  redir[]/nredir describe the child fd remap; the
514: * CALLER opened each redir[].parent_fd and CLOSES them after this returns (the
515: * kernel dup'd them into the child).  nredir == 0 behaves exactly like
516: * nxexec_spawn_search.  Returns the PID or <= 0 on failure.
517: */
518:static inline int nxexec_spawn_search_redir(int argc, char *argv[],
519:                                            char *out_path, int detached,
520:                                            const struct spawn_redir *redir,
521:                                            int nredir) {
522:  unsigned int flags = detached ? SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED : 0u;
523:  static char clean_name[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
524:  argv[0] =
525:      (char *)nxexec_strip_path_quotes(argv[0], clean_name, sizeof(clean_name));
526:  const char *name = argv[0];
527:
528:  /* The child's argv[0] is the RESOLVED path, not the bare name as typed
529:   * (Phase 9, "esecuzione da path non diretto"): a program that re-executes
530:   * itself from its own argv[0] — lua's test suite rebuilds every command as
531:   * `"<progname>" ...` — must get a DIRECT path, or the re-execution depends on
532:   * the search succeeding again.  It also makes the terminal path agree with
533:   * the launcher path, which already passes an absolute path (progname was
534:   * `/bin/lua` from the launcher but bare `lua` from the shell). */
535:  int r = nxexec_resolve_path(name, out_path, NXEXEC_PATH_MAX);
536:  if (r == 0) {
537:    argv[0] = out_path;
538:    return (int)OS1low_process_spawn_redir(out_path, argc, argv, flags, redir,
539:                                           nredir);
540:  }
541:  if (r < 0)
542:    return -1; /* malformed path (e.g. "~user") */
543:
544:  /* Bare name: search /bin then /sys/bin.  A failed candidate aborts its own
545:   * half-built child (kernel process_abort_spawn) and drops the dup'd handle
546:   * refs, so retrying the next path with the same redir list is safe. */
547:  snprintf(out_path, NXEXEC_PATH_MAX, "/bin/%s", name);
548:  argv[0] = out_path;
549:  int pid = (int)OS1low_process_spawn_redir(out_path, argc, argv, flags, redir,
550:                                            nredir);
551:  if (pid > 0)
552:    return pid;
553:  snprintf(out_path, NXEXEC_PATH_MAX, "/sys/bin/%s", name);
554:  argv[0] = out_path;
555:  return (int)OS1low_process_spawn_redir(out_path, argc, argv, flags, redir,
556:                                         nredir);
557:}
558:
559:/*
560: * nxexec_spawn_pipe_consumer - create a pipe and spawn `argv` reading from it,
561: * handing the WRITE end back to the caller.
562: *
563: * This is the pipeline's EXECUTOR half: making the channel, wiring the
564: * consumer's fd 0 to it, and honouring the consumer's own `>`/`2>`.  What
565: * PRODUCES the data stays with the caller, because that genuinely differs — a
566: * shell may feed a builtin's output straight in, while a graphical caller
567: * spawns a producer process.  Splitting it here is what stops the pipe wiring
568: * from living only inside nxshell, the way redirection used to.
569: *
570: * Returns the consumer pid (<=0 on failure) and stores the write end in
571: * *out_write_fd (-1 if none).  The caller closes the write end to signal EOF,
572: * and closes it in ANY case — a forgotten write end means the consumer waits
573: * for data that can never arrive.
574: */
575:static inline int nxexec_spawn_pipe_consumer(int argc, char *argv[],
576:                                             char *out_path, int *out_write_fd) {
577:  int pfd[2] = {-1, -1};
578:  *out_write_fd = -1;
579:  if (pipe(pfd) != 0)
580:    return -1;
581:
582:  struct spawn_redir redir[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR];
583:  int fds[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR], nredir = 0, nfds = 0;
584:  if (nxexec_strip_redirections(&argc, argv, redir, &nredir, fds, &nfds) != 0 ||
585:      argc == 0) {
586:    for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++)
587:      close(fds[i]);
588:    close(pfd[0]);
589:    close(pfd[1]);
590:    return -1;
591:  }
592:  /* stdin from the pipe, appended AFTER the command's own redirections so an
593:   * explicit `< file` on the same stage stays visible to the kernel. */
594:  if (nredir < SPAWN_MAX_REDIR) {
595:    redir[nredir].child_fd = 0;
596:    redir[nredir].parent_fd = pfd[0];
597:    redir[nredir].source_pid = 0;
598:    nredir++;
599:  }
600:  int pid =
601:      nxexec_spawn_search_redir(argc, argv, out_path, /*detached=*/0, redir,
602:                                nredir);
603:  for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++)
604:    close(fds[i]);
605:  close(pfd[0]); /* the consumer holds its own dup */
606:  if (pid <= 0) {
607:    close(pfd[1]);
608:    return pid;
609:  }
610:  *out_write_fd = pfd[1];
611:  return pid;
612:}
613:
614:/* nxexec_spawn_detached - launcher-style spawn of an explicit path: the child
615: * never inherits the spawner as ctty (kernel-enforced, SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED). */
616:static inline int nxexec_spawn_detached(const char *path, int argc,
617:                                        char *const argv[]) {
618:  return (int)OS1low_process_spawn_detached(path, argc, argv);
619:}
620:
621:/*
622: * nxexec_spawn_hosted - run PATH under the execution service /sys/bin/nxexec
623: * (the launcher path for anything that might be a terminal program).  nxexec
624: * is spawned DETACHED (the launcher never becomes anyone's ctty); nxexec then
625: * opens a terminal window, spawns PATH as its own child (becoming its ctty),
626: * and decides at runtime:
627: *   - PATH opens its own window   -> nxexec closes, PATH runs independently;
628: *   - PATH is windowless          -> nxexec's terminal shows PATH's output,
629: *     stays readable, and closes on the user's Enter (or a timeout);
630: * closing nxexec's window kills the child (kernel subtree kill).  The job is
631: * spawned exactly once, by nxexec — no double execution.
632: */
633:static inline int nxexec_spawn_hosted(const char *path) {
634:  char *argv[2];
635:  argv[0] = (char *)"/sys/bin/nxexec";
636:  argv[1] = (char *)path;
637:  return (int)OS1low_process_spawn_detached("/sys/bin/nxexec", 2, argv);
638:}
639:
640:/* nxexec_spawn_hosted_argv - same as nxexec_spawn_hosted(), but with an
641: * explicit argv forwarded to /sys/bin/nxexec (which itself forwards the
642: * whole argv to the child, see nxexec.c main()).  Used by callers that need
643: * to pass extra arguments to the launched program (nxfilem: "kilo <path>",
644: * "<assoc-prog> <path>").  argc must be in [1, NXEXEC_ARGV_MAX-1] (the -1
645: * accounts for the prepended "/sys/bin/nxexec" entry; SPAWN_MAX_ARGS=16
646: * is the kernel-side cap the dispatcher clamps to).
647: */
648:static inline int nxexec_spawn_hosted_argv(int argc, char *argv[]) {
649:  if (argc < 1 || !argv)
650:    return -1;
651:  if (argc + 1 > NXEXEC_ARGV_MAX)
652:    return -1;
653:  char *full[NXEXEC_ARGV_MAX];
654:  full[0] = (char *)"/sys/bin/nxexec";
655:  for (int i = 0; i < argc; i++)
656:    full[i + 1] = argv[i];
657:  return (int)OS1low_process_spawn_detached("/sys/bin/nxexec", argc + 1, full);
658:}
659:
660:#endif /* _USER_NXEXEC_H */

4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxicon.h
6: * Dock/launcher icon loading and caching (GFX-NXUI-02 follow-up).
7: *
8: * Icons live on the VFS at /home/Pictures/icon/{dark,light}/<name>.png — a
9: * curated, OS-shipped asset set (NOT arbitrary user images), two full sets so a
10: * theme flip never needs to touch disk again once both are warm.  This header
11: * owns the one place that knows those paths, which app a window title/exe path
12: * maps to, and how the tile-sized ARGB copy is cached — nxui.c (and later
13: * nxlauncher.c) just calls nxicon_get() and draws whatever it returns.
14: *
15: * Same header-only static-inline pattern as nxres.h/nxexec.h: dropped into
16: * any translation unit that needs it, no separate .c/link step.
17: *
18: * TOGGLE (NXICON_ENABLE): compile-time only, on purpose.  With it at 0,
19: * nxicon_get() always returns NULL and every caller's existing classic-tile
20: * fallback (flat rounded-square fill, unchanged since GFX-NXUI-02) runs
21: * instead — one guarded lookup, not a second maintained code path.  A
22: * missing/undecodable individual icon degrades the SAME way at runtime
23: * (nxicon_get returns NULL for just that one), so "some icons installed"
24: * and "icons off entirely" are handled by the exact same caller-side check.
25: *
26: * SAFETY NOTE: nxicon_get() still calls os1_image_load(), which still runs
27: * the full sanitizing decode in graphics_load_image() (bounded read off a
28: * capability-gated handle, stbi_info probe, dimension/pixel caps) — that
29: * path is not weakened for icons.  What IS skipped, because these are known
30: * square OS-shipped assets rather than arbitrary user photos, is nximage.c's
31: * aspect-preserving os1_image_fit_size()/os1_image_resample_fit() dance:
32: * icons resample straight to tile_size x tile_size, once, then are cached —
33: * never re-decoded or re-fit per frame, which matters here because nxui
34: * redraws potentially many tiles at ~30Hz.
35: */

158:/* One cache slot per (theme, app id).  `tried` distinguishes "never asked"
159: * from "asked and it's missing/bad" so a permanently-absent icon costs one
160: * failed load for the whole process lifetime, not one per redraw. */

162:  os1_image_t *img;

169:/* nxicon_ci_prefix - case-insensitive prefix test: 1 if 's' starts with
170: * 'prefix' ignoring ASCII case, 0 otherwise. This environment's os1.h only
171: * declares strcasecmp() (whole-string), not a bounded/prefix strncasecmp(),
172: * so this is a tiny self-contained helper in the same header-only style as
173: * the rest of nxicon.h — no new libc dependency. */
174:static inline int nxicon_ci_prefix(const char *s, const char *prefix) {
175:  while (*prefix) {
176:    if (!*s)
177:      return 0;
178:    char a = *s, b = *prefix;
179:    if (a >= 'A' && a <= 'Z')
180:      a = (char)(a + 32);
181:    if (b >= 'A' && b <= 'Z')
182:      b = (char)(b + 32);
183:    if (a != b)
184:      return 0;
185:    s++;
186:    prefix++;
187:  }
188:  return 1;
189:}
