191:/*
192: * nxicon_classify - map a window title to an NXICON_* id, for a RUNNING
193: * window (nxui's dock). Use nxicon_classify_path() below for an app-table
194: * entry's executable path (nxlauncher's grid) instead — a window title can
195: * carry extra text a bare exe path never would (e.g. nxshell titles its
196: * window "NXShell PID 6": different case than the binary name "nxshell",
197: * plus a trailing " PID <n>"), so this is deliberately looser:
198: *
199: *   - strips any directory prefix first (some windows carry the full exe
200: *     path as their title instead of a bare name);
201: *   - matches case-INSENSITIVELY, since an app is free to title-case its
202: *     own window ("NXShell") while its binary on disk is lowercase
203: *     ("nxshell");
204: *   - matches by PREFIX, not exact, so a trailing suffix ("NXShell PID 6",
205: *     "nxfilem — folder view") doesn't defeat the match.
206: *
207: * Checked longest/most-specific prefix first where one binary name could
208: * otherwise shadow another (none currently collide, but nxmemstat/nxsettings
209: * etc. are kept in a stable, deliberate order rather than alphabetical).
210: *
211: * Anything unrecognised is NXICON_UNKNOWN — a valid icon choice, not a
212: * failure.
213: */
214:static inline int nxicon_classify(const char *title) {
215:  if (!title)
216:    return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
217:  const char *base = strrchr(title, '/');
218:  base = base ? base + 1 : title;
219:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxlauncher"))
220:    return NXICON_LAUNCHER;
221:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxshell"))
222:    return NXICON_SHELL;
223:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxfilem"))
224:    return NXICON_FILEM;
225:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nximage"))
226:    return NXICON_IMAGE;
227:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxinfo"))
228:    return NXICON_INFO;
229:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxmemstat"))
230:    return NXICON_MEMSTAT;
231:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxperm"))
232:    return NXICON_PERM;
233:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxpower"))
234:    return NXICON_POWER;
235:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxreg"))
236:    return NXICON_REG;
237:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxsettings"))
238:    return NXICON_SETTINGS;
239:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxtop"))
240:    return NXICON_TOP;
241:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "doom"))
242:    return NXICON_DOOM;
243:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "raptor"))
244:    return NXICON_RAPTOR;
245:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "kilo"))
246:    return NXICON_TEXTEDIT;
247:  return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
248:}

250:/*
251: * nxicon_classify_path - map an app-table executable path (e.g.
252: * "/sys/bin/nxshell") to an NXICON_* id by an EXACT basename match.
253: * Anything unrecognised is NXICON_UNKNOWN (the generic app icon).
254: */
255:static inline int nxicon_classify_path(const char *path) {
256:  if (!path)
257:    return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
258:  const char *base = strrchr(path, '/');
259:  base = base ? base + 1 : path;
260:  if (strcmp(base, "nxlauncher") == 0)
261:    return NXICON_LAUNCHER;
262:  if (strcmp(base, "nxshell") == 0)
263:    return NXICON_SHELL;
264:  if (strcmp(base, "nxfilem") == 0)
265:    return NXICON_FILEM;
266:  if (strcmp(base, "nximage") == 0)
267:    return NXICON_IMAGE;
268:  if (strcmp(base, "nxinfo") == 0)
269:    return NXICON_INFO;
270:  if (strcmp(base, "nxmemstat") == 0)
271:    return NXICON_MEMSTAT;
272:  if (strcmp(base, "nxperm") == 0)
273:    return NXICON_PERM;
274:  if (strcmp(base, "nxpower") == 0)
275:    return NXICON_POWER;
276:  if (strcmp(base, "nxreg") == 0)
277:    return NXICON_REG;
278:  if (strcmp(base, "nxsettings") == 0)
279:    return NXICON_SETTINGS;
280:  if (strcmp(base, "nxtop") == 0)
281:    return NXICON_TOP;
282:  if (strcmp(base, "doom") == 0)
283:    return NXICON_DOOM;
284:  if (strcmp(base, "raptor") == 0)
285:    return NXICON_RAPTOR;
286:  if (strcmp(base, "kilo") == 0)
287:    return NXICON_TEXTEDIT;
288:  return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
289:}
290:
291:/*
292: * nxicon_classify_file - map a filesystem entry (name + is_dir) to an
293: * NXICON_* id for nxfilem's content list.  Directories always get
294: * NXICON_FOLDER regardless of name.  Files are classified by extension
295: * (case-insensitive, via os1_image_ext_eq from image.h — same helper
296: * os1_image_path_has_known_ext already uses), falling back to
297: * NXICON_FILE_GENERIC for anything unrecognised.  Kept in the same
298: * header-only, static-inline style as nxicon_classify()/nxicon_classify_path()
299: * above; deliberately independent of nxassoc.h (icon choice and launch
300: * association are separate concerns that happen to share extension lists).
301: */
302:static inline int nxicon_classify_file(const char *name, int is_dir) {
303:  if (is_dir)
304:    return NXICON_FOLDER;
305:  if (!name)
306:    return NXICON_FILE_GENERIC;
307:  const char *ext = strrchr(name, '.');
308:  if (!ext || ext == name)
309:    return NXICON_FILE_GENERIC;
310:
311:  static const char *const c_exts[] = {".c",   ".h", ".cpp", ".cc",
312:                                       ".hpp", ".s", NULL};
313:  static const char *const text_exts[] = {".txt", ".md",  ".log",
314:                                          ".rst", ".csv", NULL};
315:  static const char *const cfg_exts[] = {".cfg",  ".json", ".ini", ".toml",
316:                                         ".yaml", ".yml",  NULL};
317:  static const char *const html_exts[] = {".html", ".htm", ".css", NULL};
318:  static const char *const script_exts[] = {".lua", ".sh", ".py", NULL};
319:  static const char *const video_exts[] = {".mp4", ".mkv",  ".avi", ".webm",
320:                                           ".mpg", ".mpeg", NULL};
321:  static const char *const bin_exts[] = {".bin", ".dat", ".o", ".elf", NULL};
322:
323:  if (os1_image_path_has_known_ext(name))
324:    return NXICON_FILE_IMAGE;
325:  for (int i = 0; c_exts[i]; i++)
326:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, c_exts[i]))
327:      return NXICON_FILE_C;
328:  for (int i = 0; script_exts[i]; i++)
329:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, script_exts[i]))
330:      return NXICON_FILE_SCRIPT;
331:  for (int i = 0; html_exts[i]; i++)
332:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, html_exts[i]))
333:      return NXICON_FILE_HTML;
334:  for (int i = 0; cfg_exts[i]; i++)
335:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, cfg_exts[i]))
336:      return NXICON_FILE_CONFIG;
337:  for (int i = 0; text_exts[i]; i++)
338:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, text_exts[i]))
339:      return NXICON_FILE_TEXT;
340:  for (int i = 0; video_exts[i]; i++)
341:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, video_exts[i]))
342:      return NXICON_FILE_VIDEO;
343:  if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, ".elf"))
344:    return NXICON_FILE_EXECUTABLE;
345:  for (int i = 0; bin_exts[i]; i++)
346:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, bin_exts[i]))
347:      return NXICON_FILE_BINARY;
348:  return NXICON_FILE_GENERIC;
349:}
350:
351:/* nxicon_reset_cache - drop every cached scaled icon and retry flag (both
352: * themes).  Only needed if the tile size itself changes (a future DPI/zoom
353: * feature); a plain theme flip does NOT need this, since both themes are
354: * cached side by side already. */
355:static inline void nxicon_reset_cache(void) {
356:  for (int t = 0; t < 2; t++)
357:    for (int i = 0; i < NXICON_COUNT; i++) {
358:      if (nxicon_cache[t][i].img)
359:        os1_image_free(nxicon_cache[t][i].img);
360:      nxicon_cache[t][i].img = NULL;
361:      nxicon_cache[t][i].tried = 0;
362:    }
363:  nxicon_tile_size = 0;
364:}
365:
366:/*
367: * nxicon_get - cached tile_size x tile_size ARGB icon for (app_id, light), or
368: * NULL if icons are disabled or this asset is missing/undecodable.  Callers
369: * always treat NULL as "fall back to the classic flat-color rounded tile" —
370: * see the header comment above.
371: */
372:static inline os1_image_t *nxicon_get(int app_id, int light, int tile_size) {
373:#if !NXICON_ENABLE
374:  (void)app_id;
375:  (void)light;
376:  (void)tile_size;
377:  return NULL;
378:#else
379:  if (app_id < 0 || app_id >= NXICON_COUNT || tile_size <= 0)
380:    return NULL;
381:
382:  if (nxicon_tile_size != tile_size)
383:    nxicon_reset_cache(); /* size changed since the cache was built: rebuild
384:                           * lazily, one icon at a time, as each is next
385:                           * requested — not an eager reload of all fifteen. */
386:  nxicon_tile_size = tile_size;
387:
388:  int theme = light ? NXICON_THEME_LIGHT : NXICON_THEME_DARK;
389:  nxicon_slot_t *slot = &nxicon_cache[theme][app_id];
390:  if (slot->img)
391:    return slot->img;
392:  if (slot->tried)
393:    return NULL;
394:  slot->tried = 1;
395:
396:  os1_image_t *src = os1_image_load(nxicon_paths[theme][app_id]);
397:  if (!src)
398:    return NULL;
399:
400:  /* Trusted-asset fast path: known-square OS icon, so resample straight to
401:   * the tile size instead of nximage.c's aspect-fit dance for arbitrary user
402:   * photos.  Skip the resample entirely if the asset already matches. */
403:  os1_image_t *scaled = (src->w == tile_size && src->h == tile_size)
404:                            ? src
405:                            : os1_image_resample(src, tile_size, tile_size);
406:  if (scaled != src)
407:    os1_image_free(src);
408:  if (!scaled)
409:    return NULL;
410:
411:  slot->img = scaled;
412:  return slot->img;
413:#endif
414:}
415:
416:#endif /* _USER_NXICON_H */

41:static void buf_draw_glyph(int x, int y, uint32_t codepoint, uint32_t color) {
42:  if (!g_font)
43:    return;
44:  int idx = (int)codepoint - g_font->header.first_char;
45:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= g_font->header.num_chars)
46:    return;
47:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &g_font->glyphs[idx];
48:  uint8_t *bitmap = g_font->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
49:  int start_x = x + gi->x0;
50:  int start_y = y + g_font->header.ascent + gi->y0;
51:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
52:    for (int gx = 0; gx < gi->width; gx++) {
53:      uint8_t alpha = bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx];
54:      if (alpha > 64) {
55:        int px = start_x + gx, py = start_y + gy;
56:        if (px >= 0 && px < g_ww && py >= 0 && py < g_wh)
57:          g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = color;
58:      }
59:    }
60:  }
61:}
62:
63:static int buf_text_width(const char *s) {
64:  if (!g_font || !s)
65:    return 0;
66:  return font_string_width(g_font, s);
67:}
68:
69:static void buf_draw_text(int x, int y, const char *s, uint32_t color) {
70:  if (!g_font || !s)
71:    return;
72:  uint32_t cp;
73:  int consumed, cursor = x;
74:  size_t rem = strlen(s);
75:  const char *p = s;
76:  while (*p) {
77:    consumed = utf8_decode(p, rem, &cp);
78:    if (consumed <= 0) {
79:      p++;
80:      rem--;
81:      continue;
82:    }
83:    buf_draw_glyph(cursor, y, cp, color);
84:    int idx = (int)cp - g_font->header.first_char;
85:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < g_font->header.num_chars)
86:      cursor += g_font->glyphs[idx].advance;
87:    p += consumed;
88:    rem -= consumed;
89:  }
90:}

98:static void update_screen_size(void) {

100:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);

106:static void clear_scaled(void) {

112:static int scaled_size(const os1_image_t *img, int *out_w, int *out_h) {
113:  if (!img || !out_w || !out_h)
114:    return -1;
115:  int64_t tw = ((int64_t)img->w * g_zoom + 500) / 1000;
116:  int64_t th = ((int64_t)img->h * g_zoom + 500) / 1000;
117:  if (tw < 1)
118:    tw = 1;
119:  if (th < 1)
120:    th = 1;
121:  if (tw > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION)
122:    tw = OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION;
123:  if (th > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION)
124:    th = OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION;
125:  if ((uint64_t)tw * (uint64_t)th > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS)
126:    return -1;
127:  *out_w = (int)tw;
128:  *out_h = (int)th;
129:  return 0;
130:}

132:static int render_size(const os1_image_t *img, int *out_w, int *out_h) {
133:  if (scaled_size(img, out_w, out_h) < 0)
134:    return -1;
135:
136:  if (g_ww > 0 && g_wh > 0) {
137:    int content_w = g_ww - PAD * 2;
138:    int content_h = g_wh - PAD * 2 - top_bar_h();
139:    if (content_w < 1)
140:      content_w = 1;
141:    if (content_h < 1)
142:      content_h = 1;
143:    if (*out_w > content_w)
144:      *out_w = content_w;
145:    if (*out_h > content_h)
146:      *out_h = content_h;
147:  }
148:  if (*out_w < 1)
149:    *out_w = 1;
150:  if (*out_h < 1)
151:    *out_h = 1;
152:  return 0;
153:}

155:static int desired_window_size(const os1_image_t *img, int *ww, int *wh) {
156:  int iw = 0, ih = 0;
157:  if (scaled_size(img, &iw, &ih) < 0)
158:    return -1;
159:
160:  int max_w = (g_screen_w * 9) / 10;
161:  int max_h = (g_screen_h * 8) / 10;
162:  *ww = iw + PAD * 2;
163:  *wh = ih + PAD * 2 + TOOLBAR_H;
164:  if (*ww < MIN_W)
165:    *ww = MIN_W;
166:  if (*wh < MIN_H)
167:    *wh = MIN_H;
168:  if (*ww > max_w)
169:    *ww = max_w;
170:  if (*wh > max_h)
171:    *wh = max_h;
172:  return 0;
173:}

175:static int resize_fb(int ww, int wh) {
176:  if (ww <= 0 || wh <= 0)
177:    return -1;
178:  if ((uint64_t)ww * (uint64_t)wh > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS)
179:    return -1;
180:  uint32_t *next = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)ww * (size_t)wh * 4u);
181:  if (!next)
182:    return -1;
183:  free(g_fb);
184:  g_fb = next;
185:  g_ww = ww;
186:  g_wh = wh;
187:  return 0;
188:}

190:static int ensure_scaled(const os1_image_t *img) {
191:  int sw = 0, sh = 0;
192:  if (render_size(img, &sw, &sh) < 0)
193:    return -1;
194:  if (g_scaled && g_scaled_zoom == g_zoom && g_scaled->w == sw &&
195:      g_scaled->h == sh)
196:    return 0;
197:
198:  os1_image_t *next = os1_image_resample(img, sw, sh);
199:  if (!next)
200:    return -1;
201:  clear_scaled();
202:  g_scaled = next;
203:  g_scaled_zoom = g_zoom;
204:  return 0;
205:}

207:static void fb_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h, uint32_t color) {
208:  if (!g_fb || w <= 0 || h <= 0)
209:    return;
210:  int x1 = x < 0 ? 0 : x;
211:  int y1 = y < 0 ? 0 : y;
212:  int x2 = x + w;
213:  int y2 = y + h;
214:  if (x2 > g_ww)
215:    x2 = g_ww;
216:  if (y2 > g_wh)
217:    y2 = g_wh;
218:  for (int py = y1; py < y2; py++)
219:    for (int px = x1; px < x2; px++)
220:      g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = color;
221:}

250:  fb_rect(x, y, 1, HIDE_BTN_SIZE, 0xFF8A8F98u);
251:  fb_rect(x + HIDE_BTN_SIZE - 1, y, 1, HIDE_BTN_SIZE, 0xFF8A8F98u);
252:

254:  int cy = y + HIDE_BTN_SIZE / 2;
255:  for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
256:    fb_rect(cx - 5 + i, cy + 2 - i, 2, 2, 0xFF111827u);
257:    fb_rect(cx + 3 - i, cy + 2 - i, 2, 2, 0xFF111827u);
258:  }

261:static void draw_button(int x, int y, int kind) {
262:  fb_rect(x, y, BTN_SIZE, BTN_SIZE, 0xEEFFFFFFu);
263:  fb_rect(x, y, BTN_SIZE, 1, 0xFF8A8F98u);
264:  fb_rect(x, y + BTN_SIZE - 1, BTN_SIZE, 1, 0xFF8A8F98u);
265:  fb_rect(x, y, 1, BTN_SIZE, 0xFF8A8F98u);
266:  fb_rect(x + BTN_SIZE - 1, y, 1, BTN_SIZE, 0xFF8A8F98u);
267:
268:  int cx = x + BTN_SIZE / 2;
269:  int cy = y + BTN_SIZE / 2;
270:  if (kind == 0) {
271:    fb_line_h(cx - 7, cy, 14, 0xFF111827u);
272:  } else if (kind == 1) {
273:    fb_line_h(cx - 7, cy, 14, 0xFF111827u);
274:    fb_line_v(cx, cy - 7, 14, 0xFF111827u);
275:  } else if (kind == 2) {
276:    fb_rect(cx - 6, cy - 6, 12, 2, 0xFF111827u);
277:    fb_rect(cx - 6, cy + 4, 12, 2, 0xFF111827u);
278:    fb_rect(cx - 6, cy - 6, 2, 12, 0xFF111827u);
279:    fb_rect(cx + 4, cy - 6, 2, 12, 0xFF111827u);
280:  } else if (kind == 3) {
281:    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
282:      fb_line_v(cx - 5 + i, cy - 9 + i, 18 - i * 2, 0xFF111827u);
283:  } else if (kind == 4) {
284:    fb_rect(cx - 6, cy - 8, 4, 16, 0xFF111827u);
285:    fb_rect(cx + 2, cy - 8, 4, 16, 0xFF111827u);
286:  }
287:}

289:static void draw_view(const os1_image_t *img) {
290:  if (!g_fb || !img)
291:    return;
292:
293:  for (int i = 0; i < g_ww * g_wh; i++)
294:    g_fb[i] = 0x00000000u;
295:
296:  if (!g_bar_hidden) {
297:    fb_rect(0, 0, g_ww, TOOLBAR_H, 0xEAF8F9FBu);
298:    fb_rect(0, TOOLBAR_H - 1, g_ww, 1, 0xFFB8BEC8u);
299:
300:    int minus_x, reset_x, plus_x, by;
301:    button_rects(&minus_x, &reset_x, &plus_x, &by);
302:    draw_button(minus_x, by, 0);
303:    draw_button(reset_x, by, 2);
304:    draw_button(plus_x, by, 1);
305:
306:    int hx, hy;
307:    hide_btn_rect(&hx, &hy);
308:    draw_hide_button(hx, hy);
309:  } else {
310:    fb_rect(0, 0, g_ww, HIDE_LINE_H, 0xFFFFFFFFu);
311:  }
312:
313:  if (ensure_scaled(img) < 0 || !g_scaled)
314:    return;
315:
316:  int bar_h = top_bar_h();
317:  int content_h = g_wh - bar_h;
318:  int ox = (g_ww - g_scaled->w) / 2;
319:  int oy = bar_h + (content_h - g_scaled->h) / 2;
320:  if (oy < bar_h + PAD)
321:    oy = bar_h + PAD;
322:  if (ox < PAD)
323:    ox = PAD;
324:
325:  for (int y = 0; y < g_scaled->h; y++) {
326:    int dy = oy + y;
327:    if (dy < bar_h || dy >= g_wh)
328:      continue;
329:    for (int x = 0; x < g_scaled->w; x++) {
330:      int dx = ox + x;
331:      if (dx < 0 || dx >= g_ww)
332:        continue;
333:      g_fb[dy * g_ww + dx] = g_scaled->pixels[y * g_scaled->w + x];
334:    }
335:  }
336:}

338:static int apply_zoom_window(int win, const os1_image_t *img) {
339:  int ww = 0, wh = 0;
340:  if (desired_window_size(img, &ww, &wh) < 0)
341:    return -1;
342:  OS1_window_resize(win, ww, wh);
343:  resize_fb(ww, wh);
344:  return 0;
345:}

347:static int handle_toolbar_click(int win, const os1_image_t *img, int mx,
348:                                int my) {
349:  if (g_bar_hidden) {
350:    if (my < HIDE_LINE_H + 6) {
351:      g_bar_hidden = 0;
352:      clear_scaled();
353:      return 1;
354:    }
355:    return 0;
356:  }
357:
358:  int hx, hy;
359:  hide_btn_rect(&hx, &hy);
360:  if (mx >= hx && mx < hx + HIDE_BTN_SIZE && my >= hy &&
361:      my < hy + HIDE_BTN_SIZE) {
362:    g_bar_hidden = 1;
363:    clear_scaled();
364:    return 1;
365:  }
366:
367:  int minus_x, reset_x, plus_x, by;
368:  button_rects(&minus_x, &reset_x, &plus_x, &by);
369:  if (my < by || my >= by + BTN_SIZE)
370:    return 0;
371:
372:  int next_zoom = g_zoom;
373:  if (mx >= minus_x && mx < minus_x + BTN_SIZE)
374:    next_zoom = (g_zoom * 4) / 5;
375:  else if (mx >= reset_x && mx < reset_x + BTN_SIZE)
376:    next_zoom = 1000;
377:  else if (mx >= plus_x && mx < plus_x + BTN_SIZE)
378:    next_zoom = (g_zoom * 5) / 4;
379:  else
380:    return 0;
381:
382:  if (next_zoom < ZOOM_MIN)
383:    next_zoom = ZOOM_MIN;
384:  if (next_zoom > ZOOM_MAX)
385:    next_zoom = ZOOM_MAX;
386:  if (next_zoom != g_zoom) {
387:    g_zoom = next_zoom;
388:    clear_scaled();
389:    apply_zoom_window(win, img);
390:  }
391:  return 1;
392:}

394:static int run_window(const char *path, os1_image_t *img) {
395:  update_screen_size();
396:
397:  int fit_w = 0, fit_h = 0;
398:  int max_w = (g_screen_w * 9) / 10 - PAD * 2;
399:  int max_h = (g_screen_h * 8) / 10 - PAD * 2 - TOOLBAR_H;
400:  if (os1_image_fit_size(img->w, img->h, max_w, max_h, 0, &fit_w, &fit_h) ==
401:      OS1_IMAGE_OK) {
402:    int zw = (fit_w * 1000) / img->w;
403:    int zh = (fit_h * 1000) / img->h;
404:    g_zoom = zw < zh ? zw : zh;
405:    if (g_zoom < ZOOM_MIN)
406:      g_zoom = ZOOM_MIN;
407:    if (g_zoom > 1000)
408:      g_zoom = 1000;
409:  }
410:
411:  int ww = 0, wh = 0;
412:  desired_window_size(img, &ww, &wh);
413:  int wx = (g_screen_w - ww) / 2;
414:  int wy = (g_screen_h - wh) / 2;
415:
416:  if (resize_fb(ww, wh) < 0)
417:    return 1;
418:
419:  char title[64];
420:  snprintf(title, sizeof(title), "nximage: %s", path);
421:  int win = create_window(wx, wy, ww, wh, title);
422:  if (win < 0)
423:    return 1;
424:
425:  for (;;) {
426:    draw_view(img);
427:    window_blit(win, 0, 0, g_ww, g_wh, g_fb);
428:    /* SCHED-STACK-ISO: init pumps the compositor via flush(); blit marks
429:     * damage — no nested compositor_render() here. */
430:
431:    input_event_t ev;
432:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
433:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE && ev.resize.w > 0 && ev.resize.h > 0) {
434:        resize_fb(ev.resize.w, ev.resize.h);
435:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE &&
436:                 ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
437:                 ev.mouse.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
438:        handle_toolbar_click(win, img, ev.mouse.x, ev.mouse.y);
439:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD &&
440:                 ev.keyboard.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
441:        if (ev.keyboard.key == 'q' || ev.keyboard.key == 'Q' ||
442:            ev.keyboard.scancode == INPUT_KEY_ESC) {
443:          destroy_window(win);
444:          return 0;
445:        }
446:      }
447:    }
448:    OS1_sleep(50);
449:  }
450:}
451:
452:static int run_terminal(const char *path, os1_image_t *img) {
453:  os1_image_t *small = os1_image_resample_fit(img, TERM_W, TERM_H, 0);
454:  if (!small)
455:    return 1;
456:
457:  const char *ramp = " .:-=+*#%@";
458:  int ramp_n = 10;
459:  printf("nximage: %s (%dx%d)\n", path, img->w, img->h);
460:  for (int y = 0; y < small->h; y++) {
461:    for (int x = 0; x < small->w; x++) {
462:      uint32_t p = small->pixels[y * small->w + x];
463:      int a = (int)((p >> 24) & 0xFFu);
464:      int r = (int)((p >> 16) & 0xFFu);
465:      int g = (int)((p >> 8) & 0xFFu);
466:      int b = (int)(p & 0xFFu);
467:      int lum = (r * 30 + g * 59 + b * 11) / 100;
468:      lum = (lum * a + 255 * (255 - a)) / 255;
469:      int idx = (lum * (ramp_n - 1)) / 255;
470:      putchar(ramp[idx]);
471:      putchar(ramp[idx]);
472:    }
473:    putchar('\n');
474:  }
475:  os1_image_free(small);
476:  return 0;
477:}
478:
479:static void video_bar_rects(int *play_x, int *play_y, int *bar_x, int *bar_y,
480:                            int *bar_w, int *time_x) {
481:  *play_y = (TOOLBAR_H - BTN_SIZE) / 2;
482:  *play_x = PAD;
483:  *bar_x = *play_x + BTN_SIZE + VBAR_MARGIN;
484:  *bar_y = (TOOLBAR_H - VBAR_H) / 2;
485:  *time_x = g_ww - PAD - HIDE_BTN_SIZE - VBAR_MARGIN - VBAR_TIME_W;
486:  *bar_w = *time_x - VBAR_MARGIN - *bar_x;
487:  if (*bar_w < 10)
488:    *bar_w = 10;
489:}
490:
491:static void format_time(double seconds, char *out, size_t out_size) {
492:  if (seconds < 0)
493:    seconds = 0;
494:  int total = (int)(seconds + 0.5);
495:  int m = total / 60;
496:  int s = total % 60;
497:  snprintf(out, out_size, "%02d:%02d", m, s);
498:}
499:
500:static void draw_video_toolbar(const os1vid_t *v) {
501:  if (g_bar_hidden) {
502:    fb_rect(0, 0, g_ww, HIDE_LINE_H, 0xFFFFFFFFu);
503:    return;
504:  }
505:
506:  fb_rect(0, 0, g_ww, TOOLBAR_H, 0xEAF8F9FBu);
507:  fb_rect(0, TOOLBAR_H - 1, g_ww, 1, 0xFFB8BEC8u);
508:
509:  int play_x, play_y, bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, time_x;
510:  video_bar_rects(&play_x, &play_y, &bar_x, &bar_y, &bar_w, &time_x);
511:
512:  draw_button(play_x, play_y, os1vid_is_paused(v) ? 3 : 4);
513:
514:  int hx, hy;
515:  hide_btn_rect(&hx, &hy);
516:  draw_hide_button(hx, hy);
517:
518:  fb_rect(bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, VBAR_H, 0xFFD8DCE3u);
519:  double dur = os1vid_get_duration(v);
520:  double cur = os1vid_get_time(v);
521:  int fill_w = 0;
522:  if (dur > 0.0) {
523:    fill_w = (int)((cur / dur) * bar_w + 0.5);
524:    if (fill_w < 0)
525:      fill_w = 0;
526:    if (fill_w > bar_w)
527:      fill_w = bar_w;
528:  }
529:  if (fill_w > 0)
530:    fb_rect(bar_x, bar_y, fill_w, VBAR_H, 0xFF3B82F6u);
531:
532:  int handle_x = bar_x + fill_w - 2;
533:  if (handle_x < bar_x)
534:    handle_x = bar_x;
535:  fb_rect(handle_x, bar_y - 3, 4, VBAR_H + 6, 0xFF1D4ED8u);
536:
537:  if (g_font) {
538:    char cur_s[16], dur_s[16], label[40];
539:    format_time(cur, cur_s, sizeof(cur_s));
540:    format_time(dur, dur_s, sizeof(dur_s));
541:    snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "%s / %s", cur_s, dur_s);
542:    int lw = buf_text_width(label);
543:    int lx = time_x + (VBAR_TIME_W - lw) / 2;
544:    if (lx < time_x)
545:      lx = time_x;
546:    int ly = (TOOLBAR_H - 16) / 2;
547:    buf_draw_text(lx, ly, label, 0xFF111827u);
548:  }
549:}
550:
551:static int handle_video_toolbar_click(os1vid_t *v, int mx, int my) {
552:  if (g_bar_hidden) {
553:    if (my < HIDE_LINE_H + 6) {
554:      g_bar_hidden = 0;
555:      return 2;
556:    }
557:    return 0;
558:  }
559:
560:  int hx, hy;
561:  hide_btn_rect(&hx, &hy);
562:  if (mx >= hx && mx < hx + HIDE_BTN_SIZE && my >= hy &&
563:      my < hy + HIDE_BTN_SIZE) {
564:    g_bar_hidden = 1;
565:    return 2;
566:  }
567:
568:  int play_x, play_y, bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, time_x;
569:  video_bar_rects(&play_x, &play_y, &bar_x, &bar_y, &bar_w, &time_x);
570:
571:  if (my >= play_y && my < play_y + BTN_SIZE && mx >= play_x &&
572:      mx < play_x + BTN_SIZE) {
573:    if (os1vid_is_paused(v))
574:      os1vid_resume(v);
575:    else
576:      os1vid_pause(v);
577:    return 1;
578:  }
579:
580:  int bar_hit_y0 = bar_y - 6;
581:  int bar_hit_y1 = bar_y + VBAR_H + 6;
582:  if (my >= bar_hit_y0 && my < bar_hit_y1 && mx >= bar_x &&
583:      mx < bar_x + bar_w) {
584:    double dur = os1vid_get_duration(v);
585:    if (dur > 0.0) {
586:      double frac = (double)(mx - bar_x) / (double)bar_w;
587:      if (frac < 0.0)
588:        frac = 0.0;
589:      if (frac > 1.0)
590:        frac = 1.0;
591:      os1vid_seek(v, frac * dur);
592:    }
593:    return 1;
594:  }
595:
596:  return 0;
597:}
598:
599:static void fit_video_content(const os1vid_t *v, int ww, int wh, int *out_vw,
600:                              int *out_vh) {
601:  if (ww <= 0 || wh <= 0) {
602:    *out_vw = 1;
603:    *out_vh = 1;
604:    return;
605:  }
606:
607:  int avail_w = ww - PAD * 2;
608:  int avail_h = wh - top_bar_h() - PAD * 2;
609:  if (avail_w < 1)
610:    avail_w = 1;
611:  if (avail_h < 1)
612:    avail_h = 1;
613:
614:  int vw = v->width;
615:  int vh = v->height;
616:  if (vw > avail_w || vh > avail_h) {
617:    int fit_w = 0, fit_h = 0;
618:    if (os1_image_fit_size(v->width, v->height, avail_w, avail_h, 0, &fit_w,
619:                           &fit_h) == OS1_IMAGE_OK) {
620:      vw = fit_w;
621:      vh = fit_h;
622:    }
623:  }
624:  if (vw > avail_w)
625:    vw = avail_w;
626:  if (vh > avail_h)
627:    vh = avail_h;
628:  if (vw < 1)
629:    vw = 1;
630:  if (vh < 1)
631:    vh = 1;
632:  *out_vw = vw;
633:  *out_vh = vh;
634:}
635:
636:static int run_video(const char *path) {
637:  os1vid_t *v = os1vid_open(path);
638:  if (!v) {
639:    printf("nximage: unable to decode '%s' as MPEG1 (.mpg/.mpeg)\n", path);
640:    printf("Convert other formats first, e.g.:\n");
641:    printf("  ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v mpeg1video -c:a mp2 -format mpeg "
642:           "output.mpg\n");
643:    return 1;
644:  }
645:
646:  update_screen_size();
647:  int max_w = (g_screen_w * 9) / 10;
648:  int max_h = (g_screen_h * 8) / 10;
649:
650:  int vw = 0, vh = 0;
651:  fit_video_content(v, max_w, max_h, &vw, &vh);
652:  if (vw < MIN_W)
653:    vw = MIN_W;
654:  if (vh < MIN_H - top_bar_h())
655:    vh = MIN_H - top_bar_h();
656:
657:  int ww = vw;
658:  int wh = vh + top_bar_h();
659:  int wx = (g_screen_w - ww) / 2;
660:  int wy = (g_screen_h - wh) / 2;
661:
662:  if (resize_fb(ww, wh) < 0) {
663:    os1vid_close(v);
664:    return 1;
665:  }
666:
667:  char title[64];
668:  snprintf(title, sizeof(title), "nximage: %s", path);
669:  int win = create_window(wx, wy, ww, wh, title);
670:  if (win < 0) {
671:    os1vid_close(v);
672:    return 1;
673:  }
674:
675:  printf("nximage: playing %s (%dx%d, %.2f fps, MPEG1, no audio device)\n",
676:         path, v->width, v->height, v->framerate);
677:
678:  int quit = 0;
679:  int force_redraw = 1;
680:  while (!quit) {
681:    int decoded = os1vid_update(v);
682:
683:    if (decoded || os1vid_is_paused(v) || os1vid_has_ended(v) || force_redraw) {
684:      force_redraw = 0;
685:      for (int i = 0; i < g_ww * g_wh; i++)
686:        g_fb[i] = 0x00000000u;
687:
688:      int bar_h = top_bar_h();
689:      int content_h = g_wh - bar_h;
690:      int ox = (g_ww - vw) / 2;
691:      int oy = bar_h + (content_h - vh) / 2;
692:      if (oy < bar_h + PAD)
693:        oy = bar_h + PAD;
694:      if (ox < PAD)
695:        ox = PAD;
696:
697:      /* Use packed_pixels for safe bounds-checked drawing */
698:      if (vw == v->width && vh == v->height) {
699:        for (int y = 0; y < vh; y++) {
700:          int dy = oy + y;
701:          if (dy < bar_h || dy >= g_wh)
702:            continue;
703:          for (int x = 0; x < vw; x++) {
704:            int dx = ox + x;
705:            if (dx < 0 || dx >= g_ww)
706:              continue;
707:            g_fb[dy * g_ww + dx] = v->packed_pixels[y * v->width + x];
708:          }
709:        }
710:      } else {
711:        os1_image_t frame_view = {v->width, v->height, v->packed_pixels};
712:        os1_image_t *scaled = os1_image_resample(&frame_view, vw, vh);
713:        if (scaled) {
714:          for (int y = 0; y < scaled->h; y++) {
715:            int dy = oy + y;
716:            if (dy < bar_h || dy >= g_wh)
717:              continue;
718:            for (int x = 0; x < scaled->w; x++) {
719:              int dx = ox + x;
720:              if (dx < 0 || dx >= g_ww)
721:                continue;
722:              g_fb[dy * g_ww + dx] = scaled->pixels[y * scaled->w + x];
723:            }
724:          }
725:          free(scaled->pixels);
726:          free(scaled);
727:        }
728:      }
729:
730:      draw_video_toolbar(v);
731:      window_blit(win, 0, 0, g_ww, g_wh, g_fb);
732:      /* SCHED-STACK-ISO: init pumps the compositor via flush(); blit marks
733:       * damage — no nested compositor_render() here. */
734:    }
735:
736:    if (os1vid_has_ended(v)) {
737:      os1vid_pause(v);
738:    }
739:
740:    input_event_t ev;
741:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
742:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE && ev.resize.w > 0 && ev.resize.h > 0) {
743:        if (resize_fb(ev.resize.w, ev.resize.h) == 0) {
744:          fit_video_content(v, g_ww, g_wh, &vw, &vh);
745:          force_redraw = 1;
746:        }
747:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE &&
748:                 ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
749:                 ev.mouse.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
750:        int r = handle_video_toolbar_click(v, ev.mouse.x, ev.mouse.y);
751:        if (r == 2) {
752:          fit_video_content(v, g_ww, g_wh, &vw, &vh);
753:          force_redraw = 1;
754:        } else if (r == 1) {
755:          force_redraw = 1;
756:        }
757:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD &&
758:                 ev.keyboard.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
759:        if (ev.keyboard.key == 'q' || ev.keyboard.key == 'Q' ||
760:            ev.keyboard.scancode == INPUT_KEY_ESC) {
761:          quit = 1;
762:        } else if (ev.keyboard.key == ' ') {
763:          if (os1vid_is_paused(v))
764:            os1vid_resume(v);
765:          else
766:            os1vid_pause(v);
767:          force_redraw = 1;
768:        }
769:      }
770:    }
771:    OS1_sleep(8);
772:  }
773:
774:  destroy_window(win);
775:  os1vid_close(v);
776:  return 0;
777:}
778:
779:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
780:  int term = 0;
781:  const char *path = "/home/Pictures//globe.png";
782:
783:  if (argc >= 2 && streq(argv[1], "--term")) {
784:    term = 1;
785:    if (argc >= 3)
786:      path = argv[2];
787:  } else if (argc >= 2) {
788:    path = argv[1];
789:  }
790:
791:  if (os1vid_path_has_known_ext(path)) {
792:    if (term) {
793:      printf("nximage: --term does not support video playback; drop --term to "
794:             "open %s in a window.\n",
795:             path);
796:      return 1;
797:    }
798:    g_font = font_load("/fonts/Rewir-Light.off");
799:    return run_video(path);
800:  }
801:
802:  os1_image_t *img = os1_image_load(path);
803:  if (!img) {
804:    printf("nximage: unable to load '%s'\n", path);
805:    printf("usage: nximage [--term] [file.png|file.mpg]\n");
806:    return 1;
807:  }
808:
809:  printf("nximage: decoded %s (%dx%d, sanitized ARGB)\n", path, img->w, img->h);
810:  int r = term ? run_terminal(path, img) : run_window(path, img);
811:  clear_scaled();
812:  os1_image_free(img);
813:  free(g_fb);
814:  return r;
815:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxinfo.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxinfo.c
3: * NEXS system-information frontend (ASTRA stratified service model).
4: *
5: * Usage:
6: *   nxinfo        print a one-shot system summary (OS version, uptime, live
7: *                 process count, desktop resolution, pid, cwd)
8: *
9: * This is the THIN CLI frontend over the reusable helper nxinfo.h: it holds no
10: * policy of its own and only reads state the kernel already lets this caller
11: * read, so it is "secure by caller" — an unprivileged user and a system service
12: * each see exactly what the kernel grants them.
13: */
14:#include "nxinfo.h"
15:#include <os1.h>
16:
17:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
18:  if (argc >= 2) {
19:    printf("nxinfo: unexpected argument '%s'\n", argv[1]);
20:    printf("usage: nxinfo\n");
21:    return 1;
22:  }
23:  /* -1 → emit to the caller's stdout/own window via printf. */
24:  nxinfo_print_summary(-1);
25:  return 0;
26:}
27:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxinfo.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXINFO_H
2:#define _USER_NXINFO_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxinfo.h
6: * NEXS stratified system-information helper (ASTRA service layer).
7: *
8: * Helper layer on the nxproc.h stratified pattern, reading coarse system
9: * state: uptime, live process count, desktop resolution, the caller's own
10: * pid/cwd, and the OS version banner.  Header-only (all routines `static
11: * inline`) so consumers pull it in without Makefile churn.  Today its only
12: * consumer is nxinfo.c — kept as a header for pattern consistency, not
13: * because reuse is already demonstrated (contrast nxproc.h's 3 consumers).
14: *
15: * SECURITY MODEL: this layer adds NO ambient permission checks of its own.
16: * Every routine is a thin wrapper over an existing READ-ONLY OS1 syscall
17: * (get_time/os1_mono_ns, _sys_get_procs, _sys_display_info, get_pid, getcwd),
18: * and the kernel already gates those syscalls per caller.  Security is
19: * therefore "by caller" automatically: a privileged system app and an
20: * unprivileged user app calling the same helper each see exactly what the
21: * kernel grants them — the helper neither widens nor narrows that.  Nothing
22: * here mutates system state.
23: *
24: * Process counting reuses nxproc_snapshot() from nxproc.h rather than
25: * duplicating the SYS_GET_PS marshalling, keeping a single source of truth for
26: * the table.
27: *
28: * Consumers: user/sys/bin/nxinfo.c.
29: */
30:
31:#include "nxproc.h" /* nxproc_snapshot(), NXPROC_MAX, struct ps_info */
32:#include <os1.h>
33:
34:/* OS version banner.  Mirrors the build's VERSION (Makefile: VERSION ?=
35: * V0.0.5.4); kept as a userland constant since there is no syscall that reports
36: * it.
37: * TODO: surface the kernel build string via a syscall and read it here instead
38: * of hardcoding, so the banner can never drift from the running kernel. */
39:
40:#ifdef ARCH_AMD64
41:#define KERNEL_NAME "AMD64 NexsOS1"
42:#else
43:#define KERNEL_NAME "AArch64 NexsOS1"
44:#endif
45:
46:#define NXINFO_OS_NAME KERNEL_NAME
47:#define NXINFO_OS_VERSION "V0.0.5.4"
48:
49:/*
50: * nxinfo_uptime_ms - milliseconds elapsed since boot.
51: *
52: * Thin wrapper over get_time() (SYS_GET_TIME), which is the millisecond
53: * monotonic clock the rest of userland already uses.  Never negative in normal
54: * operation; the raw syscall value is returned unmodified.
55: */
56:static inline long nxinfo_uptime_ms(void) { return get_time(); }
57:
58:/*
59: * nxinfo_proc_count - number of entries currently in the process table.
60: *
61: * Takes a point-in-time snapshot via nxproc_snapshot() (capped at NXPROC_MAX)
62: * and returns the count it reported (0..NXPROC_MAX), or a negative value if the
63: * underlying syscall failed.  No heap allocation: the snapshot lives on the
64: * caller's stack for the duration of the call only.
65: */
66:static inline int nxinfo_proc_count(void) {
67:  struct ps_info procs[NXPROC_MAX];
68:  return nxproc_snapshot(procs, NXPROC_MAX);
69:}
70:
71:/*
72: * nxinfo_display - current desktop resolution.
73: *
74: * w/out, h/out: optional out-params; either may be NULL if the caller only
75: *               wants the other dimension (or just the side effect of probing).
76: *
77: * Thin wrapper over OS1_display_info(), which returns the packed value
78: * ((w << 16) | h).  Unpacks the two 16-bit fields into *w and *h.
79: */
80:static inline void nxinfo_display(int *w, int *h) {
81:  long info = OS1_display_info();
82:  if (w)
83:    *w = (int)((info >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
84:  if (h)
85:    *h = (int)(info & 0xFFFF);
86:}
87:
88:/*
89: * nxinfo_emit - internal: route one preformatted line to stdout or a window.
90: *
91: * win_id_or_neg: a compositor window id to write into, or any negative value to
92: *                emit to the caller's stdout/own window via printf().
93: *
94: * This is the single place that branches on the output sink so the summary
95: * formatter below can stay sink-agnostic.  `s` is expected to be
96: * NUL-terminated.
97: */
98:static inline void nxinfo_emit(int win_id_or_neg, const char *s) {
99:  if (win_id_or_neg < 0)
100:    printf("%s", s);
101:  else
102:    printf_win(win_id_or_neg, "%s", s);
103:}
104:
105:/*
106: * nxinfo_print_summary - format and emit a readable multi-line system summary.
107: *
108: * win_id_or_neg: negative -> write to the caller's stdout (printf); otherwise
109: *                write into the given compositor window (printf_win).
110: *
111: * Lines: OS banner, uptime (ms and seconds), process count, desktop resolution,
112: * own pid, and current working directory.  All values come from the read-only
113: * wrappers above, so the summary is "secure by caller" — it reveals only what
114: * the kernel already lets this caller read.  Each line is rendered into a small
115: * stack buffer with snprintf() (bounded, no heap) and then routed to the chosen
116: * sink, so the formatting is shared between the stdout and windowed paths.
117: */
118:static inline void nxinfo_print_summary(int win_id_or_neg) {
119:  char line[160];
120:  char cwd[128];
121:
122:  long up_ms = nxinfo_uptime_ms();
123:  int procs = nxinfo_proc_count();
124:  int w = 0, h = 0;
125:  nxinfo_display(&w, &h);
126:  int pid = get_pid();
127:
128:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s %s\n", NXINFO_OS_NAME, NXINFO_OS_VERSION);
129:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
130:
131:  /* Uptime shown both raw (ms) and in whole seconds for quick reading. */
132:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "uptime:     %ld ms (%ld s)\n", up_ms,
133:           up_ms / 1000);
134:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
135:
136:  if (procs < 0)
137:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "processes:  <unavailable> (err %d)\n", procs);
138:  else
139:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "processes:  %d\n", procs);
140:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
141:
142:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "resolution: %dx%d\n", w, h);
143:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
144:
145:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "pid:        %d\n", pid);
146:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
147:
148:  /* getcwd writes a NUL-terminated path; fall back to "?" on failure so the
149:   * line is always printable. */
150:  if (getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd)) != 0)
151:    cwd[0] = '\0';
152:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "cwd:        %s\n", cwd[0] ? cwd : "?");
153:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
154:}
155:
156:#endif /* _USER_NXINFO_H */
