@@@ user/sys/bin/nxinit.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxinit.c
3: * Process 1 — System Initializer and Service Supervisor
4: *
5: * This is the first userland process launched by the kernel after boot.
6: * It is responsible for:
7: *   1. Spawning the two mandatory system services (notify_srv, shell) in order.
8: *   2. Sending the "Boot Complete" notification via IPC to notify_srv.
9: *   3. Running a non-blocking supervisor loop that detects child exits and
10: *      respawns the dead service immediately.
11: *
12: * Calling convention / runtime:
13: *   _start (user/arch/<arch>/syscall.S) sets up the stack and calls main();
14: *   main() never returns (the supervisor loop is infinite).
15: *
16: * Known issues:
17: *   USR-INIT-01  (W1 REFINE) Supervisor is a correct non-blocking poll today;
18: *                the PID-reuse hazard is NOT live — next_pid is a monotonic
19: *                counter (kernel/sched/process.c:20,233); PIDs are never
20: *                recycled.  A generation/owner check would be needed if PID
21: *                recycling is ever introduced.
22: *   USR-INIT-02  (W3 MISSING·DOC) init.cfg is never read despite the TODO
23: *                comment below being stale: file_read (lib.c:72) is fully
24: *                implemented and used elsewhere.  The paths in init.cfg
25: *                (/notify_srv.elf, /nxshell) do not match the actual rootfs
26: *                layout (/sys/bin/notify_srv, /sys/bin/nxshell).
27: *   USR-INIT-03  (W2 BAD-IMPL) No respawn rate-limiting: a service that
28: *                crashes immediately will be respawned in a tight loop,
29: *                saturating the process table (MAX_PROCESSES=64, os1.h:16)
30: *                with zombies until the system stalls.
31: *   USR-SEC-01   (W3 SECURITY, RESIDUAL) srv.notify_pid has no authentication;
32: *                any process can still overwrite it.  The hijack window is now
33: *                bounded to ONE supervisor tick (~50 ms) because init
34: *                re-publishes the live pid on every respawn (see
35: *                register_notify_pid).  Full capability-based addressing
36: *                (OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS handle) is the planned upgrade; see DIR-01
37: *                M4.5 "IPC -> OBJ_TYPE_PORT".
38: */
39:#include "nxinfo.h"
40:#include <os1.h>
41:#include <sys/wait.h> /* waitpid + status decode — Phase 2 supervisor logging */
42:
43:/*
44: * LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART - gate for spawning + supervising /sys/bin/nxlauncher
45: * (LAUNCHER-01 #138).
46: *
47: * The launcher is a still-shaky feature: its always-on-bottom z-order and
48: * tile grid are actively being tuned, and an accidental respawn during
49: * development can spam the process table with half-broken launchers.  Flip
50: * this to 0 to disable BOTH the initial spawn AND the supervisor respawn,
51: * without commenting code or touching the rest of init.  Default ON; setting
52: * it to 0 keeps the rest of the desktop (shell, dock, notifications)
53: * unaffected.
54: *
55: * The launcher is spawned AFTER /sys/bin/nxui so the dock's window already
56: * has a higher z-order at boot.  The launcher then calls OS1_window_lower()
57: * itself (canonical ASTRA §6.7 WINDOW-LOWER verb) to restack itself at the
58: * back of the z-order, sitting behind the dock and every user window.
59: */
60:#define LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART 1
61:
62:/*
63: * registry_init_defaults - completa le chiavi di registro con dati reali.
64: *
65: * Chiamata DOPO tutti gli spawn iniziali. Il kernel ha già creato le chiavi
66: * base con valori placeholder; init le sovrascrive con l'architettura, la
67: * versione OS, il timestamp di boot reale e i default del compositor.
68: * Ogni binario /sys/bin gira a PLVL_ROOT (preset per-path) e quindi ha
69: * CAP_REG_WRITE come tutti gli altri servizi di sistema; init non è
70: * l'unico scrittore, ma è quello che pubblica i valori reali post-boot.
71: * registry_caller_owner() tratta MACHINE e ROOT come owner 0 (system), così
72: * le chiavi restano scrivibili da qualunque servizio di sistema anche dopo
73: * un respawn con PID diverso (kernel/lib/registry.c).
74: */
75:static void registry_init_defaults(void) {
76:    /* --- Sistema operativo e versione (da nxinfo.h) --- */
77:    OS1_registry_set("system.os", NXINFO_OS_NAME);
78:    OS1_registry_set("system.version", NXINFO_OS_VERSION);
79:
80:    /* --- Architettura (da build flags) --- */
81:#if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__amd64__)
82:    OS1_registry_set("system.arch", "amd64");
83:#elif defined(__aarch64__)
84:    OS1_registry_set("system.arch", "arm64");
85:#else
86:    OS1_registry_set("system.arch", "generic");
87:#endif
88:
89:    /* --- Hostname --- */
90:    OS1_registry_set("system.hostname", "NeXs");
91:
92:    /* --- Tempo di boot reale (secondi dall'epoch, per nxbar e orologio) --- */
93:    char boot_time[32];
94:    snprintf(boot_time, sizeof(boot_time), "%ld", OS1_time_now());
95:    OS1_registry_set("system.boot_time", boot_time);
96:
97:    /* --- Aspetto del compositor (valori predefiniti) --- */
98:    OS1_registry_set("theme.color", "dark");
99:    OS1_registry_set("style.name", "minimal");
100:    OS1_registry_set("background.name", "blue");
101:
102:    /* --- Pannello notifiche (inizialmente chiuso) --- */
103:    OS1_registry_set("sys.ntfy.panel_open", "0");
104:
105:    /* --- Input --- */
106:    OS1_registry_set("mouse.sensitivity", "1.0");
107:
108:    /* --- Environment: the MACHINE's defaults (Phase 17) ---
109:     * These are stored registry keys, not process state: they describe this
110:     * installation's layout, so they belong to the configuration namespace
111:     * (ASTRA §6.6) and outlive every process.  getenv() falls back here when a
112:     * process has no value of its own, which is why nothing has to copy PATH
113:     * into each new process at spawn.  Editing these reconfigures the machine
114:     * and needs CAP_REG_WRITE; a process changing its OWN copy does not.
115:     *
116:     * Seed ONLY what has a verified consumer.  A default with no reader is not
117:     * harmless documentation: it is a claim about the system that nothing keeps
118:     * true, and the first program to believe it finds out the hard way.
119:     *
120:     *   HOME  read by nxexec_resolve_path()'s '~' tier and nxlauncher — and
121:     *         nxexec.h already anticipates it ("a real per-user HOME later
122:     *         becomes a getenv() change alone").
123:     *   PATH  no reader YET: the bare-name search is hardcoded to /bin then
124:     *         /sys/bin inside nxexec_spawn_search.  That hardcoded list IS this
125:     *         key's meaning, and 17c makes the executor consume it, at which
126:     *         point Phase 12's move to /sys/services becomes a registry edit
127:     *         rather than a code edit.
128:     *
129:     * Deliberately NOT seeded:
130:     *   TERM    there is no terminal TYPE yet.  term.c implements a real
131:     *           ECMA-48 subset, but nothing names or describes that capability
132:     *           set, so TERM would advertise a type with nothing behind it (17d).
133:     *   USER    there is no user identity in this system.  Phase 11 owns that
134:     *           model and is blocked on its design doc; inventing a name here
135:     *           would pre-commit it.
136:     *   SHELL   no reader.  system() uses the STANDARD shell by POSIX, not
137:     * $SHELL. TMPDIR  no reader.  doom reads TEMP, and only under #if _WIN32.
138:     */
139:    OS1_registry_set("sys.env.HOME", "/home");
140:    OS1_registry_set("sys.env.PATH", "/bin:/sys/bin");
141:
142:    printf("[Init] Registry defaults initialised.\n");
143:}
144:
145:/*
146: * register_service_pid - publish `pid` as the LIVE endpoint of a singleton
147: * system service by writing it (decimal, NUL-terminated) to registry key
148: * `key`.  Generalised from the original notify-only register_notify_pid
149: * (NOTIFY-REG-01) so every long-lived /sys/bin service init supervises —
150: * nxntfy_srv (srv.notify_pid), nxui/dock (srv.dock_pid), nxbar
151: * (srv.bar_pid), nxlauncher (srv.launcher_pid) — is discoverable the same
152: * way, and stays discoverable across a respawn.
153: *
154: * Called by init on the FIRST spawn AND on every RESPAWN of the service
155: * (init.c main()).  Centralising the write in init fixes two bugs of the
156: * old "server self-registers" model:
157: *   1. A respawn left the key pointing at the corpse's pid — anything
158: *      addressing the service by that pid (notify_post(), or nxres_h's
159: *      theme-change ping, see nxres.h) resolved a dead pid and -ESRCH'd
160: *      silently, so the messages disappeared forever after a single crash.
161: *   2. Any process could overwrite the key (USR-SEC-01) and intercept
162: *      messages meant for the service.  Re-registering on respawn
163: *      overwrites any such hijack with the legitimate pid within one
164: *      supervisor tick (~50 ms).
165: *
166: * Failure to write the registry key is non-fatal: init logs and continues.
167: * Callers addressing the service will keep getting a stale/absent pid until
168: * the key is present, but init's supervisor retries on the next respawn.
169: */
170:static void register_service_pid(const char *key, int pid) {
171:    char pidbuf[16];
172:    int n = snprintf(pidbuf, sizeof(pidbuf), "%d", pid);
173:    if (n <= 0 || n >= (int)sizeof(pidbuf))
174:        return;
175:    if (OS1_registry_set(key, pidbuf) != 0)
176:        printf("[Init] WARN: failed to publish %s=%s\n", key, pidbuf);
177:}
178:
179:/*
180: * create_utmp_file - crea /etc/utmp con un record di login per root.
181: * Necessario per `who`, `logname` e altri comandi che leggono utmp.
182: */
183:#define UT_LINESIZE 32
184:#define UT_NAMESIZE 32
185:#define UT_HOSTSIZE 256
186:
187:struct exit_status {
188:    short e_termination;
189:    short e_exit;
190:};
191:
192:struct utmp {
193:    short ut_type;
194:    pid_t ut_pid;
195:    char ut_line[UT_LINESIZE];
196:    char ut_id[4];
197:    char ut_user[UT_NAMESIZE];
198:    char ut_host[UT_HOSTSIZE];
199:    struct exit_status ut_exit;
200:    long ut_session;
201:    struct timeval ut_tv;
202:    int32_t ut_addr_v6[4];
203:    char __unused[20];
204:};
205:
206:static void create_utmp_file(void) {
207:    struct utmp rec;
208:    memset(&rec, 0, sizeof(rec));
209:
210:    rec.ut_type = 7;          /* USER_PROCESS */
211:    rec.ut_pid = 1;           /* init PID (o qualsiasi) */
212:    strncpy(rec.ut_line, "tty1", sizeof(rec.ut_line) - 1);
213:    strncpy(rec.ut_id, "tty1", sizeof(rec.ut_id) - 1);
214:    strncpy(rec.ut_user, "root", sizeof(rec.ut_user) - 1);
215:    rec.ut_tv.tv_sec = time(NULL);
216:    rec.ut_tv.tv_usec = 0;
217:
218:    /* Crea la directory /etc se non esiste */
219:    mkdir("/etc", 0755);
220:
221:    if (file_write("/etc/utmp", &rec, sizeof(rec), 0) < 0) {
222:        printf("[Init] WARN: could not create /etc/utmp\n");
223:    } else {
224:        printf("[Init] Created /etc/utmp with root login record\n");
225:    }
226:}
227:
228:/*
229: * main - init entry point; never returns.
230: *
231: * Spawns notify_srv and shell, fires the "boot complete" notification, then
232: * enters the supervisor loop.
233: *
234: * No parameters, no meaningful return value (return 0 is unreachable dead code
235: * because the while(1) loop never exits).
236: *
237: * Side effects:
238: *   - Creates two child processes via SYS_SPAWN.
239: *   - Sends one IPC notify message to the notification server.
240: *   - Calls SYS_FLUSH to push any buffered output before entering the loop.
241: */
242:/* service_gone - Phase 2 supervisor probe. WNOHANG-waitpid a supervised
243: * service; if it died, log HOW (clean exit code vs killed/faulted) and return
244: * 1 so the caller respawns. 0 while still running. Replaces the ad-hoc
245: * `wait(pid) == pid || -2` checks with one standard, status-aware seam. */
246:static int service_gone(int pid, const char *name) {
247:    int status = 0;
248:    int r = waitpid(pid, &status, WNOHANG);
249:    if (r == 0)
250:        return 0; /* still alive */
251:    if (r > 0 && WIFSIGNALED(status))
252:        printf("[Init] %s died (killed, sig %d)! Respawning...\n", name,
253:               WTERMSIG(status));
254:    else if (r > 0)
255:        printf("[Init] %s exited (code %d)! Respawning...\n", name,
256:               WEXITSTATUS(status));
257:    else
258:        printf("[Init] %s gone! Respawning...\n", name); /* reaped elsewhere */
259:    return 1;
260:}
261:
262:int main(void) {
263:    print("[Init] System Initialization Starting...\n");
264:
265:    /* Completa il registro con i dati reali (timestamp, architettura, versione)
266:     * prima di ogni spawn, così l'ambiente esiste già quando il primo processo
267:     * utente parte. */
268:    registry_init_defaults();
269:
270:    /* Spawn Notification Server */
271:    /* NOTE(USR-INIT-02): Hardcoded path.  init.cfg would provide this path but
272:     * is never read; the cfg also lists wrong paths (see file header).
273:     * NOTE(NOTIFY-REG-01): init OWNS the srv.notify_pid registry key (see
274:     * register_service_pid() below).  nxntfy_srv no longer publishes its own PID
275:     * — otherwise a respawn leaves the key pointing at the corpse. */
276:    printf("[Init] Spawning Notification Server...\n");
277:    int pid_notify = spawn("/sys/bin/nxntfy_srv");
278:    if (pid_notify > 0) {
279:        printf("[Init] Notification Server started (PID %d)\n", pid_notify);
280:        register_service_pid("srv.notify_pid", pid_notify);
281:    } else {
282:        print("[Init] Failed to spawn Notification Server!\n");
283:    }
284:
285:    /*
286:     * Spawn the EXECUTION SERVICE (nxexec --service, the R6 daemon).
287:     *
288:     * It MUST be started here and nowhere else, and the reason is the capability
289:     * model rather than convention: process_create_caps applies a MONOTONIC
290:     * creator clamp, so a child is never more privileged than its creator.  A
291:     * PLVL_USER client that spawned this service itself would get a PLVL_USER
292:     * service, and the daemon's two defining powers — OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER (handing a
293:     * spawned job back to the requesting client so job control still reaches it)
294:     * and taking a client's fds — are BOTH privileged-only.  Such a service would
295:     * answer requests but silently fail to delegate, breaking jobs/fg/bg in a way
296:     * that looks like a shell bug.  Started from init (PLVL_MACHINE) it lands at
297:     * the /sys/bin ROOT preset and is genuinely privileged.
298:     *
299:     * Clients therefore never spawn it: they CONNECT, by acquiring a send
300:     * capability to the OS1nx_exec port (ASTRA §6.4 "SRL services are supervised
301:     * ELF processes, exposed via IPC/capability").
302:     *
303:     * No register_service_pid() here on purpose: the port NAME is the discovery
304:     * endpoint now, which is strictly better than a pid key — it cannot go stale
305:     * across a respawn, and possession of the capability IS the authority.
306:     */
307:    printf("[Init] Spawning Execution Service (nxexec --service)...\n");
308:    char *execsvc_argv[2];
309:    execsvc_argv[0] = (char *)"/sys/bin/nxexec";
310:    execsvc_argv[1] = (char *)"--service";
311:    int pid_execsvc = spawn_args("/sys/bin/nxexec", 2, execsvc_argv);
312:    if (pid_execsvc > 0)
313:        printf("[Init] Execution Service started (PID %d)\n", pid_execsvc);
314:    else
315:        print("[Init] Failed to spawn Execution Service!\n");
316:
317:    /* Spawn the dock (window-manager UI).  Plain spawn(): the ASTRA per-path
318:     * preset gives any /sys/bin binary ROOT authority (F1), which is exactly what
319:     * a window manager needs to acquire OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW control capabilities to
320:     * any app's window (focus / minimize / restore).  ROOT (not machine) keeps
321:     * the dock killable + respawnable like the shell. */
322:    printf("[Init] Spawning Dock (nxui)...\n");
323:    int pid_nxui = spawn("/sys/bin/nxui");
324:    if (pid_nxui > 0) {
325:        printf("[Init] Dock started (PID %d)\n", pid_nxui);
326:        /* srv.dock_pid: discovery endpoint for cross-process pushes (theme/style
327:         * change ping — nxres.h nxres_broadcast_look_changed) mirroring
328:         * srv.notify_pid, same reason: a respawn must not leave this pointing at
329:         * a corpse. */
330:        register_service_pid("srv.dock_pid", pid_nxui);
331:    } else {
332:        print("[Init] Failed to spawn Dock!\n");
333:    }
334:
335:    /* Spawn Top Bar (nxbar) — classic X11-style status bar */
336:    printf("[Init] Spawning Top Bar (nxbar)...\n");
337:    int pid_nxbar = spawn("/sys/bin/nxbar");
338:    if (pid_nxbar > 0) {
339:        printf("[Init] nxbar started (PID %d)\n", pid_nxbar);
340:        register_service_pid("srv.bar_pid", pid_nxbar);
341:    } else {
342:        print("[Init] Failed to spawn nxbar!\n");
343:    }
344:
345:    /* pid_nxlauncher is declared unconditionally so the supervisor's wait() call
346:     * below compiles regardless of LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART; when the gate is off we
347:     * pin it to 0 so process_wait() returns -2 (gone) and no respawn fires. */
348:    int pid_nxlauncher = 0;
349:#if LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART
350:    /* Spawn the launcher AFTER the dock so the dock's tiles stay on top of the
351:     * launcher's full-screen grid (LAUNCHER-01 #138 — always-on-bottom).  The
352:     * launcher also gets the per-path preset ROOT authority; it needs to
353:     * acquire WINDOW caps to spawn user apps from its tiles. */
354:    printf("[Init] Spawning Launcher (nxlauncher)...\n");
355:    pid_nxlauncher = spawn("/sys/bin/nxlauncher");
356:    if (pid_nxlauncher > 0) {
357:        printf("[Init] Launcher started (PID %d)\n", pid_nxlauncher);
358:        register_service_pid("srv.launcher_pid", pid_nxlauncher);
359:    } else {
360:        print("[Init] Failed to spawn Launcher!\n");
361:    }
362:#endif
363:
364:    /* Spawn Shell */
365:    printf("[Init] Spawning Nxshell...\n");
366:    int pid_shell = spawn("/sys/bin/nxshell");
367:    if (pid_shell > 0) {
368:        printf("[Init] NXShell started (PID %d)\n", pid_shell);
369:    } else {
370:        print("[Init] Failed to spawn NXShell!\n");
371:    }
372:
373:    /* Crea il file /etc/utmp per supportare `who`, `logname`, ecc. */
374:    create_utmp_file();
375:
376:    flush();
377:
378:    /* The "Boot Complete" notification is sent from the supervisor loop below,
379:     * NOT here: notify() resolves the target from the registry key
380:     * "srv.notify_pid", which notify_srv writes only AFTER it has created its
381:     * window and is ready to recv(). Sending immediately raced that write — the
382:     * message went to the fallback PID and was lost, so the popup never appeared
383:     * at boot. We now wait for the key to exist, then send exactly once. */
384:    int boot_notified = 0;
385:
386:    /* Supervisor loop: Monitor and respawn critical processes.
387:     *
388:     * wait(pid) maps to _sys_wait which calls kernel process_wait().
389:     * process_wait() is NON-BLOCKING and a PURE REPORTER:
390:     *   returns -1  if the named process is still alive,
391:     *   returns pid if the process is a corpse not yet drained by the
392:     *               scheduler's reaper,
393:     *   returns -2  if not found — either it never existed or it was ALREADY
394:     *               auto-reaped by schedule() (the kernel frees corpses on its
395:     *               own since the zombie-leak fix; a victim killed while
396:     *               parked is freed immediately and never appears as a
397:     *               waitable corpse).
398:     * Both pid and -2 therefore mean "child is gone": testing only ==pid made
399:     * the respawn a race against the kernel reaper (won on some boots/arches,
400:     * lost on others — the amd64 no-respawn report).
401:     *
402:     * NOTE(USR-INIT-01): This is a correct poll loop.  PIDs are monotonic
403:     * (next_pid, process.c) so a respawned service can never collide with the
404:     * surviving service's PID.  A failed spawn (pid <= 0) also yields -2 and
405:     * is retried on the next iteration.
406:     *
407:     * USR-INIT-03 (FIXED 2026-07-18): respawns were RATE LIMITED.  Previously a
408:     * service that crashed immediately was respawned on every supervisor
409:     * iteration; a single broken service therefore consumed the process table and
410:     * took the whole system down.  That is not theoretical — a one-line format
411:     * bug in the dock produced 28 respawns in a row and ended in a kernel panic,
412:     * which is how this was found.
413:     *
414:     * USR-INIT-04 (FIXED 2026-07-18): USR-INIT-03's fix was a flat LIFETIME
415:     * counter (respawns[slot] > 5 => gaveup[slot] = 1, forever).  That traded an
416:     * amplifying crash loop for a permanent one: six isolated crashes hours
417:     * apart — nothing in common, each one fully recovered from — permanently
418:     * killed the service with no further attempt, because the counter only ever
419:     * counted UP and "gaveup" never cleared.  For a MANDATORY service (dock,
420:     * execsvc, notify_srv) that is worse than the tight loop it replaced: at
421:     * least the tight loop kept the service reachable eventually.
422:     *
423:     * Fix: a small per-service SPAWN QUEUE with DECAYING exponential backoff
424:     * instead of a lifetime budget.
425:     *   - A dead service is not respawned inline; service_gone() enqueues a
426:     *     request (spawnq_request) with a "not before" deadline, and the queue
427:     *     is drained (spawnq_due) once per tick — this is what lets a boot storm
428:     *     of several simultaneous deaths get staggered instead of all firing
429:     *     spawn() back-to-back in the same 33 ms tick.
430:     *   - The backoff for a slot DOUBLES (capped at SPAWN_BACKOFF_MAX_MS) only
431:     *     when the service dies again before SPAWN_STABLE_MS of uptime — that is
432:     *     the actual crash-loop signature USR-INIT-03 was reacting to.
433:     *   - A service that survives >= SPAWN_STABLE_MS since its last (re)spawn is
434:     *     "recovered": its backoff resets to the base delay, so an occasional,
435:     *     unrelated crash months apart is never penalized by history.
436:     *   - There is no "gaveup" state.  A service stuck in a genuine crash loop
437:     *     is retried forever at the SPAWN_BACKOFF_MAX_MS ceiling — that ceiling
438:     *     is what bounds the amplification (28 respawns/tick -> at most one
439:     *     spawn per 30 s), without ever leaving a mandatory service dark.
440:     */
441:#define SPAWN_BACKOFF_BASE_MS                                                  \
442:  200 /* first retry: fast, matches the old immediate-respawn feel */
443:#define SPAWN_BACKOFF_MAX_MS                                                   \
444:  30000 /* ceiling: worst case one attempt every 30s, never zero */
445:#define SPAWN_STABLE_MS                                                        \
446:  10000 /* alive this long since last (re)spawn -> backoff resets */
447:#define SPAWN_QUEUE_MAX                                                        \
448:  8 /* one slot per supervised service, same indexing as before */
449:
450:    struct spawn_req {
451:        int pending; /* 1 if a respawn is currently queued for this slot */
452:        unsigned long long
453:            not_before_ms; /* queue drains this request once now_ms >= this */
454:        int backoff_ms;    /* current backoff for this slot; doubles on fast repeat
455:                              deaths */
456:        unsigned long long
457:            last_spawn_ms; /* when this slot was last (re)spawned; 0 = never yet */
458:    };
459:    static struct spawn_req spawnq[SPAWN_QUEUE_MAX];
460:    for (int i = 0; i < SPAWN_QUEUE_MAX; i++) {
461:        spawnq[i].pending = 0;
462:        spawnq[i].not_before_ms = 0;
463:        spawnq[i].backoff_ms = SPAWN_BACKOFF_BASE_MS;
464:        spawnq[i].last_spawn_ms = 0;
465:    }
466:    unsigned long long now_ms = os1_mono_ns() / 1000000ULL;
467:
468:    /* Seed last_spawn_ms for the services already brought up above, so a fast
469:     * crash-loop that starts right at boot is detected on its FIRST death
470:     * instead of getting one free "isolated failure" reset (last_spawn_ms==0 is
471:     * the sentinel spawnq_request() below treats as "never tracked yet"). */
472:    if (pid_notify > 0)
473:        spawnq[0].last_spawn_ms = now_ms;
474:    if (pid_execsvc > 0)
475:        spawnq[1].last_spawn_ms = now_ms;
476:    if (pid_nxui > 0)
477:        spawnq[2].last_spawn_ms = now_ms;
478:    if (pid_nxbar > 0)
479:        spawnq[3].last_spawn_ms = now_ms;
480:    if (pid_nxlauncher > 0)
481:        spawnq[4].last_spawn_ms = now_ms;
482:#ifndef LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART
483:    if (pid_shell > 0)
484:        spawnq[5].last_spawn_ms = now_ms;
485:#endif
486:
487:    /* spawnq_enqueue - queue a (re)spawn for `slot` and choose its delay.
488:     *
489:     * `penalise` forces the backoff to GROW instead of measuring uptime.  It is
490:     * set when the spawn() ITSELF failed, which has no uptime to measure: with
491:     * the uptime rule alone, `now_ms - last_spawn_ms` is large in that case, so
492:     * every failed attempt reads as an "isolated failure", resets to the base
493:     * delay, and the slot is retried five times a second forever.  That is the
494:     * amplification USR-INIT-03 was written to stop, coming back through the
495:     * other door — a missing or unloadable binary is precisely the case that
496:     * never sets last_spawn_ms at all. */
497:#define spawnq_enqueue(slot, name, penalise)                                   \
498:  do {                                                                         \
499:    struct spawn_req *q = &spawnq[slot];                                       \
500:    unsigned long long uptime = now_ms - q->last_spawn_ms;                     \
501:    if (!(penalise) && (q->last_spawn_ms == 0 || uptime >= SPAWN_STABLE_MS)) { \
502:      q->backoff_ms =                                                          \
503:          SPAWN_BACKOFF_BASE_MS; /* isolated failure: full reset */            \
504:    } else {                                                                   \
505:      q->backoff_ms *= 2;                                                      \
506:      if (q->backoff_ms > SPAWN_BACKOFF_MAX_MS)                                \
507:        q->backoff_ms = SPAWN_BACKOFF_MAX_MS;                                  \
508:      printf("[Init] %s is not staying up — next attempt in %d ms "            \
509:             "(retrying, not giving up; see USR-INIT-04)\n",                   \
510:             name, q->backoff_ms);                                             \
511:    }                                                                          \
512:    q->pending = 1;                                                            \
513:    q->not_before_ms = now_ms + q->backoff_ms;                                 \
514:  } while (0)
515:
516:    /* spawnq_idle - nothing queued for this slot, so it is worth PROBING.
517:     *
518:     * The probe must be gated on this, because service_gone() PRINTS on every
519:     * call and a queued request stays queued for its whole backoff — up to
520:     * SPAWN_BACKOFF_MAX_MS.  Probing unconditionally therefore reported the same
521:     * death once per 33 ms tick, up to ~900 identical lines per backoff cycle,
522:     * into the console the user is trying to read.  It also re-consulted a status
523:     * the kernel had already handed over: the Phase 9b reaped-status ring is
524:     * consume-on-read, so only the first probe carries real information and every
525:     * later one degrades to the anonymous "gone" branch. */
526:#define spawnq_idle(slot) (!spawnq[slot].pending)
527:
528:    /* spawnq_due - true exactly once when a queued request's backoff has
529:     * elapsed; clears `pending` so the caller's spawn() only fires once per
530:     * request.  The caller MUST then call spawnq_mark_spawned() on success, or
531:     * spawnq_enqueue(..., 1) on failure — the request has already been consumed,
532:     * so a slot that does neither is never retried. */
533:#define spawnq_due(slot)                                                       \
534:  (spawnq[slot].pending && now_ms >= spawnq[slot].not_before_ms                \
535:       ? (spawnq[slot].pending = 0, 1)                                         \
536:       : 0)
537:
538:#define spawnq_mark_spawned(slot) (spawnq[slot].last_spawn_ms = now_ms)
539:
540:    print("[Init] Entering supervisor loop\n");
541:    while (1) {
542:        /* One clock read per tick: every spawnq_* call below uses this now_ms, so
543:         * a whole supervisor pass is internally consistent even though several
544:         * services may be checked/spawned in the same iteration. */
545:        now_ms = os1_mono_ns() / 1000000ULL;
546:
547:        /* Fire the boot notification once notify_srv has registered its endpoint
548:         * (srv.notify_pid present in the registry). This makes the popup actually
549:         * appear at startup instead of racing notify_srv's registration. */
550:        if (!boot_notified) {
551:            char npid[16];
552:            if (OS1_registry_get("srv.notify_pid", npid, sizeof(npid)) == 0) {
553:                notify("System", "Boot Complete - NEXS");
554:                boot_notified = 1;
555:            }
556:        }
557:
558:        /* Check if notification server died and respawn. */
559:        if (spawnq_idle(0) && service_gone(pid_notify, "Notification Server"))
560:            spawnq_enqueue(0, "Notification Server", 0);
561:        if (spawnq_due(0)) {
562:            pid_notify = spawn("/sys/bin/nxntfy_srv");
563:            /* Refresh srv.notify_pid to the LIVE pid.  Without this, the registry key
564:             * still holds the corpse's pid and every notify_post returns -ESRCH until
565:             * a reboot.  Re-registering on respawn also overwrites any hijack a
566:             * malicious process may have written in the meantime. */
567:            if (pid_notify > 0) {
568:                register_service_pid("srv.notify_pid", pid_notify);
569:                spawnq_mark_spawned(0);
570:            } else {
571:                spawnq_enqueue(0, "Notification Server", 1);
572:            }
573:        }
574:#ifndef LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART
575:        /* Respawn the shell when it is gone (freshly dead corpse OR already
576:         * reaped by the kernel).  spawn() assigns a fresh monotonic PID. */
577:        if (spawnq_idle(5) && service_gone(pid_shell, "NXShell"))
578:            spawnq_enqueue(5, "NXShell", 0);
579:        if (spawnq_due(5)) {
580:            pid_shell = spawn("/sys/bin/nxshell");
581:            if (pid_shell > 0)
582:                spawnq_mark_spawned(5);
583:            else
584:                spawnq_enqueue(5, "NXShell", 1);
585:        }
586:#endif
587:
588:        /* Respawn the execution service.  Nothing to re-register: clients
589:         * rediscover it by PORT NAME, and the new instance re-publishes OS1nx_exec
590:         * by taking the receive right — so a respawn heals discovery automatically,
591:         * with no stale-pid window of the kind srv.notify_pid has to guard against.
592:         * (The new instance RETRIES that claim briefly, because the dead one's
593:         * receive handle is still being torn down when we get here — see
594:         * nxexec_service().)
595:         */
596:        if (spawnq_idle(1) && service_gone(pid_execsvc, "Execution Service"))
597:            spawnq_enqueue(1, "Execution Service", 0);
598:        if (spawnq_due(1)) {
599:            char *rargv[2];
600:            rargv[0] = (char *)"/sys/bin/nxexec";
601:            rargv[1] = (char *)"--service";
602:            pid_execsvc = spawn_args("/sys/bin/nxexec", 2, rargv);
603:            if (pid_execsvc > 0)
604:                spawnq_mark_spawned(1);
605:            else
606:                spawnq_enqueue(1, "Execution Service", 1);
607:        }
608:
609:        /* Respawn the dock if it dies (ROOT via the /sys/bin path preset, as
610:         * above).  Refresh srv.dock_pid on respawn — same corpse-pid hazard as
611:         * srv.notify_pid above. */
612:        if (spawnq_idle(2) && service_gone(pid_nxui, "Dock"))
613:            spawnq_enqueue(2, "Dock", 0);
614:        if (spawnq_due(2)) {
615:            pid_nxui = spawn("/sys/bin/nxui");
616:            if (pid_nxui > 0) {
617:                register_service_pid("srv.dock_pid", pid_nxui);
618:                spawnq_mark_spawned(2);
619:            } else {
620:                spawnq_enqueue(2, "Dock", 1);
621:            }
622:        }
623:        /* Respawn nxbar if it dies */
624:        if (spawnq_idle(3) && service_gone(pid_nxbar, "nxbar"))
625:            spawnq_enqueue(3, "nxbar", 0);
626:        if (spawnq_due(3)) {
627:            pid_nxbar = spawn("/sys/bin/nxbar");
628:            if (pid_nxbar > 0) {
629:                register_service_pid("srv.bar_pid", pid_nxbar);
630:                spawnq_mark_spawned(3);
631:            } else {
632:                spawnq_enqueue(3, "nxbar", 1);
633:            }
634:        }
635:
636:#if LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART
637:        /* Respawn the launcher.  Initial pid comes from the spawn above; if
638:         * LAUNCHER_AUTOSTART is disabled we never set pid_nxlauncher, so the
639:         * wait() on a stale handle would otherwise busy-loop — the #else keeps
640:         * the variable pinned to 0 so process_wait() returns -2 (gone). */
641:        if (spawnq_idle(4) && service_gone(pid_nxlauncher, "Launcher"))
642:            spawnq_enqueue(4, "Launcher", 0);
643:        if (spawnq_due(4)) {
644:            pid_nxlauncher = spawn("/sys/bin/nxlauncher");
645:            if (pid_nxlauncher > 0) {
646:                register_service_pid("srv.launcher_pid", pid_nxlauncher);
647:                spawnq_mark_spawned(4);
648:            } else {
649:                spawnq_enqueue(4, "Launcher", 1);
650:            }
651:        }
652:#endif
653:
654:        /* NOTE(GFX-DYN-01): host display-change auto-resize is intentionally NOT
655:         * polled here — a per-iteration poll wastes cycles.  It will be re-added
656:         * event-driven (virtio-gpu display-change IRQ → deferred handler).  The
657:         * manual path (nxres / SYS_SET_DISPLAY_MODE) remains.  SYS_DISPLAY_POLL is
658:         * kept for that future event-driven caller. */
659:
660:        /* SCHED-STACK-ISO (ASTRA DIR-02): DRIVE THE COMPOSITOR RENDER from here, in
661:         * process context, instead of the kernel timer IRQ.  Running the heavy
662:         * render from the tick nested it on an arbitrary interrupted task's kernel
663:         * stack and smashed live frames on other CPUs (the amd64 click/nanosleep
664:         * panic and the aarch64 current_chip #PF).  flush() ->
665:         * SYS_COMPOSITOR_RENDER runs the render on init's OWN kernel stack — never
666:         * nested.  The render is damage-clipped, so an idle pass with nothing dirty
667:         * is cheap.  ~30 FPS pacing (33 ms) matches the old tick cadence. */
668:        flush();
669:
670:        /* Sleep between supervisor passes.  33 ms ≈ 30 FPS: init is the
671:         * compositor's frame pump now, so the desktop refresh cadence lives here.
672:         * With the real kernel timer (SYS_NANOSLEEP) init is descheduled between
673:         * frames (~0% CPU at idle) and woken by its core's tick. */
674:        OS1_sleep(33);
675:    }
676:    return 0;
677:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxjobs.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXJOBS_H
2:#define _USER_NXJOBS_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxjobs.h
6: * NEXS shell job table (ASTRA service layer) — "job control, light".
7: *
8: * Tracks pids launched in the BACKGROUND (`cmd &`) and jobs suspended with
9: * Ctrl-Z, so `jobs`/`fg`/`bg` have something to operate on.
10: *
11: *   - background (&), jobs, fg   A background job is a spawned pid the shell
12: *     chose not to wait() on immediately; nxjobs_poll() drains SYS_WAIT
13: *     non-blockingly each loop tick to notice when one finishes.
14: *
15: *   - suspend (Ctrl-Z), bg, fg   REAL since Phase 2: the scheduler has a
16: *     PROC_STOPPED state with process_stop/process_cont behind the
17: *     DESTROY-gated OBJ_CTL_STOP/CONT verbs, so a stopped job genuinely
18: *     stops and genuinely resumes.
19: *
20: *   - exit status                REAL since Phase 2/9b: waitpid() carries a
21: *     POSIX status that survives reaping, so a job reports "Done (N)" or
22: *     "Killed (N)", not a bare "Done".
23: *
24: * (This header used to state the opposite for the last two — written before
25: * the kernel work landed and never updated.  The stale text was quoted back
26: * as fact by a later review, so it is corrected here rather than deleted:
27: * PLAN-2026-07-17 §"Known live bugs" records that failure mode.)
28: *
29: * Job SELECTION follows POSIX XCU §2.9.3.1 — see nxjobs_resolve().
30: */
31:
32:#include "nxexec.h" /* nxexec_window_stable() — the single shared debounce
33:                      * also used by nxexec_run_foreground() and nxexec.c's
34:                      * grace probe, see nxjobs_poll() below. */
35:#include <os1.h>
36:#include <string.h>
37:#include <sys/wait.h> /* WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS/WIFSIGNALED — Phase 2 real status */
38:
39:#define NXJOBS_MAX 16
40:#define NXJOBS_CMD_MAX 64
41:
42:enum { NXJOB_RUNNING = 0, NXJOB_DONE = 1, NXJOB_STOPPED = 2 };
43:
44:struct nxjob {
45:  int in_use;
46:  int id; /* 1-based, stable for the job's lifetime (the "%1" in fg %1) */
47:  int pid;
48:  int state;
49:  int status; /* POSIX wait status once NXJOB_DONE (Phase 2): WEXITSTATUS /
50:               * WIFSIGNALED decode it — "Done (N)" vs "Killed". */
51:  char cmd[NXJOBS_CMD_MAX];
52:  /* Debounce state for the "did this background job turn out to be a GUI
53:   * app?" test in nxjobs_poll() — same shape as nxexec_run_foreground()'s
54:   * local last_win/stable, just kept per-slot since nxjobs_poll() checks
55:   * every tracked job on a single shared tick instead of blocking on one. */
56:  int win_last;
57:  int win_stable;
58:};
59:
60:struct nxjobs {
61:  struct nxjob slot[NXJOBS_MAX];
62:  int next_id;
63:  /* POSIX current/previous job (`%%`/`%+` and `%-`, and what a bare `fg`/`bg`
64:   * operates on).  Stored as IDS and updated on the EVENTS that define them,
65:   * because "most recently stopped" is not recoverable from the table's state:
66:   * with two stopped jobs, nothing in the slots says which stopped last. */
67:  int current_id;
68:  int previous_id;
69:};
70:
71:static inline void nxjobs_init(struct nxjobs *j) {
72:  memset(j, 0, sizeof(*j));
73:  j->next_id = 1;
74:}
75:
76:/* __nxjobs_slot_of_id - slot for `id`, but only if it still names a job that
77: * can be foregrounded.  A finished job is deliberately NOT eligible: it is
78: * about to leave the table, and selecting a corpse is not a selection. */
79:static inline int __nxjobs_slot_of_id(struct nxjobs *j, int id) {
80:  if (id <= 0)
81:    return -1;
82:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++)
83:    if (j->slot[i].in_use && j->slot[i].id == id &&
84:        j->slot[i].state != NXJOB_DONE)
85:      return i;
86:  return -1;
87:}
88:
89:/* __nxjobs_pick - the POSIX current-job RULE, applied from scratch.
90: *
91: * "the most recently stopped job, or, if there are no stopped jobs, the most
92: * recently started background job".  `skip_id` asks for the next one down,
93: * which is how the previous job is chosen.  Used only to REBUILD the ids after
94: * the job they named went away — the event-driven path above is what makes
95: * "most recently stopped" mean the right thing while both jobs are stopped. */
96:static inline int __nxjobs_pick(struct nxjobs *j, int skip_id) {
97:  for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++) {
98:    int want = (pass == 0) ? NXJOB_STOPPED : NXJOB_RUNNING;
99:    int best = -1;
100:    for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
101:      if (!j->slot[i].in_use || j->slot[i].state != want)
102:        continue;
103:      if (j->slot[i].id == skip_id)
104:        continue;
105:      if (best < 0 || j->slot[i].id > j->slot[best].id)
106:        best = i;
107:    }
108:    if (best >= 0)
109:      return best;
110:  }
111:  return -1;
112:}
113:
114:/* __nxjobs_resync - drop current/previous ids that no longer name an eligible
115: * job and refill them from the rule.  Called before every resolution, so a job
116: * finishing or being disowned cannot leave `fg` pointing at nothing. */
117:static inline void __nxjobs_resync(struct nxjobs *j) {
118:  if (__nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->current_id) < 0)
119:    j->current_id = 0;
120:  if (__nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->previous_id) < 0)
121:    j->previous_id = 0;
122:  if (j->current_id == 0) {
123:    int s = __nxjobs_pick(j, j->previous_id);
124:    j->current_id = (s >= 0) ? j->slot[s].id : 0;
125:  }
126:  if (j->previous_id == 0) {
127:    int s = __nxjobs_pick(j, j->current_id);
128:    j->previous_id = (s >= 0) ? j->slot[s].id : 0;
129:  }
130:}
131:
132:/* __nxjobs_promote - `id` becomes the current job, the old current becomes the
133: * previous one.  This is the only way current_id is set on the happy path: it
134: * is called when a job is started in the background and when one is stopped,
135: * which are exactly the two events POSIX defines the current job by. */
136:static inline void __nxjobs_promote(struct nxjobs *j, int id) {
137:  if (id <= 0 || id == j->current_id)
138:    return;
139:  j->previous_id = j->current_id;
140:  j->current_id = id;
141:}
142:
143:/* nxjobs_add - register a newly-spawned BACKGROUND pid. Returns the job id
144: * (>=1), or 0 if the table is full (the process still runs, it's just
145: * untracked by `jobs`/`fg` — never a reason to refuse the spawn itself). */
146:static inline int nxjobs_add(struct nxjobs *j, int pid, const char *cmd) {
147:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
148:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use) {
149:      j->slot[i].in_use = 1;
150:      j->slot[i].id = j->next_id++;
151:      j->slot[i].pid = pid;
152:      j->slot[i].state = NXJOB_RUNNING;
153:      j->slot[i].status = 0;
154:      j->slot[i].win_last = -1;
155:      j->slot[i].win_stable = 0;
156:      snprintf(j->slot[i].cmd, NXJOBS_CMD_MAX, "%s", cmd);
157:      __nxjobs_promote(j, j->slot[i].id); /* POSIX: a new background job is
158:                                           * the current job */
159:      return j->slot[i].id;
160:    }
161:  }
162:  return 0;
163:}
164:
165:/* nxjobs_mark_stopped - record that a job has been suspended.
166: *
167: * Separate from nxjobs_stop() because Ctrl-Z is detected by the foreground
168: * watcher, which has already suspended the process — only the bookkeeping is
169: * left.  Both paths must come through here, though, because a stopped job
170: * becomes the CURRENT job, and a shell where Ctrl-Z did not change what a bare
171: * `fg` resumes is the one thing job control has to get right. */
172:static inline void nxjobs_mark_stopped(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
173:  if (slot < 0 || slot >= NXJOBS_MAX || !j->slot[slot].in_use)
174:    return;
175:  j->slot[slot].state = NXJOB_STOPPED;
176:  __nxjobs_promote(j, j->slot[slot].id);
177:}
178:
179:/* nxjobs_reap - drop a job from the table (finished, or just promoted to
180: * the foreground and waited on directly). Defined ahead of nxjobs_poll()
181: * since that now calls it directly (windowed-handoff case) rather than only
182: * being called from nxshell.c's `fg` path. */
183:static inline void nxjobs_reap(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
184:  if (slot >= 0 && slot < NXJOBS_MAX)
185:    j->slot[slot].in_use = 0;
186:}
187:
188:/* nxjobs_poll - non-blocking refresh of every tracked job's state. wait()
189: * (OS1low_process_wait / SYS_WAIT) is itself non-blocking (-1 = still
190: * running), so this is cheap to call once per shell loop tick.
191: *
192: * A background job ('cmd &') is spawned through the same non-detached path
193: * as a foreground one (nxexec_spawn_search(..., detached=0) in nxshell.c),
194: * so it never goes through nxexec_run_foreground()'s own window-ownership
195: * debounce — nothing ever told nxjobs a backgrounded child turned out to be
196: * a GUI app.  Left unchecked, such a job sits in the table as "Running"
197: * forever (wait() never returns non-(-1) for it — it only ever exits when
198: * the user closes its window, which nxjobs has no way to notice either),
199: * a phantom entry that both `jobs` misreports and `fg`/reap can never
200: * clean up.  Uses the same nxexec_window_stable() debounce nxexec.h's own
201: * watchers use (single source of truth for the threshold/reset rule) on a
202: * per-slot basis instead of blocking: once a job's window id is stable
203: * across NXEXEC_STABLE_POLLS ticks, it is handed off — reaped from this
204: * table without ever appearing as "Done" (it isn't dead, it just left the
205: * shell's job-control domain for nxwins/dock's, per nxexec.h's ownership
206: * model). */
207:static inline void nxjobs_poll(struct nxjobs *j) {
208:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
209:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use || j->slot[i].state != NXJOB_RUNNING)
210:      continue;
211:
212:    if (nxexec_window_stable(j->slot[i].pid, &j->slot[i].win_last,
213:                             &j->slot[i].win_stable)) {
214:      nxjobs_reap(j, i); /* handed off to nxwins/dock; not "Done" */
215:      continue;
216:    }
217:
218:    /* Standard waitpid (Phase 2): WNOHANG poll, real POSIX status. r>0 reaped
219:     * (status valid), r==-1 gone (reaped elsewhere), r==0 still running. */
220:    int status = 0;
221:    int r = waitpid(j->slot[i].pid, &status, WNOHANG);
222:    if (r != 0) {
223:      j->slot[i].status = (r > 0) ? status : 0;
224:      j->slot[i].state = NXJOB_DONE;
225:    }
226:  }
227:}
228:
229:/* nxjobs_find - look up a job by its %N (or bare N) id. Returns the slot
230: * index, or -1 if not found. */
231:static inline int nxjobs_find(struct nxjobs *j, int id) {
232:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++)
233:    if (j->slot[i].in_use && j->slot[i].id == id)
234:      return i;
235:  return -1;
236:}
237:
238:/* nxjobs_print - `jobs` builtin body.
239: *
240: * The current job is marked '+' and the previous one '-', as POSIX specifies:
241: * without them the output does not say what a bare `fg` would act on, which is
242: * the only reason a user needs to read it before typing one. */
243:static inline void nxjobs_print(struct nxjobs *j) {
244:  int any = 0;
245:  __nxjobs_resync(j);
246:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
247:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use)
248:      continue;
249:    any = 1;
250:    char mark = (j->slot[i].id == j->current_id)    ? '+'
251:                : (j->slot[i].id == j->previous_id) ? '-'
252:                                                    : ' ';
253:    const char *st;
254:    char stbuf[24];
255:    if (j->slot[i].state == NXJOB_RUNNING) {
256:      st = "Running";
257:    } else if (j->slot[i].state == NXJOB_STOPPED) {
258:      st = "Stopped";
259:    } else { /* NXJOB_DONE: decode the real POSIX status (Phase 2) */
260:      int s = j->slot[i].status;
261:      if (WIFSIGNALED(s))
262:        snprintf(stbuf, sizeof(stbuf), "Killed (%d)", WTERMSIG(s));
263:      else
264:        snprintf(stbuf, sizeof(stbuf), "Done (%d)", WEXITSTATUS(s));
265:      st = stbuf;
266:    }
267:    printf("[%d]%c %-12s pid=%-6d %s\n", j->slot[i].id, mark, st,
268:           j->slot[i].pid, j->slot[i].cmd);
269:  }
270:  if (!any)
271:    print("No background jobs.\n");
272:}
273:
274:/* nxjobs_parse_id - parse a `fg`/`bg` argument in either "%3" or "3" form.
275: * Returns the id, or -1 if arg isn't a valid job reference. */
276:static inline int nxjobs_parse_id(const char *arg) {
277:  if (!arg || !*arg)
278:    return -1;
279:  if (arg[0] == '%')
280:    arg++;
281:  if (!*arg)
282:    return -1;
283:  int id = atoi(arg);
284:  return id > 0 ? id : -1;
285:}
286:
287:/* __nxjobs_match - most recent job whose command matches `s`, by prefix or
288: * (with `anywhere`) by substring.  POSIX `%string` and `%?string`. */
289:static inline int __nxjobs_match(struct nxjobs *j, const char *s, int anywhere) {
290:  if (!s || !*s)
291:    return -1;
292:  size_t len = strlen(s);
293:  int best = -1;
294:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
295:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use)
296:      continue;
297:    int hit = anywhere ? (strstr(j->slot[i].cmd, s) != (char *)0)
298:                       : (strncmp(j->slot[i].cmd, s, len) == 0);
299:    if (hit && (best < 0 || j->slot[i].id > j->slot[best].id))
300:      best = i;
301:  }
302:  return best;
303:}
304:
305:/*
306: * nxjobs_resolve - turn a `fg`/`bg`/`disown` operand into a slot index.
307: *
308: * POSIX job_id syntax (XCU §2.9.3.1), which this now actually implements:
309: *
310: *   (omitted)  the CURRENT job
311: *   %% or %+   the current job          %-        the previous job
312: *   %N         job number N             %string   job whose command starts
313: *   %?string   ...whose command contains string     with string
314: *
315: * TWO CORRECTIONS, 2026-07-23:
316: *
317: * 1. A bare `fg` used to take "the highest job id still in the table"
318: *    (nxjobs_last).  That is not the current job and, worse, the table
319: *    includes FINISHED jobs — so `fg` could resume nothing, and Ctrl-Z'ing a
320: *    job did not change what a bare `fg` would bring back.  It now follows the
321: *    real rule: most recently stopped, else most recently backgrounded, never
322: *    a finished one.  Omitting the operand IS standard; picking the wrong job
323: *    for it was not.
324: *
325: * 2. A BARE NAME (`fg lua`, no `%`) used to resolve by command prefix.  That
326: *    is not a job id in any shell — `lua` there is a command name, and
327: *    accepting it means `fg` silently guesses when the user meant something
328: *    else.  Removed; `fg %lua` is the spelling.  A bare NUMBER stays: `fg 1`
329: *    for `%1` is the one extension every shell accepts.
330: *
331: * Returns the slot, or -1 if the operand names no job.
332: */
333:static inline int nxjobs_resolve(struct nxjobs *j, const char *arg) {
334:  __nxjobs_resync(j);
335:
336:  if (!arg || !*arg)
337:    return __nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->current_id);
338:
339:  if (arg[0] != '%') {
340:    for (const char *p = arg; *p; p++)
341:      if (*p < '0' || *p > '9')
342:        return -1; /* a bare name is a command, not a job id */
343:    return nxjobs_find(j, atoi(arg));
344:  }
345:
346:  arg++;
347:  if (!*arg)
348:    return -1; /* a lone "%" names nothing */
349:  if (arg[0] == '%' || arg[0] == '+')
350:    return __nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->current_id);
351:  if (arg[0] == '-')
352:    return __nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->previous_id);
353:  if (arg[0] == '?')
354:    return __nxjobs_match(j, arg + 1, 1);
355:
356:  int numeric = 1;
357:  for (const char *p = arg; *p; p++)
358:    if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') {
359:      numeric = 0;
360:      break;
361:    }
362:  if (numeric)
363:    return nxjobs_find(j, atoi(arg));
364:  return __nxjobs_match(j, arg, 0);
365:}
366:
367:/* nxjobs_stop - suspend a job (Ctrl-Z / `stop %N`): kernel PROC_STOPPED via
368: * OS1_process_stop, then mark it Stopped so `jobs` reflects it and `bg`/`fg`
369: * can resume it (Phase 2 — a real stopped state exists now). */
370:static inline int nxjobs_stop(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
371:  if (slot < 0 || slot >= NXJOBS_MAX || !j->slot[slot].in_use)
372:    return -1;
373:  int r = OS1_process_stop(j->slot[slot].pid);
374:  if (r == 0)
375:    nxjobs_mark_stopped(j, slot); /* also makes it the current job */
376:  return r;
377:}
378:
379:/* nxjobs_cont - resume a stopped job in the BACKGROUND (`bg`): OS1_process_cont
380: * + mark Running.  For `fg`, the caller conts and then waits in the foreground.
381: * Returns 0, or a negative errno (e.g. the job was not stopped). */
382:static inline int nxjobs_cont(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
383:  if (slot < 0 || slot >= NXJOBS_MAX || !j->slot[slot].in_use)
384:    return -1;
385:  int r = OS1_process_cont(j->slot[slot].pid);
386:  if (r == 0 && j->slot[slot].state == NXJOB_STOPPED)
387:    j->slot[slot].state = NXJOB_RUNNING;
388:  return r;
389:}
390:
391:#endif /* _USER_NXJOBS_H */

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxlauncher.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxlauncher.c
3: * NEXS launcher — a normal, resizable compositor window with a tile grid
4: * sized to its OWN dimensions, not to the desktop.
5: *
6: * Unlike a classic pinned-at-bottom launcher, this one opens as a regular
7: * window (with the native titlebar) in the centre of the desktop at half the
8: * screen size.  The user drags/resizes it freely via the titlebar border;
9: * the grid (cols x rows) is recomputed from the window's current w/h on every
10: * resize event, so the layout adapts naturally.
11: *
12: * Tile geometry matches nxui's dock (TILE=40, TILE_RADIUS=6, TILE_GAP=12) so
13: * the launcher and the dock read as one design family.
14: *
15: * App discovery (no hardcoded app list, no hardcoded folder list):
16: *   The root view contains EXACTLY TWO folders:
17: *     - "System" → contents of /sys/bin  (filtered)
18: *     - "User"   → contents of /bin      (filtered)
19: *   Each folder is scanned live from the filesystem on startup.  Every entry
20: *   whose name ends in one of the filtered extensions (".wad", ".txt",
21: *   ".png", ".cfg", ".dat", ".md", ".json") is SKIPPED; "." and ".." are
22: *   ALWAYS skipped so the user never has to think about them — instead, a
23: *   DRAWN back-arrow button at the top of the folder view returns to the
24: *   root (the compositor gives us a ".." replacement we own).
25: *
26: *   The optional $HOME/settings/nxlauncher.cfg can append extra entries or
27: *   pin labels, but the root view itself never changes shape — there is no
28: *   way to expose a top-level app that is not under one of the two folders.
29: *
30: * Window events handled:
31: *   - INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE (left press): hit-test against the per-page slot
32: *     tables; tile click → spawn_args(path); folder tile → enter that
33: *     folder; back arrow → leave folder; arrow buttons → page left/right;
34: *     dot click → jump to page.  AFTER a successful app spawn, the launcher
35: *     auto-minimises itself (OS1_window_minimize) so the spawned app gets
36: *     the focus and the launcher stays available in the dock — the user
37: *     restores it with another dock click.
38: *   - INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE (event-driven): the compositor reports the new
39: *     logical size.  We realloc the ARGB buffer, recompute the layout, and
40: *     force a redraw.
41: *
42: * Resize is also polled via OS1_display_info for the rare host-driven
43: * resolution change.
44: *
45: * Tile icons: each app tile shows a real per-app icon (nxicon.h,
46: * /home/Pictures/icon/{dark,light}, shared with nxui.c's dock) when one is
47: * cached for that executable's basename + the active theme, else the classic
48: * flat per-category color tile (unchanged) — the same corner-rounding code
49: * draws both, see fb_rrect_px().  Folder tiles are untouched
50: * (draw_folder_tile).
51: */

219:/* fb_rrect_px - shared rounded-rect body: one corner-quarter-circle mask
220: * test, one write loop, feeding EITHER a flat color (img == NULL — the
221: * classic per-category tile) or an icon's own pixels (img != NULL, w x h ==
222: * the icon's own dimensions).  Kept as a single function so an icon tile is
223: * rounded by the EXACT same test as every classic tile/back-button/arrow in
224: * this file — no second "icon corner rounding" to keep in sync (same
225: * approach as nxui.c's fb_rrect_px). */
226:static void fb_rrect_px(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint32_t c,
227:                        const uint32_t *img) {
228:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
229:    return;
230:  if (r < 0)
231:    r = 0;
232:  if (r > w / 2)
233:    r = w / 2;
234:  if (r > h / 2)
235:    r = h / 2;
236:
237:  for (int j = 0; j < h; j++) {
238:    for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
239:      // Corner rounding
240:      int ccx = -1, ccy = 0;
241:      if (i < r && j < r) {
242:        ccx = r;
243:        ccy = r;
244:      } else if (i >= w - r && j < r) {
245:        ccx = w - r - 1;
246:        ccy = r;
247:      } else if (i < r && j >= h - r) {
248:        ccx = r;
249:        ccy = h - r - 1;
250:      } else if (i >= w - r && j >= h - r) {
251:        ccx = w - r - 1;
252:        ccy = h - r - 1;
253:      }
254:
255:      if (ccx >= 0) {
256:        int dx = i - ccx, dy = j - ccy;
257:        if (dx * dx + dy * dy > r * r)
258:          continue;
259:      }
260:
261:      int px = x + i;
262:      int py = y + j;
263:      if (px < 0 || px >= g_ww || py < 0 || py >= g_wh)
264:        continue;
265:
266:      if (img) {
267:        uint32_t src = img[j * w + i];
268:        uint8_t alpha = (src >> 24) & 0xFF;
269:
270:        if (alpha == 0)
271:          continue;
272:
273:        if (alpha == 255) {
274:          g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = src;
275:        } else {
276:          uint32_t dst = g_fb[py * g_ww + px];
277:
278:          uint32_t dr = (dst >> 16) & 0xFF;
279:          uint32_t dg = (dst >> 8) & 0xFF;
280:          uint32_t db = dst & 0xFF;
281:
282:          uint32_t sr = (src >> 16) & 0xFF;
283:          uint32_t sg = (src >> 8) & 0xFF;
284:          uint32_t sb = src & 0xFF;
285:
286:          // renamed to avoid shadowing
287:          uint32_t out_r = (sr * alpha + dr * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
288:          uint32_t out_g = (sg * alpha + dg * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
289:          uint32_t out_b = (sb * alpha + db * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
290:
291:          g_fb[py * g_ww + px] =
292:              (0xFF000000u) | (out_r << 16) | (out_g << 8) | out_b;
293:        }
294:      } else {
295:        g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = c;
296:      }
297:    }
298:  }
299:}
300:
301:static void fb_rrect(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint32_t c) {
302:  fb_rrect_px(x, y, w, h, r, c, NULL);
303:}
304:
305:/* fb_icon_border - same 3D bevel ring as nxui.c's dock (see that file for the
306: * full rationale): a brighter top-left arc + dimmer bottom-right arc, white
307: * in dark mode / black in light mode, traced along the icon's own rounded
308: * corners. Icon tiles only — classic flat-colour tiles (folders, etc.) don't
309: * get one. */
310:static void fb_icon_border(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, int light) {
311:  uint32_t base = light ? 0x000000u : 0xFFFFFFu;
312:  if (r < 0)
313:    r = 0;
314:  if (r > w / 2)
315:    r = w / 2;
316:  if (r > h / 2)
317:    r = h / 2;
318:
319:  for (int j = 0; j < h; j++) {
320:    for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
321:      int ccx = -1, ccy = 0;
322:      if (i < r && j < r) {
323:        ccx = r;
324:        ccy = r;
325:      } else if (i >= w - r && j < r) {
326:        ccx = w - r - 1;
327:        ccy = r;
328:      } else if (i < r && j >= h - r) {
329:        ccx = r;
330:        ccy = h - r - 1;
331:      } else if (i >= w - r && j >= h - r) {
332:        ccx = w - r - 1;
333:        ccy = h - r - 1;
334:      }
335:
336:      int on_border;
337:      if (ccx >= 0) {
338:        int dx = i - ccx, dy = j - ccy;
339:        int d2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;
340:        if (d2 > r * r)
341:          continue;
342:        int r_in = r - 1;
343:        on_border = d2 >= r_in * r_in;
344:      } else {
345:        on_border = (i == 0 || i == w - 1 || j == 0 || j == h - 1);
346:      }
347:      if (!on_border)
348:        continue;
349:
350:      int px = x + i, py = y + j;
351:      if (px < 0 || px >= g_ww || py < 0 || py >= g_wh)
352:        continue;
353:
354:      int top_left = (i + j) < (w + h) / 2;
355:      uint32_t alpha = top_left ? 0x60u : 0x30u;
356:
357:      uint32_t dst = g_fb[py * g_ww + px];
358:      uint32_t dr = (dst >> 16) & 0xFF, dg = (dst >> 8) & 0xFF, db = dst & 0xFF;
359:      uint32_t sr = (base >> 16) & 0xFF, sg = (base >> 8) & 0xFF,
360:               sb = base & 0xFF;
361:
362:      uint32_t out_r = (sr * alpha + dr * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
363:      uint32_t out_g = (sg * alpha + dg * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
364:      uint32_t out_b = (sb * alpha + db * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
365:      g_fb[py * g_ww + px] =
366:          (0xFF000000u) | (out_r << 16) | (out_g << 8) | out_b;
367:    }
368:  }
369:}
370:
371:static void fb_circle(int cx, int cy, int r, uint32_t c) {
372:  int r2 = r * r;
373:  for (int j = -r; j <= r; j++) {
374:    for (int i = -r; i <= r; i++) {
375:      if (i * i + j * j <= r2) {
376:        int px = cx + i, py = cy + j;
377:        if (px >= 0 && px < g_ww && py >= 0 && py < g_wh)
378:          g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = c;
379:      }
380:    }
381:  }
382:}
383:
384:/* ============================================================
385: *                      Font rendering on g_fb
386: * ============================================================ */
387:
388:static void buf_draw_glyph(int x, int y, uint32_t codepoint, uint32_t color) {
389:  if (!g_font)
390:    return;
391:
392:  int idx = (int)codepoint - g_font->header.first_char;
393:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= g_font->header.num_chars)
394:    return;
395:
396:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &g_font->glyphs[idx];
397:  uint8_t *bitmap = g_font->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
398:
399:  int start_x = x + gi->x0;
400:  int start_y = y + g_font->header.ascent + gi->y0;
401:
402:  // Disegno diretto pixel per pixel
403:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
404:    for (int gx = 0; gx < gi->width; gx++) {
405:      uint8_t alpha = bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx];
406:
407:      // Se il pixel del font è visibile, lo disegniamo
408:      // Se vuoi gestire l'anti-aliasing, qui puoi fare un alpha blending
409:      if (alpha > 64) {
410:        int px = start_x + gx;
411:        int py = start_y + gy;
412:        if (px >= 0 && px < g_ww && py >= 0 && py < g_wh) {
413:          g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = color;
414:        }
415:      }
416:    }
417:  }
418:}
419:
420:static int buf_text_width(const char *s) {
421:  if (!g_font || !s)
422:    return 0;
423:  return font_string_width(g_font, s);
424:}
425:
426:static void buf_draw_text(int x, int y, const char *s, uint32_t color) {
427:  if (!g_font || !s)
428:    return;
429:  uint32_t cp;
430:  int consumed, cursor = x;
431:  size_t rem = strlen(s);
432:  const char *p = s;
433:  while (*p) {
434:    consumed = utf8_decode(p, rem, &cp);
435:    if (consumed <= 0) {
436:      p++;
437:      rem--;
438:      continue;
439:    }
440:    buf_draw_glyph(cursor, y, cp, color);
441:    int idx = (int)cp - g_font->header.first_char;
442:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < g_font->header.num_chars)
443:      cursor += g_font->glyphs[idx].advance;
444:    p += consumed;
445:    rem -= consumed;
446:  }
447:}
448:
449:static void buf_truncate_to_width(char *s, int max_w) {
450:  if (!g_font || !s || max_w <= 0)
451:    return;
452:  if (buf_text_width(s) <= max_w)
453:    return;
454:  int dots_w = buf_text_width("...");
455:  int target = max_w - dots_w;
456:  if (target < 0)
457:    target = 0;
458:  int len = (int)strlen(s);
459:  while (len > 0 && buf_text_width(s) > target)
460:    s[--len] = '\0';
461:  if (len + 3 < (int)sizeof(((struct app_def *)0)->label)) {
462:    s[len++] = '.';
463:    s[len++] = '.';
464:    s[len++] = '.';
465:    s[len] = '\0';
466:  }
467:}

469:/* ============================================================
470: *                    App table management
471: * ============================================================ */

473:static int apps_add(const char *path, const char *label, enum cat cat) {
474:  if (g_n_apps >= MAX_APPS)
475:    return 0;
476:  if (!path || !*path)
477:    return 0;
478:  struct app_def *a = &g_apps[g_n_apps];
479:  int n;
480:  n = 0;
481:  while (path[n] && n < PATH_MAX - 1) {
482:    a->path[n] = path[n];
483:    n++;
484:  }
485:  a->path[n] = '\0';
486:  if (!label || !*label) {
487:    const char *slash = strrchr(path, '/');
488:    label = slash ? slash + 1 : path;
489:  }
490:  n = 0;
491:  while (label[n] && n < NAME_MAX - 1) {
492:    a->label[n] = label[n];
493:    n++;
494:  }
495:  a->label[n] = '\0';
496:  a->category = cat;
497:  g_n_apps++;
498:  return 1;
499:}
500:
501:struct folder {
502:  int first_child;
503:  int child_count;
504:};
505:#define MAX_FOLDERS 16
506:static struct folder g_folders[MAX_FOLDERS];
507:static int g_n_folders;
508:
509:static int apps_add_folder(const char *name) {
510:  if (g_n_folders >= MAX_FOLDERS)
511:    return -1;
512:  if (g_n_apps >= MAX_APPS)
513:    return -1;
514:  struct app_def *a = &g_apps[g_n_apps];
515:  a->path[0] = '\0';
516:  int n = 0;
517:  while (name[n] && n < NAME_MAX - 1) {
518:    a->label[n] = name[n];
519:    n++;
520:  }
521:  a->label[n] = '\0';
522:  a->category = CAT_FOLDER;
523:  int id = g_n_apps++;
524:  g_folders[g_n_folders].first_child = g_n_apps;
525:  g_folders[g_n_folders].child_count = 0;
526:  g_n_folders++;
527:  return id;
528:}
529:
530:static void apps_end_folder(void) {
531:  if (g_n_folders == 0)
532:    return;
533:  g_folders[g_n_folders - 1].child_count =
534:      g_n_apps - g_folders[g_n_folders - 1].first_child;
535:}
536:
537:static int apps_folder_first_child(int folder_idx) {
538:  for (int i = 0; i < g_n_folders; i++) {
539:    if (g_folders[i].first_child > folder_idx)
540:      break;
541:    if (g_folders[i].first_child + g_folders[i].child_count > folder_idx)
542:      return g_folders[i].first_child;
543:  }
544:  return -1;
545:}
546:
547:static int apps_folder_count(int folder_idx) {
548:  for (int i = 0; i < g_n_folders; i++) {
549:    if (g_folders[i].first_child > folder_idx)
550:      break;
551:    if (g_folders[i].first_child + g_folders[i].child_count > folder_idx)
552:      return g_folders[i].child_count;
553:  }
554:  return 0;
555:}

557:/* ============================================================
558: *                       App discovery
559: * ============================================================ */

561:static enum cat parse_cat(const char *s) {
562:  if (!s || !*s)
563:    return CAT_USER;
564:  if (!strcasecmp(s, "system"))
565:    return CAT_SYSTEM;
566:  if (!strcasecmp(s, "user"))
567:    return CAT_USER;
568:  if (!strcasecmp(s, "utility"))
569:    return CAT_UTILITY;
570:  if (!strcasecmp(s, "games"))
571:    return CAT_GAMES;
572:  if (!strcasecmp(s, "office"))
573:    return CAT_OFFICE;
574:  if (!strcasecmp(s, "other"))
575:    return CAT_OTHER;
576:  return CAT_USER;
577:}
578:
579:static void load_cfg(void) {
580:  /* $HOME/settings/nxlauncher.cfg — same dynamic HOME lookup as nxexec.h's
581:   * '~' resolution (getenv("HOME"), falling back to NXEXEC_HOME_DIR "/home"
582:   * only if HOME is unset/empty), so this and every '~'-relative path a cfg
583:   * entry might use agree on the same HOME without a second definition of
584:   * "where is home" to keep in sync. Previously hardcoded to /sys/bin,
585:   * alongside the system binaries instead of the user's own settings. */
586:  char cfg_path[NXEXEC_PATH_MAX];
587:  const char *home = getenv("HOME");
588:  if (!home || !*home)
589:    home = NXEXEC_HOME_DIR;
590:  snprintf(cfg_path, sizeof(cfg_path), "%s/settings/nxlauncher.cfg", home);
591:
592:  int sz = file_read(cfg_path, (char *)0, 0, 0);
593:  if (sz <= 0 || sz > CFG_MAX)
594:    return;
595:  char *buf = (char *)malloc((size_t)sz + 1);
596:  if (!buf)
597:    return;
598:  int n = file_read(cfg_path, buf, sz, 0);
599:  if (n <= 0) {
600:    free(buf);
601:    return;
602:  }
603:  buf[n] = '\0';
604:
605:  int in_folder = 0;
606:  char *p = buf;
607:  while (p < buf + n) {
608:    char *eol = p;
609:    while (eol < buf + n && *eol != '\n')
610:      eol++;
611:    if (eol < buf + n)
612:      *eol = '\0';
613:
614:    while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t')
615:      p++;
616:    if (*p == '\0' || *p == '#') {
617:      p = eol + 1;
618:      continue;
619:    }
620:
621:    if (strncmp(p, "folder:", 7) == 0) {
622:      if (in_folder)
623:        apps_end_folder();
624:      if (apps_add_folder(p + 7) < 0) {
625:        free(buf);
626:        return;
627:      }
628:      in_folder = 1;
629:    } else if (strcmp(p, "end") == 0) {
630:      if (in_folder) {
631:        apps_end_folder();
632:        in_folder = 0;
633:      }
634:    } else {
635:      char *path = p;
636:      char *label = (char *)0;
637:      char *cat = (char *)0;
638:      for (char *q = p; *q; q++) {
639:        if (*q == ':') {
640:          *q = '\0';
641:          if (!label)
642:            label = q + 1;
643:          else if (!cat) {
644:            cat = q + 1;
645:            break;
646:          }
647:        }
648:      }
649:      apps_add(path, label, parse_cat(cat));
650:    }
651:
652:    p = eol + 1;
653:  }
654:  if (in_folder)
655:    apps_end_folder();
656:  free(buf);
657:}

659:/* Filter: skip file names ending in any of these extensions.  .wad is the
660: * one the user asked for; the others are defensive (the /bin directory may
661: * hold all sorts of artefacts — config, docs, images — that we never want
662: * to offer as a launchable app). */
663:// Lista delle estensioni (devono avere il punto)
664:static const char *const filtered_extensions[] = {
665:    ".wad", ".txt", ".cfg", ".dat", ".md", ".json", ".old", ".dsg", NULL};
666:
667:// Lista dei nomi di file completi (esatti)
668:/* Hidden from the tile grid: the boot/supervisor services, the launcher and
669: * dock themselves, and nxexec (the execution service — it is the thing that
670: * LAUNCHES tiles, not a tile; clicking it with no argument does nothing). */
671:static const char *const filtered_files[] = {
672:    "nxinit",     "nxntfy_srv", "nxui", "nxbar", "nxlauncher", "nxexec",
673:    "background", "env",        ".",    "..",    NULL};
674:
675:static int has_filtered_ext(const char *name) {
676:  if (os1_image_path_has_known_ext(name))
677:    return 1;
678:
679:  // 1. Controllo estensioni
680:  const char *dot = strrchr(name, '.');
681:  if (dot) {
682:    for (int i = 0; filtered_extensions[i]; i++) {
683:      if (strcasecmp(dot, filtered_extensions[i]) == 0)
684:        return 1;
685:    }
686:  }
687:
688:  // 2. Controllo nomi file completi
689:  for (int i = 0; filtered_files[i]; i++) {
690:    if (strcasecmp(name, filtered_files[i]) == 0)
691:      return 1;
692:  }
693:
694:  return 0;
695:}

697:static void scan_bin(void) {
698:  char buf[1024];
699:
700:  /* System applications (/sys/bin) */
701:  int n = list_dir("/sys/bin", buf, sizeof(buf) - 1);
702:  if (n > 0) {
703:    buf[n] = '\0';
704:    char *save = (char *)0;
705:    for (char *tok = strtok_r(buf, " \t", &save); tok;
706:         tok = strtok_r((char *)0, " \t", &save)) {
707:      if (!*tok)
708:        continue;
709:      if (has_filtered_ext(tok))
710:        continue;
711:
712:      char path[PATH_MAX];
713:      int k = 0;
714:      const char *prefix = "/sys/bin/";
715:      while (prefix[k] && k < PATH_MAX - 1)
716:        path[k] = prefix[k], k++;
717:
718:      int j = 0;
719:      while (tok[j] && k < PATH_MAX - 1)
720:        path[k++] = tok[j++];
721:
722:      path[k] = '\0';
723:      apps_add(path, (const char *)0, CAT_SYSTEM);
724:    }
725:  }
726:
727:  /* User applications (/bin) */
728:  n = list_dir("/bin", buf, sizeof(buf) - 1);
729:  if (n > 0) {
730:    buf[n] = '\0';
731:    char *save = (char *)0;
732:    for (char *tok = strtok_r(buf, " \t", &save); tok;
733:         tok = strtok_r((char *)0, " \t", &save)) {
734:      if (!*tok)
735:        continue;
736:      if (has_filtered_ext(tok))
737:        continue;
738:
739:      char path[PATH_MAX];
740:      int k = 0;
741:      const char *prefix = "/bin/";
742:      while (prefix[k] && k < PATH_MAX - 1)
743:        path[k] = prefix[k], k++;
744:
745:      int j = 0;
746:      while (tok[j] && k < PATH_MAX - 1)
747:        path[k++] = tok[j++];
748:
749:      path[k] = '\0';
750:      apps_add(path, (const char *)0, CAT_USER);
751:    }
752:  }
753:}

755:/* ============================================================
756: *                         Layout
757: * ============================================================ */

759:static void recompute_layout(void) {
760:  int usable_w = g_ww - 2 * WIN_PAD;
761:  int usable_h = g_wh - 2 * WIN_PAD;
762:
763:  int dot_row_h = DOT_DIA + DOT_BOTTOM + 4;
764:  int top_extra = 0;
765:  if (g_view == VIEW_FOLDER)
766:    top_extra = BACK_H + 10;
767:
768:  grid_origin_x = WIN_PAD;
769:  grid_origin_y = WIN_PAD + top_extra;
770:  grid_w = usable_w;
771:  grid_h = usable_h - top_extra - dot_row_h;
772:  if (grid_h < 0)
773:    grid_h = 0;
774:
775:  int tile_pitch_x = TILE + TILE_GAP_X;
776:  int tile_pitch_y = TILE + LABEL_GAP + LABEL_MAX_W + TILE_GAP_Y;
777:  cols = (grid_w + TILE_GAP_X) / tile_pitch_x;
778:  if (cols < 1)
779:    cols = 1;
780:  rows = (grid_h + TILE_GAP_Y) / tile_pitch_y;
781:  if (rows < 1)
782:    rows = 1;
783:}

785:static int current_view_first(void) {
786:  if (g_view == VIEW_PAGES)
787:    return 0;
788:  if (g_view == VIEW_FOLDER)
789:    return (g_view_top[0] >= 0) ? g_view_top[0] : 0;
790:  return 0;
791:}
792:
793:static int current_view_count(void) {
794:  if (g_view == VIEW_PAGES)
795:    return g_n_apps;
796:  if (g_view == VIEW_FOLDER && g_view_top[0] >= 0)
797:    return apps_folder_count(g_view_top[0] - 1);
798:  return g_n_apps;
799:}

801:static void populate_slots(void) {
802:  int first = current_view_first();
803:  int count = current_view_count();
804:  if (first < 0)
805:    first = 0;
806:  if (count < 0)
807:    count = 0;
808:
809:  int per_page = cols * rows;
810:  if (per_page < 1)
811:    per_page = 1;
812:
813:  int effective_cols = cols;
814:  if (count > per_page && cols > 1)
815:    effective_cols = cols - 1;
816:  per_page = effective_cols * rows;
817:  if (per_page < 1)
818:    per_page = 1;
819:
820:  int pages = (count + per_page - 1) / per_page;
821:  if (pages < 1)
822:    pages = 1;
823:  if (g_page >= pages)
824:    g_page = pages - 1;
825:  if (g_page < 0)
826:    g_page = 0;
827:  g_pages = pages;
828:
829:  int page_start = first + g_page * per_page;
830:  int page_count = count - g_page * per_page;
831:  if (page_count < 0)
832:    page_count = 0;
833:  if (page_count > per_page)
834:    page_count = per_page;
835:
836:  int grid_pixel_w = effective_cols * TILE + (effective_cols - 1) * TILE_GAP_X;
837:  int start_x = (g_ww - grid_pixel_w) / 2;
838:  int arrow_strip = 0;
839:  if (count > per_page)
840:    arrow_strip = ARROW_W + ARROW_GAP;
841:  int tile_x0 = start_x + arrow_strip;
842:
843:  int row_pixel_h = TILE + LABEL_GAP + LABEL_MAX_W + TILE_GAP_Y;
844:  int grid_pixel_h = rows * row_pixel_h - TILE_GAP_Y;
845:  int start_y = grid_origin_y + ((grid_h - grid_pixel_h) / 2);
846:  if (start_y < grid_origin_y)
847:    start_y = grid_origin_y;
848:
849:  g_slot_n = 0;
850:  for (int i = 0; i < page_count; i++) {
851:    int app_idx = page_start + i;
852:    int c = i % effective_cols;
853:    int r = i / effective_cols;
854:    int tx = tile_x0 + c * (TILE + TILE_GAP_X);
855:    int ty = start_y + r * row_pixel_h;
856:    if (g_slot_n < MAX_SLOTS_PER_PAGE) {
857:      g_slots[g_slot_n].x = tx;
858:      g_slots[g_slot_n].y = ty;
859:      g_slots[g_slot_n].w = TILE;
860:      g_slots[g_slot_n].h = TILE + LABEL_GAP + LABEL_MAX_W;
861:      g_slots[g_slot_n].kind = (g_apps[app_idx].category == CAT_FOLDER) ? 1 : 0;
862:      g_slots[g_slot_n].idx = app_idx;
863:      g_slot_n++;
864:    }
865:  }
866:
867:  if (count > per_page) {
868:    int mid_y = start_y + (rows / 2) * row_pixel_h + (TILE - ARROW_H) / 2;
869:    g_arrow_l_x = start_x + ARROW_W / 2;
870:    g_arrow_l_y = mid_y + ARROW_H / 2;
871:    g_arrow_r_x = g_ww - start_x - ARROW_W / 2;
872:    g_arrow_r_y = mid_y + ARROW_H / 2;
873:  } else {
874:    g_arrow_l_x = g_arrow_r_x = -1;
875:  }
876:
877:  g_dots_y = grid_origin_y + grid_h + DOT_BOTTOM + DOT_DIA / 2;
878:  if (count > per_page) {
879:    int dots_w = g_pages * DOT_DIA + (g_pages - 1) * DOT_GAP;
880:    g_dots_x0 = (g_ww - dots_w) / 2 + DOT_DIA / 2;
881:  } else {
882:    g_dots_x0 = -1;
883:  }
884:
885:  if (g_view == VIEW_FOLDER) {
886:    g_back_x = (g_ww - BACK_W) / 2;
887:    g_back_y = WIN_PAD;
888:  } else {
889:    g_back_x = g_back_y = -1;
890:  }
891:}

897:static void draw_label(int x, int y, const char *label) {
898:  char tmp[NAME_MAX + 4];
899:  int n = 0;
900:  while (label[n] && n < (int)sizeof(tmp) - 4) {
901:    tmp[n] = label[n];
902:    n++;
903:  }
904:  tmp[n] = '\0';
905:  buf_truncate_to_width(tmp, LABEL_MAX_W);
906:  int tw = buf_text_width(tmp);
907:  int lx = x + (TILE - tw) / 2;
908:  if (lx < 0)
909:    lx = 0;
910:  int ly = y + TILE + LABEL_GAP;
911:  if (g_font)
912:    buf_draw_text(lx + 1, ly + 1, tmp, g_col_label_shadow);
913:  buf_draw_text(lx, ly, tmp, g_col_label);
914:}

916:static void draw_folder_tile(int x, int y) {
917:  fb_rrect(x, y, TILE, TILE, TILE_RADIUS, COL_TILE[CAT_FOLDER]);
918:  int tab_w = 18, tab_h = 6;
919:  fb_rrect(x + 5, y + 6, tab_w, tab_h, 2, 0xCC000000u);
920:  int mid_y = y + TILE / 2;
921:  for (int i = 7; i < TILE - 7; i++)
922:    if (x + i >= 0 && x + i < g_ww && mid_y >= 0 && mid_y < g_wh)
923:      g_fb[mid_y * g_ww + (x + i)] = 0x33000000u;
924:}
