926:static void redraw(void) {
927:  fb_fill(g_col_bg);
928:
929:  if (g_view == VIEW_FOLDER && g_back_x >= 0) {
930:    fb_rrect(g_back_x, g_back_y, BACK_W, BACK_H, 6, g_col_back);
931:    if (g_font) {
932:      const char *t = "< Back";
933:      int tw = buf_text_width(t);
934:      buf_draw_text(g_back_x + (BACK_W - tw) / 2, g_back_y + (BACK_H - 16) / 2,
935:                    t, g_col_label);
936:    }
937:  }
938:
939:  for (int i = 0; i < g_slot_n; i++) {
940:    int idx = g_slots[i].idx;
941:    const struct app_def *a = &g_apps[idx];
942:    if (g_slots[i].kind == 1) {
943:      draw_folder_tile(g_slots[i].x, g_slots[i].y);
944:    } else {
945:      /* App tile: use the shared cache (nxicon.h) if this executable's
946:       * basename has an icon for the active theme; otherwise unchanged
947:       * fallback — the flat per-category color, same as before icons
948:       * existed. */
949:      os1_image_t *icon =
950:          nxicon_get(nxicon_classify_path(a->path), g_light, TILE);
951:      if (icon) {
952:        fb_rrect_px(g_slots[i].x, g_slots[i].y, TILE, TILE, TILE_RADIUS, 0,
953:                    icon->pixels);
954:        fb_icon_border(g_slots[i].x, g_slots[i].y, TILE, TILE, TILE_RADIUS,
955:                       g_light);
956:      } else
957:        fb_rrect(g_slots[i].x, g_slots[i].y, TILE, TILE, TILE_RADIUS,
958:                 COL_TILE[a->category]);
959:    }
960:    draw_label(g_slots[i].x, g_slots[i].y, a->label);
961:  }
962:
963:  if (g_arrow_l_x >= 0) {
964:    uint32_t lc = (g_pressed == 1) ? g_col_arrow_pressed : g_col_arrow;
965:    uint32_t rc = (g_pressed == 2) ? g_col_arrow_pressed : g_col_arrow;
966:    int ax_l = g_arrow_l_x - ARROW_W / 2;
967:    int ax_r = g_arrow_r_x - ARROW_W / 2;
968:    int ay = g_arrow_l_y - ARROW_H / 2;
969:    fb_rrect(ax_l, ay, ARROW_W, ARROW_H, 5, lc);
970:    fb_rrect(ax_r, ay, ARROW_W, ARROW_H, 5, rc);
971:    if (g_pressed == 1)
972:      ax_l += 1;
973:    if (g_pressed == 2)
974:      ax_r += 1;
975:    fb_rrect(ax_l + ARROW_W / 2 - 4, ay + ARROW_H / 2 - 3, 2, 6, 1,
976:             g_col_label);
977:    fb_rrect(ax_l + ARROW_W / 2 - 2, ay + ARROW_H / 2 - 1, 2, 2, 1,
978:             g_col_label);
979:    fb_rrect(ax_l + ARROW_W / 2 - 4, ay + ARROW_H / 2 + 1, 2, 2, 1,
980:             g_col_label);
981:    fb_rrect(ax_r + ARROW_W / 2 + 2, ay + ARROW_H / 2 - 3, 2, 6, 1,
982:             g_col_label);
983:    fb_rrect(ax_r + ARROW_W / 2, ay + ARROW_H / 2 - 1, 2, 2, 1, g_col_label);
984:    fb_rrect(ax_r + ARROW_W / 2, ay + ARROW_H / 2 + 1, 2, 2, 1, g_col_label);
985:  }
986:
987:  if (g_dots_x0 >= 0) {
988:    for (int i = 0; i < g_pages; i++) {
989:      int cx = g_dots_x0 + i * (DOT_DIA + DOT_GAP);
990:      uint32_t c = (i == g_page) ? g_col_dot_active : g_col_dot_inactive;
991:      fb_circle(cx, g_dots_y, DOT_DIA / 2, c);
992:    }
993:  }
994:  /* SCHED-STACK-ISO: init pumps the compositor via flush(); window_blit()
995:   * (called from the main loop after redraw()) marks damage. */
996:}
997:
998:/* ============================================================
999: *                       Click handling
1000: * ============================================================ */
1001:
1002:static int hit_arrow(int x, int y) {
1003:  if (g_arrow_l_x < 0)
1004:    return 0;
1005:  int ax_l = g_arrow_l_x - ARROW_W / 2;
1006:  int ax_r = g_arrow_r_x - ARROW_W / 2;
1007:  int ay = g_arrow_l_y - ARROW_H / 2;
1008:  if (x >= ax_l && x < ax_l + ARROW_W && y >= ay && y < ay + ARROW_H)
1009:    return 1;
1010:  if (x >= ax_r && x < ax_r + ARROW_W && y >= ay && y < ay + ARROW_H)
1011:    return 2;
1012:  return 0;
1013:}
1014:
1015:static int hit_dot(int x, int y) {
1016:  if (g_dots_x0 < 0)
1017:    return -1;
1018:  for (int i = 0; i < g_pages; i++) {
1019:    int cx = g_dots_x0 + i * (DOT_DIA + DOT_GAP);
1020:    int dx = x - cx;
1021:    int dy = y - g_dots_y;
1022:    if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= (DOT_DIA / 2) * (DOT_DIA / 2))
1023:      return i;
1024:  }
1025:  return -1;
1026:}
1027:
1028:static int hit_slot(int x, int y) {
1029:  for (int i = 0; i < g_slot_n; i++) {
1030:    if (x >= g_slots[i].x && x < g_slots[i].x + g_slots[i].w &&
1031:        y >= g_slots[i].y && y < g_slots[i].y + TILE)
1032:      return i;
1033:  }
1034:  return -1;
1035:}
1036:
1037:static int hit_back(int x, int y) {
1038:  if (g_back_x < 0)
1039:    return 0;
1040:  return (x >= g_back_x && x < g_back_x + BACK_W && y >= g_back_y &&
1041:          y < g_back_y + BACK_H);
1042:}
1043:
1044:static void enter_folder(int folder_idx) {
1045:  int first = apps_folder_first_child(folder_idx);
1046:  if (first < 0)
1047:    return;
1048:  g_view = VIEW_FOLDER;
1049:  g_view_top[0] = first;
1050:  g_page = 0;
1051:}
1052:
1053:static void leave_folder(void) {
1054:  g_view = VIEW_PAGES;
1055:  g_view_top[0] = -1;
1056:  g_page = 0;
1057:}
1058:
1059:static void handle_click(int mx, int my) {
1060:  if (hit_back(mx, my)) {
1061:    leave_folder();
1062:    return;
1063:  }
1064:  int a = hit_arrow(mx, my);
1065:  if (a == 1) {
1066:    g_pressed = 1;
1067:    g_page = (g_page - 1 + g_pages) % g_pages;
1068:    return;
1069:  }
1070:  if (a == 2) {
1071:    g_pressed = 2;
1072:    g_page = (g_page + 1) % g_pages;
1073:    return;
1074:  }
1075:  int d = hit_dot(mx, my);
1076:  if (d >= 0 && d != g_page) {
1077:    g_page = d;
1078:    return;
1079:  }
1080:  int s = hit_slot(mx, my);
1081:  if (s >= 0) {
1082:    int idx = g_slots[s].idx;
1083:    if (g_apps[idx].category == CAT_FOLDER) {
1084:      enter_folder(idx);
1085:    } else if (g_apps[idx].path[0]) {
1086:      /* HOSTED launch (#193, nxexec model): every tile runs under a fresh
1087:       * host shell spawned DETACHED (the launcher is never anyone's ctty).
1088:       * The host decides at runtime: windowed app -> host vanishes unseen;
1089:       * terminal program -> a shell window appears hosting its output
1090:       * ("i processi terminale ottengono una shell come padre"). */
1091:      int pid = nxexec_spawn_hosted(g_apps[idx].path);
1092:      if (pid <= 0) {
1093:        /* g_win is already up and actively self-rendering at this point in
1094:         * the session (unlike main()'s startup path) — printf() here would
1095:         * draw text straight into g_fb via window_text_write, the same
1096:         * buffer redraw()/window_blit() use (verified: both ultimately hit
1097:         * compositor.c's win->buffer) — so this goes through the existing
1098:         * notification popup (OS1_notify_warn, lib.c) instead. */
1099:        OS1_notify_warn("nxlauncher", g_apps[idx].path);
1100:      } else {
1101:        /* Auto-background: with the app launched, the launcher's job is done
1102:         * for this turn.  Send ourselves to background so the spawned app
1103:         * gets the focus.  The user can bring the launcher back from the
1104:         * dock (its green tile is always at position 0). */
1105:        OS1_window_minimize(g_win);
1106:      }
1107:    }
1108:  }
1109:}
1110:
1111:/* ============================================================
1112: *                  Window (re)initialisation
1113: * ============================================================ */
1114:
1115:static void reinit_window(int ww, int wh) {
1116:  if (ww <= 0)
1117:    ww = 400;
1118:  if (wh <= 0)
1119:    wh = 300;
1120:
1121:  if (g_win >= 0)
1122:    OS1_window_resize(g_win, ww, wh);
1123:
1124:  uint32_t *nb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)ww * wh * 4);
1125:  if (nb) {
1126:    free(g_fb);
1127:    g_fb = nb;
1128:  }
1129:  g_ww = ww;
1130:  g_wh = wh;
1131:  recompute_layout();
1132:  populate_slots();
1133:}
1134:
1135:int main(void) {
1136:  g_font = font_load("/fonts/Rewir-Light.off");
1137:  nxlauncher_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
1138:
1139:  scan_bin();
1140:  load_cfg();
1141:
1142:  g_view = VIEW_PAGES;
1143:  g_view_top[0] = -1;
1144:  g_page = 0;
1145:  g_pages = 1;
1146:
1147:  long di = OS1_display_info();
1148:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
1149:  int sh = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
1150:  if (sw <= 0)
1151:    sw = 800;
1152:  if (sh <= 0)
1153:    sh = 600;
1154:  g_dsw = sw;
1155:  g_dsh = sh;
1156:
1157:  int ww = sw / DEFAULT_W_RATIO;
1158:  int wh = sh / DEFAULT_H_RATIO;
1159:  int wx = (sw - ww) / 2;
1160:  int wy = (sh - wh) / 2;
1161:  if (ww < 320)
1162:    ww = 320;
1163:  if (wh < 240)
1164:    wh = 240;
1165:
1166:  g_fb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)ww * wh * 4);
1167:  if (!g_fb)
1168:    return 1;
1169:
1170:  g_win = create_window(wx, wy, ww, wh, "nxlauncher");
1171:  OS1_window_minimize(g_win);
1172:  if (g_win < 0)
1173:    return 1;
1174:  /* No set_window_flags() — we are a NORMAL window, not top_most.  The
1175:   * compositor draws the native titlebar; the user can drag/resize freely. */
1176:
1177:  reinit_window(ww, wh);
1178:  for (;;) {
1179:    long d = OS1_display_info();
1180:    int cw = (int)((d >> 16) & 0xFFFF), ch = (int)(d & 0xFFFF);
1181:    if (cw > 0 && ch > 0 && (cw != g_dsw || ch != g_dsh)) {
1182:      g_dsw = cw;
1183:      g_dsh = ch;
1184:    }
1185:
1186:    populate_slots();
1187:    redraw();
1188:    window_blit(g_win, 0, 0, g_ww, g_wh, g_fb);
1189:
1190:    input_event_t ev;
1191:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
1192:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE && ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
1193:          ev.mouse.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
1194:        handle_click(ev.mouse.x, ev.mouse.y);
1195:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE &&
1196:                 ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
1197:                 ev.mouse.state == KEY_RELEASED && g_pressed) {
1198:        g_pressed = 0;
1199:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE) {
1200:        int nw = ev.resize.w;
1201:        int nh = ev.resize.h;
1202:        if (nw > 0 && nh > 0)
1203:          reinit_window(nw, nh);
1204:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED) {
1205:        /* External style/theme/bg change (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h),
1206:         * surfaced through this SAME input_poll_event() loop — see nxres.h's
1207:         * header comment for why a second try_recv() loop is wrong here. */
1208:        nxlauncher_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
1209:      }
1210:    }
1211:
1212:    g_pressed = 0;
1213:    OS1_sleep(50);
1214:  }
1215:  return 0;
1216:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxline.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXLINE_H
2:#define _USER_NXLINE_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxline.h
6: * NEXS interactive line editor (ASTRA service layer) — cursor movement,
7: * persistent history, incremental search, and command/path completion for
8: * a single input line hosted in a compositor terminal window.
9: *
10: * Header-only, static-inline, same pattern as nxexec.h/nxassoc.h/nxinfo.h.
11: * Extracted out of nxshell.c's original "cmd_buf + cmd_len, backspace-only"
12: * editor so any future interactive prompt (a REPL, a debugger console) can
13: * reuse the same editing model instead of re-deriving it.
14: *
15: * RENDERING MODEL: nxline never touches window pixels or the cell grid
16: * directly. It drives the SAME VT100/ANSI terminal emulator every other
17: * program already writes through (kernel/graphics/term.c: term_write /
18: * handle_csi), via plain printf()/print() escape sequences:
19: *
20: *   \b              backspace (cursor left one cell — term.c handles it)
21: *   \033[C  \033[D   cursor right/left by N cells (final 'C'/'D', handle_csi)
22: *   \033[K           erase from cursor to end of line (final 'K', mode 0)
23: *
24: * Every edit below is expressed as a RELATIVE cursor movement from wherever
25: * the cursor already is, never an absolute column. That means nxline needs
26: * no knowledge of the visible width of a colored, theme-dependent prompt
27: * string (nxshell's prompt embeds \033[32m/\033[34m SGR codes whose glyphs
28: * take zero columns) — it only ever moves relative to its own last output.
29: *
30: * INPUT MODEL: nxshell already receives ASCII + scancode pairs via
31: * input_poll_event() (INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD). Control-letter combinations
32: * arrive as ASCII control codes (nxexec.h already treats 0x03 as Ctrl-C on
33: * this same path) — nxline follows that precedent: Ctrl-A/E/L/R/D are
34: * 0x01/0x05/0x0C/0x12/0x04 (the letter's position in the alphabet, exactly
35: * like the existing Ctrl-C=0x03). Arrow keys / Home / End / Delete have no
36: * ASCII representation and are read from ev.keyboard.scancode instead, via
37: * INPUT_KEY_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN/HOME/END/DELETE — ASSUMED to sit in input.h
38: * alongside the already-used INPUT_KEY_ENTER/INPUT_KEY_BACKSPACE. If they
39: * are not yet defined there, add them to the keyboard driver's scancode
40: * table before arrow-key/Home/End/Delete input will do anything here;
41: * everything else (Ctrl combos, history, completion, plain typing) works
42: * without them.
43: *
44: * HISTORY PERSISTENCE: the whole in-memory ring is serialized newline-
45: * separated and written with OS1_fs_write(path, buf, n, 0) on every new
46: * entry. offset 0 + ext4_write's truncate-to-length behaviour (see lib.c
47: * rename()'s comment) means this is always a clean overwrite, never stale
48: * trailing garbage from a longer previous file. Bounded to
49: * NXLINE_HIST_MAX * NXLINE_MAX bytes (16 KB at the defaults below), so a
50: * full rewrite per command is cheap enough not to need incremental append.
51: */
52:
53:#include <os1.h>
54:#include <input.h>
55:#include <string.h>
56:
57:/* nxline_contains - tiny local substring search, used only by Ctrl-R
58: * incremental search below. memmove/strlen/strncmp/strchr are confirmed
59: * present in this libc (memmove is already used in term.c; the others are
60: * used throughout nxexec.h/nxassoc.h), but strstr() appears nowhere in the
61: * existing codebase — so this avoids assuming it exists rather than risk a
62: * link failure over one call site. */
63:static inline int nxline_contains(const char *hay, const char *needle) {
64:  if (!*needle)
65:    return 1;
66:  size_t nl = strlen(needle);
67:  for (const char *p = hay; *p; p++)
68:    if (strncmp(p, needle, nl) == 0)
69:      return 1;
70:  return 0;
71:}
72:
73:#define NXLINE_MAX 256
74:#define NXLINE_HIST_MAX 64
75:
76:enum {
77:  NXLINE_NONE = 0,        /* keep editing */
78:  NXLINE_SUBMIT,          /* Enter: nl->buf/nl->len hold the finished line */
79:  NXLINE_EOF,             /* Ctrl-D on an empty line */
80:  NXLINE_CLEAR_SCREEN,    /* Ctrl-L: caller should clear the screen and repaint */
81:};
82:
83:struct nxline {
84:  char buf[NXLINE_MAX];
85:  int len;    /* bytes currently in buf (not counting the NUL) */
86:  int cursor; /* 0..len, insertion point */
87:
88:  char history[NXLINE_HIST_MAX][NXLINE_MAX];
89:  int hist_count; /* entries currently stored (<= NXLINE_HIST_MAX) */
90:  int hist_pos;   /* -1 = editing the live line; else index into history[] */
91:  char live_stash[NXLINE_MAX]; /* live buffer, saved when history browsing starts */
92:
93:  int searching; /* 1 while a Ctrl-R incremental search is active */
94:  char search_buf[NXLINE_MAX];
95:  int search_len;
96:  char search_stash[NXLINE_MAX]; /* buf contents when Ctrl-R was pressed */
97:
98:  char hist_path[64]; /* e.g. "/home/.nxshell_history"; empty = no persistence */
99:
100:  /* Caller hook: print JUST the prompt string (no leading newline, no line
101:   * content) — invoked by nxline when it needs to repaint a whole line from
102:   * column 0 (Ctrl-L, multi-match tab listing). ctx is passed through
103:   * unchanged (nxshell has no per-instance state today, but this keeps the
104:   * header reusable for a future multi-window consumer). */
105:  void (*print_prompt)(void *ctx);
106:  void *ctx;
107:};
108:
109:/* ---------------- init / history load-save ---------------- */
110:
111:static inline void nxline_init(struct nxline *nl, const char *hist_path,
112:                               void (*print_prompt)(void *), void *ctx) {
113:  memset(nl, 0, sizeof(*nl));
114:  nl->hist_pos = -1;
115:  nl->print_prompt = print_prompt;
116:  nl->ctx = ctx;
117:  if (hist_path)
118:    snprintf(nl->hist_path, sizeof(nl->hist_path), "%s", hist_path);
119:}
120:
121:/* nxline_load_history - populate history[] from hist_path, if set. Silent
122: * no-op if the file doesn't exist yet (first run) or persistence is off. */
123:static inline void nxline_load_history(struct nxline *nl) {
124:  if (!nl->hist_path[0])
125:    return;
126:  char buf[NXLINE_HIST_MAX * NXLINE_MAX];
127:  int n = file_read(nl->hist_path, buf, sizeof(buf) - 1, 0);
128:  if (n <= 0)
129:    return;
130:  buf[n] = '\0';
131:
132:  nl->hist_count = 0;
133:  char *save = NULL;
134:  for (char *line = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); line && nl->hist_count < NXLINE_HIST_MAX;
135:       line = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save)) {
136:    if (!*line)
137:      continue;
138:    snprintf(nl->history[nl->hist_count], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", line);
139:    nl->hist_count++;
140:  }
141:}
142:
143:/* nxline_save_history - flush the in-memory ring back to hist_path (a full
144: * overwrite; see the header comment on why that's safe and cheap here). */
145:static inline void nxline_save_history(struct nxline *nl) {
146:  if (!nl->hist_path[0])
147:    return;
148:  char buf[NXLINE_HIST_MAX * NXLINE_MAX];
149:  int n = 0;
150:  for (int i = 0; i < nl->hist_count; i++) {
151:    int l = (int)strlen(nl->history[i]);
152:    if (n + l + 1 >= (int)sizeof(buf))
153:      break;
154:    memcpy(buf + n, nl->history[i], l);
155:    n += l;
156:    buf[n++] = '\n';
157:  }
158:  OS1_fs_write(nl->hist_path, buf, n, 0);
159:}
160:
161:/* nxline_history_add - push a finished command onto the ring (dropping the
162: * oldest entry once full) and persist it. Skips blank lines and an exact
163: * repeat of the immediately-previous entry (the common readline behaviour:
164: * mashing Enter or repeating the same command doesn't spam history). */
165:static inline void nxline_history_add(struct nxline *nl, const char *cmd) {
166:  if (!cmd || !*cmd)
167:    return;
168:  if (nl->hist_count > 0 &&
169:      strncmp(nl->history[nl->hist_count - 1], cmd, NXLINE_MAX) == 0)
170:    return;
171:
172:  if (nl->hist_count < NXLINE_HIST_MAX) {
173:    snprintf(nl->history[nl->hist_count], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", cmd);
174:    nl->hist_count++;
175:  } else {
176:    /* ring: drop oldest, shift everyone down one */
177:    for (int i = 1; i < NXLINE_HIST_MAX; i++)
178:      memcpy(nl->history[i - 1], nl->history[i], NXLINE_MAX);
179:    snprintf(nl->history[NXLINE_HIST_MAX - 1], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", cmd);
180:  }
181:  nxline_save_history(nl);
182:}
183:
184:/* ---------------- low-level relative-cursor primitives ---------------- */
185:
186:static inline void nxline_move_left_n(int n) {
187:  if (n > 0)
188:    printf("\033[%dD", n);
189:}
190:static inline void nxline_move_right_n(int n) {
191:  if (n > 0)
192:    printf("\033[%dC", n);
193:}
194:
195:/* nxline_replace_line - wipe the currently-displayed line content (NOT the
196: * prompt) and print newtext in its place. Used by history browsing and
197: * Ctrl-R acceptance. Purely relative: moves left by the CURRENT cursor
198: * position to reach column 0 of the input, erases to end of line, prints
199: * newtext, cursor lands at the end. */
200:static inline void nxline_replace_line(struct nxline *nl, const char *newtext) {
201:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->cursor);
202:  print("\033[K");
203:  size_t tl = strlen(newtext);
204:  if (tl >= NXLINE_MAX)
205:    tl = NXLINE_MAX - 1;
206:  memcpy(nl->buf, newtext, tl);
207:  nl->buf[tl] = '\0';
208:  nl->len = (int)tl;
209:  nl->cursor = (int)tl;
210:  print(nl->buf);
211:}
212:
213:/* nxline_repaint_inline - reprint the CURRENT buffer starting at column 0,
214: * assuming the caller already positioned the cursor there (e.g. right after
215: * printing a fresh prompt on a new line). Leaves the terminal cursor at
216: * nl->cursor, not necessarily at the end. */
217:static inline void nxline_repaint_inline(struct nxline *nl) {
218:  print(nl->buf);
219:  if (nl->cursor < nl->len)
220:    nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor);
221:}
222:
223:/* ---------------- editing operations ---------------- */
224:
225:static inline void nxline_insert_char(struct nxline *nl, char c) {
226:  if (nl->len >= NXLINE_MAX - 1)
227:    return;
228:  memmove(&nl->buf[nl->cursor + 1], &nl->buf[nl->cursor], nl->len - nl->cursor);
229:  nl->buf[nl->cursor] = c;
230:  nl->len++;
231:  nl->buf[nl->len] = '\0';
232:  print(&nl->buf[nl->cursor]); /* prints the new char + the shifted tail */
233:  nl->cursor++;
234:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor); /* put the caret back after c */
235:}
236:
237:static inline void nxline_delete_before(struct nxline *nl) { /* Backspace */
238:  if (nl->cursor == 0)
239:    return;
240:  memmove(&nl->buf[nl->cursor - 1], &nl->buf[nl->cursor], nl->len - nl->cursor);
241:  nl->cursor--;
242:  nl->len--;
243:  nl->buf[nl->len] = '\0';
244:  print("\b");
245:  print(&nl->buf[nl->cursor]);
246:  print(" "); /* erase the leftover glyph from the old, longer line */
247:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor + 1);
248:}
249:
250:static inline void nxline_delete_at(struct nxline *nl) { /* Delete (forward) */
251:  if (nl->cursor >= nl->len)
252:    return;
253:  memmove(&nl->buf[nl->cursor], &nl->buf[nl->cursor + 1],
254:          nl->len - nl->cursor - 1);
255:  nl->len--;
256:  nl->buf[nl->len] = '\0';
257:  print(&nl->buf[nl->cursor]);
258:  print(" ");
259:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor + 1);
260:}
261:
262:static inline void nxline_move_left(struct nxline *nl) {
263:  if (nl->cursor > 0) {
264:    print("\033[D");
265:    nl->cursor--;
266:  }
267:}
268:static inline void nxline_move_right(struct nxline *nl) {
269:  if (nl->cursor < nl->len) {
270:    print("\033[C");
271:    nl->cursor++;
272:  }
273:}
274:static inline void nxline_move_home(struct nxline *nl) {
275:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->cursor);
276:  nl->cursor = 0;
277:}
278:static inline void nxline_move_end(struct nxline *nl) {
279:  nxline_move_right_n(nl->len - nl->cursor);
280:  nl->cursor = nl->len;
281:}
282:
283:/* ---------------- history browsing ---------------- */
284:
285:static inline void nxline_history_prev(struct nxline *nl) {
286:  if (nl->hist_count == 0)
287:    return;
288:  if (nl->hist_pos == -1) {
289:    snprintf(nl->live_stash, NXLINE_MAX, "%s", nl->buf);
290:    nl->hist_pos = nl->hist_count - 1;
291:  } else if (nl->hist_pos > 0) {
292:    nl->hist_pos--;
293:  } else {
294:    return; /* already at the oldest entry */
295:  }
296:  nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->history[nl->hist_pos]);
297:}
298:
299:static inline void nxline_history_next(struct nxline *nl) {
300:  if (nl->hist_pos == -1)
301:    return;
302:  nl->hist_pos++;
303:  if (nl->hist_pos >= nl->hist_count) {
304:    nl->hist_pos = -1;
305:    nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->live_stash);
306:  } else {
307:    nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->history[nl->hist_pos]);
308:  }
309:}
310:
311:/* ---------------- Ctrl-R incremental search ---------------- */
312:
313:/* nxline_search_render - redraw as "(reverse-i-search)`query': match". This
314: * temporarily overwrites the visible line the same way history browsing
315: * does (relative erase + reprint); the ACTUAL nl->buf is untouched until
316: * the search is accepted (Enter) or cancelled (Esc/Ctrl-G). */
317:static inline void nxline_search_render(struct nxline *nl) {
318:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->cursor);
319:  print("\033[K");
320:  char line[NXLINE_MAX];
321:  const char *match = "";
322:  for (int i = nl->hist_count - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
323:    if (nl->search_len == 0 || nxline_contains(nl->history[i], nl->search_buf)) {
324:      match = nl->history[i];
325:      break;
326:    }
327:  }
328:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "(reverse-i-search)`%s': %s", nl->search_buf,
329:           match);
330:  print(line);
331:  /* cursor tracking during search is a display-only concept: park it at the
332:   * end of the rendered line (cursor math resumes once the search ends). */
333:  nl->cursor = (int)strlen(line);
334:  nl->len = nl->cursor;
335:  /* stash the actual match so Enter can accept it without re-searching */
336:  snprintf(nl->buf, NXLINE_MAX, "%s", match);
337:}
338:
339:static inline void nxline_search_start(struct nxline *nl) {
340:  nl->searching = 1;
341:  nl->search_len = 0;
342:  nl->search_buf[0] = '\0';
343:  snprintf(nl->search_stash, NXLINE_MAX, "%s", nl->buf);
344:  nxline_search_render(nl);
345:}
346:
347:static inline void nxline_search_cancel(struct nxline *nl) {
348:  nl->searching = 0;
349:  nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->search_stash);
350:}
351:
352:static inline void nxline_search_accept(struct nxline *nl) {
353:  /* nl->buf already holds the matched command (set by nxline_search_render);
354:   * just stop searching and leave it as the live line, cursor at end. */
355:  nl->searching = 0;
356:  nl->len = (int)strlen(nl->buf);
357:  nl->cursor = nl->len;
358:  nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->buf); /* re-render cleanly without the search prefix */
359:}
360:
361:/* ---------------- tab completion ---------------- */
362:
363:/* nxline_word_start - index of the start of the word ending at nl->cursor
364: * (whitespace-delimited), for completion. */
365:static inline int nxline_word_start(struct nxline *nl) {
366:  int i = nl->cursor;
367:  while (i > 0 && nl->buf[i - 1] != ' ' && nl->buf[i - 1] != '\t')
368:    i--;
369:  return i;
370:}
371:
372:/* nxline_complete - Tab handling. Completes either a bare command name
373: * (scanning /bin then /sys/bin, mirroring nxshell's own help_list_programs)
374: * or, if the current word contains '/', a path (scanning that directory).
375: * A single match is inserted inline; multiple matches are listed on a new
376: * line and the prompt+buffer are repainted below them via print_prompt(). */
377:static inline void nxline_complete(struct nxline *nl) {
378:  int ws = nxline_word_start(nl);
379:  char word[NXLINE_MAX];
380:  int wl = nl->cursor - ws;
381:  if (wl <= 0 || wl >= NXLINE_MAX)
382:    return;
383:  memcpy(word, &nl->buf[ws], wl);
384:  word[wl] = '\0';
385:
386:  const char *slash = strrchr(word, '/');
387:  char dir[128];
388:  const char *prefix;
389:  if (slash) {
390:    int dl = (int)(slash - word);
391:    if (dl == 0)
392:      snprintf(dir, sizeof(dir), "/");
393:    else
394:      snprintf(dir, sizeof(dir), "%.*s", dl, word);
395:    prefix = slash + 1;
396:  } else {
397:    dir[0] = '\0'; /* sentinel: search /bin then /sys/bin below */
398:    prefix = word;
399:  }
400:  size_t plen = strlen(prefix);
401:
402:  char matches[16][NXLINE_MAX];
403:  int nmatch = 0;
404:  char listing[2][1024];
405:  int nlisting = dir[0] ? 1 : 2;
406:  if (dir[0]) {
407:    int n = list_dir(dir, listing[0], sizeof(listing[0]) - 1);
408:    listing[0][n > 0 ? n : 0] = '\0';
409:  } else {
410:    int n0 = list_dir("/bin", listing[0], sizeof(listing[0]) - 1);
411:    listing[0][n0 > 0 ? n0 : 0] = '\0';
412:    int n1 = list_dir("/sys/bin", listing[1], sizeof(listing[1]) - 1);
413:    listing[1][n1 > 0 ? n1 : 0] = '\0';
414:  }
415:
416:  for (int li = 0; li < nlisting && nmatch < 16; li++) {
417:    char *save = NULL;
418:    for (char *tok = strtok_r(listing[li], " \t", &save); tok && nmatch < 16;
419:         tok = strtok_r(NULL, " \t", &save)) {
420:      if (plen == 0 || strncmp(tok, prefix, plen) == 0) {
421:        int already = 0;
422:        for (int i = 0; i < nmatch; i++)
423:          if (strcmp(matches[i], tok) == 0)
424:            already = 1;
425:        if (!already)
426:          snprintf(matches[nmatch++], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", tok);
427:      }
428:    }
429:  }
430:
431:  if (nmatch == 0)
432:    return;
433:
434:  if (nmatch == 1) {
435:    const char *suffix = matches[0] + plen;
436:    while (*suffix)
437:      nxline_insert_char(nl, *suffix++);
438:    return;
439:  }
440:
441:  /* Multiple matches: list them, then repaint prompt + current buffer. */
442:  print("\r\n");
443:  for (int i = 0; i < nmatch; i++)
444:    printf("%-16s", matches[i]);
445:  print("\r\n");
446:  if (nl->print_prompt)
447:    nl->print_prompt(nl->ctx);
448:  nxline_repaint_inline(nl);
449:}
450:
451:/* ---------------- main key-feed entry point ---------------- */
452:
453:/* nxline_feed_key - handle one keyboard event. Returns an NXLINE_* code;
454: * NXLINE_SUBMIT means nl->buf (NUL-terminated, nl->len bytes) is the
455: * completed line — the caller should process it, then call
456: * nxline_history_add() and reset nl->len/cursor to 0 for the next line. */
457:static inline int nxline_feed_key(struct nxline *nl, unsigned char key,
458:                                  uint16_t scancode) {
459:  if (nl->searching) {
460:    if (key == '\n' || key == '\r' || scancode == INPUT_KEY_ENTER) {
461:      nxline_search_accept(nl);
462:      return NXLINE_NONE;
463:    }
464:    if (key == 0x07 || key == 0x1B) { /* Ctrl-G / Esc: cancel */
465:      nxline_search_cancel(nl);
466:      return NXLINE_NONE;
467:    }
468:    if (key == 0x12) { /* Ctrl-R again: skip to the next older match */
469:      return NXLINE_NONE; /* simplest correct behaviour: no-op, avoids
470:                            * accidentally cycling past the only match */
471:    }
472:    if ((key == '\b' || key == 127) && nl->search_len > 0) {
473:      nl->search_buf[--nl->search_len] = '\0';
474:      nxline_search_render(nl);
475:      return NXLINE_NONE;
476:    }
477:    if (key >= 32 && key < 127 && nl->search_len < NXLINE_MAX - 1) {
478:      nl->search_buf[nl->search_len++] = (char)key;
479:      nl->search_buf[nl->search_len] = '\0';
480:      nxline_search_render(nl);
481:    }
482:    return NXLINE_NONE;
483:  }
484:
485:  if (key == '\n' || key == '\r' || scancode == INPUT_KEY_ENTER)
486:    return NXLINE_SUBMIT;
487:
488:  if (key == '\b' || key == 127 || scancode == INPUT_KEY_BACKSPACE) {
489:    nxline_delete_before(nl);
490:    return NXLINE_NONE;
491:  }
492:
493:  if (key == 0x01) { /* Ctrl-A */
494:    nxline_move_home(nl);
495:    return NXLINE_NONE;
496:  }
497:  if (key == 0x05) { /* Ctrl-E */
498:    nxline_move_end(nl);
499:    return NXLINE_NONE;
500:  }
501:  if (key == 0x0C) /* Ctrl-L */
502:    return NXLINE_CLEAR_SCREEN;
503:  if (key == 0x12) { /* Ctrl-R */
504:    nxline_search_start(nl);
505:    return NXLINE_NONE;
506:  }
507:  if (key == 0x04) { /* Ctrl-D */
508:    if (nl->len == 0)
509:      return NXLINE_EOF;
510:    nxline_delete_at(nl); /* non-empty line: acts as forward-delete */
511:    return NXLINE_NONE;
512:  }
513:  if (key == '\t') {
514:    nxline_complete(nl);
515:    return NXLINE_NONE;
516:  }
517:
518:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_LEFT) {
519:    nxline_move_left(nl);
520:    return NXLINE_NONE;
521:  }
522:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_RIGHT) {
523:    nxline_move_right(nl);
524:    return NXLINE_NONE;
525:  }
526:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_UP) {
527:    nxline_history_prev(nl);
528:    return NXLINE_NONE;
529:  }
530:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_DOWN) {
531:    nxline_history_next(nl);
532:    return NXLINE_NONE;
533:  }
534:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_HOME) {
535:    nxline_move_home(nl);
536:    return NXLINE_NONE;
537:  }
538:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_END) {
539:    nxline_move_end(nl);
540:    return NXLINE_NONE;
541:  }
542:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_DELETE) {
543:    nxline_delete_at(nl);
544:    return NXLINE_NONE;
545:  }
546:
547:  if (key >= 32 && key < 127)
548:    nxline_insert_char(nl, (char)key);
549:
550:  return NXLINE_NONE;
551:}
552:
553:/* nxline_reset - clear the buffer for the next line (call after SUBMIT is
554: * handled and, typically, nxline_history_add() has been called). */
555:static inline void nxline_reset(struct nxline *nl) {
556:  nl->len = 0;
557:  nl->cursor = 0;
558:  nl->buf[0] = '\0';
559:  nl->hist_pos = -1;
560:}
561:
562:#endif /* _USER_NXLINE_H */
563:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxmemstat.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxmemstat.c
3: * NEXS system-statistics frontend (ASTRA stratified service model).
4: *
5: * Usage:
6: *   nxmemstat              open a window and show live system stats, redrawing
7: *                          only when a meaningful value changes (virtio UI)
8: *   nxmemstat --log [S]    headless: print one MEMSTAT CSV record every S seconds
9: *                          (default 60) to stdout/serial, for a long-duration
10: *                          stress capture analysed by tools/analyze_drift.py
11: *
12: * Thin frontend over the reusable helper nxmemstat.h.  Runs as a /sys/bin ROOT
13: * service so it may call the ROOT-gated OS1_sys_stats(); USER apps use this
14: * window, never the raw syscall.  The GUI renders to a compositor window (the
15: * virtio user interface), kept distinct from the UART kernel log.
16: */
17:#include "nxmemstat.h"
18:#include <os1.h>
19:#include <string.h>
20:
21:static int str_eq(const char *a, const char *b) { return strcmp(a, b) == 0; }
22:
23:/* Live windowed monitor (default). */
24:static int cmd_window(void) {
25:  int win = _sys_create_window(120, 120, 560, 280, "NEXS System Monitor");
26:  if (win < 0)
27:    return 1;
28:  struct os1_sysstats prev;
29:  memset(&prev, 0, sizeof(prev));
30:  unsigned long sig = 0; /* seed: forces first render */
31:  while (1) {
32:    nxmemstat_render_if_changed(win, &prev, &sig, 1000);
33:    OS1_sleep(1000);
34:  }
35:  return 0;
36:}
37:
38:/* Headless serial CSV logger for the stress campaign.  If drive_argc>0, first
39: * spawn drive_argv[0] (the load driver, e.g. /bin/stress) as a child: this
40: * service is ROOT, so the /bin child is correctly created at USER level — the
41: * shell is foreground-only and a USER process cannot spawn a ROOT logger, so
42: * the ROOT logger drives the USER load instead. */
43:static int cmd_log(unsigned long interval_s, int drive_argc, char *const drive_argv[]) {
44:  if (interval_s == 0)
45:    interval_s = 60;
46:  struct os1_sysstats s;
47:  if (nxmemstat_snapshot(&s) < 0) {
48:    print("[nxmemstat] OS1_sys_stats denied (need ROOT) or failed\n");
49:    return 1;
50:  }
51:  if (drive_argc > 0) {
52:    int pid = spawn_args(drive_argv[0], drive_argc, drive_argv);
53:    if (pid > 0)
54:      printf("[nxmemstat] spawned load driver '%s' pid=%d\n", drive_argv[0], pid);
55:    else
56:      printf("[nxmemstat] failed to spawn '%s' (err %d)\n", drive_argv[0], pid);
57:  }
58:  print("[nxmemstat] logging system stats (CSV, MEMSTAT prefix)\n");
59:  print("MEMSTAT,t_s,free,lcr,runs,alloc_calls,free_calls,search_ns_total,"
60:        "search_ns_max,km_inuse,km_hi,km_live,ctxsw,runnable,zomb,objF,objP,"
61:        "objR,objW,objC,cycles\n");
62:  unsigned long long start = os1_mono_ns();
63:  for (;;) {
64:    if (nxmemstat_snapshot(&s) > 0) {
65:      char line[256];
66:      unsigned long t = (unsigned long)((os1_mono_ns() - start) / 1000000000ULL);
67:      nxmemstat_csv_line(line, (int)sizeof(line), &s, t);
68:      print(line);
69:    }
70:    OS1_sleep((int)(interval_s * 1000UL));
71:  }
72:  return 0;
73:}
74:
75:int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
76:  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
77:    if (str_eq(argv[i], "--log")) {
78:      unsigned long iv = 0;
79:      int j = i + 1;
80:      if (j < argc && argv[j][0] != '-') { /* optional interval seconds */
81:        iv = (unsigned long)atoi(argv[j]);
82:        j++;
83:      }
84:      /* optional load driver: --run <prog> [args...] (spawned as a USER child) */
85:      int drive_argc = 0;
86:      char *const *drive_argv = 0;
87:      for (int k = j; k < argc; k++) {
88:        if (str_eq(argv[k], "--run")) {
89:          drive_argv = (char *const *)&argv[k + 1];
90:          drive_argc = argc - (k + 1);
91:          break;
92:        }
93:      }
94:      return cmd_log(iv, drive_argc, drive_argv);
95:    }
96:  }
97:  return cmd_window();
98:}
99:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxmemstat.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXMEMSTAT_H
2:#define _USER_NXMEMSTAT_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxmemstat.h
6: * NEXS stratified system-statistics helper (ASTRA service layer).
7: *
8: * Reusable header-only helper (all routines `static inline`) over the
9: * privileged OS1_sys_stats() syscall, mirroring nxproc.h.  SECURITY MODEL: no
10: * ambient checks of its own — OS1_sys_stats() is gated to ROOT/machine in the
11: * kernel, so only an NX service (this runs as /sys/bin/nxmemstat at ROOT) can
12: * read the raw stats; USER apps consume the service's GUI, never the syscall.
13: *
14: * Two surfaces:
15: *   - GUI: nxmemstat_render_if_changed() draws a compositor WINDOW (virtio UI),
16: *     redrawing only when a MEANINGFUL value changed (the signature
17: * deliberately EXCLUDES the always-incrementing cumulative counters — ctx
18: * switches, alloc /free calls, search-ns total, uptime — so the window does not
19: * "repeat" every tick; those are shown as derived rates but do not force a
20: * redraw).
21: *   - Log: nxmemstat_csv_line() formats one MEMSTAT CSV record for a headless
22: *     serial capture consumed by tools/analyze_drift.py.
23: */
24:
25:#include <os1.h>
26:
27:/* nxmemstat_snapshot - fill *out with one stats snapshot.  Returns >0 (bytes)
28: * on success, or a negative errno (-EPERM if the caller is not ROOT/machine).
29: */
30:static inline long nxmemstat_snapshot(struct os1_sysstats *out) {
31:  return OS1_sys_stats(out);
32:}
33:
34:/* Signature over the SLOWLY-changing, user-meaningful fields only.  Page counts
35: * are bucketed to MB so ordinary churn of a few pages does not force a redraw;
36: * the cumulative rate counters are intentionally absent. */
37:static inline unsigned long nxmemstat_signature(const struct os1_sysstats *s) {
38:  unsigned long h = 1469598103934665603UL; /* FNV-1a basis */
39:#define MIX(v) (h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(v)) * 1099511628211UL)
40:  MIX(s->pmm_free_pages >> 8);         /* ~MB buckets */
41:  MIX(s->pmm_largest_contig_run >> 8); /* ~MB buckets */
42:  MIX(s->pmm_free_run_count);
43:  MIX(s->km_bytes_in_use >> 10); /* KB buckets */
44:  MIX(s->km_live_allocs);
45:  MIX(s->sched_nproc);
46:  MIX(s->sched_zombie_count);
47:  MIX(s->sched_runnable);
48:  for (int i = 0; i < OBJ_TYPE_COUNT; i++)
49:    MIX(s->obj_live_by_type[i]);
50:#undef MIX
51:  return h;
52:}
53:
54:/* nxmemstat_render - draw the stats into window win_id.  prev/dt_ms give the
55: * previous sample and elapsed ms so per-interval rates can be shown; pass
56: * prev==NULL (or dt_ms==0) on the first frame to omit rates. */
57:static inline void nxmemstat_render(int win_id, const struct os1_sysstats *s,
58:                                    const struct os1_sysstats *prev,
59:                                    unsigned long dt_ms) {
60:  unsigned long free_mb = (unsigned long)((s->pmm_free_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
61:  unsigned long tot_mb = (unsigned long)((s->pmm_total_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
62:  unsigned long lcr_mb =
63:      (unsigned long)((s->pmm_largest_contig_run * 4UL) / 1024UL);
64:
65:  unsigned long csw_rate = 0, a_rate = 0, mean_srch = 0;
66:  if (prev && dt_ms > 0) {
67:    csw_rate =
68:        (unsigned long)((s->sched_ctx_switches - prev->sched_ctx_switches) *
69:                        1000UL / dt_ms);
70:    unsigned long da =
71:        (unsigned long)(s->pmm_alloc_calls - prev->pmm_alloc_calls);
72:    a_rate = da * 1000UL / dt_ms;
73:    if (da)
74:      mean_srch = (unsigned long)((s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_total -
75:                                   prev->pmm_alloc_search_ns_total) /
76:                                  da);
77:  }
78:
79:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[H\033[J", 6); /* clear */
80:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[1;34m", 7);   /* bold Blue */
81:  printf_win(win_id, "NEXS System Monitor            uptime %lus\n",
82:             (unsigned long)(s->uptime_ns / 1000000000ULL));
83:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4);
84:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "--------------------------------------------\n",
85:                    45);
86:  printf_win(win_id, "CPU    : %lu online   runnable %lu   zombies %lu\n",
87:             (unsigned long)s->sched_ncpu, (unsigned long)s->sched_runnable,
88:             (unsigned long)s->sched_zombie_count);
89:  printf_win(win_id, "ctxsw  : %lu total   (~%lu/s)\n",
90:             (unsigned long)s->sched_ctx_switches, csw_rate);
91:  printf_win(win_id, "PMM    : free %lu / %lu MB   used %lu MB\n", free_mb,
92:             tot_mb, tot_mb - free_mb);
93:  printf_win(win_id, "frag   : largest %lu MB (%lu pg)   runs %lu\n", lcr_mb,
94:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_largest_contig_run,
95:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_run_count);
96:  printf_win(win_id, "alloc  : %lu calls (~%lu/s)   search ~%lu ns (max %lu)\n",
97:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_calls, a_rate, mean_srch,
98:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_max);
99:  printf_win(win_id,
100:             "kheap  : in-use %lu KB  hi %lu KB  live %lu  pool %lu KB\n",
101:             (unsigned long)(s->km_bytes_in_use / 1024UL),
102:             (unsigned long)(s->km_high_water_bytes / 1024UL),
103:             (unsigned long)s->km_live_allocs,
104:             (unsigned long)(s->km_heap_total_bytes / 1024UL));
105:  /* NOTE(OBJ-COUNT-01): these are live CAPABILITY-HANDLE objects (created only
106:   * via SYS_HANDLE_CREATE/OS1low_handle_create — see include/api/object.h),
107:   * NOT a live inventory of "windows on screen" or "running processes".  Most
108:   * everyday operations still go through legacy direct syscalls that never
109:   * touch this layer: SYS_CREATE_WINDOW (the compositor's own window array),
110:   * SYS_SPAWN/SYS_KILL (process_pool), SYS_REGISTRY_GET/SET (the registry
111:   * tree) — none of them call kobj_alloc(), so FILE/PROC/REGKEY/WINDOW read 0
112:   * whenever nothing has an OPEN capability handle of that type at the exact
113:   * snapshot instant (e.g. a file handle from a startup WAD/font read is
114:   * already closed by the time this polls).  This is the documented state of
115:   * the call-surface refactor (DIR-01/#164, ASTRA.md §7.10): the object layer
116:   * is not yet the path every subsystem uses.  CONSOLE is the one type every
117:   * live process actually holds (process_install_stdio gives it 3 handles to
118:   * one shared object) and is shown here so the line always has a
119:   * nonzero, meaningful number when processes are running. */
120:  printf_win(win_id,
121:             "objs   : FILE %lu  PROC %lu  REGKEY %lu  WINDOW %lu  CONSOLE %lu\n",
122:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_FILE],
123:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS],
124:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY],
125:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW],
126:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE]);
127:}
128:
129:/* nxmemstat_render_if_changed - snapshot, redraw the window only when the
130: * meaningful signature changed.  *prev holds the last snapshot (for rates);
131: * *last_sig the last signature; dt_ms the loop cadence.  Returns 1 if redrawn,
132: * 0 if skipped, negative on syscall error. */
133:static inline int nxmemstat_render_if_changed(int win_id,
134:                                              struct os1_sysstats *prev,
135:                                              unsigned long *last_sig,
136:                                              unsigned long dt_ms) {
137:  struct os1_sysstats cur;
138:  long r = nxmemstat_snapshot(&cur);
139:  if (r < 0) {
140:    unsigned long err_sig = ~0UL;
141:    if (last_sig && *last_sig != err_sig) {
142:      _sys_window_write(win_id, "OS1_sys_stats denied (need ROOT) or failed\n",
143:                        43);
144:      *last_sig = err_sig;
145:    }
146:    return (int)r;
147:  }
148:  unsigned long sig = nxmemstat_signature(&cur);
149:  int had_prev = (last_sig && *last_sig != 0 && *last_sig != ~0UL);
150:  if (last_sig && *last_sig == sig) {
151:    *prev = cur; /* keep rates fresh even when we skip the redraw */
152:    return 0;
153:  }
154:  nxmemstat_render(win_id, &cur, had_prev ? prev : (struct os1_sysstats *)0,
155:                   dt_ms);
156:  if (prev)
157:    *prev = cur;
158:  if (last_sig)
159:    *last_sig = sig;
160:  return 1;
161:}
162:
163:/* nxmemstat_csv_line - format one MEMSTAT CSV record (headless --log mode),
164: * matching tools/analyze_drift.py's column order.  't_s' is seconds since the
165: * logger started; 'cycles' is not known to the service, emitted as 0. */
166:static inline int nxmemstat_csv_line(char *buf, int size,
167:                                     const struct os1_sysstats *s,
168:                                     unsigned long t_s) {
169:  return snprintf(
170:      buf, size,
171:      "MEMSTAT,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,"
172:      "%lu,%lu,%lu,0\n",
173:      t_s, (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_pages,
174:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_largest_contig_run,
175:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_run_count, (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_calls,
176:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_calls,
177:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_total,
178:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_max,
179:      (unsigned long)s->km_bytes_in_use, (unsigned long)s->km_high_water_bytes,
180:      (unsigned long)s->km_live_allocs, (unsigned long)s->sched_ctx_switches,
181:      (unsigned long)s->sched_runnable, (unsigned long)s->sched_zombie_count,
182:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_FILE],
183:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS],
184:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY],
185:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW],
186:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE]);
187:}

189:#endif /* _USER_NXMEMSTAT_H */

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxnotify.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxnotify.c
3: * Notification CLI client (the textual front-end to nxntfy_srv).
4: *
5: * Usage:
6: *   nxnotify <message...>       send a notification
7: *   nxnotify send <message...>  same, explicit verb
8: *   nxnotify list               list the recent notifications (registry log)
9: *
10: * Thin CLI over OS1_notify_post (IPC to nxntfy_srv) and the sys.ntfy.log.*
11: * registry ring that nxntfy_srv maintains — no policy of its own, so its reach
12: * is exactly the caller's (the kernel gates IPC + the registry per caller).
13: * Replaces the old 'notify' shell builtin, like nxproc/nxwins/nxres.
14: */
15:#include <os1.h>
16:
17:/* cmd_send - join argv[from..] into one message and post it. */
18:static int cmd_send(int argc, char **argv, int from, int sev) {
19:  char msg[128];
20:  int n = 0;
21:  for (int i = from; i < argc && n < (int)sizeof(msg) - 1; i++) {
22:    for (const char *p = argv[i]; *p && n < (int)sizeof(msg) - 1; p++)
23:      msg[n++] = *p;
24:    if (i + 1 < argc && n < (int)sizeof(msg) - 1)
25:      msg[n++] = ' ';
26:  }
27:  msg[n] = '\0';
28:  if (n == 0) {
29:    printf("usage: nxnotify [send|warn] <message>\n");
30:    return 1;
31:  }
32:  int r = sev ? OS1_notify_warn("nxnotify", msg) : OS1_notify_post("nxnotify", msg);
33:  if (r == 0) {
34:    printf("nxnotify: sent\n");
35:    return 0;
36:  }
37:  printf("nxnotify: failed (%d) - is nxntfy_srv up?\n", r);
38:  return 1;
39:}
40:
41:/* cmd_list - print the values of the sys.ntfy.log.* registry ring. */
42:/* one parsed record from the sys.ntfy.log.* ring: "<from>|<sev>|<state>|<text>" */
43:struct nrec {
44:  int from;
45:  int sev;
46:  char state; /* 'U' unread / received, 'R' read */
47:  char text[56];
48:};
49:
50:static int cmd_list(void) {
51:  char keys[640];
52:  int n = OS1_registry_enum_under("sys.ntfy.log.", keys, sizeof(keys));
53:  if (n <= 0) {
54:    printf("nxnotify: no notifications\n");
55:    return 0;
56:  }
57:  struct nrec recs[16];
58:  int nrec = 0;
59:  char key[64];
60:  int k = 0;
61:  for (const char *p = keys; nrec < 16; p++) {
62:    if (*p == '\n' || *p == '\0') {
63:      if (k > 0) {
64:        key[k] = '\0';
65:        char val[80];
66:        if (OS1_registry_get(key, val, sizeof(val)) == 0) {
67:          struct nrec *r = &recs[nrec];
68:          const char *q = val;
69:          r->from = atoi(q);
70:          while (*q && *q != '|') q++;
71:          if (*q) q++;
72:          r->sev = atoi(q);
73:          while (*q && *q != '|') q++;
74:          if (*q) q++;
75:          r->state = *q ? *q : 'U';
76:          while (*q && *q != '|') q++;
77:          if (*q) q++;
78:          int t = 0;
79:          for (; *q && t < 55; q++) r->text[t++] = *q;
80:          r->text[t] = '\0';
81:          nrec++;
82:        }
83:      }
84:      k = 0;
85:      if (*p == '\0') break;
86:    } else if (k < (int)sizeof(key) - 1) {
87:      key[k++] = *p;
88:    }
89:  }
90:  if (nrec == 0) {
91:    printf("nxnotify: no notifications\n");
92:    return 0;
93:  }
94:  /* Group by sender PID (the per-process distinction). */
95:  printf("\033[1;33mNotifications (grouped by process):\033[0m\n");
96:  char done[16] = {0};
97:  for (int i = 0; i < nrec; i++) {
98:    if (done[i]) continue;
99:    printf("\033[1mPID %d:\033[0m\n", recs[i].from);
100:    for (int j = i; j < nrec; j++) {
101:      if (recs[j].from != recs[i].from) continue;
102:      done[j] = 1;
103:      const char *sv = recs[j].sev == 2 ? "ERR " : recs[j].sev == 1 ? "WARN" : "info";
104:      const char *st = recs[j].state == 'R' ? "read  " : "unread";
105:      printf("  [%s][%s] %s\n", sv, st, recs[j].text);
106:    }
107:  }
108:  return 0;
109:}
110:
111:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
112:  if (argc < 2) {
113:    printf("usage: nxnotify <msg> | nxnotify send|warn <msg> | nxnotify list\n");
114:    return 1;
115:  }
116:  if (strncmp(argv[1], "list", 5) == 0)
117:    return cmd_list();
118:  if (strncmp(argv[1], "send", 5) == 0)
119:    return cmd_send(argc, argv, 2, 0);
120:  if (strncmp(argv[1], "warn", 5) == 0)
121:    return cmd_send(argc, argv, 2, 1); /* yellow warning */
122:  return cmd_send(argc, argv, 1, 0); /* nxnotify <msg...> */
123:}
124:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxntfy_srv.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxntfy_srv.c
3: * System-wide Notification Server + UI (nxntfy_srv): IPC popup service + a
4: * registry-visible log of recent notifications (read by the nxnotify CLI).
5: *
6: * Maintains a small always-on-top, PASSIVE (click-through) compositor window in
7: * the top-right corner of the screen.  The window is initially hidden; it
8: * becomes visible when an IPC message of type IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY arrives, and is
9: * automatically hidden again after 2 seconds.
10: *
11: * Render gating (USR-NOTIFY-03): the popup is shown ONLY on a freshly received
12: * NOTIFY (gated on the recv return code), never on msg.type alone —
13: * IPC_TYPE_RAW is 0 and collides with a "nothing waiting" buffer, which used to
14: * re-render the stale payload forever (the popup never auto-hid) and turned a
15: * click (delivered as IPC_TYPE_MOUSE) into a stray rendered glyph.
16: *
17: * Discovery mechanism (see USR-SEC-01):
18: *   On startup, notify_srv writes its own PID as a decimal string to the
19: *   global registry key "srv.notify_pid".  Any caller that wants to send a
20: *   notification reads this key via registry_read() and sends an IPC message
21: *   to that PID.  There is no authentication: any process can overwrite
22: *   "srv.notify_pid" and redirect all notifications to itself.
23: *
24: * Event loop design (USR-NOTIFY-02 #134):
25: *   Idle, the loop BLOCKS on recv(-1, &msg) so it consumes ~0% CPU until a
26: *   notification arrives (the old try_recv()+yield() loop busy-spun a core).
27: *   While the popup is visible it polls with try_recv() and a real blocking
28: *   OS1_sleep(100) so the 2 s auto-hide can still fire, then drops back to the
29: *   blocking branch. A recv-with-timeout (issue #135) would unify both.
30: *
31: * Known issues:
32: *   USR-SEC-01  (W3 SECURITY) registry_write("srv.notify_pid", ...) has no
33: *               authentication; any process can overwrite this key to intercept
34: *               or forge system notifications.
35: *   USR-BLOAT-01/02 (W2 BAD-IMPL·PERF) The ELF is ~500KB because lib.o
36: *               bundles stb_image/stb_easy_font unconditionally and debug
37: *               DWARF is not stripped.
38: */
39:#include <font_lib.h>
40:#include <input.h>
41:#include <os1.h>
42:#include <string.h>
43:
44:#include "nxres.h" /* nxres_theme_is_light(), IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC (posix_types.h) — see palette below */
45:
46:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
47:/* Adaptive geometry – aligned with nxbar                              */
48:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
49:#define NOTIFY_WIDTH 280
50:#define NOTIFY_HEIGHT 56
51:#define NOTIFY_RADIUS 10
52:/* NOTIFY-RESIZE-01: idle-loop poll cadence (see the event-loop comment below)
53: * — bounded so a host display resize is noticed within ~1/3 s even with the
54: * popup hidden and no notification activity, while staying near-0% CPU. */
55:#define IDLE_POLL_MS 300
56:
57:/* Matches nxbar's BAR_MARGIN_SIDE and BAR_H */
58:#define BAR_MARGIN_SIDE 7
59:#define BAR_H 26
60:#define TOP_GAP 4 /* space between bar and popup */
61:
62:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
63:/* Glass colour palette (same as nxbar) — COL_BG/COL_TEXT/COL_TITLE track
64: * theme.color (nxres.h); COL_ERROR_BG/COL_WARN_BG are severity colours and
65: * stay fixed across both themes, same reasoning as nxbar's badge/glyph. */
66:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
67:static uint32_t g_col_bg;
68:static uint32_t g_col_text;
69:static uint32_t g_col_title;
70:#define COL_ERROR_BG 0xD0FF3B30u /* red tint */
71:#define COL_WARN_BG 0xD0FF9500u  /* amber tint */
72:/* WARN/ERROR popups always sit on their OWN fixed, saturated background
73: * (COL_WARN_BG/COL_ERROR_BG above) — independent of theme.color, same
74: * reasoning as nxbar's badge/glyph staying fixed.  Their text must follow
75: * THAT background, not the desktop theme: white reads on both amber and
76: * red regardless of whether the desktop is in light or dark mode. Using
77: * the theme-derived g_col_title/g_col_text there (this file's first light-
78: * theme pass) flipped it to near-black in light mode, which is low-contrast
79: * on the red/amber tint — the bug the "manca tema light" report was about. */
80:#define COL_SEV_TEXT 0xFFFFFFFFu

82:static void nxntfy_load_palette(int light) {
83:  if (light) {
84:    g_col_bg = 0xE8F5F5F7u;    /* semi-transparent light */
85:    g_col_text = 0xFF1C1C1Eu;
86:    g_col_title = 0xFF000000u;
87:  } else {
88:    g_col_bg = 0xE81C1C24u;    /* semi-transparent dark */
89:    g_col_text = 0xFFF0F0F5u;
90:    g_col_title = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
91:  }
92:}

94:/* ============================================================
95: *           Pixel + font helpers (same technique as nxbar)
96: * ============================================================ */
97:static uint32_t *g_fb;
98:static int g_bw, g_bh; /* buffer (window) size */
99:static struct font_ctx *g_font;
100:
101:/* fb_rrect - filled rounded rectangle (corners clipped to a quarter-circle of
102: * radius r).  Same technique as nxui's fb_rrect (GFX-NXBAR-04 / GFX-NXUI-04):
103: * relies on the compositor honoring per-pixel alpha on window_blit. */
104:static void fb_rrect(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint32_t c) {
105:  for (int j = 0; j < h; j++) {
106:    for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
107:      int cx = -1, cy = 0;
108:      if (i < r && j < r) {
109:        cx = r;
110:        cy = r;
111:      } else if (i >= w - r && j < r) {
112:        cx = w - r - 1;
113:        cy = r;
114:      } else if (i < r && j >= h - r) {
115:        cx = r;
116:        cy = h - r - 1;
117:      } else if (i >= w - r && j >= h - r) {
118:        cx = w - r - 1;
119:        cy = h - r - 1;
120:      }
121:      if (cx >= 0) {
122:        int dx = i - cx, dy = j - cy;
123:        if (dx * dx + dy * dy > r * r)
124:          continue;
125:      }
126:      int px = x + i, py = y + j;
127:      if (px >= 0 && px < g_bw && py >= 0 && py < g_bh)
128:        g_fb[py * g_bw + px] = c;
129:    }
130:  }
131:}
132:
133:static void buf_draw_glyph(int x, int y, uint32_t cp, uint32_t color) {
134:  if (!g_font)
135:    return;
136:  int idx = (int)cp - g_font->header.first_char;
137:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= g_font->header.num_chars)
138:    return;
139:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &g_font->glyphs[idx];
140:  uint8_t *bitmap = g_font->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
141:  int sx = x + gi->x0, sy = y + g_font->header.ascent + gi->y0;
142:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
143:    for (int gx = 0; gx < gi->width; gx++) {
144:      if (bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx] > 64) {
145:        int px = sx + gx, py = sy + gy;
146:        if (px >= 0 && px < g_bw && py >= 0 && py < g_bh)
147:          g_fb[py * g_bw + px] = color;
148:      }
149:    }
150:  }
151:}
152:
153:static void buf_draw_text(int x, int y, const char *s, uint32_t color) {
154:  if (!g_font || !s)
155:    return;
156:  uint32_t cp;
157:  int consumed, cursor = x;
158:  size_t rem = strlen(s);
159:  const char *p = s;
160:  while (*p) {
161:    consumed = utf8_decode(p, rem, &cp);
162:    if (consumed <= 0) {
163:      p++;
164:      rem--;
165:      continue;
166:    }
167:    buf_draw_glyph(cursor, y, cp, color);
168:    int idx = (int)cp - g_font->header.first_char;
169:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < g_font->header.num_chars)
170:      cursor += g_font->glyphs[idx].advance;
171:    p += consumed;
172:    rem -= consumed;
173:  }
174:}
175:
176:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
177:/* Warning dedup — consecutive-repeat suppression, WARNINGS ONLY        */
178:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
179:/* Per-process "last warning text seen" table.  A warning (severity 1) whose
180: * text is IDENTICAL to the last one already recorded for the SAME sender
181: * pid is a repeat of something already visible in nxbar's panel — skipped
182: * entirely (no second ring entry) so a process stuck emitting the same
183: * warning in a loop cannot flood the panel with copies of one line.  A
184: * DIFFERENT warning from the same process, or the same text from a
185: * different process, is never suppressed — nothing distinct is ever
186: * dropped.  Errors and plain notifications never go through this table. */
187:#define WARN_DEDUP_MAX 16
188:static int g_warn_pid[WARN_DEDUP_MAX];
189:static char g_warn_text[WARN_DEDUP_MAX][56];
190:static int g_warn_n;      /* slots in use */
191:static int g_warn_next;   /* rotating eviction cursor once the table is full */
192:
193:static int warn_is_dup(int pid, const char *text) {
194:  for (int i = 0; i < g_warn_n; i++)
195:    if (g_warn_pid[i] == pid)
196:      return strncmp(g_warn_text[i], text, sizeof(g_warn_text[i])) == 0;
197:  return 0;
198:}
199:
200:static void warn_remember(int pid, const char *text) {
201:  for (int i = 0; i < g_warn_n; i++) {
202:    if (g_warn_pid[i] == pid) {
203:      snprintf(g_warn_text[i], sizeof(g_warn_text[i]), "%s", text);
204:      return;
205:    }
206:  }
207:  int idx;
208:  if (g_warn_n < WARN_DEDUP_MAX) {
209:    idx = g_warn_n++;
210:  } else {
211:    idx = g_warn_next; /* table full: evict the oldest tracked process */
212:    g_warn_next = (g_warn_next + 1) % WARN_DEDUP_MAX;
213:  }
214:  g_warn_pid[idx] = pid;
215:  snprintf(g_warn_text[idx], sizeof(g_warn_text[idx]), "%s", text);
216:}

218:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
219:/* Window management – adaptive position (like nxbar's bar_reinit)      */
220:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
221:static int g_win = -1;
222:static int g_sw, g_sh; /* last seen screen size */
223:
224:static void notif_reinit(int sw, int sh) {
225:  g_sw = sw;
226:  g_sh = sh;
227:  g_bw = NOTIFY_WIDTH;
228:  g_bh = NOTIFY_HEIGHT;
229:
230:  /* Position: right edge – margin, just below the top bar */
231:  int wx = sw - g_bw - BAR_MARGIN_SIDE;
232:  int wy = BAR_MARGIN_SIDE + BAR_H +
233:           TOP_GAP; /* nxbar top margin + bar height + gap */
234:
235:  if (g_win >= 0)
236:    destroy_window(g_win);
237:  free(g_fb);
238:  g_fb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)g_bw * g_bh * 4);
239:  if (!g_fb)
240:    return;
241:  memset(g_fb, 0, (size_t)g_bw * g_bh * 4);
242:
243:  g_win = create_window(wx, wy, g_bw, g_bh, "nxntfy_srv");
244:  if (g_win >= 0)
245:    set_window_flags(g_win, 1 | 4 | 8); /* top_most, hidden, passive */
246:}
247:
248:/*
249: * main - notification server entry point; does not return.
250: *
251: * Creates a top-most, initially hidden compositor window.  Registers this
252: * process's PID in the registry so callers can discover the endpoint.
253: * Enters the event loop:
254: *   1. try_recv: if a NOTIFY or RAW IPC message arrives, render its payload
255: *      (up to 64 bytes) in the window and show it.
256: *   2. Auto-hide: if the window has been visible for >2000 ms, hide it.
257: *   3. Paced sleep while visible.
258: *
259: * Returns 1 on window creation failure, never returns otherwise.
260: *
261: * Side effects: creates a compositor window; writes registry key
262: *   "srv.notify_pid"; draws to the window on each notification.
263: *
264: * NOTE(USR-SEC-01): Writing to "srv.notify_pid" is unauthenticated; any
265: *   process can overwrite it and intercept subsequent notify() calls.
266: */
267:int main(void) {
268:  g_font = font_load("/fonts/Rewir-Light.off");
269:  nxntfy_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
270:
271:  long di = OS1_display_info();
272:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF), sh = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
273:  if (sw <= 0)
274:    sw = 800;
275:  if (sh <= 0)
276:    sh = 600;
277:  notif_reinit(sw, sh);
278:  if (g_win < 0) {
279:    printf("[Notify] Failed to create window\n");
280:    return 1;
281:  }
282:
283:  printf("[Notify] Server started (PID %d)\n", get_pid());
284:
285:  /* NOTE(NOTIFY-REG-01): srv.notify_pid is now published by init (parent),
286:   * not by the server itself.  Self-publishing broke respawn: after the
287:   * server died and init spawned a fresh copy, the registry key still held
288:   * the corpse's pid and every notify_post() lost its messages.  Init owns
289:   * the key (it knows the live pid on every spawn + respawn), and re-publishes
290:   * it after each respawn so any registry hijack between respawns is undone.
291:   * Discovery of this endpoint from a caller:
292:   * OS1_registry_get("srv.notify_pid").
293:   */
294:
295:  struct ipc_message msg;
296:  long last_notify_time = 0;
297:  int is_visible = 0; /* Tracks whether the window is currently shown */
298:  int ring_idx = 0;   /* registry log ring head: sys.ntfy.log.<i>, 16 deep */
299:  /* Last logged record, kept so the auto-hide can flip its state to READ (the
300:   * read receipt): record format is "<from>|<sev>|<state>|<text>". */
301:  int last_log_idx = -1, last_from = 0, last_sev = 0;
302:  char last_text[56] = {0};
303:
304:  /* Event loop (USR-NOTIFY-02 #134): never busy-spin.
305:   *   - Idle (window hidden): poll at a LOW rate (see IDLE_POLL_MS below) so
306:   *     the process is descheduled between ticks (near-0% CPU) but still
307:   *     notices a host display resize without needing a live notification.
308:   *   - Visible (auto-hide pending): we cannot block forever or the 2 s hide
309:   *     would never fire, so poll with try_recv() and a REAL blocking
310:   * OS1_sleep(100) — 10 wakeups/s, not a yield-spin — until the window hides
311:   * and we drop back to the idle branch. A recv-with-timeout would collapse
312:   * both branches; that needs the capability timer objects of issue #135. */
313:  while (1) {
314:    /* Adaptive resolution check (like nxbar) */
315:    long d = OS1_display_info();
316:    int cw = (int)((d >> 16) & 0xFFFF), ch = (int)(d & 0xFFFF);
317:    if (cw > 0 && ch > 0 && (cw != g_sw || ch != g_sh))
318:      notif_reinit(cw, ch);
319:
320:    /* `got` is true ONLY when a message was actually received this round.
321:     * Gate the popup on the receive RETURN CODE, never on msg.type alone:
322:     * IPC_TYPE_RAW == 0 (posix_types.h) collides with a zeroed / "nothing
323:     * waiting" buffer, so the old `msg.type == IPC_TYPE_RAW` test re-rendered
324:     * the STALE payload on every empty poll — the popup never auto-hid (each
325:     * re-render reset last_notify_time), and a click on the popup delivered an
326:     * IPC_TYPE_MOUSE message whose coordinate bytes were then rendered as a
327:     * stray glyph. */
328:    int got;
329:    if (!is_visible) {
330:      /* FIX(NOTIFY-RESIZE-01): this used to be a plain blocking recv(-1,&msg)
331:       * — zero CPU while idle, but it ALSO froze the "adaptive resolution
332:       * check" above: that check only runs once per loop iteration, and a
333:       * blocking recv() means the NEXT iteration (and therefore the next
334:       * resize check) does not happen until a real notification arrives to
335:       * wake it. A host display resize that lands while idle (the common
336:       * state — the popup is hidden almost all the time) was invisible to
337:       * this process until something else woke it, leaving the popup's
338:       * window stuck at its OLD position/possibly off-screen until the next
339:       * notification "touched" it. Poll at IDLE_POLL_MS instead of blocking
340:       * forever: still near-0% CPU (a ~3 Hz sleep-based wait, same technique
341:       * nxbar/nxui already use at 30 Hz for their own resize polling), but
342:       * the resize check now runs on a bounded cadence regardless of
343:       * notification activity. */
344:      got = (try_recv(-1, &msg) == 0);
345:      if (!got) {
346:        OS1_sleep(IDLE_POLL_MS);
347:        continue;
348:      }
349:    } else {
350:      /* Visible: non-blocking poll so the 2 s auto-hide can still fire. */
351:      got = (try_recv(-1, &msg) == 0);
352:    }
353:
354:    /* A look-changed ping (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h) rides the SAME
355:     * IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY transport as a real user notification, tagged via
356:     * data2 so it never gets mistaken for one — no popup, no ring log,
357:     * just refresh this window's own palette (it draws itself with the
358:     * same glass colours as nxbar/nxsettings, so it needs to react too). */
359:    if (got && msg.type == IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY &&
360:        msg.data2 == IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC) {
361:      nxntfy_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
362:      continue;
363:    }
364:
365:    /* Only a freshly-received NOTIFY shows the popup. Any other message type
366:     * (e.g. IPC_TYPE_MOUSE from a click on the window) is drained and ignored.
367:     */
368:    if (got && msg.type == IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY) {
369:      int is_warning = (msg.data1 == 1);
370:
371:      /* Exact repeat of the last warning from THIS process: already visible
372:       * in nxbar's panel from its first occurrence — skip entirely (no
373:       * second ring entry either) instead of piling up identical lines.
374:       * Errors and plain notifications are never deduped. */
375:      if (is_warning && warn_is_dup((int)msg.from, msg.payload))
376:        continue;
377:      if (is_warning)
378:        warn_remember((int)msg.from, msg.payload);
379:
380:      /* Colour the popup by severity (msg.data1): 2 = error (red), 1 = warning
381:       * (amber), else info.  The kernel posts data1=2 for a userland crash;
382:       * userland may post data1=1 for warnings.  WARN/ERROR sit on their own
383:       * fixed, saturated tint (COL_WARN_BG/COL_ERROR_BG) — text follows THAT
384:       * background (COL_SEV_TEXT, always legible), not the desktop theme;
385:       * only the neutral info background (g_col_bg) uses the theme-derived
386:       * title/text colours. */
387:      uint32_t bg = g_col_bg;
388:      uint32_t text_col = g_col_text;
389:      uint32_t title_col = g_col_title;
390:      const char *title = "Notification";
391:      if (msg.data1 == 2) {
392:        bg = COL_ERROR_BG;
393:        title = "ERROR";
394:        text_col = COL_SEV_TEXT;
395:        title_col = COL_SEV_TEXT;
396:      } else if (is_warning) {
397:        bg = COL_WARN_BG;
398:        title = "WARN";
399:        text_col = COL_SEV_TEXT;
400:        title_col = COL_SEV_TEXT;
401:      }
402:
403:      /* Warnings are reported ONLY in nxbar's notification panel (the ring
404:       * log below) — never as an on-screen popup, so a process emitting
405:       * several DIFFERENT warnings in a row does not toast-spam the desktop
406:       * the way an error or a plain notification legitimately still does
407:       * (those are rarer and worth interrupting for). */
408:      int popup_shown = 0;
409:      if (!is_warning) {
410:        /* Non mostriamo il popup se il pannello notifiche di nxbar è già aperto.
411:         */
412:        char panel_flag[2] = {0};
413:        int panel_open = (OS1_registry_get("sys.ntfy.panel_open", panel_flag,
414:                                           sizeof(panel_flag)) == 0 &&
415:                          panel_flag[0] == '1');
416:
417:        if (!panel_open) {
418:          /* Render with modern glass style */
419:          if (g_fb) {
420:            fb_rrect(0, 0, g_bw, g_bh, NOTIFY_RADIUS, bg);
421:            buf_draw_text(12, 10, title, title_col);
422:            buf_draw_text(12, 30, msg.payload, text_col);
423:            window_blit(g_win, 0, 0, g_bw, g_bh, g_fb);
424:          }
425:
426:          /* Show window: 1=top_most, 2=visible, 8=passive (click-through, no
427:           * focus). */
428:          set_window_flags(g_win, 1 | 2 | 8);
429:          is_visible = 1;
430:          popup_shown = 1;
431:          last_notify_time = get_time();
432:          /* SCHED-STACK-ISO: blit + set_window_flags mark damage; init flush()
433:           * presents — no nested compositor_render() here. */
434:        }
435:      }
436:
437:      /* Log to a bounded registry ring so notifications are VISIBLE in the
438:       * namespace and readable by the nxnotify CLI (ASTRA: everything is a
439:       * registry node).  16 entries cap the buffer (anti-spam / fixed size).
440:       * Record = "<from>|<sev>|<state>|<text>": carries the sender PID (group
441:       * by process), severity, and the receipt state (U=unread/received,
442:       * R=read) — the registry-message model.  Always written (warnings
443:       * included, so nxbar's panel/badge see them) regardless of whether a
444:       * popup was shown. */
445:      {
446:        int idx = ring_idx & 0x0F;
447:        char key[24], rec[80];
448:        snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "sys.ntfy.log.%d", idx);
449:        snprintf(rec, sizeof(rec), "%d|%d|U|%.48s", (int)msg.from,
450:                 (int)msg.data1, msg.payload);
451:        OS1_registry_set(key, rec);
452:        ring_idx++;
453:
454:        /* The pending-read-receipt bookkeeping below (flipped to 'R' by the
455:         * auto-hide branch when the ON-SCREEN POPUP disappears) must track
456:         * whichever ring entry that popup is actually showing — NOT
457:         * unconditionally the latest ring write.  A warning (or a
458:         * panel-open-suppressed notification) never shows a popup, so it
459:         * must never steal this slot from whatever IS currently on screen:
460:         * if it did, the auto-hide would mark the WRONG entry 'R' — the
461:         * true source of the popup would stay 'unread' forever, and this
462:         * unrelated entry would be marked 'read' despite never having been
463:         * shown. */
464:        if (popup_shown) {
465:          last_log_idx = idx;
466:          last_from = (int)msg.from;
467:          last_sev = (int)msg.data1;
468:          int t = 0;
469:          for (const char *p = msg.payload; *p && t < 55; p++)
470:            last_text[t++] = *p;
471:          last_text[t] = '\0';
472:        }
473:      }
474:    }
475:
476:    /* Auto-hide 2 s (2000 ms; get_time() is real ms) after the last
477:     * notification, then the next iteration blocks on recv() again. */
478:    if (is_visible && (get_time() - last_notify_time >= 2000)) {
479:      set_window_flags(g_win, 1 | 4 | 8); /* 1=top_most, 4=hidden, 8=passive */
480:      is_visible = 0;
481:      /* SCHED-STACK-ISO: set_window_flags marks damage; init flush() presents
482:       * the hide — no nested compositor_render() here. */
483:      /* The user has now seen the popup: confirm READ in the registry record
484:       * (the read receipt of the message model). */
485:      if (last_log_idx >= 0) {
486:        char key[24], rec[80];
487:        snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "sys.ntfy.log.%d", last_log_idx);
488:        snprintf(rec, sizeof(rec), "%d|%d|R|%.48s", last_from, last_sev,
489:                 last_text);
490:        OS1_registry_set(key, rec);
491:        last_log_idx = -1;
492:      }
493:    }
494:
495:    /* While the popup is up, pace the auto-hide poll with a real blocking sleep
496:     * (descheduled, no busy-wait). Skipped once we are hidden — that path
497:     * blocks on recv() at the top instead. */
498:    if (is_visible)
499:      OS1_sleep(100);
500:  }
501:
502:  return 0;
503:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxperm.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxperm.c
3: * NEXS users/permissions manager (ASTRA) — FOUNDATION (introspection).
4: *
5: * Usage:
6: *   nxperm            show your identity (level + allowed services) = whoami
7: *   nxperm whoami     same
8: *   nxperm levels     list the privilege levels and what each grants
9: *   nxperm services   list the declared services + the capability each needs
10: *   nxperm su         (not yet) elevate — the system runs in debug mode, where
11: *                     /sys/bin services (including the shell) already run at root
12: *
13: * Thin CLI over the header-only helper nxperm.h.  This is the introspection
14: * foundation of the user/permission manager; login, named users + passwords, su
15: * elevation and UAC approval popups (rendered as kernel-trusted windows) are the
16: * dedicated users phase.  Security is "by caller": nxperm only reveals the
17: * caller's own identity (OS1_identity) and never widens authority.
18: */
19:#include "nxperm.h"
20:#include <os1.h>
21:
22:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
23:  if (argc < 2 || strncmp(argv[1], "whoami", 7) == 0) {
24:    nxperm_print_identity(-1);
25:    return 0;
26:  }
27:  if (strncmp(argv[1], "levels", 7) == 0) {
28:    nxperm_print_levels(-1);
29:    return 0;
30:  }
31:  if (strncmp(argv[1], "services", 9) == 0) {
32:    nxperm_print_services(-1);
33:    return 0;
34:  }
35:  if (strncmp(argv[1], "su", 3) == 0) {
36:    printf("nxperm: su not yet implemented.\n");
37:    printf("        debug mode: /sys/bin services (incl. the shell) run at "
38:           "root.\n");
39:    printf("        login / named users / su / UAC are the dedicated users "
40:           "phase.\n");
41:    return 0;
42:  }
43:  printf("nxperm: unknown command '%s'\n", argv[1]);
44:  printf("usage: nxperm [whoami|levels|services|su]\n");
45:  return 1;
46:}
