@@@ user/sys/bin/nxperm.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXPERM_H
2:#define _USER_NXPERM_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxperm.h
6: * NEXS users/permissions helper (ASTRA service layer) — FOUNDATION.
7: *
8: * The privilege model (include/api/caps.h): every process has one LEVEL —
9: * machine (the computer itself, NOT a login user), root, user, guest — which is
10: * the resolver for the (future) multi-user model, plus a capability MASK
11: * enforced at the syscall boundary.  nxperm presents this as a LEVEL-based view
12: * so applications reason in terms of machine/root/user/guest and never touch the
13: * raw capability bits (ASTRA goal: hide the capability layer behind a
14: * kernel-managed standard).
15: *
16: * This header is the INTROSPECTION foundation only.  The full vision — login,
17: * named users + passwords, su elevation, UAC approval popups rendered as
18: * kernel-trusted windows, and a capability-partitioned VFS — is the dedicated
19: * users phase.
20: *
21: * SECURITY: read-only, adds no checks.  Identity comes from OS1_identity(),
22: * which only ever reveals the caller's OWN level/mask — secure by caller.
23: */
24:#include <os1.h> /* pulls caps.h (PLVL_ and CAP_ macros) + OS1_identity + printf */
25:#include <string.h>
26:
27:/* Level name (machine/root/user/guest), or "?" out of range. */
28:static inline const char *nxperm_level_name(int level) {
29:  switch (level) {
30:  case PLVL_MACHINE: return "machine";
31:  case PLVL_ROOT:    return "root";
32:  case PLVL_USER:    return "user";
33:  case PLVL_GUEST:   return "guest";
34:  default:           return "?";
35:  }
36:}
37:
38:/* The capability mask a level grants.  Derives from caps_for_level() in the
39: * shared caps header — the ONE definition of the level->mask policy (B2.1).
40: * This used to be a hand-maintained copy of the kernel's level_ceiling[]; a
41: * copy is a drift bug waiting to happen, so it is now a thin alias. */
42:static inline unsigned int nxperm_level_mask(int level) {
43:  return caps_for_level(level);
44:}
45:
46:/* One capability bit -> a human service label. */
47:struct nxperm_cap {
48:  unsigned int bit;
49:  const char *label;
50:};
51:static const struct nxperm_cap NXPERM_CAPS[] = {
52:    {CAP_SPAWN, "spawn"},     {CAP_FS_WRITE, "files"},
53:    {CAP_IPC_ANY, "ipc"},     {CAP_WINDOW, "windows"},
54:    {CAP_REG_WRITE, "registry"},
55:};
56:#define NXPERM_NCAPS (int)(sizeof(NXPERM_CAPS) / sizeof(NXPERM_CAPS[0]))
57:
58:/* Render a cap mask as a space-separated label list into buf ("-" if none). */
59:static inline void nxperm_mask_str(unsigned int mask, char *buf, int n) {
60:  int p = 0;
61:  if (n > 0)
62:    buf[0] = '\0';
63:  for (int i = 0; i < NXPERM_NCAPS; i++) {
64:    if (!(mask & NXPERM_CAPS[i].bit))
65:      continue;
66:    const char *l = NXPERM_CAPS[i].label;
67:    if (p && p + 1 < n)
68:      buf[p++] = ' ';
69:    for (int k = 0; l[k] && p + 1 < n; k++)
70:      buf[p++] = l[k];
71:    buf[p] = '\0';
72:  }
73:  if (p == 0 && n > 1) {
74:    buf[0] = '-';
75:    buf[1] = '\0';
76:  }
77:}
78:
79:/* A declared system service + the capability needed to use it (ASTRA: every
80: * service is gated by a capability — only programs granted that capability may
81: * activate it).  Foundation list; extended as services land. */
82:struct nxperm_service {
83:  const char *name;
84:  const char *desc;
85:  unsigned int cap;
86:};
87:static const struct nxperm_service NXPERM_SERVICES[] = {
88:    {"windows", "create/draw windows", CAP_WINDOW},
89:    {"spawn", "launch programs", CAP_SPAWN},
90:    {"files", "write files", CAP_FS_WRITE},
91:    {"registry", "write registry", CAP_REG_WRITE},
92:    {"ipc", "message non-kin", CAP_IPC_ANY},
93:};
94:#define NXPERM_NSERVICES                                                        \
95:  (int)(sizeof(NXPERM_SERVICES) / sizeof(NXPERM_SERVICES[0]))
96:
97:static inline void nxperm_emit(int win, const char *s) {
98:  if (win < 0)
99:    printf("%s", s);
100:  else
101:    printf_win(win, "%s", s);
102:}
103:
104:/* "whoami": current level + the services it may use. */
105:static inline void nxperm_print_identity(int win) {
106:  int level = 0;
107:  unsigned int mask = 0;
108:  OS1_identity(&level, &mask);
109:  char m[96];
110:  nxperm_mask_str(mask, m, (int)sizeof(m));
111:  char line[160];
112:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "level: %s\ncan:   %s\n",
113:           nxperm_level_name(level), m);
114:  nxperm_emit(win, line);
115:}
116:
117:/* List the levels and the mask each grants. */
118:static inline void nxperm_print_levels(int win) {
119:  nxperm_emit(win, "LEVEL    SERVICES\n");
120:  for (int lv = 0; lv < PLVL_COUNT; lv++) {
121:    char m[96];
122:    nxperm_mask_str(nxperm_level_mask(lv), m, (int)sizeof(m));
123:    char line[160];
124:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%-8s %s\n", nxperm_level_name(lv), m);
125:    nxperm_emit(win, line);
126:  }
127:}
128:
129:/* List the declared services + the capability each requires, and whether the
130: * current caller holds it. */
131:static inline void nxperm_print_services(int win) {
132:  int level = 0;
133:  unsigned int mask = 0;
134:  OS1_identity(&level, &mask);
135:  nxperm_emit(win, "SERVICE   ALLOWED  DESCRIPTION\n");
136:  for (int i = 0; i < NXPERM_NSERVICES; i++) {
137:    const struct nxperm_service *s = &NXPERM_SERVICES[i];
138:    char line[160];
139:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%-9s %-8s %s\n", s->name,
140:             (mask & s->cap) ? "yes" : "no", s->desc);
141:    nxperm_emit(win, line);
142:  }
143:}
144:
145:#endif /* _USER_NXPERM_H */
146:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxpower.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxpower.c
3: * NEXS power control (nxpower) — the dedicated shutdown/restart program.
4: *
5: * Usage:
6: *   nxpower                 open a small confirm dialog (Shutdown/Restart/
7: *                            Cancel), launched by nxbar's [X] root menu's
8: *                            "Power..." item (or directly from the shell).
9: *   nxpower -cli status      report whether the kernel actually supports a
10: *                            power action yet (see "Known gap" below).
11: *   nxpower -cli shutdown    attempt a shutdown.
12: *   nxpower -cli reboot      attempt a reboot.
13: *
14: * KNOWN GAP — read before wiring this into anything (issue: no ticket yet):
15: *   Every OTHER piece of this program is a real, complete implementation:
16: *   the confirm-dialog UI, the two-step "click again to confirm" arm/disarm
17: *   flow (mirrors the deliberate friction of a real power switch), the CLI
18: *   parsing, and the plumbing that will carry the actual request down to the
19: *   kernel.  What does NOT exist anywhere in os1.h or any other file in this
20: *   codebase is a syscall that actually powers the machine off or resets it
21: *   — there is no OS1_power_*, no ACPI/PSCI wrapper, nothing.  Rather than
22: *   fabricate a call that would fail to link (a "real" API that silently
23: *   does nothing, or worse, misuse an unrelated syscall like killing pid 1
24: *   to fake it), nxpower declares the ONE symbol it needs,
25: *   `_sys_power_action`, as a WEAK extern (GCC/GNU-ld `__attribute__((weak))`
26: *   — a real, standard technique, not a hack specific to this file): if the
27: *   kernel/syscall-shim library does not yet define it, the symbol resolves
28: *   to a null function pointer at link time and nxpower reports "not
29: *   available" instead of crashing or lying; the day a real
30: *   `_sys_power_action(int action)` (0=shutdown, 1=reboot) lands in the
31: *   syscall shim — alongside the other `_sys_*` externs already declared in
32: *   os1.h, e.g. `_sys_window_enum`, `_sys_get_time` — nxpower starts working
33: *   with NO changes to this file. Suggested kernel-side contract:
34: *     - one new syscall number, handler gated by PLVL_ROOT/PLVL_MACHINE
35: *       (rebooting/halting the whole machine is strictly more privileged
36: *       than anything CAP_* currently gates — see nxperm.h's level model);
37: *     - action 0 = orderly shutdown, action 1 = reboot;
38: *     - return 0 on success, a negative errno if unsupported/denied, so
39: *       nxpower_action() below (which already handles a negative return)
40: *       needs no changes either way.
41: *
42: * SECURITY MODEL: nxpower adds no ambient authority of its own — the moment
43: * the kernel wires `_sys_power_action`, the same PLVL gate written above
44: * decides who may actually use it, exactly like every other stratified
45: * helper in this codebase; nxpower only ever relays the outcome.
46: */
47:#include <font_lib.h>
48:#include <input.h>
49:#include <os1.h>
50:#include <string.h>
51:
52:/* See "KNOWN GAP" above: real, standard weak-symbol bridge to a kernel
53: * syscall that does not exist yet.  `__attribute__((weak))` on an extern
54: * function means the linker accepts an undefined reference and resolves it
55: * to NULL instead of failing, IF nothing else in the link provides it. */
56:extern long _sys_power_action(int action) __attribute__((weak));
57:
58:#define NXPOWER_SHUTDOWN 0
59:#define NXPOWER_REBOOT 1
60:
61:/* nxpower_action - relay to the kernel if it exists; otherwise -1 (ENOSYS-
62: * shaped: "not available"), never fabricated success. */
63:static long nxpower_action(int action) {
64:  if (!_sys_power_action)
65:    return -1;
66:  return _sys_power_action(action);
67:}
68:
69:static int nxpower_available(void) { return _sys_power_action != 0; }
70:
71:/* ================================================================
72: *                              CLI mode
73: * ================================================================ */
74:static int nxs_streq(const char *a, const char *b) {
75:  return a && b && strncmp(a, b, 32) == 0;
76:}
77:
78:static int cli_main(int argc, char **argv) {
79:  if (argc < 1) {
80:    printf("usage: nxpower -cli status|shutdown|reboot\n");
81:    return 1;
82:  }
83:  if (nxs_streq(argv[0], "status")) {
84:    if (nxpower_available())
85:      printf("power control: available (kernel provides _sys_power_action)\n");
86:    else
87:      printf("power control: NOT available in this kernel build — see the "
88:             "\"KNOWN GAP\" note at the top of nxpower.c\n");
89:    return 0;
90:  }
91:  if (nxs_streq(argv[0], "shutdown")) {
92:    long r = nxpower_action(NXPOWER_SHUTDOWN);
93:    if (r == 0) { printf("nxpower: shutdown requested\n"); return 0; }
94:    printf("nxpower: shutdown not available (err %ld) — kernel has no power "
95:           "syscall yet\n", r);
96:    return 1;
97:  }
98:  if (nxs_streq(argv[0], "reboot")) {
99:    long r = nxpower_action(NXPOWER_REBOOT);
100:    if (r == 0) { printf("nxpower: reboot requested\n"); return 0; }
101:    printf("nxpower: reboot not available (err %ld) — kernel has no power "
102:           "syscall yet\n", r);
103:    return 1;
104:  }
105:  printf("nxpower: unknown command '%s'\n", argv[0]);
106:  printf("usage: nxpower -cli status|shutdown|reboot\n");
107:  return 1;
108:}
109:
110:/* ================================================================
111: *                              GUI mode
112: * ================================================================
113: * Same self-rendered-ARGB-framebuffer + font_lib technique as
114: * nxlauncher.c/nximage.c/nxsettings.c/nxbar.c — no shared header for it
115: * exists in this codebase yet, so it is duplicated here, consistent with
116: * every other GUI tool.
117: */
118:#define WIN_W 260
119:#define WIN_H 210
120:#define BTN_H 34
121:#define BTN_GAP 10
122:#define BTN_MARGIN 16
123:
124:#define CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS 4000 /* the armed state expires after this long */
125:
126:#define COL_BG 0xFF232328u
127:#define COL_TEXT 0xFFEAEAEEu
128:#define COL_TEXT_DIM 0xFF9A9AA4u
129:#define COL_BTN 0xFF34343Cu
130:#define COL_BTN_ARMED 0xFF8A2A2Au
131:#define COL_BTN_CANCEL 0xFF3C3C46u
132:#define COL_BTN_TEXT 0xFFFFFFFFu
133:
134:static uint32_t *g_fb;
135:static int g_ww = WIN_W, g_wh = WIN_H;
136:static int g_win = -1;
137:static struct font_ctx *g_font;
138:
139:static void fb_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h, uint32_t c) {
140:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return;
141:  int x2 = x + w, y2 = y + h;
142:  if (x2 > g_ww) x2 = g_ww;
143:  if (y2 > g_wh) y2 = g_wh;
144:  for (int j = (y < 0 ? 0 : y); j < y2; j++)
145:    for (int i = (x < 0 ? 0 : x); i < x2; i++)
146:      g_fb[j * g_ww + i] = c;
147:}
148:
149:static void buf_draw_glyph(int x, int y, uint32_t codepoint, uint32_t color) {
150:  if (!g_font) return;
151:  int idx = (int)codepoint - g_font->header.first_char;
152:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= g_font->header.num_chars) return;
153:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &g_font->glyphs[idx];
154:  uint8_t *bitmap = g_font->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
155:  int start_x = x + gi->x0;
156:  int start_y = y + g_font->header.ascent + gi->y0;
157:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
158:    for (int gx = 0; gx < gi->width; gx++) {
159:      uint8_t alpha = bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx];
160:      if (alpha > 64) {
161:        int px = start_x + gx, py = start_y + gy;
162:        if (px >= 0 && px < g_ww && py >= 0 && py < g_wh)
163:          g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = color;
164:      }
165:    }
166:  }
167:}
168:
169:static int buf_text_width(const char *s) {
170:  if (!g_font || !s) return 0;
171:  return font_string_width(g_font, s);
172:}
173:
174:static void buf_draw_text(int x, int y, const char *s, uint32_t color) {
175:  if (!g_font || !s) return;
176:  uint32_t cp;
177:  int consumed, cursor = x;
178:  size_t rem = strlen(s);
179:  const char *p = s;
180:  while (*p) {
181:    consumed = utf8_decode(p, rem, &cp);
182:    if (consumed <= 0) { p++; rem--; continue; }
183:    buf_draw_glyph(cursor, y, cp, color);
184:    int idx = (int)cp - g_font->header.first_char;
185:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < g_font->header.num_chars)
186:      cursor += g_font->glyphs[idx].advance;
187:    p += consumed;
188:    rem -= consumed;
189:  }
190:}
191:
192:static void draw_button(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char *label,
193:                        uint32_t bg) {
194:  fb_rect(x, y, w, h, bg);
195:  if (g_font) {
196:    int tw = buf_text_width(label);
197:    buf_draw_text(x + (w - tw) / 2, y + (h - 16) / 2, label, COL_BTN_TEXT);
198:  }
199:}
200:
201:enum { ARM_NONE = 0, ARM_SHUTDOWN, ARM_REBOOT };
202:static int g_armed = ARM_NONE;
203:static long g_armed_at_ms;
204:static char g_status_line[80] = "";
205:
206:static int g_btn_shutdown_y, g_btn_reboot_y, g_btn_cancel_y;
207:#define BTN_X BTN_MARGIN
208:#define BTN_W (WIN_W - 2 * BTN_MARGIN)
209:
210:static void redraw(void) {
211:  /* disarm automatically once the confirm window has passed */
212:  if (g_armed != ARM_NONE && get_time() - g_armed_at_ms > CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS) {
213:    g_armed = ARM_NONE;
214:  }
215:
216:  fb_rect(0, 0, g_ww, g_wh, COL_BG);
217:  if (g_font)
218:    buf_draw_text(BTN_MARGIN, 14, "System Power", COL_TEXT);
219:
220:  int y = 44;
221:  g_btn_shutdown_y = y;
222:  draw_button(BTN_X, y, BTN_W, BTN_H,
223:             g_armed == ARM_SHUTDOWN ? "Click again to confirm" : "Shut Down",
224:             g_armed == ARM_SHUTDOWN ? COL_BTN_ARMED : COL_BTN);
225:  y += BTN_H + BTN_GAP;
226:
227:  g_btn_reboot_y = y;
228:  draw_button(BTN_X, y, BTN_W, BTN_H,
229:             g_armed == ARM_REBOOT ? "Click again to confirm" : "Restart",
230:             g_armed == ARM_REBOOT ? COL_BTN_ARMED : COL_BTN);
231:  y += BTN_H + BTN_GAP;
232:
233:  g_btn_cancel_y = y;
234:  draw_button(BTN_X, y, BTN_W, BTN_H, "Cancel", COL_BTN_CANCEL);
235:  y += BTN_H + BTN_GAP;
236:
237:  if (g_status_line[0] && g_font)
238:    buf_draw_text(BTN_MARGIN, y, g_status_line, COL_TEXT_DIM);
239:
240:  window_blit(g_win, 0, 0, g_ww, g_wh, g_fb);
241:}
242:
243:static void do_action(int action) {
244:  long r = nxpower_action(action);
245:  if (r == 0) {
246:    /* A real kernel would already have cut power/reset by the time this
247:     * would run; if we are still here, treat it as success and just wait
248:     * to be torn down. */
249:    snprintf(g_status_line, sizeof(g_status_line), "requested.");
250:  } else {
251:    snprintf(g_status_line, sizeof(g_status_line),
252:             "not available in this kernel build (err %ld)", r);
253:  }
254:  g_armed = ARM_NONE;
255:}
256:
257:static void handle_click(int my) {
258:  if (my >= g_btn_shutdown_y && my < g_btn_shutdown_y + BTN_H) {
259:    if (g_armed == ARM_SHUTDOWN) do_action(NXPOWER_SHUTDOWN);
260:    else { g_armed = ARM_SHUTDOWN; g_armed_at_ms = get_time(); g_status_line[0] = '\0'; }
261:    return;
262:  }
263:  if (my >= g_btn_reboot_y && my < g_btn_reboot_y + BTN_H) {
264:    if (g_armed == ARM_REBOOT) do_action(NXPOWER_REBOOT);
265:    else { g_armed = ARM_REBOOT; g_armed_at_ms = get_time(); g_status_line[0] = '\0'; }
266:    return;
267:  }
268:  if (my >= g_btn_cancel_y && my < g_btn_cancel_y + BTN_H) {
269:    destroy_window(g_win);
270:    exit(0);
271:  }
272:}
273:
274:static int main_gui(void) {
275:  g_font = font_load("/fonts/Rewir-Light.off");
276:
277:  long di = OS1_display_info();
278:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF), sh = (int)((di) & 0xFFFF);
279:  if (sw <= 0) sw = 800;
280:  if (sh <= 0) sh = 600;
281:  int wx = (sw - WIN_W) / 2, wy = (sh - WIN_H) / 2;
282:
283:  g_fb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)WIN_W * WIN_H * 4);
284:  if (!g_fb) return 1;
285:  g_win = create_window(wx, wy, WIN_W, WIN_H, "nxpower");
286:  if (g_win < 0) return 1;
287:  /* Normal dialog window (no set_window_flags): native titlebar, closable
288:   * like any other app — Cancel and the titlebar close both just quit. */
289:
290:  if (!nxpower_available())
291:    snprintf(g_status_line, sizeof(g_status_line),
292:             "note: kernel has no power syscall yet (see nxpower.c)");
293:
294:  for (;;) {
295:    redraw();
296:    input_event_t ev;
297:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
298:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE && ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
299:          ev.mouse.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
300:        handle_click(ev.mouse.y);
301:      }
302:    }
303:    OS1_sleep(40);
304:  }
305:  return 0;
306:}
307:
308:/* ================================================================
309: *                               main
310: * ================================================================ */
311:int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
312:  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
313:    if (nxs_streq(argv[i], "-cli"))
314:      return cli_main(argc - (i + 1), &argv[i + 1]);
315:  }
316:  return main_gui();
317:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxproc.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxproc.c
3: * NEXS process-list ELF (ASTRA stratified service model).
4: *
5: * Usage (run from the shell, like /bin/stress):
6: *   nxproc                 snapshot the process table once and print it to
7: *                          stdout (the caller's TTY) — the canonical `ps`
8: *                          inline runtime.  No compositor window is created;
9: *                          every row goes through printf, the same fd 1 path
10: *                          the shell uses for its own prompt.
11: *   nxproc kill <pid>      terminate a process by pid (passes through the
12: *                          helper's thin kill wrapper).
13: *
14: * This is the INLINE counterpart to nxtop.c: nxtop opens a window and
15: * refreshes at ~1Hz, this ELF is one-shot and exits.  Both share the snapshot
16: * + signature + render logic via the header-only nxproc.h helper, so the
17: * displayed format and colours are identical regardless of which entry point
18: * the user picks.
19: */
20:#include "nxproc.h"
21:#include <os1.h>
22:#include <string.h>
23:
24:/*
25: * cmd_print - `nxproc` (no args) handler: one-shot snapshot + inline render.
26: *
27: * Fills a local array via nxproc_snapshot() and feeds it to
28: * nxproc_render_inline(), which writes the formatted, ANSI-coloured table to
29: * the caller's stdout.  No window is created; the shell's own terminal
30: * (which routed fd 1 here via the kernel's spawn-time fd inheritance)
31: * receives the bytes.  Returns 0 on success, 1 on syscall error.
32: */
33:static int cmd_print(void) {
34:  struct ps_info procs[NXPROC_MAX];
35:  int count = nxproc_snapshot(procs, NXPROC_MAX);
36:  if (count < 0) {
37:    printf("nxproc: failed to fetch process list (err %d)\n", count);
38:    return 1;
39:  }
40:  nxproc_render_inline(procs, count);
41:  return 0;
42:}
43:
44:/*
45: * cmd_kill - `nxproc kill <pid>` handler.
46: *
47: * Parses the pid argument, calls the helper's kill wrapper, and reports
48: * success/failure.  Returns a process exit code (0 ok, 1 error).  The kernel
49: * decides whether this caller may actually kill the target; we only relay the
50: * outcome.
51: */
52:static int cmd_kill(const char *pid_arg) {
53:  int pid = atoi(pid_arg);
54:  if (pid <= 0) {
55:    printf("nxproc: invalid pid '%s'\n", pid_arg);
56:    return 1;
57:  }
58:  int r = nxproc_kill(pid);
59:  if (r == 0) {
60:    printf("nxproc: killed pid %d\n", pid);
61:    return 0;
62:  }
63:  printf("nxproc: failed to kill pid %d (err %d)\n", pid, r);
64:  return 1;
65:}
66:
67:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
68:  /* nxproc kill <pid> */
69:  if (argc >= 3 && strncmp(argv[1], "kill", 5) == 0)
70:    return cmd_kill(argv[2]);
71:
72:  /* nxproc (no args): one-shot inline render on stdout. */
73:  if (argc < 2)
74:    return cmd_print();
75:
76:  printf("nxproc: bad arguments\n");
77:  printf("usage: nxproc | nxproc kill <pid>\n");
78:  return 1;
79:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxproc.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXPROC_H
2:#define _USER_NXPROC_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxproc.h
6: * NEXS stratified process-management helper (ASTRA service layer).
7: *
8: * A REUSABLE helper layer that both user and system apps may link against to
9: * inspect and act on the process table.  It is intentionally header-only
10: * (all routines `static inline`) so consumers pull it in without any extra
11: * object or link-rule churn in the Makefile.
12: *
13: * SECURITY MODEL: this layer adds NO ambient permission checks of its own.
14: * Every routine is a thin wrapper over an existing OS1 syscall, and the kernel
15: * already gates those syscalls per caller (e.g. kill is checked against the
16: * caller's capability/level).  Security is therefore "by caller" automatically:
17: * a privileged system app and an unprivileged user app calling the same helper
18: * get exactly the rights the kernel grants each of them — the helper neither
19: * widens nor narrows that.
20: *
21: * State integer to string mapping uses the values defined in the kernel's
22: * sched/process.h (PROC_CREATED=1, RUNNING=2, SLEEPING=3, ZOMBIE=4, DEAD=5,
23: * READY=6).  Any other value maps to "UNUSED".
24: *
25: * Consumers:
26: *   user/sys/bin/nxproc.c  — INLINE ELF: shell `ps`, one-shot stdout dump
27: *                            via nxproc_render_inline().  No compositor
28: *                            window is opened; every row goes through printf
29: *                            (write(1, ...)), so the shell's terminal shows
30: *                            the table.
31: *   user/sys/bin/nxtop.c   — WINDOWED realtime: opens its own compositor
32: *                            window and refreshes at ~1Hz via
33: *                            nxproc_render_if_changed(), redrawing only when
34: *                            the table actually changes.
35: */
36:
37:#include <os1.h>
38:
39:/* Hard cap on processes we ever snapshot/render in one pass (matches the
40: * kernel's MAX_PROCESSES ceiling used elsewhere in userland). */
41:#define NXPROC_MAX 32
42:
43:/*
44: * nxproc_snapshot - fill a caller-provided array with the live process table.
45: *
46: * out:       caller-owned array of at least `max` struct ps_info entries.
47: * max:       capacity of `out`; clamped to NXPROC_MAX internally.
48: *
49: * Thin wrapper over _sys_get_procs() (SYS_GET_PS).  Returns the number of
50: * entries written (0..max), or a negative value on syscall error.  No heap
51: * allocation; the snapshot is a point-in-time copy.
52: */
53:static inline int nxproc_snapshot(struct ps_info *out, int max) {
54:  if (!out || max <= 0)
55:    return 0;
56:  if (max > NXPROC_MAX)
57:    max = NXPROC_MAX;
58:  return _sys_get_procs(out, (size_t)max);
59:}
60:
61:/*
62: * nxproc_kill - request termination of a process by pid.
63: *
64: * pid: target process id.
65: *
66: * Thin wrapper over kill_process() (which routes to SYS_KILL).  Returns the
67: * syscall result (0 on success, negative on failure/denial).  The kernel
68: * enforces whether the *caller* is allowed to kill `pid`; this wrapper performs
69: * no check of its own.
70: */
71:static inline int nxproc_kill(int pid) { return kill_process(pid); }
72:
73:/*
74: * nxproc_state_str - map a numeric proc_state to a human-readable string.
75: *
76: * Values match kernel enum proc_state (kernel/sched/process.h).  Unknown values
77: * map to "UNUSED" so callers always get a printable, fixed token.
78: */
79:static inline const char *nxproc_state_str(int state) {
80:  switch (state) {
81:  case 1:
82:    return "CREATED";
83:  case 2:
84:    return "RUNNING";
85:  case 3:
86:    return "SLEEPING";
87:  case 4:
88:    return "ZOMBIE";
89:  case 5:
90:    return "DEAD";
91:  case 6:
92:    return "READY";
93:  case 7:
94:    return "STOPPED"; /* PROC_STOPPED (Phase 2 job control) */
95:  default:
96:    return "UNUSED";
97:  }
98:}
99:
100:/*
101: * nxproc_signature - fold the render-relevant fields of a snapshot into a
102: * single 64-bit value.
103: *
104: * procs: snapshot array.
105: * count: number of valid entries.
106: *
107: * Only the fields the rendered list actually shows (count, pid, state,
108: * priority, on_cpu) are mixed in, using a cheap FNV-1a-style rolling hash.
109: * Two snapshots that would render identically produce the same signature, so a
110: * renderer can compare against the previous signature and skip the redraw when
111: * nothing visible changed.  cpu_time is deliberately excluded: it ticks every
112: * sample and would defeat change-detection without altering the displayed
113: * columns.
114: */
115:static inline unsigned long nxproc_signature(const struct ps_info *procs,
116:                                             int count) {
117:  unsigned long h = 1469598103934665603UL; /* FNV-1a 64-bit offset basis */
118:  /* Mix the count itself so a process appearing/disappearing always shifts. */
119:  h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)count) * 1099511628211UL;
120:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
121:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].pid) * 1099511628211UL;
122:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].state) * 1099511628211UL;
123:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].priority) * 1099511628211UL;
124:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].on_cpu) * 1099511628211UL;
125:  }
126:  return h;
127:}
128:
129:/*
130: * nxproc_render_rows - write the formatted, ANSI-coloured process list to a
131: * window.
132: *
133: * win_id: compositor window id to write into.
134: * procs:  snapshot array.
135: * count:  number of valid entries.
136: *
137: * This is the rendering logic: a header row, a separator, then one colourised
138: * row per process (bright green
139: * for RUNNING, grey for SLEEPING, terminal default otherwise).  The screen is
140: * cleared first via ANSI so the window always reflects the current table.
141: *
142: * Unconditional: callers that want change-detection should gate this behind
143: * nxproc_render_if_changed() rather than calling it every tick.
144: */
145:/*
146: * nxproc_cpu_color - pick an ANSI 256-colour escape for the per-process CPU
147: * id column.
148: *
149: * cpu is clamped to [0, 255]; the cpu id IS the xterm-256 palette index, so
150: * every one of the 256 possible cpu ids gets its own swatch.  cpu == -1
151: * (process not currently on a cpu, sleeping/created/zombie/dead) returns a
152: * plain grey; the caller's STATE colour already telegraphs the situation, so
153: * the cpu cell should not steal the show.
154: */
155:static inline const char *nxproc_cpu_color(int cpu) {
156:  if (cpu < 0 || cpu > 255)
157:    return "\033[90m";
158:  /* Direct 1-to-1 mapping: cpu id is the xterm-256 palette index.  The
159:   * compositor's ANSI parser (\033[38;5;N in term.c:105) supports all 256
160:   * entries, so each of the 256 possible cpu ids gets its own swatch and
161:   * adjacent cpu ids are always distinguishable.  The palette is identity
162:   * (cpu → idx) by design: no remapping math, no saturation loss, the
163:   * digit carries the colour chosen by the system palette author. */
164:  static char buf[2][16];
165:  static int slot;
166:  slot ^= 1;
167:  char *p = buf[slot];
168:  int n = 0;
169:  p[n++] = '\033';
170:  p[n++] = '[';
171:  p[n++] = '3';
172:  p[n++] = '8';
173:  p[n++] = ';';
174:  p[n++] = '5';
175:  p[n++] = ';';
176:  int v = cpu;
177:  char tmp[3];
178:  int t = 0;
179:  if (v >= 100)
180:    tmp[t++] = '0' + (v / 100);
181:  v %= 100;
182:  if (v >= 10 || t > 0)
183:    tmp[t++] = '0' + (v / 10);
184:  v %= 10;
185:  tmp[t++] = '0' + v;
186:  for (int i = 0; i < t; i++)
187:    p[n++] = tmp[i];
188:  p[n++] = 'm';
189:  p[n] = '\0';
190:  return buf[slot];
191:}
192:
193:static inline void nxproc_render_rows(int win_id, const struct ps_info *procs,
194:                                      int count) {
195:  /* Clear screen using ANSI (handled by our compositor Terminal Emulator). */
196:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[H\033[J", 6);
197:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[1;34m", 7); /* bold blue header */
198:  printf_win(win_id, "%-4s %-16s %-10s %-4s %-3s\n", "PID", "NAME", "STATE",
199:             "PRIO", "CPU");
200:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4);
201:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "--------------------------------------------\n",
202:                    45);
203:
204:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
205:    const char *state_str = nxproc_state_str(procs[i].state);
206:    int cpu = procs[i].on_cpu;
207:
208:    /* Per-process STATE colour reflects the lifecycle.  READY (6) gets aqua so
209:     * a runnable-but-not-currently-running process stays distinct from
210:     * RUNNING (2, bold green).  ZOMBIE is muted brown; DEAD dim red. */
211:    const char *state_color;
212:    int state_len;
213:    if (procs[i].state == 2) {              /* RUNNING */
214:      state_color = "\033[1;32m"; state_len = 7;
215:    } else if (procs[i].state == 6) {       /* READY */
216:      state_color = "\033[38;5;51m"; state_len = 10;
217:    } else if (procs[i].state == 3) {       /* SLEEPING */
218:      state_color = "\033[90m"; state_len = 5;
219:    } else if (procs[i].state == 4) {       /* ZOMBIE */
220:      state_color = "\033[38;5;130m"; state_len = 11;
221:    } else if (procs[i].state == 5) {       /* DEAD */
222:      state_color = "\033[31m"; state_len = 5;
223:    } else {                                 /* CREATED=1 or anything else */
224:      state_color = "\033[37m"; state_len = 5;
225:    }
226:
227:    /* Identity columns in the STATE colour. */
228:    _sys_window_write(win_id, state_color, state_len);
229:    printf_win(win_id, "%-4d %-16s %-10s %-4d ", procs[i].pid, procs[i].name,
230:               state_str, procs[i].priority);
231:
232:    /* CPU column: pad left, then emit the digits in the per-cpu gradient.
233:     * The left-pad spaces stay in the STATE colour so only the digits carry
234:     * the cpu hue (the OPSERV-PROCS-02 #141 rule: "only the number is
235:     * coloured").  cpu == -1 (not on a cpu) gets grey for the whole cell.
236:     * The column is 3 chars wide (header "%-3s"), so any cpu ≥ 3 digits
237:     * overflows the cell visually — acceptable since 1000+ cores is
238:     * unrealistic for the current scheduler and the per-cpu palette still
239:     * distinguishes it. */
240:    if (cpu >= 0 && cpu <= 255) {
241:      const char *ccol = nxproc_cpu_color(cpu);
242:      int digits;
243:      if (cpu < 10)
244:        digits = 1;
245:      else if (cpu < 100)
246:        digits = 2;
247:      else
248:        digits = 3;
249:      /* pad = 3 - digits spaces in state colour */
250:      for (int s = 0; s < 3 - digits; s++)
251:        _sys_window_write(win_id, " ", 1);
252:      /* IMPORTANT: _sys_window_write takes an explicit byte count — passing 0
253:       * here would silently drop the cpu-colour escape and leave the digits
254:       * in the previous (state) colour.  Use strlen() on the NUL-terminated
255:       * escape so we always emit the whole "\033[38;5;Nm" sequence. */
256:      _sys_window_write(win_id, ccol, (unsigned long)strlen(ccol));
257:      printf_win(win_id, "%d", cpu);
258:      _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4);
259:      _sys_window_write(win_id, state_color, state_len);
260:    } else {
261:      printf_win(win_id, "%-3d", cpu);
262:    }
263:
264:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "\n", 1);
265:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4); /* Reset color */
266:  }
267:}
268:
269:/*
270: * nxproc_render_inline - emit the formatted, ANSI-coloured process list to the
271: * caller's stdout (fd 1, the TTY/window the program is running in).
272: *
273: * procs: snapshot array.
274: * count: number of valid entries.
275: *
276: * INLINE-STDOUT variant of nxproc_render_rows().  No compositor window is
277: * created: every row goes through printf(), which lib.c:429 routes to
278: * write(1, ...) — the same fd the kernel gives every spawned process as its
279: * TTY.  Used by `nxproc --inline` so the shell's `ps` command can dump the
280: * table onto its own terminal without spawning a window.  The ANSI escapes
281: * (clear-screen + colour SGRs) are identical to the windowed version so the
282: * caller's terminal emulator handles them the same way.
283: *
284: * Unconditional: one-shot callers (nxproc's `cmd_print`) render exactly once,
285: * so no change-detection wrapper exists for the inline variant — the windowed
286: * loop uses nxproc_render_if_changed() below.
287: */
288:static inline void nxproc_render_inline(const struct ps_info *procs,
289:                                       int count) {
290:  /* Inline render into the caller's controlling terminal.  Intentionally NO
291:   * "\033[H\033[J" clear-screen here: when `nxproc` runs as a child of the
292:   * shell (USR-TTY-01, inherited ctty) the clearing would wipe the shell's
293:   * prompt too, forcing the user to press Enter to repaint it.  The ANSI SGR
294:   * colour sequences below are otherwise identical to the windowed variant
295:   * so the terminal emulator in the compositor renders them the same way. */
296:  printf("\033[1;34m"); /* bold blue header */
297:  printf("%-4s %-16s %-10s %-4s %-3s\n", "PID", "NAME", "STATE", "PRIO", "CPU");
298:  printf("\033[0m");
299:  printf("--------------------------------------------\n");
300:
301:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
302:    const char *state_str = nxproc_state_str(procs[i].state);
303:    int cpu = procs[i].on_cpu;
304:
305:    const char *state_color;
306:    if (procs[i].state == 2) {              /* RUNNING */
307:      state_color = "\033[1;32m";
308:    } else if (procs[i].state == 6) {       /* READY */
309:      state_color = "\033[38;5;51m";
310:    } else if (procs[i].state == 3) {       /* SLEEPING */
311:      state_color = "\033[90m";
312:    } else if (procs[i].state == 4) {       /* ZOMBIE */
313:      state_color = "\033[38;5;130m";
314:    } else if (procs[i].state == 5) {       /* DEAD */
315:      state_color = "\033[31m";
316:    } else {                                 /* CREATED=1 or anything else */
317:      state_color = "\033[37m";
318:    }
319:
320:    printf("%s", state_color);
321:    printf("%-4d %-16s %-10s %-4d ", procs[i].pid, procs[i].name, state_str,
322:           procs[i].priority);
323:
324:    if (cpu >= 0 && cpu <= 255) {
325:      const char *ccol = nxproc_cpu_color(cpu);
326:      int digits;
327:      if (cpu < 10)
328:        digits = 1;
329:      else if (cpu < 100)
330:        digits = 2;
331:      else
332:        digits = 3;
333:      for (int s = 0; s < 3 - digits; s++)
334:        printf(" ");
335:      /* The colour escape is a NUL-terminated string built by
336:       * nxproc_cpu_color(); printf("%s", ...) emits the whole sequence
337:       * (lib.c printf goes through vsnprintf -> strlen(buf) -> write(1, ...),
338:       * so there is no count=0 silent-drop hazard like _sys_window_write). */
339:      printf("%s%d", ccol, cpu);
340:      printf("\033[0m");
341:      printf("%s", state_color);
342:    } else {
343:      printf("%-3d", cpu);
344:    }
345:
346:    printf("\n");
347:    printf("\033[0m");
348:  }
349:}
350:
351:/*
352: * nxproc_render_if_changed - OPTIMIZED render: snapshot the table and only
353: * rebuild+write the window when the visible content actually changed.
354: *
355: * win_id:   compositor window id to write into.
356: * last_sig: in/out pointer to the caller's "previous signature" state.  Seed it
357: *           with a sentinel (e.g. 0) on the first call; the helper updates it.
358: *
359: * Computes the snapshot's signature (see nxproc_signature) and compares it to
360: * *last_sig.  If unchanged, returns immediately WITHOUT touching the window, so
361: * an N-Hz refresh loop never busy-redraws an unchanged list.  If changed, it
362: * re-renders via nxproc_render_rows() and stores the new signature.
363: *
364: * Returns 1 if it (re)rendered, 0 if it skipped because nothing changed, or a
365: * negative value if the snapshot syscall failed.
366: */
367:static inline int nxproc_render_if_changed(int win_id,
368:                                           unsigned long *last_sig) {
369:  struct ps_info procs[NXPROC_MAX];
370:
371:  int count = nxproc_snapshot(procs, NXPROC_MAX);
372:  if (count < 0) {
373:    /* Surface the error once, but don't keep
374:     * rewriting it: fold the error into the signature so a persistent failure
375:     * is reported a single time. */
376:    unsigned long err_sig = ~0UL;
377:    if (last_sig && *last_sig != err_sig) {
378:      _sys_window_write(win_id, "Error fetching process list\n", 28);
379:      *last_sig = err_sig;
380:    }
381:    return count;
382:  }
383:
384:  unsigned long sig = nxproc_signature(procs, count);
385:  if (last_sig && *last_sig == sig)
386:    return 0; /* Unchanged since last render: skip the write entirely. */
387:
388:  nxproc_render_rows(win_id, procs, count);
389:  if (last_sig)
390:    *last_sig = sig;
391:  return 1;
392:}
393:
394:#endif /* _USER_NXPROC_H */
395:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxreg.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxreg.c
3: * Registry Editor (Control Panel)
4: *
5: * Windowed, read-only registry viewer: enumerates every key in the global
6: * registry (OS1_registry_enum) and renders "key = value" rows through the
7: * window terminal emulator (ANSI + printf_win), refreshing only when the
8: * registry content actually changes — same render-if-changed pattern as
9: * nxproc.h/nxtop.  Editing keys is future work (needs an input line editor).
10: *
11: * Reads are intentionally ungated kernel-side; writes elsewhere are gated by
12: * CAP_REG_WRITE (kernel/lib/registry.c) — this tool never writes.
13: *
14: * Known issues:
15: *   USR-BLOAT-01/02 (W2 BAD-IMPL·PERF) ~500KB ELF due to unconditional
16: *                  stb_image/stb_easy_font in lib.o and retained DWARF debug.
17: */
18:#include <os1.h>
19:
20:#define ENUM_BUF_SZ 2048 /* newline-separated key list from the kernel */
21:#define VAL_BUF_SZ 128   /* single value buffer */
22:
23:/* Tiny FNV-1a over the rendered content, to skip unchanged redraws. */
24:static unsigned long nxreg_hash(unsigned long h, const char *s) {
25:  while (*s) {
26:    h ^= (unsigned char)*s++;
27:    h *= 1099511628211UL;
28:  }
29:  return h;
30:}
31:
32:/*
33: * render - clear the window and print one "key = value" row per registry key.
34: * Returns the content hash so the caller can skip identical frames.
35: */
36:static unsigned long render(int win_id, int do_write) {
37:  char keys[ENUM_BUF_SZ];
38:  char val[VAL_BUF_SZ];
39:  unsigned long h = 1469598103934665603UL;
40:
41:  int n = OS1_registry_enum(keys, sizeof(keys));
42:  if (n < 0) {
43:    if (do_write)
44:      _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[H\033[Jregistry enum failed\n", 27);
45:    return ~0UL;
46:  }
47:
48:  /* First pass just hashes; the caller re-invokes with do_write=1 on change. */
49:  if (do_write) {
50:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[H\033[J", 6);
51:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[1;34m", 7);
52:    printf_win(win_id, "%-24s %s\n", "KEY", "VALUE");
53:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4);
54:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "----------------------------------------\n", 42);
55:  }
56:
57:  char *p = keys;
58:  while (*p) {
59:    char *nl = p;
60:    while (*nl && *nl != '\n')
61:      nl++;
62:    int last = (*nl == '\0');
63:    *nl = '\0';
64:
65:    if (*p) {
66:      val[0] = '\0';
67:      if (OS1_registry_get(p, val, sizeof(val)) != 0)
68:        val[0] = '\0'; /* directory node or vanished key: show empty */
69:      h = nxreg_hash(h, p);
70:      h = nxreg_hash(h, val);
71:      if (do_write)
72:        printf_win(win_id, "%-24s %s\n", p, val);
73:    }
74:
75:    if (last)
76:      break;
77:    p = nl + 1;
78:  }
79:  return h;
80:}
81:
82:int main(void) {
83:  int win_id = create_window(100, 100, 400, 300, "Control Panel");
84:  if (win_id < 0)
85:    return 1;
86:
87:  unsigned long last = 0; /* impossible hash: guarantees the first render */
88:  while (1) {
89:    unsigned long sig = render(win_id, 0);
90:    if (sig != last) {
91:      render(win_id, 1);
92:      last = sig;
93:    }
94:    OS1_sleep(1000);
95:  }
96:
97:  return 0;
98:}
99:

1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxres.c
3: * NEXS display + compositor-look tool (GFX-DYN-01 / DIR-07).
4: *
5: * Usage:
6: *   nxres                  print the current desktop resolution + applied
7: *                          style/theme/background
8: *   nxres <width> <height> set the desktop resolution at runtime
9: *   nxres style <name>     nexs | classic | material | glass | minimal | retro
10: *   nxres theme <name>     light | dark
11: *   nxres bg <name>        black | red | green | yellow | blue | magenta |
12: *                          cyan | white | gray | bred | … | bwhite
13: *                          ('blue' is the default nexs gradient)
14: *
15: * Exercises the dynamic-display chain from userland: SYS_SET_DISPLAY_MODE ->
16: * gpu_set_mode() (virtio-gpu recreates the scanout) -> compositor_resize().
17: *
18: * The actual style/theme/bg get/set logic (name tables, id lookup, the
19: * SYS_SET_STYLE call, the registry mirror) lives in nxres.h so every other
20: * app (nxsettings, nxbar, nxntfy_srv, nxui, nxlauncher, ...) shares this
21: * exact implementation instead of re-deriving it — this file is now just
22: * the CLI/stdout wrapper around it.
23: */
24:#include <os1.h>
25:
26:#include "nxres.h"
27:
28:static int is_digit_str(const char *s) {
29:  if (!s || !*s)
30:    return 0;
31:  for (const char *p = s; *p; p++)
32:    if (*p < '0' || *p > '9')
33:      return 0;
34:  return 1;
35:}
36:
37:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
38:  if (argc < 2) {
39:    /* Show current desktop resolution and the applied style/theme/bg
40:     * (single canonical getter: nxres_get_* in nxres.h). */
41:    long info = OS1_display_info();
42:    int w = (int)((info >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
43:    int h = (int)(info & 0xFFFF);
44:    printf("nxres: current desktop %dx%d\n", w, h);
45:
46:    char buf[32] = {0};
47:    if (nxres_get_style(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
48:      printf("       style       %s\n", buf);
49:    else
50:      printf("       style       unknown\n");
51:
52:    if (nxres_get_theme(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
53:      printf("       theme       %s\n", buf);
54:    else
55:      printf("       theme       unknown\n");
56:
57:    if (nxres_get_background(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
58:      printf("       background  %s\n", buf);
59:    else
60:      printf("       background  unknown\n");
61:
62:    printf("\nusage: nxres <w> <h> | nxres zoom <pct> | nxres style|theme|bg "
63:           "<name>\n");
64:    return 0;
65:  }
66:
67:  /* nxres style <name> */
68:  if (argc >= 3 && strncmp(argv[1], "style", 6) == 0) {
69:    int r = nxres_set_style(argv[2]);
70:    if (r == -1) {
71:      printf("nxres: unknown style '%s'\n", argv[2]);
72:      return 1;
73:    }
74:    if (r == 0) {
75:      printf("nxres: style -> %s\n", argv[2]);
76:      return 0;
77:    }
78:    printf("nxres: set_style failed\n");
79:    return 1;
80:  }
81:
82:  /* nxres zoom <percent> */
83:  if (argc >= 3 && strncmp(argv[1], "zoom", 5) == 0) {
84:    int p = atoi(argv[2]);
85:    if (OS1_display_set_zoom(p) == 0) {
86:      printf("nxres: zoom -> %d%%\n", p);
87:      return 0;
88:    }
89:    printf("nxres: set_zoom failed\n");
90:    return 1;
91:  }
92:
93:  /* nxres theme <name> */
94:  if (argc >= 3 && strncmp(argv[1], "theme", 6) == 0) {
95:    int r = nxres_set_theme(argv[2]);
96:    if (r == -1) {
97:      printf("nxres: unknown theme '%s'\n", argv[2]);
98:      return 1;
99:    }
100:    if (r == 0) {
101:      printf("nxres: theme -> %s\n", argv[2]);
102:      return 0;
103:    }
104:    printf("nxres: set_theme failed\n");
105:    return 1;
106:  }
107:
108:  /* nxres bg <name> */
109:  if (argc >= 3 && strncmp(argv[1], "bg", 2) == 0) {
110:    int r = nxres_set_background(argv[2]);
111:    if (r == -1) {
112:      printf("nxres: unknown background '%s'\n", argv[2]);
113:      return 1;
114:    }
115:    if (r == 0) {
116:      printf("nxres: background -> %s\n", argv[2]);
117:      return 0;
118:    }
119:    printf("nxres: set_background failed\n");
120:    return 1;
121:  }
122:
123:  /* nxres <w> <h> */
124:  if (argc >= 3 && is_digit_str(argv[1]) && is_digit_str(argv[2])) {
125:    int w = atoi(argv[1]);
126:    int h = atoi(argv[2]);
127:    if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) {
128:      printf("nxres: invalid size '%s x %s'\n", argv[1], argv[2]);
129:      return 1;
130:    }
131:    int r = OS1_display_set_mode(w, h);
132:    if (r == 0) {
133:      printf("nxres: display set to %dx%d\n", w, h);
134:      return 0;
135:    }
136:    printf("nxres: failed to set %dx%d (err %d)\n", w, h, r);
137:    return 1;
138:  }
139:
140:  printf("nxres: bad arguments\n");
141:  printf("usage: nxres <w> <h> | nxres zoom <pct> | nxres style|theme|bg "
142:         "<name>\n");
143:  return 1;
144:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxres.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXRES_H
2:#define _USER_NXRES_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxres.h
6: * Compositor look (style/theme/background) — single canonical getter/setter
7: * pair, shared by every consumer instead of each one re-reading raw registry
8: * keys and re-deriving id<->name mappings on its own (nxsettings, nxbar,
9: * nxntfy_srv, nxui and nxlauncher used to do this independently, and only
10: * nxres.c's own copy was ever kept in sync with the kernel enum order).
11: *
12: * Same pattern as nxinfo.h/nxperm.h/nxproc.h: a header-only, static-inline
13: * helper layer over the plain OS1_ syscalls, dropped into any translation
14: * unit that needs it.
15: *
16: * Ground truth: kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c's SYS_SET_STYLE handler
17: * writes style.name/theme.color/background.name into the registry itself on
18: * every successful change (any caller, not just nxres) — see
19: * kernel/lib/registry.c registry_caller_owner() for why a ROOT-level service
20: * changing the look does not get its write rejected as "not the owner".
21: * The registry mirror here is kept as a second write for callers running
22: * against a kernel build that predates that mirror; it is idempotent
23: * (same value) against a kernel that already wrote it.
24: *
25: * Change propagation: a successful nxres_set_*() posts through the EXISTING
26: * async notification transport — send()/IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY, the exact
27: * mechanism nxntfy_srv.c already uses for popups — instead of a new bespoke
28: * broadcast mechanism or per-frame registry polling:
29: *   - the user-facing popup goes to srv.notify_pid via notify(), same as
30: *     any other system notification;
31: *   - a SILENT ping (same IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY, tagged with IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC
32: *     in data2, posix_types.h, so it is never confused with a real user
33: *     notification) goes to every singleton system service's registered
34: *     pid — srv.dock_pid (nxui), srv.bar_pid (nxbar), srv.launcher_pid
35: *     (nxlauncher) — published by init the same way it already publishes
36: *     srv.notify_pid (register_service_pid, user/sys/bin/nxinit.c) and
37: *     refreshed on every respawn so the ping can never land on a corpse's
38: *     stale pid.  A windowed app sees this ping as INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED
39: *     from its EXISTING input_poll_event() loop (input.h/lib.c) — NOT a
40: *     second try_recv() loop: input_poll_event() is the single consumer of
41: *     an app's IPC mailbox, and a competing try_recv() elsewhere in the
42: *     same app would silently steal keyboard/mouse messages before
43: *     input_poll_event ever saw them (the bug in this feature's first cut).
44: *     nxntfy_srv is the one exception — it has no input_poll_event loop of
45: *     its own (its window is passive/click-through), so it checks
46: *     msg.data2 directly in its own recv()/try_recv() loop, which already
47: *     is that app's single mailbox consumer.
48: * nxsettings is on the same ping list even though it is not an init-
49: * supervised singleton: it self-registers "srv.settings_pid" when its
50: * window opens (main_gui() in nxsettings.c) so an EXTERNAL change (made via
51: * `nxres` from a shell, or by another app) still repaints its already-open
52: * window instead of only taking effect the next time it is opened. */
53:#include <os1.h>
54:#include <string.h>
55:#include <style_names.h>
56:
57:/* The well-known registry keys init.c publishes each singleton system
58: * service's live pid under (register_service_pid).  srv.notify_pid is
59: * deliberately NOT here: it already gets the user-facing notify() popup
60: * above, and a second silent ping would just be a wasted send(). */
61:static const char *const nxres_look_ping_targets[] = {
62:    "srv.dock_pid",
63:    "srv.bar_pid",
64:    "srv.launcher_pid",
65:    /* nxsettings is not init-supervised (user-launched, not a singleton
66:     * service), so it self-registers this key on window creation instead of
67:     * init publishing it — see main_gui() in nxsettings.c.  Last-opened
68:     * instance wins if more than one is ever open at once. */
69:    "srv.settings_pid",
70:    /* Same self-registration pattern as nxsettings: nxfilem is user-launched
71:     * (not a singleton), so it publishes its own pid here on window
72:     * creation (see fm_ui_init in ui.c) so an external style/theme/bg change
73:     * repaints its already-open window instead of only the next launch. */
74:    "srv.filem_pid",
75:    /* nxshell self-registers srv.shell_pid on window creation (nxshell.c);
76:     * last-opened shell wins if several are open — others still track theme
77:     * via the per-loop nxres_theme_is_light() poll in the shell event loop. */
78:    "srv.shell_pid",
79:};
80:#define NXRES_LOOK_PING_NTARGETS                                               \
81:  (int)(sizeof(nxres_look_ping_targets) / sizeof(nxres_look_ping_targets[0]))
82:
83:/* nxres_broadcast_look - silent IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY ping to every registered
84: * system service so its already-running event loop can re-derive its
85: * palette.  Best-effort: a service that is not up yet (registry key absent)
86: * or whose pid is momentarily stale (mid-respawn) is simply skipped — the
87: * next nxres_set_*() call (or the service's own startup read) catches it. */
88:static inline void nxres_broadcast_look(void) {
89:  for (int i = 0; i < NXRES_LOOK_PING_NTARGETS; i++) {
90:    char pidbuf[16];
91:    if (OS1_registry_get(nxres_look_ping_targets[i], pidbuf, sizeof(pidbuf)) !=
92:        0)
93:      continue;
94:    int pid = atoi(pidbuf);
95:    if (pid <= 0)
96:      continue;
97:    struct ipc_message msg = {0};
98:    msg.type = IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY;
99:    msg.data2 = IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC;
100:    send(pid, &msg);
101:  }
102:}
103:
104:/* nxres_get_style/theme/background - the current APPLIED look, as last
105: * mirrored into the registry by SYS_SET_STYLE (kernel-side) or a prior
106: * nxres_set_*() call.  Returns 0 and fills 'buf', or -1 if the key is
107: * absent (never set since boot — should not happen post registry_init). */
108:static inline int nxres_get_style(char *buf, size_t sz) {
109:  return OS1_registry_get("style.name", buf, sz);
110:}
111:static inline int nxres_get_theme(char *buf, size_t sz) {
112:  return OS1_registry_get("theme.color", buf, sz);
113:}
114:static inline int nxres_get_background(char *buf, size_t sz) {
115:  return OS1_registry_get("background.name", buf, sz);
116:}
117:
118:/* nxres_theme_is_light - the one boolean every app's palette switch actually
119: * needs.  Defaults to dark (0) on any read failure or unrecognised value,
120: * matching registry_init's "dark" default. */
121:static inline int nxres_theme_is_light(void) {
122:  char val[8] = {0};
123:  return nxres_get_theme(val, sizeof(val)) == 0 &&
124:         strncmp(val, "light", 6) == 0;
125:}
126:
127:/* os1_bg_colors - the 16 background anchor colours (compositor's
128: * backgrounds[].bg_color field, not the gradient stops) as parallel ARGB
129: * literals, indexed by the same id that BG_* enums use in kernel/graphics/
130: * compositor_style.h.  Same role as os1_bg_names above: the userland-
131: * facing name table that the kernel's style/theme/background mirror in the
132: * registry is keyed by.  The pattern — kernel enum + kernel struct +
133: * style_names.h os1_bg_names + this os1_bg_colors — is the SAME pattern
134: * the codebase already established for the *names*, just extended one step
135: * further so a userland app that wants to paint against the current
136: * background does not have to invent its own colour-resolution code
137: * (nxbar's "X" glyph, nxui's dock-tile bevel, any future cutout button
138: * that should read as a hole through to the desktop).  Order MUST match
139: * os1_bg_names above.  If a background is added, the chain to update is
140: * identical to the names' chain: kernel enum -> kernel backgrounds[] ->
141: * style_names.h (here) -> os1_bg_names -> os1_bg_colors. */
142:static const unsigned int os1_bg_colors[] = {
143:    0xFF121212u, /* BG_BLACK         */
144:    0xFFB33A3Au, /* BG_RED           */
145:    0xFF3E8E5Bu, /* BG_GREEN         */
146:    0xFFC9A227u, /* BG_YELLOW        */
147:    0xFF143060u, /* BG_BLUE          */
148:    0xFF8E44ADu, /* BG_MAGENTA       */
149:    0xFF2A9D8Fu, /* BG_CYAN          */
150:    0xFFD8D8DCu, /* BG_WHITE         */
151:    0xFF4A4A52u, /* BG_GRAY          */
152:    0xFFE8604Fu, /* BG_BRIGHT_RED    */
153:    0xFF52B788u, /* BG_BRIGHT_GREEN  */
154:    0xFFF2C94Cu, /* BG_BRIGHT_YELLOW */
155:    0xFF4A78C0u, /* BG_BRIGHT_BLUE   */
156:    0xFFB07CD1u, /* BG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA*/
157:    0xFF56C9C9u, /* BG_BRIGHT_CYAN   */
158:    0xFFF5F5F7u, /* BG_BRIGHT_WHITE  */
159:};
160:#define OS1_BG_COLORS_COUNT                                                    \
161:  (int)(sizeof(os1_bg_colors) / sizeof(os1_bg_colors[0]))
162:
163:/* nxres_bg_color - the ARGB colour of the currently applied background,
164: * as the userland-side lookup against the registry's "background.name"
165: * key (the same name every other app — nxsettings, nxlauncher, etc. —
166: * already reads).  Resolves the name to an id via the shared
167: * os1_bg_names table, then reads the colour out of the parallel
168: * os1_bg_colors table — the same two-step name-to-X pattern nxsettings
169: * already uses for background NAMES (NXS_BG = os1_bg_names), just
170: * extended one step further so callers can pick the actual anchor
171: * colour without re-implementing the table themselves.  Returns the dark
172: * default (0xFF1C1C24u) on any read failure, unknown name, or
173: * out-of-range id, matching the dark default every other "look" getter
174: * in this header falls back to.  Inherits the change-propagation path of
175: * the rest of the look: a successful nxres_set_background() pings every
176: * registered service via INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED, and the app re-derives
177: * its palette on that ping. */
178:static inline unsigned int nxres_bg_color(void) {
179:  char val[32] = {0};
180:  if (nxres_get_background(val, sizeof(val)) != 0)
181:    return 0xFF1C1C24u; /* read failed */
182:  for (int i = 0; i < OS1_BG_COUNT && i < OS1_BG_COLORS_COUNT; i++) {
183:    if (strncmp(val, os1_bg_names[i], 32) == 0)
184:      return os1_bg_colors[i];
185:  }
186:  return 0xFF1C1C24u; /* unknown name */
187:}
188:
189:/* nxres_name_to_id - linear lookup in one of the os1_*_names[] tables
190: * (style_names.h).  Exact match up to and including the NUL; -1 if absent. */
191:static inline int nxres_name_to_id(const char *name, const char *const *list,
192:                                   int n) {
193:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
194:    if (strncmp(name, list[i], 32) == 0)
195:      return i;
196:  return -1;
197:}
198:
199:/* nxres_set_style/theme/background - resolve 'name' against the shared
200: * tables, apply it via SYS_SET_STYLE (OS1_display_set_style/background),
201: * and mirror the name into the registry on success.  Returns 0 on success,
202: * -1 for an unknown name, -2 if the syscall itself failed. */
203:static inline int nxres_set_style(const char *name) {
204:  int id = nxres_name_to_id(name, os1_style_names, OS1_STYLE_COUNT);
205:  if (id < 0)
206:    return -1;
207:  if (OS1_display_set_style(id, -1) != 0)
208:    return -2;
209:  OS1_registry_set("style.name", os1_style_names[id]);
210:  notify("Style", os1_style_names[id]);
211:  nxres_broadcast_look();
212:  return 0;
213:}
214:static inline int nxres_set_theme(const char *name) {
215:  int id = nxres_name_to_id(name, os1_theme_names, OS1_THEME_COUNT);
216:  if (id < 0)
217:    return -1;
218:  if (OS1_display_set_style(-1, id) != 0)
219:    return -2;
220:  OS1_registry_set("theme.color", os1_theme_names[id]);
221:  notify("Theme", os1_theme_names[id]);
222:  nxres_broadcast_look();
223:  return 0;
224:}
225:static inline int nxres_set_background(const char *name) {
226:  int id = nxres_name_to_id(name, os1_bg_names, OS1_BG_COUNT);
227:  if (id < 0)
228:    return -1;
229:  if (OS1_display_set_background(id) != 0)
230:    return -2;
231:  OS1_registry_set("background.name", os1_bg_names[id]);
232:  notify("Background", os1_bg_names[id]);
233:  nxres_broadcast_look();
234:  return 0;
235:}
236:
237:#endif /* _USER_NXRES_H */

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxsettings.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxsettings.c
3: * NEXS settings & system-info aggregator (ASTRA stratified service model).
4: *
5: * nxsettings groups, in one place, the read/write surfaces already exposed by
6: * the other stratified helpers/tools (nxres, nxinfo.h, nxperm.h, nxproc.h,
7: * nxmemstat.h, nxnotify/nxntfy_srv's registry log) instead of making the user
8: * hunt across nxres/nxproc/nxperm/nxmemstat/nxnotify separately.  It holds NO
9: * policy of its own: every value shown or changed goes through the same
10: * kernel-gated syscall the standalone tool would use, so nxsettings is
11: * "secure by caller" exactly like its siblings.
12: *
13: * Two front ends, one shared data layer:
14: *
15: *   GUI (default):  a normal, resizable compositor window (native titlebar,
16: *     like nxlauncher) with a left sidebar of sections and a right content
17: *     pane, drawn with the same custom-ARGB-framebuffer + font_lib approach
18: *     as nxlauncher.c/nximage.c (no printf_win — this window owns its pixels).
19: *
20: *   CLI (`nxsettings -cli [section]`):  a one-shot textual dump on stdout,
21: *     following the plain-text style of nxinfo/nxperm/nxproc/nxres.  With no
22: *     section argument it prints everything; with one, only that section.
23: *     Sections: display | style | system | perm | proc | mem | notify.
24: *
25: * Discovery / launch model (see nxexec.h, nxshell.c): nxsettings needs NO
26: * special wiring.  Dropped into /sys/bin, it is found by nxlauncher's live
27: * /sys/bin scan (grid tile) and by the shell's generic spawn_search_args()
28: * fallback (typing `nxsettings` or `nxsettings -cli`).  run_foreground()'s
29: * window-ownership debounce already tells the two modes apart: the GUI build
30: * opens its own window and detaches; `-cli` opens none and stays hosted in
31: * the caller's terminal — exactly like `nxproc` vs `nxproc kill <pid>` today.
32: *
33: * Sections and the module each one is backed by:
34: *   Display       -> OS1_display_info/set_mode/set_zoom          (nxres.c)
35: *   Style & Theme -> OS1_display_set_style                       (nxres.c)
36: *   Background    -> OS1_display_set_background                  (nxres.c)
37: *   System        -> nxinfo.h pure readers                       (nxinfo.h)
38: *   Permissions   -> OS1_identity + nxperm.h tables               (nxperm.h)
39: *   Processes     -> nxproc_snapshot/kill                        (nxproc.h)
40: *   Memory        -> nxmemstat_snapshot (needs ROOT; see nxmemstat.h)
41: *   Notifications -> sys.ntfy.log.* registry ring                (nxnotify.c)
42: *
43: * SECURITY MODEL: identical to every helper it wraps — nxsettings widens
44: * nothing.  A caller without CAP_REG_WRITE/ROOT still sees its own identity
45: * and whatever read-only data the kernel already grants; a failed
46: * nxmemstat_snapshot() (non-ROOT caller) is reported inline instead of
47: * crashing the section.
48: */
49:#include "nxinfo.h"
50:#include "nxmemstat.h"
51:#include "nxperm.h"
52:#include "nxproc.h"
53:#include "nxres.h"
54:#include <font_lib.h>
55:#include <input.h>
56:#include <os1.h>
57:#include <stdlib.h>
58:#include <string.h>
59:
60:/* ================================================================
61: *                       Shared: notification log
62: * ================================================================
63: * Minimal reader over the sys.ntfy.log.* ring nxntfy_srv maintains (record
64: * format "<pid>|<sev>|<state>|<text>" — see nxnotify.c/nxntfy_srv.c).  Kept
65: * flat (no per-pid grouping) since both the GUI panel and the CLI dump only
66: * need a quick recent-activity glance; `nxnotify list` remains the grouped,
67: * authoritative view.
68: */
69:#define NXS_NOTIFY_MAX 16
70:
71:struct nxs_nrec {
72:  int pid;
73:  int sev;
74:  char state; /* 'U' unread, 'R' read */
75:  char text[48];
76:};
77:
78:static int nxs_notify_fetch(struct nxs_nrec *out, int max) {
79:  char keys[640];
80:  int n = OS1_registry_enum_under("sys.ntfy.log.", keys, sizeof(keys));
81:  if (n <= 0)
82:    return 0;
83:  int cnt = 0;
84:  char key[64];
85:  int k = 0;
86:  for (const char *p = keys; cnt < max; p++) {
87:    if (*p == '\n' || *p == '\0') {
88:      if (k > 0) {
89:        key[k] = '\0';
90:        char val[80];
91:        if (OS1_registry_get(key, val, sizeof(val)) == 0) {
92:          const char *q = val;
93:          out[cnt].pid = atoi(q);
94:          while (*q && *q != '|')
95:            q++;
96:          if (*q)
97:            q++;
98:          out[cnt].sev = atoi(q);
99:          while (*q && *q != '|')
100:            q++;
101:          if (*q)
102:            q++;
103:          out[cnt].state = *q ? *q : 'U';
104:          while (*q && *q != '|')
105:            q++;
106:          if (*q)
107:            q++;
108:          int t = 0;
109:          for (; *q && t < 47; q++)
110:            out[cnt].text[t++] = *q;
111:          out[cnt].text[t] = '\0';
112:          cnt++;
113:        }
114:      }
115:      k = 0;
116:      if (*p == '\0')
117:        break;
118:    } else if (k < (int)sizeof(key) - 1) {
119:      key[k++] = *p;
120:    }
121:  }
122:  return cnt;
123:}
124:
125:static const char *nxs_sev_str(int sev) {
126:  return sev == 2 ? "ERR " : sev == 1 ? "WARN" : "info";
127:}
128:static const char *nxs_state_str(char st) {
129:  return st == 'R' ? "read  " : "unread";
130:}

155:    {1280, 800},

170:/* Style/theme/bg name tables: the shared os1_style_names/os1_theme_names/

174:#define NXS_STYLES os1_style_names

186:  return a && b && strncmp(a, b, 32) == 0;
187:}

189:static void cli_display(void) {
190:  long di = OS1_display_info();
191:  int w = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
192:  int h = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
193:  printf("== Display ==\n");
194:  printf("resolution: %dx%d\n", w, h);
195:  printf("presets:    ");
196:  for (int i = 0; i < NXS_NRES; i++)
197:    printf("%dx%d%s", NXS_RES_PRESETS[i].w, NXS_RES_PRESETS[i].h,
198:           i + 1 < NXS_NRES ? "  " : "\n");
199:  printf("(nxsettings -cli does not change resolution/zoom; use the GUI or "
200:         "'nxres <w> <h>' / 'nxres zoom <pct>')\n");
201:}
202:
203:static void cli_style(void) {
204:  printf("== Style & Theme ==\n");
205:  printf("styles: ");
206:  for (int i = 0; i < NXS_NSTYLES; i++)
207:    printf("%s%s", NXS_STYLES[i], i + 1 < NXS_NSTYLES ? " " : "\n");
208:  printf("themes: ");
209:  for (int i = 0; i < NXS_NTHEMES; i++)
210:    printf("%s%s", NXS_THEMES[i], i + 1 < NXS_NTHEMES ? " " : "\n");
211:  printf("backgrounds: ");
212:  for (int i = 0; i < NXS_NBG; i++)
213:    printf("%s%s", NXS_BG[i], i + 1 < NXS_NBG ? " " : "\n");
214:
215:  char sbuf[32] = "unknown", tbuf[32] = "unknown", bbuf[32] = "unknown";
216:  nxres_get_style(sbuf, sizeof(sbuf));
217:  nxres_get_theme(tbuf, sizeof(tbuf));
218:  nxres_get_background(bbuf, sizeof(bbuf));
219:  printf("applied: style=%s theme=%s background=%s\n", sbuf, tbuf, bbuf);
220:  printf("(use 'nxres style|theme|bg <name>' or the GUI to change it)\n");
221:}

234:static void cli_proc(void) {
235:  printf("== Processes ==\n");
236:  struct ps_info procs[NXPROC_MAX];
237:  int count = nxproc_snapshot(procs, NXPROC_MAX);
238:  if (count < 0) {
239:    printf("nxsettings: failed to fetch process list (err %d)\n", count);
240:    return;
241:  }
242:  nxproc_render_inline(procs, count);
243:}

245:static void cli_mem(void) {
246:  printf("== Memory ==\n");
247:  struct os1_sysstats s;
248:  long r = nxmemstat_snapshot(&s);
249:  if (r < 0) {
250:    printf("OS1_sys_stats denied (need ROOT) or failed (err %ld)\n", r);
251:    return;
252:  }
253:  unsigned long free_mb = (unsigned long)((s.pmm_free_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
254:  unsigned long tot_mb = (unsigned long)((s.pmm_total_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
255:  printf("pmm:    free %lu / %lu MB\n", free_mb, tot_mb);
256:  printf("kheap:  in-use %lu KB  hi %lu KB  live %lu\n",
257:         (unsigned long)(s.km_bytes_in_use / 1024UL),
258:         (unsigned long)(s.km_high_water_bytes / 1024UL),
259:         (unsigned long)s.km_live_allocs);
260:  printf("sched:  cpus %lu  runnable %lu  zombies %lu  ctxsw %lu\n",
261:         (unsigned long)s.sched_ncpu, (unsigned long)s.sched_runnable,
262:         (unsigned long)s.sched_zombie_count,
263:         (unsigned long)s.sched_ctx_switches);
264:  printf("objs:   FILE %lu  PROC %lu  REGKEY %lu  WINDOW %lu\n",
265:         (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_FILE],
266:         (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS],
267:         (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY],
268:         (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW]);
269:}
270:
271:static void cli_notify(void) {
272:  printf("== Notifications ==\n");
273:  struct nxs_nrec recs[NXS_NOTIFY_MAX];
274:  int n = nxs_notify_fetch(recs, NXS_NOTIFY_MAX);
275:  if (n == 0) {
276:    printf("no notifications\n");
277:    return;
278:  }
279:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
280:    printf("PID %-5d [%s][%s] %s\n", recs[i].pid, nxs_sev_str(recs[i].sev),
281:           nxs_state_str(recs[i].state), recs[i].text);
282:}

284:static int cli_main(int argc, char **argv) {
285:  if (argc < 1) {
286:    cli_display();
287:    printf("\n");
288:    cli_style();
289:    printf("\n");
290:    cli_system();
291:    printf("\n");
292:    cli_perm();
293:    printf("\n");
294:    cli_proc();
295:    printf("\n");
296:    cli_mem();
297:    printf("\n");
298:    cli_notify();
299:    return 0;
300:  }
301:  const char *sec = argv[0];
302:  if (nxs_streq(sec, "display"))
303:    cli_display();
304:  else if (nxs_streq(sec, "style"))
305:    cli_style();
306:  else if (nxs_streq(sec, "system"))
307:    cli_system();
308:  else if (nxs_streq(sec, "perm"))
309:    cli_perm();
310:  else if (nxs_streq(sec, "proc"))
311:    cli_proc();
312:  else if (nxs_streq(sec, "mem"))
313:    cli_mem();
314:  else if (nxs_streq(sec, "notify"))
315:    cli_notify();
316:  else {
317:    printf("nxsettings: unknown section '%s'\n", sec);
318:    printf(
319:        "usage: nxsettings -cli [display|style|system|perm|proc|mem|notify]\n");
320:    return 1;
321:  }
322:  return 0;
323:}

420:/* ------------------------- Button hit-table ------------------------- */
421:struct nxs_btn {
422:  int x, y, w, h;
423:  int action;
424:  long arg;
425:};
426:#define MAX_BTNS 64
427:static struct nxs_btn g_btns[MAX_BTNS];
428:static int g_btn_n;
429:
430:static void add_btn(int x, int y, int w, int h, int action, long arg) {
431:  if (g_btn_n >= MAX_BTNS)
432:    return;
433:  g_btns[g_btn_n].x = x;
434:  g_btns[g_btn_n].y = y;
435:  g_btns[g_btn_n].w = w;
436:  g_btns[g_btn_n].h = h;
437:  g_btns[g_btn_n].action = action;
438:  g_btns[g_btn_n].arg = arg;
439:  g_btn_n++;
440:}

442:/* ============================================================
443: *                        Pixel helpers
444: * (identical technique to nxlauncher.c's fb_rrect/buf_draw_*)
445: * ============================================================ */
446:
447:static void fb_rrect(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint32_t c) {
448:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
449:    return;
450:  if (r < 0)
451:    r = 0;
452:  if (r > w / 2)
453:    r = w / 2;
454:  if (r > h / 2)
455:    r = h / 2;
456:  for (int j = 0; j < h; j++) {
457:    for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
458:      int ccx = -1, ccy = 0;
459:      if (i < r && j < r) {
460:        ccx = r;
461:        ccy = r;
462:      } else if (i >= w - r && j < r) {
463:        ccx = w - r - 1;
464:        ccy = r;
465:      } else if (i < r && j >= h - r) {
466:        ccx = r;
467:        ccy = h - r - 1;
468:      } else if (i >= w - r && j >= h - r) {
469:        ccx = w - r - 1;
470:        ccy = h - r - 1;
471:      }
472:      if (ccx >= 0) {
473:        int dx = i - ccx, dy = j - ccy;
474:        if (dx * dx + dy * dy > r * r)
475:          continue;
476:      }
477:      int px = x + i, py = y + j;
478:      if (px >= 0 && px < g_ww && py >= 0 && py < g_wh)
479:        g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = c;
480:    }
481:  }
482:}
483:
484:static void buf_draw_glyph(int x, int y, uint32_t codepoint, uint32_t color) {
485:  if (!g_font)
486:    return;
487:  int idx = (int)codepoint - g_font->header.first_char;
488:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= g_font->header.num_chars)
489:    return;
490:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &g_font->glyphs[idx];
491:  uint8_t *bitmap = g_font->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
492:  int start_x = x + gi->x0;
493:  int start_y = y + g_font->header.ascent + gi->y0;
494:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
495:    for (int gx = 0; gx < gi->width; gx++) {
496:      uint8_t alpha = bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx];
497:      if (alpha > 64) {
498:        int px = start_x + gx, py = start_y + gy;
499:        if (px >= 0 && px < g_ww && py >= 0 && py < g_wh)
500:          g_fb[py * g_ww + px] = color;
501:      }
502:    }
503:  }
504:}
505:
506:static int buf_text_width(const char *s) {
507:  if (!g_font || !s)
508:    return 0;
509:  return font_string_width(g_font, s);
510:}
511:
512:static void buf_draw_text(int x, int y, const char *s, uint32_t color) {
513:  if (!g_font || !s)
514:    return;
515:  uint32_t cp;
516:  int consumed, cursor = x;
517:  size_t rem = strlen(s);
518:  const char *p = s;
519:  while (*p) {
520:    consumed = utf8_decode(p, rem, &cp);
521:    if (consumed <= 0) {
522:      p++;
523:      rem--;
524:      continue;
525:    }
526:    buf_draw_glyph(cursor, y, cp, color);
527:    int idx = (int)cp - g_font->header.first_char;
528:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < g_font->header.num_chars)
529:      cursor += g_font->glyphs[idx].advance;
530:    p += consumed;
531:    rem -= consumed;
532:  }
533:}
534:
535:/* ui_text: draw one line at (x, *y), then advance *y by LINE_H. */
536:static void ui_text(int x, int *y, const char *s, uint32_t color) {
537:  buf_draw_text(x, *y, s, color);
538:  *y += LINE_H;
539:}
540:
541:/* ui_button: draw a rounded button + centred label AND register its hit
542: * area, in one call — the button table is rebuilt every redraw so drawing
543: * and hit-testing can never drift apart. */
544:static void ui_button(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char *label, int action,
545:                      long arg, int active) {
546:  fb_rrect(x, y, w, h, 6, active ? g_col_btn_active : g_col_btn);
547:  if (g_font) {
548:    int tw = buf_text_width(label);
549:    int tx = x + (w - tw) / 2;
550:    if (tx < x + 2)
551:      tx = x + 2;
552:    int ty = y + (h - 16) / 2;
553:    buf_draw_text(tx, ty, label, g_col_btn_text);
554:  }
555:  add_btn(x, y, w, h, action, arg);
556:}

562:static void render_sidebar(void) {
563:  fb_rrect(0, 0, SIDEBAR_W, g_wh, 0, g_col_sidebar_bg);
564:  int y = PAD;
565:  for (int i = 0; i < SEC_COUNT; i++) {
566:    int ry = y + i * ROW_H;
567:    if (i == g_section)
568:      fb_rrect(6, ry, SIDEBAR_W - 12, ROW_H - 6, 6, g_col_sidebar_sel);
569:    buf_draw_text(18, ry + (ROW_H - 6 - 16) / 2, SEC_LABELS[i],
570:                  i == g_section ? g_col_accent : g_col_text);
571:    add_btn(6, ry, SIDEBAR_W - 12, ROW_H - 6, ACT_SECTION, i);
572:  }
573:}

575:static void render_resolution_menu(int cx, int *y, int current_w,
576:                                   int current_h) {
577:  int bx = cx;
578:  int btn_w = 92;
579:  int btn_h = 28;
580:  int gap = 8;
581:  int row_h = 34;
582:  int max_x = g_ww - PAD;
583:
584:  ui_text(cx, y, "Presets:", g_col_text_dim);
585:
586:  for (int i = 0; i < NXS_NRES; i++) {
587:    char lbl[24];
588:
589:    snprintf(lbl, sizeof(lbl), "%dx%d", NXS_RES_PRESETS[i].w,
590:             NXS_RES_PRESETS[i].h);
591:
592:    if (bx + btn_w > max_x) {
593:      bx = cx;
594:      *y += row_h;
595:    }
596:
597:    int active = (current_w == NXS_RES_PRESETS[i].w &&
598:                  current_h == NXS_RES_PRESETS[i].h);
599:
600:    ui_button(bx, *y, btn_w, btn_h, lbl, ACT_RES_PRESET, i, active);
601:
602:    bx += btn_w + gap;
603:  }
604:
605:  *y += row_h;
606:}

679:static void render_system(void) {
680:  int cx = CONTENT_X, y = PAD;
681:  char line[160], cwd[128];
682:
683:  ui_text(cx, &y, "System", g_col_accent);
684:  y += 6;
685:
686:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s %s", NXINFO_OS_NAME, NXINFO_OS_VERSION);
687:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
688:
689:  long up_ms = nxinfo_uptime_ms();
690:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "Uptime: %ld ms (%ld s)", up_ms, up_ms / 1000);
691:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
692:

695:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "Active processes: <unavailable> (err %d)",

697:  else

699:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
700:
701:  int w = 0, h = 0;
702:  nxinfo_display(&w, &h);
703:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "Resolution: %dx%d", w, h);
704:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
705:
706:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "PID: %d", get_pid());
707:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
708:
709:  if (getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd)) != 0)
710:    cwd[0] = '\0';
711:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "CWD: %s", cwd[0] ? cwd : "?");
712:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
713:}

749:static void render_proc(void) {
750:  int cx = CONTENT_X, y = PAD;
751:  ui_text(cx, &y, "Processes", g_col_accent);
752:  y += 6;
753:
754:  struct ps_info procs[NXPROC_MAX];
755:  int count = nxproc_snapshot(procs, NXPROC_MAX);
756:  if (count < 0) {
757:    char line[64];
758:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "error reading process table (%d)", count);
759:    ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text_dim);
760:    return;
761:  }
762:
763:  char hdr[64];
764:  snprintf(hdr, sizeof(hdr), "%-5s %-14s %-9s %-4s", "PID", "NAME", "STATES",
765:           "PRIO");
766:  ui_text(cx, &y, hdr, g_col_text_dim);
767:  y += 2;
768:
769:  int row_h = 24;
770:  int max_rows = (g_wh - y - PAD) / row_h;
771:  if (max_rows > count)
772:    max_rows = count;
773:  if (max_rows < 0)
774:    max_rows = 0;
775:
776:  for (int i = 0; i < max_rows; i++) {
777:    char line[80];
778:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%-5d %-14s %-9s %-4d", procs[i].pid,
779:             procs[i].name, nxproc_state_str(procs[i].state),
780:             procs[i].priority);
781:    buf_draw_text(cx, y + 3, line, g_col_text);
782:    ui_button(g_ww - 74, y - 2, 58, 22, "Kill", ACT_KILL, procs[i].pid, 0);
783:    y += row_h;
784:  }
785:  if (count > max_rows) {
786:    char more[48];
787:    snprintf(more, sizeof(more), "... and %d more (resize the window)",
788:             count - max_rows);
789:    ui_text(cx, &y, more, g_col_text_dim);
790:  }
791:}

793:static void render_mem(void) {
794:  int cx = CONTENT_X, y = PAD;
795:  ui_text(cx, &y, "Memory", g_col_accent);
796:  y += 6;
797:
798:  struct os1_sysstats s;
799:  long r = nxmemstat_snapshot(&s);
800:  if (r < 0) {
801:    char line[80];
802:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line),
803:             "OS1_sys_stats denied (needs ROOT) or failed (%ld)", r);
804:    ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text_dim);
805:    return;
806:  }
807:
808:  char line[128];
809:  unsigned long free_mb = (unsigned long)((s.pmm_free_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
810:  unsigned long tot_mb = (unsigned long)((s.pmm_total_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
811:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "PMM:   free %lu / %lu MB", free_mb, tot_mb);
812:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
813:
814:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "kheap: in-use %lu KB  hi %lu KB  live %lu",
815:           (unsigned long)(s.km_bytes_in_use / 1024UL),
816:           (unsigned long)(s.km_high_water_bytes / 1024UL),
817:           (unsigned long)s.km_live_allocs);
818:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
819:
820:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "sched: cpu %lu  runnable %lu  zombie %lu",
821:           (unsigned long)s.sched_ncpu, (unsigned long)s.sched_runnable,
822:           (unsigned long)s.sched_zombie_count);
823:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
824:
825:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "ctxsw: %lu totali",
826:           (unsigned long)s.sched_ctx_switches);
827:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
828:
829:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line),
830:           "objs:  FILE %lu  PROC %lu  REGKEY %lu  WINDOW %lu",
831:           (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_FILE],
832:           (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS],
833:           (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY],
834:           (unsigned long)s.obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW]);
835:  ui_text(cx, &y, line, g_col_text);
836:}
