838:static void render_notify(void) {
839:  int cx = CONTENT_X, y = PAD;
840:  ui_text(cx, &y, "Recent notifications", g_col_accent);
841:  y += 6;
842:
843:  struct nxs_nrec recs[NXS_NOTIFY_MAX];
844:  int n = nxs_notify_fetch(recs, NXS_NOTIFY_MAX);
845:  if (n == 0) {
846:    ui_text(cx, &y, "no notifications", g_col_text_dim);
847:    return;
848:  }
849:  int max_rows = (g_wh - y - PAD) / LINE_H;
850:  if (max_rows > n)
851:    max_rows = n;
852:  for (int i = 0; i < max_rows; i++) {
853:    char line[96];
854:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "PID %-5d [%s][%s] %s", recs[i].pid,
855:             nxs_sev_str(recs[i].sev), nxs_state_str(recs[i].state),
856:             recs[i].text);
857:    uint32_t col = recs[i].sev == 2   ? 0xFFFF8080u
858:                   : recs[i].sev == 1 ? 0xFFFFD080u
859:                                      : g_col_text;
860:    ui_text(cx, &y, line, col);
861:  }
862:}

864:/* ============================================================
865: *                       Redraw + input
866: * ============================================================ */
867:
868:static void redraw(void) {
869:  fb_rrect(0, 0, g_ww, g_wh, 0, g_col_bg);
870:  g_btn_n = 0;
871:  render_sidebar();
872:  switch (g_section) {
873:  case SEC_DISPLAY:
874:    render_display();
875:    break;
876:  case SEC_STYLE:
877:    render_style();
878:    break;
879:  case SEC_SYSTEM:
880:    render_system();
881:    break;
882:  case SEC_PERM:
883:    render_perm();
884:    break;
885:  case SEC_PROC:
886:    render_proc();
887:    break;
888:  case SEC_MEM:
889:    render_mem();
890:    break;
891:  case SEC_NOTIFY:
892:    render_notify();
893:    break;
894:  default:
895:    break;
896:  }
897:}
898:
899:static void dispatch(int action, long arg) {
900:  switch (action) {
901:  case ACT_SECTION:
902:    g_section = (int)arg;
903:    break;
904:  case ACT_RES_PRESET:
905:    if (arg >= 0 && arg < NXS_NRES)
906:      OS1_display_set_mode(NXS_RES_PRESETS[arg].w, NXS_RES_PRESETS[arg].h);
907:    break;
908:  case ACT_ZOOM_DEC:
909:    g_zoom_pct -= 10;
910:    if (g_zoom_pct < 50)
911:      g_zoom_pct = 50;
912:    OS1_display_set_zoom(g_zoom_pct);
913:    break;
914:  case ACT_ZOOM_INC:
915:    g_zoom_pct += 10;
916:    if (g_zoom_pct > 300)
917:      g_zoom_pct = 300;
918:    OS1_display_set_zoom(g_zoom_pct);
919:    break;
920:  case ACT_ZOOM_RESET:
921:    g_zoom_pct = 100;
922:    OS1_display_set_zoom(g_zoom_pct);
923:    break;
924:  case ACT_STYLE:
925:    if (arg >= 0 && arg < NXS_NSTYLES) {
926:      g_cur_style = (int)arg;
927:      nxres_set_style(NXS_STYLES[arg]);
928:    }
929:    break;
930:  case ACT_THEME:
931:    if (arg >= 0 && arg < NXS_NTHEMES) {
932:      g_cur_theme = (int)arg;
933:      nxres_set_theme(NXS_THEMES[arg]);
934:      /* aggiorna la palette dell'interfaccia */
935:      load_theme_colors(
936:          g_cur_theme == 0 ? 1 : 0); /* 0=light, 1=dark nel registro */
937:    }
938:    break;
939:  case ACT_BACKGROUND:
940:    if (arg >= 0 && arg < NXS_NBG) {
941:      g_cur_bg = (int)arg;
942:      nxres_set_background(NXS_BG[arg]);
943:    }
944:    break;
945:  case ACT_KILL:
946:    if (arg > 0)
947:      nxproc_kill((int)arg);
948:    break;
949:  default:
950:    break;
951:  }
952:}
953:
954:static void handle_click(int mx, int my) {
955:  for (int i = g_btn_n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
956:    struct nxs_btn *b = &g_btns[i];
957:    if (mx >= b->x && mx < b->x + b->w && my >= b->y && my < b->y + b->h) {
958:      dispatch(b->action, b->arg);
959:      return;
960:    }
961:  }
962:}
963:
964:static void reinit_window(int ww, int wh) {
965:  if (ww < MIN_WIN_W)
966:    ww = MIN_WIN_W;
967:  if (wh < MIN_WIN_H)
968:    wh = MIN_WIN_H;
969:  uint32_t *nb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)ww * (size_t)wh * 4u);
970:  if (nb) {
971:    free(g_fb);
972:    g_fb = nb;
973:  }
974:  g_ww = ww;
975:  g_wh = wh;
976:}
977:
978:static int main_gui(void) {
979:  g_font = font_load("/fonts/Rewir-Light.off");
980:
981:  long di = OS1_display_info();
982:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
983:  int sh = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
984:  if (sw <= 0)
985:    sw = 800;
986:  if (sh <= 0)
987:    sh = 600;
988:
989:  int ww = (sw * 7) / 10;
990:  int wh = (sh * 7) / 10;
991:  if (ww > 760)
992:    ww = 760;
993:  if (wh > 520)
994:    wh = 520;
995:  if (ww < MIN_WIN_W)
996:    ww = MIN_WIN_W;
997:  if (wh < MIN_WIN_H)
998:    wh = MIN_WIN_H;
999:  int wx = (sw - ww) / 2, wy = (sh - wh) / 2;
1000:
1001:  g_fb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)ww * (size_t)wh * 4u);
1002:  if (!g_fb)
1003:    return 1;
1004:  g_ww = ww;
1005:  g_wh = wh;
1006:
1007:  g_win = create_window(wx, wy, ww, wh, "nxsettings");
1008:  if (g_win < 0)
1009:    return 1;
1010:  /* Normal window (no set_window_flags): native titlebar, free drag/resize,
1011:   * same posture as nxlauncher — not top_most, not passive. */
1012:
1013:  /* Self-register this pid as the live "srv.settings_pid" endpoint
1014:   * (nxres.h's nxres_look_ping_targets) so an EXTERNAL style/theme/bg change
1015:   * (`nxres` from a shell, or any other caller of SYS_SET_STYLE) reaches
1016:   * this already-open window instead of only applying the next time
1017:   * nxsettings is launched.  nxsettings is not init-supervised, so this is
1018:   * a plain self-registration (no respawn hazard to guard against — see
1019:   * init.c's register_service_pid for the singleton-service equivalent). */
1020:  {
1021:    char pidbuf[16];
1022:    snprintf(pidbuf, sizeof(pidbuf), "%d", get_pid());
1023:    OS1_registry_set("srv.settings_pid", pidbuf);
1024:  }
1025:
1026:  /* Carica il tema corrente (nxres_theme_is_light: getter canonico condiviso,
1027:   * nxres.h) — il registro è scritto sia dal kernel (SYS_SET_STYLE) sia da
1028:   * nxres_set_theme() dopo un cambio riuscito. */
1029:  int theme_light = nxres_theme_is_light();
1030:  load_theme_colors(theme_light);
1031:  /* Imposta g_cur_theme di conseguenza (0=light, 1=dark nell'array NXS_THEMES)
1032:   */
1033:  g_cur_theme = theme_light ? 0 : 1;
1034:  /* Idem per style/background, cosi la selezione evidenziata nella sezione
1035:   * Style & Theme rispecchia lo stato realmente applicato fin dall'apertura. */
1036:  {
1037:    char buf[32] = {0};
1038:    if (nxres_get_style(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
1039:      g_cur_style = nxres_name_to_id(buf, NXS_STYLES, NXS_NSTYLES);
1040:    if (nxres_get_background(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
1041:      g_cur_bg = nxres_name_to_id(buf, NXS_BG, NXS_NBG);
1042:  }
1043:
1044:  for (;;) {
1045:    redraw();
1046:    window_blit(g_win, 0, 0, g_ww, g_wh, g_fb);
1047:    /* SCHED-STACK-ISO: init pumps the compositor via flush(); blit marks
1048:     * damage — no nested compositor_render() here. */
1049:
1050:    input_event_t ev;
1051:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
1052:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE && ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
1053:          ev.mouse.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
1054:        handle_click(ev.mouse.x, ev.mouse.y);
1055:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE && ev.resize.w > 0 &&
1056:                 ev.resize.h > 0) {
1057:        reinit_window(ev.resize.w, ev.resize.h);
1058:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED) {
1059:        /* External style/theme/bg change (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h),
1060:         * surfaced through this SAME input_poll_event() loop — not a second
1061:         * try_recv() (that stole this window's mouse/keyboard events in an
1062:         * earlier version of this feature; see nxres.h's header comment). */
1063:        theme_light = nxres_theme_is_light();
1064:        load_theme_colors(theme_light);
1065:        g_cur_theme = theme_light ? 0 : 1;
1066:        char buf[32] = {0};
1067:        if (nxres_get_style(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
1068:          g_cur_style = nxres_name_to_id(buf, NXS_STYLES, NXS_NSTYLES);
1069:        if (nxres_get_background(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
1070:          g_cur_bg = nxres_name_to_id(buf, NXS_BG, NXS_NBG);
1071:      }
1072:    }
1073:    OS1_sleep(40);
1074:  }
1075:  return 0;
1076:}
1077:
1078:/* ================================================================
1079: *                               main
1080: * ================================================================ */
1081:
1082:int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
1083:  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
1084:    if (nxs_streq(argv[i], "-cli"))
1085:      return cli_main(argc - (i + 1), &argv[i + 1]);
1086:  }
1087:  return main_gui();
1088:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxshell.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxshell.c
3: * Interactive Graphical Shell
4: *
5: * Creates a compositor window that acts as a TTY.  Keyboard input arrives as
6: * IPC and is drained through input_poll_event() (the same path nxui/nxsettings
7: * use for resize and compositor-look notifications).  Commands are tokenized
8: * in place and dispatched from a small builtin table; anything else is resolved
9: * against /bin then /sys/bin via nxexec_spawn_search().
10: *
11: * Theme: palette follows nxres_theme_is_light() (nxres.h), refreshed on
12: * INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED (nxres_broadcast_look) and on a cheap per-loop poll
13: * so every open shell instance tracks external theme changes even when more
14: * than one is running.
15: *
16: * Resize: INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE -> OS1_window_resize() for a crisp terminal surface
17: * (compositor reflows the cell grid via term_resize).
18: *
19: * MODIFICA 2026-09-01:
20: *   - Priorità ai built‑in senza prefisso: se l'utente digita un comando
21: *     della whitelist (ls, cd, pwd, ...), la shell usa direttamente il built‑in
22: *     corrispondente (nxls, nxcd, ...) senza cercare il binario esterno.
23: *     I binari esterni vengono eseguiti solo per i comandi NON nella whitelist.
24: *   - La mappa `get_builtin_name` traduce il nome base nel nome built‑in con
25: *     prefisso `nx`.
26: */
27:#include "nxexec.h"
28:#include "nxjobs.h"
29:#include "nxline.h"
30:#include "nxperm.h"
31:#include "nxres.h"
32:#include <fcntl.h>
33:#include <input.h>
34:#include <os1.h>
35:#include <stdlib.h>
36:#include <string.h>
37:#include <unistd.h>

101:static void shell_on_resize(int w, int h) {
102:  if (my_window < 0 || w <= 0 || h <= 0)
103:    return;

107:    h = MIN_WIN_H;

116:static int tokenize(char *s, char *argv[], int max) {
117:  return cmdline_split(s, argv, max);
118:}
119:
120:static int spawn_search_args(int argc, char *argv[], char *out_path) {
121:  struct spawn_redir redir[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR];
122:  int fds[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR], nredir = 0, nfds = 0;
123:  if (nxexec_strip_redirections(&argc, argv, redir, &nredir, fds, &nfds) != 0)
124:    return -1;
125:  if (argc == 0) {
126:    print("nxshell: no command\n");
127:    for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++)
128:      close(fds[i]);
129:    return -1;
130:  }
131:  int pid = nxexec_spawn_search_redir(argc, argv, out_path, /*detached=*/0,
132:                                      redir, nredir);
133:  for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++)
134:    close(fds[i]);
135:  return pid;
136:}

138:static int run_foreground(int pid) { return nxexec_run_foreground(pid); }
139:
140:static void run_fg_job(int pid, const char *cmd) {
141:  if (nxexec_run_foreground_ex(pid, &g_last_status) == NXEXEC_JOB_STOPPED) {
142:    int id = nxjobs_add(&g_jobs, pid, cmd);
143:    nxjobs_mark_stopped(&g_jobs, nxjobs_find(&g_jobs, id));
144:    printf("[%d]+ Stopped   %s\n", id, cmd);
145:  }
146:}
147:
148:static int spawn_with_extra_redir(int argc, char *argv[], int extra_child_fd,
149:                                  int extra_parent_fd, char *out_path) {
150:  struct spawn_redir redir[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR];
151:  int fds[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR], nredir = 0, nfds = 0;
152:  if (nxexec_strip_redirections(&argc, argv, redir, &nredir, fds, &nfds) != 0)
153:    return -1;
154:  if (argc == 0) {
155:    for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++)
156:      close(fds[i]);
157:    return -1;
158:  }
159:  if (extra_parent_fd >= 0 && nredir < SPAWN_MAX_REDIR) {
160:    redir[nredir].child_fd = extra_child_fd;
161:    redir[nredir].parent_fd = extra_parent_fd;
162:    redir[nredir].source_pid = 0;
163:    nredir++;
164:  }
165:  int pid = nxexec_spawn_search_redir(argc, argv, out_path, /*detached=*/0,
166:                                      redir, nredir);
167:  for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++)
168:    close(fds[i]);
169:  return pid;
170:}

172:static void run_pipeline(int pipe_idx, int argc, char *argv[], int background) {
173:  argv[pipe_idx] = 0;
174:  int lhs_argc = pipe_idx;
175:  char **rhs_argv = &argv[pipe_idx + 1];
176:  int rhs_argc = argc - pipe_idx - 1;
177:  if (lhs_argc <= 0 || rhs_argc <= 0) {
178:    print("nxshell: syntax error near '|'\n");
179:    return;
180:  }
181:  int lhs_is_echo = (strcmp(argv[0], "nxecho") == 0);
182:
183:  char rpath[SPAWN_PATH_MAX];
184:  int wfd = -1;
185:  int rpid = nxexec_spawn_pipe_consumer(rhs_argc, rhs_argv, rpath, &wfd);
186:  if (rpid <= 0) {
187:    if (!lhs_is_echo) {
188:      print("nxshell: cannot create pipe\n");
189:      return;
190:    }
191:    const char *tmp = "/home/.nxpipe";
192:    char buf[CMD_MAX];
193:    int n = 0;
194:    for (int i = 1; i < lhs_argc && n < (int)sizeof(buf) - 1; i++) {
195:      if (i > 1 && n < (int)sizeof(buf) - 1)
196:        buf[n++] = ' ';
197:      for (const char *p = argv[i]; *p && n < (int)sizeof(buf) - 1; p++)
198:        buf[n++] = *p;
199:    }
200:    if (n < (int)sizeof(buf))
201:      buf[n++] = '\n';
202:    if (OS1_fs_write(tmp, buf, n, 0) < 0) {
203:      printf("nxshell: cannot stage pipe temp %s\n", tmp);
204:      return;
205:    }
206:    int tfd = open(tmp, O_RDONLY);
207:    if (tfd < 0) {
208:      OS1_fs_unlink(tmp);
209:      return;
210:    }
211:    char tpath[SPAWN_PATH_MAX];
212:    int tpid = spawn_with_extra_redir(rhs_argc, rhs_argv, 0, tfd, tpath);
213:    close(tfd);
214:    if (tpid > 0) {
215:      run_fg_job(tpid, rhs_argv[0]);
216:    } else {
217:      g_last_status = 127;
218:      printf("Unknown command: %s\n", rhs_argv[0]);
219:    }
220:    OS1_fs_unlink(tmp);
221:    return;
222:  }
223:
224:  int lpid = -1;
225:  if (rpid > 0 && wfd >= 0) {
226:    if (lhs_is_echo) {
227:      for (int i = 1; i < lhs_argc; i++) {
228:        if (i > 1)
229:          write(wfd, " ", 1);
230:        write(wfd, argv[i], strlen(argv[i]));
231:      }
232:      write(wfd, "\n", 1);
233:    } else {
234:      char lpath[SPAWN_PATH_MAX];
235:      lpid = spawn_with_extra_redir(lhs_argc, argv, 1, wfd, lpath);
236:    }
237:  }
238:  if (wfd >= 0)
239:    close(wfd);
240:
241:  if (rpid > 0) {
242:    if (background) {
243:      int id = nxjobs_add(&g_jobs, rpid, rhs_argv[0]);
244:      printf("[%d] %d\n", id, rpid);
245:    } else {
246:      run_fg_job(rpid, rhs_argv[0]);
247:    }
248:  } else {
249:    g_last_status = 127;
250:    printf("Unknown command: %s\n", rhs_argv[0]);
251:  }
252:  if (lpid > 0)
253:    OS1low_process_wait(lpid);
254:}

256:static int skip_bin_entry(const char *name) {
257:  if (!name || !*name)
258:    return 1;
259:  const char *dot = strrchr(name, '.');
260:  if (!dot)
261:    return 0;
262:  return strcmp(dot, ".c") == 0 || strcmp(dot, ".h") == 0 ||
263:         strcmp(dot, ".o") == 0 || strcmp(dot, ".old") == 0;
264:}

266:static void help_list_programs(const char *dir) {
267:  char buf[1024];
268:  int n = list_dir(dir, buf, sizeof(buf) - 1);
269:  if (n <= 0)
270:    return;
271:
272:  buf[n] = '\0';
273:
274:  char *save = NULL;
275:  int col = 0;
276:
277:  for (char *tok = strtok_r(buf, " \t", &save); tok;
278:       tok = strtok_r(NULL, " \t", &save)) {
279:
280:    if (skip_bin_entry(tok))
281:      continue;
282:
283:    printf("%-16s", tok);
284:
285:    col++;
286:    if (col == 4) {
287:      printf("\n");
288:      col = 0;
289:    }
290:  }
291:
292:  if (col != 0)
293:    printf("\n");
294:}

341:  print("  a ; b           run b after a, whatever a returned\n");
342:  print("  a && b          run b only if a succeeded\n");
343:  print("  a || b          run b only if a failed\n");
344:  print("\n\033[1;33mPrograms in /sys/bin:\033[0m\n");
345:  help_list_programs("/sys/bin");
346:  print("\n\033[1;33mPrograms in Bin are not listed for brevity\033[0m\n");
347:  print("\nType any program name to run it (searches /bin, then /sys/bin).\n");
348:}
349:
350:static void print_prompt_only(void) {
351:  char prompt_cwd[128];
352:  if (getcwd(prompt_cwd, sizeof(prompt_cwd)) != 0)
353:    prompt_cwd[0] = '\0';
354:  printf("\033[32mNXShell\033[0m:\033[34m%s\033[0m> ", prompt_cwd);
355:}
356:
357:static void print_prompt(void) {
358:  print("\r\n");
359:  print_prompt_only();
360:}

362:/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
363: * run_builtin - execute one of the shell's internal commands.
364: * Returns 0 if the command was handled, -1 otherwise.
365: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
366:static int run_builtin(int argc, char *argv[]) {
367:  if (argc == 0)
368:    return -1;
369:  const char *cmd = argv[0];
370:
371:  /* --- Built-in commands with 'nx' prefix (and aliases) --- */
372:  if (strcmp(cmd, "nxhelp") == 0 || strcmp(cmd, "?") == 0) {
373:    cmd_help();
374:    return 0;
375:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxclear") == 0) {
376:    print("\033[2J\033[H");
377:    shell_redraw_accent();
378:    return 0;
379:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxtime") == 0 || strcmp(cmd, "nxuptime") == 0) {
380:    printf("Uptime: %d seconds (%ld ms)\n", (int)(get_time() / 1000),
381:           get_time());
382:    return 0;
383:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxls") == 0) {
384:    const char *path = argc >= 2 ? argv[1] : ".";
385:    char buf[1024];
386:    int len = list_dir(path, buf, sizeof(buf));
387:    if (len < 0)
388:      printf("nxls: cannot list %s\n", path);
389:    else {
390:      print(buf);
391:      print("\n");
392:    }
393:    return 0;
394:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxpwd") == 0) {
395:    char buf[128];
396:    if (getcwd(buf, sizeof(buf)) == 0)
397:      printf("%s\n", buf);
398:    else
399:      print("nxpwd: error\n");
400:    return 0;
401:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxcd") == 0) {
402:    const char *path = argc >= 2 ? argv[1] : "/";
403:    if (chdir(path) != 0)
404:      printf("nxcd: no such directory: %s\n", path);
405:    return 0;
406:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxcat") == 0) {
407:    if (argc < 2) {
408:      print("usage: nxcat <path>\n");
409:    } else {
410:      char buf[256];
411:      int len = file_read(argv[1], buf, sizeof(buf) - 1, 0);
412:      if (len < 0)
413:        printf("nxcat: cannot read %s\n", argv[1]);
414:      else {
415:        buf[len] = '\0';
416:        printf("--- %s (%d bytes) ---\n", argv[1], len);
417:        print(buf);
418:        if ((unsigned int)len >= sizeof(buf) - 1)
419:          print("\n...[truncated]...\n");
420:        else
421:          print("\n");
422:      }
423:    }
424:    return 0;
425:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxecho") == 0) {
426:    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
427:      if (i > 1)
428:        print(" ");
429:      print(argv[i]);
430:    }
431:    print("\n");
432:    return 0;
433:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxrm") == 0 || strcmp(cmd, "nxunlink") == 0) {
434:    if (argc < 2) {
435:      print("usage: nxrm <path>\n");
436:    } else if (OS1_fs_unlink(argv[1]) != 0) {
437:      printf("nxrm: cannot remove %s\n", argv[1]);
438:    }
439:    return 0;
440:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxmkdir") == 0) {
441:    if (argc < 2) {
442:      print("usage: nxmkdir <path>\n");
443:    } else if (mkdir(argv[1], 0755) != 0) {
444:      printf("nxmkdir: cannot create directory %s\n", argv[1]);
445:    }
446:    return 0;
447:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxcp") == 0) {
448:    if (argc < 3) {
449:      print("usage: nxcp <source> <destination>\n");
450:    } else {
451:      char buf[1024];
452:
453:      int len = file_read(argv[1], buf, sizeof(buf), 0);
454:      if (len < 0) {
455:        printf("nxcp: cannot read %s\n", argv[1]);
456:      } else {
457:        int ret = OS1_fs_write(argv[2], buf, len, 0);
458:
459:        if (ret < 0)
460:          printf("nxcp: cannot write %s\n", argv[2]);
461:      }
462:    }
463:    return 0;
464:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxmv") == 0) {
465:    if (argc < 3) {
466:      print("usage: nxmv <source> <destination>\n");
467:    } else {
468:      char buf[1024];
469:
470:      int len = file_read(argv[1], buf, sizeof(buf), 0);
471:
472:      if (len < 0) {
473:        printf("nxmv: cannot read %s\n", argv[1]);
474:      } else {
475:        if (OS1_fs_write(argv[2], buf, len, 0) < 0) {
476:          printf("nxmv: cannot write %s\n", argv[2]);
477:        } else {
478:          if (OS1_fs_unlink(argv[1]) != 0)
479:            printf("nxmv: cannot remove original %s\n", argv[1]);
480:        }
481:      }
482:    }
483:    return 0;
484:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxwrite") == 0) {
485:    if (argc < 3) {
486:      print("usage: nxwrite <path> <text...>\n");
487:    } else {
488:      char msg[192];
489:      int n = 0;
490:      for (int i = 2; i < argc && n < (int)sizeof(msg) - 1; i++) {
491:        if (i > 2 && n < (int)sizeof(msg) - 1)
492:          msg[n++] = ' ';
493:        for (const char *p = argv[i]; *p && n < (int)sizeof(msg) - 1; p++)
494:          msg[n++] = *p;
495:      }
496:      msg[n] = '\0';
497:      if (OS1_fs_write(argv[1], msg, n, 0) < 0)
498:        printf("nxwrite: failed on %s\n", argv[1]);
499:    }
500:    return 0;
501:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxkill") == 0) {
502:    if (argc < 2) {
503:      print("usage: nxkill <pid>\n");
504:    } else {
505:      int pid = atoi(argv[1]);
506:      if (pid <= 0) {
507:        print("usage: nxkill <pid>\n");
508:      } else {
509:        printf("Killing PID %d...\n", pid);
510:        if (kill_process(pid) == 0)
511:          print("Process terminated.\n");
512:        else
513:          print("Failed to kill process.\n");
514:      }
515:    }
516:    return 0;
517:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxfocus") == 0) {
518:    if (argc < 2) {
519:      print("usage: nxfocus <window-id>\n");
520:    } else {
521:      int id = atoi(argv[1]);
522:      if (id <= 0) {
523:        print("usage: nxfocus <window-id>\n");
524:      } else {
525:        int r = OS1_window_focus(id);
526:        if (r == 0)
527:          printf("Focused window %d\n", id);
528:        else
529:          printf("focus failed (%d)\n", r);
530:      }
531:    }
532:    return 0;
533:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxid") == 0 || strcmp(cmd, "nxwhoami") == 0) {
534:    int level = 0;
535:    unsigned int mask = 0;
536:    OS1_identity(&level, &mask);
537:    char m[96];
538:    nxperm_mask_str(mask, m, (int)sizeof(m));
539:    printf("pid=%d level=%s caps=%s\n", get_pid(), nxperm_level_name(level), m);
540:    return 0;
541:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxabout") == 0) {
542:    print("\n\033[1;36mNeXs OS V0.0.5.4\033[0m\n");
543:    print("\033[33mGraphics:\033[0m Window Compositor + ANSI Terminal\n");
544:    print("\033[35mInput:\033[0m Interrupt-driven VirtIO Mouse/Keyboard\n");
545:    print("\033[32mLibrary:\033[0m POSIX-like userlib with printf support\n");
546:    print("\nSystem reported: OK\n");
547:    return 0;
548:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxexit") == 0 || strcmp(cmd, "nxquit") == 0) {
549:    print("Exiting NXShell...\n");
550:    running = 0;
551:    exit(0);
552:    return 0;
553:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxjobs") == 0) {
554:    nxjobs_poll(&g_jobs);
555:    nxjobs_print(&g_jobs);
556:    return 0;
557:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxfg") == 0) {
558:    nxjobs_poll(&g_jobs);
559:    int slot = nxjobs_resolve(&g_jobs, argc >= 2 ? argv[1] : (const char *)0);
560:    if (slot < 0) {
561:      if (argc >= 2)
562:        printf("nxfg: %s: no such job\n", argv[1]);
563:      else
564:        print("nxfg: no current job\n");
565:    } else {
566:      printf("%s\n", g_jobs.slot[slot].cmd);
567:      if (g_jobs.slot[slot].state == NXJOB_STOPPED)
568:        nxjobs_cont(&g_jobs, slot);
569:      if (run_foreground(g_jobs.slot[slot].pid) == NXEXEC_JOB_STOPPED) {
570:        nxjobs_mark_stopped(&g_jobs, slot);
571:        printf("[%d]+ Stopped   %s\n", g_jobs.slot[slot].id,
572:               g_jobs.slot[slot].cmd);
573:      } else {
574:        nxjobs_reap(&g_jobs, slot);
575:      }
576:    }
577:    return 0;
578:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxbg") == 0) {
579:    nxjobs_poll(&g_jobs);
580:    int slot = nxjobs_resolve(&g_jobs, argc >= 2 ? argv[1] : (const char *)0);
581:    if (slot < 0) {
582:      if (argc >= 2)
583:        printf("nxbg: %s: no such job\n", argv[1]);
584:      else
585:        print("nxbg: no current job\n");
586:    } else if (g_jobs.slot[slot].state != NXJOB_STOPPED)
587:      print("nxbg: job already running\n");
588:    else if (nxjobs_cont(&g_jobs, slot) == 0)
589:      printf("[%d] %s &\n", g_jobs.slot[slot].id, g_jobs.slot[slot].cmd);
590:    else
591:      print("nxbg: failed to resume\n");
592:    return 0;
593:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxattach") == 0) {
594:    if (argc < 2) {
595:      print("usage: nxattach <pid>\n");
596:    } else {
597:      int pid = atoi(argv[1]);
598:      int w = (pid > 0) ? OS1low_process_wait(pid) : -2;
599:      if (pid <= 0)
600:        print("nxattach: invalid pid\n");
601:      else if (w == -2)
602:        printf("nxattach: no such process: %d\n", pid);
603:      else if (w > 0)
604:        printf("nxattach: process %d has already exited\n", pid);
605:      else {
606:        char nm[NXJOBS_CMD_MAX];
607:        if (!nxexec_lookup_identity(pid, nm, (int)sizeof(nm)))
608:          snprintf(nm, sizeof(nm), "pid %d", pid);
609:        int id = nxjobs_add(&g_jobs, pid, nm);
610:        if (id < 0)
611:          print("nxattach: job table full\n");
612:        else
613:          printf("[%d] %d %s\n", id, pid, nm);
614:      }
615:    }
616:    return 0;
617:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxdisown") == 0) {
618:    int slot = nxjobs_resolve(&g_jobs, argc >= 2 ? argv[1] : (const char *)0);
619:    if (slot < 0) {
620:      print("nxdisown: no such job\n");
621:    } else {
622:      printf("[%d] %d %s disowned\n", g_jobs.slot[slot].id,
623:             g_jobs.slot[slot].pid, g_jobs.slot[slot].cmd);
624:      nxjobs_reap(&g_jobs, slot);
625:    }
626:    return 0;
627:  } else if (strcmp(cmd, "nxexec") == 0) {
628:    if (argc < 2) {
629:      print("usage: nxexec <program> [args...]\n");
630:    } else {
631:      char path[SPAWN_PATH_MAX];
632:      int pid = spawn_search_args(argc - 1, &argv[1], path);
633:      if (pid <= 0) {
634:        g_last_status = 127;
635:        printf("nxexec: not found: %s\n", argv[1]);
636:      } else {
637:        run_fg_job(pid, argv[1]);
638:      }
639:    }
640:    return 0;
641:  }
642:
643:  return -1;
644:}
645:
646:/*
647: * get_builtin_name - restituisce il nome del built-in corrispondente
648: * al comando base. Esempio: "ls" -> "nxls", "cd" -> "nxcd".
649: * Se il comando è già un built-in (inizia con "nx"), lo restituisce
650: * invariato.
651: */
652:static const char* get_builtin_name(const char *cmd) {
653:  /* Mappa comandi base -> built-in con prefisso nx */
654:  static const struct {
655:    const char *base;
656:    const char *builtin;
657:  } map[] = {
658:    {"help", "nxhelp"},
659:    {"clear", "nxclear"},
660:    {"time", "nxtime"},
661:    {"uptime", "nxuptime"},
662:    {"ls", "nxls"},
663:    {"cd", "nxcd"},
664:    {"pwd", "nxpwd"},
665:    {"cat", "nxcat"},
666:    {"echo", "nxecho"},
667:    {"rm", "nxrm"},
668:    {"unlink", "nxunlink"},
669:    {"mkdir", "nxmkdir"},
670:    {"cp", "nxcp"},
671:    {"mv", "nxmv"},
672:    {"write", "nxwrite"},
673:    {"kill", "nxkill"},
674:    {"focus", "nxfocus"},
675:    {"id", "nxid"},
676:    {"whoami", "nxwhoami"},
677:    {"about", "nxabout"},
678:    {"exec", "nxexec"},
679:    {"jobs", "nxjobs"},
680:    {"fg", "nxfg"},
681:    {"bg", "nxbg"},
682:    {"attach", "nxattach"},
683:    {"disown", "nxdisown"},
684:    {"exit", "nxexit"},
685:    {"quit", "nxquit"},
686:    {"?", "nxhelp"}
687:  };
688:
689:  /* Se il comando inizia già con "nx", è già un built-in */
690:  if (strncmp(cmd, "nx", 2) == 0)
691:    return cmd;
692:
693:  /* Cerca nella mappa */
694:  for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(map)/sizeof(map[0]); i++) {
695:    if (strcmp(cmd, map[i].base) == 0)
696:      return map[i].builtin;
697:  }
698:
699:  return NULL;
700:}
701:
702:/*
703: * run_command_line - execute ONE simple command (no `&&`/`||`/`;`).
704: *
705: * `line` is consumed in place by the tokeniser.  Sequencing is the caller's
706: * job (process_command below); this function is the unit a connector decides
707: * to run or skip, and it owns g_last_status for that unit.
708: *
709: * Priority order (modifica 2026-09-01):
710: *   1. Se il comando è nella whitelist (mappa get_builtin_name),
711: *      esegui il built‑in corrispondente SENZA cercare il binario.
712: *   2. Altrimenti, cerca il binario esterno in /bin e /sys/bin.
713: *   3. Se il binario non esiste, prova il built‑in come fallback (solo per
714: *      i comandi della whitelist).
715: *   4. Se nessuno funziona, "Unknown command".
716: */
717:static void run_command_line(char *line) {
718:  char *argv[MAX_ARGV];
719:  int argc = tokenize(line, argv, MAX_ARGV);
720:  if (argc == 0)
721:    return;
722:
723:  g_last_status = 0;
724:
725:  int background = 0;
726:  if (argc > 1 && strcmp(argv[argc - 1], "&") == 0) {
727:    background = 1;
728:    argc--;
729:  }
730:
731:  for (int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
732:    if (strcmp(argv[i], "|") == 0) {
733:      run_pipeline(i, argc, argv, background);
734:      return;
735:    }
736:  }
737:
738:  /* 1) Se il comando è nella whitelist, usa il built‑in direttamente */
739:  const char *builtin_name = get_builtin_name(argv[0]);
740:  if (builtin_name) {
741:    char *builtin_argv[MAX_ARGV];
742:    builtin_argv[0] = (char*)builtin_name;
743:    for (int i = 1; i < argc && i < MAX_ARGV - 1; i++)
744:      builtin_argv[i] = argv[i];
745:    builtin_argv[argc] = NULL;
746:
747:    if (run_builtin(argc, builtin_argv) == 0)
748:      return;
749:    /* Se per qualche motivo il built‑in fallisce, continuiamo con il binario */
750:  }
751:
752:  /* 2) Cerca il binario esterno */
753:  char path[SPAWN_PATH_MAX];
754:  int pid = spawn_search_args(argc, argv, path);
755:  if (pid > 0) {
756:    if (background) {
757:      int id = nxjobs_add(&g_jobs, pid, argv[0]);
758:      printf("[%d] %d\n", id, pid);
759:    } else {
760:      run_fg_job(pid, argv[0]);
761:    }
762:    return;
763:  }
764:
765:  /* 3) Se il binario non esiste e il comando era nella whitelist,
766:   *    proviamo di nuovo il built‑in (fallback). */
767:  if (builtin_name) {
768:    char *builtin_argv[MAX_ARGV];
769:    builtin_argv[0] = (char*)builtin_name;
770:    for (int i = 1; i < argc && i < MAX_ARGV - 1; i++)
771:      builtin_argv[i] = argv[i];
772:    builtin_argv[argc] = NULL;
773:
774:    if (run_builtin(argc, builtin_argv) == 0)
775:      return;
776:  }
777:
778:  /* 4) Comando sconosciuto */
779:  g_last_status = 127;
780:  printf("Unknown command: %s\n", argv[0]);
781:}
782:
783:/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
784: * Command SEQUENCING — `&&`, `||`, `;`  (plan stall S6, phase 17e)
785: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
786:#define SEQ_MAX 8
787:#define SEQ_ALWAYS 0
788:#define SEQ_AND 1
789:#define SEQ_OR 2
790:
791:static int split_sequence(char *line, char *seg[], int conn[], int max) {
792:  int n = 1;
793:  char *p = line;
794:  seg[0] = p;
795:  conn[0] = SEQ_ALWAYS;
796:
797:  while (*p) {
798:    if (*p == '"' || *p == '\'') {
799:      char q = *p++;
800:      while (*p && *p != q) {
801:        if (q == '"' && *p == '\\' && (p[1] == '"' || p[1] == '\\'))
802:          p++;
803:        p++;
804:      }
805:      if (*p)
806:        p++;
807:      continue;
808:    }
809:
810:    int kind, len;
811:    if (p[0] == '&' && p[1] == '&') {
812:      kind = SEQ_AND;
813:      len = 2;
814:    } else if (p[0] == '|' && p[1] == '|') {
815:      kind = SEQ_OR;
816:      len = 2;
817:    } else if (p[0] == ';') {
818:      kind = SEQ_ALWAYS;
819:      len = 1;
820:    } else {
821:      p++;
822:      continue;
823:    }
824:
825:    if (n >= max)
826:      return -1;
827:    *p = '\0';
828:    p += len;
829:    conn[n] = kind;
830:    seg[n] = p;
831:    n++;
832:  }
833:  return n;
834:}
835:
836:static void process_command(void) {
837:  if (g_line.len == 0)
838:    return;
839:
840:  char line[CMD_MAX];
841:  strncpy(line, g_line.buf, sizeof(line) - 1);
842:  line[sizeof(line) - 1] = '\0';
843:
844:  nxline_history_add(&g_line, g_line.buf);
845:
846:  char *seg[SEQ_MAX];
847:  int conn[SEQ_MAX];
848:  int nseg = split_sequence(line, seg, conn, SEQ_MAX);
849:  if (nseg < 0) {
850:    printf("nxshell: more than %d commands in one line\n", SEQ_MAX);
851:    g_last_status = 2;
852:    nxline_reset(&g_line);
853:    return;
854:  }
855:
856:  for (int i = 0; i < nseg && running; i++) {
857:    if (i > 0) {
858:      if (conn[i] == SEQ_AND && g_last_status != 0)
859:        continue;
860:      if (conn[i] == SEQ_OR && g_last_status == 0)
861:        continue;
862:    }
863:    run_command_line(seg[i]);
864:  }
865:
866:  nxline_reset(&g_line);
867:}
868:
869:static void shell_handle_key(unsigned char key, uint16_t scancode) {
870:  int r = nxline_feed_key(&g_line, key, scancode);
871:
872:  if (r == NXLINE_SUBMIT) {
873:    print("\r\n");
874:    process_command();
875:    if (running)
876:      print_prompt();
877:  } else if (r == NXLINE_EOF) {
878:    print("\r\n");
879:    print("Exiting NXShell...\n");
880:    running = 0;
881:    exit(0);
882:  } else if (r == NXLINE_CLEAR_SCREEN) {
883:    print("\033[2J\033[H");
884:    shell_redraw_accent();
885:    print_prompt_only();
886:    nxline_repaint_inline(&g_line);
887:  }
888:}
889:
890:int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
891:  nxjobs_init(&g_jobs);
892:  nxline_init(&g_line, NXSHELL_HISTORY_PATH, nxline_prompt_hook, NULL);
893:
894:  if (argc >= 3 && strcmp(argv[1], "-c") == 0) {
895:    strncpy(g_line.buf, argv[2], sizeof(g_line.buf) - 1);
896:    g_line.buf[sizeof(g_line.buf) - 1] = '\0';
897:    g_line.len = (int)strlen(g_line.buf);
898:    process_command();
899:    return g_last_status;
900:  }
901:
902:  nxline_load_history(&g_line);
903:
904:  print("NXShell: Alive\n");
905:  int pid = get_pid();
906:
907:  char cwd[128] = {0};
908:  getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd));
909:  if (strcmp(cwd, "/") == 0 || cwd[0] == '\0')
910:    chdir("/home");
911:
912:  shell_load_colors(nxres_theme_is_light());
913:
914:  {
915:    char pidbuf[16];
916:    snprintf(pidbuf, sizeof(pidbuf), "%d", pid);
917:    OS1_registry_set("srv.shell_pid", pidbuf);
918:  }
919:
920:  char title[32];
921:  snprintf(title, sizeof(title), "NXShell PID %d", pid);
922:
923:  long di = OS1_display_info();
924:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
925:  int sh = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
926:  if (sw <= 0)
927:    sw = 800;
928:  if (sh <= 0)
929:    sh = 600;
930:
931:  g_win_w = (sw * 3) / 5;
932:  g_win_h = (sh * 11) / 20;
933:  if (g_win_w > 800)
934:    g_win_w = 800;
935:  if (g_win_h > 560)
936:    g_win_h = 560;
937:  if (g_win_w < MIN_WIN_W)
938:    g_win_w = MIN_WIN_W;
939:  if (g_win_h < MIN_WIN_H)
940:    g_win_h = MIN_WIN_H;
941:
942:  int x_off = (pid * 40) % 200;
943:  int y_off = (pid * 40) % 200;
944:  int wx = (sw - g_win_w) / 2 + x_off;
945:  int wy = (sh - g_win_h) / 2 + y_off;
946:  if (wx < 0)
947:    wx = 100 + x_off;
948:  if (wy < 0)
949:    wy = 100 + y_off;
950:
951:  my_window = create_window(wx, wy, g_win_w, g_win_h, title);
952:  if (my_window <= 0) {
953:    print("[NXShell] Error creating window\n");
954:    exit(1);
955:  }
956:
957:  shell_redraw_accent();
958:  set_focus(get_pid());
959:
960:  print("\n[NXShell] TTY Window ");
961:  print_hex(my_window);
962:  printf(" active (PID %d).\n", get_pid());
963:  print_prompt();
964:  write(3, "NXShell> ", 7);
965:
966:  while (running) {
967:    shell_check_theme();
968:    nxjobs_poll(&g_jobs);
969:
970:    input_event_t ev;
971:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
972:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE)
973:        shell_on_resize(ev.resize.w, ev.resize.h);
974:      else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED)
975:        shell_check_theme();
976:      else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD &&
977:               ev.keyboard.state == KEY_PRESSED)
978:        shell_handle_key(ev.keyboard.key, ev.keyboard.scancode);
979:    }
980:
981:    OS1_sleep(10);
982:  }
983:
984:  exit(0);
985:  return 0;
986:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxtop.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxtop.c
3: * Realtime Process List Utility - ASTRA stratified service edition.
4: *
5: * A thin windowed front-end over the reusable process helper nxproc.h.  It
6: * opens its window and refreshes every 3 s, but the previous "spinbomb" behaviour
7: * (rewriting the FULL window every tick even when nothing changed) is gone:
8: * nxproc_render_if_changed() computes a signature of the visible fields and
9: * skips the window write entirely when the table is unchanged.  Between checks
10: * nxtop blocks on the real kernel timer (OS1_sleep) rather than busy-spinning,
11: * so an idle process list costs no CPU.
12: *
13: * Naming: renamed from `top` to `nxtop` to follow the NEXS service naming
14: * convention (every /sys/bin ELF is prefixed `nx*`).  The on-disk ELF is
15: * `nxtop.elf`; the shell has no dedicated `top` builtin — typing `nxtop`
16: * reaches it through the generic unknown-command fallback (spawn_search_args'
17: * /bin → /sys/bin probe).  main() takes no argv: there are no options.
18: */
19:#include "nxproc.h"
20:#include <os1.h>
21:
22:int main(void) {
23:  /* Window geometry/title unchanged from the original top. */
24:  int my_win =
25:      _sys_create_window(100, 100, 520, 600, "NEXS Realtime Process List");
26:  if (my_win < 0)
27:    return 1;
28:
29:  unsigned long sig = 0; /* Seed sentinel: guarantees the first render. */
30:
31:  while (1) {
32:    /* Snapshot + signature compare + (conditional) render all live in the
33:     * helper; this only rewrites the window when something visible changed. */
34:    nxproc_render_if_changed(my_win, &sig);
35:
36:    /* REFRESH RATE (~0.33 Hz): block 3 s on the real kernel timer instead
37:     * of busy-spinning yield(), so nxtop no longer burns a core idling. */
38:    OS1_sleep(3000);
39:  }
40:
41:  return 0;
42:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxui.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxui.c
3: * NEXS dock — the system taskbar (an ASTRA SRL userland service).
4: *
5: * nxui is a thin userland window manager UI.  It keeps the compositor as the
6: * pure MECHANISM and owns the POLICY itself:
7: *   - it enumerates every window with SYS_WINDOW_ENUM (OS1_window_enum);
8: *   - it draws a macOS/Darwin-style dock along the bottom of the screen, one
9: *     tile per app: a real per-app icon (nxicon.h,
10: * /home/Pictures/icon/{dark,light}) when one is cached for that app +
11: * theme, else the classic flat rounded square (GFX-NXUI-02) — the exact same
12: * corner-mask code draws both, see fb_rrect_px();
13: *   - a click on a tile FOCUSES that app, RESTORES it if it was sent to the
14: *     background, or BACKGROUNDS it if it was the focused app (toggle);
15: *   - when more apps are open than fit on screen, two scroll tiles (half-width,
16: *     rounded the same way as everything else) appear at the dock's ends and
17: *     PAGE through the app list, wrapping around at the last/first page
18: *     (GFX-NXUI-04);
19: *   - the dock remembers g_last_focus — the last app window that was REALLY
20: *     focused (set both by its own act() and by reading the WININFO_FOCUSED
21: *     bit each redraw, so it follows focus changes the system makes outside
22: *     the dock).  When a frame has no focused app (the dock itself was just
23: *     clicked, or a tile was toggled to minimized), the g_last_focus tile
24: *     stays painted blue, and a click that did not act on an app (scroll
25: *     buttons, empty dock space) hands the focus back via
26: *     OS1_window_focus(g_last_focus) — a click on a tile already drives
27: *     focus through act() so that path is unchanged.
28: *
29: * All window control goes through OS1_window_* — i.e. OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW
30: * capabilities (ASTRA §6.7): the authority is the unforgeable handle, not
31: * nxui's identity.  nxui is spawned by init at PLVL_ROOT (the /sys/bin
32: * per-path preset) — window-manager authority is enough to control any
33: * app's window, and ROOT keeps the dock killable/respawnable like the shell.
34: *
35: * Input uses the STANDARD window input API (input_poll_event / input_event_t),
36: * exactly like every other windowed app — mouse buttons are the evdev codes
37: * MOUSE_BTN_* the compositor forwards, NOT a 0/1/2 index.  The dock is itself a
38: * top_most compositor window (chromeless: a top_most window has no
39: * titlebar/buttons), drawn by blitting a self-rendered ARGB buffer.  The window
40: * is inset from the screen edges (DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE/_BOTTOM) and its own
41: * corners are rounded the same way the tiles are (GFX-NXUI-04).
42: *
43: * It re-lays-out on a desktop resolution change (polled, plus the event-driven
44: * INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE path for when the system notifies it), and only re-blits
45: * when the dock-relevant state (app set, focus, page, button-press) actually
46: * changes — it never busy-spins.
47: *
48: * NOTE(GFX-NXUI-02): resolved — per-app icons (nxicon.h) now draw over the
49: * flat rounded-square tile whenever one is available for the app + active
50: * theme; the flat tile itself is unchanged and remains the fallback.
51: * NOTE(GFX-NXUI-03): resolved — the per-path VFS capability preset
52: * (/sys/bin → PLVL_ROOT) has shipped and is what governs nxui's level today.
53: * NOTE(GFX-NXUI-04): rounded dock corners rely on the compositor honoring
54: * per-pixel alpha on window_blit — already true for COL_DOCK_BG's 0xE8 alpha,
55: * so the fully-transparent (0x00000000) corner pixels here ride the same
56: * path. If the compositor ever switches to opaque blits this degrades to
57: * square corners with a black fringe, not a crash — worth a quick visual
58: * check after dropping this in.
59: */
60:#include <input.h>
61:#include <os1.h>
62:#include <string.h>
63:
64:#include "nxicon.h" /* nxicon_get()/nxicon_classify() — dock tile icons (GFX-NXUI-02) */
65:#include "nxres.h" /* nxres_theme_is_light(), IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC (posix_types.h) — see palette below */
66:
67:#define DOCK_H 56     /* dock height in px                                   */
68:#define TILE 40       /* app tile size in px                                 */
69:#define TILE_GAP 12   /* gap between tiles                                   */
70:#define TILE_RADIUS 6 /* tile corner radius */
71:#define MARGIN                                                                 \
72:  16                 /* inset between the dock window edge and the first/      \
73:                      * last tile or scroll button (NOT the screen inset —   \
74:                      * see DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE below)                         */
75:#define MAX_TILES 32 /* matches the compositor MAX_WINDOWS                  */
76:
77:/* Outer placement: detach the dock window itself from the screen edges. */
78:#define DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE 16  /* gap to the left/right screen edges          */
79:#define DOCK_MARGIN_BOTTOM 4 /* gap to the bottom screen edge               */
80:
81:/* Scroll (paging) tiles: half the app tiles' width, same height/radius/style.
82: */
83:#define SCROLL_BTN_W (TILE / 2)
84:#define SCROLL_BTN_GAP 8 /* gap between a scroll button and the tile row */
85:#define DOCK_RADIUS                                                            \
86:  12 /* dock outer corner radius — same rounding style as                    \
87:      * the tiles, just scaled up for the bigger shape   */
88:
89:/* COL_DOCK_BG/COL_TILE/COL_TILE_MIN are the only dock colours that need to
90: * change with theme.color (nxres.h) — background translucency and the idle/
91: * minimized tile need different contrast against a light vs dark desktop.
92: * Everything else below (focus blue, scroll-button red, launcher green) is
93: * an accent/status colour, deliberately theme-INVARIANT — same reasoning as
94: * nxbar's g_col_xbtn_glyph/g_col_badge staying fixed. */
95:static uint32_t g_col_dock_bg;
96:static uint32_t g_col_tile;
97:static uint32_t g_col_tile_min;
98:static int g_light; /* current theme, mirrored here so redraw() can pick the
99:                     * matching /home/Pictures/icon/{dark,light} set without
100:                     * a second nxres_theme_is_light() read per frame */
101:
102:static void nxui_load_palette(int light) {
103:  g_light = light;
104:  if (light) {
105:    g_col_dock_bg = 0xE8F5F5F7u;
106:    g_col_tile = 0xFFAEAEB2u;
107:    g_col_tile_min = 0xFFD1D1D6u;
108:  } else {
109:    g_col_dock_bg = 0xE81C1C24u;
110:    g_col_tile = 0xFFD0CBD3u;
111:    g_col_tile_min = 0xFF555563u;
112:  }
113:}
114:
115:#define COL_TILE_FOCUS 0xFF5E9CFFu
116:#define COL_BTN_RED 0xFFE53935u     /* material red 600 — idle scroll button */
117:#define COL_BTN_PRESSED 0xFF6B6B73u /* greys out while the button is held */
118:
119:/* The /sys/bin/nxlauncher tile is the only non-generic entry in the dock: a
120: * solid green when shown (material green 600), and a dimmer, less saturated
121: * green when the launcher has been sent to the background.  It mirrors the
122: * focus/minimised split used for every other tile (blue/grey) so the dock's
123: * own design language stays consistent — only the hue differs. */
124:#define COL_LAUNCHER 0xFF43A047u     /* material green 600 (shown)       */
125:#define COL_LAUNCHER_MIN 0xFF2E5D32u /* dimmer green (backgrounded)      */
126:
127:static uint32_t *g_fb;   /* dock pixel buffer (g_sw x DOCK_H, ARGB)        */
128:static int g_sw;         /* dock window's OWN width (desktop width minus
129:                          * the two DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE insets)                */
130:static int g_dsw, g_dsh; /* last-seen DESKTOP size, used only to detect a
131:                          * resolution change (distinct from g_sw now that
132:                          * the dock window is narrower than the desktop)   */
133:static int g_win = -1;   /* the dock's own window id                       */
134:static unsigned g_sig;   /* signature of the last drawn state (no re-blit  */
135:                         /* when unchanged → the dock is never a spinbomb)  */
136:
137:/* current tile→window mapping for the VISIBLE PAGE, rebuilt every poll for
138: * click hit-testing */
139:static int g_slot_id[MAX_TILES];
140:static int g_slot_x[MAX_TILES];
141:static int g_slot_n;
142:
143:/* paging state */
144:static int g_page;               /* current page, 0-based                    */
145:static int g_pages = 1;          /* total pages for the current app count and
146:                                  * dock width — recomputed every redraw, so it
147:                                  * always tracks the real number actually used */
148:static int g_scroll_on;          /* whether the scroll buttons are shown this
149:                                  * frame (more apps than fit on one page)     */
150:static int g_btn_l_x, g_btn_r_x; /* dock-local x of the two scroll buttons */
151:static int g_pressed;            /* 0=none, 1=left, 2=right — currently held  */
152:
153:/* g_last_focus: id of the most recent app window the dock knows to be really
154: * focused.  Updated in two places: (1) every redraw, when WININFO_FOCUSED is
155: * observed on some window (so focus changes the system makes outside the
156: * dock — e.g. a user clicking into a window directly — are followed); (2) by
157: * act() when a tile click focused or restored an app.  When this frame has
158: * NO focused app, the g_last_focus tile is still painted blue, and a click
159: * that did not act on an app (scroll buttons, empty dock) refocuses it via
160: * OS1_window_focus(). 0 means "we have not seen focus yet". */
161:static int g_last_focus;
162:
163:static void fb_fill(uint32_t c) {
164:  int total = g_sw * DOCK_H;
165:  for (int i = 0; i < total; i++)
166:    g_fb[i] = c;
167:}
168:
169:/* fb_rrect_px - shared rounded-rect body: one corner-quarter-circle mask test,
170: * one write loop, feeding EITHER a flat color (img == NULL — the classic
171: * GFX-NXUI-02 tile) or an icon's own pixels (img != NULL, w x h == the icon's
172: * own dimensions).  Kept as a single function so an icon tile is rounded by
173: * the EXACT same test as every other shape in this file (dock panel, classic
174: * tiles, scroll buttons) — no second "icon corner rounding" to keep in sync.
175: * dim != 0 darkens an icon's RGB (alpha untouched) for the minimized/
176: * backgrounded state, replacing the classic path's g_col_tile_min swap. */
177:static void fb_rrect_px(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint32_t c,
178:                        const uint32_t *img, int dim) {
179:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
180:    return;
181:  if (r < 0)
182:    r = 0;
183:  if (r > w / 2)
184:    r = w / 2;
185:  if (r > h / 2)
186:    r = h / 2;
187:
188:  for (int j = 0; j < h; j++) {
189:    for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
190:      int ccx = -1, ccy = 0;
191:      if (i < r && j < r) {
192:        ccx = r;
193:        ccy = r;
194:      } else if (i >= w - r && j < r) {
195:        ccx = w - r - 1;
196:        ccy = r;
197:      } else if (i < r && j >= h - r) {
198:        ccx = r;
199:        ccy = h - r - 1;
200:      } else if (i >= w - r && j >= h - r) {
201:        ccx = w - r - 1;
202:        ccy = h - r - 1;
203:      }
204:
205:      if (ccx >= 0) {
206:        int dx = i - ccx, dy = j - ccy;
207:        if (dx * dx + dy * dy > r * r)
208:          continue;
209:      }
210:
211:      int px = x + i;
212:      int py = y + j;
213:      if (px < 0 || px >= g_sw || py < 0 || py >= DOCK_H)
214:        continue;
215:
216:      uint32_t src;
217:      if (img) {
218:        src = img[j * w + i];
219:        if (dim) {
220:          uint32_t a = src & 0xFF000000u;
221:          uint32_t rr = ((src >> 16) & 0xFFu) * 3u / 5u;
222:          uint32_t gg = ((src >> 8) & 0xFFu) * 3u / 5u;
223:          uint32_t bb = (src & 0xFFu) * 3u / 5u;
224:          src = a | (rr << 16) | (gg << 8) | bb;
225:        }
226:      } else {
227:        src = c;
228:      }
229:
230:      if (img) {
231:        uint8_t alpha = (src >> 24) & 0xFF;
232:        if (alpha == 0)
233:          continue;
234:
235:        if (alpha == 255) {
236:          g_fb[py * g_sw + px] = src;
237:        } else {
238:          uint32_t dst = g_fb[py * g_sw + px];
239:
240:          uint32_t dr = (dst >> 16) & 0xFF;
241:          uint32_t dg = (dst >> 8) & 0xFF;
242:          uint32_t db = dst & 0xFF;
243:
244:          uint32_t sr = (src >> 16) & 0xFF;
245:          uint32_t sg = (src >> 8) & 0xFF;
246:          uint32_t sb = src & 0xFF;
247:
248:          uint32_t out_r = (sr * alpha + dr * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
249:          uint32_t out_g = (sg * alpha + dg * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
250:          uint32_t out_b = (sb * alpha + db * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
251:
252:          g_fb[py * g_sw + px] =
253:              (0xFF000000u) | (out_r << 16) | (out_g << 8) | out_b;
254:        }
255:      } else {
256:        g_fb[py * g_sw + px] = src;
257:      }
258:    }
259:  }
260:}
261:
262:/* fb_rrect - filled rounded rectangle into the dock buffer (corners clipped to
263: * a quarter-circle of radius r).  The classic (icon-less) tile/panel/button
264: * path — just fb_rrect_px with no image. */
265:static void fb_rrect(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint32_t c) {
266:  fb_rrect_px(x, y, w, h, r, c, NULL, 0);
267:}
268:
269:/* fb_icon_border - a subtle 3D bevel ring traced around an icon tile only
270: * (the classic flat-colour tile already reads as a solid button and doesn't
271: * need one). Two 1px arcs split along the tile's diagonal: a brighter one
272: * along the top-left edge — the "raised" side, as if lit from above-left —
273: * and a dimmer one along the bottom-right edge, the same convention a real
274: * embossed bezel uses. White in dark mode (a light ring reads as a raised
275: * highlight against a dark tile); black in light mode (mirrored: a dark ring
276: * reads as raised against a light tile). Uses the SAME corner-quarter-circle
277: * test as fb_rrect_px so the ring hugs the icon's own rounded corners exactly
278: * — just restricted to a ~1px band instead of a fill. */
279:static void fb_icon_border(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, int light) {
280:  uint32_t base = light ? 0x000000u : 0xFFFFFFu;
281:  if (r < 0)
282:    r = 0;
283:  if (r > w / 2)
284:    r = w / 2;
285:  if (r > h / 2)
286:    r = h / 2;
287:
288:  for (int j = 0; j < h; j++) {
289:    for (int i = 0; i < w; i++) {
290:      int ccx = -1, ccy = 0;
291:      if (i < r && j < r) {
292:        ccx = r;
293:        ccy = r;
294:      } else if (i >= w - r && j < r) {
295:        ccx = w - r - 1;
296:        ccy = r;
297:      } else if (i < r && j >= h - r) {
298:        ccx = r;
299:        ccy = h - r - 1;
300:      } else if (i >= w - r && j >= h - r) {
301:        ccx = w - r - 1;
302:        ccy = h - r - 1;
303:      }
304:
305:      int on_border;
306:      if (ccx >= 0) {
307:        int dx = i - ccx, dy = j - ccy;
308:        int d2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;
309:        if (d2 > r * r)
310:          continue; /* outside the rounded shape entirely */
311:        int r_in = r - 1;
312:        on_border = d2 >= r_in * r_in; /* within ~1px of the outer arc */
313:      } else {
314:        /* straight edge: only the single outermost row/column is the ring */
315:        on_border = (i == 0 || i == w - 1 || j == 0 || j == h - 1);
316:      }
317:      if (!on_border)
318:        continue;
319:
320:      int px = x + i, py = y + j;
321:      if (px < 0 || px >= g_sw || py < 0 || py >= DOCK_H)
322:        continue;
323:
324:      /* top-left half of the tile (by the diagonal i+j) gets the brighter
325:       * "raised" alpha; bottom-right half gets the dimmer "recessed" one. */
326:      int top_left = (i + j) < (w + h) / 2;
327:      uint32_t alpha = top_left ? 0x60u : 0x30u;
328:
329:      uint32_t dst = g_fb[py * g_sw + px];
330:      uint32_t dr = (dst >> 16) & 0xFF, dg = (dst >> 8) & 0xFF, db = dst & 0xFF;
331:      uint32_t sr = (base >> 16) & 0xFF, sg = (base >> 8) & 0xFF,
332:               sb = base & 0xFF;
333:
334:      uint32_t out_r = (sr * alpha + dr * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
335:      uint32_t out_g = (sg * alpha + dg * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
336:      uint32_t out_b = (sb * alpha + db * (255 - alpha)) / 255;
337:      g_fb[py * g_sw + px] =
338:          (0xFF000000u) | (out_r << 16) | (out_g << 8) | out_b;
339:    }
340:  }
341:}
342:
343:/* dock_reinit - (re)create the dock window + buffer for a sw x sh DESKTOP,
344: * pinned to the bottom but inset by DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE/_BOTTOM on every side.
345: * Used at start and on a resolution change (there is no userland window-move
346: * primitive yet, so recreating at the new origin is the simplest correct
347: * adaptation). */
348:static void dock_reinit(int sw, int sh) {
349:  g_dsw = sw;
350:  g_dsh = sh;
351:
352:  int dw = sw - 2 * DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE;
353:  if (dw < TILE + 2 * MARGIN) /* never collapse below one tile's worth */
354:    dw = TILE + 2 * MARGIN;
355:  g_sw = dw;
356:
357:  uint32_t *nb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)g_sw * DOCK_H * 4);
358:  if (nb) {
359:    free(g_fb);
360:    g_fb = nb;
361:  }
362:  if (g_win >= 0)
363:    destroy_window(g_win);
364:  g_win = create_window(DOCK_MARGIN_SIDE, sh - DOCK_H - DOCK_MARGIN_BOTTOM,
365:                        g_sw, DOCK_H, "nxui");
366:  if (g_win >= 0)
367:    set_window_flags(g_win, 1); /* top_most → chromeless, always-on-top */
368:  g_sig = 0;                    /* force a redraw at the new size */
369:}
370:
371:/* redraw - enumerate windows, page the list to fit the dock, and blit it —
372: * but only when the dock-relevant state actually changed (force=1 overrides).
373: * Updates g_slot_x[]/g_slot_id[] and g_btn_l_x/g_btn_r_x so clicks hit-test
374: * against the live layout.
375: *
376: * Paging replaces the old hard width cutoff: every eligible window (up to
377: * MAX_TILES, the compositor's own cap) is always reachable, just possibly on
378: * another page.  g_pages is recomputed from the ACTUAL app count and the
379: * dock's current width on every call, so it always reflects exactly how many
380: * pages are really in use — never a fixed guess. */
381:static void redraw(int force) {
382:  struct window_info wi[MAX_TILES];
383:  int n = (int)OS1_window_enum(wi, MAX_TILES);
384:  if (n < 0)
385:    n = 0;
386:
387:  /* Pass 1: collect every eligible window, unfiltered by width. */
388:  /* One record per window rather than four parallel arrays.  The launcher
389:   * hoist below REORDERS this list, and a reorder that moves some of a
390:   * window's fields but not the others silently mis-attributes them: when
391:   * `pid` was a separate array that the hoist forgot to shift, every tile
392:   * before the launcher drew the icon of its neighbour — at boot that made
393:   * the shell wear the launcher's icon.  Keeping the fields in one struct
394:   * makes a reorder move the whole window by construction. */
395:  struct tile_win {
396:    int id;
397:    unsigned flags;
398:    int pid;        /* for the sys.proc.<pid>.name lookup (Phase 3 identity)
399:                     * in the draw loop below */
400:    char title[64]; /* title copy, for nxicon_classify() in the draw loop
401:                     * below — the id/flags this dock already tracked were
402:                     * never enough to pick an icon */
403:  } win[MAX_TILES];
404:  int total = 0;
405:  int seen_focus = 0; /* 1 if some window reports WININFO_FOCUSED */
406:  for (int i = 0; i < n && total < MAX_TILES; i++) {
407:    /* our own dock + system overlays (notifications) are never tiled */
408:    if (wi[i].id == g_win)
409:      continue;
410:    if (wi[i].flags & (WININFO_TOPMOST | WININFO_PASSIVE))
411:      continue;
412:    /* show real apps: shown windows, or ones the user backgrounded.  Skip a
413:     * window an app hid itself (hidden but not user-minimized). */
414:    if (!(wi[i].flags & WININFO_VISIBLE) && !(wi[i].flags & WININFO_MINIMIZED))
415:      continue;
416:    win[total].id = wi[i].id;
417:    win[total].flags = wi[i].flags;
418:    win[total].pid = wi[i].pid;
419:    memcpy(win[total].title, wi[i].title, sizeof(win[total].title));
420:    total++;
421:    /* Follow focus changes the system makes outside the dock (e.g. the user
422:     * clicks into a window's body).  Only update g_last_focus when we
423:     * actually see the flag set, so a frame where no app is focused
424:     * (because the dock just got focus, or a tile was toggled to
425:     * minimized) keeps the remembered id intact. */
426:    if (wi[i].flags & WININFO_FOCUSED) {
427:      g_last_focus = wi[i].id;
428:      seen_focus = 1;
429:    }
430:  }
431:
432:  /* Pin the launcher to position 0 so it is always the first tile of the
433:   * first page (no paging needed to reach it).  Matched by basename so any
434:   * future title suffix — e.g. "— folder view" — still pins.  Done after
435:   * the collection pass so the focus update above still fires naturally. */
436:  int launcher_id = 0;
437:  for (int i = 0; i < total; i++) {
438:    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
439:      if (wi[j].id == win[i].id && strncmp(wi[j].title, "nxlauncher", 10) == 0) {
440:        launcher_id = win[i].id;
441:        if (i != 0) {
442:          /* Rotate the whole record to the front: one element moves, so no
443:           * field can be left behind at its old index. */
444:          struct tile_win hoisted = win[i];
445:          for (int k = i; k > 0; k--)
446:            win[k] = win[k - 1];
447:          win[0] = hoisted;
448:        }
449:        break;
450:      }
451:    }
452:  }
453:
454:  /* How many tiles fit per page?  Try without scroll buttons first; only pay
455:   * their width once paging is actually needed. */
456:  int inner_w = g_sw - 2 * MARGIN;
457:  int per_page = (inner_w + TILE_GAP) / (TILE + TILE_GAP);
458:  if (per_page < 1)
459:    per_page = 1;
460:  int scroll_on = total > per_page;
461:  if (scroll_on) {
462:    int inner_w2 = inner_w - 2 * (SCROLL_BTN_W + SCROLL_BTN_GAP);
463:    int pp2 = (inner_w2 + TILE_GAP) / (TILE + TILE_GAP);
464:    if (pp2 < 1)
465:      pp2 = 1;
466:    per_page = pp2;
467:    scroll_on = total > per_page; /* re-check: a tiny dock could still fit
468:                                      everything once pp2 is known */
469:  }
470:
471:  int pages = scroll_on ? (total + per_page - 1) / per_page : 1;
472:  if (pages < 1)
473:    pages = 1;
474:  if (g_page >= pages)
475:    g_page = pages - 1;
476:  if (g_page < 0)
477:    g_page = 0;
478:  g_pages = pages;
479:  g_scroll_on = scroll_on;
480:
481:  int start = scroll_on ? g_page * per_page : 0;
482:  int shown = total - start;
483:  if (shown < 0)
484:    shown = 0;
485:  if (shown > per_page)
486:    shown = per_page;
487:
488:  int x = MARGIN + (scroll_on ? (SCROLL_BTN_W + SCROLL_BTN_GAP) : 0);
489:  unsigned dflags[MAX_TILES];
490:  int vpid[MAX_TILES];
491:  char vttl[MAX_TILES][64];
492:  unsigned sig = 2166136261u ^ (unsigned)g_sw ^ ((unsigned)g_page << 8) ^
493:                 ((unsigned)scroll_on << 16) ^ ((unsigned)g_pressed << 20) ^
494:                 ((unsigned)g_light << 24);
495:  int cnt = 0;
496:  for (int i = 0; i < shown; i++) {
497:    int idx = start + i;
498:    g_slot_id[cnt] = win[idx].id;
499:    g_slot_x[cnt] = x;
500:    dflags[cnt] = win[idx].flags;
501:    vpid[cnt] = win[idx].pid;
502:    memcpy(vttl[cnt], win[idx].title, sizeof(vttl[cnt]));
503:    sig = (sig ^ (unsigned)win[idx].id) * 16777619u;
504:    sig = (sig ^ (win[idx].flags & (WININFO_FOCUSED | WININFO_MINIMIZED))) *
505:          16777619u;
506:    cnt++;
507:    x += TILE + TILE_GAP;
508:  }
509:  g_slot_n = cnt;
510:
511:  if (scroll_on) {
512:    g_btn_l_x = MARGIN;
513:    g_btn_r_x = g_sw - MARGIN - SCROLL_BTN_W;
514:  }
515:
516:  if (!force && sig == g_sig)
517:    return; /* nothing the dock shows has changed → skip the blit */
518:  g_sig = sig;
519:
520:  /* Transparent first, then the rounded panel on top — the corner pixels
521:   * fb_rrect skips stay fully transparent so the dock itself reads as a
522:   * rounded shape (see NOTE(GFX-NXUI-04) above). */
523:  fb_fill(0x00000000u);
524:  fb_rrect(0, 0, g_sw, DOCK_H, DOCK_RADIUS, g_col_dock_bg);
525:
526:  int ty = (DOCK_H - TILE) / 2;
527:  for (int i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
528:    int is_launcher = (launcher_id != 0 && win[start + i].id == launcher_id);
529:    int minimized = (dflags[i] & WININFO_MINIMIZED) != 0;
530:    /* The "real" focus (WININFO_FOCUSED).  When the dock itself is the focused
531:     * window, or a tile was just toggled to minimized, no window reports
532:     * WININFO_FOCUSED — in that case, the remembered g_last_focus tile stays
533:     * blue so the user still sees which app owns the focus. */
534:    int focused = (dflags[i] & WININFO_FOCUSED) ||
535:                  (!seen_focus && win[start + i].id == g_last_focus);
536:
537:    /* vttl[i] is the window's own title text (e.g. nxshell's is "NXShell PID
538:     * 6", not "nxshell"), so this uses nxicon_classify() — the case-
539:     * insensitive, prefix-matching, path-stripping classifier in nxicon.h —
540:     * not nxicon_classify_path()'s exact match (that one is for
541:     * nxlauncher's app-table entries, which are real basenames). */
542:    /* Prefer the PROGRAM NAME over the window title: the title is the app's
543:     * own, noisy text, the name is the canonical launch identity.  The title
544:     * classifier stays as the fallback for a window whose pid is gone. */
545:    int app_id;
546:    if (is_launcher) {
547:      app_id = NXICON_LAUNCHER;
548:    } else {
549:      /* Ask the (virtual, always-live) per-process view for the program name
550:       * and classify THAT.  There is no icon key to consult: an icon is a
551:       * property of the program, and the program name already carries it —
552:       * nxicon_classify strips the path itself.  The intermediate
553:       * `sys.appicon.<name>` key that 5b introduced mapped a name to itself,
554:       * so it added a lookup and no information (17a). */
555:      char idkey[64], idname[40];
556:      snprintf(idkey, sizeof(idkey), "sys.proc.%d.name", vpid[i]);
557:      if (OS1_registry_get(idkey, idname, sizeof(idname)) == 0 && idname[0])
558:        app_id = nxicon_classify(idname);
559:      else
560:        app_id = nxicon_classify(vttl[i]); /* fall back to the window title */
561:    }
562:    os1_image_t *icon = nxicon_get(app_id, g_light, TILE);
563:
564:    if (icon) {
565:      /* Icon tiles don't recolor on focus (macOS-dock-style: the icon itself
566:       * plus the running dot below are enough) — only minimized dims it,
567:       * replacing the classic path's color swap. */
568:      fb_rrect_px(g_slot_x[i], ty, TILE, TILE, TILE_RADIUS, 0, icon->pixels,
569:                  minimized);
570:      /* 3D bevel ring — icon tiles only, drawn on top so it's never covered
571:       * by the icon's own pixels. */
572:      fb_icon_border(g_slot_x[i], ty, TILE, TILE, TILE_RADIUS, g_light);
573:    } else {
574:      /* Classic fallback (GFX-NXUI-02): no icon cached for this app/theme —
575:       * same flat rounded-square logic as before icons existed. */
576:      uint32_t c = is_launcher ? COL_LAUNCHER : g_col_tile;
577:      if (is_launcher) {
578:        /* Launcher stays green across both states — bright when shown/
579:         * focused, dimmer when backgrounded — so the dock never loses the
580:         * "this is the launcher" cue.  No special focused override:
581:         * COL_LAUNCHER already marks "active". */
582:        c = minimized ? COL_LAUNCHER_MIN : COL_LAUNCHER;
583:      } else if (focused) {
584:        c = COL_TILE_FOCUS;
585:      } else if (minimized) {
586:        c = g_col_tile_min;
587:      }
588:      fb_rrect(g_slot_x[i], ty, TILE, TILE, TILE_RADIUS, c);
589:    }
590:    /* running indicator: a small dot under the focused app's tile */
591:    if (focused)
592:      fb_rrect(g_slot_x[i] + TILE / 2 - 2, ty + TILE + 3, 4, 3, 1,
593:               COL_TILE_FOCUS);
594:  }
595:
596:  if (scroll_on) {
597:    uint32_t lc = (g_pressed == 1) ? COL_BTN_PRESSED : COL_BTN_RED;
598:    uint32_t rc = (g_pressed == 2) ? COL_BTN_PRESSED : COL_BTN_RED;
599:    fb_rrect(g_btn_l_x, ty, SCROLL_BTN_W, TILE, TILE_RADIUS, lc);
600:    fb_rrect(g_btn_r_x, ty, SCROLL_BTN_W, TILE, TILE_RADIUS, rc);
601:  }
602:
603:  window_blit(g_win, 0, 0, g_sw, DOCK_H, g_fb);
604:}
605:
606:/* hit_slot - map a dock-local click x to a window id, or -1 (current page
607: * only — scroll first to reach apps parked on another page). */
608:static int hit_slot(int rx) {
609:  for (int i = 0; i < g_slot_n; i++)
610:    if (rx >= g_slot_x[i] && rx < g_slot_x[i] + TILE)
611:      return g_slot_id[i];
612:  return -1;
613:}
614:
615:/* act - toggle a tile: restore if backgrounded, background if focused, else
616: * focus.  Re-reads the window's current state so the toggle is correct.
617: * Keeps g_last_focus in sync on the focus-gaining branches (focus and
618: * restore).  On the minimize branch we intentionally do NOT clear it: the
619: * app that just lost focus is still the one the user was on, so a stray
620: * click on the dock / scroll button should bring IT back, not nothing. */
621:static void act(int id) {
622:  struct window_info wi[MAX_TILES];
623:  int n = (int)OS1_window_enum(wi, MAX_TILES);
624:  unsigned int f = 0;
625:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
626:    if (wi[i].id == id) {
627:      f = wi[i].flags;
628:      break;
629:    }
630:  if (f & WININFO_MINIMIZED) {
631:    OS1_window_restore(id);
632:    g_last_focus = id;
633:  } else if (f & WININFO_FOCUSED) {
634:    OS1_window_minimize(id);
635:  } else {
636:    OS1_window_focus(id);
637:    g_last_focus = id;
638:  }
639:}
640:
641:int main(void) {
642:  /* Singleton: only one dock may run.  If a window titled "nxui" already exists
643:   * (another live instance), bow out.  init respawns the dock when it dies, and
644:   * a dead process's windows are destroyed by the compositor, so a legitimate
645:   * respawn finds none and proceeds. */
646:  {
647:    struct window_info wi[MAX_TILES];
648:    int n = (int)OS1_window_enum(wi, MAX_TILES);
649:    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
650:      if (strncmp(wi[i].title, "nxui", 5) == 0)
651:        return 0; /* another nxui is already up */
652:  }
653:
654:  long di = OS1_display_info();
655:  int sw = (int)((di >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
656:  int sh = (int)(di & 0xFFFF);
657:  if (sw <= 0)
658:    sw = 800;
659:  if (sh <= 0)
660:    sh = 600;
661:
662:  nxui_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
663:
664:  g_fb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)sw * DOCK_H * 4);
665:  if (!g_fb)
666:    return 1;
667:  g_win = -1;
668:  dock_reinit(sw, sh);
669:  if (g_win < 0)
670:    return 1;
671:
672:  redraw(1); /* force the first paint */
673:
674:  for (;;) {
675:    /* adapt to a desktop resolution change (polled — works even before the
676:     * event-driven INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE path below is wired system-wide).
677:     * Compared against g_dsw/g_dsh (the DESKTOP size) — not g_sw, which is
678:     * now the dock's own narrower width. */
679:    long d = OS1_display_info();
680:    int cw = (int)((d >> 16) & 0xFFFF), ch = (int)(d & 0xFFFF);
681:    if (cw > 0 && ch > 0 && (cw != g_dsw || ch != g_dsh))
682:      dock_reinit(cw, ch);
683:
684:    redraw(0);
685:
686:    /* Standard window input: clicks arrive as INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE while the dock
687:     * holds focus (clicking a tile both focuses the dock — so the event is
688:     * delivered here — and carries dock-local coordinates). */
689:    input_event_t ev;
690:    while (input_poll_event(&ev) == 1) {
691:      if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE) {
692:        if (ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
693:            ev.mouse.state == KEY_PRESSED) {
694:          int acted = 1; /* 0 if this click did not drive any app's focus;
695:                          * in that case we hand the focus back to the app
696:                          * that owned it before the dock stole it. */
697:          if (g_scroll_on && ev.mouse.x >= g_btn_l_x &&
698:              ev.mouse.x < g_btn_l_x + SCROLL_BTN_W) {
699:            g_pressed = 1;
700:            g_page = (g_page - 1 + g_pages) % g_pages; /* loop left */
701:            redraw(1); /* immediate feedback: pressed colour + new page */
702:            acted = 0;
703:          } else if (g_scroll_on && ev.mouse.x >= g_btn_r_x &&
704:                     ev.mouse.x < g_btn_r_x + SCROLL_BTN_W) {
705:            g_pressed = 2;
706:            g_page = (g_page + 1) % g_pages; /* loop right */
707:            redraw(1);
708:            acted = 0;
709:          } else {
710:            int id = hit_slot(ev.mouse.x);
711:            if (id > 0)
712:              act(id); /* drives focus through OS1_window_focus / restore;
713:                        * for the toggle-to-minimize branch we keep the
714:                        * previous g_last_focus so the next non-act click
715:                        * restores this very app. */
716:            else
717:              acted = 0; /* click landed on empty dock space */
718:          }
719:          /* A click on a tile already drove focus via act().  Anything else
720:           * (scroll buttons, empty space) only changed dock state — hand
721:           * the focus back to the app the user was on so the next keystroke
722:           * does not silently go to the dock. */
723:          if (!acted && g_last_focus > 0)
724:            OS1_window_focus(g_last_focus);
725:        } else if (ev.mouse.button == MOUSE_BTN_LEFT &&
726:                   ev.mouse.state == KEY_RELEASED && g_pressed) {
727:          g_pressed = 0; /* back to material red */
728:          redraw(1);
729:        }
730:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE) {
731:        /* event-driven adaptation: the system told us the geometry changed. */
732:        long d2 = OS1_display_info();
733:        int rw = (int)((d2 >> 16) & 0xFFFF), rh = (int)(d2 & 0xFFFF);
734:        if (rw > 0 && rh > 0)
735:          dock_reinit(rw, rh);
736:      } else if (ev.type == INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED) {
737:        /* External style/theme/bg change (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h),
738:         * surfaced through this SAME input_poll_event() loop — see nxres.h's
739:         * header comment for why a second try_recv() loop is wrong here. */
740:        nxui_load_palette(nxres_theme_is_light());
741:        redraw(1);
742:      }
743:    }
744:
745:    OS1_sleep(
746:        33); /* ~30 Hz poll; descheduled between ticks, never busy-spins */
747:  }
748:  return 0;
749:}

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxwins.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/bin/nxwins.c
3: * NEXS window-listing tool (ASTRA §6.7) — the textual twin of the dock
4: * /sys/bin/nxui, split out of the shell into its own system program (like
5: * nxproc/nxres/nxinfo).
6: *
7: * Usage:
8: *   nxwins              list compositor windows (id/pid/state/title)
9: *   nxwins focus <id>   give a window keyboard focus (reveal if backgrounded)
10: *
11: * Thin CLI over the same SYS_WINDOW_ENUM (OS1_window_enum) and OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW
12: * focus capability (OS1_window_focus) the kernel already gates per caller — no
13: * policy of its own, so nxwins's reach is exactly the caller's reach.
14: */
15:#include <os1.h>
16:
17:/*
18: * cmd_list - `nxwins` (no args): enumerate and print the compositor's windows.
19: */
20:static int cmd_list(void) {
21:  struct window_info wi[32];
22:  int n = (int)OS1_window_enum(wi, 32);
23:  if (n < 0) {
24:    printf("nxwins: error enumerating windows\n");
25:    return 1;
26:  }
27:  printf("\033[1;33mID   PID  STATE   TITLE\033[0m\n");
28:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
29:    const char *st = (wi[i].flags & WININFO_MINIMIZED) ? "min"
30:                     : (wi[i].flags & WININFO_FOCUSED)  ? "focus"
31:                     : (wi[i].flags & WININFO_VISIBLE)  ? "shown"
32:                                                        : "hidden";
33:    /* Phase 3: prefer nxexec's canonical launch identity (sys.proc.<pid>.name)
34:     * over the app's own window title, so nxwins/nxbar/dock all show one
35:     * stable name; fall back to the title when there is no registered id. */
36:    char idkey[48], idname[40];
37:    const char *label = wi[i].title;
38:    snprintf(idkey, sizeof(idkey), "sys.proc.%d.name", wi[i].pid);
39:    if (OS1_registry_get(idkey, idname, sizeof(idname)) == 0 && idname[0])
40:      label = idname;
41:    printf("%d  %d  %s  %s\n", wi[i].id, wi[i].pid, st, label);
42:  }
43:  return 0;
44:}
45:
46:/*
47: * cmd_focus - `nxwins focus <id>`: give a window keyboard focus.  The kernel
48: * decides whether this caller may focus the target; we only relay the outcome.
49: */
50:static int cmd_focus(const char *id_arg) {
51:  int id = atoi(id_arg);
52:  if (id <= 0) {
53:    printf("nxwins: invalid window id '%s'\n", id_arg);
54:    return 1;
55:  }
56:  int r = OS1_window_focus(id);
57:  if (r == 0) {
58:    printf("nxwins: focused window %d\n", id);
59:    return 0;
60:  }
61:  printf("nxwins: focus failed (%d)\n", r);
62:  return 1;
63:}
64:
65:int main(int argc, char **argv) {
66:  /* nxwins focus <id> */
67:  if (argc >= 3 && strncmp(argv[1], "focus", 6) == 0)
68:    return cmd_focus(argv[2]);
69:
70:  /* nxwins (no args): list windows. */
71:  if (argc < 2)
72:    return cmd_list();
73:
74:  printf("nxwins: bad arguments\n");
75:  printf("usage: nxwins | nxwins focus <id>\n");
76:  return 1;
77:}

1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/coreutils/configmake.h
3: * Directory and path constants for GNU Coreutils on NexsOS1.
4: */
5:
6:#ifndef _CONFIGMAKE_H
