@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/coreutils/coreutils_os1_glue.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/coreutils/coreutils_os1_glue.c
3: * Implementation of Coreutils glue for NexsOS1.
4: */
5:
6:#include "coreutils_os1_glue.h"
7:#include <string.h>
8:#include <stdio.h>
9:#include <errno.h>
10:#include <sys/stat.h>
11:#include <poll.h>
12:#include <unistd.h>
13:
14:int coreutils_os1_uname(struct os1_utsname *buf) {
15:    if (!buf) {
16:        errno = EFAULT;
17:        return -1;
18:    }
19:    strncpy(buf->sysname, "NexsOS1", sizeof(buf->sysname) - 1);
20:    buf->sysname[sizeof(buf->sysname) - 1] = '\0';
21:
22:    strncpy(buf->nodename, "nexsos", sizeof(buf->nodename) - 1);
23:    buf->nodename[sizeof(buf->nodename) - 1] = '\0';
24:
25:    strncpy(buf->release, "0.0.5.4", sizeof(buf->release) - 1);
26:    buf->release[sizeof(buf->release) - 1] = '\0';
27:
28:    strncpy(buf->version, "ASTRA-V0.0.5.4", sizeof(buf->version) - 1);
29:    buf->version[sizeof(buf->version) - 1] = '\0';
30:
31:#if defined(ARCH_AMD64) || defined(__x86_64__)
32:    strncpy(buf->machine, "x86_64", sizeof(buf->machine) - 1);
33:#else
34:    strncpy(buf->machine, "aarch64", sizeof(buf->machine) - 1);
35:#endif
36:    buf->machine[sizeof(buf->machine) - 1] = '\0';
37:
38:    return 0;
39:}
40:
41:int posix2_version(void) {
42:    return 200809;
43:}
44:
45:int isapipe(int fd) {
46:    struct stat st;
47:    if (fstat(fd, &st) < 0)
48:        return 0;
49:    return S_ISFIFO(st.st_mode) ? 1 : 0;
50:}
51:
52:int iopoll(int fdin, int fdout, bool block) {
53:    (void)fdin;
54:    (void)block;
55:    if (fdout < 0)
56:        return 0;
57:
58:    struct pollfd pfd;
59:    pfd.fd = fdout;
60:    pfd.events = POLLOUT;
61:    pfd.revents = 0;
62:
63:    int r = poll(&pfd, 1, block ? -1 : 0);
64:    if (r < 0)
65:        return -3; /* IOPOLL_ERROR */
66:    if (r == 0 && !block)
67:        return 0;
68:    if (pfd.revents & (POLLHUP | POLLERR | POLLNVAL))
69:        return -2; /* IOPOLL_BROKEN_OUTPUT */
70:
71:    return 0;
72:}
73:
74:bool iopoll_input_ok(int fdin) {
75:    struct stat st;
76:    bool always_ready = fstat(fdin, &st) == 0
77:                        && (S_ISREG(st.st_mode) || S_ISBLK(st.st_mode));
78:    return !always_ready;
79:}
80:
81:bool iopoll_output_ok(int fdout) {
82:    return isapipe(fdout) > 0;
83:}
84:
85:bool write_wait(int fd, void const *buffer, size_t size) {
86:    char const *buf = buffer;
87:
88:#ifndef EWOULDBLOCK
89:#define EWOULDBLOCK EAGAIN
90:#endif
91:
92:    while (size > 0) {
93:        ssize_t written = write(fd, buf, size);
94:        if (written < 0) {
95:            if (errno == EAGAIN || errno == EWOULDBLOCK) {
96:                struct pollfd pfd;
97:                pfd.fd = fd;
98:                pfd.events = POLLOUT;
99:                pfd.revents = 0;
100:
101:                int rc = poll(&pfd, 1, -1);
102:                if (rc < 0 && errno == EINTR)
103:                    continue;
104:                if (rc < 0)
105:                    return false;
106:                continue;
107:            }
108:            return false;
109:        }
110:        if (written == 0)
111:            return false;
112:        buf += written;
113:        size -= (size_t)written;
114:    }
115:
116:    return true;
117:}
118:
119:/* mbschr and mbslen: multibyte string functions for coreutils.
120: * In NexsOS1, we treat strings as UTF-8 but operate on bytes.
121: * These stubs provide basic ASCII-compatible implementations. */
122:
123:/* mbschr: find character in multibyte string.
124: * In NexsOS1, since we're ASCII-compatible, just use strchr. */
125:char *mbschr(const char *s, int c) {
126:  if (!s)
127:    return NULL;
128:  return (char *)strchr(s, c);
129:}
130:
131:/* mbslen: length of multibyte string.
132: * In NexsOS1, treat as byte length (like strlen for ASCII). */
133:size_t mbslen(const char *s) {
134:  if (!s)
135:    return 0;
136:  return strlen(s);
137:}
138:
139:/* mbrlen: minimal byte-wise multibyte-length helper used by pathchk.c.
140: * NexsOS1 treats all bytes as single-byte characters in the bootstrap layer. */
141:size_t mbrlen(const char *s, size_t n, mbstate_t *ps) {
142:    (void)n;
143:    if (ps)
144:        memset(ps, 0, sizeof(*ps));
145:    if (!s)
146:        return 0;
147:    if (*s == '\0')
148:        return 0;
149:    return 1;
150:}
151:

51:/* Qualifier in a function declaration, that asserts that the caller must
52:   pass a pointer to a different object in the specified pointer argument
53:   than in the other pointer arguments.  */

56:     || 2 < __GNUC__ + (95 <= __GNUC_MINOR__) \
57:     || __clang_major__ >= 3
58:#  define _UC_RESTRICT __restrict
59:# elif 199901L <= __STDC_VERSION__ || defined restrict
60:#  define _UC_RESTRICT restrict
61:# else
62:#  define _UC_RESTRICT
63:# endif
64:#endif
65:

67:#ifdef __cplusplus
68:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/d3d9/os1_d3d9_present.c @@@
1:/* OS1 D3D9-style presentation chain over the portability adapter. */
2:#include "os1_d3d9_present.h"
3:
4:#include <errno.h>
5:#include <stdlib.h>
6:#include <string.h>
7:
8:#include "../os1_video_platform.h"
9:
10:/* Backend dispatch table: device/context-facing entry points never branch on
11: * the backend themselves, they forward here.  A future ASTRA GPU-context
12: * backend adds one more table, not new personality code. */
13:struct os1_d3d9_present_ops {
14:  uint32_t backend;
15:  int (*create)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
16:                const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params);
17:  void (*destroy)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
18:  int (*lock)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
19:              struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out);
20:  int (*unlock)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
21:  int (*present)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
22:                 const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty);
23:  int (*reset)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain, int width, int height);
24:};
25:
26:struct os1_d3d9_swapchain {
27:  const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops *ops;
28:  int window;
29:  int width;
30:  int height;
31:  int locked;
32:  uint32_t *backbuffer;
33:};
34:
35:/* ── Software backend: CPU backbuffer presented over os1_video_platform ── */
36:
37:static int sw_create(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc,
38:                     const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params) {
39:  size_t count = (size_t)params->width * (size_t)params->height;
40:  sc->backbuffer = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
41:  if (!sc->backbuffer)
42:    return -ENOMEM;
43:  memset(sc->backbuffer, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
44:
45:  sc->window = os1_video_window_create(params->x, params->y, params->width,
46:                                       params->height, params->title);
47:  if (sc->window < 0) {
48:    free(sc->backbuffer);
49:    sc->backbuffer = NULL;
50:    return sc->window;
51:  }
52:  sc->width = params->width;
53:  sc->height = params->height;
54:  return 0;
55:}
56:
57:static void sw_destroy(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc) {
58:  if (sc->window >= 0)
59:    os1_video_window_destroy(sc->window);
60:  free(sc->backbuffer);
61:  sc->backbuffer = NULL;
62:}
63:
64:static int sw_lock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc,
65:                   struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out) {
66:  out->bits = sc->backbuffer;
67:  out->pitch = (size_t)sc->width * sizeof(uint32_t);
68:  return 0;
69:}
70:
71:static int sw_unlock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc) {
72:  (void)sc;
73:  return 0;
74:}
75:
76:static int sw_present(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc,
77:                      const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty) {
78:  int x = 0, y = 0, w = sc->width, h = sc->height;
79:  if (dirty) {
80:    x = dirty->x;
81:    y = dirty->y;
82:    w = dirty->width;
83:    h = dirty->height;
84:    /* Clamp to the backbuffer (D3D9 rejects out-of-range source rects). */
85:    if (x < 0 || y < 0 || w <= 0 || h <= 0 || x + w > sc->width ||
86:        y + h > sc->height)
87:      return -EINVAL;
88:  }
89:  const uint32_t *first_row = sc->backbuffer + (size_t)y * sc->width + x;
90:  size_t remaining =
91:      (size_t)sc->width * sc->height - ((size_t)y * sc->width + x);
92:  int rc = os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(sc->window, x, y, w, h,
93:                                              first_row, (size_t)sc->width,
94:                                              remaining);
95:  if (rc < 0)
96:    return rc;
97:  os1_video_render();
98:  return 0;
99:}
100:
101:static int sw_reset(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc, int width, int height) {
102:  size_t count = (size_t)width * (size_t)height;
103:  uint32_t *fresh = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
104:  if (!fresh)
105:    return -ENOMEM;
106:  memset(fresh, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
107:
108:  int rc = os1_video_window_resize(sc->window, width, height);
109:  if (rc < 0) {
110:    free(fresh);
111:    return rc;
112:  }
113:  free(sc->backbuffer);
114:  sc->backbuffer = fresh;
115:  sc->width = width;
116:  sc->height = height;
117:  return 0;
118:}
119:
120:static const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops software_present_ops = {
121:    .backend = OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE,
122:    .create = sw_create,
123:    .destroy = sw_destroy,
124:    .lock = sw_lock,
125:    .unlock = sw_unlock,
126:    .present = sw_present,
127:    .reset = sw_reset,
128:};
129:
130:/* ── Backend-independent dispatch ──────────────────────────────────────── */
131:
132:static const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops *select_present_ops(void) {
133:  struct os1_video_info info;
134:  if (os1_video_query(&info) != 0)
135:    return NULL;
136:  if (info.backend == OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE &&
137:      (info.capabilities & OS1_VIDEO_CAP_ARGB8888))
138:    return &software_present_ops;
139:  /* OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_GPU_CONTEXT is reserved for the ASTRA GPU object. */
140:  return NULL;
141:}
142:
143:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_create(const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params,
144:                              struct os1_d3d9_swapchain **out) {
145:  if (!params || !out || params->width <= 0 || params->height <= 0 ||
146:      !params->title)
147:    return -EINVAL;
148:
149:  const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops *ops = select_present_ops();
150:  if (!ops)
151:    return -ENOSYS;
152:
153:  struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc =
154:      (struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *)malloc(sizeof(*sc));
155:  if (!sc)
156:    return -ENOMEM;
157:  memset(sc, 0, sizeof(*sc));
158:  sc->ops = ops;
159:  sc->window = -1;
160:
161:  int rc = ops->create(sc, params);
162:  if (rc < 0) {
163:    free(sc);
164:    return rc;
165:  }
166:  *out = sc;
167:  return 0;
168:}
169:
170:void os1_d3d9_swapchain_destroy(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain) {
171:  if (!swapchain)
172:    return;
173:  swapchain->ops->destroy(swapchain);
174:  free(swapchain);
175:}
176:
177:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_lock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
178:                            struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out) {
179:  if (!swapchain || !out)
180:    return -EINVAL;
181:  if (swapchain->locked)
182:    return -EBUSY;
183:  int rc = swapchain->ops->lock(swapchain, out);
184:  if (rc == 0)
185:    swapchain->locked = 1;
186:  return rc;
187:}
188:
189:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_unlock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain) {
190:  if (!swapchain)
191:    return -EINVAL;
192:  if (!swapchain->locked)
193:    return -EINVAL;
194:  int rc = swapchain->ops->unlock(swapchain);
195:  if (rc == 0)
196:    swapchain->locked = 0;
197:  return rc;
198:}
199:
200:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_present(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
201:                               const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty) {
202:  if (!swapchain)
203:    return -EINVAL;
204:  if (swapchain->locked)
205:    return -EINVAL; /* D3D9: presenting a locked surface is illegal */
206:  return swapchain->ops->present(swapchain, dirty);
207:}
208:
209:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_reset(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain, int width,
210:                             int height) {
211:  if (!swapchain || width <= 0 || height <= 0)
212:    return -EINVAL;
213:  if (swapchain->locked)
214:    return -EBUSY;
215:  return swapchain->ops->reset(swapchain, width, height);
216:}
217:
218:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_backend(const struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain) {
219:  if (!swapchain)
220:    return -EINVAL;
221:  return (int)swapchain->ops->backend;
222:}
223:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/d3d9/os1_d3d9_present.h @@@
1:/*
2: * OS1 D3D9-style presentation chain.
3: *
4: * The presentation seam for the Direct3D 9 personality: a swapchain with a
5: * CPU backbuffer, D3D9 Lock/Unlock/Present/Reset semantics, mapped onto the
6: * os1_video_platform portability header.  Device/context dispatch is
7: * backend-independent: every entry point forwards through an ops table chosen
8: * at creation from the platform's advertised backend, so the software
9: * presenter can later be swapped for the ASTRA GPU-context object without
10: * touching D3D9-personality callers.
11: */
12:#ifndef OS1_D3D9_PRESENT_H
13:#define OS1_D3D9_PRESENT_H
14:
15:#include <stddef.h>
16:#include <stdint.h>
17:
18:struct os1_d3d9_present_params {
19:  int x;
20:  int y;
21:  int width;  /* backbuffer width in pixels  */
22:  int height; /* backbuffer height in pixels */
23:  const char *title;
24:};
25:
26:/* D3DLOCKED_RECT analogue: pitch is in BYTES, pixels are ARGB8888. */
27:struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect {
28:  uint32_t *bits;
29:  size_t pitch;
30:};
31:
32:/* Optional Present() dirty rect (D3D9 pSourceRect analogue). */
33:struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect {
34:  int x;
35:  int y;
36:  int width;
37:  int height;
38:};
39:
40:struct os1_d3d9_swapchain; /* opaque; owns window + backbuffer */
41:
42:/* Create a swapchain on the platform's active backend.  Returns 0 and a
43: * swapchain, -ENOSYS when only an unsupported backend is advertised, or a
44: * negative OS1 error. */
45:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_create(const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params,
46:                              struct os1_d3d9_swapchain **out);
47:void os1_d3d9_swapchain_destroy(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
48:
49:/* Lock grants CPU access to the backbuffer; Present while locked fails with
50: * -EINVAL (D3D9 forbids presenting a locked surface). */
51:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_lock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
52:                            struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out);
53:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_unlock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
54:
55:/* Present the backbuffer (or just `dirty` when non-NULL) and notify the
56: * compositor. */
57:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_present(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
58:                               const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty);
59:
60:/* D3D9 Reset analogue: resize window + backbuffer.  Fails while locked. */
61:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_reset(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain, int width,
62:                             int height);
63:
64:/* The enum os1_video_backend this swapchain runs on. */
65:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_backend(const struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
66:
67:#endif /* OS1_D3D9_PRESENT_H */
68:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/d3d9/README.md @@@
1:# D3D9 presentation backend
2:
3:`os1_d3d9_present.{h,c}` is the presentation seam for the Direct3D 9
4:personality: a swapchain with a CPU ARGB8888 backbuffer and D3D9
5:Lock/Unlock/Present/Reset semantics over `os1_video_platform.h`. Dispatch is
6:backend-independent (an ops table selected from the platform's advertised
7:backend), so the software presenter can later be swapped for the ASTRA
8:GPU-context object without touching personality callers.
9:
10:This is deliberately NOT a Direct3D API implementation: device/context/shader
11:dispatch belongs to the D3D9 compatibility layer sourced from the Wine
12:submodule on its `nexsos-port-d3d9` branch. Only the OS-facing presentation
13:glue lives here, per the non-negotiable constraint that upstream trees are
14:never patched for NexsOS integration.
15:
16:`demo3d` is the reference client: it renders its cube into the locked
17:backbuffer and presents through the swapchain, exercising the chain end to
18:end on both architectures.
19:

1:/* Compatibility generation for GNU libc scratch buffer internals.
2:   NexsOS1 uses the upstream Gnulib sources directly and expects the generated
3:   header that glibc-internal/scratch_buffer would normally create.  This file
4:   provides the minimal API surface required by canonicalize.c and similar
5:   helpers. */
6:
7:#ifndef _GL_SCRATCH_BUFFER_GL_H
8:#define _GL_SCRATCH_BUFFER_GL_H
9:
10:#include <stdbool.h>
11:#include <stddef.h>
12:#include <stdlib.h>
13:
14:#ifndef _GL_LIKELY
15:# define _GL_LIKELY(cond) __builtin_expect ((cond), 1)
16:# define _GL_UNLIKELY(cond) __builtin_expect ((cond), 0)
17:#endif
18:
19:#ifndef __GLIBC_LIKELY
20:# define __GLIBC_LIKELY(cond) _GL_LIKELY (cond)
21:# define __GLIBC_UNLIKELY(cond) _GL_UNLIKELY (cond)
22:#endif
23:
24:#define __libc_scratch_buffer_grow _gl_scratch_buffer_grow
25:#define __libc_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve _gl_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve
26:#define __libc_scratch_buffer_set_array_size _gl_scratch_buffer_set_array_size
27:
28:struct scratch_buffer {
29:  void *data;
30:  size_t length;
31:  union { long double __align; char __c[1024]; } __space;
32:};
33:
34:static inline void
35:scratch_buffer_init (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
36:{
37:  buffer->data = buffer->__space.__c;
38:  buffer->length = sizeof (buffer->__space);
39:}
40:
41:static inline void
42:scratch_buffer_free (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
43:{
44:  if (buffer->data != buffer->__space.__c)
45:    free (buffer->data);
46:}
47:
48:bool __libc_scratch_buffer_grow (struct scratch_buffer *buffer);
49:static __inline__ bool
50:scratch_buffer_grow (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
51:{
52:  return __GLIBC_LIKELY (__libc_scratch_buffer_grow (buffer));
53:}
54:
55:bool __libc_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve (struct scratch_buffer *buffer);
56:static __inline__ bool
57:scratch_buffer_grow_preserve (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
58:{
59:  return __GLIBC_LIKELY (__libc_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve (buffer));
60:}
61:
62:bool __libc_scratch_buffer_set_array_size (struct scratch_buffer *buffer,
63:                                           size_t nelem, size_t size);
64:static __inline__ bool
65:scratch_buffer_set_array_size (struct scratch_buffer *buffer,
66:                              size_t nelem, size_t size)
67:{
68:  return __GLIBC_LIKELY (__libc_scratch_buffer_set_array_size (buffer, nelem, size));
69:}
70:
71:#endif

1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/fts_.h
3: * Shim for Gnulib's fts_.h, generated from fts.in.h
4: * NexsOS1 doesn't have a real fts implementation, so this provides minimal stubs.

7:#ifndef FTS_H
8:#define FTS_H
9:

11:#include <dirent.h>
12:
13:/* FTS entry types */
14:#define FTS_D     1    /* preorder directory */
15:#define FTS_DC    2    /* directory that causes cycles */
16:#define FTS_DEFAULT 3  /* none of the above */
17:#define FTS_DNR   4    /* unreadable directory */
18:#define FTS_DOT   5    /* dot or dot-dot */
19:#define FTS_DP    6    /* postorder directory */
20:#define FTS_ERR   7    /* error; errno is set */
21:#define FTS_F     8    /* regular file */
22:#define FTS_INIT  9    /* initialized only */
23:#define FTS_NS   10    /* stat(2) failed */
24:#define FTS_NSOK 11    /* no stat(2) requested */
25:#define FTS_SL   12    /* symbolic link */
26:#define FTS_SLNONE 13  /* symbolic link with no file */
27:#define FTS_W    14    /* whiteout object */
28:
29:/* FTS options */
30:#define FTS_COMFOLLOW  0x0001
31:#define FTS_LOGICAL    0x0002
32:#define FTS_NOCHDIR    0x0004
33:#define FTS_NOSTAT     0x0008
34:#define FTS_PHYSICAL   0x0010
35:#define FTS_SEEDOT     0x0020
36:#define FTS_XDEV       0x0040
37:#define FTS_WHITEOUT   0x0080
38:#define FTS_MOUNT      0x0100
39:#define FTS_CWDFD      0x0200
40:#define FTS_DEFER_STAT 0x0400
41:#define FTS_OPTIONMASK 0x0fff
42:
43:#define FTS_NAMEONLY   0x100
44:#define FTS_STOP       0x200
45:
46:/* FTS levels */
47:#define FTS_ROOTPARENTLEVEL -1
48:#define FTS_ROOTLEVEL        0
49:
50:typedef struct {
51:    struct _ftsent *fts_cur;
52:    struct _ftsent *fts_child;
53:    struct _ftsent **fts_array;
54:    dev_t fts_dev;
55:    char *fts_path;
56:    int fts_rfd;
57:    int fts_cwd_fd;  /* current working directory file descriptor */
58:    size_t fts_pathlen;
59:    size_t fts_nitems;
60:    int (*fts_compar)();
61:    int fts_options;
62:} FTS;

66:/*
67: * NexsOS1 getcwd() returns int; POSIX/gnulib expects char *.
68: * Use the underlying _sys_getcwd and provide a POSIX shim.
69: */
70:extern int _sys_getcwd(char *buf, size_t size);
71:
72:static inline char *getcwd(char *buf, size_t size) {
73:  char *ret = buf;
74:  if (!buf) {
75:    size = size ? size : 4096;
76:    ret = (char *)malloc(size);
77:    if (!ret) return (char *)0;
78:  }
79:  if (_sys_getcwd(ret, size) != 0) {
80:    if (!buf) free(ret);
81:    return (char *)0;
82:  }
83:  return ret;
84:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/gnulib_os1_glue.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/gnulib_os1_glue.c
3: * Real implementation connecting Gnulib abstractions to NexsOS1 syscalls and VFS.
4: */
5:
6:#define _GNULIB_OS1_GLUE_IMPL
7:#include "gnulib_os1_glue.h"
8:#include <stdio.h>
9:#include <stdlib.h>
10:#include <string.h>
11:#include <unistd.h>
12:#include <fcntl.h>
13:#include <sys/stat.h>
14:
15:/* La variabile program_name viene impostata da gnulib (progname.c)
16:   tramite set_program_name() all'avvio di ogni programma GNU. */
17:extern char *program_name;
18:
19:static char g_progname_buf[64] = "nexsos_app";
20:
21:int gnulib_os1_getpagesize(void) {
22:    return NEXSOS_PAGE_SIZE;
23:}
24:
25:int gnulib_os1_getdtablesize(void) {
26:    return NEXSOS_MAX_FD;
27:}
28:
29:const char *gnulib_os1_getprogname(void) {
30:    /* Se il buffer contiene ancora il default, prova a usare program_name
31:       che gnulib ha impostato (es. "mkdir", "cat", "ls"). */
32:    if (strcmp(g_progname_buf, "nexsos_app") == 0) {
33:        if (program_name && program_name[0] != '\0')
34:            return program_name;
35:    }
36:    return g_progname_buf;
37:}
38:
39:void gnulib_os1_setprogname(const char *name) {
40:    if (!name || !*name)
41:        return;
42:    const char *p = strrchr(name, '/');
43:    if (p)
44:        name = p + 1;
45:    strncpy(g_progname_buf, name, sizeof(g_progname_buf) - 1);
46:    g_progname_buf[sizeof(g_progname_buf) - 1] = '\0';
47:}
48:
49:ssize_t gnulib_os1_safe_read(int fd, void *buf, size_t count) {
50:    if (fd < 0 || !buf) {
51:        errno = EBADF;
52:        return -1;
53:    }
54:    long ret = read(fd, (char *)buf, (unsigned long)count);
55:    if (ret < 0) {
56:        errno = (int)(-ret);
57:        return -1;
58:    }
59:    return (ssize_t)ret;
60:}
61:
62:ssize_t gnulib_os1_safe_write(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count) {
63:    if (fd < 0 || !buf) {
64:        errno = EBADF;
65:        return -1;
66:    }
67:    long ret = write(fd, (const char *)buf, count);
68:    if (ret < 0) {
69:        errno = (int)(-ret);
70:        return -1;
71:    }
72:    return (ssize_t)ret;
73:}
74:
75:void *gnulib_os1_rawmemchr(const void *s, int c) {
76:    const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s;
77:    unsigned char uc = (unsigned char)c;
78:    while (*p != uc) {
79:        p++;
80:    }
81:    return (void *)p;
82:}
83:
84:void *gnulib_os1_memrchr(const void *s, int c, size_t n) {
85:    if (n == 0 || !s)
86:        return NULL;
87:    const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s + n;
88:    unsigned char uc = (unsigned char)c;
89:    while (n > 0) {
90:        p--;
91:        if (*p == uc)
92:            return (void *)p;
93:        n--;
94:    }
95:    return NULL;
96:}

105:void verror(int status, int errnum, const char *format, va_list args) {
106:    fflush(stdout);
107:    if (error_print_progname) {
108:        error_print_progname();
109:    } else {

111:        if (pname && *pname) {
112:            fprintf(stderr, "%s: ", pname);
113:        }
114:    }
115:    vfprintf(stderr, format, args);
116:    if (errnum) {
117:        fprintf(stderr, ": %s", strerror(errnum));
118:    }
119:    fprintf(stderr, "\n");
120:    fflush(stderr);
121:    error_message_count++;
122:    if (status) {
123:        exit(status);
124:    }
125:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/hard_locale_compat.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/hard_locale_compat.c
3: * NexsOS1 locale compatibility layer for Gnulib hard_locale() function.
4: *
5: * Coreutils (via gnulib) calls hard_locale(category) to check if the
6: * current locale for that category (LC_TIME, LC_COLLATE, etc.) is non-C.
7: * NexsOS1 runs ONLY in the C/POSIX locale with no locale switching,
8: * so we provide minimal stubs here that declare NexsOS1 is always in C locale.
9: *
10: * This avoids compiling gnulib's complex setlocale_null.c, which has
11: * threading infrastructure and platform-specific logic we don't need.
12: */
13:
14:#include <stdbool.h>
15:#include <stddef.h>
16:#include <string.h>
17:
18:/* SETLOCALE_NULL_MAX: max size for locale category name buffer.
19: * Standard gnulib definition. */
20:#define SETLOCALE_NULL_MAX (256+1)
21:
22:/* setlocale_null_r_unlocked: get the current locale category name without locking.
23: * In NexsOS1, always returns "C" for any category.
24: * Returns 0 on success, EINVAL if category is invalid. */
25:int setlocale_null_r_unlocked(int category, char *buf, size_t bufsize) {
26:  /* Validate category */
27:  if (category < 0) {
28:    return 22; /* EINVAL */
29:  }
30:
31:  /* NexsOS1 is always in C locale */
32:  const char *locale_name = "C";
33:  size_t needed = strlen(locale_name) + 1;
34:
35:  if (bufsize < needed) {
36:    return 34; /* ERANGE */
37:  }
38:
39:  if (buf) {
40:    strncpy(buf, locale_name, bufsize - 1);
41:    buf[bufsize - 1] = '\0';
42:  }
43:  return 0; /* Success */
44:}
45:
46:/* setlocale_null_r: thread-safe version (in NexsOS1, no threading needed).
47: * Returns error code like setlocale_null_r_unlocked. */
48:int setlocale_null_r(int category, char *buf, size_t bufsize) {
49:  /* No threading in freestanding NexsOS1, so just call the unlocked version */
50:  return setlocale_null_r_unlocked(category, buf, bufsize);
51:}
52:
53:/* hard_locale: determine if the current locale category is "hard" (non-C).
54: * A "hard" locale has special behavior (collation, formatting, etc.).
55: * NexsOS1 always runs in C/POSIX locale, so this always returns false. */
56:bool hard_locale(int category) {
57:  (void)category; /* Unused in NexsOS1 */
58:  return false;
59:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/mbs_compat.c @@@
1:#include <stddef.h>
2:#include <string.h>
3:
4:/* Minimal multibyte-string compatibility shims needed by Coreutils on NexsOS1.
5: * These are intentionally small and conservative; they satisfy the GNU-like
6: * symbols referenced by expr without modifying the upstream second-repository
7: * sources.
8: */
9:
10:size_t mbslen(const char *string)
11:{
12:  size_t count = 0;
13:  if (!string)
14:    return 0;
15:
16:  while (*string) {
17:    unsigned char ch = (unsigned char)*string;
18:    if ((ch & 0x80) == 0) {
19:      string++;
20:      count++;
21:      continue;
22:    }
23:
24:    /* Count UTF-8 codepoints conservatively: skip one full codepoint. */
25:    if ((ch & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
26:      string += 2;
27:    } else if ((ch & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
28:      string += 3;
29:    } else if ((ch & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
30:      string += 4;
31:    } else {
32:      string++;
33:    }
34:    count++;
35:  }
36:
37:  return count;
38:}
39:
40:char *mbschr(const char *string, int c)
41:{
42:  if (!string)
43:    return NULL;
44:
45:  while (*string) {
46:    unsigned char ch = (unsigned char)*string;
47:    if ((ch & 0x80) == 0) {
48:      if ((unsigned char)c == ch)
49:        return (char *)string;
50:      string++;
51:      continue;
52:    }
53:
54:    /* ASCII-compatible single-byte search only; UTF-8 codepoints are treated
55:     * as opaque for the current NexsOS1 bootstrap layer. */
56:    if ((ch & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
57:      string += 2;
58:    } else if ((ch & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
59:      string += 3;
60:    } else if ((ch & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
61:      string += 4;
62:    } else {
63:      string++;
64:    }
65:  }
66:
67:  return NULL;
68:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/obstack.h @@@
1:/* obstack.h - object stack macros
2:   Copyright (C) 1988-2026 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
3:   This file is part of the GNU C Library.
4:
5:   The GNU C Library is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
6:   modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public
7:   License as published by the Free Software Foundation; either
8:   version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.
9:
10:   The GNU C Library is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
11:   but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
12:   MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the GNU
13:   Lesser General Public License for more details.
14:
15:   You should have received a copy of the GNU Lesser General Public
16:   License along with the GNU C Library; if not, see
17:   <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.  */
18:
19:/* Summary:
20:
21:   All the apparent functions defined here are macros. The idea
22:   is that you would use these pre-tested macros to solve a
23:   very specific set of problems, and they would run fast.
24:   Caution: no side-effects in arguments please!! They may be
25:   evaluated MANY times!!
26:
27:   These macros operate a stack of objects.  Each object starts life
28:   small, and may grow to maturity.  (Consider building a word syllable
29:   by syllable.)  An object can move while it is growing.  Once it has
30:   been "finished" it never changes address again.  So the "top of the
31:   stack" is typically an immature growing object, while the rest of the
32:   stack is of mature, fixed size and fixed address objects.
33:
34:   These routines grab large chunks of memory, using a function you
35:   supply, called 'obstack_chunk_alloc'.  On occasion, they free chunks,
36:   by calling 'obstack_chunk_free'.  You must define them and declare
37:   them before using any obstack macros.
38:
39:   Each independent stack is represented by a 'struct obstack'.
40:   Each of the obstack macros expects a pointer to such a structure
41:   as the first argument.
42:
43:   One motivation for this package is the problem of growing char strings
44:   in symbol tables.  Unless you are "fascist pig with a read-only mind"
45:   --Gosper's immortal quote from HAKMEM item 154, out of context--you
46:   would not like to put any arbitrary upper limit on the length of your
47:   symbols.
48:
49:   In practice this often means you will build many short symbols and a
50:   few long symbols.  At the time you are reading a symbol you don't know
51:   how long it is.  One traditional method is to read a symbol into a
52:   buffer, realloc()ating the buffer every time you try to read a symbol
53:   that is longer than the buffer.  This is beaut, but you still will
54:   want to copy the symbol from the buffer to a more permanent
55:   symbol-table entry say about half the time.
56:
57:   With obstacks, you can work differently.  Use one obstack for all symbol
58:   names.  As you read a symbol, grow the name in the obstack gradually.
59:   When the name is complete, finalize it.  Then, if the symbol exists already,
60:   free the newly read name.
61:
62:   The way we do this is to take a large chunk, allocating memory from
63:   low addresses.  When you want to build a symbol in the chunk you just
64:   add chars above the current "high water mark" in the chunk.  When you
65:   have finished adding chars, because you got to the end of the symbol,
66:   you know how long the chars are, and you can create a new object.
67:   Mostly the chars will not burst over the highest address of the chunk,
68:   because you would typically expect a chunk to be (say) 100 times as
69:   long as an average object.
70:
71:   In case that isn't clear, when we have enough chars to make up
72:   the object, THEY ARE ALREADY CONTIGUOUS IN THE CHUNK (guaranteed)
73:   so we just point to it where it lies.  No moving of chars is
74:   needed and this is the second win: potentially long strings need
75:   never be explicitly shuffled. Once an object is formed, it does not
76:   change its address during its lifetime.
77:
78:   When the chars burst over a chunk boundary, we allocate a larger
79:   chunk, and then copy the partly formed object from the end of the old
80:   chunk to the beginning of the new larger chunk.  We then carry on
81:   accreting characters to the end of the object as we normally would.
82:
83:   A special macro is provided to add a single char at a time to a
84:   growing object.  This allows the use of register variables, which
85:   break the ordinary 'growth' macro.
86:
87:   Summary:
88:        We allocate large chunks.
89:        We carve out one object at a time from the current chunk.
90:        Once carved, an object never moves.
91:        We are free to append data of any size to the currently
92:          growing object.
93:        Exactly one object is growing in an obstack at any one time.
94:        You can run one obstack per control block.
95:        You may have as many control blocks as you dare.
96:        Because of the way we do it, you can "unwind" an obstack
97:          back to a previous state. (You may remove objects much
98:          as you would with a stack.)
99: */
100:
101:/* Documentation (part of the GNU libc manual):
102:   <https://www.gnu.org/software/libc/manual/html_node/Obstacks.html>  */
103:
104:
105:/* Don't do the contents of this file more than once.  */
106:#ifndef _OBSTACK_H
107:#define _OBSTACK_H 1
108:
109:#if defined __GL_GNULIB_HEADER
110:/* This file uses _GL_ATTRIBUTE_PURE, FLEXIBLE_ARRAY_MEMBER.  */
111:# if !_GL_CONFIG_H_INCLUDED
112:  #error "Please include config.h first."
113:# endif
114:#endif
115:
116:/* For backward compatibility with older glibc,
117:   define the otherwise-unused macro PTR_INT_TYPE.  If __PTRDIFF_TYPE__ is
118:   defined, as with GNU C, use that; that way we don't pollute the
119:   namespace with <stddef.h>'s symbols.  Otherwise, include <stddef.h>
120:   and use ptrdiff_t.  */
121:#ifdef __PTRDIFF_TYPE__
122:# define PTR_INT_TYPE __PTRDIFF_TYPE__
123:#else
124:# include <stddef.h>
125:# define PTR_INT_TYPE ptrdiff_t
126:#endif
127:
128:/* An integer type wide enough to hold a pointer value,
129:   if such a type is available.  */
130:#ifdef __UINTPTR_TYPE__
131:# define _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE __UINTPTR_TYPE__
132:#elif defined __STDC_VERSION__ && 199901L <= __STDC_VERSION__
133:# include <stdint.h>
134:# ifdef UINTPTR_MAX
135:#  define _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE uintptr_t
136:# endif
137:#endif
138:
139:/* A type suitable for comparing pointers regardless of whether they
140:   point into the same object, e.g., (_OBSTACK_CPTR) p < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) q.
141:   If possible, use uintptr_t to avoid undefined behavior and pacify
142:   sanitizers.  Otherwise, use a pointer directly and hope for the best.  */
143:#ifdef _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE
144:typedef _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE _OBSTACK_CPTR;
145:#else
146:typedef char *_OBSTACK_CPTR;
147:#endif
148:
149:/* These macros highlight the places where this implementation
150:   is different from the one in GNU libc.  */
151:#if defined __GL_GNULIB_HEADER
152:/* In Gnulib, we use sane types, especially for 64-bit hosts.  */
153:# define _OBSTACK_INDEX_T size_t
154:# define _OBSTACK_SIZE_T size_t
155:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T size_t
156:# define _OBSTACK_CAST(type, expr) (expr)
157:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_CONTENTS_SIZE FLEXIBLE_ARRAY_MEMBER
158:#else
159:/* For backward compatibility, glibc limits object sizes to int range.  */
160:# define _OBSTACK_INDEX_T int
161:# define _OBSTACK_SIZE_T unsigned int
162:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T long int
163:# define _OBSTACK_CAST(type, expr) ((type) (expr))
164:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_CONTENTS_SIZE 4
165:#endif
166:
167:/* If B is the base of an object addressed by P, return the result of
168:   aligning P to the next multiple of A + 1.  B and P must be of type
169:   char *.  A + 1 must be a power of 2.  With no uintptr_t, play it
170:   safe and compute the alignment relative to B.  Otherwise, use the
171:   faster strategy of computing the alignment through uintptr_t.  */
172:#ifndef _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE
173:# define __PTR_ALIGN(B, P, A) \
174:   ((B) + (((P) - (B) + (A)) & ~(A)))
175:#else
176:# define __PTR_ALIGN(B, P, A) \
177:   ((P) + ((- (_OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE) (P)) & (A)))
178:#endif
179:
180:/* For memcpy, size_t.  */
181:#include <string.h>
182:
183:#ifndef __attribute_pure__
184:# define __attribute_pure__ _GL_ATTRIBUTE_PURE
185:#endif

187:/* Not the same as _Noreturn, since it also works with function pointers.  */
188:#ifndef __attribute_noreturn__
189:# if ((defined __GNUC__ && 2 < __GNUC__ + (8 <= __GNUC_MINOR__)) \
190:      || defined __clang__ \
191:      || (defined __SUNPRO_C && 0x5110 <= __SUNPRO_C))
192:#  define __attribute_noreturn__ __attribute__ ((__noreturn__))
193:# else
194:#  define __attribute_noreturn__
195:# endif
196:#endif

198:#ifdef __cplusplus
199:extern "C" {
200:#endif

202:struct _obstack_chunk           /* Lives at front of each chunk. */
203:{
204:  char *limit;                  /* 1 past end of this chunk */
205:  struct _obstack_chunk *prev;  /* address of prior chunk or NULL */
206:  char contents[_OBSTACK_CHUNK_CONTENTS_SIZE]; /* objects begin here */
207:};
208:
209:struct obstack          /* control current object in current chunk */
210:{
211:  _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T chunk_size;  /* preferred size to allocate chunks in */
212:  struct _obstack_chunk *chunk; /* address of current struct obstack_chunk */
213:  char *object_base;            /* address of object we are building */
214:  char *next_free;              /* where to add next char to current object */
215:  char *chunk_limit;            /* address of char after current chunk */
216:  union
217:  {
218:    _OBSTACK_SIZE_T tempint;
219:    void *tempptr;
220:  } temp;                       /* Temporary for some macros.  */
221:  _OBSTACK_INDEX_T alignment_mask;  /* Mask of alignment for each object. */
222:
223:  /* These prototypes vary based on 'use_extra_arg'.  */
224:  union
225:  {
226:    void *(*plain) (_OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T);
227:    void *(*extra) (void *, _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T);
228:  } chunkfun;
229:  union
230:  {
231:    void (*plain) (void *);
232:    void (*extra) (void *, void *);
233:  } freefun;
234:
235:  void *extra_arg;              /* first arg for chunk alloc/dealloc funcs */
236:  unsigned use_extra_arg : 1;     /* chunk alloc/dealloc funcs take extra arg */
237:  unsigned maybe_empty_object : 1; /* There is a possibility that the current
238:                                      chunk contains a zero-length object.  This
239:                                      prevents freeing the chunk if we allocate
240:                                      a bigger chunk to replace it. */
241:  unsigned alloc_failed : 1;      /* No longer used, as we now call the failed
242:                                     handler on error, but retained for binary
243:                                     compatibility.  */
244:};
245:
246:/* Declare the external functions we use; they are in obstack.c.  */
247:
248:/* Symbol mapping for gnulib.  */
249:#if defined __GL_GNULIB_HEADER && defined __GL_REPLACE_OBSTACK__

279:   more memory.  This can be set to a user defined function which
280:   should either abort gracefully or use longjump - but shouldn't
281:   return.  The default action is to print a message and abort.  */

288:   Note that this might not be the final address of the object

344:#if (defined __GNUC__ || defined __clang__ \

350:/* For GNU C, if not -traditional,
351:   we can define these macros to compute all args only once
352:   without using a global variable.
353:   Also, we can avoid using the 'temp' slot, to make faster code.  */
354:
355:# define obstack_object_size(OBSTACK) \
356:  __extension__ \
357:    ({ struct obstack const *__o = (OBSTACK); \
358:       (_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) (__o->next_free - __o->object_base); })
359:
360:/* The local variable is named __o1 to avoid a shadowed variable
361:   warning when invoked from other obstack macros.  */
362:# define obstack_room(OBSTACK) \
363:  __extension__ \
364:    ({ struct obstack const *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
365:       (_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) (__o1->chunk_limit - __o1->next_free); })
366:
367:# define obstack_make_room(OBSTACK, length) \
368:  __extension__ \
369:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
370:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
371:       if (obstack_room (__o) < __len) \
372:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len); \
373:       (void) 0; })
374:
375:# define obstack_empty_p(OBSTACK) \
376:  __extension__ \
377:    ({ struct obstack const *__o = (OBSTACK); \
378:       (__o->chunk->prev == 0 \
379:        && __o->next_free == __PTR_ALIGN ((char *) __o->chunk, \
380:                                          __o->chunk->contents, \
381:                                          __o->alignment_mask)); })
382:
383:# define obstack_grow(OBSTACK, where, length) \
384:  __extension__ \
385:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
386:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
387:       if (obstack_room (__o) < __len) \
388:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len); \
389:       memcpy (__o->next_free, where, __len); \
390:       __o->next_free += __len; \
391:       (void) 0; })
392:
393:# define obstack_grow0(OBSTACK, where, length) \
394:  __extension__ \
395:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
396:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
397:       if (obstack_room (__o) <= __len) \
398:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len + 1); \
399:       memcpy (__o->next_free, where, __len); \
400:       __o->next_free += __len; \
401:       *(__o->next_free)++ = 0; \
402:       (void) 0; })
403:
404:# define obstack_1grow(OBSTACK, datum) \
405:  __extension__ \
406:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
407:       if (obstack_room (__o) < 1) \
408:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, 1); \
409:       obstack_1grow_fast (__o, datum); \
410:       (void) 0; })
411:
412:/* These assume that the obstack alignment is good enough for pointers
413:   or ints, and that the data added so far to the current object
414:   shares that much alignment.  */
415:
416:# define obstack_ptr_grow(OBSTACK, datum) \
417:  __extension__ \
418:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
419:       if (obstack_room (__o) < sizeof (void *)) \
420:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, sizeof (void *)); \
421:       obstack_ptr_grow_fast (__o, datum); })
422:
423:# define obstack_int_grow(OBSTACK, datum) \
424:  __extension__ \
425:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
426:       if (obstack_room (__o) < sizeof (int)) \
427:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, sizeof (int)); \
428:       obstack_int_grow_fast (__o, datum); })
429:
430:# define obstack_ptr_grow_fast(OBSTACK, aptr) \
431:  __extension__ \
432:    ({ struct obstack *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
433:       void *__p1 = __o1->next_free; \
434:       *(const void **) __p1 = (aptr); \
435:       __o1->next_free += sizeof (const void *); \
436:       (void) 0; })
437:
438:# define obstack_int_grow_fast(OBSTACK, aint) \
439:  __extension__ \
440:    ({ struct obstack *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
441:       void *__p1 = __o1->next_free; \
442:       *(int *) __p1 = (aint); \
443:       __o1->next_free += sizeof (int); \
444:       (void) 0; })
445:
446:# define obstack_blank(OBSTACK, length) \
447:  __extension__ \
448:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
449:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
450:       if (obstack_room (__o) < __len) \
451:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len); \
452:       obstack_blank_fast (__o, __len); \
453:       (void) 0; })
454:
455:# define obstack_alloc(OBSTACK, length) \
456:  __extension__ \
457:    ({ struct obstack *__h = (OBSTACK); \
458:       obstack_blank (__h, (length)); \
459:       obstack_finish (__h); })
460:
461:# define obstack_copy(OBSTACK, where, length) \
462:  __extension__ \
463:    ({ struct obstack *__h = (OBSTACK); \
464:       obstack_grow (__h, (where), (length)); \
465:       obstack_finish (__h); })
466:
467:# define obstack_copy0(OBSTACK, where, length) \
468:  __extension__ \
469:    ({ struct obstack *__h = (OBSTACK); \
470:       obstack_grow0 (__h, (where), (length)); \
471:       obstack_finish (__h); })
472:
473:/* The local variable is named __o1 to avoid a shadowed variable
474:   warning when invoked from other obstack macros, typically obstack_free.  */
475:# define obstack_finish(OBSTACK) \
476:  __extension__ \
477:    ({ struct obstack *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
478:       void *__value = (void *) __o1->object_base; \
479:       if (__o1->next_free == __value) \
480:         __o1->maybe_empty_object = 1; \
481:       __o1->next_free \
482:         = __PTR_ALIGN (__o1->object_base, __o1->next_free, \
483:                        __o1->alignment_mask); \
484:       __o1->object_base = __o1->next_free; \
485:       __value; })
486:
487:# define obstack_free(OBSTACK, OBJ) \
488:  __extension__ \
489:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
490:       void *__obj = (OBJ); \
491:       if ((_OBSTACK_CPTR) __o->chunk < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) __obj \
492:           && (_OBSTACK_CPTR) __obj < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) __o->chunk_limit) \
493:         __o->next_free = __o->object_base = (char *) __obj; \
494:       else \
495:         __obstack_free (__o, __obj); })
496:
497:#else /* not __GNUC__-like */
498:
499:# define obstack_object_size(h) \
500:  ((_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) ((h)->next_free - (h)->object_base))
501:
502:# define obstack_room(h) \
503:  ((_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) ((h)->chunk_limit - (h)->next_free))
504:
505:# define obstack_empty_p(h) \
506:  ((h)->chunk->prev == 0 \
507:   && (h)->next_free == __PTR_ALIGN ((char *) (h)->chunk, \
508:                                     (h)->chunk->contents, \
509:                                     (h)->alignment_mask))
510:
511:/* Note that the call to _obstack_newchunk is enclosed in (..., 0)
512:   so that we can avoid having void expressions
513:   in the arms of the conditional expression.
514:   Casting the third operand to void was tried before,
515:   but some compilers won't accept it.  */
516:
517:# define obstack_make_room(h, length) \
518:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
519:   ((obstack_room (h) < (h)->temp.tempint) \
520:    ? (_obstack_newchunk (h, (h)->temp.tempint), 0) : 0), \
521:   (void) 0)
522:
523:# define obstack_grow(h, where, length) \
524:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
525:   ((obstack_room (h) < (h)->temp.tempint) \
526:   ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), (h)->temp.tempint), 0) : 0), \
527:   memcpy ((h)->next_free, where, (h)->temp.tempint), \
528:   (h)->next_free += (h)->temp.tempint, \
529:   (void) 0)
530:
531:# define obstack_grow0(h, where, length) \
532:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
533:   ((obstack_room (h) <= (h)->temp.tempint) \
534:   ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), (h)->temp.tempint + 1), 0) : 0), \
535:   memcpy ((h)->next_free, where, (h)->temp.tempint), \
536:   (h)->next_free += (h)->temp.tempint, \
537:   *((h)->next_free)++ = 0, \
538:   (void) 0)
539:
540:# define obstack_1grow(h, datum) \
541:  (((obstack_room (h) < 1) \
542:    ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), 1), 0) : 0), \
543:   obstack_1grow_fast (h, datum), \
544:   (void) 0)
545:
546:# define obstack_ptr_grow(h, datum) \
547:  (((obstack_room (h) < sizeof (char *)) \
548:    ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), sizeof (char *)), 0) : 0), \
549:   obstack_ptr_grow_fast (h, datum))
550:
551:# define obstack_int_grow(h, datum) \
552:  (((obstack_room (h) < sizeof (int)) \
553:    ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), sizeof (int)), 0) : 0), \
554:   obstack_int_grow_fast (h, datum))
555:
556:# define obstack_ptr_grow_fast(h, aptr) \
557:  (((const void **) ((h)->next_free += sizeof (void *)))[-1] = (aptr), \
558:   (void) 0)
559:
560:# define obstack_int_grow_fast(h, aint) \
561:  (((int *) ((h)->next_free += sizeof (int)))[-1] = (aint), \
562:   (void) 0)
563:
564:# define obstack_blank(h, length) \
565:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
566:   ((obstack_room (h) < (h)->temp.tempint) \
567:   ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), (h)->temp.tempint), 0) : 0), \
568:   obstack_blank_fast (h, (h)->temp.tempint), \
569:   (void) 0)
570:
571:# define obstack_alloc(h, length) \
572:  (obstack_blank ((h), (length)), obstack_finish ((h)))
573:
574:# define obstack_copy(h, where, length) \
575:  (obstack_grow ((h), (where), (length)), obstack_finish ((h)))
576:
577:# define obstack_copy0(h, where, length) \
578:  (obstack_grow0 ((h), (where), (length)), obstack_finish ((h)))
579:
580:# define obstack_finish(h) \
581:  (((h)->next_free == (h)->object_base \
582:    ? (((h)->maybe_empty_object = 1), 0) \
583:    : 0), \
584:   (h)->temp.tempptr = (h)->object_base, \
585:   (h)->next_free \
586:     = __PTR_ALIGN ((h)->object_base, (h)->next_free, \
587:                    (h)->alignment_mask), \
588:   (h)->object_base = (h)->next_free, \
589:   (h)->temp.tempptr)
590:
591:# define obstack_free(h, obj) \
592:  ((h)->temp.tempptr = (void *) (obj), \
593:   (((_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->chunk < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->temp.tempptr \
594:     && (_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->temp.tempptr < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->chunk_limit) \
595:    ? (void) ((h)->next_free = (h)->object_base = (char *) (h)->temp.tempptr) \
596:    : __obstack_free (h, (h)->temp.tempptr)))
597:
598:#endif /* not __GNUC__-like */
599:
600:#ifdef __cplusplus
601:}       /* C++ */
602:#endif

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/os1_time.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/os1_time.c
3: * NexsOS1 time function implementations for Gnulib portability layer.
4: * These are the canonical implementations for localtime(), gmtime(), and mktime()
5: * backed directly by OS1 syscalls, and Gnulib's time module replacements are not used.
6: */
7:
8:#include <time.h>
9:#include <os1.h>
10:#include <string.h>
11:
12:time_t time(time_t *t) {
13:  time_t sec = (time_t)OS1_time_now();
14:  if (t) {
15:    *t = sec;
16:  }
17:  return sec;
18:}
19:
20:struct tm *localtime(const time_t *timep) {
21:  static struct tm result;
22:  if (!timep)
23:    return NULL;
24:
25:  time_t t = *timep;
26:  result.tm_sec = t % 60;
27:  t /= 60;
28:  result.tm_min = t % 60;
29:  t /= 60;
30:  result.tm_hour = t % 24;
31:  t /= 24;
32:
33:  /* Epoch started Jan 1 1970, which was Thursday (wday = 4) */
34:  result.tm_wday = (t + 4) % 7;
35:
36:  int year = 1970;
37:  while (1) {
38:    int days_in_year = 365;
39:    if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)) {
40:      days_in_year = 366;
41:    }
42:    if (t < days_in_year)
43:      break;
44:    t -= days_in_year;
45:    year++;
46:  }
47:  result.tm_year = year - 1900;
48:  result.tm_yday = t;
49:
50:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
51:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)) {
52:    month_days[1] = 29;
53:  }
54:
55:  int mon = 0;
56:  while (t >= month_days[mon]) {
57:    t -= month_days[mon];
58:    mon++;
59:  }
60:  result.tm_mon = mon;
61:  result.tm_mday = t + 1;
62:  result.tm_isdst = 0;
63:  return &result;
64:}
65:
66:struct tm *gmtime(const time_t *timep) {
67:  return localtime(timep);
68:}
69:
70:time_t mktime(struct tm *tm) {
71:  int year = tm->tm_year + 1900;
72:  int mon = tm->tm_mon;
73:  int mday = tm->tm_mday;
74:
75:  long days = 0;
76:  for (int y = 1970; y < year; y++) {
77:    days += ((y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || (y % 400 == 0)) ? 366 : 365;
78:  }
79:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
80:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)) {
81:    month_days[1] = 29;
82:  }
83:  for (int m = 0; m < mon; m++) {
84:    days += month_days[m];
85:  }
86:  days += mday - 1;
87:
88:  return days * 86400 + tm->tm_hour * 3600 + tm->tm_min * 60 + tm->tm_sec;
89:}
90:
91:static const char *const os1_weekday_names[] = {
92:  "Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"
93:};
94:
95:static const char *const os1_month_names[] = {
96:  "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
97:  "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"
98:};
99:
100:size_t strftime(char *s, size_t max, const char *format, const struct tm *tm) {
101:  if (!s || !format || !tm || max == 0) {
102:    return 0;
103:  }
104:
105:  size_t out = 0;
106:  const char *p = format;
107:
108:  while (*p && out + 1 < max) {
109:    if (*p != '%') {
110:      s[out++] = *p++;
111:      continue;
112:    }
113:
114:    p++;
115:    if (!*p) {
116:      break;
117:    }
118:
119:    char temp[64];
120:    int n = 0;
121:
122:    switch (*p) {
123:      case '%':
124:        s[out++] = '%';
125:        break;
126:      case 'a':
127:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_weekday_names[(tm->tm_wday + 7) % 7]);
128:        break;
129:      case 'A':
130:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_weekday_names[(tm->tm_wday + 7) % 7]);
131:        break;
132:      case 'b':
133:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_month_names[(tm->tm_mon + 12) % 12]);
134:        break;
135:      case 'B':
136:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_month_names[(tm->tm_mon + 12) % 12]);
137:        break;
138:      case 'd':
139:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_mday);
140:        break;
141:      case 'e':
142:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%2d", tm->tm_mday);
143:        break;
144:      case 'H':
145:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_hour);
146:        break;
147:      case 'I':
148:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", (tm->tm_hour % 12) ? (tm->tm_hour % 12) : 12);
149:        break;
150:      case 'j':
151:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%03d", tm->tm_yday + 1);
152:        break;
153:      case 'm':
154:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_mon + 1);
155:        break;
156:      case 'M':
157:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_min);
158:        break;
159:      case 'n':
160:        s[out++] = '\n';
161:        break;
162:      case 'p':
163:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", (tm->tm_hour >= 12) ? "PM" : "AM");
164:        break;
165:      case 'r':
166:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d:%02d:%02d %s",
167:                     (tm->tm_hour % 12) ? (tm->tm_hour % 12) : 12,
168:                     tm->tm_min, tm->tm_sec,
169:                     (tm->tm_hour >= 12) ? "PM" : "AM");
170:        break;
171:      case 'R':
172:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d:%02d",
173:                     tm->tm_hour, tm->tm_min);
174:        break;
175:      case 'S':
176:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_sec);
177:        break;
178:      case 'T':
179:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d:%02d:%02d",
180:                     tm->tm_hour, tm->tm_min, tm->tm_sec);
181:        break;
182:      case 'Y':
183:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%d", tm->tm_year + 1900);
184:        break;
185:      case 'y':
186:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", (tm->tm_year + 1900) % 100);
187:        break;
188:      case 'z':
189:      case 'Z':
190:        temp[0] = '\0';
191:        n = 0;
192:        break;
193:      case 't':
194:        s[out++] = '\t';
195:        break;
196:      default:
197:        s[out++] = *p;
198:        break;
199:    }
200:
201:    if (n > 0) {
202:      size_t copy = (size_t)n;
203:      if (copy >= max - out) {
204:        copy = max - out - 1;
205:      }
206:      memcpy(s + out, temp, copy);
207:      out += copy;
208:    }
209:
210:    p++;
211:    if (*p == '\0' && out + 1 < max) {
212:      break;
213:    }
214:  }
215:
216:  s[out] = '\0';
217:  return out;
218:}
219:
220:bool hard_locale(int category) {
221:  (void)category;
222:  return false;
223:}
224:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/parse-datetime.c @@@
1:/* NexsOS1 compatibility shim for GNU parse_datetime() support.
2:   This lives in the portability layer, not in the upstream gnulib source tree. */
3:
4:#include <config.h>
5:
6:#include <ctype.h>
7:#include <errno.h>
8:#include <stdlib.h>
9:#include <string.h>
10:#include <time.h>
11:
12:#include "parse-datetime.h"
13:#include "posixtm.h"
14:#include "timespec.h"
15:
16:static bool
17:parse_relative_timespec(struct timespec *result, const char *p,
18:                        struct timespec const *now)
19:{
20:  if (!result || !p)
21:    return false;
22:
23:  while (*p && isspace((unsigned char) *p))
24:    p++;
25:
26:  if (!*p)
27:    return false;
28:
29:  if (strcmp(p, "now") == 0 || strcmp(p, "today") == 0 || strcmp(p, "this") == 0)
30:    {
31:      *result = now ? *now : current_timespec();
32:      return true;
33:    }
34:
35:  char *end = NULL;
36:  errno = 0;
37:  long value = strtol(p, &end, 10);
38:  if (end == p || errno != 0)
39:    return false;
40:
41:  while (*end && isspace((unsigned char) *end))
42:    end++;
43:
44:  if (!*end)
45:    {
46:      if (now)
47:        {
48:          result->tv_sec = now->tv_sec + value;
49:          result->tv_nsec = now->tv_nsec;
50:          return true;
51:        }
52:      return false;
53:    }
54:
55:  long seconds = 0;
56:  if (strncmp(end, "second", 6) == 0 || strncmp(end, "seconds", 7) == 0 ||
57:      strncmp(end, "sec", 3) == 0 || strncmp(end, "s", 1) == 0)
58:    seconds = value;
59:  else if (strncmp(end, "minute", 6) == 0 || strncmp(end, "minutes", 7) == 0 ||
60:           strncmp(end, "min", 3) == 0 || strncmp(end, "m", 1) == 0)
61:    seconds = value * 60;
62:  else if (strncmp(end, "hour", 4) == 0 || strncmp(end, "hours", 5) == 0 ||
63:           strncmp(end, "hr", 2) == 0 || strncmp(end, "h", 1) == 0)
64:    seconds = value * 3600;
65:  else if (strncmp(end, "day", 3) == 0 || strncmp(end, "days", 4) == 0 ||
66:           strncmp(end, "d", 1) == 0)
67:    seconds = value * 86400;
68:  else if (strncmp(end, "week", 4) == 0 || strncmp(end, "weeks", 5) == 0 ||
69:           strncmp(end, "w", 1) == 0)
70:    seconds = value * 604800;
71:  else if (strncmp(end, "month", 5) == 0 || strncmp(end, "months", 6) == 0)
72:    seconds = value * 30 * 86400;
73:  else if (strncmp(end, "year", 4) == 0 || strncmp(end, "years", 5) == 0 ||
74:           strncmp(end, "y", 1) == 0)
75:    seconds = value * 365 * 86400;
76:  else
77:    return false;
78:
79:  if (now)
80:    {
81:      result->tv_sec = now->tv_sec + seconds;
82:      result->tv_nsec = now->tv_nsec;
83:      return true;
84:    }
85:
86:  return false;
87:}
88:
89:bool parse_datetime(struct timespec *restrict result,
90:                    char const *p,
91:                    struct timespec const *now)
92:{
93:  if (!result || !p)
94:    return false;
95:
96:  while (*p && isspace((unsigned char) *p))
97:    p++;
98:
99:  if (!*p)
100:    return false;
101:
102:  if (parse_relative_timespec(result, p, now))
103:    return true;
104:
105:  time_t secs = 0;
106:  if (posixtime(&secs, p, PDS_TRAILING_YEAR | PDS_CENTURY | PDS_SECONDS))
107:    {
108:      result->tv_sec = secs;
109:      result->tv_nsec = 0;
110:      return true;
111:    }
112:
113:  return false;
114:}
115:
116:bool parse_datetime2(struct timespec *restrict result,
117:                    char const *p,
118:                    struct timespec const *now,
119:                    unsigned int flags,
120:                    timezone_t tz,
121:                    char const *tzstring)
122:{
123:  (void)flags;
124:  (void)tz;
125:  (void)tzstring;
126:  return parse_datetime(result, p, now);
127:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/README.md @@@
1:# Gnulib Capability & Portability Overlay per NexsOS1
2:
3:Questo capability/portability layer consente la compilazione e l'integrazione di GNU Gnulib su **NexsOS1** senza modificare il submodule upstream `user/sys/lib/gnulib`.
4:
5:## Architettura e Layering
6:
7:1. **Configurazione forzata (`gnulib_config_nexsos.h`)**:
8:   - Fornita via `-include user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/gnulib_config_nexsos.h`.
9:   - Neutralizza le assunzioni host di autoconf/gnulib e dichiara la conformità al modello standard C99/C11 e POSIX di NexsOS1.
10:
11:2. **OS1 Real Glue Layer (`gnulib_os1_glue.c` / `gnulib_os1_glue.h`)**:
12:   - Collega le API di Gnulib al runtime `os1.h`, alle reali syscall di NexsOS1 (`_sys_*`), al VFS (ext4, procfs, regfs) e al capability/process engine (`OS1low_process_*`).
13:   - Nessun mock o fake stub: tutte le operazioni sono connesse direttamente ai descrittori e servizi del sistema operativo.
14:
15:3. **Integrazione Build (`overlay.mk`)**:
16:   - Compila la suite di moduli fondamentali Gnulib in un archivio statico `libgnulib.a`.
17:   - Linkato con `user/sys/lib/lib.c`, `user/sys/lib/malloc.c`, `user/sys/lib/math.c` e `syscall.o`.
18:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/lua/lua_portability.c @@@
1:#include "lua_portability.h"
2:#include <os1.h>
3:#include <stdio.h>
4:#include <stdlib.h>
5:#include <string.h>
6:
7:#include <locale.h>
8:
9:/* Time implementation lives in the canonical NexsOS1 libc layer.
10: * Lua must use that single ABI surface instead of redefining time(). */
11:
12:char *tmpnam(char *s) {
13:  static char static_buf[128];
14:  static int temp_counter = 0;
15:  char *buf = s ? s : static_buf;
16:  /* /home is the ONLY user-writable tree (kernel/fs/vfs.c vfs_write_allowed);
17:   * the old "/tmpfile_%d" sat at the non-writable root, so os.tmpname()'s path
18:   * could never be created even once file creation via SYS_FILE_WRITE landed.
19:   * (fopen("w") still needs open(2) to honour O_CREAT for these to fully work
20:   * — tracked separately; this at least puts the name in the right tree.) */
21:  sprintf(buf, "/home/.luatmp_%d", temp_counter++);
22:  return buf;
23:}
24:
25:clock_t clock(void) { return (clock_t)os1_cpu_ns(); }
26:
27:double difftime(time_t time1, time_t time0) { return (double)(time1 - time0); }
28:
29:/* strcoll is provided by the central NexsOS libc compatibility layer so that
30: * both Coreutils and Lua share the same ABI surface without duplicate symbol
31: * definitions at link time. */
32:
33:/*
34: * os1_lua_readline - REPL line reader for nxlua (lua_portability.h's
35: * lua_readline override; see that header for why fgets(stdin) is replaced).
36: *
37: * NOTE(LUA-TTY-01): fgets()/OS1 console read() hand back keyboard.c's BASE
38: * ascii_map byte (data1's low byte), not the character after the active
39: * keyboard layout's overrides (payload) - the same .key vs .utf8 split
40: * input_event_t already exposes for windowed apps. nxlua has no window, so
41: * it decodes its own mailbox here instead. Echo is NOT done here: nxexec.h's
42: * host-side relay (USR-TTY-01 #123) already echoes every byte it forwards,
43: * in the same style as nxshell.c's read(0,...) loop; echoing again here
44: * would double every character on screen.
45: *
46: * Returns 1 with buf NUL-terminated and ending in '\n' (matches fgets(),
47: * which pushline() in lua.c strips itself), or 0 on Ctrl-C (EOF-like).
48: */
49:int os1_lua_readline(char *buf, int bufsize) {
50:  /*
51:   * NOTE(LUA-TTY-03): the keyboard-mailbox path below is ONLY correct for a
52:   * real console.  `-i` FORCES interactive mode regardless of
53:   * lua_stdin_is_tty(), so `lua -i < script` and `echo ... | lua -i` reach the
54:   * REPL with stdin redirected to a FILE or a PIPE — there the line must come
55:   * from fd 0, not from the keyboard (otherwise the REPL ignores the supplied
56:   * program and blocks on a keypress that never comes).  isatty() is the same
57:   * capability-type test the tty check uses, so the two agree by construction.
58:   */
59:  if (!isatty(0))
60:    return fgets(buf, bufsize, stdin) ? 1 : 0; /* NULL => EOF, like Ctrl-C */
61:
62:  int len = 0;
63:  while (1) {
64:    struct ipc_message m;
65:    if (try_recv(-1, &m) != 0 || m.type != IPC_TYPE_INPUT || m.data2 == 0) {
66:      OS1_sleep(15);
67:      continue;
68:    }
69:    char c = m.payload[0];
70:    if (c == 0x03) /* Ctrl-C: EOF-like */
71:      return 0;
72:    if (c == '\r' || c == '\n') {
73:      if (len + 1 >= bufsize)
74:        len = bufsize - 2;
75:      buf[len++] = '\n';
76:      buf[len] = '\0';
77:      return 1;
78:    }
79:    if (c == '\b' || c == 127) {
80:      if (len > 0)
81:        len--;
82:      continue;
83:    }
84:    if (c != 0 && len + 1 < bufsize) {
85:      buf[len++] = c;
86:      buf[len] = '\0';
87:    }
88:  }
89:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/lua/lua_portability.h @@@
1:#ifndef LUA_PORTABILITY_H
2:#define LUA_PORTABILITY_H
3:
4:/* l_noret: attribute for functions that never return.
5: * Lua's ldo.c luaD_throw is marked l_noret but GCC may not see all
6: * paths as noreturn (longjmp path). Force the attribute. */
7:#if defined(__GNUC__)
8:#define l_noret __attribute__((noreturn)) void
9:#else
10:#define l_noret void
11:#endif
12:
13:#include <setjmp.h>
14:#include <stddef.h>
15:/* time_t/struct timespec/clock_gettime already exist as the system header
16: * (include/api/time.h) - reuse it instead of a second, parallel typedef of
17: * time_t here (the exact "we have a system header the lua compat layer
18: * isn't using" mismatch: two independent `typedef long time_t;` in scope
19: * are harmless today only because they happen to agree byte-for-byte; drift
20: * between the two would silently desync the ABI Lua's time functions and
21: * every other syscall wrapper agree on). Only struct tm/localtime/gmtime/
22: * strftime/mktime below are genuinely new - time.h does not declare them. */
23:#include <math.h>
24:#include <time.h>
25:
26:/* Provide sig_atomic_t before Lua's <signal.h> include path resolves.
27: * NexsOS1's <signal.h> does not declare it, but Lua's lstate.h uses it
28: * via the l_signalT macro. Force-include this header before Lua's
29: * sources so the type is always in scope. */
30:#ifndef _SIG_ATOMIC_T_DEFINED
31:#define _SIG_ATOMIC_T_DEFINED
32:typedef int sig_atomic_t;
33:#endif
34:
35:/* Pre-define Lua's l_signalT so lstate.h's #if !defined(l_signalT)
36: * check resolves to our definition (matches the l_signalT = sig_atomic_t
37: * line in lstate.h, but takes priority). */
38:#if !defined(l_signalT) && !defined(LUA_PORT_SIGNALT_DEFINED)
39:#define LUA_PORT_SIGNALT_DEFINED
40:#define l_signalT sig_atomic_t
41:#endif
42:
43:/* NexsOS1's <math.h> now provides a full math library.
44: * The math symbols used by the Lua core and lmathlib are now in <math.h>.
45: * Only strtod and non-math symbols remain here. */
46:
47:/* HUGE_VAL/HUGE_VALF are now provided by <math.h> */
48:
49:/*
50: * Lua module search path — the SINGLE authoritative definition.
51: *
52: * luaconf.h ships /usr/local paths; because this header is force-included
53: * (-include) ahead of lua.h, our LUA_ROOT/LDIR/CDIR and
54: * LUA_PATH_DEFAULT win over luaconf.h's #ifndef guards.  The Makefile no
55: * longer passes any -DLUA_* path macro (a "...;..." -D can't survive the
56: * shell — the ';' break the compile line), so keep the paths here only.
57: *
58: * Root is /lib, NOT /home: the VFS write-ACL (kernel/fs/vfs.c
59: * vfs_write_allowed) makes /home the only user-writable tree, while /lib is
60: * read-for-all / root-write-only.  System Lua modules therefore live in /lib
61: * (any process can require them; users cannot tamper with them); /home would
62: * expose them to overwrite.  sys/lib is the build-time source tree, not a
63: * runtime VFS path.  Trailing '/' matters: luaconf.h concatenates directly.
64: */
65:#define LUA_ROOT "/lib/"
66:#define LUA_LDIR LUA_ROOT "lua/5.4/lib/"
67:#define LUA_CDIR LUA_ROOT "lua/5.4/lib/"
68:
69:/* Search the system module tree, then the current directory.  Defined
70: * explicitly (rather than left to luaconf.h) to avoid the LDIR==CDIR
71: * duplicate pair its generator would emit. */
72:#define LUA_PATH_DEFAULT                                                       \
73:  LUA_LDIR "?.lua;" LUA_LDIR "?/init.lua;"                                     \
74:           "./?.lua;./?/init.lua"
75:#define LUA_CPATH_DEFAULT LUA_CDIR "?.so;" LUA_CDIR "loadall.so;./?.so"
76:
77:/* Locale: override luaconf.h's localeconv-based macro before luaconf.h
78: * includes it.  NexsOS1 has no locale support; the decimal point is always '.'.
79: */
80:#define lua_getlocaledecpoint() ('.')
81:
82:/* time_t/struct tm/clock_gettime/nanosleep/time/mktime/difftime/localtime/
83: * gmtime/strftime are declared in <time.h> (system header).
84: * clock_t/tmpnam/clock are implemented below. */
85:typedef long clock_t;
86:#ifndef CLOCKS_PER_SEC
87:#define CLOCKS_PER_SEC 1000000000L
88:#endif
89:#ifndef L_tmpnam
90:#define L_tmpnam 128
91:#endif
92:
93:char *tmpnam(char *s);
94:clock_t clock(void);
95:
96:/* Double conversions */
97:int strcoll(const char *s1, const char *s2);
98:
99:#include <locale.h>
100:
101:/* Declaration of os1 library open function */
102:struct lua_State;
103:int luaopen_os1(struct lua_State *L);
104:
105:/*
106: * NOTE(LUA-TTY-02): lua.c chooses "interactive REPL" vs "EXECUTE stdin" with
107: * lua_stdin_is_tty(), whose ISO-C fallback (lua.c) hardcodes it to 1 —
108: * literally commented there as "assume stdin is a tty" —
109: * unless LUA_USE_POSIX is defined.  We deliberately do NOT define
110: * LUA_USE_POSIX (it also drags in popen/dlopen assumptions we do not provide),
111: * so lua ASSUMED a tty unconditionally: `echo "print(10)" | lua` and
112: * `lua < script` entered the REPL instead of executing stdin — and the REPL
113: * reads the KEYBOARD mailbox (LUA-TTY-01 below), not fd 0, so the piped program
114: * was never consumed (it printed the banner + '>' and waited for a keypress).
115: *
116: * Wire it to our REAL isatty() (lib.c): a genuine capability-type test of the
117: * descriptor's object — CONSOLE vs FILE vs PIPE — so a redirected or piped
118: * stdin correctly EXECUTES, while an interactive console still gets the REPL
119: * plus the keyboard reader below.  This is the lua-side half of the fix; the
120: * libc side was implementing isatty(), which unistd.h had only DECLARED.
121: */
122:#include <unistd.h>
123:#define lua_stdin_is_tty() isatty(0)
124:
125:/*
126: * NOTE(LUA-TTY-01): REPL line input overrides lua.c's lua_readline/
127: * _initreadline/_saveline/_freeline fallback (fgets(stdin) - see lua.c's own
128: * '#if !defined(lua_readline)' guard; force-including this header ahead of
129: * lua.c makes our definitions win, no lua.c edits needed). fgets()/read(fd
130: * 0,...) hands back keyboard.c's BASE ascii_map byte, not the character
131: * after the active keyboard layout's overrides (the .key vs .utf8 split
132: * input_event_t already exposes for windowed apps); nxlua has no window, so
133: * it decodes its own mailbox instead (lua_portability.c). Echo stays with
134: * nxexec.h's host-side relay (USR-TTY-01 #123) - os1_lua_readline only
135: * accumulates the line.
136: */
137:#define LUA_PORT_MAXINPUT 512
138:int os1_lua_readline(char *buf, int bufsize);
139:
140:#define lua_initreadline(L) ((void)L)
141:#define lua_readline(L, b, p)                                                  \
142:  ((void)L, print(p), os1_lua_readline((b), LUA_PORT_MAXINPUT))
143:#define lua_saveline(L, line)                                                  \
144:  {                                                                            \
145:    (void)L;                                                                   \
146:    (void)line;                                                                \
147:  }
148:#define lua_freeline(L, b)                                                     \

150:    (void)L;                                                                   \
151:    (void)b;                                                                   \
152:  }

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/opengl/os1_gl_platform.c @@@
1:/* OS1 software implementation of the OpenGL presentation seam. */
2:#include "os1_gl_platform.h"
3:
4:#include <errno.h>
5:#include <stdlib.h>
6:#include <string.h>
7:
8:#include "../os1_video_platform.h"
9:
10:struct os1_gl_surface {
11:  uint32_t backend;
12:  int window;
13:  int width;
14:  int height;
15:  uint32_t *color_buffer;
16:};
17:
18:int os1_gl_surface_create(const struct os1_gl_surface_params *params,
19:                          struct os1_gl_surface **out) {
20:  if (!params || !out || params->width <= 0 || params->height <= 0 ||
21:      !params->title)
22:    return -EINVAL;
23:
24:  struct os1_video_info info;
25:  if (os1_video_query(&info) != 0)
26:    return -ENOSYS;
27:  if (info.backend != OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE ||
28:      !(info.capabilities & OS1_VIDEO_CAP_ARGB8888))
29:    return -ENOSYS; /* GPU-context backend reserved for the ASTRA object */
30:
31:  struct os1_gl_surface *surface =
32:      (struct os1_gl_surface *)malloc(sizeof(*surface));
33:  if (!surface)
34:    return -ENOMEM;
35:  memset(surface, 0, sizeof(*surface));
36:  surface->backend = info.backend;
37:  surface->window = -1;
38:
39:  size_t count = (size_t)params->width * (size_t)params->height;
40:  surface->color_buffer = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
41:  if (!surface->color_buffer) {
42:    free(surface);
43:    return -ENOMEM;
44:  }
45:  memset(surface->color_buffer, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
46:
47:  surface->window = os1_video_window_create(params->x, params->y,
48:                                            params->width, params->height,
49:                                            params->title);
50:  if (surface->window < 0) {
51:    int rc = surface->window;
52:    free(surface->color_buffer);
53:    free(surface);
54:    return rc;
55:  }
56:  surface->width = params->width;
57:  surface->height = params->height;
58:  *out = surface;
59:  return 0;
60:}
61:
62:void os1_gl_surface_destroy(struct os1_gl_surface *surface) {
63:  if (!surface)
64:    return;
65:  if (surface->window >= 0)
66:    os1_video_window_destroy(surface->window);
67:  free(surface->color_buffer);
68:  free(surface);
69:}
70:
71:uint32_t *os1_gl_surface_buffer(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int *width,
72:                                int *height, size_t *pitch_bytes) {
73:  if (!surface)
74:    return NULL;
75:  if (width)
76:    *width = surface->width;
77:  if (height)
78:    *height = surface->height;
79:  if (pitch_bytes)
80:    *pitch_bytes = (size_t)surface->width * sizeof(uint32_t);
81:  return surface->color_buffer;
82:}
83:
84:int os1_gl_surface_swap(struct os1_gl_surface *surface) {
85:  if (!surface)
86:    return -EINVAL;
87:  int rc = os1_video_present_argb8888(
88:      surface->window, 0, 0, surface->width, surface->height,
89:      surface->color_buffer, (size_t)surface->width * surface->height);
90:  if (rc < 0)
91:    return rc;
92:  os1_video_render();
93:  return 0;
94:}
95:
96:int os1_gl_surface_resize(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int width,
97:                          int height) {
98:  if (!surface || width <= 0 || height <= 0)
99:    return -EINVAL;
100:
101:  size_t count = (size_t)width * (size_t)height;
102:  uint32_t *fresh = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
103:  if (!fresh)
104:    return -ENOMEM;
105:  memset(fresh, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
106:
107:  int rc = os1_video_window_resize(surface->window, width, height);
108:  if (rc < 0) {
109:    free(fresh);
110:    return rc;
111:  }
112:  free(surface->color_buffer);
113:  surface->color_buffer = fresh;
114:  surface->width = width;
115:  surface->height = height;
116:  return 0;
117:}
118:
119:int os1_gl_surface_backend(const struct os1_gl_surface *surface) {
120:  if (!surface)
121:    return -EINVAL;
122:  return (int)surface->backend;
123:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/opengl/os1_gl_platform.h @@@
1:/*
2: * OS1 OpenGL presentation seam.
3: *
4: * The surface an OSMesa-style software GL renders into: a CPU ARGB8888
5: * top-down colour buffer bound to an OS1 window, swapped through the
6: * os1_video_platform portability header.  The GL personality (Mesa's OSMesa
7: * frontend on the nexsos-port-opengl branch, pinned at the last release
8: * that ships it) binds this buffer with OSMesaMakeCurrent + OSMESA_Y_UP=0;
9: * nothing here depends on Mesa headers, so the seam builds and ships ahead
10: * of the library.  The backend field mirrors os1_video_backend: the CPU
11: * buffer is the intentional swap-in point for the future ASTRA GPU-context
12: * object, exactly like the D3D9 presentation chain.
13: */
14:#ifndef OS1_GL_PLATFORM_H
15:#define OS1_GL_PLATFORM_H
16:
17:#include <stddef.h>
18:#include <stdint.h>
19:
20:struct os1_gl_surface_params {
21:  int x;
22:  int y;
23:  int width;
24:  int height;
25:  const char *title;
26:};
27:
28:struct os1_gl_surface; /* opaque: OS1 window + CPU colour buffer */
29:
30:/* Create/destroy a presentable GL surface on the platform's active backend.
31: * Returns 0, -ENOSYS when only an unsupported backend is advertised, or a
32: * negative OS1 error. */
33:int os1_gl_surface_create(const struct os1_gl_surface_params *params,
34:                          struct os1_gl_surface **out);
35:void os1_gl_surface_destroy(struct os1_gl_surface *surface);
36:
37:/* The colour buffer a software GL binds (ARGB8888, top-down rows, tight
38: * pitch).  Geometry is reported through the out parameters; the pointer
39: * stays valid until destroy or resize. */
40:uint32_t *os1_gl_surface_buffer(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int *width,
41:                                int *height, size_t *pitch_bytes);
42:
43:/* SwapBuffers analogue: present the whole colour buffer and notify the
44: * compositor. */
45:int os1_gl_surface_swap(struct os1_gl_surface *surface);
46:
47:/* Adopt a new size (nxlauncher resize contract): kernel logical resize +
48: * buffer reallocation.  The previously returned buffer pointer is invalid
49: * after a successful resize; re-fetch it with os1_gl_surface_buffer. */
50:int os1_gl_surface_resize(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int width,
51:                          int height);
52:
53:/* The enum os1_video_backend this surface presents on. */
54:int os1_gl_surface_backend(const struct os1_gl_surface *surface);
55:
56:#endif /* OS1_GL_PLATFORM_H */

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/sdl2/README.md @@@
1:# SDL2 NexsOS overlay
2:
3:This overlay supplies the SDL2 `nexsos` video driver without editing the SDL
4:submodule. Its build manifest is `overlay.mk`; the eventual SDL cross-build
5:must compile those three sources with `SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS` and link them
6:with `lib.c`/`os1_video_platform.c`.
7:
8:Implemented scope: software ARGB8888 windows, pitch-safe partial framebuffer
9:presentation, focused keyboard/mouse/resize event pumping and resize requests.
10:OpenGL contexts, relative pointer mode, clipboard, title mutation and hardware
11:acceleration are deliberately not advertised yet.

1:/*

5: * source line; defining SDL_config_h_ here makes the submodule's own
6: * include/SDL_config.h a no-op, so the SDL tree needs no NexsOS platform
7: * branch.  Together with the DUMMY_bootstrap rename below, the SDL submodule
8: * builds completely unpatched — per the programme's non-negotiable
9: * constraint AND upstream SDL's policy that no generated code enters its
10: * tree (see the submodule's CLAUDE.md).
11: */

13:#define SDL_config_nexsos_h_
14:#define SDL_config_h_ /* neutralise include/SDL_config.h in the SDL tree */

18:#define HAVE_STDDEF_H 1
19:#define HAVE_STDINT_H 1
20:
21:/* OS1 userland allocator: malloc/calloc/realloc/free from <stdlib.h>
22: * (include/api), so SDL does not drag in its internal dlmalloc (which would
23: * need sbrk/mmap). */
