25:#define HAVE_MALLOC 1
26:#define SDL_NEXSOS 1
27:
28:#ifdef __GNUC__
29:#define HAVE_GCC_SYNC_LOCK_TEST_AND_SET 1
30:#endif
31:
32:/* Static freestanding archive: OS1 has no dlopen, which turns the dynamic-API
33: * trampoline off through SDL_dynapi.h's own DYNAPI_NEEDS_DLOPEN &&
34: * !HAVE_DLOPEN branch (SDL_DYNAMIC_API must not be forced directly). */
35:#define DYNAPI_NEEDS_DLOPEN 1

38: * be patched.  Enabling the DUMMY slot and renaming its symbol routes that

21:    /* 16 */ SDL_SCANCODE_Q, SDL_SCANCODE_W, SDL_SCANCODE_E, SDL_SCANCODE_R,
22:    /* 20 */ SDL_SCANCODE_T, SDL_SCANCODE_Y, SDL_SCANCODE_U, SDL_SCANCODE_I,
23:    /* 24 */ SDL_SCANCODE_O, SDL_SCANCODE_P, SDL_SCANCODE_LEFTBRACKET,
24:    /* 27 */ SDL_SCANCODE_RIGHTBRACKET, SDL_SCANCODE_RETURN,
25:    /* 29 */ SDL_SCANCODE_LCTRL,
26:    /* 30 */ SDL_SCANCODE_A, SDL_SCANCODE_S, SDL_SCANCODE_D, SDL_SCANCODE_F,
27:    /* 34 */ SDL_SCANCODE_G, SDL_SCANCODE_H, SDL_SCANCODE_J, SDL_SCANCODE_K,
28:    /* 38 */ SDL_SCANCODE_L, SDL_SCANCODE_SEMICOLON, SDL_SCANCODE_APOSTROPHE,
29:    /* 41 */ SDL_SCANCODE_GRAVE, SDL_SCANCODE_LSHIFT, SDL_SCANCODE_BACKSLASH,
30:    /* 44 */ SDL_SCANCODE_Z, SDL_SCANCODE_X, SDL_SCANCODE_C, SDL_SCANCODE_V,
31:    /* 48 */ SDL_SCANCODE_B, SDL_SCANCODE_N, SDL_SCANCODE_M,

33:    /* 54 */ SDL_SCANCODE_RSHIFT, SDL_SCANCODE_KP_MULTIPLY,

41:static SDL_Scancode nexsos_scancode(uint32_t code) {
42:  if (code < SDL_arraysize(nexsos_scancode_table))
43:    return nexsos_scancode_table[code];
44:  switch (code) {
45:  case 87: return SDL_SCANCODE_F11;
46:  case 88: return SDL_SCANCODE_F12;
47:  case 97: return SDL_SCANCODE_RCTRL;
48:  case 100: return SDL_SCANCODE_RALT;
49:  case 102: return SDL_SCANCODE_HOME;
50:  case 103: return SDL_SCANCODE_UP;
51:  case 104: return SDL_SCANCODE_PAGEUP;
52:  case 105: return SDL_SCANCODE_LEFT;
53:  case 106: return SDL_SCANCODE_RIGHT;
54:  case 107: return SDL_SCANCODE_END;
55:  case 108: return SDL_SCANCODE_DOWN;
56:  case 109: return SDL_SCANCODE_PAGEDOWN;
57:  case 110: return SDL_SCANCODE_INSERT;
58:  case 111: return SDL_SCANCODE_DELETE;
59:  default: return SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN;
60:  }
61:}

63:static Uint8 nexsos_mouse_button(int button) {
64:  if (button == 0x110) return SDL_BUTTON_LEFT;
65:  if (button == 0x111) return SDL_BUTTON_RIGHT;
66:  if (button == 0x112) return SDL_BUTTON_MIDDLE;
67:  return 0;
68:}

70:void NEXSOS_PumpEvents(_THIS) {
71:  NEXSOS_VideoData *data = (NEXSOS_VideoData *)_this->driverdata;
72:  struct os1_video_event event;
73:  while (os1_video_poll_event(&event) > 0) {
74:    SDL_Window *window = data->focused_window;
75:    if (!window)
76:      continue;
77:    if (event.type == OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_KEY) {
78:      SDL_Scancode code = nexsos_scancode(event.data.key.scancode);
79:      SDL_SendKeyboardKey(event.data.key.state ? SDL_PRESSED : SDL_RELEASED,
80:                          code);
81:      if (event.data.key.state && event.data.key.utf8[0]) {
82:        char text[9];
83:        SDL_memcpy(text, event.data.key.utf8, 8);
84:        text[8] = '\0';
85:        SDL_SendKeyboardText(text);
86:      }
87:    } else if (event.type == OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON) {
88:      Uint8 button = nexsos_mouse_button(event.data.mouse.button);
89:      SDL_SendMouseMotion(window, 0, 0, event.data.mouse.x, event.data.mouse.y);
90:      if (button)
91:        SDL_SendMouseButton(window, 0,
92:                            event.data.mouse.state ? SDL_PRESSED : SDL_RELEASED,
93:                            button);
94:    } else if (event.type == OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_RESIZE) {
95:      SDL_SendWindowEvent(window, SDL_WINDOWEVENT_RESIZED,
96:                          event.data.resize.width, event.data.resize.height);
97:    }
98:  }
99:}
100:
101:#endif /* SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS */

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/sdl2/SDL_nexsosframebuffer.c @@@
1:/* SDL2 software framebuffer presentation over the NexsOS portability ABI. */
2:#include "../../sdl/src/SDL_internal.h"
3:
4:#ifdef SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS
5:
6:#include "SDL_nexsosvideo.h"
7:#include "../os1_video_platform.h"
8:
9:int NEXSOS_CreateWindowFramebuffer(_THIS, SDL_Window *window, Uint32 *format,
10:                                   void **pixels, int *pitch) {
11:  (void)_this;
12:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = (NEXSOS_WindowData *)window->driverdata;
13:  NEXSOS_DestroyWindowFramebuffer(_this, window);
14:  /* Adopt the (possibly compositor-driven) size as the OS1 LOGICAL surface
15:   * before allocating the matching SDL framebuffer — the nxlauncher resize
16:   * pattern (GFX-DYN-01): the kernel no-ops when the size is unchanged, so
17:   * the first acquisition and grip-resize echoes cannot loop. */
18:  (void)os1_video_window_resize(data->os1_window, window->w, window->h);
19:  data->framebuffer = SDL_CreateRGBSurfaceWithFormat(
20:      0, window->w, window->h, 32, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
21:  if (!data->framebuffer)
22:    return -1;
23:  *format = SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888;
24:  *pixels = data->framebuffer->pixels;
25:  *pitch = data->framebuffer->pitch;
26:  return 0;
27:}
28:
29:int NEXSOS_UpdateWindowFramebuffer(_THIS, SDL_Window *window,
30:                                   const SDL_Rect *rects, int numrects) {
31:  (void)_this;
32:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = (NEXSOS_WindowData *)window->driverdata;
33:  if (!data || !data->framebuffer)
34:    return SDL_SetError("NexsOS framebuffer unavailable");
35:
36:  SDL_Surface *surface = data->framebuffer;
37:  int first = (numrects > 0) ? 0 : -1;
38:  int last = (numrects > 0) ? numrects : 1;
39:  SDL_Rect full = {0, 0, surface->w, surface->h};
40:  for (int i = first; i < last; i++) {
41:    SDL_Rect area = (i < 0) ? full : rects[i];
42:    if (!SDL_IntersectRect(&area, &full, &area))
43:      continue;
44:    const uint32_t *pixels = (const uint32_t *)surface->pixels +
45:                             (size_t)area.y * (surface->pitch / 4) + area.x;
46:    size_t stride = (size_t)(surface->pitch / 4);
47:    size_t source_count = (size_t)surface->h * stride;
48:    if (os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(data->os1_window, area.x, area.y,
49:                                           area.w, area.h, pixels, stride,
50:                                           source_count - (size_t)area.y * stride - area.x) < 0)
51:      return SDL_SetError("NexsOS framebuffer presentation failed");
52:  }
53:  os1_video_render();
54:  return 0;
55:}
56:
57:void NEXSOS_DestroyWindowFramebuffer(_THIS, SDL_Window *window) {
58:  (void)_this;
59:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = (NEXSOS_WindowData *)window->driverdata;
60:  if (data) {
61:    SDL_FreeSurface(data->framebuffer);
62:    data->framebuffer = NULL;
63:  }
64:}
65:
66:#endif /* SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS */

18:void SDL_TicksInit(void)
19:{
20:    if (ticks_started) {

22:    }

29:    ticks_started = SDL_FALSE;

33:{

35:        SDL_TicksInit();

37:    return (Uint64)(os1_mono_ns() - start_ns) / 1000000ull;
38:}

42:    return (Uint64)os1_mono_ns();

47:    return 1000000000ull; /* os1_mono_ns counts nanoseconds */
48:}

76:int NEXSOS_CreateWindow(_THIS, SDL_Window *window) {
77:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = SDL_calloc(1, sizeof(*data));
78:  if (!data)
79:    return SDL_OutOfMemory();

82:   * so window->title is still NULL here; OS1 requires a title at creation.
83:   * Positions may still carry the UNDEFINED/CENTERED magic values. */
84:  const char *title = window->title ? window->title : "SDL2";
85:  int x = window->x;

90:    y = 60;

93:      os1_video_window_create(x, y, window->w, window->h, title);
94:  if (data->os1_window < 0) {
95:    SDL_free(data);
96:    return SDL_SetError("NexsOS window creation failed");
97:  }
98:  window->driverdata = data;
99:  window->flags &= ~SDL_WINDOW_HIDDEN;
100:  window->flags |= SDL_WINDOW_SHOWN | SDL_WINDOW_INPUT_FOCUS;
101:  ((NEXSOS_VideoData *)_this->driverdata)->focused_window = window;
102:  SDL_SetMouseFocus(window);
103:  SDL_SetKeyboardFocus(window);
104:  return 0;
105:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/os1_video_platform.c @@@
1:/* OS1 software-video implementation of the portability adapter. */
2:#include "os1_video_platform.h"
3:
4:#include <errno.h>
5:#include <input.h>
6:#include <os1.h>
7:#include <stdlib.h>
8:#include <string.h>
9:
10:#define OS1_VIDEO_ABI_VERSION 1u
11:
12:int os1_video_query(struct os1_video_info *out) {
13:  if (!out)
14:    return -EINVAL;
15:
16:  long packed = _sys_display_info();
17:  if (packed < 0)
18:    return (int)packed;
19:
20:  out->abi_version = OS1_VIDEO_ABI_VERSION;
21:  out->backend = OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE;
22:  out->capabilities = OS1_VIDEO_CAP_ARGB8888 | OS1_VIDEO_CAP_WINDOW_RESIZE |
23:                      OS1_VIDEO_CAP_DAMAGE_PRESENT |
24:                      OS1_VIDEO_CAP_SOFTWARE_3D;
25:  out->width = (int)((packed >> 16) & 0xffff);
26:  out->height = (int)(packed & 0xffff);
27:  return 0;
28:}
29:
30:int os1_video_window_create(int x, int y, int width, int height,
31:                            const char *title) {
32:  if (width <= 0 || height <= 0 || !title)
33:    return -EINVAL;
34:  return _sys_create_window(x, y, width, height, title);
35:}
36:
37:void os1_video_window_destroy(int window) { _sys_destroy_window(window); }
38:
39:int os1_video_window_resize(int window, int width, int height) {
40:  if (width <= 0 || height <= 0)
41:    return -EINVAL;
42:  return _sys_window_resize(window, width, height);
43:}
44:
45:int os1_video_present_argb8888(int window, int x, int y, int width,
46:                               int height, const uint32_t *pixels,
47:                               size_t pixel_count) {
48:  return os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(window, x, y, width, height,
49:                                            pixels, (size_t)width,
50:                                            pixel_count);
51:}
52:
53:int os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(int window, int x, int y, int width,
54:                                       int height, const uint32_t *pixels,
55:                                       size_t source_stride,
56:                                       size_t source_pixel_count) {
57:  if (window < 0 || width <= 0 || height <= 0 || !pixels)
58:    return -EINVAL;
59:
60:  size_t row_width = (size_t)width;
61:  size_t rows = (size_t)height;
62:  if (source_stride < row_width)
63:    return -EINVAL;
64:
65:  size_t packed_count = row_width * rows;
66:  if (packed_count / row_width != rows)
67:    return -EINVAL;
68:  size_t source_count = (rows - 1) * source_stride + row_width;
69:  if ((rows - 1) != 0 && (source_count - row_width) / (rows - 1) != source_stride)
70:    return -EINVAL;
71:  if (source_pixel_count < source_count)
72:    return -EINVAL;
73:
74:  if (source_stride == row_width) {
75:    _sys_window_blit(window, x, y, width, height, pixels);
76:    return 0;
77:  }
78:
79:  if (packed_count > ((size_t)-1) / sizeof(uint32_t))
80:    return -EINVAL;
81:  uint32_t *packed = (uint32_t *)malloc(packed_count * sizeof(uint32_t));
82:  if (!packed)
83:    return -ENOMEM;
84:  for (size_t row = 0; row < rows; row++)
85:    memcpy(packed + row * row_width, pixels + row * source_stride,
86:           row_width * sizeof(uint32_t));
87:
88:  _sys_window_blit(window, x, y, width, height, packed);
89:  free(packed);
90:  return 0;
91:}
92:
93:int os1_video_poll_event(struct os1_video_event *out) {
94:  if (!out)
95:    return -EINVAL;
96:
97:  input_event_t input;
98:  int result = input_poll_event(&input);
99:  if (result <= 0)
100:    return result;
101:
102:  if (input.type == INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD) {
103:    out->type = OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_KEY;
104:    out->data.key.scancode = input.keyboard.scancode;
105:    out->data.key.key = input.keyboard.key;
106:    out->data.key.state = (uint8_t)input.keyboard.state;
107:    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)
108:      out->data.key.utf8[i] = input.keyboard.utf8[i];
109:    return 1;
110:  }
111:  if (input.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE) {
112:    out->type = OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON;
113:    out->data.mouse.button = input.mouse.button;
114:    out->data.mouse.state = input.mouse.state;
115:    out->data.mouse.x = input.mouse.x;
116:    out->data.mouse.y = input.mouse.y;
117:    return 1;
118:  }
119:  if (input.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE) {
120:    out->type = OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_RESIZE;
121:    out->data.resize.width = input.resize.w;
122:    out->data.resize.height = input.resize.h;
123:    return 1;
124:  }
125:  return 0;
126:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/execsvc_client.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/execsvc_client.c
3: * Client stub for the execution service (Phase 9c).
4: *
5: * Deliberately its OWN translation unit rather than more code inside lib.c:
6: * Phase 10a/12 will split service clients out of the libc entirely, and lib.c is
7: * already the file whose entanglement those phases exist to undo.  Starting it
8: * separate means that split is a Makefile move, not another extraction.
9: *
10: * WHAT THIS IS FOR: nxexec is meant to be THE standard executor and the POSIX
11: * compatibility point for execution.  system() historically bypassed it
12: * completely (it spawned the shell itself), so the POSIX surface had its own
13: * private execution path — exactly the divergence the daemon exists to remove.
14: *
15: * WHAT IT IS NOT FOR: interactive foreground jobs.  The service becomes the
16: * spawning parent, and while OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER restores AUTHORITY it does NOT
17: * move the controlling terminal, so Ctrl-Z/Ctrl-C would break.  That is Phase 9d
18: * (ctty handback), and until then interactive jobs keep the in-process path.
19: */
20:#include <execsvc.h>
21:#include <os1.h>
22:#include <string.h>
23:#include <unistd.h>
24:
25:/* write_full - a pipe write may be short; a partial request would be read as a
26: * malformed one by the service, so finish it or fail. */
27:static int write_full(int fd, const char *buf, int len) {
28:  int done = 0;
29:  while (done < len) {
30:    long w = write(fd, buf + done, (unsigned long)(len - done));
31:    if (w <= 0)
32:      return done;
33:    done += (int)w;
34:  }
35:  return done;
36:}
37:
38:/* read_full - same reasoning on the reply. */
39:static int read_full_c(int fd, char *buf, int want) {
40:  int got = 0;
41:  while (got < want) {
42:    long r = read(fd, buf + got, (unsigned long)(want - got));
43:    if (r <= 0)
44:      return got;
45:    got += (int)r;
46:  }
47:  return got;
48:}
49:
50:/*
51: * execsvc_spawn - ask the execution service to run argv, returning its pid.
52: *
53: * Returns > 0 (pid) on success, or < 0 if the service is unreachable or refuses
54: * — the caller is expected to FALL BACK to spawning directly.  That fallback is
55: * not defensive padding: the service is supervised by init and can be briefly
56: * absent across a respawn, and a POSIX system() that failed in that window
57: * would be a worse regression than the divergence being removed.
58: */
59:int execsvc_spawn(int argc, char *const argv[], unsigned int flags) {
60:  if (argc <= 0 || argc > EXECSVC_ARG_MAX || !argv)
61:    return -1;
62:
63:  int svc = OS1_port_open(OS1NX_PORT_EXEC);
64:  if (svc < 0)
65:    return -1; /* no service published: caller falls back */
66:
67:  int reqp[2] = {-1, -1}, repp[2] = {-1, -1};
68:  int pid = -1;
69:  if (pipe(reqp) != 0) {
70:    OS1low_handle_close(svc);
71:    return -1;
72:  }
73:  if (pipe(repp) != 0) {
74:    close(reqp[0]);
75:    close(reqp[1]);
76:    OS1low_handle_close(svc);
77:    return -1;
78:  }
79:
80:  /* Header + packed body: [redir][cwd\0][argv[i]\0...].  No redirections here:
81:   * system() inherits the caller's stdio, which the child gets by default. */
82:  struct execsvc_spawn_hdr hdr;
83:  char body[EXECSVC_BODY_MAX];
84:  unsigned int off = 0;
85:  int ok = 1;
86:
87:  memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr));
88:  hdr.version = EXECSVC_VERSION;
89:  hdr.flags = flags;
90:  hdr.argc = argc;
91:  hdr.nredir = 0;
92:
93:  /* cwd: the REQUESTER's, always sent.
94:   *
95:   * This used to send an empty string commented "service default", which is
96:   * not a default at all — the child is created by the service, so it inherits
97:   * the SERVICE's cwd ("/"), and every relative path in a command silently
98:   * resolved against the wrong directory.  `os.execute("lua main.lua")` from
99:   * /home/LUA/luatest looked like a missing file.  cwd is a per-process
100:   * attribute that is inherited at creation, so it is wrong for exactly the
101:   * same reason the environment is (plan S1) — the difference is that it costs
102:   * nothing to carry, because the protocol body already has a slot for it. */
103:  {
104:    char cwd[EXECSVC_PATH_MAX];
105:    if (getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd)) != 0 || !cwd[0])
106:      cwd[0] = '\0'; /* unknown: the service leaves its own cwd alone */
107:    unsigned int n = (unsigned int)strlen(cwd) + 1;
108:    if (n > sizeof(body)) {
109:      close(reqp[0]);
110:      close(reqp[1]);
111:      close(repp[0]);
112:      close(repp[1]);
113:      OS1low_handle_close(svc);
114:      return -1;
115:    }
116:    memcpy(body + off, cwd, n);
117:    off += n;
118:  }
119:  for (int i = 0; i < argc && ok; i++) {
120:    unsigned int n = (unsigned int)strlen(argv[i]) + 1;
121:    if (off + n > sizeof(body)) {
122:      ok = 0; /* refuse rather than silently truncate a command */
123:      break;
124:    }
125:    memcpy(body + off, argv[i], n);
126:    off += n;
127:  }
128:  hdr.body_len = off;
129:
130:  if (ok) {
131:    /* Transfer the channels THROUGH the port: a handle index is meaningful only
132:     * inside one process's table, and cap_grant would need the service's PID —
133:     * which the port model deliberately does not expose. */
134:    struct ipc_message m;
135:    memset(&m, 0, sizeof(m));
136:    m.type = EXECSVC_REQ_SPAWN;
137:    int give[2];
138:    give[0] = reqp[0];
139:    give[1] = repp[1];
140:    if (OS1_port_send_caps(svc, &m, give, 2) == (long)sizeof(m)) {
141:      write_full(reqp[1], (const char *)&hdr, (int)sizeof(hdr));
142:      write_full(reqp[1], body, (int)off);
143:      close(reqp[1]); /* EOF: a short body must not hang the service */
144:      reqp[1] = -1;
145:
146:      struct execsvc_spawn_rep rep;
147:      memset(&rep, 0, sizeof(rep));
148:      if (read_full_c(repp[0], (char *)&rep, (int)sizeof(rep)) ==
149:              (int)sizeof(rep) &&
150:          rep.version == EXECSVC_VERSION)
151:        pid = rep.pid;
152:    }
153:  }
154:
155:  if (reqp[0] >= 0)
156:    close(reqp[0]);
157:  if (reqp[1] >= 0)
158:    close(reqp[1]);
159:  close(repp[0]);
160:  close(repp[1]);
161:  OS1low_handle_close(svc);
162:  return pid;
163:}
164:

@@@ user/sys/lib/font_lib.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/font_lib.c
3: * Userland font rendering library
4: *
5: * Provides loading, measurement, and rendering of pre-rasterised bitmap fonts
6: * produced by nxfont.  The on-disk format is:
7: *
8: *   [ struct font_header ]
9: *   [ struct font_glyph_info * header.num_chars ]
10: *   [ raw alpha bitmap bytes ]
11: *
12: * The font_ctx structure holds pointers into a single contiguous heap buffer
13: * (raw_data) allocated by font_load().
14: *
15: * Rendering path (draw_glyph):
16: *   Each glyph row is converted into horizontal opaque spans and each span is
17: *   drawn with one window_draw() call. This preserves transparent backgrounds
18: *   while avoiding the old one-syscall-per-lit-pixel path.
19: *
20: * UTF-8 iteration (font_draw_string, font_string_width):
21: *   Calls utf8_decode() (lib.c) per character; advances by the byte count
22: *   returned.  Invalid sequences (utf8_decode returns 0) skip one byte to
23: *   prevent an infinite loop.
24: *
25: * NOTE: font_lib.c is compiled as part of lib.o (included by lib.c:57) rather
26: * than compiled separately.  Its symbols are therefore available to all ELFs
27: * that link lib.o.
28: */
29:#include <font_lib.h>
30:#include <stdio.h>
31:#include <stdlib.h>
32:#include <string.h>
33:
34:static int add_overflows_size(size_t a, size_t b) {
35:  return a > ((size_t)-1) - b;
36:}
37:
38:static int mul_overflows_size(size_t a, size_t b) {
39:  return b != 0 && a > ((size_t)-1) / b;
40:}
41:
42:static int font_validate_buffer(const void *data, size_t size) {
43:  if (!data || size < sizeof(struct font_header))
44:    return 0;
45:
46:  const struct font_header *h = (const struct font_header *)data;
47:  if (h->magic != FONT_MAGIC)
48:    return 0;
49:  if (h->num_chars == 0)
50:    return 0;
51:  if ((uint32_t)h->ascent + (uint32_t)h->descent == 0)
52:    return 0;
53:
54:  if (mul_overflows_size(h->num_chars, sizeof(struct font_glyph_info)))
55:    return 0;
56:  size_t glyph_bytes = (size_t)h->num_chars * sizeof(struct font_glyph_info);
57:  if (add_overflows_size(sizeof(struct font_header), glyph_bytes))
58:    return 0;
59:  size_t bitmap_offset = sizeof(struct font_header) + glyph_bytes;
60:  if (add_overflows_size(bitmap_offset, h->bitmap_size))
61:    return 0;
62:  if (bitmap_offset + h->bitmap_size > size)
63:    return 0;
64:
65:  const struct font_glyph_info *glyphs =
66:      (const struct font_glyph_info *)((const uint8_t *)data +
67:                                       sizeof(struct font_header));
68:  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < h->num_chars; i++) {
69:    const struct font_glyph_info *gi = &glyphs[i];
70:    if (mul_overflows_size(gi->width, gi->height))
71:      return 0;
72:    size_t glyph_size = (size_t)gi->width * (size_t)gi->height;
73:    if (add_overflows_size(gi->data_offset, glyph_size))
74:      return 0;
75:    if (gi->data_offset + glyph_size > h->bitmap_size)
76:      return 0;
77:  }
78:
79:  return 1;
80:}
81:
82:/*
83: * font_load - read a packed font file and set up a font_ctx.
84: *
85: * path: filesystem path to a packed font produced by nxfont.
86: *
87: * Reads the file in two calls (size probe then full read), validates the
88: * FONT_MAGIC header field, and sets up interior pointers into the single
89: * raw_data allocation:
90: *   ctx->glyphs  = raw_data + sizeof(font_header)
91: *   ctx->bitmap  = raw_data + sizeof(font_header) + num_chars *
92: * sizeof(glyph_info)
93: *
94: * Returns a heap-allocated font_ctx on success, or NULL on file-not-found,
95: * malloc failure, or magic mismatch.
96: *
97: * Ownership: caller must pass the returned ctx to font_free() when done.
98: */
99:struct font_ctx *font_load(const char *path) {
100:  /* Probe file size: file_read with buf=NULL, size=0 returns byte count. */
101:  int size = file_read(path, NULL, 0, 0);
102:  if (size <= 0)
103:    return NULL;
104:
105:  void *data = malloc(size);
106:  if (!data)
107:    return NULL;
108:
109:  if (file_read(path, data, size, 0) != size) {
110:    free(data);
111:    return NULL;
112:  }
113:
114:  if (!font_validate_buffer(data, (size_t)size)) {
115:    free(data);
116:    return NULL;
117:  }
118:
119:  struct font_header *h = (struct font_header *)data;
120:  struct font_ctx *ctx = malloc(sizeof(struct font_ctx));
121:  if (!ctx) {
122:    free(data);
123:    return NULL;
124:  }
125:
126:  ctx->header = *h; /* Copy header fields by value */
127:  /* glyphs array immediately follows the font_header in the packed buffer. */
128:  ctx->glyphs =
129:      (struct font_glyph_info *)((uint8_t *)data + sizeof(struct font_header));
130:  /* Bitmap bytes follow the glyph array. */
131:  ctx->bitmap =
132:      (uint8_t *)ctx->glyphs + h->num_chars * sizeof(struct font_glyph_info);
133:  ctx->raw_data = data; /* Retains ownership for font_free() */
134:
135:  return ctx;
136:}
137:
138:/*
139: * font_free - release a font_ctx and its underlying heap buffer.
140: *
141: * Frees ctx->raw_data (which also invalidates ctx->glyphs and ctx->bitmap
142: * since they point into it), then frees ctx itself.
143: *
144: * Safe to call with NULL ctx.
145: */
146:void font_free(struct font_ctx *ctx) {
147:  if (ctx) {
148:    if (ctx->raw_data)
149:      free(ctx->raw_data);
150:    free(ctx);
151:  }
152:}
153:
154:/*
155: * draw_glyph - render a single Unicode codepoint into a compositor window.
156: *
157: * win_id:    compositor window ID.
158: * ctx:       loaded font context.
159: * x, y:      pen position (baseline left corner).
160: * codepoint: Unicode codepoint to render.
161: * color:     ARGB foreground colour (0xAARRGGBB).
162: *
163: * The glyph bitmap is a row-major alpha (grayscale) image; each byte is an
164: * opacity value 0..255. Pixels with alpha > 128 are drawn as filled spans.
165: *
166: * start_y accounts for the font ascent so that the baseline is at y + ascent
167: * and gi->y0 is a signed offset from that baseline.
168: *
169: * Codepoints outside the font's first_char..first_char+num_chars range are
170: * silently skipped (no replacement glyph).
171: *
172: * Performance note: contiguous pixels on the same row are coalesced into a
173: * single rectangle, which keeps text transparent while sharply reducing
174: * compositor syscalls for normal glyphs.
175: */
176:static void draw_glyph(int win_id, struct font_ctx *ctx, int x, int y,
177:                       uint32_t codepoint, uint32_t color) {
178:  int idx = (int)codepoint - ctx->header.first_char;
179:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= ctx->header.num_chars)
180:    return;
181:
182:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &ctx->glyphs[idx];
183:  uint8_t *bitmap = ctx->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
184:
185:  /* start_y: baseline = y + ascent; gi->y0 is a signed descent offset. */
186:  int start_x = x + gi->x0;
187:  int start_y = y + ctx->header.ascent + gi->y0;
188:
189:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
190:    int gx = 0;
191:    while (gx < gi->width) {
192:      while (gx < gi->width && bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx] <= 128) {
193:        gx++;
194:      }
195:
196:      int span_start = gx;
197:      while (gx < gi->width && bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx] > 128) {
198:        gx++;
199:      }
200:
201:      if (gx > span_start) {
202:        window_draw(win_id, start_x + span_start, start_y + gy, gx - span_start,
203:                    1, color);
204:      }
205:    }
206:  }
207:}
208:
209:/*
210: * font_draw_string - render a UTF-8 string into a compositor window.
211: *
212: * Iterates the string using utf8_decode() to handle multi-byte sequences,
213: * calls draw_glyph() for each codepoint, and advances cursor_x by the
214: * glyph's advance width.
215: *
216: * Invalid UTF-8 bytes (utf8_decode returns 0) advance the pointer by one
217: * byte to prevent an infinite loop; no replacement glyph is drawn.
218: *
219: * Codepoints outside the font range are skipped (no advance applied either,
220: * so they consume no horizontal space).
221: */
222:void font_draw_string(int win_id, struct font_ctx *ctx, int x, int y,
223:                      const char *str, uint32_t color) {
224:  if (!ctx || !str)
225:    return;
226:
227:  int cursor_x = x;
228:  uint32_t codepoint;
229:  int consumed;
230:  size_t rem = 0;
231:  const char *p = str;
232:  while (*p) {
233:    p++;
234:    rem++;
235:  }
236:
237:  while (*str) {
238:    consumed = utf8_decode(str, rem, &codepoint);
239:    if (consumed <= 0) {
240:      str++; /* Skip invalid byte to avoid infinite loop */
241:      rem--;
242:      continue;
243:    }
244:    draw_glyph(win_id, ctx, cursor_x, y, codepoint, color);
245:    int idx = (int)codepoint - ctx->header.first_char;
246:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < ctx->header.num_chars) {
247:      cursor_x += ctx->glyphs[idx].advance;
248:    }
249:    str += consumed;
250:    rem -= consumed;
251:  }
252:}
253:
254:/*
255: * font_string_width - compute the rendered pixel width of a UTF-8 string.
256: *
257: * Walks the string identically to font_draw_string but accumulates advance
258: * widths without drawing.  Used by callers to centre or right-align text.
259: *
260: * Returns the total advance in pixels, or 0 for NULL/empty input.
261: *
262: * Note: does not account for kerning (stb_truetype provides per-pair
263: * kerning but the packed font format does not store a kerning table).
264: */
265:int font_string_width(struct font_ctx *ctx, const char *str) {
266:  if (!ctx || !str)
267:    return 0;
268:
269:  int width = 0;
270:  uint32_t codepoint;
271:  int consumed;
272:  size_t rem = 0;
273:  const char *p = str;
274:  while (*p) {
275:    p++;
276:    rem++;
277:  }
278:
279:  while (*str) {
280:    consumed = utf8_decode(str, rem, &codepoint);
281:    if (consumed <= 0) {
282:      str++; /* Skip invalid byte */
283:      rem--;
284:      continue;
285:    }
286:    int idx = (int)codepoint - ctx->header.first_char;
287:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < ctx->header.num_chars) {
288:      width += ctx->glyphs[idx].advance;
289:    }
290:    str += consumed;
291:    rem -= consumed;
292:  }
293:  return width;
294:}

1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/lib.c
3: * Userland C runtime and system call wrapper library
4: *
5: * This file is the sole C runtime for all userland processes.  It is
6: * compiled into lib.o and linked into every ELF (there is no shared library
7: * mechanism).  It provides:
8: *
9: *   - Thin C wrappers around every _sys_*() assembly stub from syscall.S.
10: *   - Standard I/O emulation (fopen/fclose/fread/fwrite/fseek/ftell) backed
11: *     by file_read/file_write syscalls.
12: *   - Formatting (printf, snprintf, sprintf, vsnprintf, vsscanf, sscanf).
13: *   - Input event decoding (input_poll_event: keyboard and mouse IPC msgs).
14: *   - Graphics helpers (graphics_draw_rect, graphics_blit, graphics_draw_text,
15: *     graphics_text_width, graphics_load_image).
16: *   - Partial POSIX-like shims (strdup, strtol, abs, fabs, atof, getenv,
17: *     mkdir, system, stat, puts, fflush, remove, rename, vfprintf).
18: *   - UTF-8 decoder (utf8_decode).
19: *   - Stack smash protector stub (__stack_chk_guard, __stack_chk_fail).
20: *
21: * STB libraries (NOTE USR-BLOAT-01/02):
22: *   STB_IMAGE_IMPLEMENTATION is compiled unconditionally here. Text rendering
23: *   now uses the OS1 packed bitmap font path instead of stb_easy_font.
24: *
25: * Kernel source inclusion (NOTE USR-LIB-01):
26: *   vsnprintf.c, math.c, string.c are sourced directly from kernel/lib/ via
27: *   relative #include paths.  Any internal change to those kernel files
28: *   silently changes userland behaviour.
29: *
30: * Known issues:
31: *   USR-LIB-01  (W2 BAD-IMPL) Directly #includes kernel/lib C sources;
32: *               breaks the userland/kernel boundary.
33: *   USR-LIB-02  (fixed) The stdio wrappers used to guard against NULL with
34: *               `(size_t)fp > 10`, a fragile magic-value check; replaced with
35: *               proper NULL checks.  fopen streams are now write-buffered
36: *               (FILE.wbuf) so incremental writers issue one syscall per
37: *               FILE_WBUF_SIZE instead of one per fwrite; fflush/fclose/fseek
38: *               and every fread flush the buffer first.
39: *   USR-LIB-03  (fixed locally) graphics_draw_text used to declare a 100KB
40: *               static buffer and fall back to terminal text rendering.
41: *   USR-LIB-04  (partly fixed) system/getenv are no-ops; atof truncates
42: *               decimal fractions via (double)atoi(). mkdir now composes over
43: *               a parent directory capability (real ext4 directory creation).
44: *   USR-LIB-05  (W1 DOC) vfprintf ignores the stream arg and always writes
45: *               to fd 1; stderr goes to stdout silently.
46: *   USR-SEC-01  (W3 SECURITY) registry_read/write have no authentication;
47: *               any process can overwrite any key.
48: *   USR-SEC-02  (W3 SECURITY) send()/kill_process() accept arbitrary PIDs
49: *               with no capability check.
50: *   USR-BLOAT-01 (W2 BAD-IMPL·PERF) STB libs always compiled in; no
51: * gc-sections. USR-BLOAT-02 (W2 BAD-IMPL) -g DWARF retained in every ELF; not
52: * stripped.
53: */

126:/* errno: global error variable expected by POSIX-style libc callers. */

129:/* These timezone helpers are required by the gnulib time layer and must be

135:/*
136: * errno_ret - THE POSIX errno seam for the syscall veneers below.
137: *
138: * Kernel syscalls return a NEGATIVE errno on failure (e.g. -ENOENT, -EACCES);
139: * the POSIX contract every libc caller relies on is "set errno to the positive
140: * code and return -1".  Routing the file/fd wrappers through here is what stops
141: * failures surfacing as strerror(0) == "Success" (the "(Success)" Lua's
142: * io.open printed on a missing file) — and it is deliberately generic: ANY
143: * POSIX-style consumer, not just Lua, gets correct errno/strerror from now on.
144: */
145:static long errno_ret_ctx(long r, const char *ctx) {
146:  if (r < 0) {
147:    errno = (int)-r;
148:    /*
149:     * The classifier runs HERE, so the diagnostic declaration is universal.
150:     *
151:     * OS1_report_error's own comment promises that a hard failure in ANY libc
152:     * or portability path becomes visible, but it was reached from three call
153:     * sites only — so every OTHER POSIX veneer set errno correctly and was
154:     * never classified.  A promise kept at three sites is not a policy, it is
155:     * a convention each new compatibility layer (SDL, lua, doom, tomorrow
156:     * musl) has to remember to call — and "remember to call it" is the shape
157:     * of a duplication waiting to diverge.
158:     *
159:     * Safe to route everything through it because the POLICY is already
160:     * selective: ENOENT/EAGAIN and the rest of normal control flow stay
161:     * silent, EACCES/EPERM warn, and only EIO/EFAULT/ENOMEM/ENOSPC/EROFS
162:     * raise the red one.  Probes cannot spam it.
163:     */
164:    OS1_report_error(ctx, (int)r);
165:    return -1;
166:  }
167:  return r;
168:}
169:
170:/* errno_ret - the POSIX seam without a context tag (ctx defaults to "libc").
171: * Callers that know the object they failed on should use errno_ret_ctx so the
172: * notification names it. */
173:static long errno_ret(long r) { return errno_ret_ctx(r, NULL); }
174:
175:/*
176: * OS1_report_error - THE single userland error-surfacing seam
177: * (PLAN-2026-07-17-STRATIFICATION.md, Phase 0).
178: *
179: * Maps an errno to the notification system BY SEVERITY CLASS, so a hard
180: * failure in ANY libc / portability path (SDL, lua, doom, ...) becomes visible
181: * — a red/amber notification with context — instead of a silent -1 an app can
182: * ignore and loop on.  Every layer calls THIS one policy; none hand-rolls its
183: * own notify (no duplication, uniform behaviour).  Normal control-flow errors
184: * stay silent so probes (ENOENT, EAGAIN) never spam:
185: *
186: *   EIO/EFAULT/ENOMEM/ENOSPC/EROFS -> error (red)   — unexpected / hard fault
187: *   EACCES/EPERM                   -> warn  (amber) — policy denial
188: *   everything else                -> silent        — normal control flow
189: *
190: * `err` may be given as errno (positive) or as a raw -errno syscall return.
191: * `ctx` is a short tag: a subsystem ("vfs", "mmap") or "op path".
192: */
193:void OS1_report_error(const char *ctx, int err) {
194:  if (err < 0)
195:    err = -err;
196:  if (!ctx)
197:    ctx = "libc";
198:  switch (err) {
199:  case EIO:
200:  case EFAULT:
201:  case ENOMEM:
202:  case ENOSPC:
203:  case EROFS:
204:    OS1_notify_error(ctx, strerror(err));
205:    break;
206:  case EACCES:
207:  case EPERM:
208:    OS1_notify_warn(ctx, strerror(err));
209:    break;
210:  default:
211:    break; /* normal control-flow error: no notification */
212:  }
213:}

215:/* --- Syscall Wrappers ---
216: * Each function below is a thin C-callable veneer over an assembly stub in
217: * user/arch/<arch>/syscall.S.  Arguments are passed in the arch ABI registers
218: * (x0-x5 on AArch64, rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8/r9 on x86-64) by the C compiler;
219: * the stub moves the syscall number into x8/rax and issues svc/syscall.
220: *
221: * NOTE(USR-SEC-02): send(), kill_process(), and spawn() accept arbitrary PIDs
222: * and paths with no capability check; any process has full authority.
223: */
224:long read(int fd, char *buf, unsigned long count) {
225:  return errno_ret(_sys_read(fd, buf, count));
226:}
227:long write(int fd, const char *buf, size_t count) {
228:  return errno_ret(_sys_write(fd, buf, count));
229:}
230:long OS1_time_now(void) { return _sys_get_time(); }
231:long get_time(void) { return OS1_time_now(); } /* compat shim (DIR-01 F4) */
232:
233:time_t time(time_t *t) {
234:  time_t sec = (time_t)OS1_time_now();
235:  if (t)
236:    *t = sec;
237:  return sec;
238:}

240:/* Tier 3 os1 time primitives (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4); SYS_CLOCK_GETTIME
241: * clk 0 = monotonic ns since boot, clk 1 = this process's CPU time in ns. */
242:unsigned long long os1_mono_ns(void) {
243:  return (unsigned long long)_sys_clock_gettime(0);
244:}
245:unsigned long long os1_cpu_ns(void) {
246:  return (unsigned long long)_sys_clock_gettime(1);
247:}
248:/* clock_gettime: POSIX layer over the os1 primitives (<time.h>). */
249:int clock_gettime(int clk, struct timespec *ts) {
250:  if (!ts)
251:    return -1;
252:  unsigned long long ns =
253:      (clk == CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID) ? os1_cpu_ns() : os1_mono_ns();
254:  ts->tv_sec = (time_t)(ns / 1000000000ULL);
255:  ts->tv_nsec = (long)(ns % 1000000000ULL);
256:  return 0;
257:}
258:
259:/* nanosleep: POSIX blocking sleep over the SYS_NANOSLEEP primitive (<time.h>).
260: * Not interruptible here, so it always completes: *rem is zeroed, returns 0. */
261:int nanosleep(const struct timespec *req, struct timespec *rem) {
262:  if (!req || req->tv_nsec < 0 || req->tv_nsec >= 1000000000L)
263:    return -1;
264:  unsigned long long ns = (unsigned long long)req->tv_sec * 1000000000ULL +
265:                          (unsigned long long)req->tv_nsec;
266:  _sys_nanosleep(ns);
267:  if (rem) {
268:    rem->tv_sec = 0;
269:    rem->tv_nsec = 0;
270:  }
271:  return 0;
272:}
273:/* --- Process control: OS1low_ canonical primitives (ASTRA §6.1, DIR-01 F4) ---
274: * The stable low-level process surface; each just wraps a _sys_ stub, so there
275: * is no new syscall and no behaviour change.  The bare verbs below are
276: * zero-breakage compat shims forwarding here (kill_process/wait/yield are shims
277: * defined further down, next to their original neighbours).  exit keeps the
278: * while(1): unreachable dead code that silences the "noreturn" warning in
279: * compilers that do not see svc #0 as a terminator. */
280:/* Forward declaration: every spawn primitive below propagates
281: * the caller's environment into the child's per-process registry
282: * namespace before returning the pid — see __env_propagate_to_child,
283: * defined further down with the rest of the OS1_env_* surface. */
284:static void __env_propagate_to_child(long child_pid);
285:
286:long OS1low_process_spawn(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[]) {
287:  long pid = _sys_spawn(path, argc, argv, 0);
288:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
289:  return pid;
290:}
291:/* Detached (SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED, #193): the child does NOT inherit the spawner
292: * as ctty — the nxexec launcher-mode.  See caps.h for the flag semantics. */
293:long OS1low_process_spawn_detached(const char *path, int argc,
294:                                   char *const argv[]) {
295:  long pid = _sys_spawn(path, argc, argv, SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED);
296:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
297:  return pid;
298:}
299:/* Phase 4: spawn with fd redirection (shell `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`).  The redirect
300: * targets must already be open in THIS process; the kernel dups them into the
301: * child, so the caller closes its copies after we return. */
302:long OS1low_process_spawn_redir(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[],
303:                                unsigned int flags,
304:                                const struct spawn_redir *redir, int nredir) {
305:  long pid = (nredir <= 0)
306:                 ? _sys_spawn(path, argc, argv, flags)
307:                 : _sys_spawn_redir(path, argc, argv, flags, redir, nredir);
308:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
309:  return pid;
310:}
311:long OS1low_process_spawn_caps(const char *path, int level,
312:                               unsigned long caps) {
313:  long pid = _sys_spawn_caps(path, level, caps, 0);
314:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
315:  return pid;
316:}
317:/* OS1low_pipe (Phase 4): anonymous byte pipe (OBJ_TYPE_PIPE).  fds[0]=read end,
318: * fds[1]=write end.  The kernel installs both handles; read/write/close operate
319: * on them like any other fd. */
320:int OS1low_pipe(int fds[2]) { return (int)errno_ret(_sys_pipe(fds)); }
321:/* POSIX pipe(): thin personality over OS1low_pipe (unistd.h). */
322:int pipe(int pipefd[2]) { return OS1low_pipe(pipefd); }
323:int OS1low_process_kill(int pid) { return _sys_kill(pid); }
324:/* OS1low_process_wait (F4 M4.5): wait via a PROCESS capability +
325: * OS1_object_wait. A WAIT-only handle is acquirable for any live process
326: * (wait-right is separable from kill-right); if the process is already gone,
327: * acquisition fails and we fall back to the ambient SYS_WAIT so the legacy "not
328: * found" (-2) result is preserved. */
329:/* __wait_encode - map the kernel's NEXS-neutral wait code to the POSIX status
330: * word (Phase 2). code >= 0: voluntary exit -> exit code in bits 8..15
331: * (WIFEXITED). code < 0: killed -> low byte = -code (WIFSIGNALED). */
332:static int __wait_encode(int code) {
333:  if (code < 0)
334:    return (-code) & 0x7f;
335:  return (code & 0xff) << 8;
336:}
337:
338:int OS1low_process_wait(int pid) { return OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, 0); }
339:
340:/* OS1low_process_wait_status - like OS1low_process_wait, but on reap writes the
341: * process's raw exit_code to *code (Phase 2). Carried through the PROCESS
342: * capability's OS1_object_wait(handle, &code); the ambient fallback has no
343: * status channel, so *code stays 0 there. */
344:int OS1low_process_wait_status(int pid, int *code) {
345:  char idbuf[16];
346:  sprintf(idbuf, "%d", pid);
347:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, idbuf, OS1_RIGHT_WAIT,
348:                                OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
349:  if (h < 0) {
350:    /* No capability: the process is already GONE — which since Phase 9b is the
351:     * case where a retained status is precisely what we are after, so the
352:     * ambient path must carry it back rather than drop it. */
353:    return _sys_wait_status(pid, code);
354:  }
355:  long r = OS1_object_wait((int)h, (long)code);
356:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
357:  return (int)r;
358:}
359:/* OS1_process_stop / _cont - job control (Phase 2). Acquire a PROCESS
360: * capability with the control (DESTROY) right — the same authority as kill —
361: * and issue OBJ_CTL_STOP/CONT. Returns 0 or a negative errno. */
362:static int os1_process_ctl(int pid, int cmd) {
363:  char idbuf[16];
364:  sprintf(idbuf, "%d", pid);
365:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, idbuf, OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY,
366:                                OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
367:  if (h < 0)
368:    return (int)h;
369:  long r = OS1_object_ctl((int)h, cmd, 0);
370:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
371:  return (int)r;
372:}
373:int OS1_process_stop(int pid) { return os1_process_ctl(pid, OBJ_CTL_STOP); }
374:int OS1_process_cont(int pid) { return os1_process_ctl(pid, OBJ_CTL_CONT); }

377:int OS1low_process_self(void) { return _sys_get_pid(); }
378:void OS1low_process_exit(int status) {
379:  _sys_exit(status);
380:  while (1)
381:    ;
382:}

391:/* Minimal Linux-compatible random API for GNU Coreutils and other ports.
392: * The kernel does not expose a SYS_getrandom syscall in this tree yet, so the
393: * libc layer synthesizes a non-blocking pseudo-random source from a tiny xorshift
394: * state seeded from the OS1 clock and PID.  This is intentionally sufficient to
395: * satisfy compile-time/test-time expectations and keep the userland port moving
396: * without special-casing any applet. */
397:static unsigned long long os1_rand_state = 0;
398:static unsigned long long os1_rand_next(void) {
399:  unsigned long long x = os1_rand_state;
400:  if (x == 0) {
401:    x = (unsigned long long)OS1_time_now() ^ 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
402:    x ^= (unsigned long long)getpid() << 13;
403:    x ^= (unsigned long long)os1_mono_ns();
404:  }
405:  x ^= x >> 12;
406:  x ^= x << 25;
407:  x ^= x >> 27;
408:  os1_rand_state = x;
409:  return x;
410:}
411:
412:ssize_t getrandom(void *buf, size_t buflen, unsigned int flags) {
413:  (void)flags;
414:  if (!buf && buflen != 0) {
415:    errno = EFAULT;
416:    return -1;
417:  }
418:  unsigned char *p = (unsigned char *)buf;
419:  for (size_t i = 0; i < buflen; ++i) {
420:    if ((i & 7) == 0) {
421:      unsigned long long v = os1_rand_next();
422:      for (int j = 0; j < 8 && i + j < buflen; ++j)
423:        p[i + j] = (unsigned char)(v >> (8 * j));
424:      i += 7;
425:    }
426:  }
427:  return (ssize_t)buflen;
428:}
429:
430:int getentropy(void *buffer, size_t length) {
431:  if (!buffer && length != 0) {
432:    errno = EFAULT;
433:    return -1;
434:  }
435:  if (length > 256) {
436:    errno = EINVAL;
437:    return -1;
438:  }
439:  ssize_t r = getrandom(buffer, length, 0);
440:  if (r < 0)
441:    return -1;
442:  return 0;
443:}

445:/* isatty: a descriptor is a terminal iff the object behind its handle is a
446: * CONSOLE.  This is the REAL test via the capability type (OS1low_cap_query),
447: * not the old "fd < 3" assumption: with shell redirection fd 1 may be a FILE
448: * (`cmd > out`) or a PIPE (`cmd | cmd`), and interactive programs (the lua
449: * REPL) must see isatty() == 0 in exactly those cases. */
450:int isatty(int fd) {
451:  long q = OS1low_cap_query(fd);
452:  if (q < 0) {
453:    errno = EBADF;
454:    return 0;
455:  }
456:  return OS1_CAPQ_TYPE(q) == OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE ? 1 : 0;
457:}
458:#define MAX_ATEXIT 32
459:static void (*s_atexit_handlers[MAX_ATEXIT])(void);
460:static int s_atexit_count = 0;
461:
462:int atexit(void (*function)(void)) {
463:  if (!function || s_atexit_count >= MAX_ATEXIT)
464:    return -1;
465:  s_atexit_handlers[s_atexit_count++] = function;
466:  return 0;
467:}
468:
469:void exit(int status) {
470:  while (s_atexit_count > 0) {
471:    void (*fn)(void) = s_atexit_handlers[--s_atexit_count];
472:    if (fn)
473:      fn();
474:  }
475:  fflush(stdout);
476:  fflush(stderr);
477:  OS1low_process_exit(status);
478:}

520:/* --- Service ports (ASTRA §6.5) -------------------------------------------
521: * Thin personality over handle_create + object I/O: the port is the capability,
522: * so there is no separate "port syscall" to add — acquiring the handle IS the
523: * authority decision, and send/receive are ordinary object writes/reads.
524: */
525:int OS1_port_create(const char *name) {
526:  /* RECEIVE right publishes the port and claims ownership; TRANSFER lets the
527:   * owner delegate send rights onward (cap_grant) without re-opening by name.
528:   */
529:  return (int)errno_ret(OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PORT, name,
530:                                             OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_WRITE |
531:                                                 OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER |
532:                                                 OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE,
533:                                             OBJ_TYPE_PORT));
534:}
535:int OS1_port_open(const char *name) {
536:  /* No READ: a client gets a SEND-only capability to an existing service. */
537:  return (int)errno_ret(OS1low_handle_create(
538:      OS1_NS_PORT, name, OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE, OBJ_TYPE_PORT));
539:}

646:/* Identity / privilege introspection (nxperm foundation): the caller's own

679:/* OS1_sleep: block for `ms` milliseconds via the REAL kernel timer
680: * (SYS_NANOSLEEP). The process is descheduled (no busy-wait) and woken by its
681: * core's tick, so it no longer monopolises a core while idle. This is the NEXS
682: * proprietary base API (milliseconds), deliberately distinct from POSIX
683: * sleep(seconds); see <unistd.h>/<time.h> for the POSIX usleep/nanosleep. */
684:void OS1_sleep(int ms) {

758:/* --- Registry Wrappers (OS1_registry_*, ASTRA §6.6) ---
759: * op=0 read 'key' into buf; op=1 write 'key' (kernel-side CAP_REG_WRITE +
760: * first-writer-wins ownership); op=2 enumerate, optionally under a prefix. */
761:int OS1_registry_get(const char *key, char *buf, size_t size) {

764:int OS1_registry_set(const char *key, const char *value) {
765:  int rc = (int)_sys_registry(1, key, (char *)value, strlen(value));
766:  /* The kernel only ever pr_warn/UART-logs an owner-mismatch denial — it
767:   * must not know about notifications, IPC to a specific service, or any
768:   * other userland concept (kernel/userland separation).  The CALLER
769:   * already gets -EACCES back synchronously right here, so it is the one
770:   * that reports on itself, through the ordinary notify() transport every
771:   * other warning already uses (no kernel involvement, no polling
772:   * anywhere: nxntfy_srv picks it up via its existing blocking recv(),
773:   * nxbar's already-per-frame ring read picks it up from there). */
774:  if (rc == -EACCES)
775:    OS1_notify_warn("registry", key);

818:/* file_read: buf==NULL / size==0 returns the file size without reading data;
819: * used by fopen() to probe file size before allocating a read buffer. */
820:/* OS1_fs_ functions: canonical (ASTRA §6.3); the bare file_write/file_read/
821: * list_dir/chdir/getcwd below are compat shims (DIR-01 F4). */
822:/* OS1_fs_write (M4.5-FS-WRITE resolved): data writes routed through a FILE
823: * capability, mirroring OS1_fs_read — handle_create(FS, WRITE|CREATE) →
824: * OBJ_CTL_SEEK(offset) → object_write → close.  OS1_RIGHT_CREATE gives
825: * open(O_CREAT) semantics (a missing file is created behind the same
826: * vfs_write_allowed seam the ambient path used), so creation keeps working;
827: * a size==0 call is the create/truncate-empty idiom: the creation already
828: * happened at handle_create, nothing to write. */
829:int OS1_fs_write(const char *path, const void *buf, int size, int offset) {
830:  if (size < 0) {
831:    errno = EINVAL;
832:    return -EINVAL;
833:  }
834:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(
835:      OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_CREATE, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
836:  if (h < 0) {
837:    errno = (int)-h;
838:    OS1_report_error(path,
839:                     (int)h); /* surface EACCES/EIO; ENOENT stays silent */
840:    return (int)h;
841:  }
842:  long w = 0;
843:  if (size > 0) {
844:    if (offset > 0)
845:      OS1_object_ctl((int)h, OBJ_CTL_SEEK, offset);
846:    w = OS1_object_write((int)h, buf, (unsigned long)size);
847:  }
848:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
849:  if (w < 0) {
850:    errno = (int)-w;
851:    OS1_report_error(path, (int)w);
852:  }
853:  return (int)w;
854:}
855:/* OS1_fs_read (F4 M4.5; ambient fallback removed by R1): data reads routed
856: * through a FILE capability — handle_create(FS,READ) -> OBJ_CTL_SEEK(offset) ->
857: * object_read -> close.
858: *
859: * The size<=0 / NULL-buf call is a metadata size-probe.  It used to fall back
860: * to the ambient SYS_FILE_READ verb "because the object read does not do that"
861: * — but OBJ_CTL_STAT does, and always did: the object layer was never missing
862: * the capability, only this caller was not asking for it.  Probing through the
863: * handle removes the last libc user of the ambient path (Programme R1) and, in
864: * passing, makes the probe capability-checked like every other read. */
865:int OS1_fs_read(const char *path, void *buf, int size, int offset) {
866:  /* EXIT SEMANTICS ARE PRESERVED EXACTLY.  The old guard was `size <= 0 ||
867:   * !buf` funnelling into the ambient verb, but the KERNEL branched only on
868:   * `size`, so the one guard covered three different outcomes and they must
869:   * stay distinct:
870:   *
871:   *   size < 0            (size_t)size wrapped to a huge value, tripping the
872:   *                       SYSCALL_MAX_IO_BYTES check       -> -EINVAL
873:   *   size > 0, buf NULL  the kernel read, then copy_to_user(NULL) failed
874:   *                                                        -> -EFAULT
875:   *   size == 0           probe: vfs_read_file(path,NULL,0) -> file size,
876:   *                       any failure reported as          -> -ENOENT
877:   *
878:   * Collapsing all three onto "return the size" would have made a negative
879:   * size and a NULL destination look like successful probes. */
880:  if (size < 0) {
881:    errno = EINVAL;
882:    return -EINVAL;
883:  }
884:  if (size > 0 && !buf) {
885:    errno = EFAULT;
886:    return -EFAULT;
887:  }
888:  if (size == 0) {
889:    /* THE SIZE-PROBE STANDARD (made explicit here, R1).
890:     *
891:     * `size == 0` asks "how big is this file".  That is a STAT question, and a
892:     * stat has no offset — so the offset argument is meaningless for a probe.
893:     * The old implementation silently ignored it and returned the total size,
894:     * which means a caller asking "how many bytes remain after `offset`" got
895:     * the whole size and no indication it had asked something the API does not
896:     * answer.  This refuses instead, following the rule this project already
897:     * applies to the environment ceilings: a silently different value is worse
898:     * than a failure, because the failure is diagnosable.
899:     *
900:     * Verified before enforcing: all 12 probe call sites in the tree pass
901:     * offset 0 (fopen, font_lib, nxfilem, nxlauncher, rename/truncate,
902:     * fdtest/writetest/capreg), so no application changes — the standard was
903:     * already universally observed, it just was not stated or enforced.
904:     *
905:     * Probe through the object layer: OBJ_CTL_STAT is exactly "current size in
906:     * bytes" and resolves it from the same place the ambient verb did
907:     * (vfs_stat, falling back to the node size), so the value is identical.
908:     * Read acquisition is ungated (the tree ACL gates writes), so a file
909:     * readable before is readable now — the probe is simply capability-routed
910:     * like every other read.  Failure stays -ENOENT to keep the old contract;
911:     * handle_create knows more (-EACCES, …) but changing what callers observe
912:     * is a separate decision, not a side effect of this refactor. */
913:    if (offset != 0) {
914:      errno = EINVAL;
915:      return -EINVAL;
916:    }
917:    /* ONE syscall.  The first R1 version did handle_create + OBJ_CTL_STAT +
918:     * close — three syscalls and two path resolutions for one number, on the
919:     * path every fopen() takes.  SYS_STAT asks the same VFS once. */
920:    struct abi_stat as;
921:    if (_sys_stat(path, &as) != 0) {
922:      errno = ENOENT;
923:      return -ENOENT;
924:    }
925:    return (int)as.size;
926:  }
927:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
928:  if (h < 0) {
929:    errno = (int)-h;
930:    return (int)h;
931:  }
932:  if (offset > 0)
933:    OS1_object_ctl((int)h, OBJ_CTL_SEEK, offset);
934:  long r = OS1_object_read((int)h, buf, (unsigned long)size);
935:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
936:  if (r < 0)
937:    errno = (int)-r;
938:  return (int)r;
939:}
940:/* OS1_fs_list (R1): a directory is a file you READ.  handle_create(FS,READ) ->
941: * object_read -> close, the same shape as OS1_fs_read — so listing goes through
942: * the capability layer like every other read instead of the ambient
943: * SYS_LIST_DIR verb.
944: *
945: * Exit semantics preserved: the ambient verb returned the listing LENGTH and
946: * -ENOENT for a missing/unreadable path, so acquisition failure maps to
947: * -ENOENT rather than surfacing handle_create's own errno.  The listing is
948: * NUL-terminated for callers that treat it as a string (the ambient path
949: * copied res+1 bytes for exactly that reason). */
950:int OS1_fs_list(const char *path, char *buf, size_t size) {
951:  if (!buf || size == 0) {
952:    errno = EINVAL;
953:    return -EINVAL;
954:  }
955:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
956:  if (h < 0) {
957:    errno = ENOENT;
958:    return -ENOENT;
959:  }
960:  long r = OS1_object_read((int)h, buf, size - 1);
961:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
962:  if (r < 0) {
963:    errno = ENOENT;
964:    return -ENOENT;
965:  }
966:  buf[r] = '\0';
967:  return (int)r;
968:}
969:int OS1_fs_chdir(const char *path) { return _sys_chdir(path); }
970:int OS1_fs_getcwd(char *buf, size_t size) { return _sys_getcwd(buf, size); }
971:
972:/* __fs_parent_ctl - split a pathname into a parent directory and one child
973: * name, acquire the parent with the distinct MUTATE right, then send the
974: * namespace operation through that capability. The kernel repeats the
975: * one-component validation: this split is composition convenience, not a
976: * security boundary. */
977:static int __fs_parent_ctl(const char *path, int cmd) {
978:  if (!path)
979:    return -EFAULT;
980:
981:  char work[128];
982:  size_t len = strlen(path);
983:  if (len == 0 || len >= sizeof(work))
984:    return -EINVAL;
985:  memcpy(work, path, len + 1);
986:  while (len > 1 && work[len - 1] == '/')
987:    work[--len] = '\0';
988:  if (strcmp(work, "/") == 0)
989:    return -EINVAL;
990:
991:  char *leaf = work + len;
992:  while (leaf > work && leaf[-1] != '/')
993:    leaf--;
994:  const char *parent;
995:  if (leaf == work) {
996:    parent = ".";
997:  } else if (leaf == work + 1 && work[0] == '/') {
998:    parent = "/";
999:  } else {
1000:    leaf[-1] = '\0';
1001:    parent = work;
1002:  }
1003:  if (!leaf[0])
1004:    return -EINVAL;
1005:
1006:  long h =
1007:      OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, parent, OS1_RIGHT_MUTATE, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
1008:  if (h < 0)
1009:    return (int)h;
1010:  long r = OS1_object_ctl((int)h, cmd, (long)leaf);
1011:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
1012:  return (int)r;
1013:}
1014:
1015:int OS1_fs_mkdir(const char *path) {
1016:  return __fs_parent_ctl(path, OBJ_CTL_MKDIR);
1017:}
1018:int OS1_fs_unlink(const char *path) {
1019:  return __fs_parent_ctl(path, OBJ_CTL_UNLINK);
1020:}
1021:int file_write(const char *path, const void *buf, int size, int offset) {
1022:  return OS1_fs_write(path, buf, size, offset);

1024:int file_read(const char *path, void *buf, int size, int offset) {
1025:  return OS1_fs_read(path, buf, size, offset);

1027:int list_dir(const char *path, char *buf, size_t size) {
1028:  return OS1_fs_list(path, buf, size);

1033:/*
1034: * open - POSIX fd open (ABI-03 fd table).
1035: *
1036: * The create/truncate/append semantics live in the kernel now: SYS_OPEN
1037: * honours O_CREAT/O_TRUNC through the VFS write-ACL + create seam (ASTRA §6.8,
1038: * kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c).  libc keeps only the POSIX personality
1039: * work: pass the flags straight through, map the negative errno (errno_ret),
1040: * surface a protected-path denial on the standard notify() transport, and set
1041: * the initial position for O_APPEND (a fresh handle starts at offset 0, and
1042: * the kernel does not track per-write append).  The variadic mode argument is
1043: * accepted but not applied (the ext4 driver fixes new-file perms).
1044: */
1045:int open(const char *pathname, int flags, ...) {
1046:  int fd = (int)_sys_open(pathname, flags);
1047:  if (fd < 0) {
1048:    /* Uniform surfacing (Phase 0): amber on EACCES, red on a hard fault,
1049:     * silent on an ENOENT probe — the policy lives in OS1_report_error, not
1050:     * here, so every open() caller and every portability layer behave alike.
1051:     * The report now happens INSIDE the errno seam (see errno_ret_ctx); this
1052:     * site passes the path so the notification still names the file rather
1053:     * than the generic "libc", and reports ONCE instead of twice. */
1054:    return (int)errno_ret_ctx(fd, pathname);
1055:  }
1056:  if (flags & O_APPEND)
1057:    _sys_lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END); /* best-effort: initial position at EOF */
1058:  return fd;
1059:}
1060:int close(int fd) { return (int)errno_ret(_sys_close(fd)); }
1061:long lseek(int fd, long offset, int whence) {
1062:  return errno_ret(_sys_lseek(fd, offset, whence));
1063:}

1065:/* --- Formatting & Printing ---
1066: * All formatting functions delegate to vsnprintf() from kernel/lib/vsnprintf.c
1067: * (included above).  Output goes to fd 1 (the shell/window TTY) via write().
1068: *
1069: * printf: uses a 256-byte stack buffer; output longer than 255 chars is
1070: * silently truncated by vsnprintf.
1071: *
1072: * printf_win: like printf but writes to a specific compositor window by id
1073: * via window_write() (the dedicated SYS_WINDOW_WRITE, #123) — no longer the
1074: * fd>=100 overload on write().
1075: *
1076: * vsprintf/sprintf: pass 65536 as the size limit — effectively unbounded.
1077: * Callers are responsible for providing a large enough destination buffer;
1078: * overflow is not detected.
1079: *
1080: * print_hex: renders a 64-bit value as 18-char "0xHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH" string
1081: * written directly via write(), bypassing the format engine.
1082: */
1083:int vsprintf(char *out, const char *fmt, va_list args) {
1084:  return vsnprintf(out, 65536, fmt, args);
1085:}
1086:int printf(const char *fmt, ...) {
1087:  char buf[256];
1088:  va_list args;
1089:  va_start(args, fmt);
1090:  int res = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args);
1091:  va_end(args);
1092:  write(1, buf, strlen(buf));
1093:  return res;
1094:}
1095:void window_write(int win_id, const char *buf, unsigned long count) {
1096:  OS1_window_write(win_id, buf, count);
1097:}

1099:int window_grid(int win_id, int *cols, int *rows) {
1100:  return OS1_window_grid(win_id, cols, rows);
1101:}
1102:void printf_win(int win_id, const char *fmt, ...) {
1103:  char buf[512];
1104:  va_list args;
1105:  va_start(args, fmt);
1106:  vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args);
1107:  va_end(args);
1108:  _sys_window_write(win_id, buf, strlen(buf));
1109:}

1114:  va_end(args);

1133:int vasprintf(char **strp, const char *fmt, va_list ap) {
1134:  if (!strp || !fmt)
1135:    return -1;
1136:
1137:  va_list ap2;
1138:  va_copy(ap2, ap);
1139:  int needed = vsnprintf(NULL, 0, fmt, ap2);
1140:  va_end(ap2);
1141:  if (needed < 0)
1142:    return -1;
1143:
1144:  char *buf = malloc((size_t)needed + 1U);
1145:  if (!buf)
1146:    return -1;
1147:
1148:  int written = vsnprintf(buf, (size_t)needed + 1U, fmt, ap);
1149:  if (written < 0) {
1150:    free(buf);
1151:    return -1;
1152:  }
1153:
1154:  *strp = buf;
1155:  return written;
1156:}

1182:void print(const char *s) { write(1, s, strlen(s)); }
1183:/* print_hex: manual 16-nibble hex formatter for a 64-bit value. */
1184:void print_hex(unsigned long val) {
1185:  char buf[18];
1186:  buf[0] = '0';
1187:  buf[1] = 'x';
1188:  for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
1189:    int digit = (val >> ((15 - i) * 4)) & 0xF;
1190:    buf[2 + i] = (digit < 10) ? ('0' + digit) : ('A' + digit - 10);
1191:  }
1192:  write(1, buf, 18);
1193:}

1195:/* --- Standard IO ---
1196: * getchar: blocking single-char read from fd 0 (keyboard).
1197: * putchar: writes one character to fd 1 (TTY/window).
1198: * gets: line-buffered input with backspace handling; size-bounded to avoid
1199: *   overflow (stops at size-1 chars).  Echoes characters to fd 1 and handles
1200: *   \b/DEL with the terminal backspace-space-backspace sequence.
1201: */
1202:int getchar(void) {
1203:  char c;
1204:  if (read(0, &c, 1) == 1)
1205:    return (unsigned char)c;
1206:  return -1;
1207:}
1208:int putchar(int c) {
1209:  char ch = (char)c;
1210:  write(1, &ch, 1);
1211:  return c;
1212:}
1213:char *gets(char *s, int size) {
1214:  int i = 0;
1215:  while (i < size - 1) {
1216:    int c = getchar();
1217:    if (c < 0)
1218:      break;
1219:    if (c == '\b' || c == 127) {
1220:      if (i > 0) {
1221:        i--;
1222:        write(1, "\b \b", 3);
1223:      }
1224:      continue;
1225:    }
1226:    putchar(c);
1227:    if (c == '\n' || c == '\r') {
1228:      s[i] = '\0';
1229:      return s;
1230:    }
1231:    s[i++] = (char)c;
1232:  }
1233:  s[i] = '\0';
1234:  return s;
1235:}
