1237:/*
1238: * notify - send a system notification via IPC to the notification server.
1239: *
1240: * title: short label (up to 30 chars copied); truncated silently if longer.
1241: * msg:   message body (up to 33 remaining chars after "title: "); truncated.
1242: *
1243: * The payload is assembled as "title: msg\0" into imsg.payload[64].
1244: * The target PID is read from the global registry key "srv.notify_pid".
1245: * Falls back to PID 2 if the key is absent (pid=2 is the expected notify_srv
1246: * PID under the current fixed-order spawn sequence in init.c).
1247: *
1248: * NOTE(USR-SEC-01): registry_read("srv.notify_pid", ...) has no authentication;
1249: * any process can overwrite that key to redirect all notifications to itself,
1250: * effectively hijacking the system notification channel.
1251: *
1252: * Returns the result of send() (0 on success, negative on failure).
1253: */
1254:/* notify_send - post a notification with a severity (0=info, 1=warning/yellow,
1255: * 2=error/red) in data1, which nxntfy_srv renders as the popup colour. */
1256:static int notify_send(const char *title, const char *msg, int sev) {
1257:  struct ipc_message imsg;
1258:  imsg.type = IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY;
1259:  imsg.data1 = (uint64_t)sev;
1260:  imsg.data2 = 0;
1261:  int i = 0;
1262:  /* Pack "title: msg" into the 64-byte payload field.
1263:   * 30-char limit for title leaves room for ": " and at least 32 msg chars. */
1264:  while (*title && i < 30)
1265:    imsg.payload[i++] = *title++;
1266:  imsg.payload[i++] = ':';
1267:  imsg.payload[i++] = ' ';
1268:  while (*msg && i < 63)
1269:    imsg.payload[i++] = *msg++;
1270:  imsg.payload[i] = '\0';
1271:  /* Resolve the notify_srv endpoint from the registry. If the key is absent
1272:   * (notify_srv not up / not yet registered) FAIL instead of sending to a
1273:   * guessed PID — the old pid=2 fallback delivered a stray IPC message to
1274:   * whatever process happened to hold PID 2 and the notification was lost
1275:   * anyway. Callers that need the boot popup wait for the key (see init.c). */
1276:  char pid_buf[16];
1277:  if (OS1_registry_get("srv.notify_pid", pid_buf, sizeof(pid_buf)) != 0)
1278:    return -1;
1279:  int pid = atoi(pid_buf);
1280:  if (pid <= 0)
1281:    return -1;
1282:  return (int)OS1low_ipc_send(pid, &imsg);
1283:}
1284:int OS1_notify_post(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1285:  return notify_send(title, msg, 0);
1286:}
1287:int OS1_notify_warn(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1288:  return notify_send(title, msg, 1);
1289:} /* yellow */
1290:int OS1_notify_error(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1291:  return notify_send(title, msg, 2);
1292:} /* red — previously only the kernel crash handler (fault.c) could reach
1293:   * severity 2 (m.data1 = 2, kernel_ipc_send bypassing this function
1294:   * entirely); userland callers can now post one directly too. */
1295:int notify(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1296:  return notify_send(title, msg, 0);
1297:} /* compat shim (DIR-01 F4) */
1298:
1299:/* --- Doom/LibC Compatibility ---
1300: * FILE emulation: a FILE* is a heap-allocated struct (defined in os1.h) that
1301: * records the file path, current byte position, error/eof flags, and cached
1302: * size.  All I/O is synchronous and unbuffered; every fread/fwrite call maps
1303: * directly to a file_read/file_write syscall with the current offset.
1304: */
1305:
1306:/*
1307: * fopen - open a file for buffered I/O emulation.
1308: *
1309: * Allocates a FILE struct, stores the path, probes the file size via
1310: * file_read(path, NULL, 0, 0).  SIZE-PROBE CONVENTION: the trigger is
1311: * `size == 0` (NOT `buf == NULL`, which this comment used to claim — the
1312: * distinction matters because `buf == NULL` with a NON-zero size is an error,
1313: * -EFAULT, not a probe).  `offset` must be 0: a size has no offset, and passing
1314: * one is refused with -EINVAL rather than silently answered with the total.
1315: * Returns NULL if the file does not exist and mode is "r" (read-only).
1316: * Write modes ("w", "a") do not fail on missing files — file_write will
1317: * create them on demand via the kernel VFS.
1318: */
1319:FILE *fopen(const char *path, const char *mode) {
1320:  FILE *f = malloc(sizeof(FILE));
1321:  if (!f) {
1322:    errno = ENOMEM;
1323:    return NULL;
1324:  }
1325:  /* Zero EVERY field: malloc reuses dirty blocks, and a stale has_ungetc
1326:   * injected a ghost byte at the start of the first fread (doom read
1327:   * "\0IWA" instead of "IWAD" after its 9-file IWAD probe loop), while a
1328:   * stale is_tmp made fclose() unlink real files.  memset is the whole
1329:   * fix; pos/error/eof/has_ungetc/is_tmp start 0 by definition. */
1330:  memset(f, 0, sizeof(FILE));
1331:  f->fd = -1;
1332:  strncpy(f->path, path, sizeof(f->path) - 1);
1333:  /* Probe file size; file_read with NULL buf and size=0 returns byte count.
1334:   * On a miss it sets errno (ENOENT/EACCES) — preserved below so a failed
1335:   * fopen reports the real reason (luaL_fileresult/strerror), not "Success". */
1336:  f->size = file_read(path, NULL, 0, 0);
1337:  if (f->size < 0 && mode[0] == 'r') {
1338:    int e = errno;
1339:    free(f);
1340:    errno = e; /* free() must not mask the open failure's errno */
1341:    return NULL;
1342:  }
1343:  /* Write mode truncates to empty NOW (POSIX "w"): unlink + zero-byte create,
1344:   * so the file both exists and is emptied before any fwrite — the old lazy
1345:   * path left stale trailing bytes when overwriting a longer file. Append
1346:   * mode ("a") creates-if-missing and starts the position at EOF. */
1347:  if (mode[0] == 'w') {
1348:    /* Create-and-truncate in one call: a from-start write (offset 0) now
1349:     * truncates on the FS side (ext4_write), so a zero-byte write both
1350:     * materialises a missing file and empties an existing one — no unlink
1351:     * needed, and the inode (perms/links) is preserved instead of churned. */
1352:    if (OS1_fs_write(path, "", 0, 0) < 0) {
1353:      int e = errno;
1354:      free(f);
1355:      errno = e;
1356:      return NULL;
1357:    }
1358:    f->size = 0;
1359:  } else if (mode[0] == 'a') {
1360:    if (f->size < 0) {
1361:      if (OS1_fs_write(path, "", 0, 0) < 0) {
1362:        int e = errno;
1363:        free(f);
1364:        errno = e;
1365:        return NULL;
1366:      }
1367:      f->size = 0;
1368:    }
1369:    f->pos = f->size;
1370:  }
1371:
1372:  /*
1373:   * Open a REAL handle and keep it for the stream's lifetime.
1374:   *
1375:   * Before this, a path-backed FILE carried fd = -1 and EVERY fread/fwrite did
1376:   * handle_create + seek + read/write + close — four syscalls and, far worse, a
1377:   * full VFS PATH RESOLUTION per call.  doom reads a savegame a byte at a time
1378:   * (saveg_read8), so a ~100 KB save meant ~100 000 path resolutions: that is
1379:   * the multi-minute load, and it is the "positional per-byte fread through the
1380:   * FILE layer + handle-per-call" item the plan logged at 17d.
1381:   *
1382:   * Now the handle is opened once and the KERNEL owns the offset.  fread/fwrite
1383:   * are one syscall with no resolution; fseek moves the kernel offset with
1384:   * lseek.  fp->pos is kept as a mirror so ftell costs nothing.
1385:   *
1386:   * A failure here is NOT fatal: the stream falls back to the positional path
1387:   * (fd stays -1), which still works.  Losing speed is acceptable; losing the
1388:   * ability to open a file is not — and the write modes above have already
1389:   * created/truncated, so the file exists either way. */
1390:  {
1391:    int oflags;
1392:    if (mode[0] == 'r')
1393:      oflags =
1394:          (mode[1] == '+' || (mode[1] && mode[2] == '+')) ? O_RDWR : O_RDONLY;
1395:    else
1396:      oflags = O_RDWR; /* "w"/"a" already created+positioned above */
1397:    int h = open(path, oflags);
1398:    if (h >= 0) {
1399:      f->fd = h;
1400:      /* Align the kernel offset with the logical one ("a" starts at EOF). */
1401:      if (f->pos != 0)
1402:        lseek(h, f->pos, SEEK_SET);
1403:    }
1404:  }
1405:  return f;
1406:}
1407:
1408:FILE *freopen(const char *filename, const char *mode, FILE *stream) {
1409:  if (stream) {
1410:    fclose(stream);
1411:  }
1412:  return fopen(filename, mode);
1413:}
1414:
1415:static int file_fd(FILE *fp);
1416:
1417:/*
1418: * fstream_flush - write out the pending write buffer of a positional stream.
1419: *
1420: * The buffered bytes' on-disk offset is (pos - wcount): fwrite advances the
1421: * logical position as it accumulates, so the buffer start trails 'pos' by the
1422: * pending count.  A no-op for read streams and the console std streams, whose
1423: * wcount stays 0.  On a short/failed write the error flag is set.  Returns 0 on
1424: * success, EOF on error.
1425: */
1426:static int fstream_flush(FILE *fp) {
1427:  if (!fp || fp->wcount <= 0)
1428:    return 0;
1429:  int at = fp->pos - fp->wcount;
1430:  if (at < 0)
1431:    at = 0;
1432:  int pending = fp->wcount;
1433:  int w;
1434:  if (fp->fd >= 0) {
1435:    /* Flush through the stream's own handle: one syscall, no path resolution.
1436:     * lseek first because the buffer's on-disk offset trails the logical
1437:     * position by the pending count, and interleaved reads may have moved the
1438:     * kernel offset since. */
1439:    lseek(fp->fd, at, SEEK_SET);
1440:    long r = write(fp->fd, fp->wbuf, (unsigned long)pending);
1441:    w = (int)r;
1442:    if (r > 0)
1443:      lseek(fp->fd, fp->pos, SEEK_SET); /* restore the logical position */
1444:  } else {
1445:    w = file_write(fp->path, fp->wbuf, pending, at);
1446:  }
1447:  fp->wcount = 0;
1448:  /* The file just changed: any cached read window may now be stale. */
1449:  fp->rcount = 0;
1450:  fp->rhead = 0;
1451:  if (w < 0 || w < pending) {
1452:    fp->error = 1;
1453:    return EOF;
1454:  }
1455:  return 0;
1456:}
1457:
1458:/*
1459: * fclose - flush any pending writes, then release a FILE handle.
1460: */
1461:/*
1462: * fdopen - wrap an ALREADY-OPEN descriptor in a FILE* (POSIX).  The stream is
1463: * fd-backed: fread/fwrite go straight through read()/write() on that fd, so it
1464: * works for any object the descriptor names — a file, a console, or a PIPE end
1465: * (`int p[2]; pipe(p); FILE *f = fdopen(p[0], "r");`), which is the usual way
1466: * ported POSIX code consumes a pipe through stdio.  'mode' is accepted for
1467: * source compatibility; the descriptor's own rights are the real authority
1468: * (the kernel rejects a read of a write-only handle), so we do not re-derive
1469: * access from the string.  Returns NULL on a bad fd or out of memory.
1470: */
1471:FILE *fdopen(int fd, const char *mode) {
1472:  (void)mode;
1473:  if (fd < 0) {
1474:    errno = EBADF;
1475:    return 0;
1476:  }
1477:  FILE *f = malloc(sizeof(FILE));
1478:  if (!f) {
1479:    errno = ENOMEM;
1480:    return 0;
1481:  }
1482:  memset(f, 0, sizeof(FILE));
1483:  f->fd = fd;   /* fd-backed: file_fd() routes I/O through read()/write() */
1484:  f->size = -1; /* unknown until asked */
1485:  return f;
1486:}
1487:
1488:int fclose(FILE *fp) {
1489:  if (fp && fp != stdin && fp != stdout && fp != stderr) {
1490:    fstream_flush(fp);
1491:    if (fp->is_tmp) {
1492:      OS1_fs_unlink(fp->path);
1493:    }
1494:    /* The stream owns its descriptor (POSIX): closing the stream closes it.
1495:     * This now covers fopen'd streams too — they hold a real handle for their
1496:     * lifetime instead of reopening per call — as well as fdopen'd ones.  A
1497:     * stream whose open failed carries fd = -1 and owns nothing. */
1498:    if (fp->fd >= 0)
1499:      close(fp->fd);
1500:    free(fp);
1501:  }
1502:  return 0;
1503:}
1504:
1505:size_t fread(void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *fp) {
1506:  if (!fp)
1507:    return 0;
1508:  if (size == 0 || nmemb == 0)
1509:    return 0;
1510:
1511:  /* Read-after-write consistency: persist any buffered writes before reading
1512:   * so an interleaved read at this position sees them on disk. */
1513:  fstream_flush(fp);
1514:
1515:  size_t bytes = size * nmemb;
1516:  char *buf = (char *)ptr;
1517:  size_t read_bytes = 0;
1518:
1519:  if (fp->has_ungetc) {
1520:    buf[0] = (char)fp->ungetc_buf;
1521:    fp->has_ungetc = 0;
1522:    read_bytes = 1;
1523:    if (bytes == 1) {
1524:      return 1 / size;
1525:    }
1526:  }
1527:
1528:  int fd = file_fd(fp);
1529:  if (fd >= 0 && fp->path[0] == '\0') {
1530:    /* Console/pipe: unbuffered, and never seekable. */
1531:    long r = read(fd, buf + read_bytes, bytes - read_bytes);
1532:    if (r < 0) {
1533:      fp->error = 1;
1534:      return 0;
1535:    }
1536:    fp->pos += (int)r;
1537:    if (r == 0 && bytes > read_bytes)
1538:      fp->eof = 1;
1539:    read_bytes += r;
1540:    return read_bytes / size;
1541:  }
1542:  if (fd >= 0) {
1543:    /*
1544:     * BUFFERED read for a file stream, symmetric with the write buffer and for
1545:     * the same filesystem reason: ext4 fetches a whole 4 KiB block for any
1546:     * partial read, so an unbuffered byte-at-a-time reader re-reads the same
1547:     * block once per byte.  doom loads savegames exactly that way — that is
1548:     * the multi-minute load, and buffering is what removes it, not the handle
1549:     * cache alone.
1550:     */
1551:    while (read_bytes < bytes) {
1552:      if (fp->rhead >= fp->rcount) { /* window exhausted: refill from pos */
1553:        fp->rbase = fp->pos;
1554:        fp->rhead = 0;
1555:        fp->rcount = 0;
1556:        lseek(fd, fp->pos, SEEK_SET);
1557:        long r = read(fd, fp->rbuf, FILE_RBUF_SIZE);
1558:        if (r < 0) {
1559:          fp->error = 1;
1560:          break;
1561:        }
1562:        if (r == 0) {
1563:          fp->eof = 1;
1564:          break;
1565:        }
1566:        fp->rcount = (int)r;
1567:      }
1568:      size_t avail = (size_t)(fp->rcount - fp->rhead);
1569:      size_t want = bytes - read_bytes;
1570:      size_t take = avail < want ? avail : want;
1571:      memcpy(buf + read_bytes, fp->rbuf + fp->rhead, take);
1572:      fp->rhead += (int)take;
1573:      fp->pos += (int)take;
1574:      read_bytes += take;
1575:    }
1576:    return read_bytes / size;
1577:  }
1578:  int rem_bytes = bytes - read_bytes;
1579:  int r = file_read(fp->path, buf + read_bytes, rem_bytes, fp->pos);
1580:  if (r < 0) {
1581:    fp->error = 1;
1582:    return 0;
1583:  }
1584:  fp->pos += r;
1585:  read_bytes += r;
1586:  if (r < rem_bytes)
1587:    fp->eof = 1;
1588:  return read_bytes / size;
1589:}
1590:
1591:size_t fwrite(const void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *fp) {
1592:  if (!fp)
1593:    return 0;
1594:  if (size == 0 || nmemb == 0)
1595:    return 0;
1596:
1597:  /* Write-after-read consistency, the mirror of the flush fread() does before
1598:   * reading.  The cached read window may cover the bytes about to change, and
1599:   * rhead does not move when a write advances pos — so a read following a write
1600:   * would otherwise be served stale bytes from the OLD position.  Dropping the
1601:   * window costs one refill and removes the whole hazard. */
1602:  fp->rcount = 0;
1603:  fp->rhead = 0;
1604:
1605:  size_t bytes = size * nmemb;
1606:  int fd = file_fd(fp);
1607:  /* CONSOLE/pipe streams only (no path): unbuffered, because interactive output
1608:   * must appear now.  A FILE-backed stream must NOT take this branch even
1609:   * though it now has an fd — buffering is not about syscall count here, it is
1610:   * about the FILESYSTEM: ext4_write does a read-modify-write of a whole 4 KiB
1611:   * block for any partial write, so an unbuffered byte-at-a-time writer costs
1612:   * one 4 KiB read + 4 KiB write PER BYTE.  doom saves exactly that way, and
1613:   * bypassing the buffer made saving look like a hang.  FILE_WBUF_SIZE is 4096
1614:   * precisely so a full buffer is one whole block. */
1615:  if (fd >= 0 && fp->path[0] == '\0') {
1616:    long w = write(fd, ptr, bytes);
1617:    if (w < 0) {
1618:      fp->error = 1;
1619:      return 0;
1620:    }
1621:    fp->pos += (int)w;
1622:    if (fp->pos > fp->size)
1623:      fp->size = fp->pos;
1624:    return w / size;
1625:  }
1626:
1627:  /* Positional (path-backed) stream: coalesce into the write buffer, flushing a
1628:   * full buffer to one file_write syscall.  This turns a per-byte/per-field
1629:   * fwrite loop into one syscall per FILE_WBUF_SIZE, which is what standard C
1630:   * stdio buffering does — the fix for incremental writers stalling on a
1631:   * syscall-per-call storm. */
1632:  const unsigned char *src = (const unsigned char *)ptr;
1633:  size_t done = 0;
1634:  while (done < bytes) {
1635:    if (fp->wcount == FILE_WBUF_SIZE && fstream_flush(fp) != 0)
1636:      break; /* flush failed: fp->error set, report the partial count */
1637:    int room = FILE_WBUF_SIZE - fp->wcount;
1638:    size_t chunk = bytes - done;
1639:    if (chunk > (size_t)room)
1640:      chunk = (size_t)room;
1641:    memcpy(fp->wbuf + fp->wcount, src + done, chunk);
1642:    fp->wcount += (int)chunk;
1643:    fp->pos += (int)chunk;
1644:    done += chunk;
1645:  }
1646:  return done / size;
1647:}
1648:
1649:int fseek(FILE *fp, long offset, int whence) {
1650:  if (!fp)
1651:    return -1;
1652:  /* Persist pending writes before the position moves: the buffer's on-disk
1653:   * offset is derived from the current pos, so it must be flushed here. */
1654:  fstream_flush(fp);
1655:  if (whence == SEEK_SET)
1656:    fp->pos = offset;
1657:  else if (whence == SEEK_CUR)
1658:    fp->pos += offset;
1659:  else if (whence == SEEK_END) {
1660:    if (fp->size < 0)
1661:      fp->size = file_read(fp->path, NULL, 0, 0);
1662:    fp->pos = fp->size + offset;
1663:  }
1664:  if (fp->pos < 0)
1665:    fp->pos = 0;
1666:  /* POSIX: "a successful call to fseek() shall undo any effects of ungetc()".
1667:   * The pushback byte belongs to the OLD position, so carrying it across a seek
1668:   * would inject a stray byte at the new one.  Latent before — the positional
1669:   * path re-read from the file every time — and made reachable by the read
1670:   * window, which is exactly the kind of dormant deviation a buffer exposes. */
1671:  fp->has_ungetc = 0;
1672:  /* A handle-backed stream keeps its offset in the KERNEL, so moving the
1673:   * logical position must move that too — otherwise fread would keep reading
1674:   * from wherever the last read left off and silently ignore the seek.  Only
1675:   * for path-backed streams: seeking a console/pipe is meaningless, and those
1676:   * carry no path. */
1677:  if (fp->fd >= 0 && fp->path[0]) {
1678:    /* Keep the read window if it still covers the new position — a savegame
1679:     * reader that seeks backwards a few bytes then continues would otherwise
1680:     * refill on every seek and lose the buffering entirely.  Otherwise drop
1681:     * it; a stale window would serve bytes from the OLD offset. */
1682:    if (fp->rcount > 0 && fp->pos >= fp->rbase &&
1683:        fp->pos < fp->rbase + fp->rcount) {
1684:      fp->rhead = fp->pos - fp->rbase;
1685:    } else {
1686:      fp->rcount = 0;
1687:      fp->rhead = 0;
1688:    }
1689:    lseek(fp->fd, fp->pos, SEEK_SET);
1690:  }
1691:  fp->eof = 0;
1692:  return 0;
1693:}
1694:
1695:long ftell(FILE *fp) {
1696:  if (!fp)
1697:    return -1;
1698:  /* pos already includes buffered-but-unflushed bytes (fwrite advances it as it
1699:   * accumulates), so this is the correct logical position. */
1700:  return fp->pos;
1701:}

1704:  return fseek(fp, (long)offset, whence);

1707:off_t ftello(FILE *fp) {
1708:  return (off_t)ftell(fp);

1718:  size_t len = strlen(s) + 1;

1721:    memcpy(res, s, len);

1725:char *strndup(const char *s, size_t n) {
1726:  if (!s)
1727:    return NULL;
1728:  size_t len = 0;
1729:  while (len < n && s[len])
1730:    len++;
1731:  char *res = malloc(len + 1);
1732:  if (res) {
1733:    memcpy(res, s, len);
1734:    res[len] = '\0';
1735:  }
1736:  return res;
1737:}

1742:/* --- Standard Input Library ---
1743: * Input events are delivered as IPC messages from the kernel input driver.
1744: * IPC_TYPE_INPUT carries keyboard data; IPC_TYPE_MOUSE carries mouse data.
1745: * Both are received non-blocking via try_recv(-1, ...) — poll any sender.
1746: */
1747:
1748:/*
1749: * input_poll_event - check for and decode the next pending input event.
1750: *
1751: * event: output parameter filled on success.
1752: *
1753: * Returns 1 if an event was decoded (event is valid), 0 if no message was
1754: * waiting or the message type is not a recognised input type.
1755: *
1756: * IPC_TYPE_INPUT layout (data1/data2/payload):
1757: *   data1 low byte : ASCII key code (keyboard.key)
1758: *   data1 bits 16+ : HID scancode   (keyboard.scancode)
1759: *   data2           : key state (0=released, 1=pressed, 2=repeat)
1760: *   payload[0..7]  : UTF-8 encoded character (up to 4 bytes + NUL)
1761: *
1762: * IPC_TYPE_MOUSE layout:
1763: *   data1  : button mask
1764: *   data2  : button state (pressed=1)
1765: *   payload[0..3]  : x coordinate (int32, little-endian)
1766: *   payload[4..7]  : y coordinate (int32, little-endian)
1767: *
1768: * Note: memcpy is used for mouse coordinates to handle potential alignment
1769: * constraints on the int fields within the packed payload array.
1770: */
1771:int input_poll_event(input_event_t *event) {
1772:  struct ipc_message msg;
1773:  if (try_recv(-1, &msg) < 0)
1774:    return 0;
1775:
1776:  if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_INPUT) {
1777:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD;
1778:    event->keyboard.key = (unsigned char)(msg.data1 & 0xFF);
1779:    event->keyboard.scancode = (uint16_t)(msg.data1 >> 16);
1780:    event->keyboard.state = (int)msg.data2;
1781:    memcpy(event->keyboard.utf8, msg.payload, 8);
1782:    return 1;
1783:  } else if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_MOUSE) {
1784:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE;
1785:    event->mouse.button = (int)msg.data1;
1786:    event->mouse.state = (int)msg.data2;
1787:    memcpy(&event->mouse.x, msg.payload, 4);
1788:    memcpy(&event->mouse.y, msg.payload + 4, 4);
1789:    return 1;
1790:  } else if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_RESIZE) {
1791:    /* GFX-DYN-01: the compositor told us our window's new logical size. */
1792:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE;
1793:    event->resize.w = (int)msg.data1;
1794:    event->resize.h = (int)msg.data2;
1795:    return 1;
1796:  } else if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY && msg.data2 == IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC) {
1797:    /* Silent compositor look-changed ping (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h),
1798:     * tagged via data2 so it is never confused with a real notify() call.
1799:     * Surfaced here (not drained by a second, competing try_recv() loop
1800:     * elsewhere) so this stays the single consumer of the mailbox — a
1801:     * second loop would silently steal keyboard/mouse messages before this
1802:     * function ever saw them. */
1803:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED;
1804:    return 1;
1805:  }
1806:  return 0;
1807:}

1874:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_FILE_BYTES (16u * 1024u * 1024u)
1875:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION 4096
1876:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS (4096u * 4096u)

1878:/*
1879: * graphics_load_image - load an encoded image into sanitized ARGB32 pixels.
1880: *
1881: * Encoded input is treated as hostile data: it is copied into a bounded scratch
1882: * buffer, probed before decode, rejected on dimension/pixel/file caps, decoded
1883: * to a temporary RGBA plane, then copied into an OS1-owned ARGB buffer.  The
1884: * caller never sees encoded bytes or decoder-owned storage, which keeps image
1885: * rendering an inert pixel operation suitable for the stdimage base API.
1886: */
1887:uint32_t *graphics_load_image(const char *path, int *w, int *h) {
1888:  if (!path || !w || !h)
1889:    return NULL;
1890:
1891:  *w = 0;
1892:  *h = 0;
1893:
1894:  long handle =
1895:      OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
1896:  if (handle < 0)
1897:    return NULL;
1898:
1899:  long stat_size = OS1_object_ctl((int)handle, OBJ_CTL_STAT, 0);
1900:  if (stat_size <= 0 || (uint64_t)stat_size > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_FILE_BYTES) {
1901:    OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
1902:    return NULL;
1903:  }
1904:
1905:  int size = (int)stat_size;
1906:  unsigned char *data = malloc((size_t)size + 16u);
1907:  if (!data) {
1908:    OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
1909:    return NULL;
1910:  }
1911:
1912:  int total = 0;
1913:  while (total < size) {
1914:    long got = OS1_object_read((int)handle, data + total,
1915:                               (unsigned long)(size - total));
1916:    if (got <= 0) {
1917:      OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
1918:      free(data);
1919:      return NULL;
1920:    }
1921:    total += (int)got;
1922:  }
1923:  OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
1924:
1925:  if (total != size) {
1926:    free(data);
1927:    return NULL;
1928:  }
1929:  for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
1930:    data[size + i] = 0;
1931:
1932:  int iw = 0;
1933:  int ih = 0;
1934:  int channels = 0;
1935:  if (!stbi_info_from_memory(data, size, &iw, &ih, &channels)) {
1936:    free(data);
1937:    return NULL;
1938:  }
1939:  if (iw <= 0 || ih <= 0 || iw > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION ||
1940:      ih > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION ||
1941:      (uint64_t)iw * (uint64_t)ih > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS) {
1942:    free(data);
1943:    return NULL;
1944:  }
1945:
1946:  int n = 0;
1947:  unsigned char *rgba = stbi_load_from_memory(data, size, &iw, &ih, &n, 4);
1948:  free(data);
1949:  if (!rgba)
1950:    return NULL;
1951:
1952:  uint64_t pixels = (uint64_t)iw * (uint64_t)ih;
1953:  if (pixels > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS || pixels > ((uint64_t)SIZE_MAX / 4u)) {
1954:    stbi_image_free(rgba);
1955:    return NULL;
1956:  }
1957:
1958:  uint32_t *argb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)pixels * 4u);
1959:  if (!argb) {
1960:    stbi_image_free(rgba);
1961:    return NULL;
1962:  }
1963:
1964:  for (uint64_t i = 0; i < pixels; i++) {
1965:    uint8_t r = rgba[i * 4u + 0u];
1966:    uint8_t g = rgba[i * 4u + 1u];
1967:    uint8_t b = rgba[i * 4u + 2u];
1968:    uint8_t a = rgba[i * 4u + 3u];
1969:    argb[i] = ((uint32_t)a << 24) | ((uint32_t)r << 16) | ((uint32_t)g << 8) |
1970:              (uint32_t)b;
1971:  }
1972:
1973:  stbi_image_free(rgba);
1974:  *w = iw;
1975:  *h = ih;
1976:  return argb;
1977:}
1978:
1979:/*
1980: * strtol - convert string to long integer with base and endptr support.
1981: *
1982: * Handles leading whitespace, optional sign, 0x/0 prefixes for base
1983: * auto-detection (base==0), and digits up to the given base.
1984: * Sets *endptr to the first non-consumed character if endptr != NULL.
1985: * Does not detect overflow (val accumulates without range check).
1986: * Negative values are produced by negating the unsigned accumulator,
1987: * which gives correct two's-complement representation for LONG_MIN.
1988: */
1989:long strtol(const char *nptr, char **endptr, int base) {
1990:  const char *p = nptr;
1991:  while (isspace(*p))
1992:    p++;
1993:  int neg = 0;
1994:  if (*p == '-') {
1995:    neg = 1;
1996:    p++;
1997:  } else if (*p == '+')
1998:    p++;
1999:
2000:  /* Auto-detect base from prefix: "0x" -> 16, "0" -> 8, else 10. */
2001:  if (base == 0) {
2002:    if (*p == '0') {
2003:      if (p[1] == 'x' || p[1] == 'X')
2004:        base = 16;
2005:      else
2006:        base = 8;
2007:    } else
2008:      base = 10;
2009:  }
2010:
2011:  if (base == 16 && p[0] == '0' && (p[1] == 'x' || p[1] == 'X'))
2012:    p += 2;
2013:
2014:  unsigned long val = 0;
2015:  while (1) {
2016:    int digit;
2017:    if (isdigit(*p))
2018:      digit = *p - '0';
2019:    else if (isalpha(*p))
2020:      digit = tolower(*p) - 'a' + 10;
2021:    else
2022:      break;
2023:
2024:    if (digit >= base)
2025:      break;
2026:    val = val * base + digit;
2027:    p++;
2028:  }
2029:
2030:  if (endptr)
2031:    *endptr = (char *)p;
2032:  return neg ? -(long)val : (long)val;
2033:}

2039: */
2040:int sscanf(const char *str, const char *format, ...) {
2041:  va_list args;

2043:  int res = vsscanf(str, format, args);
2044:  va_end(args);
2045:  return res;
2046:}

2048:/*
2049: * vsscanf - simplified format scanner supporting %d, %x/%X, %s with widths.
2050: *
2051: * Supports:
2052: *   %d  - signed decimal integer -> int *
2053: *   %x, %X - unsigned hex integer -> unsigned int *; skips optional 0x prefix
2054: *   %s  - whitespace-delimited string; width limits chars consumed
2055: *
2056: * Whitespace in the format string matches zero or more whitespace chars in
2057: * the input.  Literal format characters must match exactly (returns early on
2058: * mismatch).  Returns the count of successfully assigned conversions.
2059: *
2060: * Missing specifiers: %f, %c, %ld, %u, %p, etc.  Callers using unsupported
2061: * format specifiers will silently skip the conversion.
2062: */
2063:int vsscanf(const char *inp, const char *fmt0, va_list ap) {
2064:  int nassigned = 0;
2065:  const unsigned char *fmt = (const unsigned char *)fmt0;
2066:  const char *p_inp = inp;
2067:
2068:  while (*fmt) {
2069:    if (isspace(*fmt)) {
2070:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2071:        p_inp++;
2072:      fmt++;
2073:      continue;
2074:    }
2075:    if (*fmt != '%') {
2076:      if (*p_inp != *fmt)
2077:        return nassigned;
2078:      p_inp++;
2079:      fmt++;
2080:      continue;
2081:    }
2082:    fmt++; /* skip % */
2083:    /* Parse optional field width */
2084:    int width = 0;
2085:    while (isdigit(*fmt)) {
2086:      width = width * 10 + (*fmt - '0');
2087:      fmt++;
2088:    }
2089:
2090:    char c = *fmt++;
2091:    if (c == 'd') {
2092:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2093:        p_inp++;
2094:      int *res = va_arg(ap, int *);
2095:      *res = atoi(p_inp);
2096:      nassigned++;
2097:      while (isdigit(*p_inp) || *p_inp == '-')
2098:        p_inp++;
2099:    } else if (c == 'x' || c == 'X') {
2100:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2101:        p_inp++;
2102:      unsigned int *res = va_arg(ap, unsigned int *);
2103:      unsigned int val = 0;
2104:      if (p_inp[0] == '0' && (p_inp[1] == 'x' || p_inp[1] == 'X'))
2105:        p_inp += 2;
2106:      while (isxdigit(*p_inp)) {
2107:        char dc = *p_inp++;
2108:        if (isdigit(dc))
2109:          val = (val << 4) | (dc - '0');
2110:        else
2111:          val = (val << 4) | (tolower(dc) - 'a' + 10);
2112:      }
2113:      *res = val;
2114:      nassigned++;
2115:    } else if (c == 's') {
2116:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2117:        p_inp++;
2118:      char *res = va_arg(ap, char *);
2119:      while (*p_inp && !isspace(*p_inp)) {
2120:        *res++ = *p_inp++;
2121:        if (width > 0 && --width == 0)
2122:          break;
2123:      }
2124:      *res = '\0';
2125:      nassigned++;
2126:    }
2127:    /* NOTE(USR-LIB-04): Other format specifiers (%f, %c, %ld, %u, etc.) are
2128:     * silently skipped; the corresponding va_arg is NOT consumed, which may
2129:     * desync the va_list for subsequent conversions. */
2130:  }
2131:  return nassigned;
2132:}
2133:
2134:/* NOTE(USR-LIB-04): system/getenv are still no-op stubs; atof truncates
2135: * decimal fractions by delegating to atoi() and casting, so "3.14" -> 3.0.
2136: * mkdir is no longer a stub — it composes over a parent directory capability.
2137: */
2138:/* mkdir - create a directory through its parent directory capability. The
2139: * POSIX mode argument is accepted but not yet applied (the ext4 driver fixes
2140: * new directories at 0755); returns 0 on success, -1 on error (path exists,
2141: * not permitted, or provider failure), matching the POSIX contract. */
2142:int mkdir(const char *path, mode_t mode) {
2143:  (void)mode;
2144:  if (!path) {
2145:    errno = EFAULT;
2146:    return -1;
2147:  }
2148:  /* EXT4-ERRNO-01 (userland half): this returned a bare -1 without touching
2149:   * errno, so a caller doing the POSIX thing — check -1, then read errno —
2150:   * read whatever a PREVIOUS call had left there.  A stale errno is worse than
2151:   * none: it is indistinguishable from a fresh one.  Routed through
2152:   * errno_ret() like every other syscall veneer. */
2153:  return (int)errno_ret_ctx(OS1_fs_mkdir(path), path);
2154:}
2155:/*
2156: * system - run a shell command and wait for it (<stdlib.h>).
2157: *
2158: * FIX(USR-LIB-04): this used to unconditionally return 0. That silently
2159: * broke two separate contracts real POSIX-shaped code relies on:
2160: *
2161: *   1. system(NULL) must return non-zero IFF a command processor exists.
2162: *      Lua's os.execute() with no argument is exactly this check (e.g.
2163: *      `assert(os.execute())` in the Lua test suite reads "0" as "no
2164: *      shell available" and fails, even though NXShell is right there).
2165: *   2. system(cmd) must actually run cmd and hand back its real exit
2166: *      status, so os.execute(cmd)/os.execute(cmd) callers get true
2167: *      success/failure instead of a hardcoded fake "it worked".
2168: *
2169: * NOTE: NXSHELL_PATH and the "-c" argv convention below are the standard
2170: * Unix shell invocation shape (`sh -c "cmd"`). Adjust NXSHELL_PATH (and the
2171: * argv construction, if NXShell parses its command-line differently) to
2172: * match the actual shell binary shipped on this system.
2173: */
2174:#define NXSHELL_PATH "/sys/bin/nxshell"
2175:
2176:int system(const char *command) {
2177:  if (command == NULL) {
2178:    return 1; /* POSIX: non-zero only if a command processor exists.
2179:               * NXShell is available. */
2180:  }
2181:
2182:  char *argv[4];
2183:  argv[0] = (char *)NXSHELL_PATH;
2184:  argv[1] = (char *)"-c";
2185:  argv[2] = (char *)command;
2186:  argv[3] = NULL;
2187:
2188:  /* Phase 9c HELD AT THE GATE (2026-07-23) — the in-process path is the one
2189:   * that runs, and the reason is the migration rule this phase set for itself.
2190:   *
2191:   * DESIGN-2026-07-18-NXEXEC-DAEMON §6 step 3: route a caller through the
2192:   * service "keeping the in-process path behind a fallback UNTIL the suite is
2193:   * at least as green as before".  It was not.  A child created by the service
2194:   * inherits its per-process attributes from the SERVICE, and two of the three
2195:   * were simply wrong:
2196:   *
2197:   *   cwd  — FIXED: the request now carries the requester's cwd and the
2198:   *          service adopts it around the spawn (execsvc_client.c, nxexec.c).
2199:   *          It was being parsed and discarded.
2200:   *   ctty — NOT FIXED, and NOT fixable here.  sys_write resolves stdout to
2201:   *          the writer's own window, else its ctty_win (kernel/core/object.c).
2202:   *          The service has no window and no ctty, so every child it creates
2203:   *          gets ctty_win = -1 and its output goes NOWHERE.  fd redirection
2204:   *          cannot patch this: the destination comes from the process, not
2205:   *          from the handle.
2206:   *   env  — plan stall S1, same shape, already owned.
2207:   *
2208:   * Carrying ctty needs the spawn itself to carry it, which is Phase 9d — and
2209:   * 9d is gated by Phase 16.  Inventing a second mechanism for it now (a
2210:   * post-spawn ctty verb, or hanging it off OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER) is exactly the
2211:   * duplicate-mechanism mistake the plan already recorded and withdrew when it
2212:   * deleted 17b.  So the routing waits for the ONE mechanism instead.
2213:   *
2214:   * execsvc_spawn() is NOT dead: captest exercises the protocol directly
2215:   * ("exec service" section), so the daemon stays verified while it is off the
2216:   * POSIX critical path.  Re-enable here — and nowhere else — once 9d lands. */
2217:  int pid = spawn_args(NXSHELL_PATH, 3, argv);
2218:  if (pid < 0) {
2219:    errno = ENOENT;
2220:    return -1;
2221:  }
2222:
2223:  /* Blocking join through polling, using the same pattern as
2224:   * nxexec_run_foreground():
2225:   * wait() is non-blocking (-1 = still running / pid reaped / -2 = not
2226:   * found), so it must be queried in a loop until it no longer reports
2227:   * "running" — not called only once like before (that single -1 result
2228:   * was interpreted as ECHILD, causing system() to fail almost every time). */
2229:  int w, code = 0;
2230:  while ((w = OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code)) == -1)
2231:    OS1_sleep(15);
2232:
2233:  /* POSIX system() status word: WEXITSTATUS reads (status>>8)&0xff (Phase 2).
2234:   * A -2 "reaped elsewhere" leaves code 0 — the command still ran. */
2235:  (void)w;
2236:  return __wait_encode(code);
2237:}
2238:
2239:/*
2240: * waitpid - POSIX <sys/wait.h> wait (Phase 2).  Was declared but never
2241: * defined (an undefined-symbol trap for ported code).  Backed by the PROCESS
2242: * capability wait; fills *status with the POSIX-encoded exit code.  WNOHANG is
2243: * a single non-blocking poll; other options (WUNTRACED) are ignored (no
2244: * stopped-process state yet — a Phase 2 follow-up).
2245: */
2246:int waitpid(int pid, int *status, int options) {
2247:  int code = 0, w;
2248:  if (options & WNOHANG) {
2249:    w = OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code);
2250:    if (w == -1)
2251:      return 0; /* still running */
2252:    if (w == -2) {
2253:      errno = ECHILD;
2254:      return -1;
2255:    }
2256:    if (status)
2257:      *status = __wait_encode(code);
2258:    return pid;
2259:  }
2260:  while ((w = OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code)) == -1)
2261:    OS1_sleep(15);
2262:  if (w == -2) {
2263:    errno = ECHILD;
2264:    return -1;
2265:  }
2266:  if (status)
2267:    *status = __wait_encode(code);
2268:  return pid;
2269:}
2270:
2271:/*
2272: * cmdline_split - split a command line into argv[], honoring quotes.
2273: *
2274: * THE shared command tokenizer (used by nxshell for both interactive input
2275: * and `nxshell -c "<cmd>"`, which is how system()/Lua os.execute() reach a
2276: * program).  Whitespace separates words EXCEPT inside a '...' or "..." span,
2277: * which is kept as one token with its surrounding quotes REMOVED — so a
2278: * shell-style quoted program name like "lua" resolves to lua (not the
2279: * literal /bin/"lua" that broke os.execute), and a quoted argument that
2280: * contains spaces (Lua's `lua -e "a = 1"`) survives as a single argv entry.
2281: * A backslash inside a double-quoted span escapes a following '"' or '\'.
2282: *
2283: * Tokens are compacted IN PLACE inside s (out <= s always, so writing the
2284: * NUL terminators never clobbers a not-yet-scanned token).  Returns argc;
2285: * each argv[i] points into s.  Matches the previous whitespace-only splitter
2286: * when no quotes are present.
2287: */
2288:int cmdline_split(char *s, char **argv, int max) {
2289:  int argc = 0;
2290:  if (!s || !argv || max <= 0)
2291:    return 0;
2292:  while (*s && argc < max) {
2293:    while (*s == ' ' || *s == '\t')
2294:      s++;
2295:    if (!*s)
2296:      break;
2297:    char *out = s;
2298:    argv[argc++] = out;
2299:    while (*s && *s != ' ' && *s != '\t') {
2300:      char c = *s;
2301:      if (c == '"' || c == '\'') {
2302:        char q = c;
2303:        s++;
2304:        while (*s && *s != q) {
2305:          if (q == '"' && *s == '\\' && (s[1] == '"' || s[1] == '\\'))
2306:            s++; /* consume the backslash, copy the escaped char verbatim */
2307:          *out++ = *s++;
2308:        }
2309:        if (*s == q)
2310:          s++; /* consume the closing quote */
2311:      } else {
2312:        *out++ = *s++;
2313:      }
2314:    }
2315:    if (*s)
2316:      s++;       /* step past the delimiter for the next scan */
2317:    *out = '\0'; /* terminate the compacted token (out <= s) */
2318:  }
2319:  return argc;
2320:}
2321:/* atof: NOTE(USR-LIB-04) only integer part is parsed; decimal digits ignored.
2322: */
2323:/* atof: real IEEE-754 float parse via strtod (math.c) */
2324:double atof(const char *nptr) { return strtod(nptr, NULL); }
2325:/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
2326: * ENVIRONMENT — Phase 17
2327: *
2328: * TWO LAYERS, because ASTRA §6.8 and this plan's opening rule both require it:
2329: * the kernel is NOT POSIX; POSIX is a personality built ON TOP of OS1.
2330: *
2331: *   OS1_env_*   the NATIVE surface.  Owns the one fact that the kernel exposes
2332: *               the environment through the `sys.proc.<pid>.env.*` registry
2333: *               namespace, with `sys.env.*` beneath it as machine defaults.
2334: *   getenv/...  the POSIX personality: a THIN mapping over OS1_env_*, with no
2335: *               knowledge of the registry whatsoever.
2336: *
2337: * The first cut of this phase collapsed the two — POSIX built registry key
2338: * strings itself — which put the registry's path syntax into the POSIX API and
2339: * led to setenv() rejecting any name containing a '.'.  That restriction was
2340: * never real: the kernel's virtual-key router hands everything after "env." to
2341: * the scheduler as one opaque name, so dots always worked.  It was a limit
2342: * invented to serve a layering mistake.
2343: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
2344:
2345:#define OS1_ENV_KEYMAX 96
2346:
2347:/* env_self - our own pid, resolved once.
2348: *
2349: * getpid() is a syscall, and every env operation needs the pid to name its own
2350: * branch of the namespace — so the naive form costs TWO syscalls per getenv(),
2351: * on a function that path resolution calls per spawn.  A process's pid never
2352: * changes (pids come from a monotonic counter and there is no fork), so the
2353: * value is cacheable without an invalidation story. */
2354:static int env_self(void) {
2355:  static int self_pid;
2356:  if (self_pid <= 0)
2357:    self_pid = getpid();
2358:  return self_pid;
2359:}
2360:
2361:/* env_key - build the per-process namespace path.  The ONLY place in userland
2362: * that knows this syntax. */
2363:static int env_key(char *out, size_t size, const char *name) {
2364:  if (!name || !*name || strchr(name, '='))
2365:    return -1; /* POSIX: '=' separates name from value, so it cannot be in one
2366:                */
2367:  return (snprintf(out, size, "sys.proc.%d.env.%s", env_self(), name) > 0) ? 0
2368:                                                                           : -1;
2369:}
2370:
2371:int OS1_env_get(const char *name, char *buf, size_t size) {
2372:  char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2373:  if (!buf || size == 0 || env_key(key, sizeof(key), name) != 0)
2374:    return -1;
2375:  /* Process value first: it SHADOWS the machine default, which is the whole
2376:   * point of having both layers. */
2377:  if (OS1_registry_get(key, buf, size) == 0)
2378:    return 0;
2379:  if (snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "sys.env.%s", name) <= 0)
2380:    return -1;
2381:  if (OS1_registry_get(key, buf, size) == 0 && buf[0])
2382:    return 0;
2383:  return -1;
2384:}
2385:
2386:int OS1_env_set(const char *name, const char *value) {
2387:  char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2388:  if (env_key(key, sizeof(key), name) != 0)
2389:    return -1;
2390:  /* Writes always land on the PROCESS layer, never on sys.env.*: a program
2391:   * calling setenv means "for me and my children", not "reconfigure the
2392:   * machine".  Keeping that distinction here is why setenv needs no privilege
2393:   * while editing the defaults still does. */
2394:  return OS1_registry_set(key, value ? value : "") == 0 ? 0 : -1;
2395:}
2396:
2397:int OS1_env_unset(const char *name) {
2398:  char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2399:  if (env_key(key, sizeof(key), name) != 0)
2400:    return -1;
2401:  OS1_registry_del(key); /* DEL and set-to-empty both clear the slot */
2402:  return 0;
2403:}
2404:
2405:int OS1_env_enum(char *buf, size_t size) {
2406:  char prefix[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2407:  if (!buf || size == 0)
2408:    return -1;
2409:  if (snprintf(prefix, sizeof(prefix), "sys.proc.%d.env.", env_self()) <= 0)
2410:    return -1;
2411:  int n = OS1_registry_enum_under(prefix, buf, size - 1);
2412:  if (n <= 0) {
2413:    buf[0] = '\0';
2414:    return 0;
2415:  }
2416:  buf[n] = '\0';
2417:  /* Enumeration returns FULL keys; strip the namespace so callers above this
2418:   * layer never see it.  Rewrites in place, line by line. */
2419:  size_t plen = strlen(prefix);
2420:  char *w = buf;
2421:  for (char *r = buf; *r;) {
2422:    char *nl = strchr(r, '\n');
2423:    size_t len = nl ? (size_t)(nl - r) : strlen(r);
2424:    const char *nm =
2425:        (len > plen && strncmp(r, prefix, plen) == 0) ? r + plen : r;
2426:    size_t nlen = len - (size_t)(nm - r);
2427:    memmove(w, nm, nlen);
2428:    w += nlen;
2429:    if (!nl)
2430:      break;
2431:    *w++ = '\n';
2432:    r = nl + 1;
2433:  }
2434:  *w = '\0';
2435:  return (int)(w - buf);
2436:}
2437:
2438:/* --- POSIX personality (<stdlib.h>) — a thin mapping, nothing more --------
2439: *
2440: * Documented deviation: the string returned by getenv() lives in a small
2441: * rotating buffer pool, so it is valid until GETENV_SLOTS further getenv()
2442: * calls, not until the next setenv().  Callers keeping a value across many
2443: * lookups must copy it.  The alternative — a per-name heap cache that is never
2444: * freed — leaks by design. */
2445:#define GETENV_SLOTS 4
2446:#define GETENV_VALMAX 128
2447:
2448:static char *_default_environ[] = { NULL };
2449:char **environ = _default_environ;
2450:
2451:char *getenv(const char *name) {
2452:
2453:  static char slots[GETENV_SLOTS][GETENV_VALMAX];
2454:  static int next_slot;
2455:  char *out = slots[next_slot];
2456:  if (OS1_env_get(name, out, GETENV_VALMAX) != 0)
2457:    return NULL;
2458:  next_slot = (next_slot + 1) % GETENV_SLOTS;
2459:  return out;
2460:}
2461:
2462:int setenv(const char *name, const char *value, int overwrite) {
2463:  if (!overwrite && getenv(name))
2464:    return 0;
2465:  return OS1_env_set(name, value);
2466:}
2467:
2468:int unsetenv(const char *name) { return OS1_env_unset(name); }
2469:
2470:/*
2471: * putenv - POSIX's older "NAME=VALUE" form.
2472: *
2473: * POSIX says the caller's string BECOMES part of the environment, so later
2474: * edits to it are visible.  We cannot honour that — the storage is in the
2475: * kernel — so this parses and copies, like setenv.  Stated because a caller
2476: * relying on the aliasing would otherwise be silently wrong; in practice every
2477: * caller in this tree passes a string literal.
2478: */
2479:int putenv(char *string) {
2480:  if (!string)
2481:    return -1;
2482:  const char *eq = strchr(string, '=');
2483:  if (!eq)
2484:    return unsetenv(string); /* "NAME" with no '=' unsets, per POSIX */
2485:  char name[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2486:  size_t nl = (size_t)(eq - string);
2487:  if (nl == 0 || nl >= sizeof(name))
2488:    return -1;
2489:  memcpy(name, string, nl);
2490:  name[nl] = '\0';
2491:  return setenv(name, eq + 1, 1);
2492:}

2494:int clearenv(void) {
2495:  char buf[512];
2496:  if (OS1_env_enum(buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0)
2497:    return 0;
2498:  char *save = NULL;
2499:  for (char *k = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); k; k = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save))
2500:    OS1_env_unset(k);
2501:  return 0;
2502:}

2504:/*
2505: * env_names - NexsOS extension replacing POSIX `environ`.
2506: *
2507: * The POSIX way to enumerate assumes the environment is a userland array the
2508: * process can point at.  Here it is kernel state, so a `char **environ` would
2509: * mean publishing a snapshot and then lying about how fresh it is.  An explicit
2510: * enumerator says what it actually does: names only, values via getenv().
2511: */
2512:int env_names(char *names[], int max) {
2513:  static char buf[512];
2514:  int count = 0;
2515:  if (OS1_env_enum(buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0)
2516:    return 0;
2517:  char *save = NULL;
2518:  for (char *k = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); k && count < max;
2519:       k = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save))
2520:    names[count++] = k;
2521:  return count;
2522:}

2524:/*
2525: * __env_propagate_to_child - copies every variable that THIS process has
2526: * set (its own branch sys.proc.<self>.env.* — the machine defaults
2527: * under sys.env.* don't need copying, the child inherits them anyway
2528: * via the fallback of OS1_env_get) into the branch of the child just spawned.
2529: *
2530: * Without this every child starts with an EMPTY environment: nothing in
2531: * this tree wrote it, so an `export PATH=...` (or any setenv())
2532: * in a shell was invisible to everything it launched, and `printenv PATH`
2533: * in a child always failed even with the parent's PATH set.
2534: * execsvc_client.c already carries the cwd of the requester through the
2535: * service protocol for exactly the same reason ("cwd is wrong for exactly
2536: * the same reason the environment is"); this is the same correction applied
2537: * to the direct spawn path, the one that nxexec_spawn_search_redir/
2538: * nxshell use for every foreground and background command.
2539: *
2540: * Best-effort: a write failure here doesn't fail the spawn (the child starts
2541: * anyway, just without that variable) — consistent with setenv() which is
2542: * also a best-effort registry write.
2543: *
2544: * NOTE: the execsvc path (Phase 9c) is NOT covered here — a spawn routed
2545: * via /sys/bin/nxexec happens IN THE SERVICE PROCESS, so "self" in the
2546: * point where __env_propagate_to_child would run is the service, not the
2547: * requester. Fixing it requires bringing the environment into the network
2548: * protocol like already happens for the cwd (bump of EXECSVC_VERSION) —
2549: * left as a follow-on, in line with the note Phase 9d of the header on
2550: * cwd/ctty/env that must arrive together "as ONE mechanism".
2551: */
2552:static void __env_propagate_to_child(long child_pid) {
2553:  if (child_pid <= 0)
2554:    return;
2555:  char buf[512];
2556:  if (OS1_env_enum(buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0)
2557:    return;
2558:  char *save = NULL;
2559:  for (char *name = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); name;
2560:       name = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save)) {
2561:    char val[GETENV_VALMAX];
2562:    if (OS1_env_get(name, val, sizeof(val)) != 0)
2563:      continue;
2564:    char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2565:    if (snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "sys.proc.%ld.env.%s", child_pid, name) <= 0)
2566:      continue;
2567:    OS1_registry_set(key, val);
2568:  }
2569:}

2571:/*
2572: * stat - path metadata in ONE syscall (SYS_STAT).
2573: *
2574: * It used to infer the type: "list_dir succeeds ONLY on directories, so a >= 0
2575: * probe IS a directory".  That invariant was load-bearing in TWO places (here
2576: * and opendir) and R1 broke it — once a READ handle could be acquired on any
2577: * path, listing a regular FILE returned its CONTENT instead of failing, so
2578: * every file looked like a directory and the file manager tried to chdir into
2579: * them ("Cannot open directory").
2580: *
2581: * Inference replaced by a fact: the kernel is the only place that knows a
2582: * node's type, so it reports it.  One round trip instead of a listing probe
2583: * plus a size probe.
2584: */
2585:int stat(const char *path, struct stat *buf)
2586:
2587:{
2588:    if (!path) {
2589:        errno = EFAULT;
2590:        return -1;
2591:    }
2592:
2593:    if (buf)
2594:        memset(buf, 0, sizeof(struct stat));
2595:
2596:    struct abi_stat as;
2597:    int r = _sys_stat(path, &as);
2598:    if (r != 0) {
2599:        errno = ENOENT;          /* o meglio: errno = -r; se il kernel restituisce errno negativi */
2600:        return -1;
2601:    }
2602:
2603:    if (buf) {
2604:        buf->st_size  = (off_t)as.size;
2605:        buf->st_mode  = (as.type == ABI_S_TYPE_DIR) ? (S_IFDIR | 0755) : (S_IFREG | 0644);
2606:        buf->st_nlink = 1;
2607:        buf->st_uid   = 0;
2608:        buf->st_gid   = 0;
2609:        buf->st_blksize = 4096;
2610:        buf->st_blocks  = (as.size + 511) / 512;
2611:
2612:        /* Timestamp temporanei (finché il VFS non li supporta davvero) */
2613:        time_t now = time(NULL);
2614:        buf->st_atime = now;
2615:        buf->st_mtime = now;
2616:        buf->st_ctime = now;
2617:
2618:#if defined(_STATBUF_ST_NSEC) || defined(__USE_XOPEN2K8)
2619:        buf->st_atim.tv_sec  = now;
2620:        buf->st_atim.tv_nsec = 0;
2621:        buf->st_mtim.tv_sec  = now;
2622:        buf->st_mtim.tv_nsec = 0;
2623:        buf->st_ctim.tv_sec  = now;
2624:        buf->st_ctim.tv_nsec = 0;
2625:#endif
2626:    }
2627:
2628:    return 0;
2629:}

2631:int statfs(const char *path, struct statfs *buf)
2632:{
2633:    if (!buf) {
2634:        errno = EFAULT;
2635:        return -1;
2636:    }
2637:    if (!path) {
2638:        errno = EFAULT;
2639:        return -1;
2640:    }
2641:

2651:    buf->f_frsize  = 4096;

2653:    buf->f_bfree   = buf->f_blocks;
2654:    buf->f_bavail  = buf->f_blocks;
2655:    buf->f_files   = 0;
2656:    buf->f_ffree   = 0;
2657:    buf->f_fsid.__val[0] = 0;
2658:    buf->f_fsid.__val[1] = 0;
2659:    buf->f_namelen = 255;
2660:    buf->f_flags   = 0;

2665:int fstatfs(int fd, struct statfs *buf)
2666:{
2667:    if (!buf) {
2668:        errno = EFAULT;
2669:        return -1;
2670:    }
2671:    if (fd < 0) {
2672:        errno = EBADF;
2673:        return -1;
2674:    }

2677:       quindi per ora usiamo un placeholder basato su fstat.
2678:       Quando avremo fd → path o una vera syscall di fsinfo, si sistemerà. */
2679:    struct stat st;
2680:    if (fstat(fd, &st) != 0)
2681:        return -1;
2682:

2684:    buf->f_type    = 0x01021994UL;
2685:    buf->f_bsize   = 4096;
2686:    buf->f_frsize  = 4096;
2687:    buf->f_blocks  = (st.st_size + 4095) / 4096;
2688:    buf->f_bfree   = buf->f_blocks;
2689:    buf->f_bavail  = buf->f_blocks;
2690:    buf->f_files   = 0;
2691:    buf->f_ffree   = 0;
2692:    buf->f_fsid.__val[0] = 0;
2693:    buf->f_fsid.__val[1] = 0;
2694:    buf->f_namelen = 255;
2695:    buf->f_flags   = 0;
2696:
2697:    return 0;

2700:/*
2701: * vfprintf - format and write to a FILE stream.
2702: *
2703: * Routes through fwrite(), so it honours 'stream' exactly like any other
2704: * stream I/O: stdin/stdout/stderr go via file_fd()+write() (all three share
2705: * one CONSOLE object kernel-side, so stdout/stderr are visually
2706: * indistinguishable today, but a real fopen()ed FILE* now writes to its own
2707: * path/position instead of unconditionally landing on fd 1 (fixes
2708: * USR-LIB-05).
2709: *
2710: * Output is limited to 1023 chars by the stack buffer; longer output is
2711: * silently truncated by vsnprintf. Returns the formatted length (vsnprintf's
2712: * return value), not the byte count actually written.
2713: */
2714:int vfprintf(FILE *stream, const char *format, va_list ap) {
2715:  char buf[1024];
2716:  int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), format, ap);
2717:  fwrite(buf, 1, strlen(buf), stream);
2718:  return n;
2719:}
2720:
2721:int vprintf(const char *format, va_list ap) {
2722:  return vfprintf(stdout, format, ap);
2723:}
2724:
2725:int fprintf(FILE *stream, const char *format, ...) {
2726:  va_list args;
2727:  va_start(args, format);
2728:  int res = vfprintf(stream, format, args);
2729:  va_end(args);
2730:  return res;
2731:}

2757:/*
2758: * link - create a second name for the same file contents.
2759: *
2760: * The current NexsOS1 FS layer provides create/write/read and delete, but no
2761: * inode-level hard-link syscall; the correct compatibility point is therefore
2762: * the existing file-creation path, not a synthetic extra file or fake kernel ABI.
2763: * We copy the source bytes into the destination path, fail if the destination
2764: * already exists, and leave the original untouched.
2765: */
2766:int link(const char *oldpath, const char *newpath) {
2767:  int size = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, NULL, 0, 0);
2768:  if (size < 0)
2769:    return -1;
2770:  if (OS1_fs_read(newpath, NULL, 0, 0) >= 0) {
2771:    errno = EEXIST;
2772:    return -1;
2773:  }
2774:  if (size == 0) {
2775:    return OS1_fs_write(newpath, "", 0, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
2776:  }
2777:  char *buf = malloc((size_t)size);
2778:  if (!buf) {
2779:    errno = ENOMEM;
2780:    return -1;
2781:  }
2782:  int n = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, buf, size, 0);
2783:  if (n < 0) {
2784:    free(buf);
2785:    return -1;
2786:  }
2787:  int w = OS1_fs_write(newpath, buf, n, 0);
2788:  free(buf);
2789:  if (w < 0)
2790:    return -1;
2791:  return 0;
2792:}

2871:/*
2872: * getloadavg - get system load average (real implementation via OS1_sys_stats).
2873: *
2874: * NexsOS1 provides instantaneous scheduler load via OS1_sys_stats(sched_runnable).
2875: * Since there is no historical load tracking, we report the current snapshot
2876: * (number of ready+running processes) for all three intervals (1m, 5m, 15m).
2877: * This gives userland programs an accurate instantaneous load, not a moving average.
2878: */
2879:int getloadavg(double loadavg[], int nelem) {
2880:  if (!loadavg || nelem < 1) {
2881:    errno = EINVAL;
2882:    return -1;
2883:  }
2884:  
2885:  struct os1_sysstats stats;
2886:  long ret = OS1_sys_stats(&stats);
2887:  if (ret < 0) {
2888:    errno = (int)-ret;
2889:    return -1;
2890:  }
2891:  
2892:  /* Use the current runnable count (READY+RUNNING processes) as load */
2893:  double load = (double)stats.sched_runnable;
2894:  
2895:  /* Fill the array up to nelem with the same load value */
2896:  for (int i = 0; i < nelem; i++)
2897:    loadavg[i] = load;
2898:  
2899:  return nelem;  /* Return number of elements filled */
2900:}

2957:/*
2958: * localtime - convert time_t to struct tm.
2959: * Canonical OS1 userland implementation kept in lib.c so every ELF gets a
2960: * single consistent UTC conversion path.
2961: */
2962:struct tm *localtime(const time_t *timep) {
2963:  static struct tm result;
2964:  if (!timep)
2965:    return NULL;
2966:
2967:  time_t t = *timep;
2968:  result.tm_sec = t % 60;
2969:  t /= 60;
2970:  result.tm_min = t % 60;
2971:  t /= 60;
2972:  result.tm_hour = t % 24;
2973:  t /= 24;
2974:
2975:  result.tm_wday = (t + 4) % 7;
2976:
2977:  int year = 1970;
2978:  while (1) {
2979:    int days_in_year = 365;
2980:    if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0))
2981:      days_in_year = 366;
2982:    if (t < days_in_year)
2983:      break;
2984:    t -= days_in_year;
2985:    year++;
2986:  }
2987:  result.tm_year = year - 1900;
2988:  result.tm_yday = t;
2989:
2990:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
2991:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0))
2992:    month_days[1] = 29;
2993:
2994:  int mon = 0;
2995:  while (t >= month_days[mon]) {
2996:    t -= month_days[mon];
2997:    mon++;
2998:  }
2999:  result.tm_mon = mon;
3000:  result.tm_mday = t + 1;
3001:  result.tm_isdst = 0;
3002:  return &result;
3003:}

3005:/*
3006: * mktime - convert struct tm to time_t.
3007: */
3008:time_t mktime(struct tm *tm) {
3009:  int year = tm->tm_year + 1900;
3010:  int mon = tm->tm_mon;
3011:  int mday = tm->tm_mday;
3012:
3013:  long days = 0;
3014:  for (int y = 1970; y < year; y++)
3015:    days += ((y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || (y % 400 == 0)) ? 366 : 365;
3016:
3017:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
3018:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0))
3019:    month_days[1] = 29;
3020:
3021:  for (int m = 0; m < mon; m++)
3022:    days += month_days[m];
3023:  days += mday - 1;
3024:
3025:  return days * 86400 + tm->tm_hour * 3600 + tm->tm_min * 60 + tm->tm_sec;
3026:}

3035:/*
3036: * strftime - format a broken-down time in UTC using a minimal subset of
3037: * conversion directives required by Lua and Gnulib.
3038: */
3039:size_t strftime(char *s, size_t max, const char *format, const struct tm *tm) {
3040:  if (!s || !format || !tm || max == 0)
3041:    return 0;
3042:
3043:  size_t out = 0;
3044:  const char *p = format;
3045:  while (*p && out + 1 < max) {
3046:    if (*p != '%') {
3047:      s[out++] = *p++;
3048:      continue;
3049:    }
3050:
3051:    p++;
3052:    if (!*p)
3053:      break;
3054:
3055:    char buf[64];
3056:    int len = 0;
3057:    switch (*p) {
3058:    case '%':
3059:      s[out++] = '%';
3060:      break;
3061:    case 'Y':
3062:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%d", tm->tm_year + 1900);
3063:      break;
3064:    case 'm':
3065:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_mon + 1);
3066:      break;
3067:    case 'd':
3068:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_mday);
3069:      break;
3070:    case 'H':
3071:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_hour);
3072:      break;
3073:    case 'M':
3074:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_min);
3075:      break;
3076:    case 'S':
3077:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_sec);
3078:      break;
3079:    case 'a':
3080:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s", "Sun");
3081:      break;
3082:    case 'A':
3083:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s", "Sunday");
3084:      break;
3085:    case 'b':
3086:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s", "Jan");
3087:      break;
3088:    default:
3089:      s[out++] = *p;
3090:      break;
3091:    }
3092:
3093:    if (len > 0) {
3094:      size_t n = (size_t)len;
3095:      if (n >= max - out)
3096:        n = max - out - 1;
3097:      memcpy(s + out, buf, n);
3098:      out += n;
3099:    }
3100:    p++;
3101:  }
3102:
3103:  s[out] = '\0';
3104:  return out;
3105:}

3141:int rename(const char *oldpath, const char *newpath) {
3142:  int size = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, NULL, 0, 0); /* size probe; errno on miss */
3143:  if (size < 0)
3144:    return -1;
3145:  /* The destination write starts at offset 0, so ext4_write truncates any
3146:   * longer pre-existing dst to exactly the copied length — no separate unlink
3147:   * of newpath is needed to avoid trailing garbage. */
3148:  if (size > 0) {
3149:    char *buf = malloc((size_t)size);
3150:    if (!buf) {
3151:      errno = ENOMEM;
3152:      return -1;
3153:    }
3154:    int n = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, buf, size, 0);
3155:    if (n < 0) {
3156:      free(buf);
3157:      return -1;
3158:    }
3159:    int w = OS1_fs_write(newpath, buf, n, 0);
3160:    free(buf);
3161:    if (w < 0)
3162:      return -1;
3163:  } else if (OS1_fs_write(newpath, "", 0, 0) < 0) {
3164:    return -1;
3165:  }
3166:  OS1_fs_unlink(oldpath);
3167:  return 0;
3168:}

3170:/*
3171: * truncate - set a file's length to exactly `length` (POSIX <unistd.h>).
3172: *
3173: * The NexsOS write model (PLAN-2026-07-17-STRATIFICATION.md Phase 1): a
3174: * from-start write (offset 0) IS the whole-file-replace/truncate primitive at
3175: * the FS layer (ext4_write), so this builds on it with no new kernel call:
3176: *   - length == 0        -> a zero-byte offset-0 write empties the file;
3177: *   - length <  size     -> re-write the first `length` bytes at offset 0,
3178: *                           which truncates the tail;
3179: *   - length >  size     -> zero-extend from the old EOF.
3180: * Explicit truncation for programs that don't go through fopen("w").
3181: * ftruncate(fd) needs an fd->path or an OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE verb (a kernel
3182: * follow-up), so it is intentionally not provided yet rather than faked.
3183: */
3184:int truncate(const char *path, long length) {
3185:  if (length < 0) {
3186:    errno = EINVAL;
3187:    return -1;
3188:  }
3189:  int size = OS1_fs_read(path, NULL, 0, 0); /* current size; errno on miss */
3190:  if (size < 0)
3191:    return -1;
3192:  if (length == (long)size)
3193:    return 0;
3194:  if (length == 0)
3195:    return OS1_fs_write(path, "", 0, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
3196:  if (length < (long)size) {
3197:    char *buf = malloc((size_t)length);
3198:    if (!buf) {
3199:      errno = ENOMEM;
3200:      return -1;
3201:    }
3202:    int n = OS1_fs_read(path, buf, (int)length, 0);
3203:    int r = (n < 0 || OS1_fs_write(path, buf, n, 0) < 0) ? -1 : 0;
3204:    free(buf);
3205:    return r;
3206:  }
3207:  /* extend: zero-fill from the old EOF up to `length` */
3208:  {
3209:    long pad = length - (long)size;
3210:    char *z = calloc(1, (size_t)pad);
3211:    if (!z) {
3212:      errno = ENOMEM;
3213:      return -1;
3214:    }
3215:    int r = OS1_fs_write(path, z, (int)pad, size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
3216:    free(z);
3217:    return r;
3218:  }
3219:}
3220:/*
3221: * ftruncate - set an OPEN descriptor's file length (POSIX).  Closes the Phase 1
3222: * leftover ("ftruncate awaits an fd->path / OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE kernel verb").
3223: *
3224: * Composed from the primitives rather than duplicating truncate()'s path-based
3225: * logic in the kernel:
3226: *   - shrink to N>0: read the first N bytes back, then rewrite them from offset
3227: *     0 — an offset-0 write REPLACES the whole file (the Phase 1 FS standard),
3228: *     so the rewrite IS the truncation;
3229: *   - shrink to 0: needs OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE, because POSIX defines
3230: *     write(fd, buf, 0) as a NO-OP and so it cannot express "empty this file";
3231: *   - extend: zero-fill from the old EOF up to the new length.
3232: */
3233:int ftruncate(int fd, long length) {
3234:  if (length < 0) {
3235:    errno = EINVAL;
3236:    return -1;
3237:  }
3238:  long size = lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END);
3239:  if (size < 0)
3240:    return -1;
3241:  if (length == size)
3242:    return 0;
3243:
3244:  if (length == 0)
3245:    return OS1_object_ctl(fd, OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
3246:
3247:  if (length < size) {
3248:    char *buf = malloc((size_t)length);
3249:    if (!buf) {
3250:      errno = ENOMEM;
3251:      return -1;
3252:    }
3253:    int r = -1;
3254:    if (lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) >= 0) {
3255:      long n = read(fd, buf, (unsigned long)length);
3256:      if (n >= 0 && lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) >= 0 &&
3257:          write(fd, buf, (size_t)n) >= 0)
3258:        r = 0; /* offset-0 write replaced the file with n bytes */
3259:    }
3260:    free(buf);
3261:    return r;
3262:  }
3263:
3264:  { /* extend: zero-fill from the old EOF up to `length` */
3265:    long pad = length - size;
3266:    char *z = calloc(1, (size_t)pad);
3267:    if (!z) {
3268:      errno = ENOMEM;
3269:      return -1;
3270:    }
3271:    int r = (lseek(fd, size, SEEK_SET) >= 0 && write(fd, z, (size_t)pad) >= 0)
3272:                ? 0
3273:                : -1;
3274:    free(z);
3275:    return r;
3276:  }
3277:}

3287:/*
3288: * utf8_decode - decode the first UTF-8 codepoint from string s.
3289: *
3290: * s:    pointer to the start of a UTF-8 byte sequence (not necessarily NUL).
3291: * code: output parameter; receives the Unicode codepoint on success.
3292: *
3293: * Returns the number of bytes consumed (1–4), or 0 on invalid/null input.
3294: *
3295: * Encoding rules applied:
3296: *   0xxxxxxx (< 0x80)      : 1-byte ASCII
3297: *   110xxxxx 10xxxxxx      : 2-byte (U+0080..U+07FF)
3298: *   1110xxxx 10xxxxxx x2   : 3-byte (U+0800..U+FFFF)
3299: *   11110xxx 10xxxxxx x3   : 4-byte (U+10000..U+10FFFF)
3300: *
3301: * No validation of continuation bytes (0x3F mask is applied without checking
3302: * the 0x80 bit); malformed sequences may produce incorrect codepoints silently.
3303: *
3304: * Used by font_lib.c:font_draw_string() to iterate a UTF-8 string glyph by
3305: * glyph.
3306: */
3307:int utf8_decode(const char *s, size_t len, uint32_t *code) {
3308:  if (!s || !code || len == 0)
3309:    return 0;
3310:  unsigned char c = (unsigned char)s[0];
3311:
3312:  if (c < 0x80) {
3313:    *code = c;
3314:    return 1;
3315:  } else if ((c & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
3316:    if (len < 2 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80)
3317:      return 0;
3318:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x1F) << 6) | (uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F);
3319:    if (*code < 0x80)
3320:      return 0;
3321:    return 2;
3322:  } else if ((c & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
3323:    if (len < 3 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80 || (s[2] & 0xC0) != 0x80)
3324:      return 0;
3325:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x0F) << 12) | ((uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F) << 6) |
3326:            (uint32_t)(s[2] & 0x3F);
3327:    if (*code < 0x800)
3328:      return 0;
3329:    if (*code >= 0xD800 && *code <= 0xDFFF)
3330:      return 0;
3331:    return 3;
3332:  } else if ((c & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
3333:    if (len < 4 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80 || (s[2] & 0xC0) != 0x80 ||
3334:        (s[3] & 0xC0) != 0x80)
3335:      return 0;
3336:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x07) << 18) | ((uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F) << 12) |
3337:            ((uint32_t)(s[2] & 0x3F) << 6) | (uint32_t)(s[3] & 0x3F);
3338:    if (*code < 0x10000)
3339:      return 0;
3340:    if (*code > 0x10FFFF)
3341:      return 0;
3342:    return 4;
3343:  }
3344:  return 0;
3345:}

3353: * live in kernel/lib/string.c (#included above); the functions here are the

3358:char *strtok_r(char *str, const char *delim, char **saveptr) {
3359:  char *s = str ? str : *saveptr;
3360:  if (!s)
3361:    return NULL;
3362:  while (*s && strchr(delim, (int)(unsigned char)*s))
3363:    s++;
3364:  if (*s == '\0') {
3365:    *saveptr = s;
3366:    return NULL;
3367:  }
3368:  char *tok = s;
3369:  while (*s && !strchr(delim, (int)(unsigned char)*s))
3370:    s++;
3371:  if (*s) {
3372:    *s = '\0';
3373:    s++;
3374:  }
3375:  *saveptr = s;
3376:  return tok;
3377:}

3424:/* strtoul / strtoull — unsigned variants of strtol */
3425:unsigned long strtoul(const char *nptr, char **endptr, int base) {
3426:  while (*nptr == ' ' || *nptr == '\t' || *nptr == '\n' ||
3427:         *nptr == '\r' || *nptr == '\f' || *nptr == '\v')
3428:    nptr++;
3429:  int neg = 0;
3430:  if (*nptr == '-') { neg = 1; nptr++; }
3431:  else if (*nptr == '+') nptr++;
3432:  if (base == 0) {
3433:    if (nptr[0] == '0' && (nptr[1] == 'x' || nptr[1] == 'X')) {
3434:      base = 16; nptr += 2;
3435:    } else if (nptr[0] == '0') {
3436:      base = 8; nptr++;
3437:    } else {
3438:      base = 10;
3439:    }
3440:  } else if (base == 16 && nptr[0] == '0' &&
3441:             (nptr[1] == 'x' || nptr[1] == 'X')) {
3442:    nptr += 2;
3443:  }
3444:  unsigned long result = 0;
3445:  const char *start = nptr;
3446:  while (*nptr) {
3447:    int digit;
3448:    if (*nptr >= '0' && *nptr <= '9')      digit = *nptr - '0';
3449:    else if (*nptr >= 'a' && *nptr <= 'z') digit = *nptr - 'a' + 10;
3450:    else if (*nptr >= 'A' && *nptr <= 'Z') digit = *nptr - 'A' + 10;
3451:    else break;
3452:    if (digit >= base) break;
3453:    result = result * (unsigned long)base + (unsigned long)digit;
3454:    nptr++;
3455:  }
3456:  if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)(nptr == start ? start : nptr);
3457:  return neg ? -result : result;
3458:}
3459:
3460:unsigned long long strtoull(const char *nptr, char **endptr, int base) {
3461:  return (unsigned long long)strtoul(nptr, endptr, base);
3462:}

3469:/* qsort: in-place insertion sort with byte-wise swaps (no temp buffer / VLA,
3470: * no recursion).  O(n^2) but adequate for the small arrays NEXS sorts. */
3471:void qsort(void *base, size_t nmemb, size_t size,
3472:           int (*compar)(const void *, const void *)) {
3473:  char *arr = (char *)base;
3474:  for (size_t i = 1; i < nmemb; i++) {
3475:    for (size_t j = i;
3476:         j > 0 && compar(arr + (j - 1) * size, arr + j * size) > 0; j--) {
3477:      char *a = arr + (j - 1) * size;
3478:      char *b = arr + j * size;
3479:      for (size_t k = 0; k < size; k++) {
3480:        char t = a[k];
3481:        a[k] = b[k];
3482:        b[k] = t;
3483:      }
3484:    }
3485:  }
3486:}

3488:/* --- <stdio.h> ---
3489: * Standard stream handles.
3490: */
3491:FILE _stdin_struct = {.fd = 0};
3492:FILE _stdout_struct = {.fd = 1};
3493:FILE _stderr_struct = {.fd = 2};
3494:
3495:/* file_fd - the descriptor behind a stream, or -1 for a positional
3496: * (path-backed) one.  The three console streams carry fd 0/1/2 in their own
3497: * structs and fopen() sets fd = -1 to select path I/O, so returning the field
3498: * is EXACTLY equivalent to the old stdin/stdout/stderr pointer comparison —
3499: * and additionally makes fdopen()'d streams (e.g. a pipe end wrapped in a
3500: * FILE*) route through read()/write() like any other descriptor. */
3501:static int file_fd(FILE *fp) { return fp ? fp->fd : -1; }
3502:
3503:/*
3504: * fputc/fputs/fgetc delegate to fwrite/fread rather than calling write()/read()
3505: * on the descriptor themselves.
3506: *
3507: * They used to take an `if (fd >= 0)` shortcut straight to the syscall.  That
3508: * was correct while only the console had a descriptor and a path-backed FILE
3509: * had none — but a FILE now keeps an open handle for its lifetime, so `fd >= 0`
3510: * became true for ordinary files too and the shortcut started bypassing the
3511: * stream buffers.  The consequences were not symmetric and neither was
3512: * cosmetic:
3513: *
3514: *   - fgetc read one byte straight from the descriptor and never advanced
3515: *     fp->pos.  A reader that mixes getc() with fread() — which is exactly what
3516: *     Lua's loader does when it skips a `#!` line — desynchronised: fread then
3517: *     refilled from the stale fp->pos and re-read the file from the beginning.
3518: *   - fputc/fputs wrote straight through while buffered bytes were still
3519: *     pending in wbuf, so the two landed out of order: silent corruption, not a
3520: *     visible failure.
3521: *
3522: * fread/fwrite already own the one correct rule — the descriptor fast path is
3523: * for CONSOLE/pipe streams only (`path[0] == '\0'`), never for a file — so
3524: * these three defer to it instead of carrying a second, older copy of the same
3525: * decision.  ext4's 4 KiB read-modify-write granularity is why that rule
3526: * exists; see the comment in fwrite.
3527: */
3528:int fputc(int c, FILE *fp) {
3529:  unsigned char ch = (unsigned char)c;
3530:  if (fwrite(&ch, 1, 1, fp) != 1)
3531:    return EOF;
3532:  return (int)ch;
3533:}
3534:
3535:int fputs(const char *s, FILE *fp) {
3536:  size_t len = strlen(s);
3537:  if (len && fwrite(s, 1, len, fp) != len)
3538:    return EOF;
3539:  return 0;
3540:}
3541:
3542:int fgetc(FILE *fp) {
3543:  if (!fp)
3544:    return EOF;
3545:  if (fp->has_ungetc) {
3546:    fp->has_ungetc = 0;
3547:    return fp->ungetc_buf;
3548:  }
3549:  unsigned char ch;
3550:  if (fread(&ch, 1, 1, fp) != 1)
3551:    return EOF;
3552:  return (int)ch;
3553:}
3554:
3555:char *fgets(char *s, int size, FILE *fp) {
3556:  if (size <= 0)
3557:    return NULL;
3558:  int i = 0;
3559:  while (i < size - 1) {
3560:    int c = fgetc(fp);
3561:    if (c == EOF) {
3562:      if (i == 0)
3563:        return NULL;
3564:      break;
3565:    }
3566:    s[i++] = (char)c;
3567:    if (c == '\n')
3568:      break;
3569:  }
3570:  s[i] = '\0';
3571:  return s;
3572:}
3573:
3574:int ungetc(int c, FILE *fp) {
3575:  if (!fp || c == EOF)
3576:    return EOF;
3577:  fp->ungetc_buf = c;
3578:  fp->has_ungetc = 1;
3579:  fp->eof = 0;
3580:  return c;
3581:}

3583:/*
3584: * rewind - POSIX: equivalent to fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET) except that it also
3585: * clears the error indicator and returns nothing.  Added because it was the one
3586: * standard stdio entry point missing from this libc, and code ported from POSIX
3587: * reaches for it after a failed read; without it the link failed rather than
3588: * the call misbehaving, which is why it went unnoticed.
3589: */
3590:void rewind(FILE *fp) {
3591:  if (!fp)
3592:    return;
3593:  fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);
3594:  fp->error = 0;
3595:}

3739:/* --- <sys/ioctl.h> --- only TIOCGWINSZ, answered from the window grid. */
3740:int ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, ...) {
3741:  (void)fd;
3742:  if (request == TIOCGWINSZ) {
3743:    va_list ap;
3744:    va_start(ap, request);
3745:    struct winsize *ws = va_arg(ap, struct winsize *);
3746:    va_end(ap);
3747:    int cols = 0, rows = 0;
3748:    int wid = window_of_pid(get_pid());
3749:    if (ws && wid > 0 && window_grid(wid, &cols, &rows) == 0) {
3750:      ws->ws_col = (unsigned short)cols;
3751:      ws->ws_row = (unsigned short)rows;
3752:      ws->ws_xpixel = 0;
3753:      ws->ws_ypixel = 0;
3754:      return 0;
3755:    }
3756:  }
3757:  return -1;
3758:}

3760:/* --- <dirent.h> --- over list_dir() (space-separated names from ext4_list). */
3761:DIR *opendir(const char *name) {
3762:  /* Verify it IS a directory before listing.  opendir() used to rely on
3763:   * list_dir failing for a regular file; since a directory is now read through
3764:   * the same object path as a file, listing a FILE returns its content and the
3765:   * call would "succeed" on anything.  Callers use opendir() as the
3766:   * file-or-directory test (the file manager does), so this must be exact. */
3767:  struct abi_stat as;
3768:  if (_sys_stat(name, &as) != 0 || as.type != ABI_S_TYPE_DIR) {
3769:    errno = ENOTDIR;
3770:    return NULL;
3771:  }
3772:  DIR *d = malloc(sizeof(DIR));
3773:  if (!d)
3774:    return NULL;
3775:  if (list_dir(name, d->buf, sizeof(d->buf)) < 0) {
3776:    free(d);
3777:    return NULL;
3778:  }
3779:  d->pos = 0;
3780:  return d;
3781:}

3783:struct dirent *readdir(DIR *dirp) {
3784:  if (!dirp)
3785:    return NULL;
3786:  while (dirp->buf[dirp->pos] == ' ')
3787:    dirp->pos++;
3788:  if (dirp->buf[dirp->pos] == '\0')
3789:    return NULL;
3790:  int i = 0;
3791:  while (dirp->buf[dirp->pos] != ' ' && dirp->buf[dirp->pos] != '\0' &&
3792:         i < (int)sizeof(dirp->ent.d_name) - 1)
3793:    dirp->ent.d_name[i++] = dirp->buf[dirp->pos++];
3794:  dirp->ent.d_name[i] = '\0';
3795:  dirp->ent.d_ino = 0;
3796:  dirp->ent.d_type = DT_UNKNOWN;
3797:  return &dirp->ent;
3798:}

3805:size_t strspn(const char *s, const char *accept) {
3806:  const char *p = s;
3807:  while (*p) {
3808:    const char *a = accept;
3809:    while (*a && *a != *p) {
3810:      a++;
3811:    }
3812:    if (*a == '\0') {
3813:      break;
3814:    }
3815:    p++;
3816:  }
3817:  return p - s;
3818:}

3820:size_t strcspn(const char *s, const char *reject) {
3821:  const char *p = s;
3822:  while (*p) {
3823:    const char *r = reject;
3824:    while (*r) {
3825:      if (*p == *r)
3826:        return p - s;
3827:      r++;
3828:    }
3829:    p++;
3830:  }
3831:  return p - s;
3832:}

3925:static int wctype_value(wint_t wc, const char *property) {
3926:  if (!property)
3927:    return 0;
3928:  if (strcmp(property, "alnum") == 0) return iswalnum(wc);
3929:  if (strcmp(property, "alpha") == 0) return iswalpha(wc);
3930:  if (strcmp(property, "blank") == 0) return iswblank(wc);
3931:  if (strcmp(property, "cntrl") == 0) return iswcntrl(wc);
3932:  if (strcmp(property, "digit") == 0) return iswdigit(wc);
3933:  if (strcmp(property, "graph") == 0) return iswgraph(wc);
3934:  if (strcmp(property, "lower") == 0) return iswlower(wc);
3935:  if (strcmp(property, "print") == 0) return iswprint(wc);
3936:  if (strcmp(property, "punct") == 0) return iswpunct(wc);
3937:  if (strcmp(property, "space") == 0) return iswspace(wc);
3938:  if (strcmp(property, "upper") == 0) return iswupper(wc);
3939:  if (strcmp(property, "xdigit") == 0) return iswxdigit(wc);
3940:  if (strcmp(property, "any") == 0) return 1;
3941:  return 0;
3942:}

4189:ssize_t writev(int fd, const struct iovec *iov, int iovcnt) {
4190:  if (iovcnt < 0 || !iov) {
4191:    errno = EINVAL;
4192:    return -1;
4193:  }
4194:  ssize_t total = 0;
4195:  for (int i = 0; i < iovcnt; i++) {
4196:    if (iov[i].iov_len == 0)
4197:      continue;
4198:    if (!iov[i].iov_base) {
4199:      errno = EFAULT;
4200:      return -1;
4201:    }
4202:    long w = write(fd, iov[i].iov_base, iov[i].iov_len);
4203:    if (w < 0) {
4204:      return total > 0 ? total : -1;
4205:    }
4206:    total += w;
4207:    if ((size_t)w < iov[i].iov_len)
4208:      break;
4209:  }
4210:  return total;
4211:}
4212:
