4214:  if (iovcnt < 0 || !iov) {
4215:    errno = EINVAL;
4216:    return -1;
4217:  }
4218:  ssize_t total = 0;
4219:  for (int i = 0; i < iovcnt; i++) {
4220:    if (iov[i].iov_len == 0)
4221:      continue;
4222:    if (!iov[i].iov_base) {
4223:      errno = EFAULT;
4224:      return -1;
4225:    }
4226:    long r = read(fd, iov[i].iov_base, iov[i].iov_len);
4227:    if (r <= 0) {
4228:      return total > 0 ? total : r;
4229:    }
4230:    total += r;
4231:    if ((size_t)r < iov[i].iov_len)
4232:      break;
4233:  }
4234:  return total;
4235:}

4567:/*
4568: * utime - set access and modification times of a file.
4569: * times == NULL → set both to current time.
4570: */
4571:__attribute__((weak))
4572:int utime(const char *path, const struct utimbuf *times)
4573:{
4574:    if (!path) {
4575:        errno = EFAULT;
4576:        return -1;
4577:    }
4578:
4579:    /* Assicuriamoci che il file esista (comportamento di touch) */
4580:    struct stat st;
4581:    if (stat(path, &st) != 0) {
4582:        int fd = open(path, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC, 0644);
4583:        if (fd < 0)
4584:            return -1;
4585:        close(fd);
4586:    }
4587:
4588:    (void)times;   /* il filesystem non salva ancora i timestamp */
4589:    return 0;
4590:}
4591:
4592:__attribute__((weak))
4593:int utimes(const char *path, const struct timeval times[2])
4594:{
4595:    if (!path) {
4596:        errno = EFAULT;
4597:        return -1;
4598:    }
4599:
4600:    struct utimbuf buf;
4601:    if (times) {
4602:        buf.actime  = times[0].tv_sec;
4603:        buf.modtime = times[1].tv_sec;
4604:    } else {
4605:        time_t now = time(NULL);
4606:        buf.actime  = now;
4607:        buf.modtime = now;
4608:    }
4609:    return utime(path, times ? &buf : NULL);
4610:}

4624:        return -1;
4625:    }

4632:        tv[1].tv_usec = times[1].tv_nsec / 1000;

@@@ user/sys/lib/malloc.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/malloc.c
3: * Userland Heap Allocator — segregated free lists + boundary-tag coalescing
4: *
5: * Built entirely on top of OS1's SYS_SBRK (#216) via _sys_sbrk(); no other
6: * kernel primitive is required. This replaces the earlier "singly linked
7: * free/alloc chain" design with the standard technique (Knuth's boundary
8: * tags, as used by dlmalloc-family allocators) so correctness no longer
9: * depends on maintaining an address-order invariant by hand.
10: *
11: * ---- Block layout ----
12: *
13: *   [ header (16B) ][ payload (>=32B, 16B-aligned) ][ footer (8B) ]
14: *
15: *   header.size / footer.size both hold the TOTAL block size (header +
16: *   payload + footer) with bit0 used as the FREE flag. Every block's total
17: *   size is a multiple of 16 by construction, so bit0 is otherwise always
18: *   0 and safe to steal for the flag.
19: *
20: *   Storing the size at BOTH ends means any block's neighbours — forward
21: *   (address + size) or backward (read the size word immediately before
22: *   this block's header) — can be located and inspected in O(1), for ANY
23: *   block, allocated or free, however it was created. This is what makes
24: *   coalescing safe without assuming a block's list-neighbour is its
25: *   memory-neighbour (the bug in the previous design, USR-MALLOC-02).
26: *
27: *   A FREE block additionally overlays two pointers (next/prev) at the
28: *   start of its payload — the intrusive doubly-linked list node for its
29: *   size bin. Safe because payload is always >= 32 bytes when free.
30: *
31: * ---- Allocation strategy ----
32: *
33: *   8 segregated bins by payload size (32/64/128/256/512/1024/2048/+inf).
34: *   malloc() does first-fit *within and above* the requested bin — an
35: *   approximate best-fit that is O(1) amortized for the common case
36: *   instead of O(n) over the whole heap.
37: *
38: * ---- What this fixes relative to the original allocator ----
39: *
40: *   USR-MALLOC-02 (coalescing corruption): gone by construction — no
41: *     "assume physical adjacency" step exists anymore; boundary tags let
42: *     us verify it directly.
43: *   USR-MALLOC-03 (no backward coalescing): implemented (see free()).
44: *   USR-MALLOC-04 (heap never shrinks): the trailing free block is
45: *     returned to the kernel via a negative sbrk() in free().
46: *   USR-MALLOC-05 (payload not 16-byte aligned): fixed for real — the
47: *     16-byte header plus the size-residue trick below guarantee every
48: *     payload starts 16-byte aligned (given a 16-aligned heap start,
49: *     which grow_heap() enforces defensively on first use).
50: *   USR-MALLOC-06 (realloc shrink check): realloc() below compares
51: *     against actual old payload capacity, same tradeoff as before
52: *     (documented, not a correctness bug) — still returns in place when
53: *     it fits, to avoid pointless copies.
54: */
55:#include <os1.h>
56:#include <stddef.h>
57:#include <stdint.h>
58:
59:typedef struct header {
60:  size_t size;   /* total block size | FREE_BIT (see above) */
61:  size_t canary; /* unused; pads header to 16B so payload is 16B-aligned */
62:} header_t;
63:
64:typedef struct free_node {
65:  struct free_node *next;
66:  struct free_node *prev;
67:} free_node_t;
68:
69:#define HEADER_SIZE (sizeof(header_t)) /* 16 */
70:#define FOOTER_SIZE (sizeof(size_t))   /* 8  */
71:#define FREE_BIT ((size_t)1)
72:#define SIZE_MASK (~FREE_BIT)
73:#define MALLOC_ALIGN 16UL
74:#define MIN_PAYLOAD 32UL /* room for a free_node_t plus slack */
75:#define MIN_BLOCK (HEADER_SIZE + MIN_PAYLOAD + FOOTER_SIZE)
76:#define NUM_BINS 8
77:
78:static free_node_t *bins[NUM_BINS];
79:static uint8_t *heap_start = NULL;
80:static uint8_t *heap_end = NULL; /* current program break */
81:
82:/* ---------------- boundary-tag helpers ---------------- */
83:
84:static inline size_t blk_size(header_t *h) { return h->size & SIZE_MASK; }
85:static inline int blk_free(header_t *h) { return (int)(h->size & FREE_BIT); }
86:
87:/* Writes both the header and the mirrored footer in one place, so the two
88: * can never drift apart. Every size/flag change goes through this. */
89:static void set_block(header_t *h, size_t total_size, int is_free) {
90:  size_t enc = (total_size & SIZE_MASK) | (is_free ? FREE_BIT : 0);
91:  h->size = enc;
92:  *(size_t *)((uint8_t *)h + total_size - FOOTER_SIZE) = enc;
93:}
94:
95:static header_t *node_to_header(free_node_t *n) {
96:  return (header_t *)((uint8_t *)n - HEADER_SIZE);
97:}
98:
99:static int bin_index(size_t payload) {
100:  static const size_t thresh[NUM_BINS - 1] = {32,  64,   128, 256,
101:                                              512, 1024, 2048};
102:  for (int i = 0; i < NUM_BINS - 1; i++)
103:    if (payload <= thresh[i])
104:      return i;
105:  return NUM_BINS - 1;
106:}
107:
108:static void bin_remove(header_t *h) {
109:  free_node_t *n = (free_node_t *)(h + 1);
110:  int idx = bin_index(blk_size(h) - HEADER_SIZE - FOOTER_SIZE);
111:  if (n->prev)
112:    n->prev->next = n->next;
113:  else
114:    bins[idx] = n->next;
115:  if (n->next)
116:    n->next->prev = n->prev;
117:}
118:
119:static void bin_insert(header_t *h) {
120:  int idx = bin_index(blk_size(h) - HEADER_SIZE - FOOTER_SIZE);
121:  free_node_t *n = (free_node_t *)(h + 1);
122:  n->prev = NULL;
123:  n->next = bins[idx];
124:  if (bins[idx])
125:    bins[idx]->prev = n;
126:  bins[idx] = n;
127:}
128:
129:/* ---------------- sbrk shims (unchanged ABI) ---------------- */
130:
131:void *OS1low_vm_sbrk(intptr_t increment) { return _sys_sbrk(increment); }
132:void *sbrk(intptr_t increment) { return OS1low_vm_sbrk(increment); }
133:
134:/*
135: * sbrk_failed - did this sbrk() return an error rather than a break address?
136: *
137: * SYS_SBRK (kernel/sched/process.c sys_sbrk) returns a NEGATIVE errno on
138: * failure — -ENOMEM when the heap hits SBRK_HEAP_LIMIT or a page can't be
139: * allocated, -EINVAL on a bad shrink — NOT the (void *)-1 that plain sbrk()
140: * uses.  Any value in the top page ([-4095, -1]) is such an error code; a
141: * real user-heap break never lands there.  Checking only ==(void *)-1 let
142: * -ENOMEM (-12 -> 0xfffffffffffffff4) slip through as a "pointer", and
143: * grow_heap()/set_block() then wrote a block header to it: the Data Abort at
144: * addr=0xfffffffffffffff4 in malloc under memory pressure (Lua GC stress).
145: */
146:static inline int sbrk_failed(void *p) {
147:  return (uintptr_t)p >= (uintptr_t)(-4095);
148:}
149:
150:/* Grows the heap by exactly min_total bytes (already a multiple of 16) and
151: * returns a fresh block header covering the extension, marked free. On the
152: * very first call it defensively aligns the initial break up to 16 bytes
153: * (via a tiny probe + pad sbrk) in case the kernel's initial break isn't
154: * already aligned — everything after that stays aligned by induction,
155: * since every block's total size is a multiple of 16. */
156:static header_t *grow_heap(size_t min_total) {
157:  if (!heap_start) {
158:    void *probe = sbrk(0);
159:    if (!sbrk_failed(probe)) {
160:      uintptr_t addr = (uintptr_t)probe;
161:      uintptr_t pad =
162:          (MALLOC_ALIGN - (addr & (MALLOC_ALIGN - 1))) & (MALLOC_ALIGN - 1);
163:      if (pad) {
164:        if (sbrk_failed(sbrk((intptr_t)pad)))
165:          return NULL;
166:      }
167:    }
168:  }
169:
170:  void *p = sbrk((intptr_t)min_total);
171:  if (sbrk_failed(p))
172:    return NULL;
173:
174:  if (!heap_start)
175:    heap_start = (uint8_t *)p;
176:  heap_end = (uint8_t *)p + min_total;
177:
178:  header_t *h = (header_t *)p;
179:  set_block(h, min_total, 1);
180:  return h;
181:}
182:
183:/* ---------------- malloc ---------------- */
184:
185:void *malloc(size_t size) {
186:  if (size == 0)
187:    return NULL;
188:
189:  /* Round up to 16, then add an 8-byte residue so that
190:   * HEADER(16) + payload + FOOTER(8) is itself always a multiple of 16
191:   * — this is what keeps every block's payload 16-byte aligned. */
192:  size_t payload = (size + (MALLOC_ALIGN - 1)) & ~(MALLOC_ALIGN - 1);
193:  if (payload < MIN_PAYLOAD)
194:    payload = MIN_PAYLOAD;
195:  payload += 8;
196:
197:  size_t need = HEADER_SIZE + payload + FOOTER_SIZE;
198:
199:  int start_bin = bin_index(payload);
200:  for (int b = start_bin; b < NUM_BINS; b++) {
201:    for (free_node_t *n = bins[b]; n; n = n->next) {
202:      header_t *h = node_to_header(n);
203:      if (blk_size(h) < need)
204:        continue;
205:
206:      bin_remove(h);
207:      size_t total = blk_size(h);
208:      size_t remainder = total - need;
209:
210:      if (remainder >= MIN_BLOCK) {
211:        set_block(h, need, 0);
212:        header_t *rem = (header_t *)((uint8_t *)h + need);
213:        set_block(rem, remainder, 1);
214:        bin_insert(rem);
215:      } else {
216:        set_block(h, total, 0); /* keep the few extra bytes */
217:      }
218:      return (void *)(h + 1);
219:    }
220:  }
221:
222:  /* Nothing fits in any bin: extend the heap for exactly this request. */
223:  header_t *h = grow_heap(need);
224:  if (!h)
225:    return NULL;
226:  set_block(h, need, 0);
227:  return (void *)(h + 1);
228:}
229:
230:/* ---------------- free ---------------- */
231:
232:void free(void *ptr) {
233:  if (!ptr)
234:    return;
235:
236:  header_t *h = (header_t *)ptr - 1;
237:  size_t total = blk_size(h);
238:  set_block(h, total, 1);
239:
240:  /* Forward coalesce: the boundary tag lets us check the ACTUAL next
241:   * block in memory directly, whatever it is — no assumption needed. */
242:  uint8_t *next_addr = (uint8_t *)h + total;
243:  if (next_addr < heap_end) {
244:    header_t *nh = (header_t *)next_addr;
245:    if (blk_free(nh)) {
246:      bin_remove(nh);
247:      total += blk_size(nh);
248:      set_block(h, total, 1);
249:    }
250:  }
251:
252:  /* Backward coalesce: read the size word immediately before this
253:   * block's header (the previous block's footer) to jump straight to
254:   * its header in O(1) and check whether IT is free. */
255:  if ((uint8_t *)h > heap_start) {
256:    size_t prev_enc = *((size_t *)h - 1);
257:    size_t prev_size = prev_enc & SIZE_MASK;
258:    header_t *ph = (header_t *)((uint8_t *)h - prev_size);
259:    if (blk_free(ph)) {
260:      bin_remove(ph);
261:      total = prev_size + total;
262:      set_block(ph, total, 1);
263:      h = ph;
264:    }
265:  }
266:
267:  /* If the coalesced free block now reaches the end of the heap, hand
268:   * it back to the kernel instead of keeping it around unused. */
269:  if ((uint8_t *)h + total == heap_end) {
270:    heap_end = (uint8_t *)h;
271:    sbrk(-(intptr_t)total);
272:    return;
273:  }
274:
275:  bin_insert(h);
276:}
277:
278:/* ---------------- realloc ---------------- */
279:
280:void *realloc(void *ptr, size_t size) {
281:  if (!ptr)
282:    return malloc(size);
283:  if (size == 0) {
284:    free(ptr);
285:    return NULL;
286:  }
287:
288:  header_t *h = (header_t *)ptr - 1;
289:  size_t old_payload = blk_size(h) - HEADER_SIZE - FOOTER_SIZE;
290:
291:  if (old_payload >= size)
292:    return ptr; /* already fits */
293:
294:  void *new_ptr = malloc(size);
295:  if (new_ptr) {
296:    memcpy(new_ptr, ptr, old_payload);
297:    free(ptr);
298:  }
299:  return new_ptr;
300:}
301:
302:/* ---------------- calloc ---------------- */
303:
304:void *calloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size) {
305:  /* Pre-multiply overflow check (USR-MALLOC-01): rejects any input whose
306:   * product would wrap, without relying on the wraparound happening. */
307:  if (nmemb != 0 && size > SIZE_MAX / nmemb)
308:    return NULL;
309:
310:  size_t total = nmemb * size;
311:  void *ptr = malloc(total);
312:  if (ptr)
313:    memset(ptr, 0, total);
314:  return ptr;
315:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/math.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/math.c
3: * NexsOS1 Bare-Metal Math Library — IEEE-754 float/double
4: *
5: * Self-contained implementation for -nostdlib -fno-builtin -ffreestanding.
6: * No libgcc/libm dependency. Algorithms derived from musl and fdlibm
7: * (Sun Microsystems), adapted for single-file bare-metal use.
8: *
9: * Architecture: both AMD64 and AArch64 (pure C, no inline asm, no FPU
10: * intrinsics — the compiler's soft-float or hard-float codegen handles
11: * the ABI).
12: *
13: * Precision targets:
14: *   - float:  <= 1 ulp for elementary functions, <= 2 ulp for transcendentals
15: *   - double: <= 1 ulp for elementary functions, <= 3 ulp for transcendentals
16: */
17:#include <math.h>
18:#include <stdint.h>
19:#include <string.h>
20:
21:/* ============================================================================
22: * Internal helpers — bit manipulation
23: * ============================================================================
24: */
25:
26:static inline uint32_t __f32_bits(float x) {
27:  union {
28:    float f;
29:    uint32_t u;
30:  } v = {x};
31:  return v.u;
32:}
33:
34:static inline float __f32_from_bits(uint32_t u) {
35:  union {
36:    uint32_t u;
37:    float f;
38:  } v = {u};
39:  return v.f;
40:}
41:
42:static inline uint64_t __f64_bits(double x) {
43:  union {
44:    double f;
45:    uint64_t u;
46:  } v = {x};
47:  return v.u;
48:}
49:
50:static inline double __f64_from_bits(uint64_t u) {
51:  union {
52:    uint64_t u;
53:    double f;
54:  } v = {u};
55:  return v.f;
56:}
57:
58:static inline int __f32_sign(float x) { return (int)(__f32_bits(x) >> 31); }
59:
60:static inline int __f64_sign(double x) { return (int)(__f64_bits(x) >> 63); }
61:

133:float sqrtf(float x) {
134:  if (__f32_bits(x) == 0 || __f32_bits(x) == 0x80000000u)
135:    return x;
136:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) > 0x7f800000u)
137:    return x;
138:  if (__f32_bits(x) >> 31)
139:    return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
140:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) == 0x7f800000u)
141:    return x;
142:
143:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
144:  uint32_t est = (ix >> 1) + 0x1fbb67a8u;
145:  float y = __f32_from_bits(est);
146:
147:  y = 0.5f * (y + x / y);
148:  y = 0.5f * (y + x / y);
149:  y = 0.5f * (y + x / y);
150:  return y;
151:}

153:double sqrt(double x) {
154:  if (__f64_bits(x) == 0 || __f64_bits(x) == 0x8000000000000000ULL)
155:    return x;
156:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) > 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
157:    return x;
158:  if (__f64_bits(x) >> 63)
159:    return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
160:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
161:    return x;
162:
163:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
164:  uint64_t est = (ix >> 1) + 0x1ff7a7bea2a2a2a2ULL;
165:  double y = __f64_from_bits(est);
166:
167:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
168:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
169:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
170:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
171:  return y;
172:}

179:float floorf(float x) {
180:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
181:  int e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
182:  uint32_t m;
183:
184:  if (e >= 23)
185:    return x;
186:  if (e < 0) {
187:    if (ix >> 31)
188:      return -1.0f;
189:    return 0.0f * x;
190:  }
191:
192:  m = 0x007fffffu >> e;
193:  if ((ix & m) == 0)
194:    return x;
195:
196:  if (ix >> 31)
197:    ix += m;
198:  ix &= ~m;
199:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
200:}

337:/* ============================================================================
338: * Fmod — floating-point remainder
339: * ============================================================================

342:float fmodf(float x, float y) {
343:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x), iy = __f32_bits(y);
344:  int ex, ey;
345:  uint32_t mx, my;
346:
347:  if (iy << 1 == 0 || (iy & 0x7f800000u) == 0x7f800000u ||
348:      (ix & 0x7f800000u) == 0x7f800000u)
349:    return (x * y) / (x * y);
350:
351:  ex = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
352:  ey = (int)((iy >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
353:  mx = (ix & 0x007fffffu) | 0x00800000u;
354:  my = (iy & 0x007fffffu) | 0x00800000u;
355:
356:  if (ex < ey)
357:    return x;
358:
359:  while (ex > ey) {
360:    if (mx >= my)
361:      mx -= my;
362:    mx <<= 1;
363:    ex--;
364:  }
365:  if (mx >= my)
366:    mx -= my;
367:
368:  if (mx == 0)
369:    return __f32_from_bits(ix & 0x80000000u);
370:
371:  while ((mx & 0x00800000u) == 0) {
372:    mx <<= 1;
373:    ex--;
374:  }
375:
376:  ix =
377:      (ix & 0x80000000u) | (((uint32_t)(ex + 0x7f)) << 23) | (mx & 0x007fffffu);
378:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
379:}
380:
381:double fmod(double x, double y) {
382:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x), iy = __f64_bits(y);
383:  int ex, ey;
384:  uint64_t mx, my;
385:
386:  if (iy << 1 == 0 || (iy & 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL ||
387:      (ix & 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
388:    return (x * y) / (x * y);
389:
390:  ex = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 0x3ff;
391:  ey = (int)((iy >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 0x3ff;
392:  mx = (ix & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) | 0x0010000000000000ULL;
393:  my = (iy & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) | 0x0010000000000000ULL;
394:
395:  if (ex < ey)
396:    return x;
397:
398:  while (ex > ey) {
399:    if (mx >= my)
400:      mx -= my;
401:    mx <<= 1;
402:    ex--;
403:  }
404:  if (mx >= my)
405:    mx -= my;
406:
407:  if (mx == 0)
408:    return __f64_from_bits(ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL);
409:
410:  while ((mx & 0x0010000000000000ULL) == 0) {
411:    mx <<= 1;
412:    ex--;
413:  }
414:
415:  ix = (ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL) | (((uint64_t)(ex + 0x3ff)) << 52) |
416:       (mx & 0x000fffffffffffffULL);
417:  return __f64_from_bits(ix);
418:}

454:float frexpf(float x, int *exp) {
455:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
456:  int e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff);
457:
458:  if (e == 0) {
459:    if ((ix & 0x007fffffu) == 0) {
460:      if (exp)
461:        *exp = 0;
462:      return x;
463:    }
464:    x *= 0x1.0p64f;
465:    ix = __f32_bits(x);
466:    e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 64;
467:  } else if (e == 0xff) {
468:    if (exp)
469:      *exp = 0;
470:    return x;
471:  }
472:
473:  if (exp)
474:    *exp = e - 0x7e;
475:  ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | 0x3f000000u;
476:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
477:}

479:float ldexpf(float x, int exp) {
480:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
481:  int e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff);
482:
483:  if (e == 0 || e == 0xff)
484:    return x;
485:
486:  e += exp;
487:  if (e >= 0xff)
488:    return __f32_from_bits((ix & 0x80000000u) | 0x7f800000u);
489:  if (e <= 0) {
490:    if (e <= -24)
491:      return __f32_from_bits(ix & 0x80000000u);
492:    ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | ((uint32_t)(1) << 23);
493:    while (e < 0) {
494:      ix >>= 1;
495:      e++;
496:    }
497:    ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | ((uint32_t)(e) << 23);
498:    return __f32_from_bits(ix);
499:  }
500:  ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | ((uint32_t)(e) << 23);
501:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
502:}

533:double frexp(double x, int *exp) {
534:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
535:  int e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff);
536:
537:  if (e == 0) {
538:    if ((ix & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) == 0) {
539:      if (exp)
540:        *exp = 0;
541:      return x;
542:    }
543:    x *= 0x1.0p64;
544:    ix = __f64_bits(x);
545:    e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 64;
546:  } else if (e == 0x7ff) {
547:    if (exp)
548:      *exp = 0;
549:    return x;
550:  }
551:
552:  if (exp)
553:    *exp = e - 0x3fe;
554:  ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | 0x3fe0000000000000ULL;
555:  return __f64_from_bits(ix);
556:}

558:double ldexp(double x, int exp) {
559:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
560:  int e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff);
561:
562:  if (e == 0 || e == 0x7ff)
563:    return x;
564:
565:  e += exp;
566:  if (e >= 0x7ff)
567:    return __f64_from_bits((ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL) |
568:                           0x7ff0000000000000ULL);
569:  if (e <= 0) {
570:    if (e <= -53)
571:      return __f64_from_bits(ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL);
572:    ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | 0x0010000000000000ULL;
573:    while (e < 0) {
574:      ix >>= 1;
575:      e++;
576:    }
577:    ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)(e) << 52);
578:    return __f64_from_bits(ix);
579:  }
580:  ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)(e) << 52);
581:  return __f64_from_bits(ix);
582:}

585: * Exponential and logarithm
586: * ============================================================================

588:
589:static const float __expf_c[6] = {1.0f,
590:                                  0.5f,
591:                                  0.16666667163372039794921875f,
592:                                  0.041666485369205474853515625f,
593:                                  0.00833336085736751556396484375f,
594:                                  0.00137857165321695804595947265625f};
595:
596:float expf(float x) {
597:  float y, r;
598:  int n;
599:
600:  if (__f32_bits(x) >= 0x42b17218u) {
601:    if (__f32_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u) {
602:      if (__f32_bits(x) == 0x7f800000u)
603:        return x;
604:      return x;
605:    }
606:    return 0x1.fffffep+127f * 0x1.fffffep+127f;
607:  }
608:  if (__f32_bits(x) >= 0xc2d20000u)
609:    return 0.0f;
610:
611:  n = (int)(x * 1.44269504088896340736f + (__f32_sign(x) ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
612:  r = x - (float)n * 0.69314718055994530942f;
613:
614:  y = __expf_c[0] +
615:      r * (__expf_c[1] +
616:           r * (__expf_c[2] +
617:                r * (__expf_c[3] + r * (__expf_c[4] + r * __expf_c[5]))));
618:
619:  return ldexpf(y, n);
620:}

622:float exp2f(float x) { return expf(x * 0.69314718055994530942f); }
623:
624:float logf(float x) {
625:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
626:  int e;
627:  float y, z;
628:
629:  if ((ix & 0x7f800000u) == 0) {
630:    if (ix << 1 == 0)
631:      return -INFINITY;
632:    return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
633:  }
634:  if (ix >= 0x7f800000u)
635:    return x;
636:
637:  e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
638:  ix = (ix & 0x007fffffu) | 0x3f800000u;
639:  x = __f32_from_bits(ix);
640:
641:  y = (x - 1.0f) / (x + 1.0f);
642:  z = y * y;
643:  y = y * (2.0f + z * (0.666666686534881591796875f + z * 0.4f));
644:
645:  return y + (float)e * 0.69314718055994530942f;
646:}

648:float log2f(float x) { return logf(x) * 1.44269504088896340736f; }
649:
650:float log10f(float x) { return logf(x) * 0.43429448190325182765f; }

652:static const double __exp_c[8] = {1.0,
653:                                  0.5,
654:                                  0.16666666666666665741,
655:                                  0.041666666666666664353,
656:                                  0.0083333333333333332177,
657:                                  0.0013888888888888889419,
658:                                  0.0001984126984126984127,
659:                                  0.000024801587301587301587};

661:double exp(double x) {
662:  double y, r;
663:  int n;
664:
665:  if (__f64_bits(x) >= 0x40862e42fefa39efULL) {
666:    if (__f64_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) {
667:      if (__f64_bits(x) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
668:        return x;
669:      return x;
670:    }
671:    return 0x1.fffffffffffffp+1023 * 0x1.fffffffffffffp+1023;
672:  }
673:  if (__f64_bits(x) >= 0xc0874910d52d3051ULL)
674:    return 0.0;
675:
676:  n = (int)(x * 1.44269504088896340736 + (__f64_sign(x) ? -0.5 : 0.5));
677:  r = x - (double)n * 0.69314718055994530942;
678:
679:  y = __exp_c[0] +
680:      r * (__exp_c[1] +
681:           r * (__exp_c[2] +
682:                r * (__exp_c[3] +
683:                     r * (__exp_c[4] +
684:                          r * (__exp_c[5] +
685:                               r * (__exp_c[6] + r * __exp_c[7]))))));
686:
687:  return ldexp(y, n);
688:}
689:
690:double exp2(double x) { return exp(x * 0.69314718055994530942); }
691:
692:double log(double x) {
693:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
694:  int e;
695:  double y, z;
696:
697:  if ((ix & 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) == 0) {
698:    if (ix << 1 == 0)
699:      return -INFINITY;
700:    return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
701:  }
702:  if (ix >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
703:    return x;
704:
705:  e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 0x3ff;
706:  ix = (ix & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) | 0x3ff0000000000000ULL;
707:  x = __f64_from_bits(ix);
708:
709:  y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0);
710:  z = y * y;
711:  y = y * (2.0 + z * (0.66666666666666662966 +
712:                      z * (0.4 + z * 0.28571428571428569843)));
713:
714:  return y + (double)e * 0.69314718055994530942;
715:}

717:double log2(double x) { return log(x) * 1.44269504088896340736; }
718:
719:double log10(double x) { return log(x) * 0.43429448190325182765; }

721:/* ============================================================================
722: * Power function
723: * ============================================================================
724: */
725:
726:float powf(float x, float y) {
727:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x), iy = __f32_bits(y);
728:  float r;
729:
730:  if (iy == 0 || x == 1.0f)
731:    return 1.0f;
732:  if (__float32_isnan(x) || __float32_isnan(y))
733:    return x + y;
734:  if (x == 0.0f) {
735:    if ((iy & 0x7fffffffu) > 0x7f800000u)
736:      return x + y;
737:    if (y > 0.0f)
738:      return (iy >> 31) ? INFINITY : 0.0f;
739:    if (y < 0.0f)
740:      return (iy >> 31) ? 0.0f : INFINITY;
741:    return 1.0f;
742:  }
743:  if (__float32_isinf(y)) {
744:    if (fabsf(x) == 1.0f)
745:      return 1.0f;
746:    if ((ix >> 31) == 0) {
747:      if (y > 0.0f)
748:        return (fabsf(x) > 1.0f) ? INFINITY : 0.0f;
749:      return (fabsf(x) > 1.0f) ? 0.0f : INFINITY;
750:    }
751:  }
752:
753:  r = logf(fabsf(x));
754:  r = expf(y * r);
755:
756:  if (ix >> 31) {
757:    float fy = floorf(y);
758:    if (y == fy) {
759:      uint32_t iy_int = (uint32_t)(int)fy;
760:      if (iy_int & 1)
761:        r = -r;
762:    } else {
763:      return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
764:    }
765:  }
766:  return r;
767:}
768:
769:double pow(double x, double y) {
770:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x), iy = __f64_bits(y);
771:  double r;
772:
773:  if (iy == 0 || x == 1.0)
774:    return 1.0;
775:  if (__float64_isnan(x) || __float64_isnan(y))
776:    return x + y;
777:  if (x == 0.0) {
778:    if ((iy & 0x7fffffffffffffffULL) > 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
779:      return x + y;
780:    if (y > 0.0)
781:      return (iy >> 63) ? INFINITY : 0.0;
782:    if (y < 0.0)
783:      return (iy >> 63) ? 0.0 : INFINITY;
784:    return 1.0;
785:  }
786:  if (__float64_isinf(y)) {
787:    if (fabs(x) == 1.0)
788:      return 1.0;
789:    if ((ix >> 63) == 0) {
790:      if (y > 0.0)
791:        return (fabs(x) > 1.0) ? INFINITY : 0.0;
792:      return (fabs(x) > 1.0) ? 0.0 : INFINITY;
793:    }
794:  }
795:
796:  /* Fast path: integer exponent (common case in Lua) */
797:  {
798:    double fy = floor(y);
799:    if (y == fy) {
800:      long long n = (long long)fy;
801:      int neg = 0;
802:      if (n < 0) {
803:        neg = 1;
804:        n = -n;
805:      }
806:      double r_fast = 1.0;
807:      double b = x;
808:      while (n) {
809:        if (n & 1)
810:          r_fast *= b;
811:        b *= b;
812:        n >>= 1;
813:      }
814:      return neg ? 1.0 / r_fast : r_fast;
815:    }
816:  }
817:
818:  r = log(fabs(x));
819:  r = exp(y * r);
820:
821:  if (ix >> 63) {
822:    double fy = floor(y);
823:    if (y == fy) {
824:      uint64_t iy_int = (uint64_t)(long long)fy;
825:      if (iy_int & 1)
826:        r = -r;
827:    } else {
828:      return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
829:    }
830:  }
831:  return r;
832:}
833:
834:/* ============================================================================
835: * Trigonometric functions — minimax polynomial with range reduction
836: * ============================================================================
837: */
838:
839:static const float __sinf_c[4] = {
840:    0.99999999999999991673f, -0.16666666666666665741f,
841:    0.0083333333333333332177f, -0.0001984126984126984127f};
842:
843:static const float __cosf_c[4] = {1.0f, -0.5f, 0.041666666666666664353f,
844:                                  -0.0013888888888888889419f};
845:
846:/* Range-reduce x into [-pi/4, pi/4], return the quadrant (0..3) */
847:static int __sinf_reduce(float *x) {
848:  const float pi = 3.14159265358979323846f;
849:  const float two_over_pi = 0.63661977236758134308f;
850:  int q;
851:  float y;
852:
853:  if (fabsf(*x) < 1.0e6f) {
854:    q = (int)(*x * two_over_pi + (__f32_sign(*x) ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
855:    y = *x - (float)q * (pi / 2.0f);
856:  } else {
857:    float t = *x * two_over_pi;
858:    q = (int)(t + (__f32_sign(*x) ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
859:    y = *x - (float)q * 1.57079632679489661923f;
860:    y = y - (float)q * 6.12323399573676588613e-17f;
861:  }
862:  *x = y;
863:  return q & 3;
864:}
865:
866:float sinf(float x) {
867:  float z, s;
868:  int q;
869:
870:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u)
871:    return x - x;
872:
873:  q = __sinf_reduce(&x);
874:  z = x * x;
875:
876:  s = x *
877:      (__sinf_c[0] + z * (__sinf_c[1] + z * (__sinf_c[2] + z * __sinf_c[3])));
878:
879:  if (q & 1)
880:    s = copysignf(1.0f, s) - s;
881:  if (q & 2)
882:    s = -s;
883:
884:  return s;
885:}
886:
887:float cosf(float x) {
888:  float z, c;
889:  int q;
890:
891:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u)
892:    return x - x;
893:
894:  q = __sinf_reduce(&x);
895:  q = (q + 1) & 3;
896:
897:  z = x * x;
898:  c = __cosf_c[0] + z * (__cosf_c[1] + z * (__cosf_c[2] + z * __cosf_c[3]));
899:
900:  if (q & 1)
901:    c = copysignf(1.0f, c) - c;
902:  if (q & 2)
903:    c = -c;
904:
905:  return c;
906:}
907:
908:float tanf(float x) {
909:  float s, c;
910:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u)
911:    return x - x;
912:  s = sinf(x);
913:  c = cosf(x);
914:  if (c == 0.0f)
915:    return copysignf(INFINITY, s);
916:  return s / c;
917:}
918:
919:float asinf(float x) {
920:  float z, r;
921:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
922:
923:  if (ix >= 0x7f800000u)
924:    return x - x;
925:  if (ix >= 0x3f800000u) {
926:    if (ix == 0x3f800000u)
927:      return (ix >> 31) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
928:    if (ix > 0x3f800000u)
929:      return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
930:  }
931:
932:  z = x * x;
933:  r = x * (1.0f + z * (0.16666667163372039794921875f +
934:                       z * (0.07500000298023223876953125f +
935:                            z * 0.0446428574621677398681640625f)));
936:  return r;
937:}

939:float acosf(float x) { return M_PI_2 - asinf(x); }
940:
941:float atanf(float x) {
942:  float z, r;
943:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
944:  int sign = ix >> 31;
945:
946:  if (ix >= 0x7f800000u) {
947:    if (ix == 0x7f800000u)
948:      return sign ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
949:    return x - x;
950:  }
951:
952:  x = fabsf(x);
953:
954:  if (x > 1.0f) {
955:    x = 1.0f / x;
956:    z = x * x;
957:    r = M_PI_2 -
958:        x * (1.0f + z * (-0.3333333432674407958984375f +
959:                         z * (0.199999988079071044921875f +
960:                              z * (-0.14285714924335479736328125f +
961:                                   z * 0.111111111938953399658203125f))));
962:    return sign ? -r : r;
963:  }
964:
965:  z = x * x;
966:  r = x * (1.0f + z * (-0.3333333432674407958984375f +
967:                       z * (0.199999988079071044921875f +
968:                            z * (-0.14285714924335479736328125f +
969:                                 z * 0.111111111938953399658203125f))));
970:  return sign ? -r : r;
971:}

973:float atan2f(float y, float x) {
974:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x), iy = __f32_bits(y);
975:
976:  if (__float32_isnan(x) || __float32_isnan(y))
977:    return x + y;
978:  if (iy == 0)
979:    return (ix >> 31) ? (ix == 0x80000000u ? M_PI : 0.0f) : 0.0f;
980:  if (ix == 0)
981:    return (iy >> 31) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
982:
983:  if (__float32_isinf(x)) {
984:    if (__float32_isinf(y)) {
985:      return (ix >> 31) ? ((iy >> 31) ? -2.35619449019234492885f
986:                                      : 2.35619449019234492885f)
987:                        : ((iy >> 31) ? -0.78539816339744830962f
988:                                      : 0.78539816339744830962f);
989:    }
990:    return (ix >> 31) ? ((iy >> 31) ? -M_PI : M_PI)
991:                      : ((iy >> 31) ? -0.0f : 0.0f);
992:  }
993:  if (__float32_isinf(y))
994:    return (iy >> 31) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
995:
996:  return atanf(y / x) + ((x < 0.0f) ? ((y < 0.0f) ? -M_PI : M_PI) : 0.0f);
997:}

999:/* Double-precision trig */
1000:static const double __sin_c[5] = {
1001:    1.0, -0.16666666666666665741, 0.0083333333333333332177,
1002:    -0.0001984126984126984127, 0.0000027557319223985890653};
1003:
1004:static const double __cos_c[5] = {1.0, -0.5, 0.041666666666666664353,
1005:                                  -0.0013888888888888889419,
1006:                                  0.000024801587301587301587};
1007:
1008:static int __sin_reduce(double *x) {
1009:  const double two_over_pi = 0.63661977236758134308;
1010:  int q;
1011:  double y;
1012:
1013:  if (fabs(*x) < 1.0e14) {
1014:    q = (int)(*x * two_over_pi + (__f64_sign(*x) ? -0.5 : 0.5));
1015:    y = *x - (double)q * (M_PI / 2.0);
1016:  } else {
1017:    double t = *x * two_over_pi;
1018:    q = (int)(t + (__f64_sign(*x) ? -0.5 : 0.5));
1019:    y = *x - (double)q * 1.57079632679489661923;
1020:    y = y - (double)q * 6.12323399573676588613e-17;
1021:  }
1022:  *x = y;
1023:  return q & 3;
1024:}
1025:
1026:double sin(double x) {
1027:  double z, s;
1028:  int q;
1029:
1030:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1031:    return x - x;
1032:
1033:  q = __sin_reduce(&x);
1034:  z = x * x;
1035:
1036:  s = x *
1037:      (__sin_c[0] +
1038:       z * (__sin_c[1] + z * (__sin_c[2] + z * (__sin_c[3] + z * __sin_c[4]))));
1039:
1040:  if (q & 1)
1041:    s = copysign(1.0, s) - s;
1042:  if (q & 2)
1043:    s = -s;
1044:
1045:  return s;
1046:}
1047:
1048:double cos(double x) {
1049:  double z, c;
1050:  int q;
1051:
1052:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1053:    return x - x;
1054:
1055:  q = __sin_reduce(&x);
1056:  q = (q + 1) & 3;
1057:
1058:  z = x * x;
1059:  c = __cos_c[0] +
1060:      z * (__cos_c[1] + z * (__cos_c[2] + z * (__cos_c[3] + z * __cos_c[4])));
1061:
1062:  if (q & 1)
1063:    c = copysign(1.0, c) - c;
1064:  if (q & 2)
1065:    c = -c;
1066:
1067:  return c;
1068:}
1069:
1070:double tan(double x) {
1071:  double s, c;
1072:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1073:    return x - x;
1074:  s = sin(x);
1075:  c = cos(x);
1076:  if (c == 0.0)
1077:    return copysign(INFINITY, s);
1078:  return s / c;
1079:}

1081:double asin(double x) {
1082:  double z, r;
1083:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
1084:
1085:  if (ix >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1086:    return x - x;
1087:  if (ix >= 0x3ff0000000000000ULL) {
1088:    if (ix == 0x3ff0000000000000ULL)
1089:      return (ix >> 63) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1090:    if (ix > 0x3ff0000000000000ULL)
1091:      return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
1092:  }
1093:
1094:  z = x * x;
1095:  r = x * (1.0 + z * (0.16666666666666665741 + z * (0.075000000000000000000 +
1096:                                                    z * 0.044642857142857143)));
1097:  return r;
1098:}

1100:double acos(double x) { return M_PI_2 - asin(x); }
1101:
1102:double atan(double x) {
1103:  double z, r;
1104:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
1105:  int sign = (int)(ix >> 63);
1106:
1107:  if (ix >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) {
1108:    if (ix == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1109:      return sign ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1110:    return x - x;
1111:  }
1112:
1113:  x = fabs(x);
1114:
1115:  if (x > 1.0) {
1116:    x = 1.0 / x;
1117:    z = x * x;
1118:    r = M_PI_2 - x * (1.0 + z * (-0.33333333333333331483 +
1119:                                 z * (0.19999999999999995559 +
1120:                                      z * (-0.14285714285714287654 +
1121:                                           z * 0.11111111111111110494))));
1122:    return sign ? -r : r;
1123:  }
1124:
1125:  z = x * x;
1126:  r = x *
1127:      (1.0 +
1128:       z * (-0.33333333333333331483 +
1129:            z * (0.19999999999999995559 +
1130:                 z * (-0.14285714285714287654 + z * 0.11111111111111110494))));
1131:  return sign ? -r : r;
1132:}

1134:double atan2(double y, double x) {
1135:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x), iy = __f64_bits(y);
1136:
1137:  if (__float64_isnan(x) || __float64_isnan(y))
1138:    return x + y;
1139:  if (iy == 0)
1140:    return (ix >> 63) ? (ix == 0x8000000000000000ULL ? M_PI : 0.0) : 0.0;
1141:  if (ix == 0)
1142:    return (iy >> 63) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1143:
1144:  if (__float64_isinf(x)) {
1145:    if (__float64_isinf(y)) {
1146:      return (ix >> 63) ? ((iy >> 63) ? -2.35619449019234492885
1147:                                      : 2.35619449019234492885)
1148:                        : ((iy >> 63) ? -0.78539816339744830962
1149:                                      : 0.78539816339744830962);
1150:    }
1151:    return (ix >> 63) ? ((iy >> 63) ? -M_PI : M_PI) : ((iy >> 63) ? -0.0 : 0.0);
1152:  }
1153:  if (__float64_isinf(y))
1154:    return (iy >> 63) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1155:
1156:  return atan(y / x) + ((x < 0.0) ? ((y < 0.0) ? -M_PI : M_PI) : 0.0);
1157:}

1197:
1198:double strtod(const char *nptr, char **endptr) {
1199:  const char *p = nptr;
1200:  while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t' || *p == '\n' || *p == '\r' || *p == '\f' ||
1201:         *p == '\v') {
1202:    p++;
1203:  }
1204:
1205:  double sign = 1.0;
1206:  if (*p == '-') {
1207:    sign = -1.0;
1208:    p++;
1209:  } else if (*p == '+') {
1210:    p++;
1211:  }
1212:
1213:  /* INF/INFINITY */
1214:  if (strncasecmp(p, "infinity", 8) == 0) {
1215:    if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)(p + 8);
1216:    return sign * HUGE_VAL;
1217:  }
1218:  if (strncasecmp(p, "inf", 3) == 0) {
1219:    if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)(p + 3);
1220:    return sign * HUGE_VAL;
1221:  }
1222:
1223:  /* NAN */
1224:  if (strncasecmp(p, "nan", 3) == 0) {
1225:    p += 3;
1226:    if (*p == '(') {
1227:      const char *q = p + 1;
1228:      while ((*q >= '0' && *q <= '9') ||
1229:             (*q >= 'a' && *q <= 'z') ||
1230:             (*q >= 'A' && *q <= 'Z') ||
1231:             *q == '_') {
1232:        q++;
1233:      }
1234:      if (*q == ')') {
1235:        p = q + 1;
1236:      }
1237:    }
1238:    if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)p;
1239:    return sign < 0 ? -NAN : NAN;
1240:  }
1241:
1242:  /* Hexadecimal Float */
1243:  if (p[0] == '0' && (p[1] == 'x' || p[1] == 'X')) {
1244:    const char *hstart = p;
1245:    const char *q = p + 2;
1246:    double mant = 0.0;
1247:    int any_digits = 0;
1248:
1249:    while (1) {
1250:      char c = *q;
1251:      int d;
1252:      if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
1253:        d = c - '0';
1254:      else if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
1255:        d = c - 'a' + 10;
1256:      else if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
1257:        d = c - 'A' + 10;
1258:      else
1259:        break;
1260:      mant = mant * 16.0 + (double)d;
1261:      q++;
1262:      any_digits = 1;
1263:    }
1264:    if (*q == '.') {
1265:      q++;
1266:      double scale = 1.0 / 16.0;
1267:      while (1) {
1268:        char c = *q;
1269:        int d;
1270:        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
1271:          d = c - '0';
1272:        else if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
1273:          d = c - 'a' + 10;
1274:        else if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
1275:          d = c - 'A' + 10;
1276:        else
1277:          break;
1278:        mant += (double)d * scale;
1279:        scale /= 16.0;
1280:        q++;
1281:        any_digits = 1;
1282:      }
1283:    }
1284:
1285:    if (any_digits) {
1286:      int exp = 0;
1287:      if (*q == 'p' || *q == 'P') {
1288:        q++;
1289:        int exp_sign = 1;
1290:        if (*q == '-') {
1291:          exp_sign = -1;
1292:          q++;
1293:        } else if (*q == '+') {
1294:          q++;
1295:        }
1296:        int e = 0;
1297:        while (*q >= '0' && *q <= '9') {
1298:          e = e * 10 + (*q - '0');
1299:          q++;
1300:        }
1301:        exp = exp_sign * e;
1302:      }
1303:      double result = ldexp(mant, exp);
1304:      if (endptr)
1305:        *endptr = (char *)q;
1306:      return sign * result;
1307:    }
1308:    /* '0x' with no hex digits after it: not a valid hex-float. Fall back
1309:     * to decimal parsing below, which will read the leading '0'. */
1310:    p = hstart;
1311:  }
1312:
1313:  /* Decimal Path */
1314:  unsigned long long mant = 0ULL;
1315:  int mant_digits = 0;
1316:  int frac_digits = 0;
1317:  int seen_dot = 0;
1318:  int has_digits = 0;
1319:  while (1) {
1320:    char c = *p;
1321:    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
1322:      has_digits = 1;
1323:      if (mant_digits < 19) {
1324:        mant = mant * 10ULL + (unsigned long long)(c - '0');
1325:        mant_digits++;
1326:        if (seen_dot)
1327:          frac_digits++;
1328:      } else if (!seen_dot) {
1329:        frac_digits--;
1330:      }
1331:      p++;
1332:    } else if (c == '.' && !seen_dot) {
1333:      seen_dot = 1;
1334:      p++;
1335:    } else {
1336:      break;
1337:    }
1338:  }
1339:
1340:  if (!has_digits) {
1341:    if (endptr)
1342:      *endptr = (char *)nptr;
1343:    return 0.0;
1344:  }
1345:
1346:  int exp10 = 0;
1347:  if (*p == 'e' || *p == 'E') {
1348:    const char *estart = p;
1349:    p++;
1350:    int exp_sign = 1;
1351:    if (*p == '-') {
1352:      exp_sign = -1;
1353:      p++;
1354:    } else if (*p == '+') {
1355:      p++;
1356:    }
1357:    if (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9') {
1358:      int e = 0;
1359:      while (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9') {
1360:        e = e * 10 + (*p - '0');
1361:        p++;
1362:      }
1363:      exp10 = exp_sign * e;
1364:    } else {
1365:      p = estart;
1366:    }
1367:  }
1368:
1369:  double val = (double)mant;
1370:  int total_exp = exp10 - frac_digits;
1371:  {
1372:    static const double p10[] = {1e0,  1e1,  1e2,  1e3,  1e4,  1e5,  1e6,  1e7,
1373:                                 1e8,  1e9,  1e10, 1e11, 1e12, 1e13, 1e14, 1e15,
1374:                                 1e16, 1e17, 1e18, 1e19, 1e20, 1e21, 1e22};
1375:    int e = total_exp;
1376:    if (e > 0) {
1377:      while (e > 22) {
1378:        val *= 1e22;
1379:        e -= 22;
1380:      }
1381:      val *= p10[e];
1382:    } else if (e < 0) {
1383:      e = -e;
1384:      while (e > 22) {
1385:        val /= 1e22;
1386:        e -= 22;
1387:      }
1388:      val /= p10[e];
1389:    }
1390:  }
1391:
1392:  if (endptr) {
1393:    *endptr = (char *)p;
1394:  }
1395:
1396:  return sign * val;
1397:}
1398:
1399:/* ============================================================================
1400: * Fixed-point (legacy — kept for Doom compat)
1401: * ============================================================================
1402: */
1403:
1404:int32_t fixmul(int32_t a, int32_t b) {
1405:  int64_t result = (int64_t)a * b;
1406:  return (int32_t)(result >> FP_SHIFT);
1407:}
1408:
1409:int32_t sin_fp(int32_t x) {
1410:  while (x > FP_PI)
1411:    x -= FP_2PI;
1412:  while (x < -FP_PI)
1413:    x += FP_2PI;
1414:
1415:  int32_t half_pi = 102944;
1416:  if (x > half_pi)
1417:    x = FP_PI - x;
1418:  else if (x < -half_pi)
1419:    x = -FP_PI - x;
1420:
1421:  int32_t x2 = fixmul(x, x);
1422:  int32_t x3 = fixmul(x2, x);
1423:  int32_t x5 = fixmul(x3, x2);
1424:
1425:  int32_t term1 = x;
1426:  int32_t term2 = fixmul(x3, 10923);
1427:  int32_t term3 = fixmul(x5, 546);
1428:
1429:  return term1 - term2 + term3;
1430:}
1431:
1432:int32_t cos_fp(int32_t x) { return sin_fp(x + 102944); }

20:# Optional escape hatch for incomplete userland compatibility layers: when set,
21:# the user-space compile rules drop -Werror without weakening the kernel build.
22:# GNU make does not accept arbitrary --bypas-sec switches, so the supported form
23:# is a variable assignment such as: make ARCH=aarch64 BYPASS_SEC=1 run
24:BYPASS_SEC ?= 0
25:BYPASS_USERLAND_ERRORS ?= $(BYPASS_SEC)
26:ifneq ($(BYPASS_USERLAND_ERRORS),0)
27:USER_CFLAGS += -Wno-error
28:endif

37:    override ARCH := aarch64
38:else ifeq ($(findstring amd64,$(ARCH)),amd64)
39:    override ARCH := amd64

42:# Common Compiler Flags
43:# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
44:# CONTRACT GATE — read before you reach for a way around it.
45:#
46:# kernel/include/kernel/nx_contract.h turns the invariants C cannot check into
47:# build failures: NX_MUST_USE on every -errno return, NX_ASSERT_OFFSET on every
48:# layout assembly depends on.  It is ALWAYS ON.  There is deliberately no flag
49:# to disable it, and adding one would defeat the reason it exists -- an earlier
50:# version was gated behind NX_STRICT and the result was that nobody ever saw a
51:# single diagnostic, because a gate you have to remember to switch on is a gate
52:# that is off.
53:#
54:# When the build stops on one of these, the build is correct and the code is
55:# not.  The three legitimate responses, in order of preference:
56:#
57:#   1. Handle the failure.  This is almost always the right answer.
58:#   2. Make the failure visible where it happens -- pr_err with the CONSEQUENCE
59:#      named, not just the fact ("no key events" beats "irq_register failed").
60:#   3. NX_DISCARD(expr, "why") -- only for an error-unwind path where the
61:#      cleanup failing changes nothing, or a best-effort refresh whose fallback
62:#      is documented.  It requires a written reason precisely so it can be
63:#      reviewed rather than merely noticed.
64:#
65:# What is NOT a response: deleting the annotation, adding -Wno-unused-result,
66:# or a (void) cast (which does not suppress warn_unused_result under GCC and
67:# only makes the omission look intentional -- the tree already had one).
68:# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
69:
70:COMMON_FLAGS = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wwrite-strings \
71:               -Wmissing-prototypes -Wstrict-prototypes \
72:               -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -nostdlib -nostartfiles \
73:               -fno-common -fstack-protector-strong \
74:               -fno-pic -fno-pie \
75:               -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
76:               -O2 -g
77:
78:# NX_STRICT=1 turns the nx_contract.h annotations into enforced attributes
79:# (NX_MUST_USE -> warn_unused_result).  With -Werror that makes every ignored
80:# -errno a hard error, which is the point: `make NX_STRICT=1` is the report of
81:# how much of the surface still drops failures on the floor.
82:ifeq ($(NX_STRICT),1)
83:COMMON_FLAGS += -DNX_STRICT
84:endif

97:

291:# Dependency files
292:# Every %.o: %.c rule (kernel AND user, see "Common compilation rules" below)
293:# passes -MMD -MP, so a per-TU .d file listing every header it pulled in
294:# lands next to each .o.  DEPS used to be JUST the kernel ones
295:# (KERN_C_OBJECTS:.o=.d) — userland .o files (nxres.o, nxsettings.o, ...)
296:# never got their .d included, so `make` had no idea a userland .c depended
297:# on a header like nxres.h/style_names.h: editing ONLY the header left every
298:# .o that #included it stale and un-rebuilt, silently running old code with
299:# no compile error to flag it.  Globbing every .d already on disk (kernel
300:# and user alike) closes that gap; empty on a clean tree (no .d files yet),
301:# which is fine — -include tolerates a missing/empty list.
302:DEPS = $(shell find $(BUILD_ROOT) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

366:# Two-pass link for the in-kernel symbol table (Phase A, kernel/lib/backtrace.c):
367:# pass 1 links without .ksyms, gen_ksyms.sh derives the table from `nm -n` of
368:# pass 1, pass 2 relinks with it.  .ksyms sits after .text in both kernel.ld
369:# scripts, so text addresses are identical across the passes (the table stays
370:# valid).  If generation ever fails the empty-table fallback in backtrace.c
371:# keeps the kernel functional (raw addresses).
372:NM = $(CROSS_COMPILE)nm
373:KERNEL_PRE = $(BUILD_DIR)/kernel.pre.elf
374:KSYMS_S    = $(BUILD_DIR)/ksyms.S
375:KSYMS_O    = $(BUILD_DIR)/ksyms.o
376:
377:$(KERNEL_PRE): $(KERN_OBJECTS)
378:	@$(LD) $(LDFLAGS_KERN) -o $@ $^
379:
380:$(KSYMS_O): $(KERNEL_PRE) tools/gen_ksyms.sh
381:	@tools/gen_ksyms.sh "$(NM)" $(KERNEL_PRE) $(KSYMS_S)
382:	@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $(KSYMS_S)
383:
384:$(KERNEL_ELF): $(KERN_OBJECTS) $(KSYMS_O)
385:	@$(LD) $(LDFLAGS_KERN) -o $@ $^
386:
387:$(KERNEL_BIN): $(KERNEL_ELF)
388:	@$(OBJCOPY) -O binary $< $@

448:# SDL cannot build under the kernel's -Werror/-Wpedantic regime; codegen and

460:              $(SDL_NEXSOS_OVERLAY_CPPFLAGS)

512:LUA_PORT_SRCS := $(USER_LIB_DIR)/portability/lua/lua_portability.c
513:LUA_OS1_SRCS  := $(USER_LIB_DIR)/os1LUA_lib.c
514:# lua_portability.h is FORCE-INCLUDED into every Lua translation unit
515:# (-include, LUA_CFLAGS below), so it is a real prerequisite of all of them.
516:# Without it listed here, editing that header silently leaves STALE objects:
517:# the .c files it overrides (lua.c's lua_stdin_is_tty / lua_readline) keep the
518:# upstream fallbacks while lua_portability.o alone rebuilds — which is exactly
519:# how the "echo ... | lua still prints the REPL banner" bug survived a rebuild.
520:LUA_PORT_HDR  := $(USER_LIB_DIR)/portability/lua/lua_portability.h
521:
522:LUA_OBJ_DIR := $(BUILD_DIR)/lua
523:LUA_CORE_OBJS := $(patsubst $(LUA_DIR)/%.c,$(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/%.o,$(LUA_CORE_SRCS))
524:LUA_PORT_OBJ  := $(BUILD_DIR)/$(USER_LIB_DIR)/portability/lua/lua_portability.o
525:LUA_OS1_OBJ   := $(BUILD_DIR)/$(USER_LIB_DIR)/os1LUA_lib.o
526:
527:LUA_LIB     := $(BUILD_DIR)/lua.a
528:LUA_OS1_LIB := $(BUILD_DIR)/libos1lua.a
529:
530:# The Lua module search path (LUA_ROOT/LDIR/CDIR/LUA_PATH_DEFAULT) is owned
531:# SOLELY by the force-included lua_portability.h — a C header, so the ';'
532:# path separators are inside a real string literal.  It must NOT be passed
533:# as -DLUA_PATH_DEFAULT=\"...;...\" here: Make forwards the \" verbatim, the
534:# shell reads it as a literal quote (not a delimiter), and the unquoted ';'
535:# then split the gcc line into pieces ("no input files" + bogus commands).
536:LUA_CFLAGS = $(ARCH_CFLAGS) -O2 -g -Wall \
537:             -Wno-error \
538:             -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -nostdlib -nostartfiles \
539:             -fno-common -fstack-protector-strong -fno-pic -fno-pie \
540:             -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
541:             -DLUA_USE_NEXSOS \
542:             -Iinclude/abi \
543:             -Iinclude/api \
544:             -I$(LUA_DIR) \
545:             -I$(USER_LIB_DIR)/portability/lua \
546:             -include lua_portability.h
547:
548:$(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/%.o: $(LUA_DIR)/%.c $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
549:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
550:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
551:
552:$(LUA_PORT_OBJ): $(LUA_PORT_SRCS) $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
553:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
554:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
555:
556:$(LUA_OS1_OBJ): $(LUA_OS1_SRCS) $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
557:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
558:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
559:
560:$(LUA_LIB): $(LUA_CORE_OBJS) $(LUA_PORT_OBJ)
561:	@echo "  [AR]     $@"
562:	@$(AR) rcs $@ $^
563:
564:$(LUA_OS1_LIB): $(LUA_OS1_OBJ)
565:	@echo "  [AR]     $@"
566:	@$(AR) rcs $@ $^
567:
568:liblua: $(LUA_LIB) $(LUA_OS1_LIB)
569:.PHONY: liblua
570:
571:$(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/lua.o: $(LUA_DIR)/lua.c $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
572:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
573:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
574:
575:$(BUILD_DIR)/lua.elf: $(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/lua.o $(LUA_OS1_LIB) $(LUA_LIB) $(USER_LIB_O) $(USER_SYSCALL_O) $(USER_MALLOC_O)
576:	@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(USER_LINK_FLAGS) -Wl,-Ttext=0x80000000 -e _start -o $@ \
577:		$(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/lua.o \
578:		-Wl,--start-group $(LUA_LIB) $(LUA_OS1_LIB) -Wl,--end-group \
579:		$(USER_LIB_O) $(USER_SYSCALL_O) $(USER_MALLOC_O)

803:	@# /home: the ONLY user-writable tree (vfs_write_allowed tree ACL —

805:	@# /home/shared).  Pre-created because ext4 has no directory creation yet:
806:	@# Documents/doom hosts doom's config+savegames (replaces the hardcoded
807:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Documents/doom

878:# ==============================================================================
879:# QEMU Flags
880:# ==============================================================================
881:
882:# A terminal launched from a snap-packaged GUI app (VS Code's integrated
883:# terminal is the common case on Ubuntu) exports GTK_PATH/GTK_EXE_PREFIX/
884:# GTK_MODULES/GIO_MODULE_DIR/XDG_DATA_DIRS/LOCPATH pointing into that snap's
885:# own bundle (e.g. /snap/code/<rev>/usr/lib/.../gtk-3.0). Any GTK app started
886:# from that shell — including QEMU with -display default, which is a GTK
887:# frontend — inherits them and tries to dlopen its GTK module set from the
888:# wrong snap's directory tree, which pulls in an old bundled libpthread.so.0
889:# incompatible with the host's glibc (undefined symbol __libc_pthread_init,
890:# GLIBC_PRIVATE) and QEMU dies before ever opening a window. None of these
891:# vars are needed for our own display: strip them unconditionally (no-op if
892:# unset, so this is a no-op on macOS/BSD too) rather than ask every
893:# contributor to remember to launch from a "clean" terminal.
894:QEMU_RUN = env -u GTK_PATH -u GTK_EXE_PREFIX -u GTK_MODULES -u GTK_IM_MODULE_FILE \
895:               -u GIO_MODULE_DIR -u GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR -u XDG_DATA_DIRS \
896:               -u XDG_DATA_HOME -u LOCPATH $(QEMU)
897:
898:ifeq ($(ARCH), amd64)
899:QEMU_FLAGS = -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
900:             -display default,show-cursor=on \
901:			 -vga none \
902:             -device virtio-gpu-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
903:             -device virtio-keyboard-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
904:             -device virtio-mouse-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
905:             -drive if=none,file=$(DISK_IMG),id=hd0,format=raw \
906:             -device virtio-blk-pci,drive=hd0,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off
907:
908:QEMU_RELEASE_FLAGS = -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
909:                     -display default,show-cursor=on \
910:                     -device virtio-gpu-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
911:                     -device virtio-keyboard-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
912:                     -device virtio-mouse-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off
913:else
914:# AArch64: pass -dtb $(VIRT_DTB) so QEMU loads the pre-generated device tree into RAM
915:# and sets x0 = dtb_load_address in its aarch64 boot stub.  Without -dtb, QEMU does not
916:# generate/load a DTB for bare-metal ELF kernels and x0 arrives as 0 at _start.
917:QEMU_FLAGS = -M virt -cpu cortex-a57 -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
918:             -display default,show-cursor=on \
919:             -device virtio-gpu-device \
920:             -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-mouse-device \
921:             -drive if=none,file=$(DISK_IMG),id=hd0,format=raw -device virtio-blk-device,drive=hd0 \
922:             -dtb $(VIRT_DTB)
923:
924:QEMU_RELEASE_FLAGS = -M virt -cpu cortex-a57 -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
925:                     -display default,show-cursor=on \
926:                     -device virtio-gpu-device \
927:                     -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-mouse-device \
928:                     -drive if=none,file=$(RELEASE_DIR)/disk.img,id=hd0,format=raw -device virtio-blk-device,drive=hd0
929:endif

935:release:
936:	@echo "========================================"
937:	@echo "  Creating Full Release $(VERSION)"
938:	@echo "========================================"
939:	@$(MAKE) ARCH=amd64 release-arch VERSION=$(VERSION)
940:	@$(MAKE) ARCH=aarch64 release-arch VERSION=$(VERSION)
941:	@echo "========================================"
942:	@echo "✓ Full release $(VERSION) complete!"
943:	@echo "  Location: $(RELEASE_BASE)"
944:	@echo "========================================"
945:
946:release-arch: all
947:	@echo "--> Building $(ARCH) release..."
948:	@rm -rf $(RELEASE_DIR)
949:	@mkdir -p $(RELEASE_DIR)
950:	@if [ "$(ARCH)" = "amd64" ]; then \
951:		set -e; \
952:		mkdir -p $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub; \
953:		cp $(KERNEL_ELF) $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/kernel.elf; \
954:		cp $(DISK_IMG) $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/disk.img; \
955:		echo 'set timeout=0' > $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
956:		echo 'set default=0' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
957:		echo 'menuentry "NexsOS1" {' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
958:		echo '    insmod part_gpt' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
959:		echo '    insmod ext2' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
960:		echo '    insmod loopback' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
961:		echo '    multiboot2 /boot/kernel.elf' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
962:		echo '    loopback loop /boot/disk.img' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
963:		echo '    ls (loop,gpt3)/' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
964:		echo '    module2 /boot/disk.img diskimg' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
965:		echo '    boot' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
966:		echo '}' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
967:		echo "AMD64 files ready: boot/kernel.elf, boot/disk.img"; \
968:		mkdir -p $(RELEASE_DIR)/iso/boot/grub; \
969:		cp -r $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/* $(RELEASE_DIR)/iso/boot/; \
970:		GRUB_MKRESCUE=""; \
971:		for c in i686-elf-grub-mkrescue grub-mkrescue; do \
972:			if command -v $$c >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
973:				GRUB_MKRESCUE=$$c; break; \
974:			fi; \
975:		done; \
976:		if [ -z "$$GRUB_MKRESCUE" ]; then \
977:			echo "Errore: grub-mkrescue non trovato"; \
978:			exit 1; \
979:		fi; \
980:		echo "-> Creo ISO con $$GRUB_MKRESCUE..."; \
981:		$$GRUB_MKRESCUE -o $(RELEASE_DIR)/NexsOS1-amd64-$(VERSION).iso $(RELEASE_DIR)/iso; \
982:		echo "-> Rimuovo MBR hybrid per renderla leggibile da macOS..."; \
983:		dd if=/dev/zero of=$(RELEASE_DIR)/NexsOS1-amd64-$(VERSION).iso bs=512 count=1 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null; \
984:		echo "ISO creata: $(RELEASE_DIR)/NexsOS1-amd64-$(VERSION).iso"; \
985:	else \
986:		cp $(KERNEL_BIN) $(RELEASE_DIR)/kernel.img; \
987:		cp $(DISK_IMG) $(RELEASE_DIR)/disk.img; \
988:		echo "AArch64 release: kernel.img + disk.img"; \
989:	fi
990:
991:test-release: release-arch
992:	@echo "Starting QEMU Release Test for $(ARCH) (Version: $(VERSION))..."
993:ifeq ($(ARCH), amd64)
994:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_RELEASE_FLAGS) \
995:		-drive if=none,file=$(RELEASE_DIR)/NexsOS1-amd64-$(VERSION).iso,id=hd0,format=raw \
996:		-device virtio-blk-pci,drive=hd0,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off
997:else
998:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_RELEASE_FLAGS) -kernel $(RELEASE_DIR)/kernel.img

1001:# ==============================================================================
1002:# Development Execution
1003:# ==============================================================================
1004:
1005:# AArch64: generate the QEMU virt device tree for the exact machine configuration
1006:# used in the run target.  The DTB must match the devices, memory size, and SMP
1007:# count so that fdt_get_mem_regions() and fdt_count_cpus() see accurate data.
1008:# dumpdtb exits immediately after writing the DTB; no kernel is required.
1009:# amd64 does not use a DTB (discovery via multiboot2), so this target is aarch64-only.
1010:ifeq ($(ARCH), aarch64)
1011:$(VIRT_DTB): disk | $(BUILD_DIR)
1012:	@echo "  [DTB]    Generating QEMU virt device tree -> $@"
1013:	@ERRLOG=$$(mktemp); \
1014:	if ! $(QEMU_RUN) -M virt -cpu cortex-a57 -m 5G -smp 4 \
1015:	         -device virtio-gpu-device \
1016:	         -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-mouse-device \
1017:	         -drive if=none,file=$(DISK_IMG),id=hd0,format=raw \
1018:	         -device virtio-blk-device,drive=hd0 \
1019:	         -machine dumpdtb=$@ 2>"$$ERRLOG"; then \
1020:	    cat "$$ERRLOG" >&2; rm -f "$$ERRLOG"; \
1021:	    echo "  [DTB]    $(QEMU_RUN) failed — see stderr above (broken/snap-shadowed QEMU install is a common cause)." >&2; \
1022:	    exit 1; \
1023:	fi; \
1024:	rm -f "$$ERRLOG"
1025:	@echo "  [DTB]    Done ($$($(STAT_SIZE) $@) bytes)"
1026:
1027:# AArch64 run: use kernel.bin (raw binary) so QEMU's aarch64 boot stub sets x0 = dtb_addr.
1028:# A raw binary triggers QEMU's arm_load_kernel image-loading path; combined with -dtb,
1029:# QEMU loads the DTB into RAM and passes its address in x0 before jumping to the entry.
1030:# Using kernel.elf (ELF) without a Linux image header leaves x0=0 (no DTB handover).
1031:run: all $(VIRT_DTB)
1032:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_BIN)
1033:
1034:run-direct: run
1035:
1036:debug: all
1037:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_BIN) -s -S
1038:else
1039:run: all
1040:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_ELF)
1041:
1042:run-direct: run
1043:
1044:debug: all
1045:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_ELF) -s -S
1046:endif
1047:

1049:# lockcheck — the two memory/lock rules as a build gate (scripts/check-lockrules.py).
1050:# Not yet wired into `all`: the transitive closure is deliberately over-eager
1051:# and the current output needs a triage pass before it can block a build.
1052:# Run it before touching the scheduler or any teardown path.
1053:lockcheck:
1054:	@python3 scripts/check-lockrules.py

1065:	@which $(QEMU) > /dev/null && echo "✓ QEMU: $(QEMU)" || echo "✗ QEMU not found"
1066:	@if [ -n "$(GRUB_MKRESCUE)" ]; then echo "✓ GRUB: $(GRUB_MKRESCUE)"; else echo "✗ GRUB mancante"; fi
